entityDescription:
ANcybernetics is an Italian deep-tech company developing bio-inspired autonomous underwater robotic systems for environmental monitoring, infrastructure inspection and the collection of high-quality subsea data. Founded as an academic spin-off of Università Politecnica delle Marche (UNIVPM), ANcybernetics has been registered in the Italian Special Register of Innovative Start-ups since September 2024.
The company designs and develops compact Biomimetic Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (BAUVs) combining bio-inspired propulsion, autonomous navigation, modular sensor integration and onboard artificial intelligence. Its flagship platform, POSEIDRONE, uses fin-based propulsion inspired by fish locomotion instead of conventional propellers, enabling high manoeuvrability while reducing disturbance to the surrounding environment and seabed.
POSEIDRONE is designed to perform autonomous and repeatable missions and can be deployed directly from shore or from small vessels, reducing the logistical complexity typically associated with underwater robotic operations. Its modular architecture allows the platform to be configured according to the specific mission and data requirements, integrating optical cameras, acoustic sensors, environmental probes and other specialised payloads. Onboard computing and AI enable real-time data processing, perception and the identification of features or anomalies of interest.
ANcybernetics targets applications including the inspection and monitoring of submerged infrastructure, ports, pipelines, cables, reservoirs and coastal assets, as well as seabed mapping, marine habitat monitoring, biodiversity assessment and environmental data collection. The company is developing solutions aimed at making underwater monitoring more autonomous, scalable, repeatable and accessible, while reducing human exposure to hazardous underwater operations.
ANcybernetics develops its core robotic, control and autonomy technologies in-house and is building an ecosystem of specialised sensors, communication systems and industrial partners around its platforms. The company is also exploring the integration of underwater robotics with satellite-enabled services, including satellite navigation, Earth Observation and satellite communications, to support georeferenced surveys, remote operations and integrated monitoring of maritime, coastal and water-related assets.
Through its combination of robotics, AI, bio-inspired engineering and environmental sensing, ANcybernetics aims to bridge the gap between traditional remotely operated vehicles and large, complex autonomous underwater systems, enabling a new generation of flexible and cost-effective subsea monitoring services.

Martinr B.V. is a Netherlands-based micro-enterprise specialising in front-end development and user interface design for space engineering, Earth observation, human spaceflight and civil protection.
Core capabilities: front-end web application development in TypeScript, user experience design for complex technical and scientific data, interactive data visualisation and dashboards, design systems and accessibility, and real-time and interactive web applications. Technologies include TypeScript, React, WebRTC, WebGL and mapping libraries, and REST/OpenAPI integration.
The company draws on four years of experience delivering software for ESA and related institutional programmes within teams at Starion Group, ATG Europe and Space Applications Services. This work included review interfaces for ECSS-E-TM-10-25 models in support of model-based systems engineering (UI-DSM), an ESA Earth Observation mission database supporting capability mapping and long-term planning (EORSA-DB), a live meeting tool used during Axiom Mission 4 to connect the ISS crew with audiences on Earth, and the PPRD Med disaster prevention and response platform. This provides working familiarity with ECSS standards, MBSE tooling and ESA review processes.
Martinr B.V. is available to ESA and to prime contractors as a subcontractor or consortium partner for front-end development, UI/UX design, data visualisation and interactive web applications.

Impact Ninja is a specialised Poland-based consultancy and expert firm focused on social impact evaluation, evidence-based assessment, and narrative modeling for research, technology, and innovation.Founded and led by Dr. Marta Wróblewska—a leading European expert on impact assessment with a PhD from the University of Warwick—the firm integrates academic rigor with practical policy experience. Dr. Wróblewska brings extensive experience from the public agency sector, having served in operational and strategic roles at the National Centre for Research and Development (NCBR) in Poland, where she also chaired expert evaluation panels. Her research has been supported by major competitive research grants (including the Volkswagen Stiftung and NCN) and active membership in the Research on Research Institute (RoRI) at University College London (UCL). She is author of a PhD Thesis, a practical ebooks and several academic papers dedicated to research impact evaluation policies and related institutional change.

Impact Ninja offers a complete suite of impact assessment services, including strategic verification, custom narrative modeling, and executive training. The firm’s methodologies are continuously informed by state-of-the-art international research. Having advised dozens of institutions across diverse disciplines and trained hundreds of experts, Impact Ninja specializes in translating complex scientific, technological, and corporate efforts into clear, credible, and measurable social outcomes.

entityDescription: Klimaforge AS is a Norwegian company building satellite-based evidence infrastructure for EU forest regulation and forest-carbon markets. Its EUDR compliance engine turns Copernicus Sentinel-1/2 change detection into audit-ready compliance verdicts by cross-checking flagged forest clearings against independent government land registries — live today in Norway and Germany — rather than relying on supplier-submitted paperwork. A parallel above-ground biomass platform, using satellite radar, optical and spaceborne LiDAR data, extends the same detection core into forest-carbon measurement, reporting and verification (MRV), delivered nationally in Estonia and piloted in Norway. Klimaforge is downstream of ESA's Earth Observation systems (Copernicus Sentinel-1/2, NASA GEDI, ALOS PALSAR-2) and is preparing to launch commercially in Norway from January 2027.

Entity Description / Overview:
SustainGenix GmbH (Lörrach, Germany) is a space-downstream software, social impact, and geo-information enterprise specialising in high-altitude climate resilience, spatial risk analytics, and off-grid hazard intelligence. The company owns and governs the intellectual property of the 1,700 km Great Himalaya Trail (GHT) spatial dataset, built upon fifteen years of georeferenced field exploration, high-altitude mapping, and extensive research on tourism impacts across fragile mountain ecosystems.
SustainGenix develops the "Human-Digital Twin" Safety Engine, a 3-tier technology architecture bridging space-borne sensors with community-based observation and research, and storytelling:

Space Layer: Ingestion and automated processing of European Space Agency (ESA) Copernicus Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data for cloud-penetrating interferometry (InSAR), surface deformation tracking, and Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) monitoring across complex mountain terrain.

AI & Cloud Layer: Dialect-adapting, offline-first speech-to-text AI models (Sherpa, Tamang, Nepali) and serverless cloud analytics that convert spoken local reports into structured, georeferenced spatial vectors and real-time B2B enterprise risk APIs.

Ground-Truth & Community Layer: Deployment of ruggedised satellite communicators and mobile tools to local micro-entrepreneurs (female teahouse hosts) and licensed trekking guides. This layer functions both as an off-grid safety network and as a digital platform for community storytelling, preserving cultural heritage and publishing local narratives in native dialects.

Research & Commercial Capabilities: SustainGenix conducts field research into mountain tourism impacts, socio-economic equity, and climate adaptation. The company actively promotes responsible tourism along Himalayan corridors by supporting firewood elimination, waste management, and direct economic inclusion. SustainGenix commercialises its spatial assets through enterprise hazard APIs for tour operators and travel insurers (Duty of Care compliance), B2C dynamic safety navigation apps (FarOut, OutdoorActive and ride with GPS, B2G/NGO cryosphere change analytics, and white-label "Dynamic Trail OS" software licensing for international mountain trail authorities worldwide.

description:
NEMA Systems Ltd combines advanced electrical and electro-mechanical design capability, decades of aerospace, defence and space actuation and certification experience and established UK manufacturing capability to develop and industrialise high-performance motors, power electronics, drives and actuation systems. Our integrated approach brings together engineering, manufacturing and test capability to reduce development risk, accelerate programmes and provide customers with a single, experienced partner for demanding applications.
Quality and traceability are embedded throughout our approach. Decades of experience through our parent company NEMA Ltd allows us to design and manufacture to AS9100 Rev D, alongside ISO 9001 and relevant OEM supplier approvals. Space-product development and assurance activities are aligned with the requirements of ISO 14300-1:2023 and ISO 14300-2:2023, together with the applicable ISO/ECSS technical standards identified through the project requirements and compliance matrix. Specific actuator verification and qualification tests under ECSS-Q-ST-60 / ECSS-E-ST-33 may be performed via established test houses and national facilities. 
NEMA Systems was formed following a decade of close working between NEMA UK Ltd, The University of Nottingham and Ultema Consultancy Ltd. It formalises the trusted relationship and allows NEMA Systems to benefit from the abilities and experience of all three founding parents of the business. Our team has a long history of developing and manufacturing actuators, motors and drives to create electro-mechanical systems for demanding environments. This experience informs the way we approach engineering, verification, manufacturing and programme delivery.
entityDescription:
NEMA Systems Ltd is a UK-based engineering company specialising in advanced electro-mechanical, power electronics, and high-performance drive systems for aerospace, defence, and electrified transport applications.

Formed from a collaborative foundation bringing together expertise across industrial manufacturing, systems engineering, and academic research, NEMA Systems operates at the intersection of innovation and application. The company integrates capabilities spanningelectrical machines, power electronics, control systems, and full system architecture design, enabling the rapid development of high-performance, certifiable technologies for demanding environments.
Our heritage is rooted in a strong UK engineering ecosystem combining:
•Advanced machine design and manufacturing capability.

entityDescription:
Darwins Geospatial S.L. is a Spanish Earth-observation company that turns satellite, aerial and drone data into environmental indicators and the software platforms that deliver them. Its work spans two integrated capabilities: the scientific side — deriving and validating indicators of vegetation condition, soil moisture, water stress, soil degradation and habitat conservation status from Copernicus Sentinel and complementary missions, using remote sensing and machine learning — and the engineering side — building the cloud infrastructure, data pipelines and web platforms through which those indicators reach end users, with tenant and user management, large-raster serving and export tooling.Darwin delivers as a technical partner within consortia and directly for institutional clients, covering habitat
mapping and conservation-status assessment, environmental exposure indicators for public-health research, biodiversity and canopy analysis from drone data, and soil erosion modelling. It operates on Google Cloud and object-storage architectures and works with open standards and open-source tooling.

entityDescription:
Comobi – Orchestrating multimodal, autonomous-ready mobility
Ambition
Comobi BV (Gent, Belgium) runs a mobility platform for shared airport and station transfers. At its core is a proprietary pricing and matching algorithm. It groups passengers into shared rides, sets fair dynamic prices and assigns each trip to the right vehicle. Our ambition goes beyond one vehicle type or one fleet. We want to optimise the mobility system as a whole, planning across cars, vans, buses and, soon, autonomous shuttles as one coordinated network. This means fewer empty kilometres, higher occupancy and a lower cost and carbon footprint per passenger.
Why navigation and satellite technology matter in the shift to autonomy
Today a human driver fills the gaps in any mobility service. They read the traffic, handle a closed road, find the right terminal entrance and adjust when a flight lands early. Autonomous operations remove that human layer, so the intelligence has to move into the system itself.
In an autonomous model, Comobi acts as the service owner. It holds the customer demand, builds the trips and hands assignments to vehicle owners: autonomous operators running their own fleets. For this handover to work reliably, both sides need a shared, precise and constantly updated picture of the operating environment:
- High-integrity positioning and navigation (GNSS, including Galileo's high-accuracy and authentication services), so assignments, pick-up points and handovers are exact and trustworthy
- Satellite-based situational awareness, such as Earth observation, weather and real-time disruption data, so the service layer can re-plan routes, timing and vehicle allocation before problems reach the passenger
- Resilient connectivity, including satellite links where terrestrial networks fall short, so vehicles and the platform stay in contact at all times
Space-based data makes it possible to go from "dispatching a driver" to "orchestrating an autonomous fleet." It gives the service owner the context a human driver used to supply.
Multivendor collaboration
Comobi does not aim to build every component itself. We want to act as the neutral orchestration layer in a multivendor ecosystem. That means working with autonomous vehicle operators, navigation technology providers, satellite data providers and data storage and processing partners, with a preference for local and European partners. Our aim is to launch multivendor pilot operations. In these pilots, assignments, positioning data and situational information flow through open interfaces between the service owner and several vehicle operators. That makes autonomous mobility scalable, interoperable and grounded in European space capabilities.

description:
Zero Gravity Works is a European contract manufacturer of pharmaceutical crystals grown in low Earth orbit.
In microgravity the absence of gravity-driven convection lets crystals grow under diffusion-limited conditions, yielding a narrower and more uniform crystal size distribution than terrestrial processes reliably achieve at industrial scale. We crystallise a partner's small-molecule active pharmaceutical ingredient in orbit and deliver the drug substance back on Earth. For the partner it is a standard API supply relationship: the space complexity stays with us.
Two problems make this worth doing. A molecule can be stalled in development by its crystal form: a metastable polymorph that does not survive shelf life, or a commercial form whose quality varies from batch to batch in a narrow therapeutic index product. And a product approaching patent expiry can be defended with a new, patentable crystal form that a generic manufacturer cannot reproduce.
The system is a crystallisation module developed in four configurations: a ground unit that reproduces the process in the laboratory and establishes the reference data; a qualification unit for environmental and acceptance testing; a 12U CubeSat flight unit that crystallises in orbit and returns its measurements by telemetry; and a recovery module that brings material back to Earth. On-board process monitoring is based on Raman spectroscopy and microscopy.
Zero Gravity Works is participating in the ESA Business Incubation Centre Milan.
We are looking for partners and suppliers in CubeSat systems engineering and payload accommodation; ruggedisation and space qualification of optical instruments, in particular Raman spectrometers; thermal control and heat rejection for a liquid payload; launch and ground segment services; and solid-state analytical services for pharmaceutical materials.
entityDescription:
Zero Gravity Works (ZGW) is an Italian deep-tech company based in Milan, developing an orbital platform for the crystallisation of small-molecule pharmaceutical active ingredients.
In low Earth orbit, the absence of gravity-driven convection allows crystals to grow under diffusion-limited conditions, producing a narrower and more uniform size distribution than terrestrial processes reliably achieve at industrial scale. ZGW operates as a contract manufacturer of drug substance rather than as a drug developer: the molecule of a pharmaceutical partner is crystallised in orbit and the material is returned to Earth, while the space complexity remains with ZGW.
The system is built around a crystallisation module developed in successive configurations: a ground laboratory unit establishing the reference process, a qualification unit for environmental testing, a flight unit built to the 12U CubeSat standard returning its measurements by telemetry, and a recovery module returning the crystallised material in a re-entry capsule.
Core technical areas:
- macroscopic crystallisation reactor and fluidic handling for autonomous operation in microgravity
- in-situ Raman spectroscopy and optical microscopy, ruggedised for launch loads and the orbital environment
- thermal control, payload accommodation and mission and ground-segment design for a small satellite platform
- computational modelling of crystallisation dynamics in microgravity
Current activities focus on the preliminary design and feasibility of the orbital crystallisation module and on the feasibility and ruggedisation of the on-board Raman instrument, in collaboration with Politecnico di Milano and the University of Pavia. Technology Readiness Level: 3.
ZGW has been selected for incubation at ESA BIC Milan (2026–2028) and is registered as an innovative startup in the Italian Companies Register.

entityDescription:
SENSE AI S.r.l. is an Italian innovative technology startup focused on the research, development and industrialisation of advanced Artificial Intelligence solutions, semantic data infrastructures and intelligent process automation.
The company develops a proprietary, scalable SaaS platform based on Large Language Models, multi-agent architectures, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), semantic knowledge graphs, vector databases, predictive analytics and intelligent workflow automation. Its technological approach combines structured domain knowledge with generative AI, enabling the creation of specialised systems capable of processing complex information, supporting decision-making and automating highly regulated operational processes. 
SENSE AI adopts a model-agnostic architecture, integrating both commercial AI models through APIs and open-weight models deployed on dedicated GPU infrastructure. This approach reduces technological dependency on individual providers and allows sensitive information to be processed within controlled environments when required. The platform uses PostgreSQL with vector search capabilities, a proprietary knowledge graph and multi-agent RAG pipelines to retrieve, interpret and validate structured and unstructured information. 
A central element of the SENSE AI technology is its semantic knowledge infrastructure, designed to transform complex public and private datasets into interconnected, machine-readable knowledge. AI agents operate on this semantic layer to generate, classify, match and validate information, while automated validation mechanisms and mandatory human supervision ensure traceability, explainability and control over critical outputs. 
The technology is currently applied through two integrated vertical platforms, Sense Academy and Sense Worknet, dedicated respectively to digital learning, skills intelligence, workforce management and employment services. Both systems share the same semantic engine and knowledge infrastructure, creating a continuous data-driven connection between skills, training, professional profiles and operational requirements. 
SENSE AI's R&D activities include the development of knowledge graphs, generative AI systems, semantic matching engines, predictive models, explainable AI mechanisms, automated validation systems and specialised digital workflows. The company follows a human-in-the-loop approach in which AI supports professionals and operators without replacing human responsibility in critical decisions. 
The technological infrastructure is designed around security, scalability, interoperability and regulatory compliance. The architecture includes EU-based cloud infrastructure, granular role-based access control, immutable audit trails, secure data management and dedicated computing resources for AI workloads involving sensitive information. The company's development roadmap also includes compliance with GDPR and the EU AI Act, together with ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 42001 certification pathways. 
SENSE AI's objective is to build specialised AI systems capable of transforming complex data, domain knowledge and operational rules into secure, explainable and scalable digital solutions.

entityDescription:
The IMDEA Energy Institute is a research center created by the Regional Government of the Community of Madrid as a non-profit foundation to develop R&D activities, prioritizing scientific excellence, technology transfer, and social impact in the development of clean and renewable energy technologies in its objectives and daily work.
The IMDEA Energy Institute's main objective is to contribute to the development and establishment of a sustainable, fully decarbonized, economically competitive energy system that guarantees security of supply throughout the entire energy production, transformation, and end-use chain.
The IMDEA Energy Institute develops energy-related R&D activities by combining a policy of excellence in recruiting researchers, the implementation of appropriate scientific infrastructure, and the promotion of intense collaboration with the industrial sector. The quality of the research carried out by IMDEA Energy was recognized in 2020 with the prestigious accreditation as a "María de Maeztu" Research Unit awarded by the Ministry of Science and Innovation and in 2025 with th accreditation as a "Severo Ochoa" center.
R&D activities at IMDEA Energy are focused on seven main research themes:
- Production of sustainable fuels for effective decarbonization of the transport sector: hydrogen, biofuels, and other alternative fuels from renewable and/or residual sources.
- Solar energy systems and technologies, with a special emphasis on concentrated solar thermal energy for electricity production and industrial process heat.
- Energy storage using thermal, electrochemical, and thermochemical methods to increase the security of supply and penetration of renewable energy and distributed electricity generation.
- Smart management of electricity demand and improved reliability and stability of future power grids.
- Development of technologies and strategies for efficient end-use energy, with particular application to the development of a net-zero emissions industry.
- CCU routes for conversion into products of interest and high demand.
- Conducting sustainability studies on new energy technologies and systems and scenario modeling for energy planning.
The research objectives have been prioritized based on the main recommendations of the Scientific Council, as well as the challenges to be met in terms of decarbonization and circularity by 2030 and the future achievement of a carbon-neutral economy by 2050. These priorities have been complemented by the valorization and acceleration of the development of technological solutions for energy supply security, as promoted by the REPower Europe initiative to reduce energy dependence, and the preparation of strategies to anticipate the new challenges in industrial decarbonization envisaged in the Clean Industrial Deal.

entityDescription:
ENT is a social economic initiative integrated by a multidisciplinary group of highly trained and experienced professionals dedicated to the elaboration, analysis and implementation of public environmental policies. Our activities are centred on the development of projects with a high component of innovation, with the desire to contribute to social change.
We focus on environmental taxation and economic instruments of environmental policy at international, national and local levels (environmentalization of tax ordinances or waste charges). We are experts in the evaluation of economic and environmental policies, through the use of applied economics methods, such as advanced statistical techniques, econometric modeling, input-output analysis, general equilibrium computable with environmental extensions, material flow accounting, etc.
We highlight our experience in economic aspects (costs and economic implications of waste policies) and in the design and evaluation of economic and fiscal policies (waste charges, pay-as-you-throw schemes, taxes on landfilling and incineration, deposit-refund schemes, fee-rebate systems, etc.).
We have also produced various waste management plans for local authorities. In particular, we have a lot of experience in the design and implementation of separate door to door collection schemes. Another priority area of work is waste food prevention.

entityDescription:
Safe passage for your mission.
 
Testspring is a one-stop shop for space systems verification and validation. We plan and execute full qualification campaigns under a single contract through:
1. Our Orbital TestLabs (in-orbit test platforms)
2. Our network of established test facilities and analog sites
3. Simulation environments.
 
We also support clients on a modular basis: running a single test, providing qualified testers, or taking on particular V&V tasks within a larger programme.
 
Whether you need the full campaign or a single test, you get one point of contact instead of five.
 
Our campaigns support clients across the full maturity range, from TRL 3 breadboard validation to TRL 9. We structure our work around the ECSS framework, including: ECSS-E-ST-10-02 (Verification), ECSS-E-ST-10-03 (Testing), ECSS-E-ST-40 (Software engineering), and ECSS-Q-ST-80 (Software product assurance).
 
We are an ideal partner for:
1. Primes qualifying new technology
2. Startups seeking flight heritage for software components
3. Developers of robotics, rovers, payloads, and autonomy systems who need to verify concepts, procedures, and designs before committing to a full mission
We accommodate hardware payloads on a case-by-case basis.
 
We help you reduce:
1. Time-to-orbit
2. Risk
3. Programme costs.
 
You find failures before they become expensive, uncover unknowns that pose a risk to a mission, and arrive at launch with systems and software that have already flown.
 
Our mission:
To democratise access to space by improving accessibility and reducing the overall cost of getting there. We want to provide a unified platform for all European Space Sector participants, bridging the gap between well-established businesses and new space initiatives.

entityDescription:
B2Space is a UK-based aerospace company headquartered in Newport, Wales, developing and operating high-altitude stratospheric platforms for near-space testing, Earth observation, surveillance, communications, and future launch applications.
Founded with the long-term ambition of becoming the first UK satellite launch company using the “rockoon” concept — where a stratospheric balloon lifts a launch platform to near-space altitude before deploying a rocket — B2Space has progressively built a strong commercial and technical foundation around reusable stratospheric systems, balloon operations, mission control, payload integration, and high-altitude flight services.
Today, B2Space operates across three complementary business lines.
The first is Near Space Testing, originally developed with the support of ESA BIC UK. This service enables companies, universities, research organisations, and public institutions to test and validate technologies, sensors, materials, payloads, communications systems, and mission concepts in the stratosphere. These flights provide access to a near-space environment with low pressure, low temperature, high radiation exposure, and operational conditions relevant to space missions, helping customers accelerate technology development and increase Technology Readiness Levels at a significantly lower cost than orbital demonstration.
The second business line is the development and operation of High Altitude Pseudo-Satellite platforms, including stratospheric balloons, MicroHABS systems, and other high-altitude assets. These platforms can support applications such as Earth observation, environmental monitoring, wildfire detection, surveillance, communications, intelligence gathering, and rapid-response missions. B2Space’s approach combines flexible deployment, low operating cost, payload adaptability, and the ability to provide persistent or repeated coverage from the stratosphere.
The third area remains B2Space’s long-term rockoon launch system, which builds on the company’s expertise in high-altitude operations, autonomous flight systems, airborne launch architectures, and stratospheric platform development. While the company’s commercial activity today is focused on near-space testing and HAPS services, the rockoon programme continues to form part of B2Space’s strategic roadmap toward affordable and responsive access to space.
B2Space has developed substantial operational heritage, having performed numerous stratospheric flights with payloads ranging from small experimental systems to large and complex platforms. The company has delivered services and systems to commercial, institutional, defence, and space-sector customers, including work related to technology validation, high-altitude operations, Earth observation, and HAPS development.
To date, B2Space has secured several million euros in private equity, grant funding, and commercial revenues, and has generated multi-million-euro B2B sales through its high-altitude services and technology programmes. This commercial traction, combined with its operational experience and growing portfolio of stratospheric platforms, positions B2Space as one of the leading European companies in high-altitude balloon and HAPS operations.

entityDescription: The Institute is dedicated to a broad portfolio of research and education, ranging from fundamental questions concerning symmetries and interactions in nuclear and particle physics, neutron physics, atomic physics, quantum physics and quantum optics to radiation physics and reactor technology. Its activities also include applied research in areas such as environmental analysis, radiation protection and testing the radiation resistance of modern materials. A central facility of the Institute is the TRIGA Mark II research reactor, together with the associated teaching and laboratory facilities, which enable research and teaching involving radioactive substances and ionizing radiation. In this context, the Institute also makes an important contribution to the training and education of experts from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). At present, the Institute's staff comprises approximately 32 scientific employees (18 in permanent positions and 14 on six-year contracts) and 29 non-scientific employees. In addition, around 70 project staff are financed through third-party funding. Their contribution to the Institute's research and teaching activities has grown continuously in recent years. Furthermore, approximately 70 students are currently working on their bachelor's theses, diploma theses or doctoral dissertations at the Institute. The teaching offered by the Institute covers all of its research areas and is integrated into the curricula of the Faculty of Physics.

entityDescription:
Magnestar Technologies, S.L. designs, manufactures and qualifies high temperature superconducting (HTS) magnets and magnet subsystems for equipment manufacturers. 

Magnestar sits between the HTS tape suppliers and the OEMs that need a working magnet. The customer brings an application requirement: field, current, operating temperature, envelope and duty cycle. Magnestar covers electromagnetic and mechanical design, conductor selection and sourcing, winding and impregnation, cryogenic integration, quench detection and protection, and cold testing, and delivers a magnet subsystem that the customer integrates into its own equipment. Magnestar does not sell the end product and does not compete with its customers.

Magnestar currently runs paid engineering contracts on gyrotron magnets for plasma heating, fusion test infrastructure, and superconducting linear ny. Ongoing engineering discussions cover medical imaging, particle therapy, semiconductor crystal growth equipment and power delivery for data centers. For space applications the capability is the sa magnets, superconducting linear machines, andthe cryogenic and protection hardware around them.

software design and optimisation for large-scale data processing;

HPC infrastructure design, deployment, and management;

software performance optimisation;

AI and machine learning for scientific and industrial applications;

training in technologies related to the activities above.

The Development BU covers all software development activities and is divided into Data Science and HPC sub-units. As is typical of a SME, boundaries between units are intentionally permeable: project teams are cross-disciplinary and staff contribute across the full stack, so that expertise in HPC, data engineering, and scientific software is distributed rather than siloed.

eXact lab has extensive experience across the full value chain of Earth Observation data: from devising and deploying the compute-intensive processing pipelines that turn raw sensor data into scientific products, to designing and managing the data infrastructure that makes those products discoverable and accessible, to building the programmatic interfaces that end users rely on in operational workflows. This end-to-end familiarity — spanning production, distribution, and use of EO data — is directly relevant to a contract requiring user-driven maintenance and development of a key component of the Copernicus Marine Service ecosystem such as the toolbox.

entityDescription:
Balogh Statikus Iroda Kft is an engineering firm specializing in complex structural and civil engineering analysis and design. Our core operations focus on providing detailed static and dynamic calculations for both vertical (building) and horizontal (civil) structures, with a design portfolio primarily spanning across Europe and the United States. This international presence has equipped our team with extensive experience in operating under diverse regulatory frameworks, ensuring full compliance with Eurocode as well as US-specific building codes and standards.
The office manages the complete structural design process, from conceptual development to the delivery of detailed construction documentation. Our expertise in building construction includes the design of reinforced concrete, structural steel, and masonry load-bearing systems. In the field of civil engineering, our experience extends to the specialized design of underground spaces and subsurface structures, as well as large-scale retaining structures. Our tunnelling expertise encompasses various methodologies, including the Shotcrete Lining (SCL), Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM) technology, and Cut-and-Cover techniques, along with deep foundation systems and complex soil-structure interaction analysis.
We utilize advanced Finite Element Method (FEM) software to model non-linear structural behaviour and optimize material efficiency in challenging subterranean environments. Balogh Statikus Iroda Kft. prioritizes analytical accuracy and structural safety, delivering engineering solutions that meet the rigorous technical demands of both the European and American construction markets.

All proposed scientific activities and laboratories are indeed designed and implemented by Space42 experts and coordinated, during the event, by scientific explainers directly provided by the company. All materials needed for workshops are also prepared by the team and made available to the students during the activities. Each event is run by Space42 professionals, eventually supported by volunteers provided by partner institutions. Space42 has collaborations with the European Space Agency, the Italian Space Agency, the Distretto Tecnologico Aerospaziale, Il Cielo Itinerante, Asia Onlus, Camera di Commercio di Roma, Parmalat, Frascati Scienza, Unicef and ENEL for the organization of scientific events, festivals and tours throughout Italy addressed to young generations, with the aim of disseminating Space and Science in general and promoting the study of STEM disciplines. In particular, the network collaborates with the European Space Agency since 2017, for the organization of a wide variety of dissemination events in Italy and in Europe. As such, Space42 is responsible for all visits to the ESA - ESRIN Italian establishment for primary and secondary schools. On behalf of the Agency, Space42 participates in major scientific events and festivals in Italy and abroad. The group collaborated with the Italian Space Agency as well, in the years 2018, 2019 to plan, manage and coordinate the ASI one-week Open Days and the European Researchers Night in 2022. In 2020, 2021 and 2022 Space42 worked with Il Cielo Itinerante organization bringing scientific labs throughout Italy, with a special focus on educationally disadvantaged areas. The 2022 tour covered 45 dates throughout the country.

entityDescription:
LUMETIS is a young start-up founded after 10 years of technology and know-how development in scientific and technical optical instrumentation. LUMETIS has recently been selected to reach the lunar incubation programme called “TechTheMoon” thanks to strong perspectives of its patented technologies for human and robotic exploration. 
One of our most noteworthy results is the invention and development of a fluorescence and reflectance hyperspectral imaging system reaching unprecedented spectral range (300 nm – 1000 nm) and sensitivity. Besides, LUMETIS has demonstrated being able to acquire fluorescence images of rocks, plants and contaminations on sensitive surfaces outside dark conditions of laboratories and therefore allowed the exploration of new technical and scientific fields. Last but not least, we have imagined and set up a multispectral (8 wavelengths) high resolution demonstrator for art applications. 
LUMETIS employs technologies invented by its founders within CNES and CNRS ecosystems. Some of the inventions were patented for space applications, improved for art applications and will be made even more outstanding before going back to space.

entityDescription:
AgrOps GmbH is a Dortmund-based (NRW, Germany) technology start-up developing an AI-powered digital service for European agriculture.The company builds an end-to-end platform that supports farmers with Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) subsidy applications, mandatory documentation obligations (e.g. plant protection product records), and services e.g. for the transition from conventional to organic farming, accessed through a low-threshold, messaging-based interface.

AgrOps is currently extending its service with a satellite-based crop stressanalysis module, combining Earth observation data (Copernicus Sentinel-2)with proprietary (private) farm data to detect early plant and soil stress indicators.The goal is to enable more precise, resource-efficient use of fertilisers and plant protection products, reducing environmental impact while improving yield outcomes for small and medium-sized agricultural businesses.

AgrOps GmbH is a startup (Kleinstunternehmen) registered in the commercial register of the Amtsgericht Dortmund (HRB 38382), founded in 2026.

entityDescription:
The company is established with the primary objective of transferring and disseminating technological innovations to the agricultural sector to promote sustainable agriculture models.
Specifically, the company aims to develop the use of remote sensing as an information framework for operating agricultural machinery equipped with Variable Rate Technology (VRT), as well as to provide technology transfer services. These services encompass the acquisition, processing, and distribution of data derived from remote sensing, advanced sensor systems, and IT infrastructure to business entities—including agricultural enterprises, machinery manufacturers, agricultural contractors, and producers' associations—for precision and sustainable agriculture applications.
The company's activities include support actions (dissemination, demonstration, training, system design, technical consultancy) aimed at implementing a georeferenced information service platform. Supported by the qualified contributions of consortium partners and external service providers, this platform enables the application of satellite imagery to precision farming and the broader agro-environmental sector.
A further objective of the company is to diversify and expand its addressable market by offering technological innovation services to the agricultural sector and agricultural machinery manufacturers, as well as remote sensing services applied to the environmental sector and to land management issues that benefit from satellite mapping. Furthermore, the company will participate in research projects, experimental trials, promotional campaigns, outreach, and training activities across the agricultural supply chain, agricultural machinery engineering, and environmental/land management sectors.

entityDescription: Timbeter OÜ is an Estonian technology company, founded in 2013 and headquartered in Tallinn, providing AI-powered precision measurement solutions for the forestry and timber industry. Its core products include AI-based log and lumber measurement (Timbeter PRO), a fixed-site stereometric solution (Timbeter Stationary), and Timbeter Forest, a prototype dedicated stereometric-vision device and software solution for standing forest inventory. entityDescription:
LGr Technologies AS is a Norwegian deep-tech SME based in Trondheim, developing modular, lightweight sensor systems for situational awareness in harsh and remote environments.
The company's core products are MLTS (Mobile Lightweight Tactical Sensor), a rapidly deployable perimeter sensor node that can be carried and installed by a single person and operates unattended for up to two weeks (approximately eight days at -30 degC), and Heimdall, a command-and-control software platform that fuses data from distributed MLTS nodes into a single real-time situational picture. A third system, Munin, a semi-autonomous human-in-the-loop UAV platform that responds to a triggered MLTS node with live thermal imaging, is under development.
Core technical competences include low-power embedded sensor electronics, edge processing and sensor fusion, resilient communication between distributed nodes over low-bandwidth and intermittent links, and operator-centred software for sensor networks. The systems are designed for robustness in Arctic and subarctic conditions, autonomy under severe energy constraints, modularity and scalability - design drivers shared with space and remote-asset applications.

entityName: UNIVERSITY OF HEIDELBERG - Institute of Environmental Physics
entityDescription: Founded in 1975, the Institute of Environmental Physics conducts research in a field that emerged in the 1950s from the development and application of nuclear physics measurement methods to study the Earth's climate and environmental system. Today, its scientific mission as a branch of physics encompasses questions that investigate the flow of energy and matter in our environment. Research areas include the physics and chemistry of the atmosphere, greenhouse gases, and remote sensing (Prof. André Butz), as well as aquatic processes and the Earth's climate history (Prof. Werner Aeschbach and Prof. Norbert Frank). The measurement and simulation of the radiative impact of aerosols in the climate system (Prof. Stephanie Fiedler). Image processing in the environmental sciences takes place at the Interdisciplinary Center for Scientific Computing at the University of Heidelberg (Prof. Carsten Rother, em. Prof. Bernd Jähne), and remote sensing of the atmosphere is carried out at the Max Planck Institute for Chemistry in Mainz (Prof. Thomas Wagner). Research into aerosols is carried out at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (Prof. Thomas Leisner). Further links exist with the Klaus Tschira Laboratory for Physical Age Determination (KTL), a facility of the Curt Engelhorn Center for Archaeometry (CEZA) and the Curt Engelhorn Foundation.

entityName: MATERIA NOVA ASBL - Project support Office-Materia Nova R&D centre
entityDescription:
Materia Nova is a non-profit applied research centre in materials science and process engineering based in Mons, Belgium, founded by the University of Mons. With more than 330 collaborative and industrial R&D projects, it takes technologies from laboratory proof of concept to pilot and demonstrator scale (TRL 2 to 6).
Its multidisciplinary teams cover polymers and composites (bio-based resins and biopolymers, bio-based flame retardants and fire testing, advanced recycling, reactive extrusion, electrospinning); surface engineering and thin films (PVD, PECVD, atmospheric plasma, ion implantation, plasma treatment and spheroidisation of powders for additive manufacturing); wet-chemistry coatings and electrochemistry (sol-gel, electroplating, chemical metallisation, electrolytes and electrocatalysis); gas sensors and electronic noses; and industrial biotechnology (fermentation, biomethanation, bioelectrochemical systems, enzymatic recycling, CO₂ utilisation).
Two transversal capabilities support all developments: an advanced characterisation platform (SEM, XPS, ToF-SIMS, XRD, Raman, IR, ICP, tribology) and a dedicated team for life cycle assessment, life cycle costing and Safe and Sustainable by Design.
Main application fields are decarbonisation and hydrogen, circular economy and substitution of substances of concern (Cr(VI), PFAS, cobalt, boric acid), coatings for extreme environments, bio-based materials, health and diagnostics, and aerospace, including ESA contracts on thin-shell multilayer mirrors.
Keywords: materials, coatings, thin films, polymers, composites, flame retardancy, bio-based materials, recycling, additive manufacturing, sol-gel, electrochemistry, sensors, biotechnology, surface analysis, LCA, SSbD, REACH substitution.

entityDescription:
The Nauka. To Lubię Foundation is a Polish non-governmental organization established in August 2020 and based in Gliwice. It was founded by Dr. Tomasz Jan Rożek, a physicist, science journalist, and popularizer of science, to develop educational, multimedia, and science communication initiatives.
Mission and Objectives
The Foundation promotes science, technology, digital skills, and education, with particular attention to supporting families. Its main objectives are to:
- develop future skills and critical thinking among children and adults;
- promote digital hygiene and media literacy;
- strengthen resistance to misinformation, cyber threats, and scientific disinformation;
- support equal access to education;
- provide free, high-quality educational materials to schools, underserved regions, and Polish communities abroad.
Scale and Impact
The Foundation operates throughout Poland and internationally through digital platforms, social media, and educational events.
Between August 2020 and January 2026, its three YouTube channels generated more than 97 million views, 8.7 million hours of watch time, and over 886,000 subscribers. The Foundation’s social media community exceeds 600,000 followers, while its website attracts approximately 3,000 users per week.
The organization also regularly hosts a popular science stage during the annual science festival in Katowice, connecting experts from various fields with tens of thousands of visitors.
Key Projects
Academy of Superheroes is a long-term project presenting Polish scientists as real-life heroes in order to inspire young people. It has distributed 15,000 free books to primary schools, while its animated series has received more than 220,000 views. The project also includes multilingual educational games and e-books.
Digital Parent Academy is an online educational platform for parents and teachers. It offers free webinars, articles, and expert materials on digital hygiene, screen-time management, online privacy, FOMO, and internet safety.
Micrometeorite Hunters is a nationwide science education program combining astronomy and environmental studies. Under teacher supervision, students search for cosmic dust and analyze air pollution. Participating schools receive free research kits, including microscopes, magnetic detectors, and educational guides.
Cosmic Week is a free interdisciplinary campaign focused on space exploration. It has engaged more than 30,000 students across Poland and provides teachers with ready-to-use lesson plans and educational materials.
Partnerships
The Foundation works with universities, scientific institutions, companies, public organizations, and social partners. Its cooperation includes developing educational programs, organizing science events, implementing social campaigns, and distributing free educational resources.
One campaign promoting Polish science reached more than one million passengers nationwide.

entityDescription:
The National Museum of Natural History Goulandris is a non-profit foundation with a mission to conduct research, provide education, and protect nature. Since its establishment, it has been a point of reference for the study and understanding of Greece’s natural wealth, as well as for cultivating environmental awareness in society. Its goals are:the collection, documentation, research, and promotion of Greek flora, fauna, geology, and paleontology; environmental education and public awareness, helping people understand the impact of their daily choices on the environment and encouraging them to take action for its protection; the study and tackling of critical environmental issues of our time, such as pollution, biodiversity loss, and the climate crisis; participation in research programs and collaboration with scientific institutions and organizations in Greece and abroad; monitoring of the natural environment and the impacts of climate change, protection of ecosystems, promotion of innovative cultivation methods, and research into the use of Greek plants in pharmaceutical production and overall quality-of-life improvement.
The Greek Biotope/Wetland Centre (EKBY) is a branch of the Museum in Thessaloniki. entityDescription:
Hydra Manufacturing Limited is a private company limited by shares, incorporated in England and Wales (company number 15939081), based at Nexus, Discovery Way, Leeds, LS2 3AA, United Kingdom. It is a deep-tech spinout from the University of Leeds, engaged in the production and sale of ceramic manufacturing equipment and ceramic components.
Hydra develops and commercialises CHAMP, a hybrid additive and subtractive manufacturing platform for high-performance technical ceramics. CHAMP combines layer-wise deposition with in-process machining and closed-loop, AI-assisted defect detection and correction, producing near-net-shape ceramic parts with accuracy and surface quality that conventional ceramic additive routes cannot reach without extensive post-processing. The platform is designed, built and programmed in-house across mechanical design, motion control, firmware, process software and materials formulation, so Hydra holds the full technical stack for its own product. The process has been demonstrated in alumina, hydroxyapatite, reaction-bonded silicon carbide and tungsten carbide cobalt chrome, with monolithic silicon carbide in development and AI defect control validated on alumina through doctoral and Innovate UK funded work. These materials and the associated geometric freedom apply directly to space hardware such as thermal protection structures, optical and structural substrates, propulsion components and wear-critical mechanisms, where low volumes make tooling-dependent ceramic routes prohibitive on cost and schedule.
Under Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC Hydra is a micro-enterprise: three full-time staff and one part-time employee at 0.4 FTE (3.4 annual work units), with turnover well below the relevant threshold. It has no subsidiaries, holds no participation in any other undertaking and is not a subsidiary of any organisation.
Issued capital is 1,143,236 shares across two classes carrying identical voting, dividend and capital rights. The three full-time executive officers, all co-founders, hold 57.3 per cent between them; founder and employee shareholders hold 78.7 per cent in total. The University of Leeds retains a founder stake of 8.7 per cent, and 12.5 per cent is held by nominees acting for two SFC Capital managed funds. No shareholder or group of connected shareholders holds 25 per cent or more of the capital or voting rights, so Hydra is an autonomous enterprise.
The board comprises Matthew Shuttleworth, Louis Masters, Daniel Davie, Robert Kay and Luke Watson, chaired by Keith Jackson, and is responsible for supervision, management and day-to-day administration. Investors hold conventional minority protections: one non-executive appointment right, a non-voting observer, quarterly reporting and reserved matters covering corporate actions such as changes to share capital or the nature of the business. These do not reach operational, technical or engineering decisions. Hydra holds its own premises, employs its own staff, owns its own equipment and contracts in its own name, and is not subject to direction by any parent or controlling entity.
All foreground intellectual property, including the CHAMP platform design, control software and materials formulations, is owned by Hydra. University of Leeds background IP is held royalty-free under agreement, with full assignment to Hydra after a two-year term, giving unrestricted exploitation rights over its core technology.
Hydra supplies capital equipment through the CHAMP X3 platform alongside a manufacturing-as-a-service offering. Its first production system has been sold to Lucideon, a UK materials technology organisation. The company is backed by pre-seed equity through the SFC Capital funds and competitive Innovate UK grant funding. Target sectors are aerospace, space and defence, with ISO 9001 certification on the near-term roadmap.

entityDescription:
Theia Sense is an early-stage deep-tech company developing advanced fiber optic sensing systems for structural health monitoring (SHM) in harsh and extreme environments, with a primary focus on space applications.
The company specializes in Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG)-based sensing technologies, combined with proprietary packaging solutions that enable the measurement of mechanical parameters beyond conventional capabilities, including shear stress, which is typically not accessible with standard FBG sensors.
Theia Sense’s approach integrates hardware and software into a unified platform, including optical sensors, space-compatible packaging, interrogation systems, and data processing tools aimed at enabling real-time monitoring, diagnostics, and predictive maintenance of critical structures.
The technology is designed to operate in demanding conditions such as vacuum, radiation, thermal cycling, and high-vibration environments, making it suitable for spacecraft structures, launch systems, and advanced composite materials.
The company is currently focused on ground validation and early-stage system development, with the objective of progressing towards in-orbit demonstration and space qualification. Theia Sense leverages strong links with research and industrial partners in the aerospace sector and builds upon expertise in photonics, materials engineering, and sensor integration.

entityName: A.N.G.O.P.I. Associazione Nazionale dei gruppi ormeggiatori e barcaioli dei porti italiani
entityDescription:
The Linesmen and Boatmen National Association of the Italian Ports (ANGOPI) is the trade association which represents the linesmen and boatmen interests at the international, national and local level in a unitary way. In particular the ANGOPI defends the linesmen and boatmen profession through the unity, the connection and the coordination of the associated Groups.
It promotes the recognition, at normative and organizational level, of the mooring and of the boating as a service of general interest useful for the safety of navigation in ports and the safety of landing. It promotes, as well, the organizational models provided for every ports at national level, which ensure each linesmen and / or boatmen Group the function of universal service provider.
· It represents, in a unitary way, the linesmen and boatmen interests at national and at local level: in particular, during the investigation aimed to determine the organization and discipline of the Groups, the public service obligations and the tariffs.
· It protects and develops the associated Groups general interests about economic, organizational, administrative, legal, tax issues, anyway connected to their activity.
· It contributes to the creation and regulation of new working relationships and collaboration between associated Groups and third parties, where it is recognizable also a more general interest of all members in the protection of the category. 
· It takes care of the members professional development and of the Groups growing qualification, through the study of the problems concerning the category.
· It stipulates with the trade unions representing the employees the Category National Collective Agreement on behalf of the linesman and/or Boatmen Groups. With trade unions defines tools for the professional growth of the category and for the its welfare.
· It provides, to the associated Groups, all possible assistance and general and/or particular advice that they need.
· It advances and develops proposals to set up the method for the service tariffs and in general to make proposals for legislation and administration acts to be submitted to the competent authorities.
· It designates, where relevant, their representatives in all the committees in which the Association is involved in its own or is invited in accordance with specific laws or other measures taken at national or local level by the competent authorities, as well as in the commissions for the public examination provided to enter into the profession, so that also from the Association the highest contribution in the technical selection of candidates is guaranteed;
· It promotes, and if necessary manages, initiatives to establish and regulate relations of cooperation and friendship between the Association and boatmen Associations from other countries.
· With regard to the initiatives above mentioned, the Association has exclusive competence both with respect to individual Groups, and with respect to individual linesman / boatmen with particular regard to those who can produce effects modifying the organizational model of the mooring/boating service;

entityDescription:
Apricot Studio is the trading name of Jonathan Kerr Technology Ltd, a United Kingdom company developing resilient position, navigation and timing (PNT) technology for small uncrewed aircraft systems, with engineering based in Edinburgh.
The company's core product, Octant, is a low-SWaP companion module that maintains an aircraft's position, velocity and attitude estimate when GNSS is unavailable, degraded, jammed or spoofed. It fuses a global-shutter camera with an inertial measurement unit (visual-inertial odometry) on commodity CPU hardware, requiring no GPU, and streams the resulting navigation solution to standard autopilots over the MAVLink protocol so that it can be integrated into existing airframes rather than requiring a purpose-built platform.
The distinguishing capability is navigation integrity: the module publishes a quantified confidence and health signal alongside every pose estimate, enabling an aircraft to detect and respond to degradation in its own navigation solution instead of acting on an unreliable position.
Capabilities: visual-inertial odometry, multi-sensor fusion, navigation integrity monitoring, embedded real-time software (C++, ROS 2), simulation-based validation, and flight-test hardware integration.
Current maturity: validated in closed-loop simulation and against public benchmark datasets, with flight-hardware testing underway.

entityName: Budapest University of Technology and Economics - Department of Atomic Physics
entityDescription:
Introduction

The Department of Atomic Physics was established in 1938 with an intent to adopt modern applied physics in Hungarian research. This tradition has been continued uninterruptedly since then: our present research activities focus on optics / laser physics and surface physics, especially new laser technologies, optical design, measurement techniques and functional materials. We successfully work in cooperation with numerous top-level Hungarian and international scientific and industrial research institutes. They utilize our results and welcome our students.

Optics/Photonics

The main research areas of the Optical Laboratory of Department of Atomic Physics are applied optical and laser physics applications, optical technology research and the development of optical diagnostic equipments. Main research topics are:
Optical data storage, acousto-optic modulators, deflectors, Q switches, mode-lockers, filters, fsec pulse shapers, integrated optics, guided wave devices, fiber optic systems, optical signal processing, new optical technologies, modelling and design of optical systems, nonlinear optical devices, photo-acoustic and time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy of biological materials, light sources, optical measurement techniques, optics for medical diagnosztics, laser material processing, coherent infrared differential absorption lidar, holography, spectroscopic measurement techniques (NIR, VIS, fluorescence, LIBS, color), displays, photovoltaics, design/implementation and testing of entangled photon sources, simulation and measurement of the human eye.

Material Science

The subject of research of Surface Physics Laboratory of Department of Atomic Physics are applied materials science research/investigations, examination of functional materials, developing advanced measurement technologies, measurement methods and equipments. Main research areas are: quantum mechanical calculation of the properties and behavior of defects and surfaces in solids, investigation of surface compositions by secondary ion mass spectroscopy (SIMS), Auger electron spectroscopy (AES, SAM ), and X-ray photoemission spectroscopy (XPS), in situ plasma diagnostics and gas analysis by QMS (IBMS), application oriented experimental and theoretical study of wide band gap materials (CVD-diamond, SiC), study of gas sensing behavior of semiconducting oxides, oxidation behaviour of new anode materials for solid electrolyte capacitors, corrosion and contamination studies in discharge lamps, experimental and theoretcial investigation of heat transfer in practical plasmas, experimental and theoretical studies of functional glass coatings, design of quadrupole mass filters, secondary ion mass spectrometers (SIMS), and gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (GC/MS), design of Ion and Electron Optics, software for data acquisition and evaluation, control, image processing, semiconductor measurement techniques.

entityDescription:
CERMAT is a Polish SME specialising in advanced technical ceramics and precision surface finishing. The company manufactures and machines components from alumina (Al₂O₃), zirconia-toughened alumina (ZTA), zirconia (ZrO₂), silicon carbide (SiC) and sintered carbides, serving industrial customers across Poland and the EU.
Core competencies include precision lapping and polishing of ceramic components down to sub-micron flatness, diamond grinding, cutting-edge geometry for ceramic and carbide tools, and dimensional metrology to ISO 1101 (CMM-based flatness, parallelism and coaxiality verification). The company operates its own production and finishing facility, including flat lapping equipment for components up to 600 mm, and provides dye-penetrant inspection of ceramic parts.
The company additionally offers ceramic additive manufacturing (vat photopolymerisation / DLP) of alumina components, covering the full process chain from green-body printing through debinding and sintering to post-sinter precision grinding and lapping of functional surfaces — enabling complex geometries such as thin-walled (0.5 mm) monolithic parts, internal channels and near-net-shape components with machined datum surfaces.

entityDescription:
LoreSpace develops decision-support software for spacecraft systems engineering, based on a formal Space Systems Engineering Ontology in OWL/RDF aligned with ECSS practice and the spacecraft lifecycle (Phases A–F).
The system ingests programme artefacts — system and subsystem requirements, interface control documents, verification matrices, test and anomaly records — and connects them into a programme knowledge graph. Engineers query the graph in natural language and receive evidence-backed, cited answers; the system generates and maintains engineering artefacts from the same model, providing digital continuity across organisational and disciplinary boundaries in model-based system approaches.
Capabilities: ontology and knowledge-model development; requirements and verification traceability; automated change-impact and variant-delta analysis; configuration management support; document-to-graph ingestion pipelines; SPARQL/SHACL validation; agentic workflow automation over programme data.
LoreSpace AB is a Swedish company based in Stockholm, incubated at ESA BIC Sweden.

Quantum Valley Ideas Lab (QVIL) is a not-for-profit advanced technology R&D organization based in Waterloo, focused on accelerating the development and commercialization of quantum technologies. Its mission is to generate high-value IP, create globally competitive companies, and deliver economic, societal, and national security benefits for Canada.

Founded in 2016, QVIL has become one of Canada’s leading applied quantum R&D organizations, building the infrastructure and capabilities needed to accelerate the research and development of quantum sensing technologies.

QVIL operates a focused portfolio model, advancing multiple high-impact projects at a time to translate scientific breakthroughs into deployable technologies and commercialization opportunities. The organization has built a multidisciplinary team of over 40 researchers and engineers with expertise spanning atomic physics, photonics, nanofabrication, and systems engineering. QVIL has developed more than 50 patent families and advanced multiple quantum sensing technologies, including world-leading capabilities in radio frequency sensing, with applications across defence, telecommunications, and advanced industrial sectors.

QVIL maintains active collaborations with more than 20 partners across defence, aerospace, telecommunications, and academia, and has engagements with multiple Canadian. These collaborations support technology validation, system integration, and alignment with real-world operational requirements.

entityDescription:
Eckert & Ziegler Cesio manufactures sealed radioactive sources with Cs-137 and Co-60 emitting high-energy gamma radiation, Am-241 emitting low-energy gamma radiation and X-rays, Am-241/Be sources emitting neutron radiation, Kr-85 emitting beta radiation and foil radioactive sources with Am-241 emitting alpha particles.
Sealed radioactive sources with Cs-137 and Co-60 are primarily used as high-energy gamma sources in level gauges and material thickness measuring gauges in industrial plants, some models of Cs-137 sources are designed for use in well logging applications.
Sealed sources containing Am-241 are applied in X-ray fluorescence analysis of materials. Especially suitable for this purpose are Am-241 radioactive sources with an output window made of Beryllium enabling the emission of X-rays and low-energy gamma radiation. Low-energy gamma radiation of Am-241 is used in level gauges for scanning of the content of small objects, such as beverage cans and bottles, and also in thickness measuring gauges, as it allows to measure materials with lower area density compared to gauges fitted with Cs-137 and Co-60 sources.
Neutron radiation of radioactive sources with Am-241/Be is used for oil well logging, calibration of neutron measuring devices, as well as for determination of moisture in soil and in building materials in agriculture and construction industry, respectively. Am-241/Be sources also find use in education and research projects at universities.
Radioactive sources with Kr-85 are suitable particularly for beta thickness gauging, including measurement of very thin materials such as plastic, thin metal sheets, textiles and rubber. The emission of beta radiation is enabled through a specially designed thin output window with the thickness of 0.025 mm or 0.05 mm.
Foil radioactive sources with Am-241 contain americium homogeneously dispersed in gold mounted on a silver backing. Alpha particles are emitted from the source surface through a front cover made of gold or gold-palladium alloy. Foil sources are used in smoke detectors and in electrostatic charge eliminators.

Am-241/Be sources also find use in education and research projects at universities.
Radioactive sources with Kr-85 are suitable particularly for beta thickness gauging, including measurement of very thin materials such as plastic, thin metal sheets, textiles and rubber. The emission of beta radiation is enabled through a specially designed thin output window with the thickness of 0.025 mm or 0.05 mm.
Foil radioactive sources with Am-241 contain americium homogeneously dispersed in gold mounted on a silver backing. Alpha particles are emitted from the source surface through a front cover made of gold or gold-palladium alloy. Foil sources are used in smoke detectors and in electrostatic charge eliminators.

description:
Vulcanis SAS is a French deep-tech SME, founded in 2025 and based in Paris, developing integrated optical sensing instruments for the in-situ characterisation of geological materials. Our core technology fuses shortwave-infrared hyperspectral imaging (HSI), standoff laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) and LiDAR into a single co-registered instrument governed by physics-constrained edge AI executing onboard. The architecture is cue-and-confirm: the dense passive hyperspectral scene identifies candidate targets and directs a limited budget of active LIBS acquisitions, whose elemental ground truth is then propagated back across the LiDAR-co-registered scene. The output is a georeferenced mineralogical and elemental map delivered within the same working shift, in place of the multi-day sampling and laboratory assay cycle it replaces. Standoff LIBS is engineered around a 20–30 m working envelope.

Related activities: instrument architecture and optical design; LIBS and hyperspectral spectroscopy; multi-sensor calibration, co-registration and spectral data fusion; and physics-constrained machine learning for autonomous onboard analysis. The primary terrestrial application is grade control and tailings characterisation for the mining industry; the same sensing stack addresses planetary surface prospecting and ISRU site characterisation. Current maturity is TRL 4.

Vulcanis holds a signed memorandum of understanding with Exploration Labs (EXlabs) on instrument accommodation for future deep-space missions, and is incubated at Télécom Paris / Institut Polytechnique de Paris. The team combines planetary-instrument science with two decades of industrial computer-vision engineering.
entityDescription:
Vulcanis SAS is a French deep-tech SME headquartered in Paris, France, incorporated as a Société par Actions Simplifiée under French law. The company designs and develops modular multi-sensor payloads for real-time, in-situ mineralogical characterization, with applications spanning terrestrial critical raw materials exploration and planetary surface prospecting.
Vulcanis's core technology is the Vulcanis Mapping Payload (VMP), a sensor-fusion instrument integrating Shortwave Infrared (SWIR) Hyperspectral Imaging (900–2500 nm), Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS), LiDAR, and physics-constrained edge AI on NVIDIA Jetson-class compute. The architecture fuses dense passive hyperspectral data with sparse active LIBS sampling, co-registered through LiDAR, to deliver real-time mineral classification and ore grade estimation without lab turnaround.
For space applications, Vulcanis is developing VMP-Lunar, an instrument variant for in-situ mineralogical prospecting of lunar regolith and pyroclastic deposits in support of In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) objectives. The lunar variant targets a 10–14 kg mass envelope, 40–60 W nominal power, and aligns with NASA Moon-to-Mars objective AS-03.

description:
InnoviGuard AB doesn't ask you to trust your data and your commands. It proves them.

We build P55 Nexus, a proof engine for space communications. A satellite can go long stretches without contact with the ground. Most security models assume that connection is always there: a certificate authority reachable, a revocation list current, a key rotation schedule kept. P55 Nexus does not depend on any of that. It lets a satellite prove that a command came from mission control, and lets mission control prove that data came from the satellite, using proof that stands on its own.

Each proof is bound to the specific hardware that produced it. Nothing captured from one system can be reused to impersonate another. Ground stations, satellites, and the links between them are proven independently, with no shared infrastructure to fail or be compromised.

InnoviGuard develops this technology and applies it across the space communications chain: ground segment, uplink command authentication, inter-satellite links. We are currently engaged in an ESA BIC Sweden project. InnoviGuard was founded by Carl Hendrix, who brings close to 30 years of experience in security.

P55 Nexus is designed to complement existing CCSDS standards rather than replace them. SDLS secures the link layer; P55 Nexus operates at the space packet level, adding proof of origin and destination that SDLS's frame-level protection does not address. The two coexist in the same stack.
entityDescription:
Every day, critical data moves between systems that don't fully trust each other. A command reaches a satellite. A model reaches an edge device. A sample reaches a lab. Each time, there's a moment of doubt: is this really what it claims to be, from who it claims, unchanged along the way?
InnoviGuard AB, a Swedish deep-tech company, built P55 Nexus to close that gap. Proof, not permission. It's already at work today: authenticating biodiversity data collected in the field, and confirming AI models reaching space-edge devices are genuine and untouched. InnoviGuard is part of ESA BIC Sweden, bringing this to satellite command and control, working with partners in edge AI for space and satellite-based ocean surveillance.
We don't ask anyone to trust us. We give them proof.
Founded and led by Carl Hendrix, InnoviGuard is based at Ideon Science Park, Lund.

The Sanitary Engineering Laboratory (SEL) operates within the Department of Water Resources and Environmental Engineering of the School of Civil Engineering at the National Technical University of Athens (NTUA). As one of Greece’s foremost research and education centres in the fields of water resources management and environmental protection, SEL combines academic excellence with real-world impact, fostering innovation and developing smart, sustainable solutions to contemporary environmental challenges.
Its activities encompass both fundamental and applied interdisciplinary research in water resources management, drinking water treatment, wastewater and sludge treatment, solid waste management, bioremediation, water and sludge reuse, nutrient and energy recovery from waste, mathematical modelling of biological processes, aquatic environment quality assessment, the fate of priority pollutants and emerging contaminants in aquatic environments, nature-based solutions, and ecosystem and environmental impact assessments.
SEL is committed to advancing water treatment, the circular economy, water reuse, and resource recovery. By combining cutting-edge science with practical applications, its interdisciplinary research contributes to the transition towards a greener and more climate-resilient future. Through its research and educational activities, SEL also supports the development of the next generation of engineers, scientists, and leaders, equipping them with the knowledge and skills required to address future environmental challenges.
