entityDescription:
ATELIER ETUDE VOLTA (ADEV)
Independent power electronics design house for space, defence and scientific instrumentation
ADEV is a French SAS and an independent SME in Palaiseau, Paris-Saclay. It takes power conversion hardware from concept to characterised engineering model (TRL 1 to TRL 6) for primes, space SMEs and research infrastructures, on conventional and nanosatellite platforms, regulated and unregulated buses.

CORE COMPETENCES
High voltage power supplies: regulated 2 kV to 50 kV from 28 V to 120 V buses, analogue control loops avoiding radiation sensitive digital controllers, corona and partial discharge control, Paschen margin, low outgassing potting (ECSS-Q-ST-70-02).
Electric propulsion: PPU stages, anode, cathode heater and keeper supplies for Hall effect, FEEP and electrospray thrusters.
Spacecraft power: EPS and PCDU architectures, bus regulation, battery management, protected distribution.
DC/DC conversion and point of load: isolated and non-isolated converters from watts to kilowatts, resonant LLC and dual active bridge topologies, gallium nitride and silicon carbide power stages, gate drivers, custom magnetics, multi-rail sub-volt regulation at tens of amperes, low noise instrumentation front ends and traction inverters.

DESIGN AND CHARACTERISATION
Schematic capture, PCB layout and DfM in Altium, KiCad or customer toolchain on request. SPICE and thermal simulation, worst case and part stress analysis with derating (ECSS-Q-ST-30-11), FMEA, EEE parts selection for total ionising dose and single event effects. Laboratory in France, EMC pre-compliance (CISPR, MIL-STD-461, DO-160), thermal testing -55°C to +180°C, BGA and QFN rework.

SMALL SERIES AND QUALIFICATION
ADEV covers breadboard (BB), elegant breadboard (EBB) and engineering model (EM), and manufactures small series of non flight qualified hardware for ground support equipment, test benches and instrumentation. Hardware is architected against ECSS from the outset, so moving to flight standard needs no redesign, and delivered with a build to print package (DDF, DJF, DCL, DML, DPL). ADEV supports qualification campaigns and coordinates European partners for space grade EEE procurement, qualified assembly and accredited testing, giving one technical interlocutor through to qualified hardware. Customer intellectual property and bills of materials remain theirs.

COMPANY
Founded in 2025 by Thomas Harmand, PhD on GaN space power converters (SATIE, ENS Paris-Saclay), and Raphael Filipe, 18 years in industry, 6 in space on flight qualified DC/DC converters, 12 in automotive at Valeo and Continental. A network of independent senior specialists, all in France, adds mechanical engineering, FPGA, radiation and system engineering competences on demand, so substantial multidisciplinary projects are addressed, with design authority retained by ADEV. ADEV is open to ESA TDE, GSTP and ARTES programmes and collaborative R&D, working to SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR reviews.

entityDescription:
Marcos Aerospace I.K.E. is a Greek aerospace engineering company developing unmanned aircraft systems and space-enabled technologies for wildfire management and aerial firefighting.
Its principal programme, Quencher, is a purpose-built unmanned amphibious firefighting aircraft with a planned suppressant payload of approximately 4,500 litres. It is being developed for large-scale, day and night wildfire operations, including AI-assisted coordinated multi-aircraft missions and remotely supervised or autonomous operation, subject to the applicable regulatory and certification framework.
The concept combines GNSS, satellite communications and Earth observation data with onboard sensing and mission-management systems to support navigation, situational awareness, wildfire monitoring and mission planning. Quencher is conceived as a scalable, lower-cost firefighting system in which multiple aircraft can operate cooperatively to deliver substantial aggregate suppression capacity.

description:
microXpace is a French biotechnology SME developing microbiome-derived technologies based on the functional interactions between microorganisms, host physiology and metabolism.

Our core capabilities include microbiome and microbial-metabolism research, host–microbiome interactions, functional microbiology, omics-based analysis, biomarker and target identification, and the design and experimental validation of microbiome-derived interventions. microXpace combines scientific discovery with translational development, from mechanistic studies and proof-of-concept testing to product-oriented R&D.

Building on this expertise, microXpace is expanding its activities into Space Health and Human Spaceflight, with a particular interest in how the space environment may alter microbial functions and host–microbiome metabolic interactions, and how these changes could contribute to physiological risks during long-duration missions. Current R&D explores microbial metabolic pathways, including bile-acid metabolism, as potential targets for monitoring and for the future development of microbiome-derived countermeasures.

microXpace is interested in collaborations with research organisations, space-industry partners and technology providers in areas including space life sciences, human health, microbiome research, microbial metabolism, omics, biosensing, experimental platforms and biological payload development. We are particularly interested in research partnerships, technical collaborations, consortium participation and opportunities to adapt biotechnology developed outside the space sector to space applications.

entityDescription:
cubesys GmbH is a German small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) and a wholly owned (100 %) subsidiary of nfiniity GmbH. The company is a hardware and firmware house specialising in compact, production-ready embedded systems for connected mobility and Cooperative Intelligent Transport Systems (C-ITS).

Its engineering capability covers the complete hardware and firmware value chain: schematic design and PCB layout, antenna engineering for GNSS and V2X (including multi-band and ground-plane-constrained designs), enclosure, thermal, vibration and IP-rated mechanical design, power management and energy-harvesting concepts, embedded Linux board support and driver development, GNSS receiver and IMU integration across multiple vendor families, GNSS and RTK / correction-service handling, sensor data acquisition and diagnostic and end-of-line test firmware. The company also covers manufacturing readiness, production test concepts and small-batch production.

cubesys is the developer of the cube:evk, an all-purpose device and development platform for V2X applications, validated across a wide range of vehicle types and infrastructure environments, and of the cube:nano compact C-ITS platform for two-wheeled vehicles, combining dual-radio V2X (ITS-G5 and C-V2X) with high-accuracy GNSS-based positioning.

Together with its parent company nfiniity GmbH, which contributes ITS software, V2X protocol stacks and system integration, cubesys forms a vertically integrated group covering hardware, firmware and software for standards-compliant connected-mobility products. Target markets include two-wheeler and vehicle manufacturers, mobility service operators, road operators and research institutions.

entityDescription:
Siora is an Earth Observation and AI company developing satellite-based soil and crop intelligence solutions for agriculture.
Our core soil intelligence solution provides field-level estimates of parameters including nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), pH, soil organic matter, cation exchange capacity (CEC), soil texture and other physical soil properties. The resulting spatial maps can be used to identify variability within fields, support fertilisation planning, create management zones and enable variable-rate applications.

Our technology transforms satellite imagery and other geospatial data into actionable information about agricultural fields. By combining Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 observations with terrain, climate, geological and other environmental data, together with machine learning models, Siora can estimate key soil characteristics at high spatial resolution without requiring extensive physical soil sampling.
In addition to soil analysis, Siora develops Earth Observation tools for continuous agricultural monitoring, including vegetation condition, water stress and moisture-related indicators. Our objective is to turn complex remote sensing data into information that farmers, agronomists and agricultural companies can use directly in operational decision-making.
The platform is designed to provide analysis rapidly and at scale, from individual agricultural fields to large farming portfolios. Results can be delivered through Siora's web platform as well as through standard geospatial and data formats for integration into other farm management and precision agriculture systems.
Siora is particularly interested in collaboration and R&D projects involving Earth Observation, precision agriculture, soil monitoring and mapping, sustainable fertilisation, variable-rate application, crop and vegetation monitoring, water stress, climate-smart agriculture, land management and the development of new downstream applications of satellite data.
We are open to participating in ESA and European collaborative projects as a technology provider, Earth Observation data analytics partner, AI/ML partner, agricultural use-case provider or pilot and validation partner.

entityDescription:
AquaGuard Technologies AB (AGT) is a Swedish dual use deep tech company developing NEXUS, its proprietary AI enabled operational intelligence platform for Civil, Security and Defence applications. With a primary specialisation in the maritime domain, AGT addresses the technically challenging detection, classification, monitoring, tracking and identification of small and non cooperative vessels, including vessels operating without AIS, MMSI or other RF based identification. NEXUS combines AGT's proprietary software, AI/ML models, algorithms, processing pipelines, Multi Source Fusion and Correlation, Decision Intelligence, system architecture and operational workflows to transform fragmented observations into decision ready operational intelligence.
AGT has developed and validated AI/ML capability for precise small vessel detection and classification from high resolution satellite data, generating confidence, geolocation and associated object information independently of cooperative vessel transmissions. High resolution Optical and SAR provide complementary sensing capabilities, enabling observations from different acquisition times and conditions to be correlated within NEXUS. This extends vessel detection, classification and monitoring beyond the limitations of individual sensors and conventional cooperative tracking systems.
NEXUS brings together three complementary intelligence pillars: Space Data from high resolution Optical and SAR sources; Ground Edge AI from UAVs, USVs, fixed sensors and other local assets; and Ancillary and Contextual Data including AIS, historical records, weather, OSINT, infrastructure and partner data. Multi Source Fusion and Correlation associates these observations through entity resolution, spatial and temporal correlation, track association, confidence fusion and contextual enrichment. Decision Intelligence converts the resulting operational picture into confidence and risk assessments, anomaly and pattern analysis, operational alerts and decision support.
The same architecture supports persistent object association and cross modal vessel Re Identification (ReID), allowing observations across different times, locations and sensing modalities to contribute to an evolving digital identity and history for each vessel. Where AIS, MMSI or other identifying information is available, it can be correlated with that identity; where conventional identifiers are absent, NEXUS can maintain the observed vessel intelligence independently. This creates a pathway for persistent monitoring and identification of small and non cooperative vessels across multiple observations and sensing sources.
NEXUS is modular, sensor agnostic and interoperable, enabling additional sensors, data sources, AI models and intelligence functions to be incorporated within the same operational environment. Secure dashboards, APIs and structured geospatial outputs support direct use of NEXUS intelligence and integration with existing operational, GIS and command environments. The platform is designed to deliver timely intelligence to operational and regulatory users, with near real time capability where source acquisition and data availability permit.
NEXUS supports Civil applications including maritime safety, environmental monitoring and compliance, critical infrastructure, energy and emergency response; Security applications including maritime, border, coastal and critical infrastructure security; and Defence applications including ISR, maritime domain awareness, force protection and defence asset monitoring. The current NEXUS beta platform is deployed on AWS at TRL 6 and is progressing toward TRL 7 through continued system integration and representative operational validation.

entityDescription:
nfiniity GmbH is a Germany-based SME and a provider of connected mobility and C-ITS solutions, supporting customers in the development, integration, and validation of V2X systems across specification, simulation, and test environments. The company focuses on open standards, interoperability, and flexible system integration. As an active partner of the Connected Motorcycle Consortium (CMC), ITS mobility, and the Coalition for Cyclist Safety (C4CS), nfiniity contributes early-stage expertise to the development of practical V2X applications.

nfiniity is actively involved in the development of open-source ETSI ITS communication technologies as both a sponsor and contributor to Vanetza and Artery. Vanetza provides an open-source implementation of the ETSI ITS communication protocol stack, while Artery integrates Vanetza into a simulation environment to enable system-level modelling, simulation, and evaluation of ETSI ITS-G5 and V2X communication systems.
On this foundation, nfiniity provides a future-oriented platform that supports research, industry, and emerging mobility applications through open, adaptable, and standards-compliant technology.

entityDescription:
Taranis develops a dedicated Molniya‑orbit constellation that delivers persistent polar coverage and merges optical/IR imaging with communications relay. By integrating connectivity, data and transport into a single system, we bring fiber‑like service to the world’s most underserved regions.
Conventional geostationary satellites cannot see above ~55–60° latitude, and current LEO constellations require hundreds of spacecraft to provide only intermittent coverage. Our platform uses highly elliptical Molniya orbits to maintain high elevation angles and an eight‑hour dwell over the Arctic and Antarctic, offering reliable connectivity and precise observations where infrastructure is lacking.
Through vertical integration we monetize three layers of value: connectivity – delivering broadband and IoT services at high latitudes; data – high‑quality imagery and analytics in near real‑time; and transport – reliable relay of observation data directly to users. The result is an exceptionally capital‑efficient solution designed for aviation, maritime, energy, research and government sectors.

Técnicas Digitales Globales S.L. — operating under the brand Gemminis‑Civaxis — is a Spanish engineering technology company specializing in the digital inventory, diagnosis, and condition assessment of urban infrastructure. The company combines geolocated image capture (terrestrial, aerial, and orthophoto-based), computer vision, and GIS analysis to produce georeferenced inventories and condition indices for municipal assets, including pavements, sidewalks, roadways, pedestrian crossings, and street furniture.
The Gemminis‑Civaxis platform delivers a proprietary condition-rating methodology (the Gemminis‑Civaxis Index) used to support pavement conservation planning, accessibility diagnostics, and preventive maintenance programs for local and regional public administrations in Spain. Data pipelines integrate PostgreSQL/PostGIS (Supabase), Power BI dashboards, and Kizeo Forms for field data capture, feeding into inventory, work-order, and citizen-incident-reporting workflows (including WhatsApp-based reporting channels for municipal defect management).
Gemminis‑Civaxis has delivered infrastructure inventory and diagnostic services to public-sector clients including the Ajuntament de Granollers and Ajuntament de Mataró (Catalonia), and is actively pursuing large-scale pavement conservation and technical-assistance contracts with municipalities such as the Ayuntamiento de Madrid.

SiWeGO’s technology integrates real-time matching, geolocation and shipment tracking, secure digital payments, verified users, OTP-based pickup and delivery confirmation, and feedback systems. The objective is to reduce empty or underutilised vehicle journeys, lower delivery costs and minimise the environmental impact of freight transport.
SiWeGO operates across B2C and B2B models and is developing pilot projects with mobility operators, companies and industrial partners to integrate collaborative logistics into public mobility, employee welfare, commercial transport and existing transport infrastructure. The company owns an Italian invention patent and has filed a European patent application for its technology.

description:
REDAR is a Greek deep-tech company developing lightweight optical sensing payloads for unmanned aerial vehicles, bringing space-grade measurement technology to terrestrial applications. Our first product is a methane and greenhouse-gas instrument that measures emissions through laser absorption rather than chemical reaction, identifying and quantifying leaks at their source across energy, industrial and waste sites. Engineered as a compact payload for integration on standard UAV platforms, it enables mobile, source-level emissions monitoring that fixed and handheld methods cannot provide.

The system is built around a single modular optical core: by reconfiguring the sensing module, the same platform extends across environmental monitoring, industrial safety and defence, allowing one engineering effort to serve multiple civil and dual-use markets. Incubated at ESA BIC Greece, REDAR has a working demonstrator validated in both laboratory and field conditions and is now advancing toward a flight-ready instrument.

description:
StormGeo is a global provider of advanced weather intelligence and decision-support solutions for shipping, energy and weather-sensitive industries. Founded in Bergen, Norway, in 1998 and part of Alfa Laval, we transform complex environmental data into actionable insights that help organizations improve safety, operational efficiency and resilience.

Our capabilities include the ingestion and fusion of Earth-observation data, satellite and radar imagery, meteorological and ocean models, in-situ observations and customer asset data. We apply remote sensing, geospatial analytics, AI and machine learning to deliver site-specific forecasts, hazard monitoring, maritime and offshore decision support, energy-market intelligence, and infrastructure-risk services. Solutions are delivered through scalable cloud platforms, APIs, operational dashboards and automated alerts, supported by meteorologists and domain experts operating 24/7/365.

StormGeo processes more than 15 TB of data per day and delivers over 10 million forecasts annually across approximately 68,000 locations. Our services support thousands of offshore sites and vessels worldwide.

StormGeo was the prime contractor for GridEyeS, an ESA Business Applications project integrating Copernicus Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data, commercial high-resolution imagery, AI-based analytics and meteorological intelligence. GridEyeS demonstrated scalable vegetation monitoring, change detection, infrastructure-risk assessment and emergency-response support for electricity transmission and distribution networks. The service was validated with grid operators and developed into a commercially available operational solution.

We welcome collaboration with satellite and Earth-observation data providers, geospatial and AI technology partners, research organizations, infrastructure operators and downstream service providers. We are particularly interested in partnerships that turn space-derived data into scalable operational services for energy, maritime operations, critical infrastructure and climate resilience.

entityDescription:
For 45 years, Stichting De Noordzee (The North Sea Foundation) has been committed to protecting the largest natural area of the Netherlands: the North Sea. We stand for a clean and healthy North Sea that is used sustainably. We work towards a healthy ecosystem that is resilient and adapts to external influences. North Sea nature must always be the foundation for sustainable use. We advocate for the North Sea and collaborate with other stakeholders to find solutions for current and future challenges.

Three core roles are central to our work
- Agendasetting of pressing issues and solutions;
- Collaboration within the (international) level playing field;
- Accelerating the research – policy interface
We bring these roles into practice by partnering with policymakers, (energy) sectors and operators, funders, the scientific community, and by reaching out to the general public. Our key influence lies in firmly anchored North Sea marine, spatial and nature protection policies and regulation – based on the latest scientific insights. Therefore we actively focus on national and international policy advocacy and communication. Since pressing issues do cross borders, we focus on the North Sea Basin level, stressing the importance of international marine policy cooperation and regulation. 
To realize our mission, we work on four core strategic themes: nature protection, sustainable fisheries, nature-friendly energy, and a clean sea. The nature protection program aims to safeguard large areas of the sea from human activity, allowing species space to recover – free from disturbance. In connection with this, we promote sustainable fishing practices and improved ecosystem-based fisheries management. The nature-friendly energy program is based on the idea that the North Sea is central to the energy transition, and the sustainable energy transition at sea must mitigate environmental risks and ensure nature protection and enhancement. Finally, a healthy North Sea is a clean sea – free from visible and invisible marine litter.

entityDescription:
Prepared International (PPI) specializes in consultancy, research and training services in the field of Disaster Risk Reduction, Preparedness and Resilience, in order to inform political decision-making and to provide effective capacity-building strategies in the long term. The PPI approach encompasses a holistic set of tools for approaching Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), including the development of preparedness models, organizational development and restructuring, self-adaptive systems, and strategies for governance and mass evacuation. 
As guiding mission PPI seeks to offer detailed, specialized expertise in the field of Disaster Management to design strategies for resilience that are both practical and detailed. This includes Operational Continuity Management for urban areas, developing and mature economies, strategies for high-risk zones, and cooperation in Disaster Risk Management for conflicting communities, including in post-conflict regions. PPI also offers long-standing expertise in simulation design and capacity-building strategies. Our team of international and local experts works towards applying lessons gathered at the forefront while developing and implementing new concepts and tools, such as the new concept of United Nations Disaster Assessment and Coordination (UNDAC) Disaster Response Preparedness Missions, the development and implementation of the mission methodology for Mass Evacuations in Natural Disasters (MEND) Preparedness Missions, or the application of the stress-test methodology. Our long-standing experience in capacity assessments and investment planning was developed in missions for the UNDAC Disaster Preparedness System, UNDP, EU or national systems; therefore, systemic Emergency and Preparedness assessment methodologies like the World Bank’s Ready to Response (R2R) concept fits perfectly in our portfolio and services. In 2020, PPI developed a methodology to analyze the ability of a EP&R system to fight pandemics based on the R2R methodology.
Our experience features a strong regional focus on the Western Balkans, with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) as a point of reference both during assessments and in our recommendations for future development. In addition, PPI is part of the Advisory Group to the Disaster Preparedness and Prevention Initiative (DPPI SEE), which offers valuable knowledge on the broader region. The team suggested for this assignment consists of recognized international experts and a leading country expert. Their valuable experience will facilitate an effective and efficient assessment process, build on best practices and lead to concise recommendations tailored to the needs of Ukraine.
On top of our first-class regional and country expertise, a clear advantage of PPI is its recent experience in applying the R2R Diagnostic methodology to assess the Emergency Preparedness and Response systems of Cabo Verde and six Western Balkan states resulting in PPI experts having detailed and updated knowledge on how to implement similar tools and conduct investment planning. The fact that all countries were very pleased with the diagnostic results and recommendations made by PPI is a clear indication of the company´s ability and capacities to deliver similar assignments to the satisfaction of all stakeholders involved.
While the organization is registered under German law in the State of Bavaria (HRB 27352), the highly experienced staff is multi-national and include key local experts. All our colleagues are driven by the same understanding, namely that stronger preparedness of communities and societies is possible with the current investments in this field. In 2023, PPI received as first private organization the Special Recognition of the Averted Disaster Award, and in 2024, no less than 11 PPI colleagues received the UN Heroes Award.

entityDescription:
Calsens is a Spanish engineering company specializing in structural monitoring and optical sensor technology. Based in Spain, they provide 24/7 online monitoring services for civil and industrial structures, combining advanced sensor hardware with their own proprietary IoT software platform.
Their work falls across three main areas:
Structural Health Monitoring — Calsens deploys optical sensors to monitor the condition of infrastructure ranging from bridges and viaducts to pedestrian walkways. Monitoring can be short-term (a few hours, for a specific test) or permanent (continuous data collection and analysis over multiple years), supporting predictive maintenance of critical infrastructure.
Optical Sensor Development — The company designs and manufactures optical sensors for a wide range of applications, including FBG (Fibre Bragg Grating) sensors for strain measurement in civil engineering, high-temperature sensors for aerospace environments, pressure sensors for pressurized conduits, and pH sensors for concrete structures. R&D is central to their identity, with the team active in both academic and private research.
Load Testing & Structural Assessment — Calsens carries out static and dynamic load tests on civil and industrial structures, complemented by finite element numerical modelling, structural fitness reports, and engineering calculations.
Their portfolio includes projects on multiple bridges and viaducts across Spain (such as the Mascarat Bridge, Viaducto Las Rosas, Viaducto Río Algar, and others), and they collaborate with a range of companies and institutions across different sectors.

description:
Datum Vega is a Toulouse-based aerospace engineering company specializing in the development, structural analysis, verification, and qualification of spacecraft and space hardware. We support organizations in translating mission and system objectives into robust engineering requirements, verified designs, and qualified flight hardware.

Our team brings senior-level experience gained through work at Boeing, Northrop Grumman, and Airbus U.S. Space & Defense. Our expertise encompasses spacecraft structures, human spaceflight systems, finite element modeling, structural dynamics, static loads, vibration and shock, fatigue and fracture mechanics, optimization, margin-of-safety assessment, and qualification engineering.

Datum Vega also provides requirements, verification, and test support, including requirements traceability, verification planning, test planning and supervision, model correlation, qualification evidence, and flight-readiness support. Our work draws upon extensive practical knowledge of NASA and ESA standards, requirements, handbooks, and specifications.

Alongside engineering services, we develop specialized software and automated workflows that reduce errors, improve productivity, preserve technical rationale, and strengthen engineering traceability. description:
SustainStruct UG is a German technology start-up developing space-enabled Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) solutions for bridges and other critical infrastructure. 

Based in Langen, Germany, the company is supported by the ESA Business Incubation Centre Hessen & Baden-Württemberg. Our approach combines satellite-based technologies, particularly GNSS and Earth Observation data such as SAR/InSAR, with in-situ structural sensors including accelerometers and environmental sensors. High-precision GNSS positioning is used to monitor structural displacement and provide an absolute positioning reference, complementing accelerometer-based measurements of dynamic structural behaviour. 

In parallel, we are exploring the integration of SAR/InSAR-derived deformation information to extend monitoring from individual sensor locations toward larger structures and infrastructure areas. SustainStruct develops the complete monitoring chain, including sensor and GNSS integration, edge data acquisition, secure data transmission, cloud-based processing, data analytics, and web-based visualization. 

By combining space-derived and terrestrial measurements, our goal is to support continuous condition monitoring, deformation analysis, anomaly detection, and ultimately predictive maintenance of critical infrastructure. The technology is currently being validated through a real bridge monitoring pilot in cooperation with academic and infrastructure partners, with the objective of developing scalable monitoring solutions for infrastructure owners, engineering companies, and asset operators.

entityDescription:
Netguru S.A. is an AI-native software engineering and product design company founded in 2008 and headquartered in Poznań, Poland, employing approximately 500 specialists. The company designs, builds and operates production artificial intelligence systems together with the software platforms around them, with a deliberate focus on established, asset-heavy industries where digital and AI adoption has historically lagged behind.
Core competencies cover applied AI engineering — large language model systems, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic workflows, computer vision, document understanding and evaluation frameworks — alongside full-cycle software delivery from discovery and architecture through implementation to long-term maintenance. Supporting competences include backend and distributed systems engineering, web, mobile and integration development, cloud and platform engineering on AWS, Azure and GCP, data engineering and analytics platforms, and digital product design. AI capability is not organised as a separate practice but applied as the default engineering method across the delivery organisation.
Netguru operates dedicated AI inference infrastructure independent of third-party model providers. GPU capacity is leased from European sovereign cloud and high-performance computing operators in Poland, and the company also deploys model serving on-premise inside a client's own network. This allows engagements to be executed without sending data outside a defined jurisdiction, and supports air-gapped or otherwise restricted environments where commercial model APIs cannot be used.
The client portfolio is concentrated in traditional and regulated sectors: industrial and manufacturing operations, energy and HVAC systems, medical technology and healthcare, logistics and field service, financial services, and enterprise commerce. Typical engagements connect AI and modern software to legacy estates — ERP and MES systems, installed hardware, field operations and long-lived operational data — under real constraints of safety, certification, data protection and system reliability.
Delivery is governed by a documented internal framework of standard operating procedures covering estimation, earned-value progress reporting, quality assurance, risk management, change control and security, with a named Delivery Manager, Engineering Manager and quality owner assigned to every engagement. The company maintains an ISO 27001-certified information security management system and is a certified B Corporation. All engineering, design and delivery personnel are employed or contracted within the European Union, and infrastructure, source code repositories and AI inference can be confined to EU-resident environments in line with GDPR and EU data sovereignty requirements.

entityDescription:
ORMIA Systems OÜ is an Estonian deep-tech SME developing Taevas, a passive acoustic drone detection and situational awareness platform for civilian critical infrastructure operators (ports, energy, utilities). The system fuses a proprietary biomimetic MEMS acoustic sensor mesh with European space assets: Galileo High Accuracy Service with OSNMA-authenticated positioning for precise node synchronisation, and Copernicus services (Sentinel-1/2, CAMS atmospheric data) for terrain context and real-time recalibration of acoustic detection confidence. 
Delivered as a multi-tenant SaaS, Taevas provides RF-silent, non-emitting detection supporting operator compliance with the EU CER Directive (2022/2557) and NIS2. 
ORMIA is incubated at ESA BIC Estonia (Tehnopol, Tallinn), with R&D partnerships including the University of Tartu. 
Field-validated at TRL 5, with pilot deployment underway at the Port of Tallinn (Muuga harbour).

Composites ATE is a Spanish industrial company specialised in advanced composite manufacturing, industrialisation and high-performance insulation solutions, serving the aerospace, space, railway, defence, industrial and other demanding mobility and engineering sectors.
At its Barcelona facility, ATE develops and industrialises composite manufacturing processes for carbon, glass and natural-fibre components, with particular expertise in prepreg compression moulding, out-of-autoclave processing and accelerated curing technologies. Its capabilities include tooling and production means development, CNC trimming and machining, bonding, assembly, painting and the industrialisation of both prototypes and recurring series. ATE works mainly on a built-to-print basis, supporting customers from process definition and tooling through qualification and serial production.

Activities include machining of insulating materials and technical laminates, production of customised insulation components, mould and tooling machining, casting and related industrial processes, as well as the manufacture and integration of components for demanding industrial applications.
Together, the two sites provide ATE with a broad multisector industrial capability combining advanced composites, insulation technologies, tooling, machining and production engineering, from low-volume high-performance applications to recurrent industrial manufacturing.

Since 2004, we have been successfully operating in the digital communication sector, exploring new approaches and forms of expression with the aim of providing our clients with a comprehensive service based on coherent and effective creativity. We help our clients transform ideas into coordinated actions and into products with strong creative and commercial value.
We are a team of professionals who combine their distinctive skills and expertise to provide solutions, consultancy services and technical support tailored to the different needs of each client.
Le Fucine communication agency began its operations in Perugia in 2004, where it is still based today. Its 160-square-metre premises are located in a building surrounded by greenery in Strada Tuderte. The agency has a permanent team of six employees and three external collaborators working across a range of areas, including project development and creative services, video production, web development, account management, copywriting, administration and secretarial support.
Le Fucine provides companies and clients with specialised and efficient services designed to support their growth in the fields of marketing and communication. Its contribution covers a broad range of activities, from strategic and marketing analysis to consultancy in communication and public relations.
Since 2022, Le Fucine has been responsible of managing Unipg Shop Official Merchandising. This assignment plays an important role for the University of Perugia, ensuring the careful and consistent development and implementation of products carrying the University’s institutional brand.
Le Fucine oversees detailed production planning and works closely with established suppliers to ensure that all products comply with the high quality standards required.
At the same time, Le Fucine develops highly targeted marketing strategies across a variety of communication and distribution channels, with the aim of increasing the visibility and market penetration of the University of Perugia’s merchandising products.
This strategic approach not only strengthens the University’s institutional identity, but also creates a strong and tangible connection between the University and its community of supporters, fostering deeper and more lasting engagement.

Truco y Trufa SL (T&T) is a Spanish SME based in Madrid. Its technology unit, t&tech, applies statistical modelling and machine learning to problems where labelled data is scarce, signals are weak, and decisions must be made under real constraints.

Current work spans unsupervised anomaly detection in time-series telemetry, including a detector for spacecraft housekeeping data validated against real in-orbit events; synthetic population modelling built on national statistical microdata for simulating behaviour at population scale; geospatial and remote-sensing analysis; and automated intelligence systems that extract structure from heterogeneous public sources.

A recurring focus is making these methods deployable: deterministic, reproducible, auditable, and small enough to run within tight memory and compute budgets rather than only in a research notebook.

entityDescription:
Zenith Pulse GmbH — Company Description (EN)
Zenith Pulse GmbH is a German company based in Baden-Württemberg developing a software platform that calculates a company's actual carbon footprint directly from its suppliers' invoices, processed through a proprietary algorithm, and generates a Scope 1/2/3 emissions report with concrete reduction recommendations. Built on this core engine, Zenith Pulse is developing additional verticals that integrate Copernicus (Sentinel) and NASA Earth observation data to enrich the analysis with land-use monitoring, coastal-zone assessment, pollution and urban heat-island detection, physical climate risk, and resource-use intelligence.
The product addresses a regulatory-driven need: the EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) requires companies to report Scope 1/2/3 emissions, while smaller suppliers face indirect pressure to provide the same data to larger corporate customers. Target customers include both private companies (B2B) and German municipalities, served through modular subscription packages.
A working prototype of the core Scope 1/2/3 calculation engine is operational, using recognized, publicly documented emission-factor sources. The satellite-data verticals are in development and have not yet been validated with a paying customer.
The founding team combines engineering and entrepreneurial experience with software architecture and IoT research expertise, supported by a specialist in GIS and remote sensing for satellite data integration.

Sagittal Optics S.L. is a specialized engineering company delivering high-performance optical and opto-mechanical solutions for space and ground-based instrumentation, broadband imaging, laser systems, and sensing applications. The company supports the full development cycle: optical architecture trade-offs, detailed optical design and simulation, tolerance and sensitivity analysis, stray light and ghost mitigation (non-sequential analysis), and opto-mechanical design validated through structural, thermal, and optical simulations (STOP).
Sagittal Optics is based in the Canary Islands (Spain) and is built around a team with extensive international experience in space and astronomy instrumentation, including long-term work on major observatories and complex opto-mechanical/cryogenic systems, as well as industrial R&D and prototyping environments. This background enables practical, verification-driven designs that consider manufacturing, alignment, and test constraints from the earliest phases.
Sagittal Optics also provides AIV-oriented engineering, including alignment strategies, test setup definition, and performance verification planning, helping customers reduce technical risk and shorten development timelines. The company maintains prototyping and integration capability, including laboratory setups for optical/mechanical integration and testing, as well as in-house tooling and rapid iteration resources.
Sagittal Optics’ design philosophy focuses on achieving broadband chromatic correction with a minimized number of optical elements, improving transmission, reducing complexity, and enabling more robust, cost-effective systems.

entityDescription: Paraxiom Technologies Inc. is a Canadian SME (Montréal, incorporated 2023) specializing in post-quantum secure communications software. Its core product, PQTG (Post-Quantum Transport Gateway), secures the ETSI GS QKD 014 key-delivery layer of quantum key distribution networks with post-quantum cryptography (ML-KEM-768, Falcon-512, SLH-DSA; pure-Rust implementation), closing the residual classical-TLS exposure in front of quantum-distributed keys. PQTG completed a 9/9 ETSI-014 conformance validation against a production evolutionQ Basejump KMS on Canada's KirQ national quantum testbed and operated live with Toshiba QKD hardware supplying keys. Supporting capabilities include an operating post-quantum distributed ledger for attestation and notarization, a post-quantum SSH implementation, and a formal-verification discipline in Lean aligned with certification-oriented assurance. Areas of interest for ESA activities: ground-segment security for optical and QKD satellite communications, post-quantum key management and identity for governmental 5G/6G non-terrestrial networks, and crypto-agile key-combination architectures (ETSI TS 103 744 / NIST SP 800-227 direction). The company's cryptographic core is under contract for independent technical assessment (BeatQuantum Ltd., UK).

Company description: The Common Wadden Sea Secretariat (CWSS) supports, facilitates and coordinates the Trilateral Wadden Sea Cooperation (TWSC). Located in Wilhelmshaven, the Secretariat was founded in 1987 by the Wadden Sea states Denmark, Germany, and the Netherlands.
The Secretariat
- coordinates, promotes and supports activities of the Cooperation;
- is responsible for the preparation and production of documents for ministerial conferences, meetings of the Wadden Sea Board (WSB) and trilateral work groups;
- collects and evaluates information on monitoring, protection and the ecological condition of the entire Wadden Sea;
- is the central contact for the UNESCO Wadden Sea World Heritage;
- produces and publishes reports by the Cooperation;
- involves the public in the protection of the entire Wadden Sea area through communications, awareness building and environmental education.
Since the inscription of the Wadden Sea on the UNESCO World Heritage List, the Secretariat moreover deals with the implementation of the obligations derived from the UNESCO World Heritage Convention.
The legal status and the functions of and regulations governing CWSS are stipulated in the Administrative Agreement concluded between the Danish, Dutch and German Ministries responsible for the Wadden Sea. Each Ministry finances a third of its budget. The working language of the Trilateral Cooperation and the CWSS is English.

INGECID S.L. is an engineering firm founded in 2009, with its headquarters in Santander and offices in Madrid and Bilbao, as well as international subsidiaries in Germany, Norway, South Africa, and the United States. Its corporate purpose is to conduct research and innovation in the fields of construction technology, software engineering, renewable energy, and nuclear energy, collaborating with research groups on the development of R&D projects. Innovation is a central element of its business strategy, which has resulted throughout its history in the generation of a large number of national and international patents and in the delivery of high-value-added technological solutions to the market.
INGECID has a multidisciplinary technical team of approximately 100 people (40% women), organized into areas of activity that include the management and development of R&D&I projects, software development, generative design, structural engineering, technical consulting, and radiological engineering, among others. entityName: University of Passau - Chair of Computer Networks and Computer Communications
entityDescription:
The Chair of Computer Networks And Computer Communications at the University of Passau has its main areas of research in satellite communication, network analysis and virtualization, self-organizing systems, IT security, safety and energy efficiency.
In regard to satellites, the team's research assesses the potential of satellite technologies for the energy system, particularly of satellite communications and Earth observation. In Earth observation, the team's interest is in studying how satellites can enhance situational awareness by acting as an additional source of information and by processing data at the edge. In satellite communications, the research focuses on how satellites can contribute to the resilience of the power grid, for example by providing a redundant communication path.
The Chair of Computer Networks And Computer Communications has experience in satellite communications from both completed and ongoing projects: In EnerSat, a feasibility study, satellite networks were studied for reliable monitoring of critical infrastructure. In STARS, the potential of satellite communication to combat blackouts was assessed. In KRISNet a flat sat is being developed to demonstrate multi-channel communication via both terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks to enhance the resilience of the power grid.

description:
First Light Fusion operates a globally unique capability for reproducing, measuring and modelling extreme physical environments relevant to space systems. Originating from inertial fusion research, we bring together hypervelocity impact testing, extreme pressure and radiation environments, world-class diagnostics, and AI-driven data science and simulation. This integrated capability delivers assurance-grade experimental data and validated predictive insight in regimes that are difficult, or impossible, to access using conventional space test infrastructure. These capabilities directly support spacecraft resilience, shielding design, subsystem survivability, radiation effects assessment, and digital engineering for space missions. Capabilities Integrated testing, diagnostics and simulation for space-grade assurance. 
Hypervelocity Impact Testing — Up to 14 km/s 
We operate the UK's largest two-stage light gas gun and one of the most capable systems worldwide. Patented velocity amplifier technology accelerates projectiles from 0.1 km/s to greater than 14 km/s for controlled, repeatable, highly instrumented hypervelocity impact experiments. Access to the 10–14 km/s regime is globally unique and extends beyond conventional testing facilities, delivering critical experimental data for spacecraft qualification and mission assurance. 
Extreme Pressure, Shock & Radiation Environments 
A suite of patented amplifier technologies, manufactured in-house, provides access to extreme pressure, shock, thermal and radiation environments at significantly lower cost and faster iteration than large national facilities. First Light Fusion also operates the second-largest pulsed power facility in the world (and the largest in the UK), generating multi-megaampere currents, multi-megabar magnetic pressures, extreme pulsed X-ray and K-shell radiation environments, and transient plasma and electromagnetic loading. 
Diagnostics, Data Quality & Experimental Validation 
All experimental platforms are supported by world-class diagnostics, enabling high-resolution, time-resolved measurement of extreme events: ultra-high-speed optical imaging, velocity interferometry and shock diagnostics, time-resolved optical and X-ray measurements, and post-test material and structural characterisation. The emphasis is on generating assurance-grade datasets suitable for space qualification, model validation and digital engineering workflows, with full traceability and reproducibility aligned to ESA and ECSS testing expectations. Intelligence & Engineering Excellence From experiment to digital twin. 
AI, Data Science & Simulation 
A defining strength is the tight integration of physical experimentation with advanced data science and AI-driven simulation: high-fidelity hydrodynamic, structural and MHD modelling; physics-informed machine learning; reduced-order and surrogate modelling; uncertainty quantification and sensitivity analysis; and sovereign high-performance computing. Experimental data is used to validate, calibrate and extend predictive models, enabling reliable extrapolation beyond directly testable regimes and supporting digital twins and mission-level decision-making. 
A Powerful Capability for Space 
Experimental and computational infrastructure located in the UK providing access to national laboratory style facilities to support sensitive space programmes and early-stage validation. First Light enables faster iteration, lower programme risk, and world leading capability.

Forestio.ai, operated by Generation Forest s.r.o. in Prague, is an environmental technology startup focused on global reforestation and rainforest protection. Its mission is to empower individuals and businesses to combat climate change through transparent, tech-driven forest conservation.
The platform allows users to support either reforestation projects (planting new trees) or protection projects (safeguarding existing rainforests). Once selected, each forest is digitized and tracked using satellite imagery and analytical tools that monitor carbon sequestration, vegetation health, and environmental risks. Users receive quarterly reports with data and imagery showing the impact of their contribution.
A distinctive feature of Forestio.ai is its use of blockchain technology. Each digital forest is represented as an NFT, ensuring unique ownership and transparency, while CO₂ credits are issued as fungible tokens on the Polygon blockchain, with one token representing 1 kg of sequestered carbon. This system provides both traceability and credibility in climate impact reporting.

entityDescription:
Meccanica 42 S.r.l. is an Italian engineering company specialized in the development of advanced mechatronic systems, special-purpose vehicles, and testing and validation solutions for high-performance and safety-critical applications. The company combines mechanical, electrical, software, and systems engineering capabilities to design, integrate, and deploy innovative products from concept definition to operational validation.
Originally established in the automotive sector, Meccanica 42 supports vehicle manufacturers, technology suppliers, motorsport organizations, and research institutions in the development of complex vehicle functions and advanced mobility technologies. The company delivers real-time test systems, embedded control devices, and customized vehicle platforms, including demonstrators and special-purpose vehicles designed for research, validation, and operational activities. 
A distinctive strength of Meccanica 42 is its ability to bridge simulation, laboratory testing, and real-world deployment. Through the integration of hardware, software, sensors, actuators, and control systems, the company develops solutions that operate reliably in demanding environments where precision, safety, and performance are critical.
In addition to proprietary products, Meccanica 42 provides system integration, engineering consultancy, commissioning, technical support, and the development of customer-specific equipment and vehicles. This end-to-end approach enables customers to accelerate innovation, reduce development risks, and transform complex technical requirements into deployable solutions. 
Based in Sesto Fiorentino, Italy, Meccanica 42 operates dedicated engineering offices, laboratories, and workshops and invests continuously in research and development to expand its technologies beyond automotive applications into other sectors requiring advanced mechatronics, automation, and reliability-focused engineering.

Meccanica 42 is particularly interested in applying its expertise in mechatronic systems, special-purpose vehicles, embedded electronics, remote operations, and complex system integration to environmental monitoring, emergency response, and space-enabled services.

lean hardware

lean software

generic causal prediction

Our company specializes in advanced Research and Development across the fields of satellite communications, mobile networks, artificial intelligence, and next-generation digital technologies.
We have extensive expertise in the design, development, and validation of satellite-based communication systems, with a particular focus on Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations, integrated terrestrial–non-terrestrial networks, and innovative communication architectures for future connectivity services.

entityName: UNIVERSITAET KLAGENFURT - Control of Networked Systems Group
entityDescription:
The Control of Networked Systems Group (CNS) is part of the Institute of Smart Systems Technologies at the University of Klagenfurt (Austria) and the engaged research activities cover control theory, state estimation and motion planning, modeling of dynamic systems, simulation, and (mobile) robot automation in multi-agent scenarios. We pursue these activities both from a classical and data-driven AI perspective. The field of interests include, but are not limited to, the following: Collaborative (mobile) robot autonomy in 3D space, state estimation aware control and motion planning, on-board environment perception and decision making, long-term task execution in changing environments, networked mission planning for multiple agents. The Control of Networked Systems Group seeks to push the current limits in AI supported state estimation, cooperative visual perception, and multi-modal sensor fusion for autonomous and networked systems. 

Key Research Facilities, Infrastructure, and Equipment:
There is direct access to a 150m² drone hall to test drone and other (mobile) robotic related frameworks. The hall features a volume of more than 1,300m³ with a high-precision tracking system, a cable robot to emulate low-gravity environments, and high-performance computer units for AI training. 
Additionally, an outdoor arena with 1,000m2 and 15,000m3 volume will be available with an identical tracking system.

Our Expertise
* GNSS independent modular sensor fusion: Resilient equivariant methods (vision, radar, IR, lidar, UWB, etc)
* Data alignment across different reference frames using real-time sensor fusion and state estimation
* Self-aware and self-calibrating robotic systems able to re-calibrate and re-initialize online with self-healing capabilities
* Heterogeneous multi-agent collaborative state estimation and sensor fusion onboard compute constraint platforms
* Application oriented implementation on real platforms, large RAS test and validation facilities (1’300m³ indoor, 15’000m³ outdoor)

entityDescription:
GDL Innovation SA is a Swiss deep-tech company pioneering explicit, non-anthropomorphic spatial AI. Its core technology, the SGDL Exolanguage, is the first Multidimensional Logical World Model Language: a symbolic reasoning system grounded in primitive recursive functions, n-dimensional projective geometry and exact integer (bignum) arithmetic, originating from research at the Université de Montréal in the 1990s.
Unlike statistical AI, which extracts implicit intelligence from data, the Exolanguage encodes spatial intelligence explicitly — making geometry, topology, indexing and encoding exact, reversible and fully auditable. The system serves as the logical counterpart to learned world models, with applications ranging from digital twins and neuro-symbolic AI (explicit spatial priors for foundation models) to HPC-scale rendering and indexation, currently deployed on the Alps supercomputer at CSCS (Lugano). The company's technology is protected by international patents.

InGeoLab S.r.l. is an Italian multidisciplinary engineering company established in 2016, providing advanced technical services in civil and environmental engineering, Earth sciences, structural diagnostics, infrastructure monitoring and risk assessment.
The company combines engineering expertise with innovative technologies, including Earth Observation, InSAR, remote sensing, GIS, geophysics, numerical modelling and advanced monitoring systems, developing integrated solutions for infrastructure and environmental applications.
Research & Development is a key component of InGeoLab's strategy. The company actively develops and tests innovative methodologies by integrating satellite observations, ground-based monitoring, advanced data processing and digital technologies. InGeoLab's commitment to innovation has also been recognised within the SMAU Innovation Award framework.
InGeoLab operates according to a structured quality and sustainability-oriented management approach. The company is certified according to UNI EN ISO 9001:2015 and UNI/PdR 125:2022, and is currently undergoing the certification process for ISO/IEC 27001, strengthening its information security and data management framework.
Through the combination of engineering expertise, applied R&D and digital innovation, InGeoLab aims to transform advanced monitoring technologies and Earth Observation data into operational decision-support solutions for infrastructure managers, public authorities and industrial stakeholders.

entityDescription:
Founded in 1996 as a joint approach by Universities, cooperative banks (Volksbanken), saving banks (Sparkassen) and the Giessen-Friedberg Chamber of Industry and Commerce, TransMIT GmbH serves as a professional facilitator between science and industry by making accessible and commercializing the potential of approximately 7,000 scientists located at several research institutions in and beyond Hesse.
Drawing particularly from the three founding universities (Justus-Liebig-Universität Giessen, Technische Hochschule Mittelhessen and Philipps-Universität Marburg), the business division “TransMIT-Centers” with its currently approximately 150 business units offers innovative products and services from all areas of science and scientific research.
The business division Patents, Innovation and Start-Up Consulting identifies and assesses product ideas and research results for its clients and offers them internationally for commercialization through either licensing or participating in newly founded joint ventures.
The managed technology portfolio comprises all technology areas covered by German universities.
The business division IT-Solutions focusses on services enabling the efficient use of information and communication technology.
The TransMIT-Academy organizes continuing education seminars based on the Know-how of the universities and the TransMIT- Centers as well as other events and seminars on its clients’ behalf.
TransMIT GmbH has been repeatedly ranked first among the 21 largest German technology transfer companies in studies commissioned by several Federal Ministries.
Reference projects include “timm - Clustermanagement für die Medizinwirtschaft in Mittelhessen” (timm - Cluster Management for Medical Industries), “Mathematikum” (Museum of Mathematics), H-IP-O (Hessian Intellectual Property Organization), the Hesse teleworking action line, the Hesse biotech! action line, the science portal of the European Polymer Federation (EPF) and the BMWi-SIGNO-projects “KMU-Patentaktion” (SME Patent Campaign) and “Erfinderfachauskunft” (Technical Information for Inventors).
 
We offer solutions for operational business management and for specific questions pertaining to all technology areas.
Our services address almost all company divisions. 
 
We provide services for almost all essential management divisions dealing with human resources, accounting, facility management, procurement and IT-administration.
 
Furthermore, we offer a variety of services for your technical divisions like production, sales or research and development taking up any technological or subject-specific challenges.

description:
AIMEN is a private non-profit Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) founded in 1967 and headquartered in O Porriño (Spain), where it operates more than 11,000 m² of state-of-the-art research and testing facilities and employs over 330 highly qualified professionals. AIMEN has established itself as one of Europe's leading technology centres in advanced manufacturing, materials engineering and industrial digitalization. 
Over the last decade, AIMEN has successfully executed more than 300 R&D&I projects and has participated extensively in European collaborative programmes, including over 75 Horizon Europe projects. Through long-standing collaboration with major industrial stakeholders, the centre has developed strong expertise in transferring advanced technologies from research to industrial deployment across highly demanding sectors such as aeronautics, automotive, energy, and advanced manufacturing.
Particularly, AIMEN has a well-established track record within the aerospace ecosystem, actively participating in European initiatives, including the Clean Aviation Joint Undertaking, and collaborating with leading aerospace OEMs, Tier-1 suppliers, SMEs and research organisations. This experience provides a strong foundation for supporting the development of next-generation space systems and manufacturing technologies. AIMEN's capabilities are structured around two main pillars particularly relevant to the space sector: 
Advanced Materials and Structures: 
•Thermoplastic and thermoset composite technologies. 
•Advanced metallic materials and alloys. 
•Multifunctional and smart materials (including nano-enabled functional materials and self-sensing structures). 
•Materials characterization, qualification and testing. 
Advanced Manufacturing Technologies: 
•Large scale robotic additive manufacturing for polymers, composites and metals (AFP, ATL, FFF, FPF, DED). 
•Laser-based manufacturing, including DED, laser cladding, welding, high-precision laser micromachining/functionalization and hybrid manufacturing. 
•Advanced joining technologies for metallic and composite structures. 
•Out-of-autoclave composite processing (VBI, LRI, LRTM, RTM, hot-press curing). 
These capabilities are complemented by extensive expertise in digital technologies, including: 
•Robotics, autonomous systems and industrial automation. 
•In-line monitoring, quality assurance and non-destructive inspection. 
•Computer vision and optical inspection systems. 
•Digital twins and predictive maintenance. 
•Artificial intelligence and machine learning for manufacturing and materials design. 
For the space sector, AIMEN is particularly interested in applications related to lightweight structures, advanced materials, additive and hybrid manufacturing, high-performance structures, structural health monitoring solutions, and in-space manufacturing. By combining advanced materials expertise, manufacturing process development and digital technologies under one organization, AIMEN can support the development, qualification and industrialization of innovative space solutions from early-stage concepts to higher TRL demonstrators.

entityDescription: MobyGIS Srl is a start up company located in Trento (Italy) active in the environmental business. It delivers professional services and consultancy in the sector of renewable energies, civil protection and tourism in the form of tailored analysis and geographically based visualization platforms. Our background is hydrology with a strong focus on GIS and mathematical modeling. We have developed a calculation tool that predicts water resources (snow evolution and flow discharge) at large scale. The technology is based on a physically based approach that takes in input the terrain morphology and the meteorological evolution from weather forecast and measured ground data. Thanks to Open Data legislation, we have contacted all alpine regions to access the data from their meteorological sensors network. At the current date we have daily access to more then 1.000 stations, creating the the biggest database on snow and meteo in the Alps. The calculation algorithm turns into three services: 1) one for consumers in the touristic sector, called Mysnowmaps (www.mysnowmaps.com). It is a web and app that displays snow evolution in all the Alps (176.000 km2) and high resolution, especially off piste, and collects snow measures and reviews from the users. 2) one for Public Administrations, called "SnowMaps": it is a tool to monitor the snow evolution (accumulation and melting) at regional scale, tailored to help the realization of the avalanche bulletin and to monitor water resources stored in the snow. At the moment SnowMaps is used used by Italian Avalanche Services. 3) a service for hydropower companies, called "Waterjade", capable of predicting water inflow in production plants with 72 h advance.

entityDescription:
We are building a solution that combines Copernicus satellite data with data from agri-food and agro-industrial product manufacturers to assess, in near real time, their regulatory compliance and environmental footprint at the level of specific plots and product batches.

We identified a market problem: Earth observation data and commercial data both exist, but no one combines them at the scale required by EU regulations such as EUDR, CSRD, and CSDDD — as a result, neither producers, importers, insurers, nor lenders are able to estimate the risk of reduced production volume or quality over a given time horizon, or the risk of losing regulatory compliance, at the level of a specific plot or a specific link in the supply chain.

Our solution is aimed at producers and their associations, importers and exporters, insurers, and lenders who need to report supply chain compliance and manage regulatory and portfolio risk. It is distinguished by combining plot-level satellite data with producer data, anchoring it in digital product passports (GS1 / DPP), and making it available as risk models for insurers and creditors. The solution is built on an Environmental Intelligence layer: Earth observation (EO) and weather signals, producer operational data, blockchain-based DPP anchoring, and a predictive engine generating risk indicators for forests, crops, and infrastructure assets.

entityDescription: Diatope GmbH is a Germany‑based deep‑tech SME founded in 2021 as a spin‑off from the Institute of Quantum Optics at Ulm University. The company specializes in the development and production of quantum‑grade diamond materials with engineered nitrogen‑vacancy (NV) centers, which serve as key enabling components for quantum sensing, quantum communication, and quantum computing applications. Diatope operates a uniquely integrated fabrication infrastructure covering the full value chain from chemical vapour deposition (CVD) growth of isotopically enriched diamond to deterministic NV center creation via nitrogen doping and ion implantation, followed by high‑temperature annealing and quantum characterization. This end‑to‑end capability allows precise control over critical material parameters such as NV density, depth, and spin coherence properties, enabling the delivery of application‑specific diamond platforms.

entityDescription: Safety critical systems require extensive documentation for qualification in space applications like satellites, probes and manned spacecraft. Writing documentation is sometimes more extensive than the development of the system itself as it undergoes multiple iterations and constant change. Especially small and medium enterprises can’t afford to hire dedicated teams to manage a project's documentation for qualification. Even in large enterprises, documentation effort is one of the most significant drivers for project cost. Astra Labs is developing a next generation documentation tool to automate these manual tasks. Our goal is to supercharge the European space industry by reducing cost and time for the development of safety critical spacecraft and ground systems. We utilize novel algorithms and artificial intelligence to generate review-ready documentation that adheres to industry standards like ECSS and DO-178C. Just review and submit to your customer.

entityDescription:
IdeaCorp s. r. o. is a Slovak software engineering company established in 2013, specialising in systems for regulated and safety-critical operations — software that carries the burden of proof: who did what, under which authorisation, according to which revision of which document, and how that is demonstrated to a regulator on demand.
Ground-segment software and mission-control technologies. Telemetry acquisition and processing pipelines, append-only archives with deterministic full replay, and digital-twin integration. A single telemetry contract carries live, recorded and simulated sources, so the operational display does not distinguish between them.
Evidence-grade state handling. Event sourcing and CQRS with independent hash-chained audit trails, canonical serialisation, idempotency and compensating actions, risk-classified operations requiring recorded human approval, and data classification enforced as a routing constraint.
Simulation-first engineering. The company builds digital twins ahead of hardware and follows a simulation-first approach: software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop and batch modes; Monte Carlo campaigns with dispersion analysis feeding formal safety gates; every run recorded with its seed, model versions and inputs, so results are reproducible.
Applied cryptography for constrained links. A written wire specification with reference test vectors, implemented as protocol and client libraries: hybrid post-quantum key establishment (ML-KEM-768 with X25519) and ML-DSA-65 signatures in a canonical CBOR/COSE envelope, protecting payloads end to end independently of transport, with enforced crypto agility.
Platform. The company develops Aether, a modular software ecosystem built on a contract-first architecture, comprising over a dozen interoperable services in continuous internal operation. Aether integrates distributed AI orchestration with deterministic workflows and evidence-grade audit: AI-invoked capabilities are risk-classified, carry full provenance, and critical actions require recorded human approval. It provides the shared foundations — identity, audit, capability contracts, orchestration and telemetry — on which mission software, digital twins and AI-assisted decision support are built. Dedicated research programmes address unmanned aviation and the space ground segment.
Twelve consecutive profitable years, production systems in continuous business-critical use, and wholly owned and controlled by an EU natural person.
We are seeking opportunities to contribute to ESA programmes related to ground software, mission operations, AI-assisted autonomy, digital twins, telemetry processing and secure data infrastructures, as a partner or subcontractor on well-defined work packages.

entityDescription:
Mitterberger:Lab is an independent digital product and innovation studio based in Austria, operating under the legal entity Claus Nisslmüller e.U. The company specializes in the design and development of human-centered digital systems, with a strong focus on data-intensive environments, decision-support interfaces, and AI-enabled applications.
The core mission of Mitterberger:Lab is to transform complex technical systems and datasets into clear, usable, and efficient digital solutions. By combining structured analysis with user-centered design methodologies, the company enables organizations to improve decision-making, system transparency, and operational performance.
Mitterberger:Lab operates at the intersection of User Experience (UX), Human-Machine Interface (HMI) design, data analytics, and frontend engineering. The studio develops scalable digital interfaces that allow users to interact effectively with complex information systems, particularly in contexts where clarity, reliability, and performance are critical.
Core competencies include:
Design and implementation of data-driven user interfaces and dashboards 
Development of decision-support systems and analytical tools 
UX optimization for complex technical and research platforms 
Integration of AI-supported insights into user workflows 
Development of scalable frontend architectures and design systems 
The company follows a structured and system-oriented approach, combining problem analysis, iterative prototyping, and validation with a strong alignment between technical feasibility and user requirements. Emphasis is placed on clarity, efficiency, and long-term sustainability of digital solutions.
Mitterberger:Lab’s expertise is particularly relevant for applications involving complex data interpretation and interaction, including Earth Observation data platforms, monitoring and control systems, research environments, and advanced analytics interfaces.
Through its interdisciplinary approach, Mitterberger:Lab acts as a specialized partner for organizations seeking to enhance the usability and effectiveness of their digital systems, ensuring that advanced technologies can be fully leveraged through intuitive and well-structured user interaction.

entityDescription:
Environmental consulting services supporting companies and organizations in GHG reporting, climate resilience, sustainable development and circular economy strategies.
Green Goals is a for-profit environmental consultancy offering integrated environmental and sustainability services to public authorities and private organisations. The company focuses on delivering scientifically robust, policy-relevant and implementation-oriented solutions, supporting climate action, sustainability transition and innovation processes at local, regional and European level.
The core thematic areas of Green Goals include:
• climate change mitigation and adaptation
• air quality assessment, micrometeorology and environmental monitoring
• sustainable development and alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
• ESG strategies and sustainability reporting
• energy
• circular economy approaches
• European projects
• innovation and entrepreneurship
Green Goals combines scientific expertise with applied policy and project experience. The founder, Christiana Polyzou, is an Environmental Engineer holding a PhD in Atmospheric Science, with specialisation in air quality, micrometeorology, fluxes and land-atmosphere and sea-atmosphere interactions. Furthermore, she was consultant to the Municipality of Ioannina, as member of the Climate Transition Team, working on the Climate City Contract of the Municipality in the context of the EU Mission of Climate Neutral Cities.
This background enables the company to contribute to advanced climate and environmental monitoring, data interpretation and evidence-based decision support.

We work with entrepreneurs, SMEs, universities, and local authorities to support the development and growth of innovative UK companies and industry clusters. GeoFusion Analytics: Empowering Location-Aware Decision Making
GeoFusion Analytics Limited transforms raw data into actionable intelligence. With roots in public safety, healthcare, and emergency services, we provide advanced geospatial data integration to enhance organizational decision-making.
The GeoFusion Analytics Platform
Our cloud-based, AI-driven platform makes complex geospatial insights accessible, scaling seamlessly from spreadsheets to enterprise APIs.
Core Capabilities:
Instant Contextualization: Automatically pairs internal metrics with curated demographic, environmental, and human geography datasets.

Near Real-Time Data Signals: Layers live context such as weather, traffic, and satellite data for a 360-degree view of external factors.

AI-Prioritized Insights: Highlights the most impactful information so analysts can focus on critical decisions.

Automated Reporting: Transforms analysis into presentation-ready reports and slide decks.

Bilateral APIs: Enables direct integration with your infrastructure for prioritized insights.

Geospatial Alerting: Provides real-time alerts for pending emergencies.

Version One Additions:
Image-to-3D Map: Creates simulated 3D environments by overlaying satellite or drone data onto building and contour maps.

Terrain Analysis: Assesses surface characteristics (e.g., tarmac, sand, mud).

Vehicle Simulation: Models vehicle movement, including range and time-to-target.

KSI Blockchain Assurance: Ensures data integrity and provenance.

Version Two Additions:
Edge Computing: Delivers prioritized insights directly from satellites, bypassing ground-based parsing.

LoRA Messaging: Facilitates real-time, low-data HTML reporting outside network coverage.

By turning complex data into clear, automated insights, GeoFusion Analytics empowers organizations to deploy resources effectively, respond faster, and make smarter, location-aware decisions.
