entityDescription:
At ENUSA our purpose is to develop innovative nuclear and environmental solutions at a global level, contributing to the sustainable progress of society.
Our bussiness areas are:

Uranium Supply:

We maintain a policy of diversification of flexibility sources, supply security, and demanding pricing
In ENUSA, we manage theenriched uranium supplyto the electric companies that own the Spanish nuclear power plants. 
We carry out the procurement of supplies with major global suppliers and maintain contracts withmain global suppliersof uranium concentrates, conversion services, and enrichment services.
Our portfolio of suppliers allows us to maintain apolicy of diversificationof sources of flexibility, security of supply and very demanding prices.
In addition to the purchase, we carry out thelogistics managementde los movimientos de uranio que se tienen que producir hasta la obtención del producto final: el uranio enriquecido.
Enusa guarantees supply to its customers, managing uranium stocks in several countries in order to provide service and security in this phase of the nuclear fuel cycle.

Design and Engineering
We have the latest technological advances through transfer agreements with our partners and licensors Westinghouse and General Electric (GE).This allows us to cover the design, manufacture and supply of fuel to domestic and foreign nuclear power plants, as well as all engineering services related to the management and optimisation of fuel use in the reactor.
The fuel engineering developed at ENUSA covers all technical aspects of the nuclear fuel lifetime: from conceptual development and introduction of new products for irradiation in commercial PWR and BWR reactors, to storage and transport in dry casks as irradiated fuel.
Thanks to our experience, we cover nuclear design aspects and radiological, mechanical, thermo-mechanical, thermo-hydraulic calculations of materials.
These activities are made possible because of the high qualification of ENUSA personnel and the use of calculation tools developed in-house and/or by our licensors Westinghouse and GE.
This knowledge and experience of fuel, its design and behaviour, as well as the integrated view of the whole life of nuclear fuel allow us to provide our customers with a unique set of high added-value services. They also allow us, either autonomously or in collaboration with technology partners, to develop new nuclear fuel fabrication and inspection equipment.
In ENUSA, engineering is supported by powerful R&D&I, cooperating with Spanish universities through collaboration projects or participation in training activities, and in the promotion of and/or participation in national and international projects on key technical aspects of fuel.
Manufacturing

We manufacture for Spanish and European nuclear power plants, integrating the most innovative technology and the latest advances on the market.
The fuel assemblies are manufactured in our factory in Juzbado (Salamanca).
The activity focuses on the collection of uranium and the components necessary for the process, engineering and the manufacture of fuel assemblies for Spanish and European nuclear power plants, integrating the most innovative technology and the latest advances on the market.

description:
GRDprocess Sàrl is a Swiss research and technology company focused on the design, prototyping and experimental validation of artificial-intelligence architectures and autonomous systems. Originally active in information systems, process analysis and data-based decision support, the company refocused its primary activity in late 2025 on research and development in embodied and distributed intelligence.

Its main programme, Darwin Zero, develops an end-to-end architecture for autonomous units whose internal structures and behaviour improve through their own operation. The architecture couples bounded internal regulation, action, movement, local sensing, distributed prediction, error feedback and persistent reconfiguration within one continuous and traceable process.

GRDprocess develops the associated controlled digital environments, explicit body and sensor geometries, distributed processing layers, causal logging, replayable configurations, observer dashboards, and functional and causal-ablation tests. Current work is focused on demonstrating persistent adaptation under changing and partially unknown conditions, before progressively transferring the validated architecture to physical robotic units and connected multi-unit systems.

GRDprocess is seeking collaboration with research institutes, robotics companies, space-sector organisations and technology partners in embodied AI, autonomous exploration, resilient robotics, sensorimotor systems, distributed intelligence, simulation, hardware integration and experimental validation.

In parallel, GRDprocess develops THE FRAME, a structural-analysis methodology for decomposing and testing the coherence of normative and technical rules.

entityDescription: Mawashi Science and Technology Inc. is a Canadian science-and-engineering firm specializing in wearable systems: engineered equipment worn on and carried by the human body under load. The company brings together, under one roof, the disciplines required to engineer equipment that interfaces directly with the human body: mechanical engineering, biomechanics and human-performance testing, human factors and ergonomics, industrial design, and technical textiles. Mawashi is a full-cycle developer, taking wearable systems from concept and biomechanical analysis through prototyping and instrumented laboratory validation into operational products. It designs, develops and manufactures its own product lines, including passive exoskeletons, load-carriage systems and personal protection and delivers the same multidisciplinary engineering as a service to external partners and OEMs. A distinguishing strength is in-house instrumented validation (motion capture, electromyography, metabolic measurement), which lets Mawashi objectively quantify how equipment affects the wearer rather than only design it. Its systems have been evaluated by tier-one defense and special-operations users. The company's design philosophy is rooted in biomimicry; engineering that follows the natural mechanics of the human body

eBigData sp. z o.o.is a Poland-based DeepTech company specializing in the development of advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) solutions for industrial control and predictive diagnostics. The company's core expertise lies in Physical AI and Physics-Informed ML, seamlessly combining physical modeling with data science to optimize complex energy-intensive processes in real-time.
Our flagship technology, AI4MFC (Autonomous Master Flow Control), is a TRL-9, hardware-agnostic Edge Computing solution deployed in critical infrastructure. It autonomously executes a continuous "Sense -> Think -> Act" control loop, achieving up to 30% energy reduction and providing non-intrusive fault detection capabilities (NILM - Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring). By understanding the physical state of machinery rather than relying solely on statistical data, our proprietary algorithms ensure maximum operational safety, process continuity, and immediate anomaly isolation.
We serve clients across various sectors, including water/wastewater utilities, manufacturing, and HVAC systems. As an agile and innovative SME, recognized in programs such as the ABB StartUp Challenge and Hello Tomorrow DeepTech Pioneer, eBigData is currently expanding its Industrial DNA into the New Space sector. We aim to leverage our proven autonomous diagnostic frameworks to develop next-generation, self-aware space systems and virtual on-board engineering capabilities for satellites and space exploration missions.

entityDescription:
Rosswag GmbH is mainly known under the name Edelstahl Rosswag for over 100 years of experience in dealing with metal materials. Founded in 1911, the family-run company with more than 200 employees is one of the world's leading suppliers of open-die forged products weighing up to 4.5 tons, which are manufactured in-house in a holistic process chain. The in-depth know-how in the manufacturing and testing processes is reflected in the high quality of the end products, which are used under heavy loads, for example in the aerospace industry or in energy engineering. With more than 30 employees in the area of ​​quality assurance alone, individual process flow plans are defined in order to be able to meet the specific requirements for mechanical-technological component properties. In addition, after the forging process, the heat treatment or the CNC machining, the products are examined for their quality-relevant properties in the own testing and materials laboratory.
Founded in 2014, Rosswag Engineering is expanding the product portfolio with engineering services and innovative manufacturing processes. The incorporation of the additive manufacturing process Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) enables the production of functionally optimized metallic components in addition to the forging operation. The know-how accumulated over decades in the field of materials science and materials technology, in conjunction with the holistic, company-internal process chain, serves as the basis for establishing and expanding the future business. In 2017, the globally unique process chain was expanded to include in-house metal powder production for the qualification of new materials. As a result, over 35 materials have now been qualified for additive manufacturing. Since 2018, Rosswag has a cooperation with the software developer ANSYS regarding process simulation for demanding manufacturing and qualification projects. Rosswag was the first company to be certified by TÜV SÜD both for the production of metal powders and for the serial production of functional components in the field of additive manufacturing. Rosswag's research-intensive innovation strategy has been honored with numerous awards in recent years.

description:
IGASPIN - WE MASTER INTERFERENCE
IGASPIN GmbH is a technology company specializing in GNSS resilience, signal intelligence, and software-defined receiver technologies. We develop solutions that improve the robustness, integrity, and availability of satellite-based navigation and timing in challenging RF environments.

Core activities
	•	Software-defined GNSS receivers (SDR) and software receiver development: design and implementation of flexible receiver architectures for rapid prototyping, advanced signal processing, and feature validation across multi-constellation and multi-frequency signals.
	•	Interference detection and characterization: monitoring and analysis of RF environments to identify disruptions, classify events, and quantify operational impact on receiver performance.
	•	Multi-constellation signal processing (“meta-signals”): combining information from multiple GNSS constellations to enhance accuracy, stability, and continuity of service under degraded conditions.
	•	AI-enabled analytics: machine-learning methods for anomaly detection, RF event classification, and decision support for operators and system integrators.
	•	R&D and prototyping: rapid development of algorithms and demonstrators, including integration into embedded and edge-processing platforms where low latency and reliability are essential.
	•	Testing and validation: verification approaches and field testing concepts for performance evaluation in realistic scenarios, supporting technology maturation from prototype to deployable solutions.

Relevance to ESA and space programs

IGASPIN supports space and downstream applications where dependable PNT is mission-critical—such as space operations support, aviation, critical infrastructure, and autonomous systems. Our SDR-based receiver approach enables fast iteration and transparent performance evaluation, accelerating technology maturation for navigation assurance and resilience across the European GNSS ecosystem.

Collaboration approach

We work with public institutions, research partners, and industrial primes to deliver measurable results: clear requirements, transparent KPIs, and engineering-grade documentation. IGASPIN can contribute as a specialist partner for work packages covering software receiver/SDR development, algorithm design, system engineering support, prototyping, and validation.

entityDescription:
The Institute on Membrane Technology "Enrico Drioli" (CNR-ITM) is a research institute of the National Research Council of Italy (CNR), dedicated to advancing membrane science and engineering for energy, environmental, industrial, biotechnological, and biomedical applications.
Its research focuses on the development of advanced polymeric and inorganic membranes, including mixed-matrix, biohybrid, bioinspired, and catalytic membranes, as well as nanostructured membranes for gas and vapor separation. CNR-ITM also develops catalytic membrane reactors for CO₂ conversion and hydrogen, methanol, and biofuel production, while carrying out multiscale modelling and simulation of membrane transport phenomena. Additional research areas include membrane contactors, integrated membrane processes for water treatment, gas separation, and the agri-food and energy sectors, as well as membrane technologies for regenerative medicine, tissue engineering, biorefineries, biosensors, and membrane bioreactors.
Through multidisciplinary research, state-of-the-art facilities, and strong collaborations with academia and industry, CNR-ITM contributes to the development of sustainable membrane-based technologies with significant scientific, industrial, and societal impact.

entityDescription: Streamline Systems Ltd is a Cambridge-based SME developing resilient, GPS-independent positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) technology for UAVs, autonomous systems and Critical National Infrastructure. Our core technology uses networks of low-cost radio modules that range off one another to establish a shared terrestrial reference frame, delivering centimetre-level positioning without reliance on GNSS. The system provides resilient navigation in environments where satellite signals are degraded, denied or electronically contested. The technology has reached TRL 6, developed in-house, with demonstrated autonomous waypoint navigation and position hold in the absence of GPS or manual input. The company holds an integration partnership with a UK drone OEM and is advised by senior figures from UK defence and national metrology. Streamline Systems' capabilities span PNT systems engineering, radio-frequency hardware, embedded firmware and autonomous navigation.

entityDescription:
Raysilience is an Italian company operating in the field of resilient navigation and autonomy for uncrewed systems. The company develops technology that enables autonomous vehicles to determine their absolute position and continue their mission when satellite navigation is degraded, denied, jammed or spoofed - a capability increasingly recognised as critical across security, surveillance, public safety and civil aviation applications.

Its activity is a downstream space application: Raysilience converts georeferenced Earth Observation imagery into an onboard navigation reference layer, allowing absolute positioning to be recovered independently of live GNSS signals. This approach establishes a new operational use case for Earth Observation data and for the European infrastructures that produce it.

The company's first solution, MONDRIAN, targets small and medium uncrewed aerial systems and is designed as an open, platform-agnostic subsystem for integration by manufacturers, system integrators and mission-critical operators, rather than as a closed vertical product. Its development is supported by an industrial Proof of Concept Contract with Leonardo S.p.A. Autonomous System Lab, and by recognition within European innovation programmes, including the CASSINI Hackathon for Space and Defence, the EUDIS Hackathon. Raysilience won the Telespazio S.p.A. T-TeC award.

Raysilience is fully European from the ground up by design: ITAR-free, aligned with Copernicus and European Earth Observation infrastructures, and positioned to contribute to Europe's strategic autonomy in assured positioning, navigation and timing.

entityDescription:
Mapx Tech Kft. is a young Hungarian startup founded by Zsolt Perőcsényi with the mission to make Earth Observation (EO) data accessible and actionable for the general public. We aim to bridge the gap between raw satellite imagery and easy-to-understand, decision-ready information products.
Our focus areas include climate change adaptation and precision agriculture, two domains where timely, localized EO insights can drive significant impact. By leveraging AI and machine learning techniques, our mission is to process multi-spectral data from Sentinel and other EO missions into intuitive visualizations, interactive web apps, and alert services.
Some of our planned products include:
- Drought and vegetation stress monitoring for farmers and agricultural insurers- Flood and water level change detection for river basin authorities- Urban heat island and land-use change analytics for city planners- Forestry and wildfire risk assessment for forest managers
Our goal is to democratize access to planetary-scale EO data by presenting it in formats that integrate seamlessly into users' existing workflows, from interactive maps embedded into news articles to ML-powered analytics dashboards for specialist users. We envision our products enabling better-informed decisions from the farm field to the policy desk.
As a lean startup, we are looking to the ESA BIC program for access to technical expertise, computing resources, and the unparalleled EO data pipeline of the Copernicus program. With the right support, we are confident we can grow into an innovative EO data analytics provider in the CEE region and beyond.
We are excited for the opportunity to join the ESA community and accelerate our journey from concept to impact.

entityName: Big Data Research and Innovation Excellence
description:
BI-REX (Big Data Innovation & Research Excellence) is one of the Italian Competence Centers established under the Industry 4.0 national plan. BI-REX supports companies in research, innovation, technology transfer, and the adoption of advanced digital and manufacturing technologies through collaborative R&D projects, testing facilities, training, and consultancy services.

The Competence Center operates a state-of-the-art pilot line and advanced laboratories covering additive manufacturing, printed and hybrid electronics, industrial automation, artificial intelligence, machine learning, digital twins, industrial IoT, big data analytics, cybersecurity, edge and cloud computing, and advanced simulation. BI-REX collaborates with universities, research organizations, SMEs, and large enterprises to accelerate the development and industrialization of innovative technologies.

For the aerospace and space sectors, BI-REX provides expertise in advanced manufacturing, rapid prototyping, lightweight structures, thermal management, embedded electronics, digital engineering, predictive maintenance, quality control based on AI and machine vision, and the validation of innovative products and processes. The organization actively participates in national and European research programs and supports industrial partners in developing next-generation solutions for high-performance and mission-critical applications.

BI-REX is headquartered in Bologna and operates through a network of industrial and academic partners, offering access to multidisciplinary competencies and advanced infrastructures to foster technological innovation and competitiveness.

Company description: The University of Cassino and Southern Lazio (UNICAS) was established in 1979 as a response to the educational needs represented by an area characterized by a growing focus on innovation and cultural and social promotion. Due to its geographical location, UNICAS serves as a natural hub between the cities of southern Lazio, Campania, Molise and Abruzzo, from which it channels most of its students.
The University Community of the University consists of more than thirteen thousand people:
- 12,525 students enrolled in study courses and Postgraduate paths (a.y. 2021/2022);
- 275 faculty and researchers;
- 254 managers, technical and administrative staff;
- 9 staff and language experts;
- 122 PhD students;
- 42 research fellows.
Teaching and research activities take place mainly at the Cassino campus; 2 undergraduate and 2 master's degree courses in economics and engineering disciplines are hosted at the Frosinone decentralized pole, in order to contribute to the development of an increasingly fruitful interaction with the territory.
At the Gaeta campus, on the other hand, conference, public engagement and technology transfer activities are concentrated, as well as some continuing education activities.
The University provides paths for teaching qualification, structured according to current regulations. Services to students are provided through the 3 area libraries (economic-legal, engineering, humanities), the University Center for Orientation (CUOri), the University Center for Disability, Inclusion and Research (CUDIR), the Center for International Relations (CRI), The University Center for Information Services (CASI), and the Job Placement Office, at which an Information Desk is active, an interface between students, undergraduates and graduates with the world of work.
Teaching is supported by a lively and qualified research activity, developed within the Departments in all the fields of interest of the University (antiquistics, historical-artistic studies, historical, linguistic, philological-literary, paleographic-codicological, pedagogy and social service; mechanical, management, civil, environmental, electrical, computer, telecommunications engineering; economic, business and legal disciplines; motor and health sciences), with results of average high quality and peaks of national and international visibility and excellence. Research activities are supported by the presence of highly specialized laboratories, which are functional for the development of projects carried out also in the framework of national and international collaborations and for the release of technological consultancy for the benefit of institutions, entities and industries.
The research infrastructure and related equipment provided by the University is an important support for researchers' participation in competitive calls.

entityDescription: Slot Consulting is a research and innovation-focused consulting company. The company has a rich aviation reference portfolio and provides services to other innovation-intensive industries. Slot Consulting was founded in 2001 in Budapest, Hungary. The term “slot” partly reflects the strong airport relationship and our focus on securing slots and niche areas for our clients or developments. Slot Consulting has been involved in European research programmes from the beginning. We have an outstanding track record in European aviation research projects, making Slot Consulting one of the leading European SMEs in this field. Performing research in a consortium with leading European players is an opportunity to learn the directions of European air transport and aerospace research trends, and general research and development principles, and to improve our expertise in the focus areas. This helps us to be more innovation-focused. The experience gained through these product developments is then transformed into our research skills portfolio. Slot Consulting provides different types of services to stakeholders. We offer consulting services to help customers improve their business operations. entityDescription:
Founded in 2021, GreenAnt has been focusing on developing tools for climate resilience and has operated in Thailand and Vietnam. In 2023, we merged with SarVision, a Wageningen University’s data analysis spin-off, to become a leader in analyzing radar satellite data to provide climate adaptation tools and services.
 
We have developed unique intellectual property for analyzing radar data. Desidera, our flagship product, offers data-backed services to help manage climate risks. This includes predicting harvest failures, assessing flood risks, and estimating damages promptly after such events. Our approach combines artificial intelligence with extensive satellite data, offering a powerful tool for insurers, farmers, and traders to collaboratively tackle climate risks.
 
Using our AI-powered SaaS platform, Desidera, users have the flexibility to choose from a variety of subscription packages to obtain services such as EUDR certifications, comprehensive floods and harvest insurance policy bundles, and a variety of data-driven tools for evaluating and managing climate risks.
 
By making satellite data analysis accessible to the sectors most exposed to climate risk, we aim to promote sustainability and climate stewardship, across agriculture, real estate, and insurance.

entityDescription:
Alpine Data Ventures GmbH (ADV) is an independent data and artificial intelligence consultancy based in Munich, Germany. Founded in 2025 by four partners with senior backgrounds in corporate data leadership, data engineering, business intelligence and AI product development, ADV supports organisations in building the data foundations, architectures and AI capabilities required to operate in regulated and mission-critical environments.
The company covers the full data lifecycle across three practice areas. Data Strategy and Governance includes data strategy development, governance frameworks, data catalogues, master data management, maturity assessments and organisational enablement. Data Engineering and Architecture includes data warehouses, data lakes, data mesh implementations, ETL and pipeline development, enterprise architecture management and sovereign, European hosted data platforms. AI and Data Science includes machine learning, computer vision for automated visual inspection and object detection, anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, forecasting and demand planning, digital twin and simulation, and retrieval augmented generation for technical documentation and knowledge access.
Information security and data protection form a cross-cutting fourth competence. ADV provides external Data Protection Officer mandates under GDPR, external Information Security Officer mandates, ISMS implementation aligned to ISO 27001, NIS2 compliance assessments, and identity and access management concepts. Members of the management team hold TÜV certification as Data Protection Officer and as IT Security Officer.
ADV operates on a principle of accountability the company describes as Skin in the Game: it stands behind what it recommends and implements it where required. Engagements are delivered by senior consultants working directly with the client, from short assessments through to multi-year mandates.
Clients include industrial and manufacturing companies as well as public sector bodies at federal, state and municipal level in Germany. Working languages are German and English.

Xplore 4D is a Slovak SME specialized in digital twins, geospatial visualization, immersive XR technologies (VR/AR), AI-assisted spatial analysis and advanced 3D data integration. The company develops digital platforms and interactive environments that combine geospatial information, GIS technologies, 3D modelling, simulation tools and data-driven decision support systems.
Xplore 4D focuses on the creation of digital twins for territories, cultural heritage sites, tourism destinations, natural environments and infrastructure assets. The company delivers solutions for visualization, monitoring, planning, education, public engagement and operational support through interactive digital environments.
The company’s activities include geospatial data processing, integration of Earth Observation and remote sensing data, spatial analytics, artificial intelligence applications, interactive visualization, virtual and augmented reality experiences, simulation environments, and digital transformation projects for public and private sector stakeholders.
Xplore 4D supports the preservation and interpretation of cultural and natural heritage through advanced digital technologies, including 3D reconstruction, immersive storytelling, educational applications and interactive knowledge platforms. The company also develops innovative solutions for environmental monitoring, smart territory management and data-driven spatial decision-making.
The legal entity was incorporated on 18 December 2021. Following a strategic transformation completed in September 2025, the company adopted its current technology-focused business model and operates under the Xplore 4D brand. Since then, its activities have been dedicated to the development of digital twin technologies, geospatial applications, AI-enabled analytics and immersive visualization solutions.
Xplore 4D seeks collaboration with research organisations, industry partners, public institutions and international consortia in the fields of Earth Observation, digital twins, space-enabled applications, environmental monitoring, cultural heritage, smart territories, education and advanced visualization technologies.

entityDescription:
OMEGA Space Technology GmbH is a German space-tech start-up developing satellite-based crop analytics for the European agricultural insurance market. The company was incorporated on 10 February 2026 in Munich, Germany (share capital €25,000) and operates from Munich/Oberpfaffenhofen, at the heart of Europe's largest space cluster. OMEGA currently has three full-time founders; a Customer Success & Sales manager and a Junior Developer are planned for mid-2027.
OMEGA's mission is to close the structural data gap that prevents Multi-Peril Crop Insurance (MPCI) in Europe. While the US MPCI market ($17.3B in premiums) is built on decades of field-level yield and loss history, no equivalent dataset exists in Europe. OMEGA reconstructs and builds this field-level data layer by fusing multiple Earth observation sources — Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, Landsat, EnMAP hyperspectral, weather, soil and ground-truth data — through a combination of physics-based, auditable algorithms and selectively deployed machine learning. This architecture is designed for the regulatory requirements of the insurance sector (BaFin auditability, EU AI Act explainability).
The company's first commercial capability — deterministic SAR-based storm damage detection (Patent #1, filed with WIPANO funding) — is in production and has been validated against historical insurer claims data with very high agreement to on-site loss assessments. Building on this foundation, OMEGA is developing SecureEye, a preventive crop monitoring service distributed to farmers through their insurers, together with a portfolio-level risk and underwriting dashboard for insurance customers.
Customer engagement includes Vereinigte Hagel (Germany's largest crop insurer, >5M ha; technology validated against 2025 claims cases), Allianz Agrar (Letter of Intent; software validated against historical claims; evaluation under the Allianz Agrar "Vision 2030" strategy), Versicherungskammer Bayern (specialty-crop discussions) and Munich Re (structural validation of the field-level data gap; invitation to present at Munich Re's 2026 crop insurance customer event). In the precision-farming vertical, OMEGA operates commercial pilots with Dina Farms, Egypt (1,000 feddan; 20% demonstrated water savings) and Lotus, Egypt (700 ha), and validates its platform in Southern Europe through the EIT Food Test Farms Programme. The platform runs on Google Cloud infrastructure ($75,000 in secured credits).
The founding team combines the disciplines required for the project. Sherif Elsayed (CEO) and Marcel Winzen (CFO/COO) each bring 9 years of satellite engineering experience at Airbus Defence & Space, covering EO payload characterisation and calibration for NASA/ESA/JAXA missions, satellite assembly, integration and test, and ESA/EU programme management; they previously co-founded Nabta Playa e.V., a non-profit EO research institute for food security applications. Ahmed Daker (AI/ML Lead, formerly SAS and Omdena) owns the technical stack end-to-end, from Sentinel data ingestion to ML models and cloud-native deployment.
OMEGA's recognition and funding track record includes winning the ESA BA Challenge of the INNOspace Masters 2026, acceptance into the EIT Food Accelerator Network (2026 cohort), participation in the final selection round of ESA BIC Bavaria, and WIPANO patent funding. The company's long-term roadmap includes KingTut, a planned agri-optimised multispectral satellite constellation (from 2029), which is financed separately and is not part of this proposal.

entityDescription:
QRBIT is a private capital company, founded by researchers from the Institute of Communication and Computer Systems (ICCS) of the National Technical University of Athens (NTUA). The company was co-founded by Dr. Ioannis (Giannis) Giannoulis, Dr. Aristeidis (Aris) Stathis, and Mr. Argyrios (Argiris) Ntanos, leveraging a strong foundation of research in optical communications and quantum cryptography developed within the Photonic Communications Research Laboratory (PCRL) at ICCS/NTUA.
Dr. Giannoulis serves as the company’s administrator, while Dr. Stathis and Mr. Ntanos are also shareholders. Small equity shares in QRBIT are held by prominent faculty members of the School of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) at NTUA, including Prof. Iraklis Avramopoulos (Head of PCRL), Prof. Athanasios Panagopoulos, and Asst. Prof. Dimitrios Apostolopoulos, who provide strategic guidance and contribute to the company’s R&D and consulting activities.
The QRBIT team is a multi-disciplinary group of quantum engineers—comprising two electrical engineers and a physicist—combining deep expertise in physics, optical engineering, and electrical engineering to advance laser and quantum communication technologies for terrestrial free-space and satellite links. Their work spans both theoretical and experimental domains, including the formulation and simulation of quantum communication protocols and the practical deployment, testing, and integration of QKD (Quantum Key Distribution) systems in both fiber and free-space networks.
QRBIT is actively developing state-of-the-art quantum and optical technology prototypes, such as QKD sub-systems, optical telescope assemblies, and specialized software tools (e.g., QuantLink, QBER modeling tools for noisy channels). The team also conducts experimental research using both portable and large astronomical telescopes, integrating custom optical systems to enable quantum and advanced optical applications.

description:
Melsa Biotech (Toggam Enterprises Limited) is an Irish advanced-materials company producing high-purity eumelanin, a bio-derived functional biopolymer, from circular natural-origin biomass using a proprietary multi-stage extraction process.
 Eumelanin combines broadband ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared absorption, photothermal energy dissipation, free-radical scavenging, thermal stability and potential charge-dissipative behaviour in a single lightweight, sustainable material. These properties make it a candidate active for multifunctional protective coatings addressing UV shielding, thermal management, oxidative protection and partial radiation mitigation. Our material has been independently validated: to 99% purity confirmed by third-party assay, and a six-technique characterisation study by the University of Galway (TGA, 13C NMR, TEM, AFM, SAXS, XPS) confirming eumelanin structure and demonstrating high thermal stability, with approximately 35 to 40% mass retention at 900 degrees Celsius.

Space and aerospace relevance: bio-derived multifunctional coatings for spacecraft and satellite materials (thermal, UV and radiation protection of lightweight polymers, composites and surfaces), aligned with sustainable and EU-sovereign advanced-material supply. Adjacent capabilities span defence, semiconductor, electronics and high-performance industrial coatings.
Core competencies: bio-based advanced materials, functional biopolymers and pigments, protective and functional coatings, materials characterisation, and specialty high-value material supply. Based in Ireland with in-house production and analytical capability, supported by academic and industry partnerships.

entityDescription:
QRCL Technologies OÜ — Post-Quantum Space & Critical Infrastructure Security

QRCL Technologies OÜ (Estonia) develops quantum-resistant cryptographic systems for satellite operations, aerospace coordination, and critical infrastructure. Our core innovation addresses the EU quantum-safe migration imperative outlined in NIS2, DORA, and emerging space-sector standards (ESA CCSDS, ECSS-E-80-3-520 spacecraft security).

EU Regulatory Alignment: 
- DORA (Digital Operational Resilience Act): Cryptographic agility framework for authorized parties 
- NIS2 (Network & Information Security Directive 2): Quantum-risk mitigation for essential services (energy, transportation, communications) 
- MiCA / PSD2: Post-quantum digital signatures for financial settlement finality 
- AI Act: Explainable Byzantine consensus for space-segment AI/ML operations 
- CRA (Cyber Resilience Act): ML-DSA-65 / ML-KEM-768 / SLH-DSA-SHAKE-192f (FIPS 204/203/205)

Technical Pillars: 
1. QRCL-GUARD — GNSS integrity (dual-frequency correction, Kalman fusion, BFT arbitration) 
2. QRCL-COSMOS — Orbital-mechanics decisioning (CCSDS-compliant telemetry, audit-chain commitment) 
3. QRCL-DEBRIS — Conjunction-alert coordination (6-of-7 Byzantine validator, 40 ms latency SLA) 
4. QRCL-QKD — FIPS 203 key establishment with BB84 simulation & privacy amplification 
5. QRCL-QNET — Entanglement-link coordination (Quantum Internet Alliance compliance) 
6. QRCL-ATM — Air-traffic & drone coordination (EASA TCAS II / airspace-risk integration)

entityDescription:
Duisburger Hafen AG (duisport) operates the largest inland port in the world. As a trimodal logistics hub, duisport is one of Europe’s key nodes for the flow of goods. Each year, more than 20,000 ships and 25,000 trains are handled in Duisburg, with over 100 million tons of cargo and around four million containers (TEU) moved through the port. The Port of Duisburg comprises 21 port basins, 10 container terminals, and approximately 200 kilometers of its own rail network.
Around 300 transport and logistics companies are located at the site, with approximately 52,000 jobs directly or indirectly dependent on the port and logistics sector.
The duisport Group combines a strategic geographic location and ideal site conditions with extensive logistics expertise. It provides customers from around the world with end-to-end solutions for the development and optimization of global supply chains – across real estate, rail freight, industrial logistics, contract logistics, and packaging logistics

entityDescription:
Blockchain & Cie. is a French EURL (Entreprise Unipersonnelle à Responsabilité Limitée) specialised in AI-agentic engineering, Web3/blockchain development, and production-hardened software for regulated industries.
Founded and operated by Antoine Delamare (PharmD, RS5000-certified blockchain developer, and full-stack lead developer), the company bridges clinical/regulatory judgment with modern software delivery.

Core competences:
- AI-generated code rescue: audit, stabilisation, and security hardening of AI-assisted/vibecoded repositories (TypeScript, Node.js, React/Next.js, Python/FastAPI).
- Production AI agents: deployment of autonomous agent stacks in hardened Docker environments, using multi-LLM routing, MCP, WhatsApp/Matrix bridges, and human-in-the-loop guardrails.
- Web3 & traceability: Solidity smart contracts, OpenZeppelin standards, Chainlink oracle integration, and traceability systems for EUDR/CSDDD, DSCSA/FMD, and supply-chain compliance.
- Geospatial & data interfaces: interactive mapping, GeoJSON field capture, role-based dashboards, and multi-language onboarding flows.

Relevant experience:
- ESA OCTAVE / Parametry UG: full-stack system engineer on an ESA-funded, EU-regulated traceability project for organic cotton, delivering a React geospatial mapper, Solidity SBT/ERC-1155 certificates, Chainlink Functions oracle, and a WhatsApp farmer-onboarding AI agent (Nanobot).
- Celestical Cloud : delivery and hardening of 6+ Docker-based AI agent stacks (Nanobot, Hermes) with multi-LLM, MCP, and multi-channel integration (Telegram, Whatsapp, etc.).
- Compositex (materials and technical textiles manufacturing company) : repo rescue and improvements of a production ERP (security patch, dependency vendoring, QA tests, architecture documentation, new features, etc.)

Blockchain & Cie operates full-remote from UTC-3 with daily overlap with EU and US East Coast timezones.

We work in French, English, and Spanish.

We are interested in teaming, subcontracting, and consortium partnerships for ESA, EU, and national space/health/AI programmes requiring reliable agentic systems, blockchain traceability, or regulated software engineering.

entityDescription:
Qalio Quantum Computing is a established Spanish startup, specializing in quantum algorithms for space applications. The company focuses on solving complex optimization challenges in the space sector. Qalio bridges the gap between theoretical quantum computing research and practical space mission requirements, delivering hybrid quantum-classical solutions optimized for near-term hardware.
The company's flagship platform, Phoeqiss, emerged directly from this research, providing a comprehensive environment for designing, simulating, and benchmarking quantum optimization algorithms. Phoeqiss enables rapid prototyping of mission-specific quantum oracles, visualization of superposition-based search processes, and direct comparison against classical baselines—critical capabilities for demonstrating operational value to ESA
Qalio's strategic focus on space positions the company at the intersection of Europe's quantum technology ecosystem and ESA's roadmap. With deep knowledge of both quantum algorithm design and space mission constraints, Qalio delivers credible technology assessments that translate academic quantum speedups into mission-relevant metrics for lunar autonomy and beyond.

entityDescription:
Energy@Work is an innovative Italian research-driven SME, established as a cooperative and headquartered in Triggiano (Bari, Apulia, Italy). The company develops advanced digital technologies that support the digital and sustainable transformation of regional ecosystems and industrial value chains, with a people-centred approach and a strong commitment to concrete technology transfer from research to deployment.
The company operates at the intersection of applied research, software engineering and system integration. Its core activity is the design, development and operational deployment of digital platforms, data-driven services and interoperable middleware solutions for complex socio-technical systems, with particular attention to data interoperability, real-time data acquisition, AI-based analytics, decision-support and edge/cloud architectures. Energy@Work is consistently ranked among the top-100 Italian SMEs for participation in competitive research grants, and among the top-10 SMEs in Southern Italy by the same indicator.Throughout its history Energy@Work has participated in several EU-funded research and innovation projects under H2020 and Horizon Europe and has built a stable network of long-term collaborations with European research and technology organisations, universities, industrial partners, public authorities and end-user communities, and contributes to several European clusters and policy-oriented initiatives. Beyond R&D activities, Energy@Work delivers professional services to industrial, institutional and public-sector clients, with a structured methodology covering requirements engineering, system architecture, software development, integration, validation and after-deployment support. The company invests systematically in the professional growth of its staff, in the consolidation of its internal know-how and in the responsible adoption of emerging technologies, with the long-term objective of being a reliable European technology partner for digital transformation and sustainable innovation.
E@W competences also include the design and management of sensor networks, the continuous monitoring of metrics and consumption, and the integration of heterogeneous field data sources, ranging from local and wide-area network buses (LAN/MAN/WAN) to satellite-based geolocation services such as Copernicus, Galileo and EGNOS, which can be exploited for the tracking and management of distributed assets. E@W also works on semantic schemas and information models for interoperability, supporting sectorial dataspaces and cross-domain data exchange across federated platforms, as well as on the secure and decentralized sharing of data through distributed ledger technologies (eg. HLF) combined with standardized data-space connectors such as IDS-RAM. E@W also has competences in the design and development of AI-based Digital Twins that integrate process, asset and human-related data to enable real-time monitoring, "what-if" simulations and explainable decision support, with built-in privacy-preserving mechanisms.

entityDescription:
ODES Space P.C. is a New Space software company developing simulation and validation technology for the satellite mission lifecycle. Its SaaS platform is built around a "living digital twin" — a high-fidelity model of the spacecraft and mission that evolves from early design through integration, launch, and in-orbit operations. It enables mission teams to simulate spacecraft behaviour, validate flight procedures and software, verify subsystem performance, and de-risk operational decisions before and during flight.
Targeting microsatellite and CubeSat missions, where affordable high-fidelity simulation is scarce, ODES unifies design-phase modelling with operational simulation in one continuous environment to reduce mission risk, shorten validation cycles, and improve operational readiness. The company combines expertise in spacecraft systems engineering, simulation (ECSS-SMP/SIMULUS-class), ground segment and mission operations.

entityName: Dr. Bratzel Center of Automotive Management GmbH & Co. KG
entityDescription:
The Center of Automotive Management (CAM) was founded by Prof. Stefan Bratzel in 2004 with the support of the University of Applied Sciences of Bergisch Gladbach. Its function is to serve as a partner for car manufacturers, suppliers and retailers concerning market research and strategic consultancy. Currently the CAM consists of a regular staff of five team members and is located in the town of Bergisch Gladbach near Cologne. 
Shortly after its foundation the CAM established two separate approaches to analyse and determine the competitiveness of the global automotive industry. The first approach was the establishment of an innovation database. Since 2005 the CAM systematically gathered more than 20.000 product and technological innovations of 40 global car manufacturers and their 100 brands. Sources of information are, amongst others, journals, press releases and on-site surveys on international automobile exhibitions. CAM only accepts identified technological improvements as „innovation“ if they meet three conditions: Innovations must have a perceptible benefit for customers (compared to the status quo), they must be appropriately presented, so that a broad public could take notice of it and they must be available as products, at least as prototypes. If the innovation matches this criteria it is then systematically categorized in seven main technology fields and currently more than 700 innovation types. Finally each innovation is then individually assessed using four different criteria which are its innovation level, originality, maturity level and customer benefit.
Together with our annual patent analysis of the automotive industry this approach allows us to determine the innovation landscape of the industry and to forecast its technological development on a mid- and long-term range perspective. As the database also provides insights in the innovation performance and priorities of each manufacturer it can also be used as a tool for competitive analyses and is therefore licensed by a couple of notable OEMs. 
The other approach focuses on the market and financial performance of the industry competitors. The CAM has established a performance database which contains the sales, financial and other performance figures of each car manufacturer since back in 2002 and is updated quarterly. The financial figures are derived from the official financial statements and include performance indicators like R&D expenditures, EBIT and operative cash flow. The market figures contain information about the global and regional performance (e.g. Europe, NAFTA, BRICs) and are gathered from official statements and reports from manufactures, governmental bodies and advocacy groups. 
Both approaches are used as an empirical foundation for in-depth studies and projects for manufacturers, suppliers as well as governmental and non-governmental organisations. The results of both approaches are also used to provide an annual study about the performance of the industry’s competitors by aligning the innovation, market and financial success of each competitor, resulting in a ranking of the competitors by applying our ‘Automotive Performance Index’ (API) scheme. This approach allows us not only to identify the high, medium and low performers of the competition, but also to provide reliable empirical evidence for the results and statements.

entityDescription:
Satlantis France SAS is an independent company, legally distinct from Satlantis Microsat (Spain), although both entities share a common technological heritage and vision. Operating autonomously, Satlantis France defines its own R&D agenda, strategic roadmap, and industrial partnerships, with a core focus on high-resolution polarimetric imaging and advanced Earth observation solutions for both civil and defense applications.
As the group’s center of excellence for optical polarimetry, Satlantis France develops innovative payloads that integrate compact, high-performance sensors, onboard image processing, and AI-driven analytics. Our current developments focus on generating fused imagery that combines polarimetry, multispectral data, and very high spatial resolution, enabling the detection of subtle spectral and directional features in complex or obscured environments.
Key application domains under investigation include:– Methane detection with advanced atmospheric discrimination,– Monitoring of microplastics in marine environments,– Air quality assessment,– Detection of camouflaged or concealed structures,– High-resolution environmental surveillance.
In parallel, Satlantis France contributes to the group’s near real-time satellite video capability, delivering native resolutions enhanced through proprietary algorithms to achieve effective ground resolutions of approximately 1 meter. This functionality enables dynamic monitoring of rapidly evolving scenarios, including:– Convoy tracking and route surveillance,– Observation of active conflict zones,– Wave pattern analysis for coastal monitoring and bathymetry,– Fast-response disaster impact assessment.
Our mission is to transform satellite data into actionable geospatial intelligence, tailored to the operational needs of space agencies, public authorities, and industrial stakeholders.
Through these capabilities, Satlantis France contributes to Europe’s strategic autonomy in space-based technologies, offering a unique polarimetric and video imaging solution deployable on agile LEO platforms and scalable to constellation architectures. We actively participate in European collaborative initiatives and welcome scientific and institutional partnerships to bring this critical capability into operational service.

entityDescription:
Retree&Space Solutions SL es una empresa dedicada a la regeneración de ecosistemas degradados mediante la reforestación con especies autóctonas. Su misión combina la restauración ambiental con un impacto económico y social.
Qué hace:
- Crea sumideros de carbono rastreables mediante la plantación de especies autóctonas que regeneran los suelos, fortalecen la biodiversidad y apoyan las economías rurales.
- Adopta una postura explícita en contra del ecoblanqueo, ofreciendo mediciones de absorción de CO2 trazables en lugar de meras declaraciones de intenciones.
- Integra la tecnología satelital y la observación de la Tierra para monitorear y verificar el progreso de la reforestación a lo largo del tiempo, sin depender únicamente de la verificación sobre el terreno.
Dos ofertas principales:
- El servicio de reforestación regenerativa es el núcleo del negocio y está dirigido a empresas que buscan medir y verificar su absorción de CO2 a través de proyectos de impacto demostrable.
- Carbin es la herramienta de trazabilidad del carbono de Retree&Space Solutions SL (actualmente en desarrollo): combina datos satelitales con monitoreo sobre el terreno para verificar y rastrear continuamente el carbono capturado y la salud de los ecosistemas restaurados.
Público objetivo: Empresas que buscan una medición verificable y trazable de la absorción de CO2, no una simple declaración de intenciones.

entityDescription:
Cerberus Nuclear was created to approach technical consultancy with an emphasis on creativity and innovation. We bring together highly specialist skills and industry-wide experience to offer comprehensive Radiation Shielding, Criticality Safety, Nuclear Characterisation, Data Science and Software Development services for Nuclear, Medical, Research, Defence, Fusion and Space sectors.
Radiation Shielding 
Our highly experienced team provide radiation shielding design, dose assessment and peer review services covering the full project design life-cycle. We utilise the latest calculation methods combined with high-power computing to efficiently deliver accurate and reliable results. Our team are skilled in communicating complex data to stakeholders and regulatory bodies. 
Criticality Safety 
Cerberus Nuclear has the largest independent criticality safety team in the UK and has significant experience supporting key clients across the nuclear industry. We provide support across the full nuclear fuel cycle and offer a complete range of criticality services, including working on the behalf of regulators within the UK and internationally. 
Nuclear Innovation
Cerberus Nuclear have produced high-level strategies for characterisation of high-profile nuclear facilities. Using our established expertise in nuclear data science we utilise the latest developments in machine learning and computer vision to develop new innovative techniques to support on-site characterisation and data analysis.

Space Applications

With Cerberus Nuclear looking to utilise its nuclear heritage in the space sector, we are already able to handle the complete process required to find the actual radiation exposure a spacecraft and its components experience in a given orbit using Monte Carlo radiation transport codes. This covers the radiation shielding impacts of the outer structure of the spacecraft as well as its internal geometry, and can be completed to ECSS standards. Our current capabilities include:
- Radiation Mission Environment Specification
- Total Ionising Dose (TID) Assessment
- Total Non-Ionising Dose (TNID) Assessment
- Single Event Effects (SEE) Assessment
- Bulk Shielding Analysis
- Component and Material Radiation Threat Analysis

entityName: ZORA Reentry Systems s. r. o.
entityDescription: ZORA Reentry Technologies is an early-stage Slovak deep-tech company developing advanced thermal protection systems (TPS) for spacecraft re-entry applications. Founded by four engineers with hands-on experience from the HARTS heatshield project, ZORA is commercializing a 3D-woven, carbon-fiber thermal protection material designed to compete with established high-performance ablative solutions such as PICA, while offering superior geometric adaptability and material configurability. The company addresses a clear gap in the European space market: the lack of accessible, configurable TPS materials that can be tailored to different mission envelopes without costly full redesigns. ZORA's material platform enables controlled variation of density, weave architecture, and thickness, allowing integration into non-standard geometries for re-entry vehicles, payload return capsules, and high-temperature aerothermal components. Currently at TRL 2–3, ZORA is targeting TRL 4–5 by the end of its ESA BIC Slovakia incubation period (2026–2028), with a focus on repeatable in-house manufacturing, standardized characterization datasets, and first customer evaluation samples. The company targets European institutional space programmes and commercial re-entry startups, with a longer-term roadmap extending into reusable thermal protection architectures and non-space high-temperature industrial applications.

entityDescription: GUIDE is a GNSS testing laboratory accredited in Geolocation. It is specialized in the performance characterization of positioning systems inland environments where GNSS measurements are highly distorted. Two test methodologies are implemented. One, to assess their "typical" performance relative to the usual accuracy/precision according to areas and the other, for their performance in "critical" situations where the integrity of the measurements must remain under control. In the first case, GUIDE digitizes real GNSS signals and then replays them on test benches many times. These iterations have the advantage of • increase the number of measurement samples for a better characterization of uncertainties. • reveal local constraints of test scenarios impacting the positioning measurements. In the second case, GUIDE uses tools of simulations of last generation to reconstruct the conditions of propagation within synthetic environments representative of the reality (Bridge, Buildings, Foliage, ...). These typical virtual scenes, modeled in 3D, are used to simulate the reception conditions of GNSS signals. The local biases are rendered in the first stratum of scenario which can be enriched with the second stratum to add Global "feared events", such as those from satellites or high layers of the atmosphere, ie. especially the ionosphere. Different types of interferences (domestic, industrial or intentional ones) can be mixed with all these GNSS signals to assess the resilience level of positioning systems.

From autonomous vehicles and industrial robots to smart energy grids and aerospace platforms, physical AI systems depend on data they can trust, captured at the edge and delivered at scale to the data center.

entityDescription:
We are a non-profit association with a keen interest and active involvement in science, based in the Garching area. We collaborate on the GraviHAB project, which focuses on habitat design, mobile plant cultivation, biomass recycling, and artificial gravity. In addition to habitat design and hardware testing, our work examines aspects such as seed selection and efficiency; plant lighting systems; the simplified composition and delivery of nutrient solutions; leaf and root respiration and their impact on air composition; biomass methanization and improved biogas-to-electricity conversion; the suitability of plant produce for human consumption; and the benefits and risks associated with the biome developing within our partially or fully closed habitat.

Our goal is twofold: to offer students the opportunity to conduct research on these topics free of charge, and to develop our own ideas and solutions—thereby fostering knowledge exchange in areas such as human space exploration, disaster and crisis relief, or local food supply.

entityDescription:
Philip Jackson is an independent researcher, aerospace systems innovator, and former Commissioned Aerospace Battle Manager Officer in the Royal Air Force (RAF), having completed rigorous leadership and operational officer training at RAF Cranwell. Bringing a diverse blend of operational command experience, technical quality assurance, and a foundational background in the physical sciences, he specializes in synthesizing complex system architectures for deep-space applications.
His technical and academic foundation includes advanced coursework via MITx in Astronautical Engineering and Human Space Flight, alongside a strong background in physical sciences (A-Levels in Physics and Chemistry). This theoretical grounding is reinforced by extensive professional expertise in industrial quality assurance and process optimization. Notably, during his tenure at Sigma Aldrich, he managed complex technical responsibilities involving MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry, held ISO 9001 auditing credentials, and utilized Six Sigma methodologies to drive rigorous process improvements.
Currently based in Valencia, Spain, where he balances educational management with advanced technical design, Jackson leverages his unique cross-disciplinary background—spanning tactical aerospace operations, strict industrial quality standards, and orbital mechanics modeling—to develop novel, scalable solutions for space domain awareness and planetary protection. Project HELIOS-3 represents the culmination of this expertise, bridging tactical command oversight with cutting-edge deep-space logistics.

entityDescription:
Polimak Space S.A. is a Luxembourg-based company founded by seasoned space-technology and material-handling experts. By transposing decades of terrestrial material handling and conveying technology experience into the space sector, we develop solutions for the efficient and safe handling of regolith. Our patented Modular Drum Conveyor (MDC) and vertical conveying technologies are designed to operate reliably on the lunar surface, integrated into rovers, landers, and regolith processing units to enable end-to-end ISRU operations.

Our core technology is defined by a mechanical approach that is intentionally simple yet highly efficient and powerful. Unlike complex alternatives, our systems are inherently scalable and require extremely low maintenance, making them the ideal technology to engage in rigorous, long-term ISRU (In-Situ Resource Utilization) activities. By prioritizing mechanical reliability, Polimak Space provides the robust infrastructure necessary to bridge the gap between lunar excavation and resource processing.

A defining feature of our system is its modular component architecture, which allows for the seamless integration of:
- Sensors and Monitoring: For real-time data on material flow and composition.

- Sieving and Mixing Technologies: Enabling the precise preconditioning and beneficiation of regolith.

- Stockpiling and Delivery: Facilitating organized storage and transport for construction or thermal energy storage.

By prioritizing mechanical reliability and modularity, Polimak Space provides the robust infrastructure necessary for regolith beneficiation—a critical step in converting raw lunar soil into usable resources—bridging the gap between excavation and final processing.

Municipality of the City of Budapest (Budapest Főváros Önkormányzata) is a public body, representing Budapest which is the capital and the largest city of Hungary. Budapest is the country’s principal political, cultural, commercial, industrial, and transportation centre. The city covers an area of 525 square km and is home to 1,736 million people. The city is situated along the Danube, in the heart of the Carpathian basin.
Budapest consists of twenty-three districts. The Hungarian capital city has a particular dual self-government system. This means that in addition to the Budapest Municipality, the local government of Budapest, each of the twenty-three districts have their own government, the so-called district governments, with elected mayors and a body of representatives. Both the City and the Districts are local governments, not subordinated to one another, each having specific duties and powers, specified by law.

QSA Technology B.V. is a Dutch deep‑tech start‑up developing photonic Physical Unclonable Function (PUF) technology for quantum‑secure authentication in optical communication systems. The company focuses on creating hardware‑rooted security primitives that provide high‑entropy, tamper‑resistant authentication suitable for telecom operators, defense applications, and quantum‑resilient network infrastructures.
QSA’s technology is based on proprietary photonic structures that generate unique, unclonable optical responses, enabling secure authentication without relying on classical cryptographic secrets. This approach provides resilience against quantum attacks and aligns with emerging requirements for secure optical networks. The company is currently advancing its technology through pilot engagements with telecom and defense stakeholders and preparing for integration into larger European programmes.

entityDescription: The Landbanking Group is a Munich-based nature fintech company on a mission to stop and reverse nature loss by making nature investable: turning it from a cost into an asset class.⁠ ⁠Founded in 2022, the company is building the infrastructure for an economy indexed on nature, grounded in the conviction that nature is humanity's most critical infrastructure and must be visible, valued, and integrated into business and investment decisions.⁠ Its core product, Landler (landler.io), is the world's first end-to-end natural capital management platform: it fuses satellite remote sensing, in-field measurements (eDNA, bioacoustics, soil) and process-based and ML models into nature condition scores and natural capital accounts at fine spatial resolution, measuring outcomes across biodiversity, carbon, water, and soil.⁠ Builging on top of these MRV layers, The Landbanking Group develops economic models of risk and resilience and facilitates various financial investment pathways.⁠

entityDescription: Retrüv Ltd is an early-stage UK company (SIC 62012) building a provenance, authentication and regulatory-compliance platform based on Digital Product Passports. The platform captures verified evidence of a product's origin, materials and chain of custody, binds it to the physical item through NFC authentication (NTAG 424 DNA) and GS1 Digital Link identifiers, and anchors it in a signed, append-only transparency log so that provenance becomes independently verifiable rather than self-declared. It spans seven modules covering origin and supplier intelligence, marking, secure record-keeping, authentication, ownership, resale and regulatory intelligence. Retrüv addresses the verification and due-diligence obligations created by EU regulation, including the ESPR/Digital Product Passport framework, the Deforestation Regulation and corporate sustainability due diligence, anchored initially in premium fashion and extending across natural-fibre and agricultural-commodity supply chains.

entityDescription:
Nexus Dynamix is a deep-tech company specializing in microgravity simulation hardware, automated real-time control software, and terrestrial microgravity environment replication. The company's core technology platform, AstroPod, is a patented, high-precision mechatronic instrument designed to provide on-demand, sustained low-gravity environments (<0.008g) within standard laboratory workflows.
Unlike conventional analog clinostats that rely on blind, continuous rotation (introducing disruptive fluid shear stresses that damage crystal formation) our technology employs an AI-driven, multi-axis active nullification system. By utilizing custom real-time sensor loops and precision motion platforms, the platform dynamically maps local ambient gravity fields and cancels acceleration vectors. This active intervention delivers a motionless, highly stable space-grade physical environment on Earth with zero destructive vibrations.
The entity operates at a demonstrated Technology Readiness Level of TRL 7, backed by multiple filed US provisional patent applications covering both the physical hardware mechanics and the environmental simulation control loops. Nexus Dynamix actively develops advanced mechatronics, predictive simulation frameworks (digital twins), and material gravity-response datasets. Our primary objectives within the European Space Agency ecosystem are to expand downstream application capabilities, advance our digital twin modeling toward true orbital-range microgravity performance (<0.001g), and collaborate with aerospace partners on high-value crystal growth, structural biology, and advanced materials initiatives.

entityDescription:
The Particle Therapy Research Center (PARTREC) offers beamtime on its advanced cyclotron facility to support research, testing, and development for both science and industry. With ion beams ranging from protons to oxygen and energies up to 190 MeV for protons and 90 MeV per nucleon for helium to oxygen, PARTREC provides a unique platform for a wide range of applications.

In addition to facilitating external research, PARTREC is embedded within the UMCG Departments of Radiation Oncology and Biomedical Sciences. The facility focuses on experimental research in radiation physics and biology, aiming to advance radiotherapy techniques and explore the use of proton and ion beams for cancer treatment. The cyclotron also plays a key role in nuclear chemistry studies conducted by the University of Groningen and supports radiation hardness testing for industrial applications. A team of 25 FTE technical staff ensures expert support for designing, building, and operating experimental setups.

entityDescription:
Endelevu OÜ is an Estonian research and technology company developing satellite-based Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) solutions for afforestation and reforestation carbon projects in sub-Saharan Africa.
The company processes ESA Copernicus Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellite data through a proprietary algorithm stack built specifically for East African ecological conditions — addressing the persistent cloud cover, bi-modal growing seasons, and smallholder parcel scales that make standard global monitoring tools unreliable in the region. The intended output is audit-ready compliance documentation aligned with Verra's VM0047 ARR carbon methodology, enabling project developers and landowners to meet regulatory verification requirements through satellite-derived data rather than costly field surveys.
Endelevu's pipeline integrates cloud-penetrating SAR monitoring, multispectral optical analysis, and AI-based land cover classification into a single automated workflow — from raw satellite data to formatted compliance document. The service targets individual project developers, carbon aggregators, and Verra-accredited Verification and Validation Bodies operating across Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, and Tanzania, with planned expansion to wider sub-Saharan Africa and South America.
The founding team combines first-hand operational experience in East Africa, satellite Earth Observation engineering, and research-grade machine learning expertise. Endelevu OÜ was incorporated in October 2025 and is registered in the Estonian Business Register under number 17343299.

entityName: Johann Heinrich von Thünen Institute - Thünen Institute of Forest Ecosystems
entityDescription:
The Thünen Institute of Forest Ecosystems is a federal research body under the German Federal Ministry of Food and Agriculture. Located in Eberswalde, it conducts ecological research to develop sustainable strategies for forest management, climate protection, and nature conservation. The institute's activities are divided into four main areas:
Forest Resources & Climate Protection: Uses remote sensing and the National Forest Inventory to model forest development and report on forests' contribution to carbon storage and renewable resources.
Soil Protection & Forest Health: Monitors forest soils and vitality to understand risks, particularly how changing environments and pollution affect tree health.
Forest Ecology & Biodiversity: Measures material and energy flows to analyze the resilience and adaptability of forest ecosystems.
Wildlife Ecology: Studies the intersection and balance between forest management and game / wildlife populations.
Additionally, the institute houses the International Cooperative Programme (ICP Forests) Programme Coordinating Centre to monitor forest conditions across Europe.

Reference engagements include national-scale crop monitoring and procurement validation systems, forest parcel administration platforms, and land rights titling programs serving government and multinational clients. entityDescription:
The Institute for European Energy and Climate Policy (IEECP) is a non-for-profit, independent research organisation. We act as a knowledge-hub sharing pragmatic results as well as innovative ideas providing policymakers, and all private and public decision-makers, independent expertise and science-based research to support their work towards the energy transition and a sustainable future.
Founded in 2015, IEECP’s international interdisciplinary team of experts has grown progressively to reach 36 persons by 2024, working on science-based climate change mitigation, energy efficiency and renewable energy policy, generating and disseminating scientific knowledge, and proposing data-driven solutions, hands-on solutions and policy recommendations as well as strategic communication.
IEECP has a rich experience in managing EU, climate action and energy transition projects, primarily within EU-funded programmes (previously Horizon 2020 and now LIFE and Horizon Europe). Since 2015, IEECP has been coordinator of 25 EU-funded projects, and partner of further 41 projects.
Most of the projects are related to the energy efficiency field: cross-cutting energy efficiency policies (e.g. EEOS – Energy Efficiency Obligation Schemes), energy efficiency financing and energy efficiency in companies, energy performance of buildings, behavioural changes. Part of these projects have a focus on tackling energy poverty and supporting vulnerable households. All these projects are strongly related to the implementation of the EU Directives in the field, especially the EED and EPBD, and support experience sharing among Member States to improve national policies. Another part of our projects deal with local action for climate and energy, for integrated approaches addressing climate mitigation and adaptation.
Our roles in these projects included policy review and benchmarking, data analysis, preparing policy briefs and recommendations, developing tools and libraries of resources, leading capacity building and training programmes. In addition, we have been leading the Work Packages for stakeholder engagement, and for communication and dissemination in many of these projects.
The IEECP team is multidisciplinary, with backgrounds in policy analysis, economics, engineering, and social and communication sciences. While being a Dutch-based foundation, IEECP experts are based all over Europe, in Belgium, Croatia, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Portugal, the Netherlands and the UK. The team is highly multicultural, speaking more than 20 languages, and pays particular attention to gender equality, diversity and inclusivity, both in the organisation and in its work.
IEECP experts are also actively involved in the expert and scientific communities. For example, Vlasis Oikonomou and Jean-Sébastien Broc were guest editors of a special issue on Energy Efficiency First of theEnergy Efficiencyjournal (Springer ed.) and are reviewers for several scientific journals of Elsevier (Energy,Energy Policy,Energy Economics,Smart Energy,Energy Research & Social Science,Journal of Cleaner Production) and Springer (Energy Efficiency,Journal of Government and Policy,Mitigation and Adaptation Strategies for Global Change). They also have been panel leaders for the ECEEE (European Council for an Energy Efficient Economy) Summer Study. Jean-Sébastien is also a board member of the Energy Evaluation association (formerly IEPPEC), and has been co-chair of the IEPPEC conference in 2014 and 2016. Ivana Rogulj has been member of the Steering Committee of the Covenant of Companies for Climate and Energy, and of EEFIG (Energy Efficiency Financial Institutions Group). Giulia Pizzini is board member of ECEEE (European Council for an Energy Efficient Economy).
