description:
Vimotek — Controlled spacecraft encounters from validation to orbit
Vimotek is a European space technology company helping mission teams turn spacecraft encounters into controlled, predictable outcomes.
As orbital density increases and proximity operations become more central to future missions, operators need to validate encounter logic before flight, execute rendezvous and close-proximity operations in orbit, and assess uncertain proximity behaviour with confidence.
Vimotek builds productised capabilities across two complementary domains: mission-specific digital twins for simulation and validation, and onboard sensing and perception.
Orbittwin — digital twin platform and mission environment for modelling, validation, rehearsal and operational decision support.
Navcam — RPO system for onboard target acquisition, tracking and characterisation during mission encounters.
Sentinel — SSA system for onboard detection, monitoring and assessment of nearby objects and anomalous proximity behaviour.
Together, these products help mission teams reduce encounter risk across development, assurance, operations and asset resilience.
Vimotek works with commercial, institutional and programme partners to support safer, more predictable spacecraft operations.

entityDescription:
Prometheus Plasma Systems S.r.l. is a deep-tech company developing a novel plasma-based configuration that merges the functional capabilities of turbomachinery with the extreme, controllable conditions enabled by plasma physics. This configuration forms the basis of a broad, modular technological platform applicable across high-vacuum systems, plasma processing, advanced radiation sources, electric space propulsion, and—longer term—nuclear fusion technologies.
Rather than addressing a single product category, Prometheus Plasma Systems (PPS) targets a class of systemic limitations shared by many advanced industries: the difficulty of operating reliably, efficiently, and economically in extreme environments where conventional mechanical, electromagnetic, or thermal solutions face intrinsic constraints. These limitations appear in different forms across sectors—mechanical wear and contamination in vacuum systems, power-supply inefficiencies in plasma propulsion, lack of flexible and affordable plasma diagnostics, and escalating complexity and cost in fusion reactor concepts—but stem from a common root: architectures that are not designed to fully exploit plasma as an active, controllable medium.
PPS aims to address structural inefficiencies in two high-value sectors: industrial turbomachinery—where system complexity, high capital costs, and intensive maintenance constrain growth—and plasma and nuclear fusion technologies, where over-engineered architectures and extreme costs confine applications largely to research environments.
Our mission is to introduce a new class of turbomachines that operate with plasma as the working fluid and eliminate mechanical power transfer entirely. By replacing rotating and mechanically coupled components with electromagnetic energy transfer systems, PPS removes all moving parts from the core architecture. The result is a fundamentally simpler, modular, and stackable platform with significantly reduced mechanical wear, lower maintenance requirements, enhanced scalability and lower costs.
This no-moving-part turbomachinery approach unlocks a whole new paradigm in high-performance fluid systems, enabling broader industrial adoption through improved reliability, lower lifecycle costs, and adaptable integration across multiple advanced technology sectors.

entityDescription:
Serenity Corporation is a French SAS founded in 2024, headquartered in Cannes, specializing in the design, manufacture, and commercialization of autonomous Atmospheric Water Generators (AWGs). These eco-designed, modular systems extract humidity from the air to produce pure drinking water, without relying on public infrastructure, piping, or plastic distribution.
Serenity offers a product range from S10 to custom industrial models (up to 10,000 L/day), with configurations adapted for indoor, outdoor, and extreme environments. Each unit follows a five-stage process—capturing, condensing, filtering, disinfecting (UV), and mineralizing water.
The company’s innovation lies in its dual-use approach:
Terrestrial: Providing decentralized, sustainable water solutions to hotels, eco-lodges, coworking spaces, municipalities, and NGOs.

Space: Adapting AWG systems for closed-loop space habitats and developing AI-powered climate forecasting software integrating Copernicus satellite data with local sensor networks.

Serenity also delivers Serenity Care subscription services, IoT modules, maintenance, and leasing. Backed by BFTE funding and in application for ESA BIC Sud France, Serenity collaborates with partners such as INPHYNI (CNRS/UCA), IMREDD, Somanity, Hautier IP, and Spartan Space to advance R&D, industrialization, and intellectual property protection.

entityName: Hamburg University of Technology - Smart Sensors Group
entityDescription:
The Smart Sensors Group at the Hamburg University of Technology (TUHH) specializes in the development of resource-efficient digital systems for use under extreme conditions. The Smart Sensors Group’s general research focuses on digital data and signal processing on smart sensors, real-time data processing, energy-efficient processing, as well as reliability, fault tolerance, and embedded fault diagnosis, with numerous previous projects demonstrating expertise in these areas (PotatoNet, REAP, INGA, 5GSatOpt, TRIPLE-nanoAUV/TRIPLE-MoDo). Furthermore, the group has more than 10 years of experience in research on the energy efficiency of embedded systems, enabling energy-autonomous operation of sensor systems through low-power processing strategies in both hardware and software.
A key application focus of the Smart Sensors Group’s research lies in the field of sensors under space conditions as well as space electronics, where extremely high reliability is required. In the ongoing space projects AuRelia and SArES, funded by the DLR and BMFTR, methods for the autonomous yet reliable operation of an SCG sensor under space conditions are currently being researched and developed, complemented by the SatelLight project for intra-satellite communication using LiFi. As part of the EduSat project, a CubeSat is currently being developed in collaboration with students as part of a teaching and research initiative.
The Smart Sensors Group is currently involved in numerous IOV missions, including the MAPHEUS-15 campaign and the development of a payload for the DLR satellites PLUTO I and PLUTO II.

TUHH: The Hamburg University of Technology (TUHH) is a public university in Hamburg and is one of the youngest technical universities in Germany. It was founded in 1978.

As part of the EduSat project, a CubeSat is currently being developed in collaboration with students as part of a teaching and research initiative.

S.A.F.E. is a Belgian company that offers end-to-end solutions to help its customers transform complex challenges into resilient solutions. We help you protect your people, data and operations by delivering integrated consultancy, expert training and engineered solutions that safeguard your organisation from modern, emerging threats. With turnkey solutions and a commitment to uncompromising resilience, we help our clients operate with confidence in an increasingly complex world.
The result: hardened facilities, prepared teams, and secure systems capable of withstanding physical, cyber and electromagnetic threats.
Our solutions
Infrastructure Security: Security by Design
a. Design, Build & Maintain: integration of layered security mechanisms throughout the planning, design, construction and maintenance process. A holistic and cost-effective approach that integrates physical barriers and electronic systems for resilient protection, based on the deter – detect – delay – respond methodology.
b. Site audits: analysing and evaluating the effectiveness of the site security system. Where necessary, proposing improvements to mitigate vulnerabilities.
c. Physical penetration testing: identifying vulnerabilities in the site security system using intrusion and social engineering techniques.
Our expertise includes physical barriers, hostile vehicle mitigation, explosion and intrusion resistance, anti-espionage measures, electronic security systems, drone and anti-drone measures, electromagnetic and radio-frequency shielding (TEMPEST), operational control and crisis training rooms, and redundancy.
Secure Operations Support
a. Security accreditation support (SAA/NSA) for FSC, PSC, physical and CIS environments
b. EMI/RFI shielded solutions (Faraday cages)
c. TEMPEST and rugged IT equipment
d. Secure wireless connections
e. Burglary-resistant infrastructure/secure storage & safes
f. Control/operational/crisis/training room solutions
g. R&D of new EMI/RFI and EW solutions
Training & Consultancy
a. Resilience: building structured and compliant resilience, business continuity and crisis management.
b. Security & Emergency services: expat and travel risk management (Duty of Care).
c. Training Capability Development: Plan, prepare, execute and evaluate exercises and training courses.

entityDescription:
Euphyia Tech Ltd is a Cyprus-based technology company specialising in digital solutions for smarter, more sustainable and future-ready buildings. Established as a spin-off of Frederick University and Frederick Research Center, Euphyia develops cloud-based tools that support the assessment, benchmarking and improvement of building performance, with a focus on smart readiness, lifecycle sustainability, building intelligence and digital visualisation.
The company’s product ecosystem includes Smart Ready Go!, a platform for Smart Readiness Indicator assessment and improvement planning; EcoHestia, a lifecycle environmental assessment platform for buildings; and Smart BEAR, a smartness assessment and VR-based visualisation platform. Euphyia combines building physics, sustainability assessment, BIM/IFC integration, data analytics and software engineering to transform advanced research methodologies into practical, market-ready digital services.
For ESA-related activities, Euphyia is interested in developing space-enabled services that use Earth observation and satellite-derived data to support climate-neutral, smart and resilient buildings. Relevant areas include building renovation prioritisation, urban climate resilience mapping, cooling demand and summer energy poverty observatories, renewable energy and heat-pump suitability mapping, embodied carbon monitoring, and digital twins enriched with space-based environmental data.
Euphyia seeks collaboration with partners active in Earth observation, satellite data processing, urban analytics, climate services, municipalities, energy agencies and building-sector innovation.

The Fraunhofer Institute for Large Structures in Production Engineering IGP in Rostock focuses on tasks in the field of production and manufacturing of large structures.
On the basis of applied research, concepts for product and process innovations are developed and realised for many future-oriented branches of the economy such as shipbuilding and steel construction, energy and environmental technology, rail and commercial vehicle construction as well as mechanical and plant engineering within the framework of research and development projects with our cooperation partners.

Within the framework of a cooperation agreement, the Fraunhofer IGP works closely with the chairs of production engineering and joining technology of the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Marine Technology at the University of Rostock and is a member of the Fraunhofer Transportation Alliance, the Fraunhofer Group for Production and various research associations and networks.

Since 2005, more than 4000 square meters of laboratory and office space has been created in three construction phases at the Rostock site in order to be able to offer industry tailor-made services for engineering tasks.

GreenX S.r.l. is an Italian early-stage technology company developing VeriCarbon®, a hardware-based decarbonisation meter designed to measure, authenticate, and certify avoided CO₂ emissions linked to renewable energy generation. The company combines secure edge hardware, trusted data capture, cryptographic attestation, and distributed digital infrastructure to create tamVeriCarbon® integrates three verification layers into a single system: direct physical measurement of electrical output at the point of generation, authenticated positioning and timing through Galileo OSNMA, and environmental cross-verification based on Copernicus and ECMWF data sources. Each attestation is signed through secure hardware and recorded on GreenX’s distributed ledger, enabling a trusted audit trail designed to reduce fraud risk and improve the reliability of emissions-related data.

entityDescription: TRACK Technologies UG (haftungsbeschränkt), founded in 2025 and based in Darmstadt, Germany, develops an integrated outdoor safety and positioning platform. The system combines a mobile application, a wearable device and a backend infrastructure to deliver high-precision positioning, automated safety functions and offline reliability in demanding outdoor environments. The platform integrates Galileo High Accuracy Service (HAS) to provide sub-metre positioning and predictive location estimation in case of signal degradation. A proprietary algorithm for alpine and high-dynamic environments enables trajectory modelling and proactive risk assessment beyond conventional GNSS-based systems. Target applications include endurance sports events, alpine activities and remote outdoor operations, with customers among event organisers, tourism stakeholders and safety-relevant institutions. The company is incubated at ESA BIC Hessen & Baden-Württemberg (Darmstadt site, operated by cesah GmbH), co-located with ESA's European Space Operations Centre (ESOC).

Core-Vision excels in low-volume, high-complexity projects requiring advanced real-time processing, high-speed digital design and tightly integrated hardware-software architectures. With experience in high-reliability environments, the company applies structured engineering methodologies and rigorous validation processes to deliver robust and performance-driven solutions.

entityName: SYCONS Tanácsadó, épitőipari fővállalkozó, kivitelező és tervező Korlátolt Felelősségü Társaság
entityDescription:
SYCONS Kft. was founded in 1990 by private persons, and is in 100% Hungarian ownership until this day. In the beginning, our activities consisted of trenchless utility construction, technical consulting for ground surface stabilization projects, and application of state-of-the-art trenchless (No-Dig) utility rehabilitation technologies mainly abroad (Kuwait, Libya).
Today our company is a key actor of the underground construction industry in Hungary. We offer complex solutions of utility construction, environment protection, specialized underground works, earthworks and road construction works to our Partners.
Thanks to the long years of experiences of our colleagues, we are able to offer services of the highest level to our clients. From the beginning, we continuously develop our know-how and equipment, and we continuously seek new, innovative underground construction solutions, based on old, well-proven technologies.
Our patented deep drilled drainage system construction technology offers a unique solution since March 2001 for the stabilization of loose, dangerous embankments or other ground surface movements.
One of our most important references is the construction of METRO line 4, where we performed protective layer stabilizations using one our new technologies, the soil anchoring, combined with an old technology (pipe jacking).
Our second patent has been developed in 2015: this is the construction technology of drainpipe installation by high-precision (in cm) directional drilling in great depth, in high lengths.
We are proud to be known by our partners as a company being able to offer technical solutions even when others considers the task insoluble.
 
Our objective:
- Complete execution of complex, big projects, in continuous contact with the client.
- Identification of the best technical/economical solution for underground construction tasks to be executed by investors, designers or municipalities, that often seem insoluble using traditional technologies.
- Participation in the solution of a given task or problem, even already in design phase. 
- Elaboration of complete solutions in collaboration with our partners, using our professional experiences.
- Flexible and economic execution of our projects in perfect quality.
Our company, as a company executing underground construction works, attaches importance to be member of different professional organizations, and to support them by our professional experiences and financial aids.
We participate in the activities of the following organizations: 
- HSTT - Hungarian Society for Trenchless Technologies
- Association of Hungarian Water Well Drillers
 
We are active participants of the following conference series, even as lecturers: 
- Geotechnical conferences
- Geological sources of danger - conferences
- NO-DIG conferences
 
Other organizations, of which our colleagues are members:
- Hungarian Chamber of Engineers
- Hungarian Society of Hydrology
Furthermore, we attach a particular importance to professionally and financially support the professional activities of the educational institutions.
In the last years, we supported the activities of the below listed institutions and organizations:
- Budapest University of Technology and Economics

entityDescription:
Noah's Ark Quantum Tech Lab is the research and innovation engine behindNoah's Ark Technology Digital Solidarity— an initiative dedicated to harnessing cutting-edge technologies to bridge the digital divide and promote digital solidarity globally.
Born from a deep conviction thatthe boundaries of conventional science are not walls, but doors, our laboratory stands at the convergence of quantum research, artificial intelligence, and human-centered innovation.
Founded by Noah Kouadri Khazar
Our Mission
We integrateartificial intelligence, quantum computing, simulation, and advanced physicsto improve the living conditions of underrepresented communities and enhance resilience in the face of global challenges.
Our work is particularly focused on:
- Education— democratizing access to knowledge through digital tools
- Digital Health— leveraging technology to serve communities left behind
- Social Innovation— designing solutions that address real-world inequalities
 

What We Do
⚛️ Noah Ark Core — Quantum Technology at the Service of Humanity
A groundbreaking quantum technology project combining advanced quantum computing principles with energy efficiency models to revolutionize resource management and sustainability.
 
 Quantum Research for Global Challenges
Exploring the potential of quantum computing to solve complex global problems — from optimizing resource distribution to modeling climate dynamics and securing critical infrastructures.
 
 Secure Quantum Networks
Developing unbreakable next-generation communication infrastructures through quantum entanglement and superposition.
 
 Dark Matter & Advanced Gravitational Research
Studying dark matter as a potential technological lever — exploring its gravitational properties to unlock applications in advanced space propulsion and field manipulation.
 
️ Space Exploration & Human Resilience
Making humanity multi-planetary through propulsion and gravitational research — not out of necessity, but out of a vocation for exploration and resilience.

entityDescription:
ADENERA is a technology company based in Slovenia, specialising in the application of Earth Observation data and artificial intelligence to electricity grid operations. The company develops data-driven services that give electricity distribution operators and other energy-sector actors improved visibility of distributed generation and consumption patterns across their networks. Its core technology combines satellite observation, weather modelling, and machine learning to derive operational insight at network scale, without requiring additional on-site measurement infrastructure. The services are delivered digitally and are designed to integrate with the operational and planning systems already used by network operators.

ADENERA's team brings together competences in electricity grid operations, network planning, and energy market regulation, alongside AI and data engineering and the commercialisation of technology-based services. The company operates at the intersection of space-based data and energy infrastructure, addressing the growing need for scalable, non-intrusive solutions that support the management of rapidly expanding distributed renewable generation in Europe and beyond. The company was founded as a spin-off of Abelium d. o. o., a Slovenian data science and AI firm with established experience in system architecture, machine learning model development, and analytics for the energy sector, in order to commercialise services developed under the ESA ARTES 4.0 Downstream Applications programme.

entityDescription:
ColliMate Space R&D S.L. is a space technology company developing AI-driven software to optimize satellite communications and data transport across space and ground networks. The company’s core platform enables autonomous, real-time orchestration of data flows, improving latency, reliability, and cost efficiency in increasingly congested and dynamic space environments. By combining physics-based models with machine learning, ColliMate Space enhances decision-making for satellite operators, ground station providers, and government users.
A key aspect of the platform is its capability to process and leverage signal intelligence (SIGINT) and RF data to improve situational awareness and optimize communication strategies. Its technology addresses critical bottlenecks in space data delivery, enabling faster access to time-sensitive information for applications such as Earth observation, defense, and emergency response.

In addition, the company develops capabilities aligned with Delay/Disruption Tolerant Networking (DTN) and next-generation communication protocols to enable resilient data transport across LEO, cislunar, and deep space environments. These capabilities support operations over heterogeneous and intermittently connected networks, enabling adaptive routing, scheduling, and resource allocation under dynamic link conditions, interference, and environmental constraints.

entityDescription:
dataHEARD is a Geneva-based non-profit association dedicated to transforming fragmented health and environmental data into integrated, actionable systems. At a time of shrinking aid and eroding institutional knowledge, we fill a critical gap of connecting governments, communities, researchers, and innovators to build lasting data capacity where it is needed most. 

We work across four pillars: collaboration and advocacy, capacity building, innovation and technology, and research and monitoring services. Through technical assistance, south-to-south learning, and responsible use of digital innovation, we empower low- and middle-income countries to make evidence-based decisions that strengthen resilience, inform policy, and drive sustainable impact. Based at the heart of global decision-making in Geneva, we operate across borders to ensure that every relevant insight is counted and heard.
Our vision is simple: a future where every country and community owns its data and uses it to thrive.

DI Industrial is a Czech-based engineering and manufacturing company specializing in the production of high-precision components, sub-assemblies, and complete systems for demanding high-tech industries. Founded in 1994, the company builds on a strong legacy of advanced engineering and precision manufacturing. 
The core expertise of DI Industrial lies in delivering complex, customer-specific solutions, particularly for applications in electron microscopy, vacuum technology, and cryogenics. 
The company provides a comprehensive “one-stop-shop” capability covering the full production cycle:
High-precision CNC and conventional machining (turning, milling, grinding) 
Advanced welding and brazing, including electron beam welding and vacuum brazing 
Surface treatments (anodizing, plating, special coatings) 
Clean-room assembly of mechanical and electromechanical systems 
Testing and metrology, including 3D measurement and helium leak testing for vacuum-tight components 
Heat treatment, laser marking, and ultrasonic cleaning 
DI Industrial is particularly strong in manufacturing components that require:
ultra-high precision 
excellent surface quality 
vacuum compatibility and cleanliness 
The company operates under certified quality systems, including ISO 9001 and EN 9100 (aerospace standard), ensuring reliability for critical applications. 
With a highly skilled workforce and integrated technologies under one roof, DI Industrial acts not only as a manufacturer but also as an engineering partner, supporting customers with design optimization and technological solutions to improve performance, cost-efficiency, and lead times

entityName: Max-Delbrück-Centrum für Molekulare Medizin in der Helmholtz-Gemeinschaft
entityDescription:
The Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine in the Helmholtz Association aims to transform tomorrow’s medicine through our discoveries of today. At locations in Berlin-Buch, Berlin-Mitte, Heidelberg and Mannheim, our researchers harness interdisciplinary collaboration to decipher the complexities of disease at the systems level – from molecules and cells to organs and the entire organism. Through academic, clinical, and industry partnerships, as well as global networks, we strive to translate biological discoveries into applications that enable the early detection of deviations from health, personalize treatment, and ultimately prevent disease. First founded in 1992, the Max Delbrück Center today inspires and nurtures a diverse talent pool of 1,800 people from over 70 countries. We are 90 percent funded by the German federal government and 10 percent by the state of Berlin.
The MDC was established by law (the MDC Act: https://gesetze.berlin.de/bsbe/document/jlr-MDCGBE2023rahmen).

entityDescription:
Finova Motors S.L. is a Madrid-registered, innovative startup specializing in the design and manufacture of hubless brushless DC (BLDC) outer-rotor electric motors and space-grade attitude-control actuators.
Founded in November 2023 by Dinesh Babu (PhD, Aerospace Engineering) and Pedro Miranda (MBA), the company develops proprietary hubless motor technology across two primary market segments: electric mobility and space systems. In the electric mobility segment, Finova designs and supplies 10-inch and 12-inch hubless BLDC outer-rotor motors for electric scooters and mopeds, with active customers in Spain and international markets. In the space segment, Finova is developing the Hubless Motor-based Control Moment Gyroscope (HM-CMG) and the Hubless Motor-based Reaction Wheel (HM-RW) as compact, high-torque-to-mass attitude-control actuators for small satellites in the 30 to 3,000 kg category.
The HM-CMG integrates a proprietary hubless outer-rotor BLDC spin motor directly with the flywheel, co-axially housing the nutation motor, hollow-through encoder, and hollow slip ring within the central bore of the spin motor assembly. This architecture eliminates the central shaft present in all conventional CMG designs, delivering up to 50% reduction in volume and mass for equivalent angular momentum output, with a scalable design that adjusts axial flywheel width without modifying the overall volumetric envelope.

Snowpack is a French start-up specializing in cybersecurity, a spin-off from CEA, created in 2021. It was awarded the I-lab 2022 prize, supported by the Cyber Acceleration Strategy, DeepNum20, and won the Grand Prix of the Startup Forum InCyber 2024.
Snowpack develops the VIPN (Virtual & Invisible Private Network) technology – highly innovative and patented – which makes users, data, information system components, and web services exposed on the Internet invisible, eliminating any need for trust in the infrastructure.
Snowpack VIPN thus protects against numerous network attacks, such as surveillance and interception of communications, external scanning of the information system, and exploitation of vulnerabilities in components or services exposed on the Internet. It significantly reduces the external attack surface of organizations by making it invisible and effectively acts as a layer of independence between the infrastructure and the data.
Our technology offers unique properties in terms of cybersecurity and eliminates any need for trust in the Internet infrastructure (i.e., hardware, software, encryption layers, and even Snowpack…).

entityName: RWTH AACHEN UNIVERSITY - Welding and Joining Institute - ISF
entityDescription:
For more than 70 years the Welding and Joining Institute, ISF, of RWTH Aachen University has been doing research work about modern welding and joining technologies. The work of the ISF comprises almost all industrially relevant, non-detachable joining methods. Those methods include the arc joining methods with their modern process variations, the entire spectrum of the electron and laser beam welding methods, resistance and friction welding processes and also adhesive bonding. In connection, also work about the processing of modern materials with welding methods, about automation and mechanisation, process simulation and also about occupational safety and environmental protection is carried out.
Besides fundamental process analyses which are carried out within the scope of the above-mentioned fields, main emphasis is put on the application-oriented implementation of the gained results into advancement and further development of joining technologies for innovative material and structural design. Within the scope of our scientific work, great importance is placed on the direct industrial cooperation, reaching from smaller projects up to long-term development cooperation.

entityName: UNIV FEDERICO II - Department of Industrial Engineering
entityDescription:
The Department of Industrial Engineering (DII) of the University of Naples Federico II was established on January 1, 2013, inheriting the scientific and educational legacy of five historic departments: Energetics, Applied Thermofluid Dynamics and Environmental Conditioning (DETEC), Aerospace Engineering (DIAS), Management and Industrial Engineering (DIEG), Naval Engineering (DIN), and Mechanical and Energetics Engineering (DiME). Today, the DII is recognized as a center of excellence at both national and international levels, active in the fields of education, scientific research, technology transfer, and the third mission initiatives. The DII operates with a strong multidisciplinary approach and a clear focus on contemporary challenges, such as energy transition and sustainable mobility, which are also central themes in the “Department of Excellence 2023–2027” project.

Consistent with its scientific and educational mission, the DII pursues its strategy along the following key directions: Training highly qualified professionals in the fields of Industrial Engineering, with strong integration into the job market; Promoting and advancing scientific research and its international reach; Supporting technology transfer and innovation, including through the creation of spin-offs; Strengthening partnerships with national and international industrial sectors; • Promoting the internationalization of education and research; Reinforcing inclusion, gender equality, and active student engagement.
The Department’s research activities cover numerous areas, reflecting the breadth and multidisciplinarity of its expertise. entityDescription:
The Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières, a member of the Université du Québec network, was created on March 19, 1969 with the integration of the Centre d'études universitaires de Trois-Rivières and the École normale d'état Maurice-L.-Duplessis. The founding rector of the UQTR was Gilles Boulet, a leading figure in regional development.

Located on a campus of almost 59 hectares, and initially housed in buildings that had belonged to the Séminaire Saint-Antoine, run by the Franciscans, the UQTR developed in the heart of the modern part of the city of Trois-Rivières. The physical environment it occupies offers an interesting feature with its rugged topography, the result of a morphological history dating back some 10,000 years.

In 1973, the first educational building to be erected under the aegis of the Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières saw the light of day. This was the Ringuet Pavilion. The construction of new buildings continued over the years, in step with the growth of the clientele and the emergence of new needs.

Today, the UQTR campus comprises more than fifteen buildings, welcoming nearly 14,500 students every year, more than half of whom come from other regions of Quebec. The UQTR also has a campus in Drummondville, as well as eight off-campus university centers.

The Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières has a distinct personality. Accessible and lively, it opens its doors to a world of knowledge and challenges. Its medium-sized size, deep roots in the community and openness to the world make UQTR a great place to study. It offers 289 training programs at all three levels of study and, since its creation, has awarded over 98,000 diplomas to nearly 79,000 graduates.

At Embed Rover Sp z o.o., our vision is simple to Make IT Simple. We help companies work smarter by offering a EMBRA - a pre-configured, scalable platform based on affordable hardware like Raspberry Pi and LabJack DAQ. Instead of repeatedly building support environments from scratch, businesses can now plug in our solution and start working on developing their products, accelerating development cycles and cutting costs.

During our years as an engineers, we noticed a recurring inefficiency: companies spend too much time setting up environments for development, testing, and simulation. While necessary, these tasks divert attention from the core objective — creating better products. This realization sparked the idea for EMBRA: a platform to automate and optimize these activities, allowing companies to focus on innovation.

Our goal is to provide products and services that support and simplify operations related to spacecraft or instrument simulations, such as so-called flat-sats. Potential users include all companies in the space sector that utilize software elements in their systems, primarily spacecraft/satellite integrators and subsystem/instrument providers.

entityDescription:
CloudZen Innovations is a Europe-based data engineering and software automation firm headquartered in Nuremberg, Bavaria, Germany. Established in 2024, the company specializes in designing customized digital solutions for businesses globally.
The firm operates as a one-stop engineering provider delivering enterprise-grade expertise across cloud migration, automation, security, and compliance. Its core competencies include data engineering, data mesh solutions, multi-cloud automation, DevSecOps implementation, data lake infrastructure, advanced data analytics, and machine learning model deployments.
With a team of over 60 professionals comprising data engineers, full-stack developers, designers, and AI and MLOps specialists, CloudZen has successfully delivered more than 50 tailored digital solutions across diverse industry sectors. The company emphasizes collaboration and pioneering research and development to create next-generation applications suited to evolving technological landscapes.
Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) Offerings:
CloudZen Innovations brings extensive multi-year expertise within the Siemens Teamcenter PLM ecosystem, with core team members possessing 15-18+ years of specialized experience. The company delivers comprehensive PLM solutions across multiple domains:
Simulation Data Management: Teamcenter simulation data management and Teamcenter SMW for managing engineering simulation assets.
CAD Data Management: Full integration and support for major CAD platforms including Siemens NX, Siemens Solid Edge, SolidWorks, and Catia, enabling seamless design data management across diverse engineering environments.
Application Lifecycle Management: Implementation of Siemens Polarion for requirements management, test management, and complete application lifecycle orchestration.
Production Solutions: Teamcenter Easyplan for production planning, Teamcenter-SAP integration capabilities, and Siemens Opcenter for manufacturing operations management.
Service Data Management: Teamcenter Service Lifecycle Management and Capital Asset Lifecycle Management for post-production service operations and asset management.
Analytics and Low-Code Platforms: Siemens MindSphere IoT platform integration and Siemens Mendix low-code application development for digital transformation initiatives.
The company has successfully implemented enterprise-scale PLM projects across the European region, delivering solutions including engineering change management, BOM/BOP management under change control, AR/VR-enabled electronic work instructions, PLM-ERP integration, configuration management, data migration, and DevOps deployment for PLM environments. CloudZen's certified PLM-Cloud-Data practitioners provide both offshore implementation capabilities and onshore workshop facilitation to support global client needs.
SAP Solutions:
CloudZen Innovations provides SAP expertise through its leadership team's deep knowledge in SAP ERP integration, particularly in Material Management and procurement domains. The company specializes in Teamcenter-SAP integration using T4S (Teamcenter for SAP) and T4EA (Teamcenter for Enterprise Applications), enabling bidirectional BOM synchronization between PLM and ERP systems. This includes configuration of multiple SAP version connections, data exchange automation, and seamless integration between product development and enterprise resource planning environments.

Baader Planetarium is a medium-sized enterprise with more than 50 years of experience in producing and installing observatories for ground based surveillance and observation with more than 600 observatory dome installations around the world ranging from 2m up to 8.5m in diameter, serving a multitude of applications for scientific use. 
Core competence lies in development, integration, installation and implementation of turnkey robotic and/or remote controlled ground observing stations with highly specialized individual technical solutions, to work under the hardest of environments, with installations in Antarctica (Dome Concordia -84°C) to high Arctic regions such as Svalbard (NyAalesund -45°C), Ellesmere Island (Eureka -60°C), in desert conditions with hermetic seals against dust and a number of high Alpine locations.
Additionally the company specializes in high end robotic telescopes for SLR, SSA and Site Testing as well as astrographs with apertures of up to one meter; telescope mounts with load capacity of up to 750kg; Echelle spectrographs featuring a resolution up to 20 000 lambda/delta lambda.
Our customers are Institutions, Universities, observatories and companies around the world, among them AWI (Alfred Wegener Institute for polar research); MPI (Max Planck Institution); University of Hamburg (PIST-Project Mallorca); Open University UK (PIRATE-COAST project Tenerife); European Southern Observatory; Ludwig Maximilian University Munich (Mt. Helicon’s sensing platform is designed for high-throughput applications including carbon-fibre prepreg, battery materials, and coated films, supporting improved process control, reduced scrap, and higher manufacturing consistency. Based in Oxford, Helicon works with industrial partners to validate scalable sensing solutions for advanced manufacturing.

description:
Astro42 (legal name: Wozify Engineering Group Kft) is a custom software development and contract R&D company operating at the intersection of software, AI and Space. We build web and mobile applications that serve as user interfaces to space-based assets, build ground segment operations, end-to-end Earth Observation applications, and we push the boundaries of what's possible with AI.
What we do 
We build custom software for the space sector, with a particular focus on applying AI and machine learning to space-domain problems. Our work spans the full stack from satellite-side algorithms and ground segment systems through to web and mobile interfaces for operators and end users. We are equally comfortable taking on R&D-heavy enabling studies and delivering production software for operational systems. 
Domains of experience 
We have hands-on project experience in Earth Observation, flight dynamics, space weather, satellite mission planning, ground segment operations, spacecraft thermal engineering, and 3D simulation of physical environments. On the AI side, we work across classical ML, deep learning for EO imagery, reinforcement learning for control problems, and generative AI for operator-facing tooling. 
Selected projects
Power System Expert Space Weather Service 
ESA enabling study, AO/1-12676/25/NL/AL/jxh, 2025-2026). Astro42 leads the AI feasibility component of a study analysing the technical and economic viability of a commercial space weather service for protecting electricity networks, aviation, and GNSS-dependent infrastructure. 

MELT-B (ESA) 
Analysis of nighttime IR satellite imagery to assess heat loss from buildings and inform energy-efficiency interventions at city scale.

LunaSpace
A SaaS platform that uses AI to automate mission operations for small satellite constellation operators, reducing operator workload as fleets scale. 

Reef Intelligence (with SensFish and ReefCircular) 
Satellite and AI-based monitoring of marine and coastal habitats, combining EO data with KPIs and interactive dashboards to surface risks like heat stress, turbidity changes, and salinity shifts.

Seagrass Monitoring (with SensFish and the Solway Firth Partnership) 
Satellite imagery and AI for tracking seagrass habitat health and recovery in Scottish coastal waters.

Space Needle (ESA technology transfer) 
Application of reaction-wheel stabilisation principles and reinforcement learning to vibration control in scanning tunnelling microscopes; a non-space commercialisation of space-derived control technology

ESA Rocketry Training Programme (2025-2026)
As consortium partner alongside UK industry partners and the University of Glasgow, Astro42 delivers the software, numerical methods, and AI/ML modules of a rocketry training programme for university students. Module content includes, for example, training students to land a simplified 1D rocket using reinforcement learning.

entityDescription:
Novotech is an Italian aerospace company founded in 1992 as a spin-off of the University of Naples “Federico II”, with consolidated expertise in the design, certification, and manufacturing of advanced composite structures for aerospace applications. The Company is specialized in automated composite manufacturing technologies such as AFP, RTM, PCM, and LRI, combined with advanced finite element simulations, structural testing, and the development of complex composite prototypes featuring variable thicknesses and intricate geometries. Starting from the end of 2014, Novotech has been identified by Syensquo (Cytec Solvay Group) as qualified laboratory for development and testing on new materials for AFP process and Resin Transfer Moulding (RTM) process. Novotech has proven capabilities in the design and manufacture of composite structures through low-cost, out-of-autoclave automated production processes and it relies on a team of highly qualified researchers and engineers for the development of advanced manufacturing methods, draping and formability studies, composite warpage prediction, and the production of complex composite prototypes.
Novotech is a key partner for many industries working in the aerospace field and other advanced technology sectors and in order to keep high competitiveness on the market it has developed well consolidated know-how on aircraft and aircraft components. Novotech offers solutions addressed to all companies interested to increase their competitiveness through the development of advanced manufacturing processes in the field of composite materials. The Company has extensive experience in the development and manufacture of cryogenic hydrogen tanks, including the third-stage VEGA launcher tank and the COCOLIH2T cryogenic hydrogen tank demonstrator and it has also been recognised by the European Commission Innovation Radar as a “Key Innovator” for the development of hydrogen-conformable thermoplastic fuel tanks.
Novotech has produced several demonstrators by AFP (Automated Fiber Placement) process, as a tail-cone portion of the Next Generation Turboprop Regional Aircraft (NGTP) or a portion of the lower skin of the M-346 trainer aircraft, as well as testing activities for the qualification and validation of design methodologies implemented.

entityDescription: IKWIND Systems Inc. is a Canadian technology company developing AI-driven mission planning and operational decision-support solutions for UAV and distributed sensing systems in complex, remote, and communication-constrained environments. Its core product, Aquti Mission Planner, transforms Earth Observation data, environmental inputs, and sensor outputs into executable multi-UAV deployment strategies, enabling efficient resource allocation, route optimization, and real-time adaptive operations. The platform is designed for applications such as disaster response, search and rescue, infrastructure monitoring, and defence ISR, with a strong focus on integrating EO data into actionable field operations. IKWIND combines expertise in geospatial optimization, autonomous systems, and satellite-enabled environments to bridge the gap between data-driven situational awareness and real-world execution.

entityDescription:
Our mission
Our business is simple: enabling companies to unlock the full potential of their data. We are experts in the creation, management and operation of data platforms to enhance the value of our customers’ data patrimony. Thanks to our unique “data-centric” methodology, and strong partnerships with all the major software publishers, we help our customers make the most of their data, and treat it as a patrimony that will enable them to differentiate themselves in the marketplace.Because nobody else has your data. Thanks to this methodology, your technical debt is erased and your ecological impact is reduced.

Our vision
Since 2020, data flows have overtaken goods flows in world trade. 30% of GDP is now linked to data-centric services. Clearly, data is now the beating heart of innovation and growth. If data is indeed the world’s leading industry, every company needs to treat it as such, with a value chain that contributes to respecting environmental, societal and ethical standards.
We envision a world where every company, whatever its sector, can transform its data into a lever for sustainable and responsible development.

Our history
JEMS was founded in 2002 by Éléna Gihan, focusing on IT services for the financial markets. In 2012, the company turned to big data with the acquisition of EDIS Consulting, led by Nicolas Laroche and Cyrille Coqueret. In 2018, the offering expanded into digital services, followed by a succession of strategic acquisitions and a change of shareholder in 2023.
These key milestones have shaped our expertise and broadened our spectrum of action, enabling us to become the leading expert in the data industry today.

SEVALTA S.r.l. is an Italian innovative start-up based in Bari, focused on the development, production and commercialisation of high-technology products and services in the fields of Earth Observation, geospatial intelligence, satellite data processing, GIS platforms, digital twins and decision support systems.
The company develops solutions for the acquisition, processing, validation, fusion and analysis of multi-source geospatial data, including satellite imagery, in-situ data and sensor data. Its activities include software platforms, data services, artificial intelligence models, digital twin solutions, monitoring systems, predictive analytics and technical reporting for public and private decision-makers.
SEVALTA operates with particular focus on environmental monitoring, climate adaptation, natural risk management, infrastructure resilience, smart cities, precision agriculture, blue economy and advanced geospatial analytics. The company also performs research and development, prototyping, pilot projects and operational testing, with the objective of transforming space-enabled data into actionable information for safer, more resilient and more sustainable territories and infrastructures.

entityDescription:
FARSIGHT SENTINEL, a UK-based aerospace firm, develops and operates High-Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS) as a managed service, offering persistent sensing, communications, and testing at about 20 km altitude. Instead of selling hardware, they provide end-to-end mission delivery, including platform integration, launch, operations, data, and recovery.
Their core product is on-demand HAPS missions using hydrogen fuel cells and electric propulsion, supporting payloads for Earth observation, communications, environmental monitoring, infrastructure surveillance, defense, and space testing. Services include regional campaigns or custom missions with payload integration and testing.
The platform features low-drag balloon architectures, plasma propulsion, modular payload bays, and fuel systems for persistent station-keeping. Some system elements are being patented for long-term advantage.
Target clients are government, environmental groups, infrastructure operators, satellite firms, and research institutions needing quick, local aerial capabilities. It complements satellites by offering resilience, relay, and high-revisit monitoring at lower costs.
Operations involve a small fleet of reusable HAPS platforms, managing launch, airspace coordination, autonomous station-keeping, payload operations, descent, and recovery, with costs mainly for helium and hydrogen.
Currently in development, FARSIGHT SENTINEL aims to be operational within 24 months, conducting at least one mission monthly. By Year 3, they plan to triple missions, and by Year 4, to expand again through fleet growth and regulatory efficiency.
Revenue is per mission or deployment, based on duration, payload, and data needs, with additional income from bespoke testing, resilience services, and repeat contracts. Early focus is on recurring revenue.
Operational costs are kept low, decreasing with increased missions via reuse and automation, enabling sustainable margins. The team comprises experts in medical, engineering, operational, and space sectors, ensuring technical and operational strength

entityDescription:
Nextage provides spacecraft systems engineering, avionics design/products and electrical systems engineering, electrical ground support equipment (EGSE), and mission operations support for space missions. The company delivers expertise in spacecraft integration and test, ground systems, mission operations infrastructure, simulator development, telemetry and command systems, and operational tool development supporting spacecraft development, commissioning, and on-orbit operations.
Core engineering capabilities include spacecraft mission operations and ground systems, electrical systems engineering, avionics architecture and design, automated electrical test equipment (ATE) development, electrical harness design/analysis and integration, and development of spacecraft simulators and payload test systems. Nextage also develops and leads environmental and system-level testing including functional and performance testing, end-to-end mission testing, electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) and thermal-vacuum testing (TVAC).

We deliver expertise across the full mission lifecycle, including mission concept and system architecture, trade studies and decision analysis, requirements/interface development and management, design and development, verification and validation, operations products and preparation, launch operations support and mission operations.

Nextage provides comprehensive Mission Operations and Control Infrastructure (MOCI) development and mission operations services supporting the transition from spacecraft/satellite development to operational missions. These services include development of command procedures, sequence-of-events scripts, telemetry monitoring tools, and operational displays that enable reliable spacecraft command and control. Nextage engineers support the complete mission operations lifecycle, including pre-launch operations preparation, commissioning operations, mission rehearsal campaigns, on-console operations, health and safety monitoring, anomaly response, and post-handover operational support.

FNG Invest operates the Commercialization Reactor, a prestigious startup accelerator dedicated to fostering the success of innovative and impactful startups on a global scale. With a comprehensive suite of resources, mentorship, funding, and unparalleled access to industry experts and potential customers, the Commercialization Reactor empowers startups to realize their vision and bring their groundbreaking ideas to market.

Through our meticulously curated events and accelerator program, we continuously nurture and accelerate the growth of startups like Eventech, propelling them towards unprecedented success in their respective industries.

This collaboration further exemplifies the caliber of startups supported by the Commercialization Reactor, as Eventech's advanced timing technology will play a critical role in ensuring the mission's success. By delivering exceptional accuracy and reliability, Eventech's timetag timer will contribute to the precise synchronization and coordination of critical events during the ESA Hera mission, solidifying Eventech's reputation as a trusted partner in the space exploration domain.

entityName: UNIVERSITY OF PISA – Dipartimento di Fisica
entityDescription:
The Department of Physics at the University of Pisa is an international center for scientific research and advanced education. Covered fields include the Physics of Fundamental Interactions, Physics of Matter, Theoretical Physics, Astrophysics and Applied Physics, with highly interdisciplinary research carried out in Nanotechnologies, Medical Physics, and in the Physics of the Universe.
The Department takes part in many international research projects at the frontier of Science, and collaborates tightly with the Pisa Division of the National Institute for Nucler Physics, and with several Institutes of National Research Council. A relevant partnership subsists with the European Gravitational Observatory, whose gravitational wave detector VIRGO strongly involves our Department.
The Department of Physics is the focus of a unique eco-system for higher education, in which we develop programmes jointly with researchers and professors of INFN, CNR, the Scuola Normale Superiore and the Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna in Pisa.
External funds for research, raised in recent years, amount to several tens MEuros. We also collaborate with the Italian Institute of Technology, and with industry at national and international level, through technology transfer projects carried out with companies in various fields (e.g. new materials, quantum technologies, aerospace).
In the current National Research Quality Assessment (VQR-ANVUR), our Department is the highest in ranking among other Physics departments in its size quartile.
Broad and intense teaching activities are performed for about 1000 undergraduate students, and 60 PhD students and postgraduate students specializing in Medical Physics, all interacting with current frontier research.

entityName: UCA/UNIVERSITE CLERMONT AUVERGNE - Institut de Chimie de Clermont-Ferrand
entityDescription:
The Institute of Chemistry of Clermont-Ferrand (ICCF) is a Joint Research Unit (UMR6296) under the supervision of the National Center for Scientific Research (CNRS), Clermont Auvergne University, and the Clermont-Ferrand University Hospital. ICCF is affiliated with the Institute of Sciences and Clermont Auvergne INP and the Doctoral Schools in Fundamental Sciences and Sciences for Engineering.
ICCF conducts fundamental and applied research with strong industrial partnerships in various fields of chemistry, such as Thermodynamics, Inorganic Materials, Biocatalysis and Metabolism, Organic and Medicinal Chemistry, Photochemistry, as well as Materials Chemistry for Health.
The research activities address societal challenges linked to three main research areas: Chemistry and Environment, Chemistry and Materials, Chemistry for Life. These areas are particularly focused on the design of innovative materials, the synthesis and study of the biological potential of organic molecules or materials, the biodegradation of organic compounds, the durability of polymer materials, and molecular simulation. The institute offers its technical expertise, instrumental resources, and know-how to meet the current needs of society and industry.

entityDescription: The Institute of Science, Technology and Sustainability for Ceramics (ISSMC) is the Italian Hub of Excellence on Ceramic Materials, where the idea, design and development of new ceramic and hybrid materials takes place for the benefit of industry and the whole society, and where advanced training is carried out in the field of materials science addressed to fields of major current interest: Aero-space, Wellness and Health, Energy, Nano-remediation & safety, Environment, Construction and Cultural Heritage. ISSMC has several collaborations in Europe and overseas (USA, Japan, etc) and is involved in numerous national and international research and training programs, many of which with the role of Project Coordinator. The interaction and collaboration with the industrial field are developed and supported by numerous technology transfer projects through the creation of spin-offs and / or licensing of patents related to new processes and products developed in ISSMC.

WIRED 3D GmbH is a German high-tech startup specializing in advanced metal 3D printing (additive manufacturing).
Founded as a spin-off from the Ravensburg-Weingarten University of Applied Sciences,
the company focuses on developing and operating proprietary 3D printing systems designed to produce complex metal components with high precision and efficiency.
Core Activities & Technology The company has developed an integrated 3D printing ecosystem, which includes:
- Proprietary Hardware & Software: Development of custom 3D printers and process-specific algorithms to optimize production speed and component quality.

- Large-Scale Metal Printing: Capability to produce metal parts in various sizes, ranging from small, intricate components to large-scale objects (up to 500 x 500 x 1500 mm).

- Material Diversity: Expertise in working with different metals, including steel and stainless steel, ensuring high material integrity (minimal impurities) and reproducible mechanical properties.

- Engineering Services: Providing bionic and intelligent component design to maximize strength while minimizing wall thickness and weight.

Mission & Target Markets WIRED3D aims to offer a faster, more cost-effective, and sustainable alternative to traditional metal manufacturing. They serve industrial clients requiring high-strength components and have also engaged in creative sectors, such as architectural art and design competitions.

Entity Description: Wavelet BeamWavelet Beam is a high-tech engineering entity specializing in advanced digital signal processing and video enhancement for mission-critical applications. The core of our innovation is the IRIS Video Noise Management system, a proprietary, CUDA-accelerated HPC framework designed to surgically lift valid video signals out of the noise floor, recovering critical image information that was previously hidden by video noise. Unlike conventional denoising solutions that often blur image content and sacrifice spatial resolution in challenging low-light sequences, IRIS preserves fine structures, textures, and edge integrity.Our technology ecosystem is built around four primary pillars: 
• IRIS & IRIS.RAW: Providing high-precision noise reduction at the earliest stage of the imaging chain to maintain raw data integrity. • IRIS.ANALYST: An enhancement engine optimized to maximize information density for human and automated analysis in low-SNR (Signal-to-Noise Ratio) environments.• IRIS.BROADCAST: Delivering unmatched real-time HPC performance up to 8K@60fps for demanding live-stream and ground-segment applications. • IRIS Adaptive Encoding: An intelligent pre-processing layer that optimizes data streams for transmission and storage. By removing irrelevant noise while maintaining data integrity, we enable bit-rate reductions of 30% or even higher.

To ensure the physical correctness required for space-grade data and scientific analysis, we utilize a dedicated 16-bit processing pipeline that eliminates rounding errors and banding. Wavelet Beam leverages advanced CUDA core development to position these specialized capabilities for the space and ground segments, with a focus on satellite imagery optimization, space debris detection, and high-performance archival and video distribution workflows within HPC environments.

entityDescription:
MapScan is a Denmark-based geospatial services provider specializing in GIS, Earth Observation, LiDAR, and UAV-based data collection. The company delivers high-precision, standardized spatial data and analytical products for B2B clients across environmental monitoring, infrastructure, and engineering domains.
With over 19 years of professional experience, MapScan focuses on systematic, SLA-driven data acquisition and processing, ensuring consistent, repeatable, and high-quality geospatial outputs. The company provides end-to-end solutions, from field data collection (UAV, LiDAR, bathymetric and terrestrial surveys) to advanced data processing, GIS integration, and development of custom geospatial platforms.
Core competencies include environmental and biodiversity monitoring using time-series spatial data, volumetric analysis and stockpile monitoring, orthomosaic and Digital Elevation Model (DEM) generation, vectorization, and Scan-to-BIM workflows. MapScan also delivers hydrographic and bathymetric surveys, supporting water resource management and coastal monitoring.
The company has strong expertise in building interoperable geospatial systems aligned with international standards, supporting integration into CAD, BIM, and GIS environments. MapScan develops tailored GIS solutions using modern spatial technologies such as PostGIS, GeoServer, and web mapping frameworks.
Its services are applied across multiple sectors, including environmental protection, municipalities and asset management, construction and BIM, natural resources, infrastructure, and water management.
MapScan’s mission is to provide reliable, ready-to-integrate geospatial data and digital infrastructure that support evidence-based decision-making, operational efficiency, and sustainable resource management.

entityDescription:
Meteogrid S. L. is a privately owned company based in Madrid, Spain, offering high value-added products and services in the field of weather and applied meteorology, weather forecasting and risk management. Its technical team has been working in these fields since 1992.
The range of services offered by Meteogrid covers various application fields, such as natural disasters, extreme weather, civil protection emergencies, hydrology, energy, transport, agriculture and civil engineering among others, for which accurate weather forecasting is required and is used in high value-added products such as Early Warning Systems (EWS). Our clients are both administrations and public entities, for example in the field of natural risks, civil protection, hydrology, etc., and private companies, as in the case of energy, agriculture and transport.

Since 1996 Meteogrid's technical team has developed and improved Weather Forecasting Systems (WFS), bringing together highly qualified experts in the areas of meteorology, natural hazards and computing. After a detailed analysis of society's needs in the field of meteorological services, the first version of the WFS was designed to meet these needs, focusing on technical users. The developed WFS produces high added value probabilistic forecasts for the next ten days, using in a robust way the Ensemble Prediction System (EPS) of the European Centre for Medium Term Prediction (ECMWF). The reliability of the WFS is very high, as verified by independent third parties who have tested it and compared it with other available predictions (including those of the Spanish State Meteorological Agency, AEMet).
Meteogrid's technical team has developed a sophisticated EWS integrated into a Geographical Information System (GIS) environment, in a process of continuous improvement since 2000. This GIS integrates weather observations and forecasts from as many data sources as available (including Meteogrid's own WFS). The EWS includes multiple functionalities and tools, such as the user-configurable alert module (according to the area of interest, thresholds of significant variables, alert communication mode, etc.), or various simulation modules coupled with the weather forecast.
As a result, in Spain, most of the technical management for activities depending on or affected by meteorology uses the products and services that the system offers. Application areas include water management, emergencies (civil protection operations, wildfires, floods, etc.), energy (production -hydroelectric, wind, solar...-, distribution, consumption forecasting), transport and traffic (road network, railway network, etc.), precision agriculture, environmental protection, etc.

Although Meteogrid has focused its operations in Spain and the Mediterranean countries of Europe, the company has also developed its activity in other parts of the world, more particularly Latin America and Asia.

entityDescription:
STRAIN S.r.l. is an innovative aerospace technology company and accredited spin-off of the University of Rome Tor Vergata (Italy), officially authorized in 2025. The company originates from more than a decade of academic research in advanced composite materials, smart structures, and sustainable manufacturing technologies developed within the university’s Manufacturing Technology Research Group.
STRAIN was established to industrialize research results in smart polymer composites and transform them into space-qualified mechanical subsystems and high-value aerospace solutions. The company operates at the intersection of advanced materials engineering, mechanical subsystem design, and sustainable space technologies.
The founding team combines academic excellence and industrial aerospace experience. STRAIN’s technical leadership includes senior professors in Manufacturing Technology and Sustainable Production Systems with extensive experience in ESA and ASI research programs on composite materials, structural design, and smart systems. The CEO brings over 18 years of industrial experience in aerospace composite structures and European collaborative R&D projects.
This multidisciplinary background enables STRAIN to bridge academic research and industrial qualification, ensuring both scientific rigor and engineering reliability.
The company’s core competencies include:
Design and development of composite-based mechanical subsystems

Smart material engineering and thermo-mechanical modeling

Finite element analysis and structural optimization

Prototype manufacturing and composite processing

Integration and testing in accordance with ECSS standards

Technology transfer and intellectual property management

STRAIN operates through a structured collaboration framework with the University of Rome Tor Vergata and industrial partners, ensuring access to laboratory facilities, composite processing infrastructure, and environmental testing capabilities. This hybrid academic–industrial model allows the company to maintain high innovation capacity while aligning with industrial qualification requirements.
The company is positioned within the European upstream space sector as a technology-oriented SME focused on lightweight, sustainable, and ITAR-free mechanical solutions. STRAIN aligns its development roadmap with ESA strategic priorities, including Clean Space, Zero Debris, and European technological autonomy.

Company description: STRAIN S.r.l. is an innovative aerospace technology company and accredited spin-off of the University of Rome Tor Vergata (Italy), officially authorized in 2025. The company originates from more than a decade of academic research in advanced composite materials, smart structures, and sustainable manufacturing technologies developed within the university’s Manufacturing Technology Research Group.
STRAIN was established to industrialize research results in smart polymer composites and transform them into space-qualified mechanical subsystems and high-value aerospace solutions. The company operates at the intersection of advanced materials engineering, mechanical subsystem design, and sustainable space technologies.
The founding team combines academic excellence and industrial aerospace experience. STRAIN’s technical leadership includes senior professors in Manufacturing Technology and Sustainable Production Systems with extensive experience in ESA and ASI research programs on composite materials, structural design, and smart systems. The CEO brings over 18 years of industrial experience in aerospace composite structures and European collaborative R&D projects.
This multidisciplinary background enables STRAIN to bridge academic research and industrial qualification, ensuring both scientific rigor and engineering reliability.
The company’s core competencies include:
Design and development of composite-based mechanical subsystems

Smart material engineering and thermo-mechanical modeling

Finite element analysis and structural optimization

Prototype manufacturing and composite processing

Integration and testing in accordance with ECSS standards

Technology transfer and intellectual property management

STRAIN operates through a structured collaboration framework with the University of Rome Tor Vergata and industrial partners, ensuring access to laboratory facilities, composite processing infrastructure, and environmental testing capabilities. This hybrid academic–industrial model allows the company to maintain high innovation capacity while aligning with industrial qualification requirements.
The company is positioned within the European upstream space sector as a technology-oriented SME focused on lightweight, sustainable, and ITAR-free mechanical solutions. STRAIN aligns its development roadmap with ESA strategic priorities, including Clean Space, Zero Debris, and European technological autonomy.

entityDescription:
HydroAI is a deep-tech startup dedicated to water resources management through advanced Earth Observation and intelligent data processing. Born from scientific research and validated through international collaboration, the entity specializes in providing actionable intelligence for the monitoring and preservation of freshwater resources.
The core mission of HydroAI is to bridge the gap between complex environmental data and practical decision-making. The startup operates primarily in the downstream sector of the space economy, transforming raw satellite data into high-value information services. By focusing on the entire water cycle within reservoir and catchment systems, the entity addresses critical challenges such as water scarcity, drought resilience, and storage infrastructure integrity.
HydroAI’s service portfolio is designed to provide a broad view of water assets. This includes the continuous monitoring of water availability and surface extent, the assessment of water quality to safeguard ecosystem health, and the delivery of predictive insights to anticipate future water stress. Additionally, the startup offers specialized surveying capabilities to map the physical characteristics of water storage reservoir, ensuring that managers have an accurate understanding of their total capacity.
As a science-based venture, HydroAI acts as a strategic partner for the agricultural sector, public water authorities, and environmental agencies. By delivering clarity in an increasingly unpredictable climate, the startup empowers stakeholders to optimize irrigation, improve resource allocation, and implement sustainable governance strategies. Currently supported by leading impact incubators and recognized in innovation competitions, HydroAI is positioned at the forefront of digital transformation for rural and water-dependent communities.

entityDescription:
Founded in 2024, LSC360 is the result of the merger of seven Luxembourg-based entities within the LSC Engineering Group. By combining the expertise of Luxplan, Simon-Christiansen & Associés, Zilmplan, Mersch Ingénieurs-Paysagistes, Luxsense Geodata, LSC Environmental Engineering, and Devolux, we ensure service continuity while offering a unique and strengthened synergy. With over 50 years of experience, we position ourselves as an innovative and committed engineering consultancy, providing an integrated and sustainable approach to meet the current and future demands of our sector.

LSC360 embodies an ambitious vision where 360° engineering means a holistic approach to each project, connecting skills and solutions to create a positive impact on society. Our core values—centered on well-being, empathy, and social responsibility—are at the heart of our approach. We firmly believe that the success of each project relies as much on high-performing technical solutions as on respecting human aspirations.
Today, LSC360 brings together over 60 professions and experts, offering a wide range of services, from feasibility studies to financial analysis, authorization files, execution, work supervision, and project coordination. Our strong emphasis on teamwork and the skills of our personnel allows us to work on a wide variety of projects, ensuring the complexity and diversity of required studies. We have established our market position through the completion of major national and international projects, always guided by client satisfaction as our top priority.
LSC360 is committed to exemplary quality management, with ISO 9001 certification highlighting our continuous improvement process. Our social and environmental responsibility is reflected in the ESR (Socially Responsible Company) label, as well as ISO 14001 for environmental management and ISO 45001 for health and safety at work. Through our Integrated Management System (IMS), we ensure the monitoring and implementation of our actions in terms of quality, health, safety, and environment. We are also proud to carry the Made in Luxembourg label, a symbol of our expertise and local roots.
Thanks to advanced IT tools, continuous training, and the rigor of our teams, we guarantee the quality and precision of every plan and report. At LSC360, we combine expertise, innovation, and commitment to be a key player in the transformation toward a sustainable future.

Our mission is to support our clients in the realization of integrated projects of all scales, combining efficiency and empathy. Our vision is based on the union of diverse talents and engineering expertise to design, inspire, and shape a meaningful society.
Our core values are expressed through three main commitments:
360° Well-being: placing people, empathy, and community connection at the heart of our actions
360° Engineering: ensuring technical expertise and innovative solutions
360° Sustainability: embodying a global approach that integrates environmental, economic, and social responsibility

description:
Based in Rotterdam, SPHERICAL provides full-stack space electronics designed to meet the rigorous demands of the modern orbital economy. Our core focus is on high-performance Power Conditioning and Distribution Units (PCDUs) and advanced control electronics.

What sets SPHERICAL apart is our silicon-driven architecture. Rather than relying entirely on commercial off-the-shelf components, we develop custom, system-specific silicon. This capability allows us to deliver electronics that are significantly more reliable, dynamically software-configurable on orbit, and superior in Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP) efficiency.

Beyond our proprietary PCDUs and controllers, we apply our expertise across the broader Electrical, Electronic, and Electromechanical (EEE) landscape. SPHERICAL offers comprehensive, end-to-end ASIC design services, equipping aerospace primes and robotics partners with dedicated silicon solutions tailored to their exact mission parameters. We don't just supply hardware; we architect the reliable electronics foundation required for complex space operations.

entityDescription:
Earth Observation (EO) satellites are perfectly suited for the monitoring and the reporting of geopolitical events affecting the global economy and the well-being and security of millions of people (e.g., wars, humanitarian crises, energy crises, pandemics, supply chain disruptions…). Extracting geospatial intelligence from satellite imagery usually involves at least some degree of manual work by human image analysts. However, over the last few years the amount of available data has increased dramatically. This makes it practically impossible to effectively process all the available imagery through visual exploitation, thus increasing the need for software tools which can automatically extract actionable insights from the data.
TerraLens, a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center (DLR), offers cutting edge solutions to exploit EO data for political and strategic decision making. We fill the gap between scientific prototyping and operational requirements by implementing state-of-the-art algorithms into professional software solutions for security-relevant applications. Our automatic monitoring solutions enable non-technical end-users to easily define their specific problem, analyze vast amounts of data with little effort, interact with the original data and the extracted insights, and take actions based on these insights.
