entityDescription:
QKZ is a deeptech venture focused on enabling quantum safe communications for the next generation of connectivity, especially in hybrid terrestrial and non terrestrial networks, including NTN. We believe the future internet will be built across multiple layers of infrastructure such as fiber, 5G, private networks, satellite links, and emerging NTN architectures. Trust and security must work seamlessly across all of them.
Mission: Make quantum safe security deployable and operational in real networks. We reduce the barrier to adopting quantum resistant security by turning complex cryptographic capabilities, including QKD, PQC, and classical mechanisms, into infrastructure grade building blocks that network operators and critical organizations can use without bespoke engineering.
Vision: Become the system layer that makes quantum safe connectivity a standard feature of global networks. As NTN expands coverage to remote areas, maritime, aviation, and space ground links, the security model must evolve beyond best effort encryption toward measurable, auditable, and resilient security. Our long term vision is a world where secure connectivity is not limited by geography or dependence on third party infrastructure, and where cryptographic strength can adapt over time as threats and regulations change.
Technical vision: We focus on system level crypto agility for heterogeneous networks. Networks will increasingly combine classical transport paths with intermittent or variable quality links, including satellite and NTN. This requires security mechanisms that can dynamically adapt to changing link conditions and risk profiles. Our technical direction is hybrid orchestration of QKD and PQC, where quantum key material can be used when available, and robust PQC based mechanisms maintain continuity when quantum links are degraded or unavailable. The key challenge is not inventing new algorithms, but making security choices operational through policy driven selection, controlled fallback, lifecycle management, and auditability of decisions.
From a networking perspective, NTN introduces unique constraints such as latency variability, intermittent connectivity, diverse trust boundaries, and complex supply chains. These constraints amplify the need for transparent and resilient security controls. QKZ emphasizes end to end policies, survivable degradation strategies, and evidence based security, including logs and audit trails that explain which cryptographic posture was active at a given time and why.
In summary, QKZ bridges the gap between quantum security research and deployable, resilient security for global connectivity. We build foundations for quantum safe networking that can scale from terrestrial infrastructure to NTN enabled architectures, ensuring that future networks are both globally reachable and trustworthy.

entityName: BlueZ C Institute - Asssociação para a conservação marinha e economia do carbono
entityDescription:
BlueZ C – Institute for Marine Conservation and Carbon Economy is a UAlg spin-off, SME certificated with non-profit proposes. Founded by Rui Santos, Claudia Sil and José Pedro Batista, aims to contribute with innovative solutions to the mitigation of climate change and the preservation, conservation, and recovery of coastal marine ecosystems. BlueZ C emerged from over 30 years of scientific research developed in CCMar about coastal marine ecosystems protection and restoration through sustainable management practices and community engagement to combat climate change and effectively manage local livelihoods. Dedicated to the transfer of blue biotechnology, BlueZ C is a vehicle to make international conservation and restoration goals possible, such as the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration 2021-2030, based on scientific and new technological products.
Despite being a recently constituted NGO, registered on 30 June 2022, with the commencement of activity on 15 September 2022, BlueZ C has already been rewarded with several awards. Firstly, winner of the “Ideias em Caixa” competition, in the sea category, which allowed it to become a spin-off of UAlg and be incubated by the Entrepreneurship and Technology Transfer Division – CRIA. Also in 2022, the institution was awarded the first prize, in the Startup category, of the first edition of the “StartAAAP 2022” competition, promoted by the Euroregion Alentejo-Algarve-Andaluzia. Additionally, it was the winner within the scope of the ATLAZUL project, in the ideas/good practices category of the “Innovação Atlazul no Guadiana” competition. Recently, it was also awarded the “Promove 2023”, prize awarded by BPI / “La Caixa” Foundation, for the “SalC – Valorization of Salt Pans for Carbon Sequestration and Climate Change Mitigation” project.
BlueZ C acknowledge and detains the know-how to contribute effectively for managing marine and maritime sectors sustainably, through balancing economic growth, social welfare, and environmental protection. Environmental management and marine spatial planning are vital tools for achieving this balance. They assess and mitigate environmental risks, optimize resource use, and ensure inclusive decision-making. Collaboration, innovation, and responsible stewardship are essential for a prosperous and resilient future for coastal communities and marine ecosystems.

description:
PERFORMANCE INTERCONNECT offers advanced electrical and thermal interconnect solutions employing superior, proprietary technologies.

What are we famous for?

HYPERBITS™ - the industry’s first single body solderless HDR connector which does not require press-fit tooling because it employs S-FECT™ solderless technology. https://www.pisas.fr/hyperbits

HEATBIND™ - solid retainer system for enhanced thermal conduction in embedded computing. https://www.pisas.fr/heatbind

PHENOMENA™ - advanced thermal materials based on high quality mono-crystalline diamonds. The PHENOMENA™ thermal interface paste employs gap dependent monolayer diamond skeleton for the lowest possible thermal resistance at the junction between surfaces in contact. The PHENOMENA™ copper-diamond composite material is used to transfer heat away from hot surfaces with a thermal conductivity of 760W/m*k.
https://www.pisas.fr/phenomena

HYPERVPR™ - is a pulsating heat pipe plate used for 3U and 6U Plug-In Modules, with thermal transfer capabilities starting from 150W.

SOFT-PAD™ - ultimate high density interposers with contact pitch from 100µm. 100 contacts per millimeter square, solderless, surface-mount to address any mezzanine interface challenge.

ART-SERIES™ - RF connector line with solderless mounting technology for straight and 90º PCB installations.
https://www.pisas.fr/rf-connectors

entityDescription:
MAE is a Machinery Manufacturing Company, specialised in the engineering and manufacturing of units and complete lines for Monomers and Polymers, processed in the form of fibers or foams.
MAE’s extended services range from the process design to the assembly, installation and testing of complete production lines and plants.

MAE’s history begins in the late sixties when the company was mainly focused on producing machinery and components for the biggest Italian Man-Made fibers producers such as Montefibre, SNIA and ENI.
In the following decades MAE’s experience progressively increased from the production of simple components to the more complex assemblies and complete units, entire lines and full complete plants. Consequently MAE design competences grew and today MAE can be considered a strong partner for any fiber producer willing to outsource the development of important parts of their facilities.
Carbon Fiber PAN Precursor has now become MAE’s core business. MAE designs and builds complete plants for PAN Precursor with small production capacity (Lab Scale), medium capacity (Pilot Scale or Small Industrial Scale), and large capacity (Industrial Scale).
MAE’s product list covers: Polymerization lines with different solvent technologies, wet or dry-jet Spinning lines and also specific key equipment of the Carbonization line like: Fiber Tensioning System, Surface Treatment, Sizing, Non-contact or Contact Dryers.
Furthermore, some specific MAE’s products like the SDC Jumbo Crimpers for cotton type PET, spunbonding plants for 100% recycled PET are considered today as the state-of-the art benchmark in their field.

In the vast range of MAE facilities are also available: a Material/Textile laboratory, Pilot Spinning Lines and a Rapid Prototyping Unit for R&D trials, product development, testing and investigations. These facilities are centralized in MAE Experimentation Center (GALILEO) in Italy.

MAE owns, in its “Galileo” Experimentation Center, the only complete Precursor and Carbon Fiber Pilot Plant in Europe. This also includes Solvent Recovery and Graphitization Units. Built with the support of Leonardo Spa, it is a semi-industrial plant potentially capable to produce all grades of carbon fiber.

Antigravity is a technology-driven company focused on the design and development of advanced software solutions for the space sector. The company specializes in building experimental platforms, simulation systems, and mission-critical software to support research, prototyping, and early-stage innovation in aerospace and space exploration.
Antigravity works at the intersection of software engineering, applied physics, and systems architecture, developing tools for orbital simulation, data processing, automation, and control systems. Its approach is strongly oriented toward prototyping, rapid iteration, and proof-of-concept development, enabling teams to test, validate, and refine complex ideas before deployment in real or constrained environments.
By combining deep technical expertise with a research-first mindset, Antigravity supports space agencies, research institutions, and private aerospace initiatives in turning theoretical concepts into functional, testable systems. The company emphasizes reliability, scalability, and precision, addressing the unique constraints of space-grade software while remaining flexible enough for experimental and next-generation applications.

entityDescription:
Ethicronics Ltd is a Cambridge (UK)–based deep-tech company specialising in hardware assurance, low-level software, and hardware security for safety-critical and mission-critical systems, including applications relevant to space, defence, and critical infrastructure.
Modern space and critical systems increasingly rely on complex, globally sourced electronic components. Physical compromise, substitution, or interference at the hardware level undermines system integrity at its foundation, and cannot be mitigated by software security alone. Existing assurance approaches are often slow, manual, and difficult to scale to modern compute platforms.
Ethicronics addresses this challenge by developing scalable, software-driven methods to verify the integrity of electronic hardware, from system level down to fine-grained physical resolution. The company’s core hardware assurance platform is under active development, with current work focused on security hardening, scalability, and system integration. In parallel, Ethicronics provides a tamper-evident hardware monitoring capability available today, delivering secure detection and forensic evidence of physical interference across manufacturing, transport, storage, and deployment.
The company is led by a small, senior, and complementary team combining deep technical expertise with programme and stakeholder management capability. The team includes PhD-qualified engineers and University of Cambridge alumni, with experience across defence programmes, academic research, and advanced compute environments. Ethicronics is accustomed to operating in regulated and security-sensitive contexts and has secured $1.5M in non-dilutive funding, supported by UK public funding and defence-aligned innovation programmes.

entityDescription:
Fortaegis is developing a new computing paradigm that fundamentally strengthens security and resilience by embedding trust directly into the semiconductors at the core of digital systems. Instead of adding protection after deployment, Fortaegis integrates security at the hardware level, enabling hardware and software to operate together with integrity and reliability across large, distributed networks - including those supporting AI-driven workloads in both civilian and defence systems.

Most computing systems today depend on security measures implemented primarily in software, layered on top of standard hardware. As these systems scale in complexity and data intensity - particularly with the rise of AI and distributed inference - this approach increases cost, degrades performance, introduces fundamental limits on the number of nodes that can operate securely within a network, and expands the attack surface. Fortaegis takes a fundamentally different approach by embedding security directly into the chip. Each semiconductor incorporates a unique, unclonable physical identity, allowing systems to authenticate devices and processes without relying on stored cryptographic keys or external certificate authorities.

This silicon-rooted trust extends upward through the entire compute stack, from the chip into firmware and system software. As a result, data - including models, weights, and inference results - remains protected while being processed, stored, or transmitted at high speed, while maintaining compatibility with existing digital infrastructure. By anchoring trust in hardware, Fortaegis eliminates many of the performance trade-offs traditionally associated with secure computing, enabling secure AI at scale, while providing resilience against advanced cyber threats, including those posed by future quantum technologies.

Fortaegis’ technology is already suited for environments that demand real-time response and high reliability under hostile or safety-critical conditions. In the automotive sector, it enables low-latency secure computing for autonomous systems. In defence, it supports instant authentication of sensors, vehicles, and command systems in contested environments. Additional applications include industrial automation and (sovereign) AI cloud-to-edge computing, where large volumes of data and AI workloads must be processed securely and at speed across distributed networks.

description: PURR.AI is a Portuguese deep-tech biotechnology startup developing advanced AI-driven platforms for the discovery and optimisation of neurotherapeutics, with a particular focus on age-related neurological and central nervous system (CNS) disorders. The company leverages European Space Agency–derived digital assistant technology (AIDA), adapted into its proprietary biomedical reasoning engine MIRA, to integrate heterogeneous biological data, knowledge graphs, and machine-learning models into a unified decision-support environment. PURR.AI’s core platform, AGELESS, combines curated multi-omics data (AGELESS.DB), predictive and generative algorithms (AGELESS.MAP), and modular tools such as B3Pass, a peptide blood–brain barrier permeability predictor, to support early-stage drug discovery and candidate prioritisation. Operating as a computational, research-driven organisation with a remote-first model, PURR.AI collaborates with academic, clinical, and industrial partners to translate complex biological knowledge into actionable insights, while applying responsible AI, data governance, and sustainability-by-design principles aligned with ESA values.

entityDescription:
Aegion is an ESA BIC UK supported advanced materials venture headquartered at Space Park Leicester, UK. We are dedicated to the development and qualification of high-performance materials designed to withstand the harshest frontiers of space exploration and deep-tech industry
Aegion operates at the intersection of metallurgy and aerospace engineering, delivering solutions for environments where traditional materials fail. Our primary application domains include: Space Propulsion: High-temperature superalloys for rocket engines and thrusters, Orbital Assets: Lightweight, high-strength structures for satellites and space stations, Deep Space Exploration: Radiation-hardened materials and thermal protection systems for lunar and Martian missions and Future Energy: Material integrity for Space-based Nuclear Power and Small Modular Reactors (SMRs).
The core of Aegion’s intellectual property lies in Advanced Thermomechanical Process Engineering. Moving beyond simple alloy blending, we manipulate materials at the crystal lattice and microstructural levels to achieve unprecedented performance benchmarks.
Our portfolio is tailored to meet the rigorous qualification standards of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the broader UK space ecosystem:
- Next-Gen Superalloys: Titanium- and Nickel-based systems, including Titanium Aluminides for high-efficiency propulsion components.

- Advanced Composites: Graphene-reinforced metal matrix composites and refractory systems.

- Technical Ceramics: Ultra-high-temperature ceramics (UHTCs) for re-entry shielding and thermal management.

- Atmospheric Management: Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) for advanced carbon capture and life-support systems.

description:
Akilaris — Space Intelligence

Transforming raw orbital data into actionable intelligence

Space Intelligence is the ability to understand, predict, and act upon what's happening in the orbital environment — in real-time, autonomously, and at scale.

What is Space Intelligence?

As Earth's orbits become increasingly congested with satellites, debris, and mega-constellations, operators face an overwhelming flood of data: tracking information, conjunction warnings, sensor feeds, and environmental conditions. Traditional approaches rely on human operators to process this data, make decisions, and command maneuvers — a model that doesn't scale.

Space Intelligence changes this paradigm.

Akilaris builds AI systems that transform raw space data into autonomous action

entityDescription:
UWRC sp. z o.o. (UWRC Ltd) established in 2012, is the special purpose vehicle (spv) of the University of Warsaw (UW), Poland, which is a sole shareholder of the company. The UWRC Ltd was established to support University researchers and students in indirect commercialization of their scientific activity results (setting up spin-off companies). The company is established to comply with Polish Higher Education and Research legal framework, which allows universities to setup companies and hold shares only through the spv.
The UWRC Ltd offers to students and faculty members a range of services from mentoring, business idea assessment, definition of value proposition, business model development, market validation, monetisation strategies, etc. Since establishment in 2012 the UWRC Ltd supported setting up of more than 30 university based, deep-tech spin-off companies. At present the UWRC Ltd manages a portfolio of more than 20 spin-offs.
The UWRC Ltd offers also to UW students and researchers the preincubation services. It allows sciencepreneurs to develop Proof of Concepts, MVPs and test the market with their early products and services under an umbrella of UWRC Ltd legal entity, without taking a risk of setting up their own ventures. The company offers also number of trainings and workshops in areas related to its core activity.
The UWRC Ltd creates also a favourable condition for university – business cooperation. The company offers access to university infrastructure, laboratories and research teams managing several industrial contracts per year.
Since 2017, the UWERC Ltd participated in three editions of the Innovation Incubator Program (Innovation Incubator Plus, Innovation Incubator 2.0, Innovation Incubator 4.0) financed by the Polish Ministry of Science and Higher Education with the purpose to strengthen commercialisation processes at universities. The UWRC Ltd was always a consortium member with the University of Warsaw as the Leader and two other academic partners. The company was responsible for developing and implementation of an effective model for university spin-off creation and support for academic entrepreneurship. The most visible effect of the Program was support for establishment of 25 university spin-offs.
The UWRC Ltd is an active member of the Polish Alliance of University Knowledge Transfer Companies, which represents a community of more than 30 university spv from all Polish research universities.

Prio Optics GmbH is a pioneering deep-tech startup based in Eggenstein-Leopoldshafen, Germany, specializing in the development and production of advanced optical coatings using cutting-edge inkjet printing technology. 
Prio Optics leverages proprietary processes to manufacture multilayer optical interference coatings under ambient conditions, eliminating the need for traditional vacuum-based deposition methods. This approach enables cost-effective, scalable, and customizable production of optical coatings on a variety of substrates, including flexible and large-area formats. 
Prio Optics offers a broad portfolio of optical coatings, such as anti-reflection coatings, dichroic coatings, and long-pass filter coatings, catering to applications in smartphone cameras, displays, building window and photovoltaics. 
Prio Optics' inkjet-printed coatings are characterized by higher throughput at lower costs, fast production, low material waste, and minimal environmental impact, aligning with sustainable manufacturing practices.

AHEAD Institute for Societal Advancement Ltd is a Maltese entity specialising in EO downstream services and geospatial R&D for climate and environmental applications. We transform Copernicus and complementary datasets into operational products and services, including high-resolution mapping, change detection, risk indicators, and scenario-based assessments to support adaptation planning and emergency preparedness.
Our technical strengths cover remote sensing, GIS, spatial analytics, AI-enabled decision support, and the development of digital-twin-style modelling environments that integrate terrain, land use, exposure and climate inputs. We deliver stakeholder-ready outputs through interactive web tools, technical reporting, and workflows designed for transparency, reproducibility and integration into existing geospatial infrastructures.
AHEAD’s work targets measurable outcomes: improved situational awareness, better prioritisation of interventions, and scalable methods that can be replicated across small island and coastal contexts relevant to ESA and European resilience objectives.

NOK-G is an industry-leading supplier of end-to-end intelligent networking solutions that provide the foundation for the largest and most demanding Tier 1 carriers, cable operators, internet content providers (ICP)s, government and enterprise networks worldwide. With a distinguished heritage of optical networking innovation and over two thousand patents, Nokia’s end-to-end solutions uniquely enable network operators to efficiently scale network bandwidth, accelerate service provisioning and automate operational tasks, resulting in substantially improved network economics. From the metro edge to the optical core, the Nokia solutions portfolio is built upon proven expertise in optical, packet-optical and IP transport, and leverages software-enabled automation capabilities that simplify service provisioning and reduce operational complexity in multi-layer, multi-domain and multi-vendor networks. Nokia’s differentiation includes industry leadership in vertically integrated solutions that include in-house developed photonic integrated circuit (PIC) and application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) chips and unique software solutions packaged together to deliver networks that offer ultra-high performance, yet remain easy to deploy, use and operate. 

Coriant R&D GmbH was part of Coriant, which was founded upon the combination of Nokia Siemens Networks Optical Networks, Tellabs, and Sycamore Networks. Coriant R&D GmbH has a significant presence and a proven record of accomplishment in numerous European projects with service providers, component suppliers, universities and research institutes, namely under the EU Seventh Framework Programme (FP7) and Horizon 2020 (H2020). In 2018, Infinera acquired Coriant.
From 2025, Nokia owns Coriant R&D GmbH which is the legal entity participating in the consortium.

entityDescription: Deplotic is an innovative startup with a mission to enhance the sustainability of space operations by prolonging the operational lifespan of satellites through advanced robotic solutions. Deplotic was founded by a team of researchers from the Politecnico di Torino, who have been working for years on robotics for space applications. Deplotic is developing IDRA, an inflatable and deployable robotic arm. By integrating advanced inflatable technology with modular electric actuation, IDRA offers a solution for space logistics and in-orbit servicing (IOS) operations—enabling satellite operators and service providers to significantly reduce costs, complexity, and integration time associated with traditional robotic systems. Thanks to its inflatable structure, IDRA achieves an unprecedented workspace—up to 64 times larger than conventional manipulators with the same stowed volume—while remaining lightweight, compact, and customizable. Its modular design allows rapid adaptation to specific mission requirements, with adjustable link lengths, degrees of freedom, and tool configurations. IDRA is engineered to support a wide range of tasks, including inspection, repair, refueling, upgrading, satellite relocation, and debris removal, both in-orbit and on planetary surfaces. Unlike traditional manipulators, IDRA can be stowed compactly and deployed on demand, making it ideal for spacecraft with tight volume constraints. Moreover, it enables to perform self-maintenance operations—reaching any part of the host satellite—providing unprecedented autonomy and cost-effectiveness for medium-to-large-sized space assets.

description:
Bringing lifecycle insights into your space mission's design
EcoDeltaV spun out of a multi-year project initiated by the European Space Agency’s Future Launchers Preparatory Program (ESA’s FLPP) and led by the Space Center of the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne (EPFL). Between 2022 and 2025, EPFL Space center’s expertise in space sustainability was distilled into the conception of the Assessment and Comparison Tool (ACT), creating a much-needed means for the space industry to integrate environmental impact assessment into the design process of space missions. 
Today, EcoDeltaV carries the legacy of the EPFL Space Center’ s space sustainability expertise and combines specialized knowledge in launcher emissions from the University of Stuttgart. With this, it has positioned itself uniquely in the space sector by enabling companies to comply with environmental requirements and regulations on sustainability.

entityDescription:
Calnex NE-ONE Network Emulators enable the easy creation of Software Defined SATCOM Test Networks.
Satellite networks represent a big challenge for applications that are being developed to run on them, or deployed having been built for other network types. This is due to their relatively High Latency, with Jitter, Bit Error and Loss all playing a part.
Any application which can be regarded as SATCOM-Ready needs to be thoroughly tested in a wide range of satellite conditions.
The issue is that obtaining a real and representative SATCOMS network to test over is a challenge, and the costs of doing this are frequently prohibitive.
NE-ONE Software Defined Test Networks (powered by Calnex NE-ONE's hardware and virtual Network Emulators) allow the creation of an end-to-end network which behaves just like a SATCOM network, allowing easy testing of the applications. Unlike real SATCOM networks, it is relatively inexpensive and allows full controllability and repeatability of different Satellite Network Conditions and Types.
NE-ONE Software Defined Test Networks are trusted and relied upon by enterprises, governments and military organisations around the world.

description:
To meet the evolving demands of space photovoltaic applications, we have developed two innovative, technology-agnostic solutions compatible with all major PV platforms, including GaAs, silicon, and perovskite technologies :
1. Cover Glass Booster The Cover Glass Booster is designed to significantly enhance the performance and durability of space PV solar cells and panels, delivering several percentage points of improvement in conversion efficiency while extending operational lifetime. Initially developed for triple-junction PV systems, this solution offers broad compatibility and can be readily adapted to virtually any PV cell or panel architecture. 
2. High-Performance, Long-Longevity UV Filter
As the space sector increasingly explores cost-effective silicon and perovskite PV technologies, resistance to ultraviolet-induced degradation has become a decisive factor for long-term mission success. Our advanced UV filter effectively mitigates degradation caused by UVC, UVB, and UVA radiation, preserving photovoltaic performance and reliability over the entire operational lifespan of the cell or panel.

entityDescription:
Objectives of the activity

The subject of the PSE S.A. activity is to provide the services ofelectricity transmission in compliance with the required criteria of the security of the Polish Power System operation.The main objectives of the PSE S.A. activity are:- providing electricity transmission services and ensuring secure and cost-effective operation of the Polish Power System whilst meeting the conditions of synchronous operation with other European systems,
- ensuring the necessary development of the domestic transmission grid and cross-border interconnections,
- making transmission capacity available on market based methods for cross-border exchange purposes,
- creating the technical infrastructure for the operation of the domestic wholesale electricity market.

Role and ResponsibilitiesWithin the responsibilities specified in the Energy Law Act (art. 9c par 2) the transmission system operator:- contributes to the security of electricity supply by ensuring security of the power system operation and adequate transmission capacity,
- provides the operation of the transmission system in an effective manner whilstensuring the required reliability and quality of supply and in cooperation with Distribution System Operators - in the coordinatedpart of the 110 kV network,
- maintains the transmission system, including interconnections with other power systems, in a manner which ensures reliable operation of the power system,
- ensures the long-term ability of the power system to meet reasonable domestic and cross-border demands for the transmission of electricity, including development of the transmission power system, and, where appropriate, development of interconnections with other power systems,
- cooperates with other transmission system operators and energy enterprises in order to ensure reliabe and effective operation of the power systems and to coordinate their development,
- dispatches the generation units connected to the transmission grid and the generation units of the installed capacity equal to or more than 50 MW, connected to the coordinated part of the 110 kV network with due regard to the contracts with the transmission system users and technical constraints in the system,
- manages congestion on the interconnections with other systems,
- purchases the ancillary services and provides system services necessary for the secure, reliable and efficient electricity system functioning,
- balances the power system, including the service of the imbalance settlement of system users,
- manages electricity flows in the transmission system and in cooperation with Distribution System Operators - in the coordinated 110 kV network,
- purchases electricity to cover the transmission losses, with due observation of transparent and non-discriminatory market-based procedures,
- provides system users and other interconnected transmission system operators with the information necessary for the access to and use of the transmission network, regarding conditions for transmission services, including in relation to the cross-border exchange of electricity, network operation and balancing,
- prepares the power system defence and restoration plans,
- exercises power supply restrictions imposed in line with the laws and regulations in force.

entityDescription:
Independent research and consulting enterprise specializing in atmospheric optics, light pollution science, satellite remote sensing, and dark sky preservation. The company provides scientific expertise in quantifying artificial light at night impacts, developing light management strategies, and supporting International Dark Sky Place certifications.
Core competencies include: light pollution measurement and modeling, all-sky photometry, atmospheric radiative transfer, satellite data analysis (VIIRS DNB) for radiance trend assessment and urban planning applications, space debris impact assessment on astronomical observations, and development of evidence-based lighting policies for protected areas and municipalities.
The principal investigator brings extensive experience from dual affiliations with the Slovak Academy of Sciences and the University of Vienna's Institute for Astrophysics, with proven track record in EU-funded research (Marie Curie fellowship, INTERREG Central Europe projects) and leadership roles in international astronomical organizations (IAU working groups, DarkSky International). Demonstrated expertise in processing and analyzing satellite nighttime imagery for temporal radiance trend development and supporting municipal lighting planning initiatives.
Services offered: scientific consulting for lighting projects, satellite-based light pollution assessments, environmental impact assessments for artificial light, dark sky certification support, light pollution monitoring network design and implementation, expert reports for public authorities, and capacity building in sustainable outdoor lighting practices.
Relevant project experience includes establishment of Europe's largest regional light pollution monitoring network, scientific leadership of Austria's first International Dark Sky Park certification, VIIRS DNB-based radiance analyses for city planning authorities, and research publications in high-impact journals (Science, Nature Astronomy) on light pollution and space sustainability topics.

entityDescription:
SeedFence is a cybersecurity company focused on securing embedded systems, founded in 2023 by a highly experienced team.
SeedFence has developped an on-premises and cloud-based eXtended Detection & Response (XDR) platform designed for Android smartphones and embedded systems.The platform relies on lightweight XDR agents that is flexible enough to be deployed on many embedded devices and a centralized management system that can be hosted either in the cloud or on-premises, including within highly sensitive environments. 
SeedFence’s cutting-edge XDR technology is boosted by AI and is designed to detect, analyze, and block cyberattacks targeting Android devices, as well as IoT and Operational Technology (OT) systems.
While smartphones are often treated as closed or opaque systems, SeedFence aims to deliver best-in-class security for Android devices while providing unprecedented visibility into Android’s internal behavior.
Beyond smartphones, SeedFence’s XDR platform addresses the specific constraints of IoT and OT environments, offering a highly flexible solution adapted to a wide range of systems such as satellites, defense platforms, electric vehicle charging stations, and railway systems.

Together with its partner Thales, SeedFence has recently won a contract with CNES to deploy one of the very first satellite-based cyber detection solutions in France and Europe, following a public call for tenders.

entityDescription:
Global Space Services Technologies AB (GSST) is a Swedish space technology company focused on the development and operation of ground segment infrastructure and services for satellite missions. The company provides ground station services, system integration, and related technologies supporting satellite missions, with a current focus on polar and high-latitude operations.

GSST develops and operates ground station infrastructure in northern Sweden, optimized for near-polar and sun-synchronous orbits, and offers Ground Station as a Service (GSaaS), antenna hosting, and mission support services across the full mission lifecycle, including Launch and Early Orbit Phase (LEOP) and routine operations. The company also works with regulatory processes, spectrum licensing, and operational integration to enable secure and reliable satellite communications.

In addition to operational services, GSST is engaged in technology development related to satellite communications, ground segment automation, simulation tools, and future ground infrastructure concepts. This includes work on communication system simulation, mission preparation tools, and scalable architectures for next-generation satellite systems.

GSS collaborates with commercial, institutional, and governmental stakeholders and is actively expanding its international footprint, including planned activities in Southeast Asia, while maintaining its core operational base in Sweden. The company aims to contribute to a resilient and competitive European space ecosystem by enabling accessible, flexible, and high-quality ground segment solutions for emerging and established satellite operators.

entityDescription:
benntec Systemtechnik GmbH is a German technology company specializing in the development of digital training systems, immersive simulation environments, and operational Digital Twins for complex and safety-critical domains. For more than 30 years, the company has designed and implemented customized digital training solutions that support effective, reproducible, and operationally relevant education and training in environments characterized by high system complexity and stringent reliability requirements.
Headquartered in Bremen, with an additional site in Rostock (Warnemünde), benntec employs more than 120 interdisciplinary specialists with expertise in learning sciences, instructional design, software engineering, simulation technologies, system development, and project management. The company combines didactic methodology with deep system understanding and high-fidelity digital representations to enable sustainable knowledge transfer and procedural competence.
benntec develops practice-oriented, system-centric training environments that prepare users for real operational contexts. Its solutions range from computer- and web-based training and SCORM-compliant e-learning modules to desktop simulations, mobile learning and maintenance applications, and integrated blended learning architectures supported by learning management systems.
A central focus is the integration of immersive Extended Reality technologies, including Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality, and Mixed Reality, with operational Digital Twins. These Digital Twins are designed for training purposes and represent system architecture, internal structures, functional relationships, and dynamic system states. This enables users to explore cause–effect relationships, subsystem interactions, and off-nominal behavior beyond externally observable system states.
Building on extensive experience in mission-critical operational domains, benntec develops multi-user XR training ecosystems supporting supervised and self-paced training for maintenance, operational, and contingency procedures. Scenario configuration, disturbance injection, real-time system-state visualization, and structured debriefing are integral components. Training can be conducted entirely in virtual environments, reducing dependence on physical mock-ups while improving scalability and repeatability.
benntec is a long-standing supplier to German and international defense organizations and collaborates closely with the defense industry. This background has shaped a strong focus on robustness, traceability, security, and process reliability. The underlying methodologies and technologies are transferable to spaceflight-related applications, including astronaut training, mission operations, and systems engineering, where deep system understanding and precise procedural execution are critical.
The company operates under a certified quality management system in accordance with DIN EN ISO 9001:2015.

Munster Technological University (MTU) is a multi-campus public university located in the south of Ireland, established in 2021 with over 18,000 learners and a growing research ecosystem with an annual expenditure of greater than �33m. MTU offers a broad range of undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programmes across engineering, science, computing, business, humanities, and the creative arts. A defining feature of the university is its strong emphasis on applied learning, industry collaboration, and practice-based education, ensuring graduates are well prepared for real-world careers.
Research is a core pillar of MTU’s mission, with active research centres focusing on areas such as advanced manufacturing, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, sustainable energy, biotechnology, and smart maritime technologies. MTU supports a strong research and innovation ecosystem delivering impactful outputs to benefit regionally and globally. MTU has also developed a growing reputation in space-related research, particularly through its work in aerospace engineering, satellite systems, communications technologies, and data analytics. Researchers at MTU collaborate with international universities, space agencies, and industry partners on projects related to Earth observation, space systems engineering, and emerging space technologies.
With campuses across Cork and Kerry, MTU plays a vital role in regional development, innovation, and entrepreneurship. The university fosters a research-led environment that addresses global challenges while contributing to Ireland’s expanding role in high-tech and space research sectors.

entityName: Thessaloniki Water Supply and Sewerage Co, SA
entityDescription:
Thessaloniki Water Supply and Sewerage Co, SA (EYATH S.A.), a company listed on the Athens Stock Exchange since 2001, provides water supply and sewerage services to more than 1.2 million citizens in the greater Thessaloniki Urban Area every day. It specialises in the design, construction, installation, operation, utilisation, management, maintenance, extension and renewal of water supply and sewerage systems. Its activities include projects such as desalination, pumping, treatment, storage, transport, distribution and management of all types of water, as well as the collection, transport, treatment, storage and management of waste (other than toxic).
Moreover, the company undertakes the utilisation of products from waste water treatment, the provision of telecom services via the water supply and sewerage networks it operates and is also involved in the generation and sale of own-produced electricity (which is primarily generated by utilising water from springs, dams, aqueducts and pipelines). The EYATH’s competencies also include extensions to new areas or changes to water supply-sewerage systems (networks and facilities), to improve the quality and quantity of water supplied to consumers.

description: Light Bridges (LB) is a pioneering Spanish R&D company, establishing itself as a leader in specialized scientific infrastructures for advanced astronomy and satellite tracking. LB designs, builds, and manages private scientific facilities that enable top international research groups to conduct high-impact research in astronomy, satellite tracking, and optical communications. Core Infrastructure LB’s flagship infrastructure, the Two-meter Twin Telescope (TTT), is located at the Teide Observatory and achieved First Light on December 5, 2022. Under the leadership of Economist Dr. Antonio Maudes and Astronomy PI Dr. Miquel Serra-Ricart, the TTT leverages cutting-edge technology, including robotic professional telescopes, high-performance GPUs and advanced data storage solutions, to push the limits of astronomical and space research. The TTT provides a highly automated, robust platform optimized for precise and rapid observations. Business Lines LB operates three core business areas, each designed to harness the full potential of its specialized infrastructure: Astronomy Research Projects. The TTT enables pioneering observations of astronomical phenomena, such as exoplanets, asteroids, and transient events. Through these capabilities, researchers gain unprecedented insights into the universe with high precision and depth, utilizing LB’s extensive image processing power. Satellite Tracking and Space Situational Awareness. LB applies its expertise in robotic telescope systems to satellite tracking, addressing the growing need for accurate space situational awareness. This service is critical for monitoring satellite orbits, managing collision risks, and providing data for secure, efficient satellite operations. Optical Communications Research. LB is at the forefront of developing ground-based infrastructure for classical and quantum optical communications. The TTT is strategically positioned to serve as a future ground segment for these advanced systems, reinforcing LB's role in supporting secure, high-capacity data transmission technologies. Supporting Scientific Talent. In collaboration with Spanish ICEX, LB manages the Light Bridges Fellowship program, which nurtures emerging talent in astronomy. This program allows fellows to work on international projects using LB’s high-performance data processing infrastructure, fostering innovation and expanding LB's research network globally. LB fosters global collaborations, ensuring that its state-of-the-art facilities remain at the forefront of scientific advancement.
entityDescription:
Light Bridges (LB) is a pioneering Spanish R&D startup specializing in cutting-edge astronomy. We are creating a new vertical in new space and digital treatment of scientific images. LB focuses in the creation and management of private infrastructures of science to be used by international top groups. The first project was the "Two-meter Twin Telescope" (TTT) at the Teide Observatory with First Light the 5th of December 2022. At the forefront of LB's endeavors is the TTT project, which facilitates groundbreaking observations of astronomy phenomena (exoplanets, asteroids, optical counterparts) and showcases the company's prowess in managing sophisticated robotic telescope systems that will be used in the future as ground segment for optical communications (classical and quantum). Leveraging state-of-the-art flash storage and CPU/GPU technology, LB ensures efficient data storage and processing, enabling researchers to delve deep into the mysteries of the cosmos with unprecedented clarity and precision.
In addition to their telescope management expertise, LB spearheads the "Light Bridges Fellowship" program, a collaborative initiative with Spanish ICEX aimed at nurturing young talent in astronomy. Through this program, participants benefit from LB's advanced data processing capabilities, supported by powerful GPU infrastructure, to conduct innovative research projects both locally and internationally.
Among LB's remarkable achievements is the development of the innovative "Derechos de Tiempo de Observación" (DTO) concept, which revolutionizes access to observation opportunities, particularly focusing on the best universities and research centers that are the initial step on our internationalization.

ATELIER BRÜCKNER is an internationally leading exhibition design firm for museums, cultural institutions and visitor centers. With more than 150 completed projects and 120 full-time professionals coming from 25 nations, ATELIER BRÜCKNER has an extensive experience in designing exhibitions and museums around the world. Since 1997, ATELIER BRÜCKNER designs high quality narrative architecture, experience-based exhibitions and cognitively as well as emotionally challenging projects of scenography. ‘Form follows content’ is ATELIER BRÜCKNER's design philosophy with the aim to create unique and content-driven narratives.
Among our highlights are the Parlamentarium in Brussels, the BMW Museum in Munich or the ITHRA - King Abdulaziz Center for world cultures in Dhahran, KSA. Among our approx. 20 ongoing projects are the GEM – Grand Egyptian Museum in Cairo, the Museum of the Future in Dubai and the Museum of London, new galleries at the West Smithfield Market, to name only a few.

description:
At Revolv Space, we unlock the full potential of small satellites by designing, manufacturing, and testing next-generation mechanisms and power systems that ensure uninterrupted payload availability and maximize the monetization of space assets.

Operating from Torino (Italy) and Delft (The Netherlands), we offer a family of affordable, high-performance Solar Array Drive Assemblies (SADAs) designed specifically for small satellites, supporting power ranges from 100W to 5kW. With its innovative redundancy systems and advanced sun-tracking technology, our SADAs optimize solar array exposure, doubling power generation compared to fixed arrays and vastly boosting smallsat platform capabilities and mission returns.

Our power generation systems are tailored to diverse small satellite missions, from Earth observation to communication and scientific research. As an agile alternative to established suppliers, we specialize in delivering reliable and cost-effective solutions with low-lead times, addressing urgent industry needs and aligning with the business models of large constellations.

RAR SRL è un’azienda italiana con sede a San Giovanni Lupatoto (Verona) specializzata nella progettazione e produzione di apparecchiature elettromedicali e radiologiche. L’azienda sviluppa sistemi per imaging a raggi X, con competenze specifiche in CT e Micro‑CT, tomografia computerizzata Cone Beam e soluzioni di imaging per applicazioni medicali e industriali. L’attività comprende ricerca e sviluppo, progettazione hardware e software, integrazione di algoritmi di ricostruzione e realizzazione di sistemi completi per acquisizione e visualizzazione delle immagini. RAR SRL opera come fornitore tecnologico per aziende del settore radiologico e per applicazioni di controllo non distruttivo, combinando competenze ingegneristiche, elettroniche e software in un approccio orientato all’innovazione.

RAR SRL is an Italian company based in San Giovanni Lupatoto (Verona), specialized in the design and production of electromechanical and radiological equipment. The company develops X‑ray imaging systems with specific expertise in CT and Micro‑CT, Cone Beam tomography, and imaging solutions for both medical and industrial applications. Its activities include research and development, hardware and software design, integration of reconstruction algorithms, and the creation of complete systems for image acquisition and visualization. RAR SRL operates as a technological partner for companies in the radiology sector and for non‑destructive testing applications, combining engineering, electronics, and software competencies with a strong focus on innovation.

entityDescription: ZikaSeal is a Danish company combining satellite-based mosquito risk mapping with innovative hardware to combat mosquito-borne diseases in urban environments. Using satellite data and predictive models, ZikaSeal identifies high-risk stormwater drains where its patented barrier system can be installed to block mosquito breeding. The solution targets invasive species such as Aedes albopictus (Asian tiger mosquito), a known vector of the Zika, Dengue, and Chikungunya viruses. The barrier prevents mosquitoes from entering or escaping drains while allowing water, leaves, and debris to flow freely. ZikaSeal offers municipalities and utility companies a pesticide-free, scalable, and environmentally sustainable method of vector control.

kuafu offers an AI- and automation-powered energy management platform for electrical grid operators to intelligently manage congestion by leveraging local resources from e-mobility and smart buildings. Serving as a grid-edge orchestration hub, it coordinates resources like electric vehicles, batteries and heat pumps, typically managed by energy management system providers, to support grid operations. This reduces the need for costly grid reinforcement and energy portfolio balancing, while also unlocking new revenue streams for energy management system providers. kuafu accelerates grid decarbonization, supports net-zero goals, and empowers individuals to directly contribute to the fight against climate change -creating meaningful societal impact.

kuafu extends this same intelligence to spacecraft power management. The platform dynamically schedules payload operations, shifts non-critical tasks to periods of surplus generation, and ensures reserves for mission-critical functions, reducing conservative power overestimation, maximizing payload utilization, extending battery life, and improving mission efficiency in satellites and shared platforms.

entityDescription:
With the foundation of CYCLO GmbH in 1931, Lorenz Braren, the inventor of the unique CYCLO reducer, made a piece of industrial history. The bestowal of a licence on Sumitomo Heavy Industries in 1935 was the commencement of one of the oldest examples of German-Japanese industrial co-operation, which led in 1974 to a share bolding and in 1994 to the total inclusion of CYCLO GmbH into the Sumitomo Corporation.The Sumitomo Group is one of the largest industrial concerns in Japan and is active in widely varied industries. Sumitomo Heavy Industries is the market leader in drive technology in Japan and also one of the largest suppliers in the world.
SM CYCLO ITALY SRL is the Italian subsidiary of Germany's Sumitomo Cyclo Europe, in turn part of Japan's Sumitomo Group, active in distributing Sumitomo Drive Technologies products throughout the country. The Cornaredo (MI) office, thanks to a highly qualified staff, acts as a problem-solver, offering solutions for the world of precision. The Sumitomo Group is active in the most diverse industrial sectors: production automation, plastics and rubber processing, civil engineering, food industry, agriculture, metal processing, textile industry, and many others. 
The main business activities of SM CYCLO ITALY SRL consist of the design, assembly and sale of (i) precision and zero-backlash gearboxes, (ii) gearboxes and gearmotors, and (iii) special gearboxes for centrifugal applications. The Company is controlled by Sumitomo (SHI) Cyclo Drive Germany GmbH, a company that exercises management and coordination activities, is headquartered in Markt Indersdorf (Munich - DE), holds 100% of the share capital, and carries out the manufacturing activities of a large part of the gearboxes sold by SM CYCLO ITALY SRL in the domestic market.

By supporting both satellites and human space exploration missions, we will ensure that space weather no longer hinders financial or intellectual advancements in space.

entityDescription:
Pannon Business Network (PBN) is a leading applied innovation and ecosystem-building organisation based in Western Hungary, operating at the intersection of industry, research, education, and regional development. PBN acts as a cross-border innovation hub connecting Hungarian, Austrian, German, and wider European ecosystems, with a strong focus on Industry 4.0/5.0, advanced manufacturing, robotics and humanoid systems, AI-enabled solutions, digital twins, circular economy, and health- and age-tech applications. Its mission is to translate emerging technologies into practical, scalable, and market-ready solutions for SMEs, public actors, and industrial partners.
The organisation operates three complementary laboratories, forming an integrated applied innovation environment:
- a Humanoid Test Centre Laboratory, dedicated to human-centric robotics, physical AI, and real-world validation of humanoid and assistive systems;

- am-Lab, advanced manufacturing - embedded in a Teaching and Learning Factory framework, supporting advanced manufacturing, supplier transformation, skills development, and Industry 4.0/5.0 pilot implementations;

- Space Lab, currently under development, focusing on space-related technologies, testing, and cross-sector technology transfer with downstream industrial and dual-use applications.

Together, these labs enable technology validation, experimentation, training, and deployment in real operational contexts, bridging the gap between research excellence and industrial uptake.
PBN is an experienced coordinator and partner in EU-funded programmes (Interreg, Horizon Europe, I3, EIT-related actions), with a strong track record in cross-border cooperation, ecosystem orchestration, and institutional capacity building. It works closely with universities, research institutes, chambers, clusters, municipalities, and industry leaders to strengthen regional competitiveness and resilience.
Strategically, PBN positions itself as a neutral innovation integrator, aligning policy objectives, technological development, workforce skills, and business models. Through this role, it enables regions and organisations to adopt human-centric, sustainable, and future-proof industrial solutions, while actively contributing to Europe’s twin transition and long-term strategic autonomy.

entityDescription:
Farmers’ Parliament (ZSA) is the most influential and constructive non-governmental organization of agricultural and horticultural produce producers in Latvia. The ZSA was founded in 1999, uniting 134 strong and far-sighted farms with a common goal – to fight for the interests of Latvian farmers and to strengthen the competitiveness of Latvian farmers. Currently, the union brings together around 800 purposeful members representing all agricultural sectors.
We work to give you a voice, protect your lifestyle in the countryside of Latvia now and in the future. The aim of the organization is to support Latvian agriculture and horticulture by promoting stable and sustainable growth for Latvian farmers!
The main work of the ZSA is representation of interests of Latvian farmers, involvement in the legislative process at the level of national and European Union (EU). We explain and help implement the latest laws, regulations and EU regulations in farms. The union regularly organizes seminars and conferences about the latest and most up-to-date information on the various agricultural sectors.
Our board and members regularly participate in interviews, TV and radio broadcasts, expressing their views on hot topics in the agricultural sector. We also cooperate with other NGOs and institutions.
Our work has paid off – ZSA members in Latvia manage over 662,000 ha of available agricultural land, and each year these areas grow. There are more than 6,000 jobs in the member farms for the local population. So we represent not only our members, but we also protect families that are maintained by our farm workers.
Agriculture is the strongest sector in Latvia and we can be proud of being the leading NGO in this sector!

entityDescription:
Founded in 1972, Tecnologie Meccaniche quickly established itself in the national market by supplying custom-designed equipment for the entire Ferrovie dello Stato Group.The company’s guiding principle of continuous evolution led Tecnologie Meccaniche, in the 1990s, to embark on a path focused on the study, design, and production of equipment.
The company is ISO 9001:2015 certified and is currently in the process of obtaining ISO 9100:2018 certification. It currently employs a workforce of 100 staff members, distributed across Production, Quality Control, Technical Office, Research and Development, and Verification and Validation. Thanks to our in-house expertise and qualified partners, we are capable of designing, manufacturing, and validating mechanical, electromechanical, electronic, and hydraulic equipment with SIL4 safety levels, specifically for the safety systems of Rete Ferroviaria Italiana (RFI), in compliance with CENELEC standards 50126, 50128, and 50129.
Tecnologie Meccaniche is divided into four plants, covering approximately 40,000 m² each and located in close proximity to one another, for a total area of 110,000 m², including 3,600 m² of offices.
Production at Tecnologie Meccaniche is organized into eight departments:
Department 01: Machining Centers

Department 02: CNC Lathes

Department 05: Tooling, Prototypes, Electrical Discharge Machining (EDM)

Department 06: Laser Cutting

Department 07: Washing, Sandblasting, Weighing, and Part Inspection

Department 08: Metalworking / Sheet Metal Fabrication

Department 09: Electrical Assembly

Department 10: Mechanical, Hydraulic, and Electromechanical Assembly

Tecnologie Meccaniche can rely on a team of more than 20 engineers engaged in research and development as well as mechanical, electronic, electrical, software, and firmware design.Project activities are aimed at combining innovation and safety in compliance with strict industry standards.The project team is supported by a dedicated Verification and Validation team that oversees the entire product certification process in accordance with international safety standards.

entityDescription:
empiriQa is a high-tech spin-off company emerging from the Single Photon Application Laboratory (SPALab) at the Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń, Poland. Structured as a Limited Liability Company (Sp. z o.o.), the company commercializes over 20 years of specialized research and know-how in quantum optics and Quantum Key Distribution (QKD). The company bridges the gap between advanced academic research and industrial implementation, specifically addressing the critical security threats posed by future Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computers (CRQC).
The company’s mission is to secure global data infrastructure against the "harvest now, decrypt later" threat by providing physics-based, unconditionally secure communication solutions. The company operates on a "Full-Stack" model, delivering proprietary hardware and specialized verification services. The core value proposition is built upon three pillars:
1. Quantum Communication Hardware (Upstream & Ground Segment): The company designs and manufactures critical components for the quantum supply chain. This includes proprietary Optical Ground Stations (OGS) for satellite-based QKD and high-performance Quantum Key Generators (Entangled Photon Sources) designed for both terrestrial and space-based applications.
2. Verification & Validation (V&V) Services: A unique auditing capability that distinguishes the company in the European market. The entity provides independent "Quantum-Safe Readiness Audits" and security certifications to ensure that third-party QKD installations are free from implementation flaws and "backdoors". This service leverages methodologies aligned with ETSI and ECSS standards.
3. System Integration and quantum resistance audits: Expertise in integrating quantum layers into existing telecommunications infrastructure for government and defense clients

entityName: Fundación para la Investigación del Clima
entityDescription:
The Climate Research Foundation (FIC) is an independent non-profit private entity which has a solid scientific profile and specializes in research into the climate, environment and climate change. The FIC is recognized as a Non-Governmental Organisation for Development under the Resolution of 17th May 2018 by the Directorate of Multilateral, Horizontal and Financial Cooperation of Spain.
The technical team at the FIC have been providing consultancy and research projects on the issue of climate change since 1992 and are specialists in the evaluation, design and start-up of initiatives aimed at strengthening the resilience of different countries in Europe, Asia and America, as well as in the development of plans for adaptation to future climate scenarios.
The experts at the FIC have wide-ranging experience in the development of analytical approaches and quantitative evaluation of meteorological and/or climatic risks, at different scales and in multiple sectors, as well as in the design and programming of computer-based tools based on Geographical Information Systems (GIS) for developing cartography of physical risks and to aid multicriteria decision making. In this regard, the products designed by the FIC have a clear communicative focus, through dynamic, interactive tools which allow simple yet flexible use by the end users, whether technical personnel or the general public.
The FIC has participated in numerous projects analysing vulnerability of infrastructures to climate change, including criteria for the design and application of measures aimed at risk management and reduction, giving particular importance to the use of Nature-based solutions (NBS).
The FIC has developed a statistical approach for regionalization or downscaling, to simulate future climate at local scale and has achieved excellent results, leading to international recognition and the opportunity to work with leading European research groups in the field of climate studies.
Having consolidated its capacity to generate future climate scenarios, the FIC has focused its efforts on providing high value-added assistance services to evaluate the impacts of climate change on various sectors and areas of intervention, including the analysis of socioeconomic impacts and the formulation of adaptation methods. In this regard, the FIC has carried out a number of important projects along with the provision of technical assistance to institutions in Asia, America and Europe, aimed at identifying, assessing, quantifying and managing the impacts of climate change on energy, biodiversity, agriculture, food safety, water resources, urban planning, infrastructures, health or tourism, among other sectors.

entityDescription:
Université Grenoble Alpes (UGA) is both firmly anchored at the local level and has a solid international reputation.

Its foundation stems from the aggregation of the former Université 
Grenoble Alpes and the most prestigious higher education and research 
institutions in Grenoble: Grenoble INP (School of Engineering), Sciences
Po Grenoble (School of Political Science and Public Policy) and ENSAG 
(Grenoble School of Architecture).

Over 60,000 students are registered at Grenoble Alpes University. 3,000 
of them study at the doctoral level and 9,000 are international 
students.

It has 7,500 members of staff based in its two campuses, in Grenoble and Valence.

Université Grenoble Alpes will pursue its collaborations, locally and 
nationally, with research institutions and networks such as the CNRS, 
the French Commission for Alternative Energies (CEA), the IT Research 
Center (INRIA), the University Hospital (CHU), and the French Institute 
of Health and Medical Research (INSERM). These strong collaborations and
the pursuit of joint research projects focusing on shared scientific 
interests will contribute to strengthening and widening the university’s
broad international partnerships.

Université Grenoble Alpes has three main missions.

- As a world-class university, it will seek to maintain and 
strengthen its local and international connections as a means of making a
valuable contribution to social, cultural and economic development
- It will fully and boldly embrace social challenges by offering a 
wide range of academic programs, by supporting research projects, which 
push back the frontiers of human knowledge
- It will address social, political, cultural and environmental 
challenges in a global context, whilst respecting its specific identity 
and diversity, and working in partnership with local stakeholders

University of Warsaw (UW), established in 1816, is Poland's largest and finest university. From its beginning the University of Warsaw has played a major role in the intellectual, political and cultural life of Poland, and has been recognized throughout the world as a leading academic centre in this part of Europe. Dynamic political, social, and economic changes accompanying Poland's democratisation have brought the University new opportunities and challenges. In the beginning of 21st century, University of Warsaw is moving forward with a plan to modernise its structure, organisation and curricula in an effort to prepare its faculties, students and graduates to function freely in the international community.
 Today UW employs over 6,200 people, including 3,240 academic teacher and educates almost 53,700 undergraduate and graduate students. Each year over 20,000 young people enroll as students at the University of Warsaw. entityDescription:
MoS is a newly established company founded by a team with deep roots in the Università Politecnica delle Marche (UNIVPM) and a long-standing track record in European research and innovation projects. While MoS is a new legal entity, it draws on the consolidated expertise of its founding team in all phases of EU project design and implementation – from proposal writing and technical coordination to administrative management, reporting, and project governance. This enables the delivery of high-quality, innovative solutions with measurable impact.
MoS brings together academic rigor and operational know-how, with team members experienced in interdisciplinary research across sustainability, energy efficiency, digital innovation, and industrial transformation. Our portfolio spans diverse sectors – including environment, health, and manufacturing – with proven competencies in pilot demonstration management, ensuring effective implementation, monitoring, and replication of results in real-world settings. Our involvement in Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe projects such as CLIMRES, DIGIBUILD, DEDALUS, SOCIOBEE, and BIMSPEED reflects our strong foundation in environmental intelligence, smart buildings, and digital services.
Beyond technical capabilities, MoS has extensive expertise in the Social Sciences and Humanities (SSH) dimension, supporting the integration of human and societal aspects into R&I actions. We design and implement co-creation processes, behavioural studies, and participatory methodologies that foster engagement, inclusiveness, and social acceptance. Our team is particularly skilled in managing stakeholder engagement, facilitating collaboration between public authorities, civil society, industry, and academia to ensure that project outcomes are relevant, actionable, and aligned with end-user needs.
MoS offers strategic services in communication, dissemination, and exploitation, including the definition of impact pathways, audience-tailored messaging, and the design of high-quality materials for multiple media channels. We organize and moderate international conferences, workshops, webinars, and training sessions, bridging the gap between research results and societal uptake. Our work is grounded in a results-oriented approach that links dissemination activities with measurable indicators, policy uptake, and replication potential.

entityDescription:
Ineo Defense is a company specialized in defense and security technologies. It provides high-performance, integrated solutions to meet the needs of armed forces, government agencies, and companies in the defense sector.
As a recognized player and trusted partner of the armed forces and defense manufacturers, Ineo Defense plays a key role in researching and implementing tailored solutions. The expertise and commitment of our teams help strengthen our country’s resilience against current and future challenges, particularly by providing:
Specialized communication systems
Armed forces must be equipped with modern equipment adapted to their environment. This includes advanced and secure communication systems that allow them to remain interconnected, ensuring effective and seamless coordination of operations. These specialized communication systems (HF, Satcom, digital, etc.) may include radio equipment, secure messaging devices, GPS location systems, and more.
Tactical intelligence sensors
Armed forces need access to accurate information on potential threats and enemy movements, particularly through the use of intelligence systems and electronic warfare sensors (tactical SIGINT alert systems, direction-finding, jammers, countermeasures, etc.).
Mobile operational centers
During operations, armed forces require hardened, discreet, deployable command centers that can be rapidly deployed, optimized for energy efficiency and ergonomics to provide users with the best possible working environment.
Logistical support services
To ensure operations, the forces need strong logistical support. This includes guaranteeing fleet availability, calculating exact requirements, managing spare parts and repairs, optimizing strategic stocks, and delivering to operational sites, among other tasks.

Garofoli S.p.A. operates as a qualified supplier for the space sector, supporting institutional and commercial programs through the production of: 
Mechanical Ground Support Equipment (MGSE) for satellites, payloads, and launch vehicle subsystems 
Transport and handling equipment for space hardware, compliant with ECSS standards 
Mobile shelters and clean-environment containers for the protection, integration, and testing of sensitive electronic and space equipment 
Precision mechanical structures and assemblies, including welded and machined components with tight tolerances 
Custom tooling and special-purpose equipment for Assembly, Integration and Test (AIT) activities 
The Company provides end-to-end capabilities, covering: Mechanical design and structural analysis Manufacturing, assembly, and system integration Functional testing, verification, and acceptance support Configuration control, documentation, and quality assurance in accordance with ECSS and space-industry requirements.
Garofoli’s space activities are characterized by high reliability, traceability, and compliance with international standards, enabling the Company to collaborate with space agencies, prime contractors, and Tier-1 suppliers on national and international space programs. Since 2004, Garofoli S.p.A. has operated through its Spanish subsidiary, Garofoli Ibérica, headquartered in Madrid, established to strengthen the Company’s presence in the Spanish market and to support the development of space-sector activities in collaboration with local and international partners.

entityDescription:
CBRE Group, Inc. (including CBRE GWS) is the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm, with 2021 revenues of $27.7 billion. We have been included on the Fortune 500 since 2008, currently ranking #122. Our shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol “CBRE.”
CBRE has more than 105,000 employees (excluding Turner & Townsend employees) and serves real estate investor and occupier clients in more than 100 countries. 
We provide services globally in a broad range of verticals, both public as private sectors, such as: Corporate Head Quarters, Financials, Industrial, Logistics, Life Science, Quality Retail, High Street Retail, Hotels, Stadia, Major Theatres, HealthCare, Universities, Central & Local Government and Museums & Art Galleries.

We provide services for real estate occupiers and investors. For occupiers, we provide facilities management, project management, transaction (both property sales and leasing) and consulting services, among others. For investors, we provide capital markets (property sales, mortgage origination, sales and servicing), leasing, investment management, property management, valuation and development services, among others. We provide services under the following brand names: “CBRE” (real estate advisory and outsourcing services); “CBRE Investment Management” (investment management); “Trammell Crow Company” (U.S. development) and “Telford Homes”. CBRE holds a 60% ownership interest in Turner & Townsend Holdings Limited, a global professional services company specializing in program management, project management, and cost consulting across the commercial real estate, infrastructure and natural resources sectors. We are the largest shareholder in Industrious, a provider of premium flexible workplace solutions, and we are a financial sponsor of and strategic partner with Altus Power, Inc. (NYSE: AMPS), a leading provider of solar energy solutions for commercial and industrial properties.

entityDescription:
The Universitat Jaume I in Castelló (UJI), founded in 1991, is the public university serving the north of the Valencian Community (Spain). After 25 years of history, the UJI is now among the Top 500 universities in the world, according to the Academic Ranking of World Universities 2017 (ARWU), conducted by the Shanghai Ranking Consultancy. 
Our university seeks to promote social, economic and cultural development through the creation and transmission of knowledge. Our endeavours in this regard have enabled us to obtain a rating of excellence in teaching and research in the international U-Multirank ranking and the 500+ Gold Seal of European Excellence by the Excellence in Management Club.
The UJI hosts over 14,000 students and more than 2,000 researchers distributed in 27 university departments and 14 research institutes, focused on four main areas: Technology and Experimental Sciences; Medicine and Psychology; Humanities and Social Sciences; and Law and Economics. Our university offers 32 undergraduate degrees, 47 State-regulated master’s degrees, 21 UJI-specific master’s degrees and 20 doctoral programmes. All programmes comply with the objectives of the European Higher Education Area and students receive individual attention without problems of overcrowding.
The UJI offers modern facilities and services to support research, such as the Central Scientific Instrumentation Service (SCIC), a prestigious Library, the Animal Experimentation Service (SEA), the Ethics Committee, the Scientific Culture and Innovation Unit (UCC + i) and the Office for Cooperation in Research and Technological Development (OCIT), which helps with the management of research projects and the protection of industrial and intellectual property. Technology transfer is carried out through the Science, Technology and Business Park (ESPAITEC), which brings together innovative technology-based companies, research groups and public organisations.
