entityDescription:
The Silesian University of Technology (SUT) is the oldest technical university in Upper Silesia and one of the largest in the country. It was established in 1945 as a scientific and educational facility for the most industrialized area in Poland, and one of the most industrialized in Europe. For over 75 years it has been an important institution of public life. It plays a significant cultural and opinion-forming role in the region. The mission of the Silesian University of Technology, as a prestigious European technical university, is to conduct innovative scientific research and development works, as well as to educate highly qualified staff for the benefit of the knowledge-based society and economy, and to actively influence the development of the region and local communities. The university, through continuous improvement of processes and organization, is a friendly and open place for work and development of the academic community.

Silesian University of Technology is the only university in Silesia to be included in the prestigious group of 10 Polish universities, winners of the "Excellence Initiative-Research University" competition organized by the Ministry of Science and Higher Education. The university identified 6 main Priority Research Areas:
1.Computational oncology and personalized medicine
2.Artificial intelligence and data processing
3.Materials of the future
4.Smart cities and future mobility
5.Process automation and Industry 4.0
6.Climate and environmental protection, modern energy.

entityDescription: CUS-GNC is an innovative aerospace technology company specializing in advanced Guidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC) solutions for spacecraft and autonomous space systems. The company develops high-performance flight software that enables satellites and other space vehicles to operate with significant autonomy, reducing reliance on ground control and enhancing mission efficiency. Their flagship product, SpacePilot, is a modular onboard software suite that integrates classical guidance algorithms with modern machine-learning techniques to support real-time decision-making, precision attitude control, and complex orbital operations across a range of mission profiles. SpacePilot is designed to be adaptable for Low Earth Orbit (LEO), Medium Earth Orbit (MEO), Geostationary Orbit (GEO), and beyond, providing robust autonomy even in environments with limited computational resources. Independent deployments of their software have been successfully commissioned, demonstrating real-world flight capability and reinforcing the company’s position in the emerging autonomous space systems market. CUS-GNC was founded in 2023 and operates as a privately-held enterprise with a focus on delivering cutting-edge GNC software that supports next-generation space missions with improved performance, safety, and reduced operational costs.

entityDescription:
The University of Greifswald is one of the oldest universities in Germany and the Baltic Sea Region. Founded in 1456, it is also the oldest Swedish university, as the region was ruled by the Swedes after the Thirty YearsWar and up until 1815.
Still today, the University of Greifswald is closely tied to the universities of the Baltic Sea Region. But now the international relationships in both research and teaching have spread to regions and countries across the globe. The University today sustains international exchange relationships to more than 200 universities. There are currently international students and scholars from more than 100 different countries.
The University of Greifswald is a research university. Its research strength mainly originates in the intensive interdisciplinary collaboration of the five faculties, including University Medicine. Cutting-edge research evolves in close collaboration with regional, national and international research partners and is based on the solid foundation provided by an excellent research infrastructure.“Challenges and solutions of a changing environment and society” is the University of Greifswald’s research mission. There are three interdepartmental and collaborating research domains,which are based on 12 very well-established interdisciplinary key research topics.
The University is at the centre of the science location that is Greifswald and works together closely with the four internationally renowned external research institutions in the town, the Federal Research Institute for Animal Health (FLI), the Leibniz Institute for Plasma Science and Technology (INP),the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP), and the Helmholtz Institute for One Health (HIOH). The University is also a benefactor of the Alfried Krupp Wissenschaftskolleg Greifswald (Institute for Advanced Studies), which supports research and teaching at the University of Greifswald by inviting national and international fellows to Greifswald for periods of research and holds conferences and lectures.
The University of Greifswald sets itself high standards for good teaching. It offers outstanding study conditions in modern buildings and arduously restored historical buildings with an excellent infrastructure for research-led teaching. Small groups and passionate teaching staff guarantee intensive supervision of the students. Five faculties offer a broad range of subjects with a total of 131 possible degree courses, several of which are interdisciplinary, and 13 continuing education courses.
A proven quality assurance system encourages the high quality of teaching through regular external and internal evaluations of the degree courses and student feedback. The University received its system accreditation in 2015 and is taking part in several audit procedures.
The University of Greifswald has a positive effect on the town and the region. It is a major catalyst for the economic and social development of the region and the state. By holding Idea Competitions and putting material and structural measures into effect, the University supports the start-up culture and the transfer of research results to the industry. At the same time, it uses its applied research to tackle specific challenges of the rural region, such as the problems regarding the provision of healthcare in structurally weak regions.
The University shapes and enriches the life and culture in the historic Hanseatic town of Greifswald with its academic ceremonies and culture festivals, student clubs and initiatives, international events, broad and diverse academic communication with the general public and its members’ high levels of active citizenship.

Shobolinsky SRL is an engineering company developing modular electronics, embedded computing platforms, robotics systems, and applied AI solutions for research and early stage technology development. Our work is built on fast iteration, practical testing, and an inventive approach to solving technical constraints. This has allowed us to produce reliable hardware in situations where conventional methods would not have delivered results.
Our portfolio includes custom microcontroller and compute modules, sensing systems, low power communication platforms, and onboard data processing architectures designed for autonomous and intelligent operation in constrained environments. We also develop compact AI models and lightweight acceleration techniques that enable real time classification, prediction, and signal processing on embedded devices.
The team has participated in ESA aligned workshops, research events, and collaborative activities that provided exposure to space focused engineering workflows. In parallel, we have gained hands on experience through student robotics projects and the development of multiple CanSat missions, which strengthened our abilities in system integration, sensing, communication, and rapid prototyping.
Shobolinsky maintains a compact in house research and development environment in Romania where we handle design, validation, and small batch manufacturing. This setup allows us to work efficiently and iterate quickly while maintaining professional engineering standards. Our long term goal is to grow our modular hardware and AI platforms into dependable tools for education, applied research, and early stage space related technology development. We aim to build practical systems that scale toward more demanding environments through disciplined engineering and continuous improvement.

entityName: EROFIO Engenharia e Fabricação de Moldes SA
description:
EROFIO Additive is one of Europe’s most advanced metal additive manufacturing centres, integrated within EROFIO’s long-established mould-making and high-precision engineering ecosystem. The company has been incorporating metal Additive Manufacturing into its tooling processes since 2011, enabling the production of conformal-cooled mould inserts and complex functional components long before AM became mainstream.
The additive division operates multiple L-PBF systems:
•	GE Concept Laser MLINE (500 × 500 × 500 mm, 4 × 400 W) – a large-format, serial-production machine for Corrax parts.
•	Concept Laser M2 (250 × 250 × 300 mm, 400 W) – optimized for 1.2709 and Corrax inserts with conformal cooling, high-strength structures, and advanced thermal management.
•	Concept Laser M3 (350 × 250 × 200 mm, 100 W) – for fine-feature components and engraving.
The portfolio expands in 2025 with the DMG-MORI LASERTEC 30 SLM 3rd Gen, supporting AlSi10Mg, Ti6Al4V and Mar55, powered by 4 × 1000 W lasers for high productivity and multi-material capability.
EROFIO also operates a DMG-MORI LASERTEC 65 DED Hybrid (735 × 650 × 560 mm), combining 5-axis machining and DED deposition for multi-material builds, large components, functional repairs and copper-enhanced thermal systems—unique in Europe.
Engineering capabilities include CFD/rheological simulation (SIGMASOFT), structural analysis (ANSYS), and topology optimization (nTop), ensuring that moulds and technical components are fully optimized before manufacturing. Extensive post-processing—heat treatment, machining/EDM, blasting and polishing—delivers aerospace-grade quality.
Through the integration of mould-making expertise and more than a decade of AM innovation, EROFIO delivers end-to-end metal additive solutions for conformal-cooled tooling, lightweight structures, thermal components and high-precision industrial and space-grade applications.

Advanced Microturbines is a spin-off company of the Italian Institute of Technology (IIT) in Genoa, Italy. It was established in April 2013, after winning the National Prize for Innovation and a startup business training period of the founder in Silicon Valley, the company.
Advanced Microturbines Srl is dedicated to the commercialisation of the microturbine technology, the result of a 2-year research programme at the Italian Institute of Technology on high-speed micro-turbomachinery, and turning it into a market-ready product as a power supply solution for off-grid applications, based on the microturbine as the enabling technology. 
The gas-driven microturbine has reached TRL9, being fully tested, CE marked. certified for operation in hazardous environments (ATEX) and installed in a number of sites, with sales and strong commercial interest received from utility companies, and IoT suppliers in EU countries. description: Kili Technology is a leading enterprise-grade Training Data Management Platform (TDMP) designed to help organizations move from raw data to high-performance AI models. While many tools focus solely on "labeling," Kili positions itself as a central hub for the entire data-centric AI lifecycle: from initial curation and annotation to quality control and model iteration. For the Aerospace and Defense industry, where data is often massive, sensitive, and technically complex, Kili offers a specialized environment that addresses challenges general-purpose tools cannot. Key Differentiators for the Aerospace Industry In the aerospace sector, the "cost of error" is exceptionally high—whether it’s identifying a structural defect in a turbine or a target in satellite imagery. Kili’s platform is built around three core pillars that cater specifically to these high-stakes requirements: 1. Advanced Geospatial & High-Res Capability Aerospace projects rely heavily on Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT). Kili provides native support for ultra-high-resolution satellite and aerial imagery (including TIF and multi-spectral formats). Tiling & Performance: It can handle massive files without lag, allowing annotators to zoom into centimeter-level details (e.g., identifying specific aircraft models or infrastructure damage). Specialized Tooling: Features like Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2) integration allow for rapid, pixel-perfect masking of complex objects like runways, forests, or moving vehicles in video feeds. 2. "Defense-Grade" Security & Compliance Security is often the primary barrier for aerospace companies. Kili is one of the few platforms that offers deployment flexibility tailored for regulated environments: On-Premise & Air-Gapped: For classified missions, Kili can be deployed completely offline or within a private cloud (AWS GovCloud, Azure Government), ensuring that sensitive data never leaves the organization’s secure perimeter. Certifications: The platform is SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and HIPAA compliant, meeting the stringent data governance standards required by defense contractors and government agencies. 3. Programmatic Quality & Expert Collaboration Aerospace data often requires Subject Matter Expertise (SME)—for example, a maintenance engineer must label engine cracks, or an intelligence officer must label military hardware. Consensus & Honey-Potting: Kili uses "consensus" workflows where multiple experts label the same asset to ensure ground-truth accuracy. Programmatic QA: Instead of manual spot-checks, users can write Python scripts (via Kili’s SDK) to automatically flag anomalies, such as a "plane" labeled in the middle of an ocean, significantly reducing the "garbage in, garbage out" risk in safety-critical systems.
entityDescription:
Today's challenge to train machine learning models is not to get the data itself - but to get the clean labelled data - to avoid having a "garbage in garbage out" loop. While current evolution in AI is powered by machine learning models, this process of data annotation becomes critical. Moreover, even more challenging is getting the know-how to get the most efficient, most flexible, and most cost-effective way to label these data to scale up the projects.

entityDescription: The Institute for Ethnic Studies is one of the oldest interdisciplinary institutes in Europe. It was established in 1925 with the aim to produce the relevant statistics and mapping for the Slovene-speaking population left in Italy after the demise of Austro-Hungary. With the formation of the Socialist Yugoslavia in 1945, the institute took the leading role in demographic analysis of the national minorities. After the independence of Slovenia in 1991, the institute broadened its scope of analyses to international and internal migration and especially to vulnerable groups of population in the more peripheric regions of Slovenia. The Institute carried out numerous national and international projects and was part of transnational consortia in many interdisciplinary subfields of research.

SatRev, headquartered in Wroclaw, Poland, is a leading NewSpace company focused on providing sovereign satellite solutions and end-to-end space mission services. entityDescription:
To address the challenges in the implementation of machine learning, ADAGOS has developed NeurEco. A new neural network approach based on parsimony.
NeurEco reduces the resources (size of learning data, energy consumption, size of neural network and memory requirement, computing time, development time) required to implement machine learning methods by several orders of magnitude when compared with the current state of the art.
Their first significant fields of application are embedded systems and the Internet of Things. By achieving the smallest sufficient network structure, they minimize the network’s battery consumption and make it possible to embed AI on small devices and to increase their autonomy. Thanks to its parsimony, NeurEco requires less data for learning. It is even possible to embed the learning process and to update the neural network on the fly, avoiding the need for waiting weeks and months to collect enough data.
Their second major field of application is healthcare. Thanks to parsimony, any prediction given by ADAGOS’s neural networks comes with a clear explanation

entityDescription:
The non-profit foundation Urban Street Forest (USF) was founded on 19th of February 2016, registered at the Chamber of Commerce (KvK) of Amsterdam in Holland with the registry number 65388259. The foundation holds the status of a non-profit organisation (the Dutch “ANBI” status) and is accredited to the Conference of the Parties to the UNCCD (United Nations Convention to Combat Deserfication):
https://www.unccd.int/cso/urban-street-forest-foundation

The main USF objective is to plant as many trees as possible for the large-scale restoration of landscapes in countries suffering from desertification, and also in urban areas. Tree planting is preferably carried out together with local farmers involved in agroforestry projects, or local tree planting organisations.

Thanks to the planting of trees & our sponsors, USF has auto-finanzed the development of a web-app MRV platform named TreeWallet (TRL 6-7) using 100% open-source technologies, that has allowed us to register online all the single small trees that we have pianted registering its specie, photo, planting date and geo-position in whatever place of the world. Our prototype has been demonstrated in 2021-2025 with ~100 users, registering ~85.000 new trees on TreeWallet (in Spain, Holland, Morocco, Tanzania, Uganda) planting ~30 native tree species specific to each country, of which 50% are fruit trees:
https://app.treewallet.eu/public

Mission:
The mission of USF is to restore the ecological, social and economic potential of landscapes, by planting trees with local farmers, communities and partner organisations.

Vision:
We see an important role for companies to help restore degraded landscapes worldwide by supporting restorative and productive tree-planting projects. We envision a world where there is ecological, social and economic health. We see tree-planting as crucial to achieve this goal.

Strategy:
USF connects corporations and other sponsors who want to help restore landscapes/plant trees with landowners and planters in tree-planting projects, currently in the Netherlands, Spain and sub-Saharan African countries. We help corporations and other sponsors to use a sustainable approach when offsetting carbon, by steering tree-planting projects also on other environmental, social and economic benefits. USF provides accountability/proof of work of the planted trees by giving information such as the GPS location, a photo and the name of the planter, thus providing a transparent proof of work and direct connection with our planting partner on the ground.

entityName: Genius loci, obrt za edukacije, prostorne analize, strateško planiranje i GIS usluge, vl. Patricija Velečki
entityDescription:
Genius Loci is a sole proprietorship founded and managed by Patricija Velečki, MSc in Geography, specialising in Spatial Planning and Regional Development. The degree was obtained in 2025 at the Faculty of Science, University of Zagreb.
Through academic education and professional development, the founder has built strong expertise in spatial analysis, GIS technologies and sustainable development. This knowledge has been continuously expanded through active participation in numerous scientific conferences and congresses, where she has contributed as both an author and presenter of professional and scientific papers.
In addition to her geographical and technical competencies, the founder has completed pedagogical, psychological, didactic and methodological training at the Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences in Osijek, qualifying her to work in primary and secondary education. Practical experience gained through school-based and field activities (such as environmental actions, orientation sports and educational workshops for children) has further strengthened her ability to design and deliver educational content tailored to different age groups.
In her professional work, Patricija Velečki combines:
extensive experience in GIS software (QGIS, ArcGIS),

scientific and research skills, including data processing, analysis and academic writing,

communication with diverse user groups, ranging from pupils and parents to professionals from various sectors.

Particular emphasis is placed on interdisciplinary cooperation, based on the belief that the most sustainable and functional spatial solutions emerge through collaboration between experts from different fields, each contributing their unique perspective.
The mission of Genius Loci is to connect space, knowledge and social value through education, professional spatial analyses, visualisation of spatial data and support for projects in both the public and private sectors. The entity is founded on the concept of genius loci – the spirit of place – recognising that space is never neutral or empty, but shaped by its natural characteristics, history, people, landscapes and everyday functions.
Rather than applying standardised solutions, Genius Loci adopts an individual and context-sensitive approach to each spatial setting. Every analysis and proposal respects the local identity, social context and symbolic value of space, whether dealing with settlements, rural areas, cultural landscapes or urban cores.
Genius Loci commenced its operations on 8 September 2025, with the aim of contributing to more thoughtful, sustainable and meaningful spatial development by listening to space, not merely drawing it.

The mission of Genius Loci is to connect space, knowledge and social value through education, professional spatial analyses, visualisation of spatial data and support for projects in both the public and private sectors. The entity is founded on the concept of genius loci – the spirit of place – recognising that space is never neutral or empty, but shaped by its natural characteristics, history, people, landscapes and everyday functions.
Rather than applying standardised solutions, Genius Loci adopts an individual and context-sensitive approach to each spatial setting. Every analysis and proposal respects the local identity, social context and symbolic value of space, whether dealing with settlements, rural areas, cultural landscapes or urban cores.
Genius Loci commenced its operations on 8 September 2025, with the aim of contributing to more thoughtful, sustainable and meaningful spatial development by listening to space, not merely drawing it.

entityDescription:
KineMo uses AI to accurately track and quantify in 3D the movement of an individuals joints during exercise and rehabilitation, just using video from a single camera device. How an individual moves is critical to their safe athletic development, rehabilitation & recovery from injury and progression of specific movement competency skillsets.
KineMo’s innovation has been validated through peer-reviewed studies and collaborations with top sports, performance, health & wellness organizations around the world.
Accurately tracking and quantifying human motion has traditionally required a biomechanics lab or costly marker-based systems. As a result, most professionals (Trainers, Coaches, Physio’s etc.) simply rely on subjective observation techniques which are not quantified and are prone to bias. KineMo bridges this gap with its simple to use, accurate and scalable technology, which transforms single-camera videos into detailed 3D joint-angle analyses. This enables on demand feedback during athletic development, rehabilitation, and skills progression, making high-quality biomechanical insights accessible to professionals and athletes worldwide.

entityDescription:
IntuitivAnalytix.com (IAG) specializes in Geographic Analytics (GA), Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Data Analytics, Data Science, and Artificial Intelligence. IAG offers consulting and software in these areas.
IAG follows a „starting with the end in mind”, business-canvas-driven methodology to quickly derive market-oriented hands-on recommendations. This allows IAG to achieve results in 20% of the time compared to traditional data analytics driven approaches. At the same time, IAG puts great emphasis on transparency and intuitive understanding of data.
​IAG leverages satellite imaging paired with pattern / image recognition and AI to drive easy-to-use and intuitive spatial management decision systems. We aim to replace complex & expensive ground-based management systems with highly cost and time-efficient space observations. 
The project ESA-GEOCAP aims at establishing a Data-as-a-Service platform combining satellite-based air-pollution indicators with Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) data to analyze geo-correlations between environmental factors and CAP. With this, IAG enables decision makers in the Public Health Sector (i.e. Health Insurers, Hospitals, government agencies) to find new connections between air-pollutants and CAP in order to take appropriate countermeasures.

entityDescription: At Orcintech, we combine big data analytics, cloud computing, and AI to deliver actionable insights for environmental and infrastructure sustainability. Our platform integrates satellite imagery, drone footage, IoT sensor networks, and GIS-based predictive modeling to generate detailed ecological reports and conservation strategies. As an example, in 2025, Orcintech was awarded a contract by the Canadian Space Agency (CSA) for developing an AI-powered cloud-based multi-technology platform to prevent moose-vehicle collisions and protect biodiversity. This project will reduce accidents, improve conservation, and support sustainable infrastructure. By integrating community knowledge with cutting-edge technology, including satellite data, drone imageries, and IoT sensors for safer roads while protecting Canada’s biodiversity. Orcintech’s TerraXai Cloud-Intelligent Platform is a cutting-edge, cloud-based system that fuses AI and Remote Sensing (RS) for near real-time environmental decision intelligence. Designed as a fully cloud-native, AI-driven system, TerraXai integrates multi-source data streams, including satellite imagery, aerial and UAV datasets, IoT telemetry, and ground-based sensors, within a unified data fabric and governance framework. Through its agentic AI pipeline, the platform automates every stage of the data lifecycle: from ingestion and benchmarking to model training, validation, and autonomous deployment. This architecture enables continuous, stream-based data processing and event analytics, allowing users to generate nearreal-time insights into environmental nd infrastructure resilience. TerraXai’s modular design ensures flexibility and scalability, supporting applications that range from land reclamation monitoring to disasterresponse, habitat mapping, and climate-risk assessment. The uniqueness of TerraXai lies in its AI-driven Decision Intelligence Suite, designed to synthesize multi-source geospatial data into interpretable and operational environmental intelligence. Integrated analytic modules, including vegetation intelligence and biomass analytics, wildfire prediction and early-warning systems, and wildlife management and ecosystem resilience assessment, provide end-to-end situational awareness for environmental managers, regulators, and researchers. The platform’s secure data dissemination and edge-synchronization architecture enables seamless collaboration between cloud and field operations, ensuring real-time information exchange, rapid decision-making, and streamlined regulatory reporting. By uniting AI, Earth Observation (EO), and cloud computing within a single, intelligent ecosystem, TerraXai delivers unmatched analytical depth, transparency, and operational agility. This powerful integration positions Orcintech at the forefront of digital environmental intelligence, driving innovation in sustainable land management and evidence-based environmental stewardship.

entityName: L-Universita' ta' Malta - Dept. of Anatomy
entityDescription:
The Anatomy Department, situated on campus, is one of the first departments to welcome students starting the Medical course. The Anatomy Department also services the B.Pharm. and Medical Biochemistry courses within the Faculty of Medicine and Surgery, as well as most of the paramedical courses within the Faculty of Health Sciences, both at under- and post- graduate level. The Department of Anatomy also collaborates with the Faculty of Dental Surgery and the Faculty of Engineering.

The Department hosts a Lecture Hall, a Histology Demonstration Lab equipped with audiovisual equipment, two Dissection halls with a depository of prosected specimens, Living Anatomy demonstration rooms, and a number of rooms for small group tutorial discussion sessions. A facility is also available for quiet study.

Tuition within the Department of Anatomy has shifted to emphasize the applied aspect of Anatomy. Clinicians from various clinical fields including different specialities of surgery, general practice, obstetrics and gynaecology, pathology, forensics and cytogenetics are involved in teaching at all levels together with specialist academics. Clinical visits to various departments in the nearby Mater Dei Hospital are also held, to help illustrate the clinical relevance of the subject.

The Department of Anatomy carries out Biomedical Research into local natural products. Other areas of interest include embryology, cytogenetics and epidemiology of birth defects, stem cell and cancer differentiation, gene regulation and pedagogical research. Collaborations with various European and International universities and hospitals are ongoing and around 30% of the student body who make use of the Anatomy Department are International Students studying in Malta.

Osmos X is a French space startup that aims to develop multi-purpose Orbital Transfer Vehicles (or OTVs) based on a multi-charged electro-plasmic propulsion technology. It offers a considerable improvement specific impulse compared with existing electric technologies (HET, GIT) and boasts operational features that are ideal for space operations:
- Flexibility: continuous or pulsed operation
- Adjustability: selectable ion charge state and velocity, offering adjustable intensity and thus variable thrust.

These caracteristics position our technology as a enabler of profitable in-space logistics missions (last mile delivery, satellite repositioning, deorbiting).

description: Astroport develops autonomous construction technologies and architectural solutions for lunar infrastructure. entityDescription:
Waves of Change is a non-profit coalition based in Biarritz, France, founded in 2019. Its mission is to help coastal cities around the world become “future proof” by fostering sustainable and resilient development of their ecosystems. The organization brings together a diverse set of stakeholders — including startups, research centers, corporations, NGOs, public-sector actors, investors, and local communities — to collaborate on environmental challenges.

Waves of Change focuses on seven main areas (verticals): coastal adaptation, water management, waste & circularity, sustainable mobility, energy transition, sustainable tourism & local communities, and biodiversity & public health.
It also supports two horizontal dimensions: talent development and funding, to ensure long-term viability and innovation capacity.
Some of their past initiatives include: creating a system for marine pollution monitoring and bioremediation, electrifying quayside logistics in a major port, organizing plastic-waste collection and recycling in the Global South, and developing low-cost water-supply solutions for coastal regions under water stress.

entityDescription:
The American College of Greece Research Center (ACG-RC), a not-for-profit Research Center, acts as a platform for the promotion of research and innovation in the fields studied and taught in schools and divisions of The American College of Greece (ACG). These areas of inquiry range from the natural, social, and computational sciences to technology (including telecom networks, AI, cybersecurity, and space technology), education and communications, as well as the liberal and fine arts.
ACG-RC fosters a diverse range of research, learning and innovation-oriented activities, hosts researchers and scholars from different countries and backgrounds, participates in collaborative projects — such as research grants funded by various entities — and collaborates with an array of partners from the academic, research, industrial, non-governmental and other domains. ACG-RC serves as the prime vehicle for hosting the funded research activities (such as European Union funded projects) involving the faculty members of all ACG’s educational divisions, as well as the members and fellows of ACG’s Institutes, Centers of Excellence and other units. Since 2022, ACG- RC obtained a considerable number of EU grants from various funding schemes and calls (indicatively, Horizon Europe, Maria Skłodowska-Curie, Erasmus +, Interreg, EIT-Food) in research areas such as food and nutrition, tourism and hospitality, special planning, sports management, transportation, shipping and energy, and engineering, just to mention a few.

Founded in Smyrna, Asia Minor, in 1875, by missionaries from Boston, Massachusetts, The American College of Greece (ACG) is the oldest and largest US accredited college or university in Europe. For almost 150 years, ACG has been offering transformative education and cultivating a fertile intellectual and cultural collaboration between Greece and the United States.
ACG is an independent, not for profit, nonsectarian, co-educational academic institution with, currently, three divisions: Pierce (a premier, co-educational primary and secondary school (grades Pre K -12), offering both a Greek-based national curriculum – Elementary, Gymnasium & Lyceum – and an International Baccalaureate Diploma Program), Deree (undergraduate programs in liberal arts and sciences, business, fine and performing arts as well as graduate programs in the arts and sciences), & Alba Graduate Business School (MBA and MSc degrees in specialized areas of business and management as well as an extensive Executive Education program).

entityDescription:
QuDef is a pioneering firm specializing in quantum technology security. It focuses on the security of quantum systems and networks themselves. Our mission is to enable a faster adoption of quantum technology by providing innovative services and products that enable the seamless, but moreover, secure integration of quantum communication and computing into existing classical infrastructure.
QuDef focuses on the following three pillars:
- SQOUT, our quantum threat and intelligence tool which can be used by end-users to perform security analyses on their quantum system.
- Quantum Security Monitoring systems, aiming to continuously monitor and investigate events happening in a quantum system or network and identify which attacks are potentially taking place.
- Providing consultancy and intelligence services using our expertise in quantum technology threat intelligence, comprehensive security assessments, and strategic consulting. Our key focus areas include quantum communication, military applications of quantum technology, and intelligence on emerging quantum developments.

entityDescription:
The Instituto de Fomento de la Región de Murcia (INFO) is the Regional Development Agency, a Public Entity linked to the Regional Ministry for Enterprises. Its main objective is to promote regional economic growth and competitiveness in the Region of Murcia by boosting its Economy, increasing investment, removing obstacles and establishing an environment that favours competitiveness. INFO focuses on the following lines of action:

- Research & Innovation - promoting technological development ensuring that each company can access the technology that best suits its needs.
- Internationalisation - For boosting international corporate expansion through the Foreign Trade Promotion Plan.
- Investment - For promoting investment, development and growth projects by providing companies from inside and outside the Region with information and consultancy services.
- Entrepreneurship - Support for entrepreneurs, creation, consolidation and transfer of companies.
- Access to finance - For helping businesses to access lines of finance for investments in assets, quality, technology, internationalisation and industrial equipment.

INFO provides personalised advice throughout the lifecycle of regional SMEs and from different approaches: R+D+i, technology transfer, new technologies, ICT transformation, internationalisation and access to finance.

Also, as the leading regional institution for entrepreneurship promotion and business creation, plus a strong political commitment to entrepreneurship and business development, INFO offers institutional, technical and specialised support for entrepreneurs and business starts up, carrying out specific actions to support business creation and entrepreneurs, and supporting the regional innovation ecosystem by developing synergies between companies, universities, technological and research centres and the regional government.

Moreover, INFO offers personalised and integrated consultancy services in the field of access to finance for SMEs, entrepreneurs, internationalisation, investors, innovation, EU programmes and infrastructures.Financial aid is tailored to support entrepreneurial initiatives and satisfy the needs of consolidated companies. In joint operation with financial entities and other public bodies, various support lines are offered consisting of non-refundable grants, microcredits and other financial instruments such as Loan Guarantee and Venture Capital schemes, amongst others.

INFO has extensive expertise and technical capacity in EU funding management. It has been the leading intermediary organisation in charge of implementing a Global Grant from ERDF in the European Union since 1990. INFO is also the regional leader and coordinator of the Research and Innovation Smart Specialization Strategy (RIS4 Región de Murcia).

INFO works to facilitate the participation of regional companies and intermediate business organisations in EU funding programmes.
INFO participates in a wide variety of EU projects in a range of areas including regional economic development, business innovation, entrepreneurship support, cluster promotion, etc., and in the framework of different EU programmes such as Horizon Europe, EDF, COSME, LIFE and Interreg.

Currently leading CAETRA Programme, boosting a regional Dual-use Technologies Ecosystem for Defence, Security, Reconstruction and Development. Within this framework, a specific Aerospace Hub Incubator is being developed close to San Javier's Military Air Base in the Region of Murcia.

i‑4P is a European systems partner specialising in mission‑critical communications and edge‑data infrastructure for space ground segment, defence, critical national infrastructure and emergency services. description:
Software for Satellite Operations and Space Cybersecurity

Spaceit provides software and services for satellite operations and space cybersecurity. Founded in 2015, Spaceit makes space access affordable through efficient resource utilization, extensive ground station networks, and a flexible pay-as-you-go pricing model. Their platform ensures satellite missions benefit from automated operations, low latency, high data rates, and robust security. 
Spaceit's key offerings include: 
1. Mission Operations Platform: Enables comprehensive satellite operations management, including satellite monitoring, command and control (C2), telemetry, data handling, and communication. Available as both a cloud-based and on-site solution, it supports various satellite protocols. 
2. Marketplace for Ground Station Services: Integrates standalone ground stations along with virtual and physical networks into a unified ecosystem. It enables users to orchestrate different ground stations, to book services, manage contacts, and communicate with satellites across multiple networks—radio and optical—within a single platform. This ensures seamless mission operations and near-real-time connectivity. 
3. The Space Cyber Range: Provides a virtual environment for testing, validation, and certification of various space assets and processes. Cybersecurity training and exercises. Industry knowledge sharing and networking. Developed in collaboration with ESA, it delivers safe and cost-effective services for the space industry and its related sectors. 
Spaceit operates OPS-SAT ORIOLE, a 16U OPS-SAT satellite mission backed by ESA, set to launch in 2026. The mission will feature an In-Orbit Demonstration (IOD) of a hybrid optical telecommunication and thermal infrared camera as its primary payload. The mission seeks to demonstrate the full duplex optical telecommunication capabilities from space to ground, with potential expansion to space-to-space communication.

entityDescription:
EurA Sofia EOOD is a Bulgarian-registered single-member limited liability company and the official subsidiary of EurA AG, a recognised European provider of innovation, technology, and funding consultancy services. The company operates from Synergy Tower within Sofia Tech Park and functions as the regional representation of the EurA Group in Bulgaria and South-Eastern Europe. As part of this pan-European network, EurA Sofia applies established consultancy standards, structured methodologies, and multidisciplinary expertise in support of innovation-driven organisations.
EurA Sofia’s core mandate is to deliver professional services across the full spectrum of the innovation lifecycle. These services include the formulation and structuring of R&D and innovation projects, preparation of funding proposals, coordination of consortia, implementation of project management tasks, and development of strategies for market entry, technology transfer, and exploitation of project results. The company has extensive experience with EU funding programmes, including Horizon Europe, the European Innovation Council, Digital Europe, ERDF initiatives, LIFE, and other national and international mechanisms.
The organisation provides specialised competencies in sustainability and green transition advisory, circular economy strategies, environmental assessment, and alignment with EU Green Deal objectives. Through its integrated approach, EurA Sofia supports beneficiaries in achieving technical, commercial, and regulatory readiness levels required for successful project execution and market uptake.
EurA Sofia operates with an in-depth understanding of the Bulgarian innovation ecosystem and the wider SEE region, complemented by direct access to EurA AG’s European network of experts, academic institutions, industrial partners, and innovation stakeholders. This positioning enables the company to facilitate cross-border collaboration, strengthen consortium capacity, and contribute to the successful delivery of complex, multi-actor projects.
In tendered assignments, EurA Sofia typically assumes roles related to project design, proposal development, work package leadership, exploitation and dissemination planning, stakeholder engagement, market analysis, and sustainability advisory. The company acts in accordance with established quality management practices, ethical guidelines, and EU requirements for professional integrity, transparency, and data protection.
EurA employees have been active in the space industry both nationally and internationally for over 30 years. The EurA office in Aachen has been a very successful part of ESA Technology Broker Germany for several years and acts as the head of the ESA SparkFunding program. In addition, EurA in Aachen manages the ESA BIC North Rhine-Westphalia. For many years, EurA has also managed the cross-industry networks Space2Motion, Space2Agriculture, and Space2Health, as well as the Copernicus municipal project for the DLR Space Agency.

entityDescription:
Institute for Driver Assistance and Connected Mobility (IFM) of Kempten University: 
Assisted and automated driving, electric mobility and smart networking are megatrends in the automotive industry that herald major upheaval. Sponsored by the Free State of Bavaria, the recently formed IFM pools research into the fields ofAdvanced Driver Assistance SystemsandConnected Mobility. The Institute’s activities focus on:
- Developing methods and specifications for new driver assistance systems
- Holistic simulation
- Checking and validating safety and reliability
- Connected mobility
The IFM has immediate access to an adjacent test site and can thus activate numerous projects advancing driver assistance, automated driving and connected mobility. The Institute cooperates with other application-focused partners (e.g. Munich University of Applied Sciences), but also institutions oriented more towards basic research (e.g. Technical University of Munich).
At the same time, we are keen to expand collaboration efforts with industrial companies, who in such an innovative field of work greatly require research and development and need both well-trained young staff and research capacity and expertise.

entityDescription:
autonomIQ is a deep-tech startup founded by engineers and AI specialists from TU Darmstadt, developing simplymill—an autonomous, AI-driven CAM system designed to transform how complex metal components are manufactured. The company targets the upstream space domain, where suppliers must machine highly precise, small-batch parts from materials such as titanium or Inconel under demanding time and quality constraints. simplymill automatically analyzes 3D CAD models and generates optimized machining strategies and NC programs, drastically reducing programming time and increasing process reliability.
The solution leverages space-related benefits by addressing a critical bottleneck in the production of spacecraft structures, propulsion components, and satellite housings: long, manual CAM planning. By enabling faster preparation and more consistent machining, simplymill helps reduce lead times and stabilize supply chains in space manufacturing. Pilot collaborations with space-industry suppliers will validate the system under real conditions, including tight tolerances, complex clamping setups, and traceability requirements. Through ESA-BIC support, autonomIQ aims to bring its prototype to commercial readiness and establish autonomous CAM as a new standard in space component production.

entityDescription:
HUN-REN SZTAKI is a research institute, governed by the Hungarian Research Network (HUN-REN).
SZTAKI is theacronymof the Hungarian name of the institute, while its full English name is "Institute for Computer Science and Control".
The Institute was founded in 1964. Its staff consists of more than 300 full-time employees, more than 200 with university diploma and more than 70 with scientific degrees.
The fundamental task of the Institute is to perform basic and application-oriented research in an interdisciplinary setting in the fields of computer science, engineering, information technology, intelligent systems, process control, wide-area networking and multimedia.
Contract-based target research, development, training and expert support for domestic and foreign industrial, governmental and other partners are important activities at the Institute.
The mission of HUN-REN SZTAKI includes the transfer of up-to-date research results and state-of-the-art technology to university students. The Institute is very active in graduate and postgraduate education, co-operating with most technical universities in Hungary and operating common chairs, postgraduate programs with them. More than 40 members of the Institute’s researchers conduct regular lectures/classes at graduate and postgraduate levels, and senior researchers hold part-time positions as university professors. 20-30 Ph.D. students and 20-30 graduate students participate in the work of the Institute.

entityDescription:
In 1992, Transsolar KlimaEngineering was founded by Thomas Lechner, Matthias Schuler and Peter Voit in Stuttgart. Three pillars to the practice were, and still are: To follow an integrated design process, knowing that this process leads to the most successful solutions; to constantly question assumptions and conventions, knowing that building performance can always be improved; to substantiate our design concepts with sound technical analysis. We started off believing that a successful, sustainable building included not only a low energy footprint, but also high user comfort.
By working collaboratively with clients, architects, mechanical engineers, and other consultants from the earliest stages of the building design process, we consider each step from the standpoint of fundamental thermodynamics and physics. This generates a solution in which local conditions, form, material, and mechanical systems are integrated components of a well-orchestrated climate control system which reduces operating costs while increasing occupant comfort. Our work considers more than energy conservation based upon optimizing thermal properties of the building envelope and efficiency of technical equipment.
We seek a more holistic design recognizing the interdependence of factors affecting comfort. We address air temperature, natural ventilation as well as air quality, acoustics, daylight, material and the well-being of people – the human scale.

entityDescription:
Bioversity delivers research-based solutions that address the global crises of malnutrition, climate change, biodiversity loss, and environmental degradation. The Center focuses on the nexus of agriculture, the environment and nutrition. We work with local, national, and multinational partners across Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, and with the public and private sectors and civil society. With novel partnerships, Bioversity generates evidence and mainstreams innovations to transform food systems and landscapes so that they sustain the planet, drive prosperity and nourish people in a climate crisis.
Bioversity is part of the Alliance Bioversity CIAT through the Partnership Agreement between the two international Centers, in force since January 1, 2020, having a director general and a common board of trustees as part of its governance structure. The objective of the Alliance is to have a common operational framework, governance and a research strategy with the mission to deliver research-based solutions that harness agricultural biodiversity and sustainably transform food systems and landscapes to improve people’s lives. This Alliance is being built upon the two current organizations and the hosting agreements both institutions have with Italy and Colombia correspondingly; therefore, both centers will still be independent entities, while operating under a single Board of Trustees, one Director General and one Strategy.

entityDescription:
Data for Sustainability is an independent research consultancy, specialized in environmental remote sensing, which started in 2020.

Vision
Natural systems are degraded globally by human activities. Tropical coastlines, peatlands and other wetlands especially are hotspots of rapid decline through logging and drainage, while also suffering from sea-level rise and soil subsidence. Improved understanding of such vulnerable systems is required to define management requirements to deal with future threats, but is often limited by data availability for practitioners. Data providers are often either consultants focused on profit maximization or scientists focused on research maximization. We aim to maximize benefits for sustainable wetland management and conservation by providing innovative data and analyses while minimizing cost and time requirements where possible.

Activities and products
Remote sensing data: We collect, analyze and apply a range of publicly available satellite datasets, as well as airborne LiDAR data on a project basis, to create innovative products. Products to date include global and regional datasets of elevation, peat thickness / carbon, water depth and flood risk that we place in the public domain when possible, and refined local datasets tailored to suit requirements on a paid project basis. Our focus area is SE Asia that has the most extensive and degraded coastal lowlands, but we can apply our methods anywhere.
Peatland restoration project support: We work with projects that aim to conserve or restore degraded peatland forest systems in SE Asia, by applying our data to quantify hydrological impacts, carbon stocks and carbon losses for specific areas. We also help identify and design restoration solutions.

entityName: University of Nova Gorica - Center for Astrophysics and Cosmology
entityDescription:
The Center for Astrophysics and Cosmology (CAC) at the University of Nova Gorica (UNG) is a vibrant hub for high-energy, multi-messenger astrophysics research. As the largest Slovenian research group in this field, CAC plays an active role in a number of international collaborations, trains the next generation of researchers, and strongly engages in public outreach. In doing so, it not only pushes the boundaries of fundamental science but also strengthens Slovenia’s presence in global research activities. CAC aims to apply the multi-messenger approach – combining information carried by different cosmic messengers such as photons, charged particles, neutrinos, and gravitational waves – to reveal high-energy phenomena and fundamental processes. This approach is further enhanced by the use of advanced machine-learning techniques. The center’s research focuses on the sources and properties of ultra-high energy cosmic rays, transient astrophysical phenomena (including gamma-ray bursts, neutron star/black hole mergers, and tidal disruption events) and dark matter physics and the matter-antimatter asymmetry of the Universe.
CAC is located on the UNG campus in Ajdovščina, in the Vipava Valley of southwestern Slovenia, close to the Italian border. Ajdovščina is a rapidly growing industrial hub, hosting high-tech businesses in aeronautics, the food industry, and chemical engineering. Ajdovščina boasts rich history, dating back to the days of the Roman Empire. Around the year 270 AD, the Romans erected a fortress with defensive towers on its grounds, known as Castra ad Fluvium Frigidum (fortress at the Cold River – Hubelj), which formed a part of an Ancient Roman defensive system known as Claustra Alpium Iuliarum. A pivotal historical event was the Battle at Frigidus on September 5th and 6th, 394 AD, between today's Vrhpolje and Ajdovščina. Assisted by powerful Bora wind, the Eastern Roman Emperor Theodosius emerged victorious over the Western Roman throne usurper, Eugenius. This strategic location enables close collaboration with Italian institutions, including SISSA, ICTP, and Università degli Studi di Trieste.
The CAC team comprises of permanent faculty members, postdoctoral researchers and PhD students, forming a vibrant and interdisciplinary research community.
The center is involved several prominent international projects, including the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory, Pierre Auger Observatory, Vera C. Rubin Observatory, Fermi-LAT, Gaia, Liverpool Telescope, and ENGRAVE. CAC leads the Marie Sklodowska-Curie COFUND project SMASH, within which novel machine-learning applications for science and the humanities are being developed, and through the TALES Doctoral Network, the center hosts a PhD student investigating tidal disruption events using Rubin Observatory data and advanced machine-learning techniques.
Looking ahead, CAC aims to further expand its multi-messenger astronomy research - combining cosmic rays, gamma rays, neutrinos, and gravitational waves to explore extreme astrophysical phenomena - by developing and applying advanced data analysis techniques based on machine learning and modern data science. Specific goals include expanding transient studies using Rubin Observatory LSST data, enhancing education and training programs, and increasing its contribution to the infrastructure of international observatories as well as national capabilities in astrophysics.

entityName: UNIV BIRMINGHAM - Materials for Extremes Group
entityDescription:
Sandy Knowles is Professor of Nuclear Materials& UKRI Future Leaders Fellowin the School of Metallurgy & Materials, University of Birmingham. He leads theMaterials for Extremes research group.
He is an experimental metallurgist focused on the design & development of new alloys for extreme environments, including nuclear fusion, fission and aerospace gas turbines. He is a forerunner in the development of new “bcc superalloys”. Unlike current γ-γ’ nickel superalloys, β-β’ bcc superalloys make use of a bcc tungsten, titanium or steel matrix, with their higher melting points, for increased operating temperatures. This work, as well as his work on commercial alloys and ‘high entropy alloys’ (HEAs), is supported by industry partnerships with: UK National Nuclear Laboratory (UKNNL), UK Atomic Energy Authority (UKAEA),TIMET and Roll-Royce plc.

entityDescription:
Space applications require compact, efficient, and long-term reliable power electronics capable of withstanding extreme operating conditions. Silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN) power semiconductors are key technologies for these demanding environments, operating at increasingly higher voltages and switching frequencies. Ensuring reliable energy conversion under such conditions over long lifecycles requires a deep understanding of the dielectric aging and failure behavior of insulation systems under high-voltage and high-frequency stress.
HVsys Testing addresses this challenge by developing automated long-term testing methods, equipment and services to analyze the dielectric aging and degradation behavior of insulation systems under HV/HF stress for next-generation SiC and GaN power semiconductor technologies. Semiconductor manufacturers can submit test samples, which are exposed to long-term dielectrical HV/HF stress until failure. The resulting insights provide valuable data to understand and control the underlying degradation mechanisms in insulation materials.
This is particularly important in reliability-critical fields such as space applications, where extreme environmental conditions and high failure costs demand the utmost reliability and durability of power electronics. By advancing the understanding of HV/HF degradation mechanisms in insulation systems, HVsys Testing supports the development of more efficient, durable, and resilient power electronics for space environments.

entityDescription:
Solithor, a spin-off from Imec founded in 2021, develops and commercializes advanced all-solid-state lithium batteries. Their research and development primarily focus on enhancing the solid-state electrolyte and lithium anode.
The core of their technology consists of:
- Nano-Solid Composite Electrolyte (nano-SCE): A novel electrolyte that is neither sulfide-, oxide-, nor polymer-based and does not require high temperatures for high lithium-ion conductivity.
- Lithium nano-anode: Contributes to higher energy density and faster charging performance.
Their batteries surpass the practical limit of conventional lithium-ion cells (800 Wh/L) and offer advantages such as improved energy density, faster charging speeds, and enhanced safety. Additionally, they are environmentally friendly and recyclable, with a lower CO₂ footprint than traditional Li-ion batteries.
Thanks to their patented electrolyte, these batteries are easier to manufacture than competing solid-state batteries and do not require costly modifications to existing production lines. SOLiTHOR is committed to sustainable battery production, avoiding rare earth metals and minimizing cobalt and solvent usage. SOLiTHOR’s next generation rechargeable all-solid-state lithium battery technology will be used in a range of transport applications with initial focus on Aviation, Urban Air Mobility and Aerospace.

entityDescription: 0g Propulsion Systems leads with an OTV-centric in-orbit operations stack: we architect and prototype systems for propellant refueling, active debris removal (ADR), close-proximity spacecraft inspection, cargo handover/logistics, and the enabling blocks for in-space manufacturing. To support these missions, we’re developing combined spacecraft configurations—tug + depot/servicer—built around standard fluid, power, and data couplers to enable fast dock-transfer-redeploy cycles. Closing the loop, we provide ECSS-aligned consulting to de-risk execution: chemical propulsion design and verification (mono, biprop, hybrid, solid), TRL maturation from component → subsystem → system → flight demo (EM/QM/FM), and rigorous numerical analysis & mathematical modeling (ΔV/mass budgets, pressurization and blowdown, feed-system transients, plume–thermal interactions, reliability/Monte-Carlo) tied directly into verification plans and qualification test matrices.

BeamGrid Technologies Ltd is a UK-based deep-tech company specialising in advanced Radio Frequency (RF), antenna systems, and wireless sensing technologies. The company develops high-performance solutions across three core verticals: (1) Structural Health Monitoring using passive RF resonator tags, (2) 5G/6G Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) and direct-to-device antenna systems, and (3) Space-Based Solar Power (SBSP) and wireless power transmission. BeamGrid integrates expertise in RF engineering, phased arrays, SDR-based signal processing, AI-enabled optimisation, and system-level architecture to deliver compact, efficient, and scalable products.
The company combines strong technical R&D capabilities with practical engineering and commercial focus. Its work spans concept design, electromagnetic simulation, prototyping, testing, and technology demonstration at early TRL levels, with a long-term vision to scale into operational products for telecom, aerospace, energy, and infrastructure markets. BeamGrid operates with an agile, innovation-driven model, working closely with industry partners, research institutions, and funding bodies to accelerate development and deployment of next-generation RF technologies

entityDescription:
ŽIPO Lenart Ltd. is an advanced agricultural company (SME) from Slovenia, established in 1994 and led by Mitja Krajnc. The company specializes in precision crop production, livestock management, renewable energy sources, and applied agricultural R&D, with a focus on sustainable resource management and innovative technologies.
Key R&D activities include precision agriculture using GPS and satellite imagery, optimization of feed and forage crops, plasma treatment of seeds and grains, fertilization and weed management, and monitoring of crop and livestock quality. The company is also owner of a patent for precision application of mineral fertilizers. These activities combine practical farm operations with research, enabling data-driven testing and implementation at field scale.
ŽIPO Lenart has developed partnerships with some leading research institutions and is an active member of key industry organizations.
The company has adopted advanced digital and sustainable solutions, including GPS-guided machinery, satellite crop mapping, variable-rate fertilization, laboratory analytics, and modern grain drying and storage. These efforts were recognized with the “Best User of Digital Technologies” award at the Agrobiznis Hi-Tech 2022 competition. Renewable energy production via solar power plants further reinforces efficient and environmentally responsible practices.
With decades of experience, ŽIPO Lenart continues to advance expertise in precision agriculture, digital farming, and sustainable livestock management, positioning itself as a reliable and innovative partner for data-driven agricultural solutions in Slovenia and Europe.

entityDescription:
Idego is an Italian company based in Rome, founded in 2016, that designs and develops digital tools for psychology, training, and mental well-being through immersive technologies. It operates at the intersection between psychology, neuroscience, and digital innovation, combining scientific expertise with software development to create virtual and augmented reality environments that support therapy, rehabilitation, and learning.
The company’s mission is to make advanced immersive technologies accessible to mental health professionals and educators, enabling them to integrate VR and AR experiences into their work in a way that is scientifically grounded and user-friendly. Idego’s projects are built around the idea that virtual environments can recreate realistic emotional and behavioral experiences in safe, controlled conditions — useful both for psychological assessment and for therapeutic exposure or cognitive rehabilitation.
Over the years, Idego has developed several applications and platforms for mental health and tele-rehabilitation, such as virtual reality scenarios for anxiety and phobia treatment, stress management, cognitive training, and social skills development. The solutions are compatible with major VR devices such as HTC Vive and Meta Quest, and can also be deployed on mobile devices, ensuring flexibility and scalability.
The company collaborates with universities, hospitals, and innovation networks (including Lazio Innova) to validate and deploy its systems. One notable example is Cerebrum, a project focused on virtual telerehabilitation for psychiatric and neurological patients, designed to allow clinicians to monitor and guide patients remotely within immersive environments.
Idego positions itself as a pioneer of “digital psychology,” promoting the integration of human sciences with technological innovation. Its vision extends beyond clinical settings to include corporate well-being, professional training, and educational programs, reflecting a broader ambition to use immersive technologies to enhance human potential and quality of life.

Idego’s expertise in immersive digital environments makes its technologies highly adaptable to broader domains where human interaction, spatial awareness, and data visualization are key. Its psychologically grounded approach to virtual design can be applied beyond clinical contexts — for instance, to create realistic, interactive simulations, enhance user experience in training or remote collaboration, and integrate behavioral insights with sensor-based or geospatial data for advanced monitoring and decision-support systems.

description:
Overview Welcome to Pro CISO®, a boutique cybersecurity firm certified ISO/IEC 27001 and 9001. We simplify Cybersecurity Management for our customers by defining the program and executing it to achieve the established posture and compliance objectives.
Pro CISO®-as-a-Service : Unlike traditional models that assign a single fractional Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), we offer a dynamic blend of seasoned professionals. While still having a dedicated CISO as a primary point of contact, our model ensures access to a pool of specialized experts in their fields of cybersecurity.
M365 Security : While migrating to Microsoft 365 Cloud environment is relatively straightforward, securing it and maintaining it secure, is a huge challenge for any company. As an authorized Microsoft AI Cloud Partner, Pro CISO® provides M365 Security as a managed service through Microsoft's official CSP platform. Additionally Pro CISO® provides Security Monitoring capabilities to identify malicious events before they degenerate into a security breach, thus facilitating compliance to NIS2 and DORA requirements as well.
CA/CR® Assessments : Pro CISO®'s comprehensive Security Assessments, enhanced by our overlining CA/CR® methodology, verify the maturity posture of our customers towards international standards, such as ISO 27001 or NIST CSF, and compliance with regulations such as GDPR, NIS2, DORA.
As a natural extension, we perform Threat Modeling integrated with Penetration Testing of customer environments and applications to counter-check the declarations during the assessment phase and identify weaknesses and vulnerabilities before they can be exploited by bad actors.
Our toolkit of cybersecurity tools and managed services offers the following solutions:
- Enterprise Password Manager - To ensure unique, strong passwords in the organization. With possibility to share credentials and MFA, while monitoring that they are not compromised on the Darkweb.
- Attack Surface Intelligence - AI based scan of the public facing technology assets of an enterprise, to identify vulnerabilities, weaknesses, phishing domains, weak and expiring TLS certificates.
- Security Awareness Program - Education platform to continuously inform employees of cybersecurity risks and improve their detection of phishing attacks. AI based, very lightweight to manage.
- XDR anti malware - to protect user endpoints from malware and malicious websites

entityDescription: We would like to introduce our company, which has been engaged in the production of technical textile products for more than twenty years. Our headquarters and production facilities are located in Kamnik, at Polčeva pot 1, where we operate on a total of 1,200 m² of business premises. We currently employ 23 highly skilled professionals who ensure high-quality manufacturing and the development of advanced technical solutions.The company was founded in 1999 as T-Tekstil Vanja Sušnik s.p.. Due to business expansion, T-Tekstil d.o.o. was later established, and in 2020 the original sole proprietorship was merged into T-Tekstil d.o.o., combining expertise, experience, and technology and further strengthening our development and production capabilities. Over the years, we have built extensive experience in several fields, including industry, defense, nautical applications, sports, and environmentally oriented programs. We offer development, engineering, and manufacturing of high-quality, small-series, and specialized products.We are particularly proud of our long-standing work in the field of parachutes, where we have developed numerous specific and technologically demanding solutions. For C-Astral, we developed landing parachutes; we also collaborate with a Ukrainian partner for the production of various parachute systems. Additionally, we worked with UP International, for whom we manufactured rescue parachutes and landing parachutes for drones (Porter X2).Our technological equipment enables us to carry out even the most demanding projects. We are equipped with state-of-the-art sewing machines, automated systems, an ultrasonic welding machine, and advanced cutting equipment including a laser cutter, as well as single-layer and multi-layer digital cutting systems. We also use a 3D scanner that allows rapid and precise pattern development and optimization of the design process.We are strongly committed to digitalization; therefore, our entire production process has been fully digitized—from documented production stages to recorded videos of individual operations—ensuring improved traceability, efficient planning, and consistent product quality.In December, we will obtain the ISO 9001 and AQAP certifications, further confirming our commitment to standardized, high-quality and well-organized processes.We are dedicated to quality, precision, and innovation, and we always strive to provide the best possible solutions for our business partners. We look forward to the opportunity to present our knowledge and capabilities to you in person and to discuss potential cooperation.

entityDescription:
Scuolab is an Italian Ed-Tech company committed to driving meaningful innovation in the education sector, with the goal of making learning and training processes more engaging, interactive inclusive and accessible through advanced technological and methodological solutions designed to support schools, teachers, and students.
Our mission is to foster a modern, stimulating, and inclusive learning experience by empowering the potential of new generations through the responsible use of technology, strengthening their digital skills, and valuing their individual talents.
Founded in 2021 as a spin-off of Protom Group, the first Italian KTI (Knowledge & Technology Intensive) Company, Scuolab was created to bring the most advanced educational solutions and products to schools and educational institutions. The company has rapidly evolved as a concrete response to the growing needs of digital education, building a solid bridge between technology and the school environment and enabling continuous training for teachers and students through cutting-edge innovative tools.
Scuolab develops solutions that integrate state-of-the-art technologies — from Virtual Reality to Robotics and Artificial Intelligence — offering accessible and effective resources that make the teaching and learning process more dynamic, immersive, and impactful. Each solution is supported by dedicated training programs that guide educators and learners in seamlessly integrating these technologies into their daily educational activities.
Working in close synergy with the educational community, co-designing solutions with those who experience the classroom every day, Scuolab has already been adopted by more than 80 Italian schools, with over 70,000 platform accesses recorded since its launch.
Our growth is strengthened by collaborations with prestigious institutions recognized for their commitment to education, innovation, and social impact, including Fondazione FOQUS, the educational network Dalla Parte dei Bambini, the National Research Council (CNR), Fondazione Intesa Sanpaolo, and Fondazione Cariplo.
Through these partnerships, Scuolab continues to expand its reach and impact, positioning itself as a reliable, forward-looking player in digital education — and a strategic partner for initiatives with a strong technological, scientific, and societal dimension.

entityName: University of Zagreb Faculty of Kinesiology
entityDescription:
Introduction to the Faculty of Kinesiology

As the oldest educational and scientific institution in the field of kinesiology in the Republic of Croatia, and
alongside the Faculty of Kinesiology of the University of Split and the undergraduate study of Kinesiology at the Faculty of Education of Josip Juraj Strossmayer University of Osijek, the Faculty of Kinesiology of the University of Zagreb has a long tradition of education and research work, but also a responsibility in promoting kinesiology as a science, quality of class performance and supporting Croatian sport, sports recreation and Physical and Health Education. Through a strong social role, the Faculty of Kinesiology is often the organizer or conceptual initiator of actions that promote physical activity, movement and health. Through the work of its teaching staff, it has helped launch other kinesiology faculties in the Republic of Croatia and some in the region.
Vision
As the leading higher education institution in kinesiology in the region, the Faculty of Kinesiology at the
University of Zagreb aims to become integrated and competitive in the European higher education and research area and to create new and improve existing knowledge transfer systems in all fields of applied kinesiology.

Mission
The Faculty of Kinesiology of the University of Zagreb is a leading higher education institution in the field of
kinesiology in the region educating staff in all areas of applied kinesiology based on the latest scientific and
professional knowledge. The Faculty of Kinesiology bases its work on high academic and ethical values,
knowledge based on research and expertise, and optimal infrastructure conditions. The Faculty of Kinesiology contributes significantly to the promotion of sports, physical recreation, physical and health education of pupils and students, as well as the quality of active life and health of Croatian citizens.
Strategic goals are aimed at quality advancement of the teaching process, ensuring the conditions for creative scientific research work aimed at creating new and deepening existing knowledge in all fields of general and applied kinesiology, and better positioning of the Faculty in the international academic community.

entityDescription:
SensFish is developing a smart, scenario-based and comprehensive technology to monitor the ocean. We are the crosssection of the sectors of space and ocean, disrupting the value chain of the global sustainable fishing industry.
 
The scalable solution leverages multi-modal data with AI and ML to enhance understanding of the fish population sizes by species and predict those trends and movements.
 
While functioning as SaaS, the technology factors in multi-modal sources of data through related applications for verification of ocean sustainability and big ‘ocean players' impact mitigation.
For example, the fusion of satellite fishing vessel tracking data and ocean protective measures attend to scenarios like illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, ocean pollution and seabed damage, through real-time alerts and risk scores, through parameters like marine protected areas (MPAs), vessel gear types, fishing concentration, effort and other.
 
Followed by the integration of satellite Earth Observation (EO) data on ocean conditions, such as salinity and temperature, combined with satellite tracking of warm-blooded marine mammals, carbon flux measurements between fish and sea sediments, and fish population statistics, provides valuable proxies for estimating fish population sizes. This approach also considers the impacts of climate change, including shifts in fish habitats to new locations, increased mortality rates, altered life cycles, and other ecological changes.
 
Seafood processors, on one hand, gain the ability to automate operations aligned with sustainability goals, ensuring compliance with ocean regulations and reporting requirements. This leads to improved efficiency, increased profitability, and greater consumer satisfaction with sustainable seafood products. On the other hand, regulatory bodies and agencies benefit from consistent ocean insights and predictive data, enabling enhanced fisheries management, informed decision-making, and support for decarbonization initiatives.
 
As a transformative solution for the future, aligned with the goals of achieving net zero emissions, sustainability, and the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), this vision encompasses the future of food security, ocean biodiversity, and the well-being of societies and fishing communities. These objectives converge to drive a rejuvenated and resilient economy, benefiting all stakeholders.
