With a highly talented international team, EDI GmbH empowers companies to leverage AI without requiring specialized knowledge or experience. Our services include customized software solutions, innovative digital products, and the development of sustainable business models. Our core mission is to simplify the optimization, control, and monitoring of processes, machines, and systems.
Our AI solutions span a wide range of industries, including Industry 4.0, autonomous driving, electric vehicles, battery technology, mechanical and plant engineering, life sciences, e-health, process engineering, and forestry. entityDescription:
While Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) technology has become omnipresent in consumer, automotive, and industrial applications, the adoption of high precision GNSS technology continues to be inaccessible to the mass market due to the lack of a global, dense and optimally distributed GNSS infrastructure network facilitating improvements of positioning to the sub-centimeter level. Such a network would represent the basis to serve an existing market of C6.7B and facilitate novel applications benefiting humanity such as early tsunami warning systems, crustal deformation monitoring and space weather monitoring, on a more larger and more accurate scale than previously possible.

onocoy incentivizes the transparent construction of such a network in a decentralized way with blockchain-based tokens, open standards and hardware, and participatory governance that includes all stakeholders of the ecosystem including existing competing actors and users of their services. In this way, a collectively-owned, community-powered and decentralized GNSS infrastructure as a commons is created that benefits everyone by fostering accessibility, collaboration, and innovation.

description:
4D Fusion sp. z o.o. is a Polish deep-tech SME focused on advanced additive manufacturing and functional materials. The company was founded in 2024 and has been organically developed since then through collaboration with Polish academia on new functional materials and processes. 4D Fusion commercialises a new class of 4D printing technology that enables rapid development and industrialisation of polymer-based composites and smart structures, from laboratory concepts through functional demonstrators to scalable series production and technology transfer to customers’ lines.

Our mission is to provide a "materials technology sandbox" – an integrated ecosystem of hardware, materials and services that allows engineers and scientists to design, prototype, validate and scale up production of new materials and devices, from gram-scale R&D batches to mass-manufacturing, with very short iteration cycles and minimal material consumption.

The company is based in Poland and builds on more than 20 years of experience of the founders in polymer processing, additive manufacturing, special-purpose systems and technology commercialisation. 4D Fusion already collaborates with leading Polish universities and institutes (e.g. AGH University of Krakow, Silesian University of Technology, Military University of Technology, Lukasiewicz – Institute of Non-Ferrous Metals, Institute of Physical Chemistry Polish Academy of Science).

Core technology – 4D Fusion Additive Manufacturing System

4D Fusion develops and supplies a proprietary multi-material additive manufacturing platform that combines classic FDM with a new extrusion head called BFG on a common motion system. The core system consists of the 4D Fusion BFG head, a patented extrusion module with a modular plastification system and actively controlled thermal zones; dual FDM modules (1.75 mm and 2.85 mm) for structural polymers and standard engineering materials; and a unified motion and control system that enables the combination of multiple deposition modes in a single build and can be customised and extended with quality-assurance and process options (e.g. heated build chamber, vision/QC, additional process sensors). The BFG head can use virtually any thermoplastic polymer as a base matrix, achieve very high loading of functional additives (metals, ceramics, magnetic powders, bio-fillers, regolith simulants) up to ~70–80% vol., maintain precise formulation control with minimal need for processing aids, print shear-sensitive or temperature-sensitive additives and produce material inserts with minimal use of heat, water and feedstock.

The BFG head supports several deposition techniques in one platform, including classical 2.5D/3D printing (layer-by-layer), pouring and over-moulding into cavities, foaming for lightweight cellular structures, smearing for thin functional layers and interfaces, sedimentation for graded structures with controlled particle distribution, and matrix extrusion through shaped dies.

This architecture allows users to develop and print advanced multi-material parts that combine structural, sensing, magnetic, shielding or bio-functional roles in a single component.

Heritage and TRL 
The present 4D Fusion AM System is in advanced industrial stage, with first units planned for delivery to research and industrial customers. The technology has been validated with multiple material families, including highly filled composites, magnetic materials, regolith-polymer blends and bio-related formulations. 
Space-related capabilities and use cases
4D Fusion technology is particularly relevant for ESA activities in advanced manufacturing, ISRU and future habitats, where flexible use of local resources and complex functional materials is required.
Key space-related capabilities: 4D Fusion can process regolith-based and regolith-polymer composite materials and work with polymers that are normally not printable (e.g. PVC-based or highly doped matrices). The platform enables rapid screening of new formulations with gram-scale feedstock quantities, production of functionally graded materials with controlled changes in filler content or type, and direct integration of sensing, shielding, magnetic or antimicrobial functions into printed parts. Together with ESA and industrial partners, 4D Fusion can co-develop and validate new functional materials for mechanisms and satellite structures.
Illustrative applications under discussion or exploration: potential use cases include structural and non-structural components for surface habitats and infrastructure based on regolith-polymer composites, radiation and particle shielding elements combining polymer matrices with high-Z or magnetic fillers, embedded ion, pH or chemical sensors and smart inserts for environmental monitoring, lightweight magnetic components and mechanisms produced with highly filled elastomer matrices, as well as hybrid armour and functional protection systems using gradient or multi-layer composites.
The system is designed with in-situ operations in mind: compact form factor, modular process chain, and a clean, gram-scale material insert concept that can be coupled with an automated material preparation unit.
Products and services
4D Fusion offers an integrated portfolio of products and services. The 4D Fusion AM System is a modular multi-material printer with BFG + FDM, tailored to R&D labs, industrial innovation centres and space-related testbeds. The company develops and supplies gram-scale material inserts for specific polymers and composites, both from an open catalogue and as customer-specific or licensed materials. In addition, 4D Fusion provides R&D and engineering services covering formulation of new polymer composites and smart materials, design and fabrication of demonstrators, samples and functional prototypes, as well as participation in joint EU, ESA and national research projects where it delivers the AM platform, material know-how and process development.
Why 4D Fusion is relevant for ESA stakeholders
For ESA stakeholders, 4D Fusion offers a single platform to explore structural, electrical, magnetic, shielding and sensor functions within one printed component, providing true multi-material and multi-physics capability. Technology delivers high information density per kilogram of material, enabling many iterations and variants from very limited feedstock, which is particularly important when working with scarce or expensive materials and simulants. The technology is aligned with ISRU strategies through its ability to incorporate and characterise local granular resources such as regolith, recycled polymers and bio-derived fillers in robust polymer matrices. Because the same platform can be used in academic research, industrial R&D and early pilot production, it helps bridge the gap between science and industry and accelerates the transfer of novel materials into real applications.
4D Fusion is interested in partnering with ESA directorates, primes and research institutions on on-ground technology maturation for in-situ manufacturing and ISRU, advanced polymer and composite materials for space systems, and the development of functional demonstrators for habitats, robotics, sensors and protection systems.

entityDescription:
The National Institute for Research and Development for Earth Physics - NIEP is the successor of research institutions that aimed to study earthquakes.
In 1895, the first seismic station in Romania was established, within the Meteorological Institute of Bucharest.
The institutions that dealt with research in the field of Earth physics were, in order: the Center for Geophysical Research (CCG) of the Romanian Academy (1961-1970), followed by the Institute of Applied Geophysics (1970-1974) and the Institute of Geology and Geophysics (IGG, 1974-1977), both belonging to the Ministry of Mines, Petroleum and Geology.
In February 1977, the Center for Earth Physics (CFP) was established by merging the Department of Seismology within the Institute of Geology and Geophysics of Romania with the Geodynamics laboratory within the Romanian Academy.
In 1994 the Center for Earth Physics (CFP) was transformed into the National Institute for Earth Physics - NIEP, and in 1996, it became the National Institute for Research and Development for Earth Physics - NIEP.

Structure The National Institute for Research and Development for Earth Physics carries out scientific research and technological development activities in the field of Earth Physics, in general, and seismology in particular.

entityName: Centro Europeo de Empresas e Innovación de Aragón SA
entityDescription:
CEEIARAGON is a Business Innovation Centre founded in 1992 to promote the creation, growth, and scale-up of innovative companies in Aragon (Northeast of Spain). For more than 33 years, we have been incubating and accelerating entrepreneurial projects, helping innovative ideas evolve into consolidated businesses.
This EU|BIC, supported mainly by the Regional Government of Aragon in partnership with regional stakeholders such as business organisations, trade unions, the Chamber of Commerce, and the University of Zaragoza, covers an area of 48,000 km².
Since its creation, CEEIARAGON has held the EU|BIC label, which is a quality label recognized by the EU and that is periodically renewed after a revision process.
We operate across the three provinces of Aragon—Zaragoza, Huesca, and Teruel—**offering 7,000 m² of incubation space and a comprehensive range of support services that accompany companies from early-stage ideation to scale-up and consolidation. We offer incubation space in the three capitals, Zaragoza, Huesca and Teruel. 
We have more than 33 years of experience incubating and scaling technology-based projects, including aerospace projects. The aerospace cluster is located in our Zaragoza incubator since its foundation.
CEEIARAGON is an active member of several networks. In addition to being part of the European Business and Innovation Centres Network -EBN-, we are members of ANCES (the Spanish association of BICs), Red ARCE (the Aragonese network of entrepreneurship support centres), and the PI+D+I network (R&D+I network) led by the Centre for the Development of Industrial Technology (CDTI), a public entity fostering innovation in Spanish companies. We are open to collaborating with any network that helps us and our clients grow, cooperate, and learn.
We remain faithful to our traditional role as a BIC/CEEI, while continuously evolving and adapting to new methodologies and innovation models. In the last years, we have intensified our incubation and acceleration programs, providing mentoring to startups with our own personnel, in all the different areas.

entityName: Faculdade de Farmácia da Universidade Lisboa
entityDescription: The Faculty of Pharmacy of Universidade de Lisboa (FFUL) is a highly regarded research-oriented institution in Pharmaceutical Sciences in Portugal, providing programs of excellence in scientific and professional areas. FFULisboa has around 1564 students (ca. 1171 in Integrated Master of Pharmaceutical Sciences, ca. 270 in other 2nd Cycles and ca. 123 PhD students). FFUL hosts the Research Institute for Medicines (iMed.ULisboa), a multidisciplinary R&D Unit in Life and Health Sciences supported by FCT where science, technology and translation converge. iMed.ULisboa mission is to develop innovative medicines and benefit human health through top-class multidisciplinary research. Capabilities are built around a network of 29 research groups, spanning the drug discovery and development spectrum, with an emphasis on innovative, multidisciplinary, and collaborative research. iMed.ULisboa hosts 592 researchers, including 26 postdoctoral fellows (including postdoctoral and CEEC) and 123 PhD students. Leading the PhD Programme in Pharmacy and partnering in several networks and consortia, iMed.ULisboa promotes national productivity and competitiveness in drug discovery and development, and facilitates international academic and industrial partnerships. FFUL provides administrative support, office and laboratory space, access to infrastructures, human resources and technical support. FFUL is member of several networks promoting initiatives to increase national competitiveness in medicines and health care.

entityName: Technical University of Sofia -  - Faculty of Transport
entityDescription:
The Faculty of Transport is an educational and research structure at the Technical University of Sofia. It educates specialists who can design, operate and service various types of transport vehicles in the field of land, air and space transport. The Faculty has specialists who can solve tasks related to problems in aviation and space technology. It has a modern material and technical base for simulation and experimental /real-life/ studies of specific characteristics of various types of objects intended for use in aviation and space technology. The faculty has laboratories for:
1) Vibroacoustic tests
2) Aerodynamic tests
3) Thermal tests
4) Clean room for assembly and testing of CubeSat satellites
The laboratories can perform some of the mandatory tests required for the flight of CubeSat and other satellites, such as:
1. Vibration Test: Sine and Random
2. Acoustic Test
3. Thermal Cycling test
4. Functional Test / Power-On Test
5. EMC/EMI Test
6. Fit Check
7. Subsystem tests /EPS Test, ADCS Test, Payload Test/

entityDescription: Feron Technologies P.C. (FERON, GR) is an Athens-based private technology SME (4 employees) with 9 years of experience in developing advanced ICT and IoT testbeds and products. entityDescription: ASTRO is a startup focused on delivering high-quality Earth observation data through innovative space solutions. Its technology is based on tethered satellite systems, which keep satellites in fixed formation to ensure greater stability and precision in data collection. This approach enhances the resolution and effectiveness of remote sensing for applications such as 3D structure reconstruction, moving object detection, and subsurface stratigraphy. The first mission, ODRADEK, uses two 12U CubeSats connected by a deployable tether of up to 200 meters. This link ensures zero-latency communication and improved stability, enabling superior imaging performance compared to traditional solutions. Modular by design, ODRADEK can host different payloads (optical and/or radar) tailored to customer needs, and is built with commercial off-the-shelf components to reduce costs. ASTRO manages the design and development of critical technologies such as guidance, navigation, and control algorithms, as well as the tether and its deployment system, while collaborating with industrial partners for system integration. Its patented solution positions ASTRO to deliver unique imaging capabilities that combine higher accuracy with lower costs. The company’s primary business model focuses on the sale of satellite imagery. By operating its own systems, ASTRO provides customers with advanced products for environmental monitoring, urban planning, infrastructure management, and defense applications. To diversify before full-scale operations, ASTRO also explores near-space demonstrators (e.g., stratospheric balloons, tethered drones) that validate technologies and generate early revenues.

entityDescription:
atmoky is an Austrian SME specializing in high-fidelity spatial audio and acoustic simulation technologies for immersive and interactive environments. Building on expertise in psychoacoustics, signal processing, and real-time 3D rendering, atmoky develops toolkits that enable realistic sound propagation, binaural rendering, and dynamic room acoustics in virtual and mixed-reality scenarios.
Its core platforms, trueSpatial and the upcoming trueAcoustics, are optimized for VR/XR training, simulation, and mission rehearsal applications. These systems allow 3D sound fields to respond to user movement (6DOF), environment geometry, and contextual events, enabling highly immersive and cognitively natural training experiences, particularly valuable in scenarios where visual load is high and auditory cues enhance orientation, situational awareness, and stress management.
atmoky’s solutions integrate seamlessly with established development environments such as Unity, Unreal Engine, FMOD, and Wwise, supporting deployment across head-mounted displays, PC simulators, and multi-speaker training facilities. The company has contributed spatial audio expertise to multiple international research collaborations, focusing on immersive learning, human–machine teaming, and adaptive acoustic environments for cognitive performance, music education and well-being.
Through scientifically grounded design and cross-disciplinary collaboration, atmoky advances spatial audio as a key enabler for next-generation XR training and simulation, including applications relevant to space operations and remote cooperation.

💻 Elemwave Description
 
Elemwave is a company specialized in the development of Computational Electromagnetics (CEM) software, with a particular focus on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) applications.
The company works with major players in the industry, including aerospace giants like Airbus, as a client.
 
What does their software offer?
 
Their main tool, the Elemwave workbench, allows for modeling and simulating typical EMC problems, which often involve the complex interaction between various components:
- Lumped circuits: Discrete circuit elements.

- Cable bundles: Collections of electrical conductors.

- Geometry: Physical 3D structures.

The software is especially useful for:
- Cable bundle modeling: It allows for defining and solving cross-sections of cable bundles with arbitrary shapes. This is crucial for determining the coupling between different conductors and predicting potential electromagnetic interference issues.

In essence, Elemwave provides a solution for engineers who need to analyze, simulate, and mitigate electromagnetic interference problems in the design of products and systems, ensuring they comply with EMC standards.

description:
Alén Space is a Spanish company dedicated to the design, manufacturing and operation of small satellites. Its main objective is to help space agencies, companies, institutions and high-tech centers advance their objectives with its state-of-the-art space/ground segment products and with the development of end-to-end nanosatellite missions.
 

Thanks to a highly qualified team of more than 70 engineers and technicians, Alén Space has been able to implement cutting-edge software and hardware for its own small satellites with a 100% success rate. In addition, its products and processes are endorsed by ESA standards (ECSS) and several recognised industry certifications, such as ISO 9001. 

Alén Space will bring its recognized experience of more than 15 years in the development of Cubesats and Payloads. The services of Alén Space cover all essential aspects of any type of space project: platform and mission design; payload development and manufacturing; assembly, integration and verification (AIV) phase and support of specific satellite operations through its Mission Control Software. 

Alén Space ensures that it meets the demands of the industry through its own technologically integrated facilities: central offices, development and assembly laboratory, cleanroom area and a satellite control room. 

Alén Space’s portfolio includes advanced space products and communication subsystems divided into small satellite platforms (1U-16U), closed payloads for space missions, on-board computers (OBC), Software Defined Radios (SDRs) designed for communication applications and ground segment solutions (ground stations and communication systems) prepared to operate in different radio frequency bands (UHF, VHF & S-band). 

Recognition and success have marked the trajectory of Alén Space. Therefore, its achievements have led the company to become part of the technology multinational GMV in 2023, a strategic alliance with the purpose of growing together in a highly competitive and constantly innovative environment. 

Alén's success rate combined with state-of-the-art technology and processes based on European sector standards has earned the trust of the world’s leading space organizations and agencies, such as the European Space Agency (ESA), the German Aerospace Center (DLR), the Brazilian Space Agency (AEB)and the Spanish National Institute of Aerospace Technology (INTA).

Since its beginnings back in 2008 in the aerospace strategic group of the University of Vigo, the Alén Space team has developed, manufactured, launched and operated several SmallSats. In chapter 2.3, Heritage and Starting Point, some of the projects that Alén Space has developed are presented.

Alén Space has 2 main product lines, one for the Space Segment and one for the Ground Segment.

Regarding the Space Segment, Alén Space offers 2 SDR platforms, TOTEM and TREVO, with both of them having flight heritage. These SDRs can be the core of communications payloads and are able to be integrated in various types of space missions. Alén Space also offers the closed RF payloads based on the aforementioned SDRs. Additionally, the company offers Cubesat Platforms ranging from 1U to 16U. These platforms can be offered as standard solutions in which customers can integrate their payloads, or can be offered as highly optimized solutions, including the payload, and as part of turnkey missions. Finally, Alén Space offers 2 On-Board Computer Models, DARA and TRISKEL. The latter also integrates a UHF Telemetry and Telecommand submodule. 

In parallel, in terms of Ground Segment products, Alén Space has designed and developed a ready-to-assemble Ground Station Kit solution, which is offered in various versions. It can work in the UHF, VHF, L- and S- Bands.

 
More information regarding the products offered by Alén Space can be retrieved from the company´s website. Upon request, Alén Space can provide further information regarding its products, such as their datasheets and more.

description: PowerIn Space is advancing wireless energy transmission systems utilizing optical (laser) technology, capable of delivering power over distances of 1-2 km on Earth and up to 1000 km in space. This system provides a continuous power supply, overcoming the limitations of solar panels and batteries in space and significantly enhancing operational capabilities. Additionally, our system supports laser communication, facilitating efficient data exchange alongside power delivery. It distinguishes itself by offering both low and high-power solutions at competitive prices, making it particularly effective for space applications such as recharging lunar rovers in permanently shadowed regions or during lunar nights. Furthermore, we are developing power-over-fiber technology, which features strong electromagnetic interference resistance and is substantially lighter than traditional metal cables.

entityDescription: The Lighting and Photometry Laboratory (LRF) was founded in 1921 as part of the Electrical Engineering Department of the then Faculty of Technology. In addition, we design lighting and carry out calculations of illuminance and brightness in indoor and outdoor spaces. We are also consultants to major Slovenian lighting companies. In our laboratory we also perform photometric measurements: integrating luminous flux measurements, directional and goniophotometric luminance measurements, luminance and brightness measurements with portable instruments and spectroradiometers. These also allow measurements of the spectral content of light, the colour of light and the colour appearance index. The laboratory also performs calibrations of brightness and luminance meters and develops photometric measurement equipment for our own needs and for clients.

entityDescription:
Involve Space – Insight from above, Impact on the ground
Involve Space is an Italian aerospace company that designs, develops, and launches intelligent pseudo-satellite platforms based on space balloons for Earth observation, defense, flight validation, and scientific research. With over 30 successfully launched missions, it is the leading Italian provider and one of the European leaders in the stratospheric mission sector.
The proprietary technology, capable of reaching altitudes of 30 km in suborbit, allows for close-up observation of the Earth with resolutions of up to 0.3 meters/pixel, eliminating the typical revisiting time of satellites, enabling constant and real-time monitoring. The asset can maintain its position and optimize routes based on atmospheric conditions.
Involve Space integrates aerospace hardware, artificial intelligence, and a sustainable approach: its balloons are reusable, zero-emission, and produced in-house. The next frontier is LoonHive®: constellations of decentralized stratospheric balloons for targeted large-scale monitoring, distributed through the tools of the intelligent geospatial platform CLEAR, positioning Involve Space as an end-to-end provider.
Based in Como and with an expanding presence in Europe and the United States, Involve Space aims to be a global reference point in the High Altitude Platforms (HAPS) market, with a clear vision: to bring strategic data from near-Earth space to generate concrete and sustainable impacts.

Optagon Photonics is a start-up focusing on the development of products for optical sensing and optical communication applications, leveraging more than 15 years of R&D expertise. Our main activity is to develop compact, photonic integrated OFDR engine products for Distributed Acoustic Sensing applications. Optagon's expertise and capabilities also include the design of Photonic Integrated Circuits and components such as grating couplers for integrated optical phased arrays, algorithms for the control and tuning of PIC-based External Cavity Lasers and the development of robust, in-house control electronics for these PICs, for numerous optical sensing applications such as LiDAR, laser vibrometry, optoelectronic THz generation etc.
Our control electronics are also available as stand-alone products, offering multi-channel current sources, multi-channel voltage sources and temperature control for PICs in a compact device. Prosix is a company focused on high performance composites engineering and in house manufacturing with more than 15 years of experience in design, development, manufacturing, and qualification of extreme high-demanding carbon fiber space structures.
Prosix is a multidisciplinary engineering team trained in the fields of chemistry, materials, design, analysis, manufacturing, assembly and validation of complex composite aerospace structures with a wide fabrication proven track record under EN ISO9100.
Prosix Engineering has 5 main business units: space, defense, energy, marine and science. The partnership with the key players of each sector as Airbus Defense and Space or ESA (European Space Agence) has allowed Prosix to push composite carbon structures to the edge, developing successfully structures under the most extreme temperatures, cryogenic conditions, high radiation ambient, ultra-high vacuum and pressure conditions, etc.
PROSIX offers comprehensive engineering services that include primary FRP material research, FRP materials properties modification and qualification for specific environments (high temperature, cryogenic, high vacuum, radiation…), definition, testing and validation of manufacturing procedures, part and mould design, costs analysis, prototype and series production and quality control (mechanical and chemical testing, NDT and SHMS).
PROSIX has an extensive knowledge on OoA pre-preg manufacturing procedures and resin injection/infusion process due to its intensive experience on the composites sector and the wide range of R & D developed programs. It develops its projects in every industrial sector for those that regularly use composites, as well as for potential users. The purpose of PROSIX is to reach the optimal level of composites usage in every single project.

entityDescription: The Radiation and Optics Laboratory's research fields are radio and optical communications, with the primary focus being on the physical layer of the telecommunications network. Currently, the laboratory’s research activity includes the transmission of a synchronization signal via optical fibres, a new generation of optical access networks, adaptive antennas and advanced radio interfaces for next-generation mobile communications, including satellite communications for small satellites. The laboratory team is responsible for the design and development of both analogue and high-speed digital microwave electronics for optical and microwave communication equipment, the 3D modelling and simulation of passive microwave structures and the development of antennas to include the terahertz frequency range.

entityName: Technical University of Sofia - Faculty of Telecommunication
entityDescription:
The Faculty of Telecommunications at the Technical University of Sofia is the nation's premier hub for engineering innovation in the Information and Telecommunication field. We don't just keep pace with the digital world; we build networks that connect it. 
The Bachelor's curriculum provides elective courses for further specialization in radiocommunications, audio and video technologies, telecommunications networks and technologies, and communication systems management.
Our programs now also explore the cutting-edge of aerospace communication, equipping students with the skills to design systems for satellites, aircraft, and deep-space probes. Through practical projects, you can learn the principles behind secure data links for UAVs and robust communication for next-generation satellite constellations, connecting the world from the stratosphere to orbit.
Industrial and Corporate Networksprogram equips you to design the secure, ultra-reliable, and mission-critical communication backbones for the 4th Industrial Revolution. You'll learn to build the smart factory networks, corporate cloud infrastructures, and IoT systems that drive global enterprise.
In ourAR/VR Communicationstrack, you will pioneer the technologies behind the metaverse and real-time interactive media. Focus on the unique challenges of transmitting ultra-high-definition, low-latency 3D content, and developing the systems that will power the next generation of telepresence, gaming, and virtual collaboration.
Telecommunications is one of the most modern and dynamically developing fields of engineering and technology today, characterized by significant investments, the presence of leading global technology companies. The faculty maintains close ties with leading Bulgarian telecommunications operators, as well as domestic and foreign ICT companies, which offer students internship programs, scholarships, and various types of additional specialized training.

TT Electronics provides engineering solutions for Aerospace and Defence companies globally, specialising in Power Conversion, Power Distribution and Power Components. Our business is built on custom solutions for safety critical applications in harsh environments. 

TT has an Advanced Technology Centre located on site at the University of Nottingham, where our team of engineers work with the University on R&D programmes. We also have manufacturing sites located in Oldham and Barnstaple. The Engineering Team at TT consists of a highly skilled, mixed discipline team of engineers, all with considerable experience in the aerospace and defence industry. 

Main areas of expertise are as follows: System Engineering, Power Systems Engineering, Hardware Engineering, Software Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Requirements management and Integrated logistics support. TT has internal capability to perform extensive environmental qualification testing, including: Temperature, Altitude, Humidity, Normal & Gunfire Vibration, HALT Testing, EMC Testing.

description:
Optonics is developing a polymer Selective Laser Sintering (SLS) platform and a qualified manufacturing service for spaceflight and high-reliability industrial applications. The solution targets repeatable, traceable, and certifiable production of polymer components that meet stringent mechanical and outgassing requirements typical in aerospace programs. Optonics is currently in development and is an incubatee at ESA BIC Latvia. 
Capabilities
High-performance polymer SLS production for flight and ground support hardware, with process control designed for repeatability and certification.
Turnkey manufacturing service for space applications that enables access to flight-ready parts without machine ownership.
Part-level digital traceability linking each component to build parameters, thermal history, inspection data, and post-process records.
entityDescription:
Optonics is developing affordable polymer Selective Laser Sintering (SLS) 3D printing systems with integrated manufacturing intelligence software for aerospace and industrial applications. The company combines two core products: the ONE - a polymer SLS printer with integrated post-print annealing at a fraction of incumbent pricing - and TRACE - a manufacturing intelligence platform that automates traceability, parameter selection, and quality documentation across additive manufacturing workflows.

By reducing hardware cost by over 70% compared to industrial systems and embedding process intelligence directly into the platform, Optonics enables organisations to bring high-performance polymer manufacturing in-house - with full traceability from powder to finished part. TRACE is technology-agnostic and already operational on FDM printers, with SLS integration following the ONE hardware development.
Target sectors include space hardware manufacturers, satellite and launch vehicle teams, defence, automotive, and industrial R&D - any environment where part quality, traceability, and supply chain independence are non-negotiable.

entityDescription:
Impulso.Space was founded in 2019 in Padova, Italy, and has grown into a trusted launch services provider supporting satellite missions from integration to orbit. The company also operates a dedicated facility in proximity of Cape Canaveral, Florida, USA, equipped with an ISO 8 cleanroom to handle advanced payload processing and integration activities.
Impulso’s services cover every step of pre-launch preparation. Launch capacity procurement, satellite integration, storage, fueling activities, logistics, and customs support are all managed within one framework, reducing unnecessary complexity and delays. Insurance coordination and final handover to launch providers are also included, ensuring that every mission requirement is addressed before flight. The team brings extensive know-how in navigating administrative processes and coordinating directly with launch operators, allowing missions to move forward quickly and with confidence.
To this date, Impulso.Space has supported 15+ missions, consisting of 35+ minisatellites and CubeSats with a 100% success rate. Partnerships, such as the multi-mission launch services contract with D-Orbit, further strengthen the company’s role in delivering complete end-to-end launch solutions.
With origins in Italy and a global presence in the United States, Impulso.Space reflects the NewSpace mindset: reliable, fast, and flexible. By combining infrastructure, expertise, and streamlined processes, the company enables a wide range of mission profiles and helps satellite operators transform ambitious plans into successful launches.

description:
VYRONIS Technologies Ltd
Sector: Space Biotech • AI & Radiation Biology • Astronaut Health
Location: Glasgow, Scotland
Founder: Varun Cruz
Overview 
VYRONIS Technologies is a space biotechnology company developing radiation-adaptive bio-AI systems to enhance astronaut health, radiation resilience, and biological safety in deep-space missions. The company’s flagship platform, GENORA™, integrates radiobiological data, molecular AI, and predictive genomics to model how living systems adapt to ionising radiation; enabling early detection, intervention, and countermeasure design for spaceflight and nuclear medicine environments. 
ESA BIC Focus 
Through the ESA Business Incubation Centre UK, VYRONIS is advancing the GENORA™ Translational Framework (TRL 3–7) — combining laboratory data, in-silico simulations, and microgravity-exposed biological datasets. The aim is to produce adaptive bio-AI algorithms that can predict and mitigate radiation damage for astronauts, satellites, and terrestrial healthcare systems. Vision To pioneer a new era of bio-adaptive intelligence for human space exploration — ensuring every mission beyond Earth is powered by biologically informed, AI-driven health resilience. Applications Space Health: Predictive modelling for astronaut exposure and countermeasure optimisation. Terrestrial Medicine: Radiotherapy safety, oncology insights, and emergency-response biotechnologies. Dual-Use AI Systems: Algorithms for defence, nuclear energy, and planetary colonisation research. 
Key Partners 
ESA BIC UK (incubation support) 
Innovate UK (funding) 
Academic collaborations with UK and EU research institutions 
Website (in development): www.vyronis.tech

description: Devanthro is a Munich-based robotics and AI trailblazer tackling the global elderly care crisis to make humanoid robots for every household. Building on 9 years of full-stack robotics R&D and three generations of humanoid robots, the company is setting a new standard for 24/7 elderly care. By augmenting human caregivers with Robodies - advanced robotic avatars - Devanthro offers a groundbreaking solution to caregiver shortages and enhances the quality of life for seniors. No longer a concept of the future, after several successful prof of concepts in the care sector, Robodies are set to prove their real-world applications in a 12-week pilot with Charité Berlin already in 2024, marking a pivotal step in the company's commercialization journey.
entityDescription:
Robody Cares is a new type of ambulatory care service where local nursing staff perform some visits to patients in person and some via remote-operated, humanoid robots – “Robodies”. This provides protection and assistance to the patient 24/7 while the patient maintains personal contact with people in their community.
With an aging population and families more distant than ever, we are sleep walking into a care crisis. This new challenge needs a new solution – Robody Cares – that combines the benefits of modern technology with human care, ensuring that your loved ones are always well taken care of and receive the help they need.
Combining AI, AR, and 5G, Robodies are human robotic avatars allowing its operator to teleport their senses, action, and presence anywhere on the planet or in space. This makes Robodies an alternative for space based operations in the future.

description:
SI Robotics is a Warsaw-based deep-tech company developing sovereign European humanoid and robotic systems for industrial, defence, and space applications. We are a Physical-AI-first company, integrating advanced actuators, tendon-based joints, and compliant control systems with reinforcement-learning frameworks to create embodied intelligence for the physical world.

Our mission is to advance Physical AI — the fusion of mechanical design, sensing, and neural control that allows robots to understand, interact with, and adapt to their environment with human-like precision. We believe this domain will define the next generation of autonomy across terrestrial and orbital contexts.

Within the space sector, SI Robotics develops lightweight, ECSS-compliant actuator systems for robotic arms, EVA/IVA assistance, and on-orbit servicing. Our modular joint architecture and torque-controlled drives are designed to operate under the mechanical, radiation, and thermal constraints of space environments.

We are fully aligned with European AI, data, and machinery regulations (including the 2027 AI Act and Machinery Regulation). SI Robotics’ architecture ensures full traceability, explainability, and data sovereignty, making our Physical AI stack natively compliant with EU ethical and legal frameworks — a key differentiator from non-EU robotics providers.

SI Robotics contributes to the emerging European Physical AI policy agenda, supporting ESA and the European Commission in building safe, transparent, and sovereign autonomy for robotic systems. We work closely with research institutions and industrial partners to develop embodied AI models that meet dual-use and security-sensitive requirements, ensuring resilience and interoperability across ESA, defence, and industry ecosystems.

entityDescription:
Mariborski vodovod is a regional public utility company responsible for supplying safe and healthy drinking water to the Municipality of Maribor and 15 surrounding municipalities in northeastern Slovenia. In addition to water supply, the company is also responsible for the operation and management of the Central Wastewater Treatment Plant Maribor, ensuring environmentally responsible and sustainable wastewater treatment for the wider region. With more than a century of tradition and extensive professional expertise, the company operates the largest water distribution network in Slovenia, managing 1.723 kilometers of pipelines and over 260 facilities. Each year, it supplies approximately 14 million cubic meters of drinking water to more than 160.000 residents.
The company’s vision is to be a modern, efficient, responsible, and innovative public utility that delivers top-quality services to its users, partners, and owners. Its core mission focuses on the long-term reliability of water sources, infrastructure, and service quality.
To improve efficiency and sustainability, Mariborski vodovod emphasizes the reduction of water losses, which currently stand at approximately 29%, with an Infrastructure Leakage Index (ILI) of 3.4, highlighting potential for further improvement. The water network is divided into 138 District Metered Areas (DMAs), enabling localized flow monitoring, faster leak detection, and targeted interventions.
Technologically advanced and innovation-driven, the company employs modern IT systems, including enterprise resource planning (ERP), geographic information systems (GIS), and SCADA industrial systems. It takes pride in its use of smart technologies, having installed 99.8% of smart meters, enabling accurate billing based on real consumption. Around 260 control meters and sensors throughout the network provide continuous monitoring, while the integration of GIS with a business intelligence (BI) system supports effective management through detailed dashboards and analytics.
Corporate social responsibility is embedded in the company’s operations, encouraging all employees, from staff to leadership, to contribute to sustainable and socially responsible strategies. Mariborski vodovod continuously invests in system modernization, reduces water and energy losses, promotes innovation, and builds a motivated, highly skilled workforce. Through efficient, rational business practices and a process-based organization, the company ensures long-term financial stability while maintaining a strong focus on customer satisfaction, high-quality service, and open, responsive communication.

entityDescription:
SOLEIL is one of France'sTrès Grandes Infrastructures de Recherche (TGIR)(Very Large Scale Research Infrastructures), i.e. tools with unique features required for high-level research activities, open to any scientific community wishing to use them, and accessible on the basis of project excellence.
As an ultra-high-tech facility, SOLEIL is at once a platform open to all academic and industrial communities, a cutting-edge, multidisciplinary research laboratory, and a place for general public to share scientific culture. SOLEIL, located at the heart of the Paris-Saclay science cluster, is a civil company* jointly founded by CNRS and CEA.
More concretely, SOLEIL produces synchrotron radiation, an extremely bright light that can be used to explore inert or biological matter down to the atomic scale, thanks to particle accelerators (electrons). The light produced covers a wide range of wavelengths (from infrared to X-rays) and is used in experimental facilities known as “beamlines”.
SOLEIL's missions are, as described in the company's charter:

- To build and operate a synchrotron radiation source and associated experimental facilities

- To conduct research programs using this synchrotron radiation, and to develop its applications

- Make its facilities available to interested national, European, and international scientific communities, and encourage their use by them

- Collaborate and exchange with other synchrotron facilities.

The synchrotron SOLEIL, a unique tool for both academic research and industrial applications, opened to the scientific community in 2008. It is used every year by several thousand researchers from France and abroad, across a wide range of disciplines including physics, biology, chemistry, astrophysics, the environment, and earth sciences. These users are welcomed and accompanied on the beamlines by SOLEIL's scientific and technical teams.

entityDescription:
INTRODUCTION
The profile of thePrototyping and Innovation Centre (PaIC) is based on the outstanding characteristics incorporated already in the concept of its foundation. In terms of material equipment this includes the most advanced manufacturing technology, the structure of which makes it suitable also for very precise tool manufacture. The technology is situated in new premises which has a positive effect on the final accuracy and general quality of manufacture. In terms of human resources, PaIC is staffed to provide an optimal mix of expert knowledge, age structure and good knowledge of both academic and industrial environment, benefitting from the excellent research capacities of the whole university.
The commitment/mission ofPaICis its (PaIC is dedicated to) active performance in the following areas:
- Implementation of research results of faculty staff and students
- Research, development and innovations for industry
- Mentoring and manufacturing support for start-ups and small businesses in the field of prototype development and manufacture
- Enabling students to directly participate in the research of new products and technologies
- Coordination of complex industry-university collaboration projects with international outreach

entityDescription:
NAPOP AS is a Norwegian technology company developing circular and symbiotic energy value chains based on hydrogen. Its core competence lies in integrating renewable energy, advanced electrolysis, and smart energy management with industrial and aquaculture processes to achieve resource-efficient, zero-emission operation. The company designs and delivers fuel-cell-based generator systems for mobile and stationary power generation, as well as catalytic hydrogen combustion units (NAPOP IP) for waterborne and airborne heating and industrial steam. These systems serve the construction, infrastructure, and process industries, where low-carbon, flexible, and reliable off-grid energy is essential. NAPOP also delivers hydrogen infrastructure solutions, including storage, transport, pressure management, and safety compliance, enabling full-lifecycle hydrogen utilization.
NAPOP has co-founded DRIV Hydrogen AS (50 % ownership), which produces hydrogen through reforming of biomethanol. Pilot production started in September 2025, with commercial operation planned for December 2025. DRIV Hydrogen supplies Umoe Advanced Composites and Hexagon Purus—two of Europe’s leading Type IV hydrogen-tank manufacturers—with services such as initial filling, testing, and maintenance of hydrogen storage systems.
NAPOP’s patented Integrated Symbiotic Industrial Park (ISI-P) concept couples local renewable-energy generation (solar, wind, or hydro) with electrolysis and land-based recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS). A shared energy- and data-management platform reuses surplus heat and oxygen from electrolysis as inputs to fish farming, while dynamic grid connection and local storage enable the provision of grid-balancing services such as frequency and voltage control. The concept achieves up to 40 % local energy self-sufficiency, improving resource utilization, reducing grid dependency, and enhancing energy security. The first ISI-P facility is under development at Åkrestrømmen, Rendalen, where NAPOP owns land and holds aquaculture licences; a second site is planned in Krødsherad. Patent protection was granted on 7 July 2025, and the ISI-P concept is designed as a replicable, integrated industrial module deployable nationally and internationally.
NAPOP wholly owns VIRIDIH2 AS, focusing on hydrogen production and energy systems, and PISCI AS, focusing on sustainable Arctic-char farming. Together they form a cohesive, technology-driven platform for circular industrial development aligned with the European Green Deal and ESA initiatives for sustainable, data-integrated resource systems.
NAPOP’s technologies and data-driven integration model align closely with ESA’s priorities for sustainability, resilience, and digitalization of energy systems. Its operations use Earth-Observation (EO) and satellite-navigation (SatNav) data for site evaluation and optimization of renewable-energy potential, environmental and water-quality monitoring in aquaculture, and dynamic energy management where real-time EO, IoT, and grid data support predictive control and system resilience. These capabilities position NAPOP as a relevant downstream use case within ESA’s Earth Observation for Green Transition and Energy & Environment programmes, demonstrating how space-based data can optimize circular, low-carbon industrial ecosystems on Earth.

entityDescription:
Company OverviewUncharted AI is a deep-tech robotics and artificial intelligence company pioneering autonomous systems for planetary exploration and in-situ resource utilization (ISRU). Originating from research at Polytechnique Montréal’s MIST Lab, Uncharted AI combines multi-robot autonomy, advanced perception, and AI-driven geological intelligence to enable sustainable exploration and extraction of space resources.
Core ExpertiseOur technologies bridge autonomy, sensing, and analytics for robotic operations in GPS-denied, communication-limited, and unstructured environments. We design and deploy AI-powered robotic platforms capable of autonomous exploration, mapping, excavation, and processing of extraterrestrial regolith.Key capabilities include:• Risk-aware multi-robot exploration and mapping for complex terrains such as craters, lava tubes, and regolith fields.• Autonomous excavation and beneficiation of lunar and Martian soil using robotic manipulators and onboard analytical instruments.• Multi-sensor fusion frameworks integrating LiDAR, hyperspectral, GPR, and thermal sensing for sub-surface characterization.• Digital twin and mission planning software for closed-loop control between Earth-based operators and autonomous agents.
Space ApplicationsUncharted AI’s developments directly address challenges in space mining and ISRU operations, including prospecting, excavation, beneficiation, and material handling in lunar and Martian environments.Our robotic systems autonomously identify high-value mineral or volatile-rich zones, perform in-situ processing, and generate actionable insights for science and engineering missions.
Experience and CollaborationsUncharted AI participated in the European Space Agency (ESA) – ESRIC Space Resources Challenge, demonstrating an end-to-end autonomous beneficiation system at the DLR LUNA analog lunar environment in Cologne, Germany.We collaborate with academic institutions, research centers, and industrial partners across Europe and Canada to develop next-generation robotic systems for planetary operations, defense, and extreme-environment exploration.
Mission StatementAt Uncharted AI, we envision a future where intelligent robotic systems extend human capability beyond Earth, enabling responsible and scalable utilization of extraterrestrial resources. Our mission is to make space mining autonomous, sustainable, and data-driven—transforming planetary exploration into a self-reliant, science-enabled industry.

Its technology supports aerospace, automotive, energy, and electronics industries by integrating seamlessly with existing digital engineering workflows. Spaider’s AI networks learn from historical simulation data to create self-improving predictive models, preserving engineering know-how and enhancing design efficiency.

entityDescription:
PYTHAGOR is a FinTech / PropTech / TravelTech algorithm that supports the analysis of current and potential local markets allowing users to calculate and delve into the characteristics of customers present in a city area.​​
Furthermore, Pythagor was born from the desire to revolutionize the methods of analysis of the retail and tourism markets for the purposes of assigning and monitoring creditworthiness, thus improving access to credit by micro, small and medium-sized enterprises.
​Pythagor may be variously utilized by players involved in the establishment, management and evaluation of companies: entrepreneurs and future entrepreneurs, investors, banks, credit managers and other facility providers, risk managers of investment funds.

One of the main success factors of a point of sale or an accommodation facility is the location (= potential customers = turnover): the current methods of calculating potential customers in a territory require resources in terms of time and money and are not easily accessible, understandable or economical.

Our platform helps companies understand the best location in an urban area, taking into account the customer target and the potential basin, allows them to compare themselves with the reference category and validate the business plan, improving access to credit, allowing banks to monitor financed companies against expectations.

entityDescription:
Sofia SAT CLUB
"Empowering the Next Generation of Space Innovators Through EU Collaboration"
Sofia SAT Club is an NGO dedicated to advancing space science and technology education across Bulgaria and Europe. Building on our roots in Bulgaria, we foster cooperation with EU partners— universities, research centers, industries, and other ESA nodes—to create a vibrant, multicultural learning environment. Together, we nurture young talent, promote STEM excellence, and drive impactful educational projects.
Mission and Vision
- Mission: To provide a sustainable, multilingual platform for hands‑on satellite research, STEM training, and international exchanges that inspire and prepare students and enthusiasts for careers in space.
- Vision: A dynamic European network where diverse teams collaborate on small satellite missions, share resources, and develop innovative solutions to global challenges.
Core Objectives
- International Mentorship & Exchange
- Partner with ESA/ESERO Austria, Romania, Greece and other EU offices for best‑practice workshops and teacher training programs.
- Host annual exchange visits for students and mentors.
- Multidisciplinary Research & Development
- Form mixed teams (professionals, university students, school pupils) to design and build CubeSats for real Earth‑observation missions.
- Share data openly within the EU network for joint scientific analysis.
- Sustainable STEM Education
- Deliver courses in person and online (e‑learning modules).
- Develop Bulgarian‑English curricula that can be localized across the EU.
- Community Outreach & Partnerships
- Establish Fab Labs equipped with 3D printers, laser cutters, various tools and robotics kits.
- Collaborate with schools to launch satellite‑robotics competitions.
EU Cooperation & Mutual Benefits
- For Partners:
- Access to a pan‑European network of young innovators and expert mentors.
- Shared IP and data from student satellite missions.
- Joint funding opportunities via Erasmus+, Horizon Europe, and ESERO grants.
- For Sofia SAT Club:
- Enhanced visibility and credibility through established ESA nodes.
- Diverse cultural perspectives and best practices from across Europe.
- Scalable model adaptable to other EU regions.
Together, let’s explore space, advance science, and build lasting European partnerships!

entityDescription:
Fundación CEL – Iniciativas por Lugo is anon-profit organization established in 1997, dedicated to promoting entrepreneurship, innovation, and business development. It acts as a comprehensive support agent for entrepreneurs and startups, with a particular focus on high-value and technology-based sectors.
Its main areas of activity include:
- Business incubation and acceleration, through itsBusiness Incubator and specialized programs providing workspace, mentoring, training, and access to finance.
- Management of public entrepreneurship and innovation programs, in cooperation with regional, national, and European institutions.
- Support for the creation and consolidation of businesses in rural areas, through thePolos de Emprendemento (Entrepreneurship Hubs), fostering territorial development and economic diversification.
- Promotion of entrepreneurial culture and social economy, in collaboration with educational centers, universities, and entrepreneurship networks.
Fundación CEL is the managing entity of BFAero, the aeronautical and aerospace incubator and accelerator of the Government of Galicia (Xunta de Galicia), integrated within the Galician Aerospace Hub.
Since its launch, BFAero has consolidated its national leadership, being rankedNo. 1 in Spain in the Advanced Accelerators category according to theFUNCAS–Rey Juan Carlos University (URJC) ranking for 2024-2025 and 2025-2026.
Through BFAero, Fundación CEL has incubated, accelerated, and consolidated nearly 50 projects in the aeronautics, space, and unmanned systems (UAS)fields, with a focus on technological innovation, scalability, and access to private investment.

Notable space-related success stories include Kreios Space, Valar Espace, and SLIMOP Space, all of them developing disruptive technologies inAir-Breathing Electric Propulsion (ABEP), microsatellites, and advanced optical systems for space telescopes.
Fundación CEL maintains close collaboration with public institutions, universities, technology centers, and leading aerospace companies(such as Airbus, Avincis, Telespazio, and Tecnobit-Aertec), reinforcing technology transfer and international cooperation.
With a methodology based on continuous support, combined public-private financing, and collaborative ecosystems, Fundación CEL actively contributes to strengthening the Galician technological and entrepreneurial fabric, particularly in the fields of aerospace innovation and dual-use technologies (space and defense).

entityDescription:
AFS (Arfima Financial Services) develops and operates Alpha-Klima, a SaaS platform focused on physical climate risk with a strong emphasis on hazard modelling. We transform Earth Observation and climate data into operational hazard footprints and indices for banks and insurers, with full traceability, validation, and delivery through APIs and dashboards.
Our modelling spans extreme heat, riverine/pluvial/coastal flood, wildfire, wind, hail, and drought. Methods include bias-corrected ensembles, statistical downscaling, extreme-value analysis (GEV/GP), and hindcast calibration against observations and claims. We quantify intensity, duration, and severity; derive return-period and IDF curves; estimate annual exceedance probabilities; and provide uncertainty ranges with sensitivity to inputs. Outputs integrate with exposure and vulnerability modules to support underwriting, pricing, and regulatory reporting.

entityDescription: The Centre of Excellence MARBLE (Maritime Robotics and Technologies for Sustainable Blue Economy) is a not-for-profit research organization founded by the University of Zagreb Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computing (UNIZG-FER). MARBLE was formed based on the extensive experience in maritime robotics of the Laboratory for Underwater Systems and Technologies (LABUST). LABUST (https://labust.fer.hr/) has undertaken over 40 projects in the past 15 years, with half of these international, including several FP7, H2020, and Horizon Europe projects, both as a partner and coordinator. That experience led to the creation of MARBLE with the goal of increasing capabilities in applied R&D in maritime robotics for the sustainable blue economy. As part of the planned activities, Centre of Excellence MARBLE will perform research in 4 key research areas: (i) Maritime robotics and autonomous systems, (ii) Maritime green endurance, (iii) Maritime Internet-of-Things, and (iv) Maritime digital twins applied to four blue economy sectors aligned with the Croatian Smart Specialization Strategy: a) Maritime security and protection, b) Aquaculture and fisheries, c) Coastal tourism and smart marinas, and d) Maritime transportation.

KAR Architects Ltd (trading as ViableSite) is a UK-registered architecture and technology company developing an AI-powered feasibility assessment platform that integrates machine learning, financial modelling, and geospatial data — including Ordnance Survey, satellite navigation, and Earth Observation datasets.
The ViableSite platform enables rapid and cost-effective evaluation of small housing development sites, transforming what is traditionally a multi-week, consultant-heavy process into an automated, data-driven assessment completed in hours. The system provides clear go/no-go investment decisions by combining spatial constraints, planning policy, and real construction and market data — helping SME developers identify viable sites and avoid financial risk.
By leveraging space-derived data for site identification, constraint mapping, and environmental analysis, ViableSite demonstrates the practical application of Earth Observation and satellite navigation technologies in the built environment. The platform contributes to more sustainable land use, efficient housing delivery, and improved investment decisions, supporting ESA’s objectives of advancing digital innovation through the use of space assets.
KAR Architects Ltd brings together expertise in architecture, planning, and data science to democratise development intelligence — making property development more accessible, transparent, and sustainable through applied AI and spatial data technologies.

The system provides clear go/no-go investment decisions by combining spatial constraints, planning policy, and real construction and market data — helping SME developers identify viable sites and avoid financial risk.
By leveraging space-derived data for site identification, constraint mapping, and environmental analysis, ViableSite demonstrates the practical application of Earth Observation and satellite navigation technologies in the built environment. The platform contributes to more sustainable land use, efficient housing delivery, and improved investment decisions, supporting ESA’s objectives of advancing digital innovation through the use of space assets.
KAR Architects Ltd brings together expertise in architecture, planning, and data science to democratise development intelligence — making property development more accessible, transparent, and sustainable through applied AI and spatial data technologies.

Dr Bake is a freelance data scientist and analyst with over 6 years of experience as a freelance consulting data scientist, and over 7 years of experience as an academic ecologist working with geospatial and environmental data. He has developed machine learning and computer vision solutions for industry, federal, state, and local governments in the USA, UK, and Australia in a diverse range of domains and technologies including agriculture, aerospace, and economics using tools including but not limited to R, Python, SQL, AWS, and DataBricks.
Most recently, as a senior data scientist for US-based data consultancy EcoData technology he led machine learning development for a decision-support tool to forecast crop disease, including build-out of a cloud-based data infrastructure to automatically ingest and process big data such as climate imagery. Previously he assisted the South Australian Landscape Board with wetland surveying using an automatic wildlife detection tool for fieldcam imagery. He has also contributed to the aerospace sector, developing a novel agent-based market simulation model for a British Interplanetary Society small satellite feasibility study to evaluate the business case for a small satellite launch vehicle.

entityDescription:
University ofPlovdiv “Paisii Hilendarski”
University ofPlovdiv “Paisii Hilendarski” is a leading higher education institution in the Republic of Bulgaria. As the largest university in Southern Bulgaria and the second largest in the country, it plays a significant role in Bulgaria’s academic landscape. Established in 1961 as the Higher Institute of Pedagogy for Natural Sciences and Mathematics, it was officially granted university status in 1972.
The institution educates more than 13,200 full-time students and approximately 5,000 part-time students across 128 bachelor’s and 110 master’s programs. These programs span various disciplines, including natural sciences, humanities, social sciences, engineering, and economics, and are organized within the following nine faculties:
· Faculty of Biology
· Faculty of Mathematics, Informatics, and Information Technology
· Faculty of Economics and Social Sciences
· Faculty of Pedagogy
· Faculty of Physics and Technology
· Faculty of Philology
· Faculty of History and Philosophy
· Faculty of Chemistry
· Faculty of Law
The University maintains two branches in the towns of Smolyan and Kardzhali.
The University ofPlovdiv “Paisii Hilendarski” is equipped with a library, its own publishing house, an information center, scientific laboratories, language and multimedia laboratories, a distance-learning center, a career-guidance service, a research and development division, a sports center, a student theatre, and other technical and service units.
Support for Scientific Research and Project Implementation at Plovdiv University
Plovdiv University “Paisii Hilendarski” is dedicated to fostering scientific research and innovation through a diverse portfolio of research projects. Each year, the university administers numerous research contracts, supported by key national and institutional funding bodies, including the Bulgarian National Research Fund and the Scientific Research Fund at Plovdiv University. In addition to securing public research grants, the University actively collaborates with industry partners through commercial agreements, facilitating knowledge transfer between academia and the private sector. These funding sources support the advancement of scientific inquiry, the development of innovative solutions, and the promotion of knowledge transfer, reinforcing the University’s role as a leading research institution.
Furthermore, the university actively participates in European Union research and education funding programs, including Erasmus+, Horizon Europe, Interreg NEXT, and various other international funding initiatives. These programs play a crucial role in expanding research opportunities, promoting interdisciplinary collaboration, and strengthening global academic networks. The University secures funding both independently and through strategic partnerships with higher education institutions across Europe. By engaging in these initiatives, the University enhances its research capacity, facilitates knowledge exchange, and contributes to addressing both global and regional challenges through interdisciplinary and cross-border cooperation.

- Space for at least 250 long-term aircraft parking.
- A free-congestion international airport.
- Easy access to all services and high quality employees.
Alejandro Ibrahim Perera
General Manager of Teruel AirportPLATA is owned by a Consortium formed by the Government of Aragon and Teruel City Council, and it does not belong to AENA Group. It is designed to be an open platform in a strategic location where aeronautical companies around the world could base their operations in a very competitive conditions.
Near Toulouse, Teruel is located between the largest cities in Spain: Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Zaragoza and Bilbao (60% of Spanish GDP and more than 20 million people in the 400 km surroundings).
PLATA is an appropriate Aero-Industrial site, offering to the companies the most favorable opportunities for locating and expanding their aeronautical and aerospace business.
In addition, PLATA is well known for its leadership and expertise in maintenance, MRO, parking and recycling for aircraft and helicopters. PLATA is also endeavoring new business for executive and general aviation, UAV-RPA research & developments, and other aerospace activities.
Moreover, it is noteworthy the modern airport infrastructure, its flexible features allowing in future the possibility to expand to passenger traffic and air cargo, as an alternative development for the Airport.
PLATA offers exceptional economical operating conditions for those companies willing to establish at the airport to carry out any aeronautical activity. The Consortium has advantages packages for landing fees, rental of camp, hangar rental and possibility to sale industrial land.
Investment and Incentives: The Government of Aragon offers incentives for those new companies willing to set up operations at PLATA, through investing in new activities, hiring and training new staff, and assistance with job-creation schemes, R&D and technological innovation activities, etc.

entityDescription:
The Scientific Association for Mechanical Engineering (GTE) is Hungary’s prominent professional and scientific organisation uniting the engineering-intellectual community in the field of mechanical and processing industry. Founded in 1949 as an independent association and tracing its roots back to earlier engineer-associations from the 19th century, it has evolved into one of the largest technical and social organisations in Hungary with more than a thousand individual and corporate members across 27 divisions and all regions of the country. 
GTE’s mission emphasises reinforcing technical competency, facilitating collaboration among academia, research institutions and industry, and promoting the industrial transformation of manufacturing. Its public-benefit goals include supporting research and development, enhancing the added value of domestic mechanical and processing industries, disseminating advanced manufacturing technologies, supporting SMEs, organising training and publishing professional journals. 
GTE has been placing strong emphasis on supporting the digital and sustainable transformation of the Hungarian manufacturing sector. The Association is founding member of national “Industry 4.0” technology platform, helping to facilitate cooperation between university research groups, SMEs and large enterprises. Its programmes increasingly address topics such as additive manufacturing (3D printing), data-driven production, artificial intelligence in manufacturing, and smart factory logistics 
Moreover, GTE is striving to elevate Hungary’s mechanical industrial competitiveness by acting as a conduit for internationally leading technologies and standards. It brings together domestic engineering intellectuals and foreign partners via its membership in international bodies such as the International Academy for Production Engineering (CIRP) and the Fédération Internationale des Sociétés d’Ingénieurs des Techniques de l’Automobile (FISITA). Its current development roadmap also places emphasis on supporting SMEs in integrating advanced manufacturing technologies, promoting industrial standardisation, and publishing research results that facilitate the transition to higher value-added production.

GEE BioTech works on biological and engineering aspects of microbial bioreactors. Our process can produce sustainable biomaterials and aid life support on space stations.
We are conducting R&D on these system with the goal of deploying microbial factories on Lunar and Martian stations so microbial biochemicals can be extracted to produce bioproducts, including but not limited to biofuel, bioplastics, carbon fiber, biominerals, antioxidants, and food stuffs. 
Our technology can also capture and use space station waste (e.g. urine and carbon dioxide), while producing oxygen for the station atmosphere.
GEE BioTech works closely with the ESA Biotesc group at the Hochschule Luzern in deisgning experiments of the ISS and other space missions.

entityDescription:
The Aragon Aerospace, Space and Defence Cluster (AERA) is the regional industrial cluster representing the aerospace, space and defence sectors in Aragón (Spain). Established in 2007, AERA brings together more than 60 members, including large companies, SMEs, technology centres, universities and public institutions. Its mission is to foster innovation, competitiveness and collaboration within the regional and European aerospace and defence ecosystem.
AERA acts as a regional driver for advanced manufacturing, digitalisation, circular economy and dual-use innovation, fully aligned with the Smart Specialisation Strategy (RIS3) of Aragón. The cluster promotes cooperation between industry, research and public administration, serving as a bridge to connect regional capabilities with European strategic priorities.
AERA is a founding member of the European Aerospace Cluster Partnership (EACP), which brings together over 45 clusters from more than 20 European countries, and a founding member of the Aragón Defence Hub, a strategic regional initiative that unites industry, academia, research and public institutions to strengthen defence-related innovation, technology development and industrial cooperation in Aragón.
Through its participation in European networks and projects, AERA contributes to the development of resilient and sustainable industrial value chains, promotes training and skills development, and supports the dual-use application of technologies for both civil and defence markets. Its close collaboration with the Government of Aragón and its active role within European cluster networks make AERA a key player in fostering interregional innovation and industrial transformation.

entityDescription:
The recently established spin-off company, OPMET Labs s.r.o., focuses on developing innovative technologies and measuring devices in the field of optical metrology, primarily aimed at measuring the shape of optical surfaces and wavefronts of optical systems. These devices are intended for use in the manufacture of optical elements or complex systems designed for applications in space, high-power lasers, and sensitive diagnostic instruments. In addition, they are expected to find broad application in the production of consumer electronics and other industries.
The measuring devices employ several innovative approaches and unconventional principles, including absolute interferometry based on tunable lasers, generation of optical twins of the simulated system, utilization of graphic multicore units, and the application of selected machine learning principles.
The company’s team builds upon and further develops the expertise transferred from the TOPTEC research centre (Institute of Plasma Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences). The core group of the company has been intensively dedicated to developing metrological methods and instrumentation for more than 12 years.

entityDescription:
The Reiner Lemoine Institute is an independent non-profit research institution that contributes to a transformation towards a sustainable energy supply based on 100 % renewable energy since its founding in 2010. In our many years of experience we have conducted applied research to scientifically support the long-term transition of the energy supply system towards renewable energy. Open source models developed here have firmly established themselves in energy system modeling. Our mobility and electrification concepts have been implemented by private companies as well as the public sector worldwide.

Our scientific research is conducted in three interconnected research units:
Theresearch unit Transformation of Energy Systemsdevelops, investigates, and optimizes future scenarios for a sustainable energy supply. For this, self-developed open source tools are mostly used. Among others these include dialogue and visualization tools for the energy transition
Theresearch unit Mobility with Renewable Energyconducts research at the interface between sustainable drive systems and renewable power generation. As a contribution to the energy transition in the transport sector, we examine how alternatives to gasoline and diesel engines can be incorporated in renewable energy systems in an economically and ecologically reasonable manner and what charging infrastructure will be needed in the future.
Theresearch unit Off-Grid Systemsdevelops electrification strategies based on renewable energy for developing regions and optimizes hybrid mini-grids with the help of simulation models and geographic information software. By this we especially support the UN Sustainable Development Goal for affordable and clean energy (SDG7) as well as climate action (SDG13).
