entityDescription:
Sogetel S.r.l. is an Italian company operating in the ICT sector since 1981, with its legal and operational headquarters in Rome. The company provides high-tech services and solutions, supporting its clients in their digital transformation journey. It specializes in data management, processing, and valorization, customized software development, complex systems design, and the implementation of innovative solutions in fields such as Big Data, Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things (IoT), and Cybersecurity.
Sogetel’s revenues come from three main business lines:
- Specialized ICT Consulting: Sogetel offers its clients highly skilled technical-managerial professionals, thanks to a continuous talent scouting and acquisition process.
- Turnkey Software Development: Design, development, and maintenance of custom software applications for clients.
- Proprietary Innovative Solutions: The company has a dedicated department for the design and development of proprietary products and innovative solutions, based on market research insights and client/prospect feedback (e.g., Isaac, Higitus, Zencluster, KaiSafe, Kainet).
Over the last five years, the company has recorded an average annual turnover of around €8 million, totaling over €22 million in the 2022–2024 period. As of December 31, 2024, shareholders’ equity amounted to €2.49 million.
Across all business lines, Sogetel maintains strong quality control, supported by ISO 9001 and ISO 27001 certifications, and by the constant involvement of technical and commercial managers throughout the entire service lifecycle, ensuring alignment between client expectations and delivered results.
Sogetel has long-standing collaborations with key players in the ICT and industrial sectors, including:
- Main clients: TIM, Vodafone, Fastweb, Engineering, DXC Technology, Capgemini, IBI (pharmaceutical), Octo Telematics, ALD Automotive, Latteria Soresina.
- Strategic and technology partners: Red Hat, Noovle (TIM Group), Confluent, Mare Consulting, Alleantia, Crico Italia.
Thanks to this solid ecosystem of relationships, Sogetel is able to deliver end-to-end solutions, integrating ICT know-how with hardware, sensors, and strategic consulting.
- Proprietary platforms:
- Kainet – Industrial IoT platform
- Isaac DE – Big Data management (NoSQL)
- Isaac TS – Time-series sensor data analytics
- Higitus – AI-based automation and data classification
- Zencluster – Distributed cloud environment for real-time applications

description:
At Lios, we believe the world shouldn’t have to choose between performance and peace. Our breakthrough acoustic material, SoundBounce, is transforming industries by delivering superior noise reduction in a compact, lightweight, sustainable, and high performance material. 
Born from over a decade of acoustic research, Lios is driven by science, innovation, and a commitment to creating a quieter, greener world. Whether it’s protecting workers from harmful noise, enhancing vehicle acoustics, or improving urban environments, we partner with forward thinking companies to solve their toughest noise challenges. 
SoundBounce will revolutionise how we combat noise in our world.
entityDescription:
Lios, formerly Restored Hearing, was founded in 2009 by Rhona Togher and Eimear O’Carroll.Our company mission of eradicating noise pollution is achieved through the development of materials which reduce the initial risk of exposure to loud noise and technologies which alleviate damage after it has occurred. Over the past decade, the company has grown into a powerhouse of innovative, expert problem-solvers. We have combined our advanced knowledge in physics with our experience of avoidable hearing damage. At Lios, we work tirelessly to combat noise pollution, meeting industry challenges head-on with a fresh perspective.
SoundBounce is a game-changing innovation in the acoustic materials industry. • Physical & PCB Design
Intecs Engineering employs around 160 professionals, over 90% of whom hold university degrees in engineering, computer science, or other technical disciplines.

entityDescription:
If today Università degli Studi di Camerino - UNICAM is one of the most interesting and innovative Italian institutions, it is, without doubt, the merit of the strength and momentum attributed to it by its rich history. UNICAM was fundend on XIII century (1259) and became State University on 1958 (Italian Law n. 254 13.03.1958).
With a solid scientific-cultural tradition,the University of Camerino now has five University Schools:Architecture and Design, Biosciences and Veterinary Medicine, Pharmaceutical and Health Products, Law, Science and Technology. As a university of European ambitions, Camerino has always been committed to developing a differentiated and cutting-edge educational offer; the highly innovative Master’s programmes and Doctoral PhD Programmes, the delocalisation of institutional teaching activities through the adoption of the most modern remote and online technologies, and the average first employment waiting time, which for the majority of UNICAM graduates is less than a year, testify to this fact. UNICAM is known for its strong commitment to scientific research, supported by state-of-the-art laboratories and research facilities. Its scientific laboratories, distributed across the various schools—such as the School of Science and Technology, the School of Biosciences and Veterinary Medicine, and the School of Pharmacy—are equipped for advanced research in areas like molecular biology, environmental science, chemistry, physics, and computer science. These labs play a central role in fostering innovation, supporting both fundamental and applied research, and encouraging collaboration at national and international levels. UNICAM is a key player in numerous national and international research projects, including European Union-funded initiatives under programs like Horizon Europe. These projects foster interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation, reinforcing UNICAM’s role within the global research community and contributing to technological and scientific advancement.

Backend and frontend development for aerospace platforms

Machine learning applied to launch matchmaking and mission feasibility analysis

entityDescription:
SpaceGuardian is a subscription-based Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform that provides automatic satellite collision prevention and maneuver optimization for commercial satellite operators. By continuously monitoring satellite trajectories and leveraging predictive algorithms, SpaceGuardian proactively identifies potential collisions and autonomously calculates, simulates, and executes optimal avoidance maneuvers.
Unlike traditional tools that rely on manual, error-prone, and fuel-intensive post-collision detection processes, SpaceGuardian delivers a fully automated, intelligent, and fuel-efficient response system. The platform considers long-term satellite health by optimizing for fuel usage, future collision risk, and mission efficiency.
It supports advanced scenarios such as:
- Maneuverable vs. Non-Maneuverable satellite encounters,
- Maneuverable vs. Maneuverable cases using an integrated bidding system where the lower bidder performs the maneuver,
- Future collision prediction with early, minor adjustments to prevent major course corrections later.

entityDescription:
FAST Aerospace is developing a launcher with a Launch as a Service (LaaS) business model. In the meantime, it is also capitalizing on intermediary technological products. Today, it focuses on ramjet propulsion systems, building proprietary know-how and corporate value. Through partnerships and a “make-to-order” model, private or public customers can request custom-built ramjet engines tailored to their mission profiles and performance specifications.
After the ramjet, FAST aims at commercializing StratoDart, a high-speed flight test platform designed for supersonic and hypersonic applications. This technological milestone can be leveraged thanks to a Test as a Service (TaaS) model, in which customers can lease onboard payload space to flight-test advanced materials, software, or components at high Mach numbers in relevant atmospheric conditions.
Finally, once HyperDart reaches the market, FAST enter the space access market. With LaaS, customers send their satellites to one of FAST’s integration hubs, where the payload is prepared and integrated in a cleanroom according to mission-specific requirements. The payload faring is then mounted on HyperDart’s second stage, ready for takeoff and orbit insertion.

entityDescription:
Portolan Association, established in 2021 and based in Geneva, Switzerland, is a non-profit organization focused on the monitoring of water resources and climate to support integrated water resources management. Its core activities include hydrometeorological monitoring, hydraulic analysis, and the improvement of water data availability for end-users and decision-makers. Portolan works across diverse geographic contexts, with a particular emphasis on data-driven approaches to support sustainable water governance and climate adaptation strategies.
Portolan collaborates closely with leading academic institutions such as the Technical University of Munich (TUM), University of Fribourg, Brunel University, University of Twente, Grenoble University, Delft Technical University, and the Central Asian Institute for Applied Geosciences. These partnerships have enabled Portolan to carry out extensive fieldwork and applied research, contributing to both academic knowledge and practical applications in water and environmental management.
Portolan has also contributed to the preparation of ecosystem research and restoration, particularly in relation to the monitoring of Nature-Based Solutions (NbS) and their performance under varying hydrological conditions. Our expertise spans mountainous regions, wetlands, and river basins.
The association’s strength lies in its interdisciplinary approach, combining hydrological and climate monitoring (including soil moist, snow and groundwater where relevant) with the analysis of impacts of hydraulic structures on lakes and rivers. This enables us to support adaptive water management practices that are responsive to both environmental variability and infrastructure dynamics.

LifeWatch ERIC is the European e-Science Infrastructure for Biodiversity and Ecosystem Research, set up as a European Research Infrastructure Consortium (ERIC) under EU law in 2017. Headquartered in Seville, Spain, it brings together contributions from several member countries to provide the scientific community with advanced digital tools and services. Its mission is to integrate data, models, and research capacities across Europe to help address pressing environmental challenges such as climate change, habitat loss, invasive species, and the sustainable management of natural resources. By offering interoperable and open access to data and services, LifeWatch ERIC plays a central role in strengthening the European Research Area.
Through its virtual research environments, high-performance computing resources, and advanced data integration services, LifeWatch ERIC enables scientists and policymakers to better understand, monitor, and protect biodiversity and ecosystems. It supports cutting-edge research, fosters innovation in environmental management, and builds capacity through training and collaboration, ultimately acting as a bridge between science, governance, and society.

entityDescription: Delphea is a technology company specialized in the development of the European ECORCE TCAD tool, an advanced simulation software designed to model and predict the impact of radiation on semiconductor devices, including Total Ionizing Dose (TID), Total Non-Ionizing Dose (TNID), and Single Event Effects (SEE). Combining a powerful dynamic mesh generator with high-accuracy algorithms, ECORCE enables efficient multidimensional simulations in a single run, supporting industries where reliability under harsh environments is critical, such as aerospace, space exploration, nuclear energy, medical technology, and automotive electronics. Founded in 2019 with roots at the University of Montpellier, Delphea also provides consulting, case studies, and training, bridging simulation with experimental data to help organizations analyze radiation sensitivity, interpret test results, qualify new devices, and improve overall robustness in extreme conditions.

description: Synchronous Science is on a mission to equip defence and national-security leaders with clear, actionable insights into electromagnetic sensing and communication challenges. Through a systems-thinking approach and extensive engineering expertise, we swiftly identify hidden vulnerabilities and untapped opportunities
entityDescription:
We perform research and development on a broad range of defence-related electromagnetic problems. These have included studies of the threats and vulnerabilities of contemporary and novel communication systems, including 4G LTE and 5G NR cellular, and the increasingly popular Internet of Things technologies such as LoRA and SigFox. A particular focus has been their potential use in adversaries' triggering mechanisms of RCIEDs and how to thwart this. In addition, we are interested in the resurgence of modern HF systems, the prediction of propagation-related phenomena, and the transmission of RF and microwave over optical links. Additional work has included the agile design and implementation of novel RF test and measurement environments over short timescales. 

Outside of work on communication systems, we have performed research into improved intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition, and reconnaissance techniques in synthetic aperture radar and optical domains. This has included research into the theoretical design and practical characterisation of novel low-observable materials. 

Our director has a PhD in Optoelectronics, an MSc (with distinction) in Communication Systems Engineering and a BSc in Mathematics. He has a solid theoretical, computational and experimental physics and engineering background and has contributed to academic and industrial works. He has also obtained memberships of the Institution of Engineering and Technology (IET), Institute of Physics (IoP) and Institute of Mathematics and Its Applications (IMA), as well as being a corporate member of ADS Group and Team Defense Information. 

We enjoy meeting with customers and suppliers to develop new generation-after-next solutions. Technological advancements are only made through discussions with the end-user.

Epona AI Labs is an Irish deep-tech company based in Kinsale, Co. Cork, focused on developing next-generation contextual acoustic sensing systems for industrial applications. The company’s core innovation lies in fusing AI-driven acoustic analysis with environmental intelligence derived from ESA Sentinel satellite data. This approach enables more accurate machine health monitoring and hazard detection in complex environments such as quarries, construction sites, and agricultural settings.
Founded in 2023 by a multidisciplinary team with expertise in AI, acoustics, and industrial technology strategy, Epona is committed to building scalable, energy-efficient sensing solutions that operate effectively in visually degraded and remote locations. The company is currently advancing its prototype toward commercial deployment and has secured strategic collaborations with industry leaders and research institutions.
Epona has been awarded a grant from ESA BIC Ireland to support the integration of satellite data into its sensing platform, accelerating its development and market readiness. Through a combination of R&D, strategic IP development, and pilot deployments, Epona aims to position itself as a European leader in satellite-enhanced industrial sensing solutions.

description:
We develop the long-lasting heart of fuel cells and electrolysers. 
Hydrogen fuel cells and electrolysers play a key role in the global energy transition. The heart of both technologies is the membrane electrode assembly (MEA), which enables the conversion of hydrogen into electricity—and vice versa. The MEA is the component that largely determines the lifetime and cost of electrolysers and fuel cells. Duramea plans to revolutionise MEA production with a patent-pending technology: a polyaniline coating that protects the MEA against corrosion without impairing its performance. This innovation doubles MEA lifetime while maintaining efficiency. 
Our initial focus is to supply durable, high-performance MEAs for the scientific market. In the long term, Duramea aims to scale production and enable cost-efficient mass manufacturing of robust MEAs for applications on Earth, in lunar stations, and beyond. 
USP: Our patent-pending membrane electrode assembly doubles the service life of fuel cells and electrolysers.

entityDescription:
Everimpact, established in 2014, has a core mission to empower local authorities and industrial sectors to adopt more decisive climate action. This mission aligns with the goals of influential global organizations such as C40, R20, and ICLEI, which are all dedicated to driving climate action on a global scale.
However, the climate action efforts of French local authorities face significant hurdles due to the centralized nature of greenhouse gas reduction responsibility and a lack of resources. This centralized structure can stifle local initiatives and innovation, while resource constraints can limit the scope and ambition of climate action plans.
To address these challenges, Everimpact initially developed a solution that utilizes IoT sensors in urban spaces to gather data and inform climate action strategies. Proof of concept (POC) projects using this technology are currently underway in various cities around the world, demonstrating the potential of this approach.
Looking ahead, Everimpact recognizes that satellite measurement will be crucial for future success. Satellite technology can gradually reduce the reliance on IoT sensors while providing a broader and more comprehensive picture of greenhouse gas emissions and climate impacts. In particular, NewSpace, a burgeoning sector of the space industry, is poised to play a key role. NewSpace companies are developing innovative and cost-effective satellite technologies that can significantly improve the quality and frequency of measurements, all while driving down costs. This advancement will enable more accurate and timely data collection, which is essential for effective climate action planning and decision-making.

entityDescription:
Acusttel (Acústica y Telecomunicaciones, S.L.) is a Spanish engineering company founded in 1997 and headquartered in Gandía, Valencia. With more than 25 years of experience, it specializes in acoustic and vibration engineering, offering consulting, measurement, and turnkey solutions for environmental noise, building acoustics, and industrial sound control. Its accredited laboratory and test chambers, certified by ENAC, allow the company to perform product testing and acoustic certification in compliance with national and European regulations.

The company provides a broad range of services: acoustic design and insulation for buildings and industrial facilities, noise and vibration diagnostics, and environmental acoustic quality control. It develops customized solutions for ventilation systems, machinery, and other noise sources, supporting clients through every stage of a project—from initial measurements and modelling to final mitigation strategies. Acusttel also conducts design and analysis of materials’ acoustic behavior, evaluating how different construction or industrial materials absorb, transmit, or attenuate sound to optimize their performance in real-world applications.

A key differentiator is Acusttel’s underwater acoustics division. This specialized area covers the measurement and analysis of sound propagation in aquatic environments such as ports, offshore platforms, and marine construction sites. Using hydrophones and advanced modelling, the team assesses underwater noise, predicts sound transmission, and designs mitigation measures to protect marine ecosystems and comply with environmental regulations. These services are essential for activities like dredging, underwater piling, and coastal engineering projects.

Combining terrestrial and subaquatic expertise with advanced material analysis, Acusttel offers a complete acoustic engineering portfolio backed by rigorous technical standards and decades of know-how. Its mission is to improve environmental quality and reduce acoustic pollution on land and underwater, ensuring regulatory compliance while safeguarding human comfort and marine life.

Company description: Acusttel (Acústica y Telecomunicaciones, S.L.) is a Spanish engineering company founded in 1997 and headquartered in Gandía, Valencia. With more than 25 years of experience, it specializes in acoustic and vibration engineering, offering consulting, measurement, and turnkey solutions for environmental noise, building acoustics, and industrial sound control. Its accredited laboratory and test chambers, certified by ENAC, allow the company to perform product testing and acoustic certification in compliance with national and European regulations.

The company provides a broad range of services: acoustic design and insulation for buildings and industrial facilities, noise and vibration diagnostics, and environmental acoustic quality control. It develops customized solutions for ventilation systems, machinery, and other noise sources, supporting clients through every stage of a project—from initial measurements and modelling to final mitigation strategies. Acusttel also conducts design and analysis of materials’ acoustic behavior, evaluating how different construction or industrial materials absorb, transmit, or attenuate sound to optimize their performance in real-world applications.

A key differentiator is Acusttel’s underwater acoustics division. This specialized area covers the measurement and analysis of sound propagation in aquatic environments such as ports, offshore platforms, and marine construction sites. Using hydrophones and advanced modelling, the team assesses underwater noise, predicts sound transmission, and designs mitigation measures to protect marine ecosystems and comply with environmental regulations. These services are essential for activities like dredging, underwater piling, and coastal engineering projects.

Combining terrestrial and subaquatic expertise with advanced material analysis, Acusttel offers a complete acoustic engineering portfolio backed by rigorous technical standards and decades of know-how. Its mission is to improve environmental quality and reduce acoustic pollution on land and underwater, ensuring regulatory compliance while safeguarding human comfort and marine life.

entityDescription:
AXID is a French engineering firm specializing in power electronics. We offer tailor-made solutions combining innovation and reliability, thus meeting the performance and quality requirements of manufacturers in the defense, aerospace, aviation, automotive, hydrogen, and special vehicle industries.
At AXID, we strive to stay ahead in the field of power electronics by leveraging the latest scientific advancements and collaborating with research laboratories.
We develop modern converters, particularly resonant architectures, to design increasingly compact and efficient solutions with high performance.
Our activity is closely linked to the energy transition, as the majority of our projects address this major challenge.We thus design:
photovoltaic inverters converting solar energy into electricity,

onboard battery chargers to enhance the performance of electric vehicles,

converters for electrolyzers, promoting hydrogen production,

the adaptation of fuel cells to operate efficiently with hydrogen,

bidirectional chargers for stationary energy storage.

Our commitment to the environment is also reflected in our internal operations: our wooden facilities are equipped with 200 kWp of photovoltaic panels, allowing us to actively contribute, on our scale, to the energy transition.
Our expertise covers a wide range of technologies:
wide bandgap transistors (GaN, SiC),

but also IGBTs and thyristors, when required by the applications,

advanced magnetic design (inductors, planar transformers, Litz wire windings).

These skills are essential for mastering very high frequencies, a specialty of our team, and for developing high-efficiency converters.As a design office, we aim to push the limits of components and sometimes even encourage manufacturers to step out of their comfort zones. Our goal: to design increasingly compact and efficient power converters, in the service of sustainable innovation and enhanced energy efficiency.

entityDescription:
The Port Network Authority of the Eastern Adriatic Sea is a public body having as its primary task to direct, plan, coordinate, promote and control port operations and commercial and industrial activities in the ports of Trieste and Monfalcone, being respectively core and comprehensive nodes in the TEN-T network.
Port of Trieste is an international hub for overland and sea trade with the dynamic markets of Central and Eastern Europe, and it is the top-ranking Italian port for total throughout, with more than 56 million tons (2024) as well as for intermodal trains – almost 10,000 trains.
By the national legislation on ports – D.Lgs. 169/2016, art. 4bis – Italian Port Authorities are responsible for measuring the port’s carbon footprint and setting an action plan for reducing CO2 emissions and monitoring and mitigating the impact of climate change.
The Port Network Authority of the Eastern Adriatic Sea is a member of the North Adriatic Port Association (NAPA), which has the goal of promoting the Northern Adriatic route as an alternative to the North-European ports and the development of maritime and hinterland connections, environmental protection, safety and information technology.

The Port Network Authority of the Eastern Adriatic Sea does not perform economic activities on the market.

entityDescription:
Company Overview - GEMINI Space Solutions & Consulting (SSC)
GEMINI Space Solutions & Consulting (SSC) is a Netherlands-based SME operating at the forefront of Earth Observation (EO) innovation, data fusion, and applied artificial intelligence. Backed by a trusted international network of research and industry partners, GEMINI SSC delivers tailored EO-based services and consulting across Europe and beyond - empowering public authorities, research institutions, and commercial actors with insights that drive sustainability, resilience, and innovation.
As a long-standing contributor to ESA’s EO ecosystem, GEMINI SSC specialises in multi-source satellite data processing - integrating Copernicus Sentinel missions, Contributing Missions (CCM), and very high-resolution datasets with in-situ and municipal data streams. Its work focuses particularly on urban environments, smart-city services, and climate adaptation, aligning with ESA’s Φ-lab and InCubed priorities and supporting digital-green transitions across Europe.
Core Business Lines: Urban Analytics & EO Services: EO-based monitoring and analytics across climate adaptation, mobility, pollution, green infrastructure, and energy transition - with AI-enhanced tools for municipalities and agencies. AI and Data Fusion Models: Integration of satellite data with mobility, IoT, and socio-economic indicators to deliver fine-grained, predictive insights tailored to user needs. End-to-End Project Deployment: From concept design to system prototyping, including field validation and co-development with local users. Capacity Building & Policy Support: Technical training and institutional capacity development to support uptake of EO and AI by cities, ministries, and research organisations. Geospatial Data Provisioning: On-demand delivery of fused EO datasets for calibration, validation, and operational use - including pre-processed ML-ready indices (NDVI, NO2, change detection, impervious surfaces, etc.).
Vision and Mission: GEMINI SSC’s vision is to harness the power of satellite data, artificial intelligence, and cloud infrastructure to support next-generation urban resilience and planetary sustainability. We aim to make geospatial intelligence more accessible, interpretable, and actionable - serving as a catalyst for evidence-based decision making across sectors.
Forward Capabilities and Strategic Outlook: With deep domain expertise and cross-sector engagement, GEMINI SSC is positioned to incubate and scale innovative solutions such as Space-enabled Urban Digital Twins for predictive planning and climate adaptation, powered by AI-ready Copernicus pipelines; Edge-AI EO CubeSat Prototypes enabling on-board analytics for fast-response monitoring of urban heat, emissions, land change, and mobility; Impact Dashboards for Municipalities translating EO/AI outputs into operational tools for decision-makers; Smart Resilience Indices to support EU Green Deal, Climate Law, and SDG tracking across urban contexts; Capacity building and co-design pilots with cities in the Netherlands, Germany, France and other ESA Member States, particularly in synergy with Φ-lab, InCubed and Destination Earth frameworks; Bridging Science, Innovation, and Policy by translating cutting-edge Earth Observation research into actionable frameworks for EU missions, national space strategies, and smart-city programmes - with active engagement in Φ-lab initiatives, InCubed, Horizon Europe, and key fora such as EC, EARSC, NEREUS, IAC, and UN-led platforms.
GEMINI SSC is well positioned to support ESA EO programmes - from InCubed and DestinE to Φ-sat and AI-enhanced CubeSat demonstrators - with an emphasis on scalability, cross-sector engagement, and transformational impact.

Backed by a trusted international network of research and industry partners, GEMINI SSC delivers tailored EO-based services and consulting across Europe and beyond - empowering public authorities, research institutions, and commercial actors with insights that drive sustainability, resilience, and innovation.
As a long-standing contributor to ESA’s EO ecosystem, GEMINI SSC specialises in multi-source satellite data processing - integrating Copernicus Sentinel missions, Contributing Missions (CCM), and very high-resolution datasets with in-situ and municipal data streams. Its work focuses particularly on urban environments, smart-city services, and climate adaptation, aligning with ESA’s Φ-lab and InCubed priorities and supporting digital-green transitions across Europe.
Core Business Lines: Urban Analytics & EO Services: EO-based monitoring and analytics across climate adaptation, mobility, pollution, green infrastructure, and energy transition - with AI-enhanced tools for municipalities and agencies. AI and Data Fusion Models: Integration of satellite data with mobility, IoT, and socio-economic indicators to deliver fine-grained, predictive insights tailored to user needs. End-to-End Project Deployment: From concept design to system prototyping, including field validation and co-development with local users. Capacity Building & Policy Support: Technical training and institutional capacity development to support uptake of EO and AI by cities, ministries, and research organisations. Geospatial Data Provisioning: On-demand delivery of fused EO datasets for calibration, validation, and operational use - including pre-processed ML-ready indices (NDVI, NO2, change detection, impervious surfaces, etc.).
Vision and Mission: GEMINI SSC’s vision is to harness the power of satellite data, artificial intelligence, and cloud infrastructure to support next-generation urban resilience and planetary sustainability. We aim to make geospatial intelligence more accessible, interpretable, and actionable - serving as a catalyst for evidence-based decision making across sectors.
Forward Capabilities and Strategic Outlook: With deep domain expertise and cross-sector engagement, GEMINI SSC is positioned to incubate and scale innovative solutions such as Space-enabled Urban Digital Twins for predictive planning and climate adaptation, powered by AI-ready Copernicus pipelines; Edge-AI EO CubeSat Prototypes enabling on-board analytics for fast-response monitoring of urban heat, emissions, land change, and mobility; Impact Dashboards for Municipalities translating EO/AI outputs into operational tools for decision-makers; Smart Resilience Indices to support EU Green Deal, Climate Law, and SDG tracking across urban contexts; Capacity building and co-design pilots with cities in the Netherlands, Germany, France and other ESA Member States, particularly in synergy with Φ-lab, InCubed and Destination Earth frameworks; Bridging Science, Innovation, and Policy by translating cutting-edge Earth Observation research into actionable frameworks for EU missions, national space strategies, and smart-city programmes - with active engagement in Φ-lab initiatives, InCubed, Horizon Europe, and key fora such as EC, EARSC, NEREUS, IAC, and UN-led platforms.
GEMINI SSC is well positioned to support ESA EO programmes - from InCubed and DestinE to Φ-sat and AI-enhanced CubeSat demonstrators - with an emphasis on scalability, cross-sector engagement, and transformational impact.

entityDescription:
Astranova Partners is a strategic consulting firm specializing in accelerating the growth of fintech companies, payment platforms, brokers, and wealthtech organizations across Europe and LATAM. With over 15 years of experience, Astranova combines proven methodologies—such as its proprietary S.C.A.L.E. framework—with hands-on execution, strategy, and advanced technology to deliver sustainable commercial growth.
The team focuses on designing and implementing expansion strategies, optimizing revenue, and supporting international go-to-market efforts. Astranova Partners works closely with clients as genuine strategic allies, integrating with their teams to drive impact, generate real value, and establish lasting relationships.
Astranova leads and manages several projects across the fintech and digital sectors. One of these projects is Sentinel Crop (sentinelcrop.com), for which the company is currently applying to a development program.

Sentinel Crop is transforming agricultural insurance through innovative technology. The platform combines real-time satellite monitoring, blockchain, and AI-powered risk assessment to deliver accurate, transparent, and fully automated crop insurance solutions.
Using Copernicus Sentinel satellite data, Sentinel Crop continuously tracks crop health, employing NDVI analysis and advanced vegetation indices. Its machine learning models analyze weather patterns, soil conditions, and historical records to predict crop risks with up to 95% accuracy. Blockchain technology, specifically Ethereum-based smart contracts, ensures that all insurance policies and claims are processed automatically, transparently, and immutably.
Farmers easily register their parcels, access real-time monitoring, and purchase customized parametric insurance policies—receiving instant, paperwork-free payouts when pre-set conditions are met. For insurance companies, Sentinel Crop delivers robust AI-driven risk data, enables creation of objective policies, and streamlines portfolio management with live analytics and automated claims processing.
Sentinel Crop stands out for its instant payouts, high accuracy, transparency, and always up-to-date satellite insights—making it a next-generation solution for both agricultural producers and insurers.

entityDescription:
Neutron Star Systems (NSS)is a European deep-tech SME headquartered in Cologne, Germany, developing advanced propulsion and power systems for the next generation of spacecraft. At the core of our approach is the integration ofhigh-temperature superconductors (HTS)into propulsion and power architectures, enabling spacecraft that are more powerful, compact, and efficient than the current state of the art.
Our flagship product is SUPREME™, Europe’s first HTS-based Applied-Field Magnetoplasmadynamic (AF-MPD) thruster. SUPREME delivers unprecedented thrust density and scalability, operating from 3–10 kW per unit today with a roadmap towards 100 kW-class systems. It can use affordable, storable propellants such as argon, ammonia, or water, providing operational flexibility compared to xenon-dependent systems. SUPREME can also be hybridised with chemical propulsion, enablingmulti-mode systemsthat combine the high efficiency of electric propulsion with the rapid response of chemical thrusters. This allows more agile orbital manoeuvres, cost-effective logistics, and dual-use applications acrossLEO, GEO, cislunar and interplanetary domains.
In parallel, NSS is developing HTS-based power management and distribution solutions, including superconducting harnesses, delivering near-lossless power transfer and improved thermal stability. These are complemented by AI-driven autonomy and digital twin architectures that enable spacecraft to plan, adapt, and operate with greater resilience in congested and contested environments.
Key projects and validation:
- SUPREME (EIC Transition project):Critical Design Review completed, progressing to TRL 5–6 by 2026 with full prototype testing.

- STORM (EIC Pathfinder, €3.6M):A solar weather forecasting constellation providing early-warning data to enhance spacecraft autonomy and resilience.

- MEESST (EIC Pathfinder):Demonstrated superconducting-based re-entry technologies with >50% heat flux mitigation.

- BEEHIVE (EIC Accelerator, submission 2025):Development of a Digital Twin Mission Emulator and multimode propulsion architectures for scalable orbital logistics.

NSS has built a strongintellectual property portfolio, covering propulsion systems, thermal management, superconducting harnesses, and smart spacecraft architectures. We have confirmedFreedom-to-Operatein the EU, US, UK, and Japan. The company has an international footprint through its German headquarters (NSS Germany UG), a U.S. subsidiary (NSS USA Corp) with prior AFRL contract execution, and expansion in Italy through ESA BIC Milan and industrial partnerships.
Our business mode lis to provide Space Mobility as a Service (SMAAS), delivering integrated solutions for orbital servicing, debris removal, refueling, constellation maneuverability, and cislunar cargo logistics. These capabilities address critical needs inspace situational awareness, OSAM (On-Orbit Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing), resilient defence constellations, and heliophysics monitoring.
In summary, NSS is building the superconducting backbone of European space mobility. By combining propulsion, power, and autonomy in a single scalable architecture, we are positioning Europe as a leader in resilient space infrastructures with global commercial reach.

This allows more agile orbital manoeuvres, cost-effective logistics, and dual-use applications acrossLEO, GEO, cislunar and interplanetary domains.
In parallel, NSS is developing HTS-based power management and distribution solutions, including superconducting harnesses, delivering near-lossless power transfer and improved thermal stability. These are complemented by AI-driven autonomy and digital twin architectures that enable spacecraft to plan, adapt, and operate with greater resilience in congested and contested environments.
Key projects and validation:
- SUPREME (EIC Transition project):Critical Design Review completed, progressing to TRL 5–6 by 2026 with full prototype testing.

- STORM (EIC Pathfinder, €3.6M):A solar weather forecasting constellation providing early-warning data to enhance spacecraft autonomy and resilience.

- MEESST (EIC Pathfinder):Demonstrated superconducting-based re-entry technologies with >50% heat flux mitigation.

- BEEHIVE (EIC Accelerator, submission 2025):Development of a Digital Twin Mission Emulator and multimode propulsion architectures for scalable orbital logistics.

NSS has built a strongintellectual property portfolio, covering propulsion systems, thermal management, superconducting harnesses, and smart spacecraft architectures. We have confirmedFreedom-to-Operatein the EU, US, UK, and Japan. The company has an international footprint through its German headquarters (NSS Germany UG), a U.S. subsidiary (NSS USA Corp) with prior AFRL contract execution, and expansion in Italy through ESA BIC Milan and industrial partnerships.
Our business mode lis to provide Space Mobility as a Service (SMAAS), delivering integrated solutions for orbital servicing, debris removal, refueling, constellation maneuverability, and cislunar cargo logistics. These capabilities address critical needs inspace situational awareness, OSAM (On-Orbit Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing), resilient defence constellations, and heliophysics monitoring.
In summary, NSS is building the superconducting backbone of European space mobility. By combining propulsion, power, and autonomy in a single scalable architecture, we are positioning Europe as a leader in resilient space infrastructures with global commercial reach.

description:
SPACEMEDEX is an innovative biotechnology and health research company specializing in human spaceflight and the transfer of space technologies to terrestrial medicine. Headquartered in Sophia-Antipolis, our mission is to leverage extreme environments (microgravity, hypogravity, hypergravity, radiation) and space technologies (satellites, exoskeletons, biosensors) to develop new approaches in regenerative medicine, rehabilitation, neuroscience, and telemedicine.
Core Activities: Space and Translational Medicine: studying the effects of microgravity and space exposure on human physiology, with direct applications for terrestrial health. Rehabilitation and Assistive Technologies: development and distribution of exoskeletons and robotic platforms for motor and neurodegenerative disorders. Space Neurosciences: research on neuroplasticity and cognition in relation to spaceflight, with applications for neurodegenerative disease management. Telemedicine and Satellite Communication: medical monitoring solutions for remote and isolated environments. Crisis and Real-Time Health Data Management: integrated systems for health and environmental data collection, monitoring, and early warning. 
Partnerships and Projects: SPACEMEDEX collaborates with clinical centers, universities, and industrial partners across Europe, North Africa, and North America. We are engaged in collaborative R&D programs in physical medicine and rehabilitation, biomedical remote monitoring, and accelerated clinical trials. 
Vision: Our goal is to build a lasting bridge between space exploration and medical innovation, improving human health on Earth while supporting future lunar and Martian missions.

entityDescription:
AeroBeam is developing the world’s first drone-delivered, machine learning-guided laser cleaning and surface analysis system. Our system combines advanced imaging, precision laser ablation, and autonomous drones to identify and remove contaminants safely and efficiently. At AeroBeam, we are developing drone-mounted LIBS and laser ablation systems for terrestrial applications, such as the decontamination and inspection of wind turbines. We have proven the efficacy for LIBS-based machine learning and effective, precise ablation of wind turbine contamination. Classification between turbine and contamination was approximately 100% accurate and processed in less than half a second. Wind turbines can lose up to 40% of their power output due to contamination on blade surfaces, and AeroBeam aims to address this issue, allowing our customers to reach their full revenue generating potential .

By merging drones and laser technologies into a novel platform, we are creating systems that we believe could be adapted for future use in space missions. The integration of drone-based laser deployment for ablation and spectroscopy represents a promising direction for next-generation planetary exploration and in-situ resource analysis. Also, as the space launch market expands, rapid drone-based inspection analysis and maintenance for reusable rockets between launches is envisaged as a further application.

Our initial product is a ground-based machine vision contamination detection system to be sold in 2026, followed by the full drone system in 2027–2028. Revenue will come from product sales, pilot programs, and service contracts. We’ve received positive strong early feedback, including a pilot project expression of interest from ESB, Wind energy Ireland and a letter of interest from Irish space company MBRYONICS.

The founding team includes domain experts in LIBS, precision optics, AI, and drone engineering. AeroBeam offers a scalable, space-ready technology with immediate terrestrial and long-term non terrestrial application.

entityDescription:
THALENSIA Institute is a high-level training and consulting organization dedicated to cybersecurity, risk governance, and the protection of critical and strategic infrastructures. Positioned at the crossroads of innovation, regulation, and sovereignty, THALENSIA operates with a strong focus on the space, defense, maritime, industrial, and public sectors, helping organizations navigate the complex landscape of digital threats and compliance challenges.
We train and advise executives, CISOs, engineers, and operational teams across Europe to address the evolving requirements of cybersecurity, with a specific expertise in space security frameworks and regulations.

Our areas of expertise include:

- Cybersecurity & Risk Governance Training

Custom-tailored programs covering the full cybersecurity lifecycle: from governance and strategy to operational and technical mastery. 

THALENSIA delivers certified training programs in:
 - GRC, risk analysis, and ISO/IEC 27001/27005
 - Defense and space sector regulations (French, EU, NATO)
 - DevSecOps and secure architecture for critical systems, such as ISO 34000 or IEC62443 and SCADA.

We are an accredited training partner of PECB (ISO/IEC standards) and CompTIA, ensuring globally recognized certifications and high pedagogical standards.

- ECSS Training & Space Sector Compliance

As a specialized institute in the space domain, THALENSIA provides training and advisory services aligned with the European Cooperation for Space Standardization (ECSS) framework. 
We prepare organizations and contractors for compliance with ECSS-Q-ST-80, ECSS security norms, and other technical standards essential to European space missions.

- European Space Cybersecurity Frameworks

We help stakeholders integrate emerging space cybersecurity frameworks such as SPARTA, SpaceShield, and other EU initiatives, enabling secure-by-design approaches to spacecraft, ground segment, and data communication security.
Our experts also support the interpretation and operationalization of the EU Space Law, NIS2, Cyber Resilience Act, and other relevant acts shaping the regulatory ecosystem of the European space industry.

- CISO Coaching & Strategic Security Support

THALENSIA accompanies New/Old space industries and startups, CISOs and Product security officers in strategic positioning, roadmap definition, and implementation of best practices. We offer coaching programs tailored for security transition phases and regulatory readiness.

- Cyber & Space Intelligence

We maintain a continuous intelligence capability to monitor technological advances, threat evolutions, and normative shifts in the cyber and space domains. This supports our clients in proactive decision-making and long-term resilience building.

Our Commitment:
"At THALENSIA Institute, we believe that security is the foundation of European technological sovereignty. By bridging regulatory requirements and operational excellence, we prepare our clients to thrive in an increasingly contested and interconnected space and cyber environment."

Alexandre OTTER
CEO at THALENSIA

entityName: UNIVERSITY OF ROME TOR VERGATA - CEIS
entityDescription:
The Centre for International Studies on Economic Growth (CEIS – Tor Vergata) is an interdepartmental centreestablished in 1987 in the Faculty of Economics at the University of Rome “Tor Vergata”, which is a public university. 
Its aim is to promote advanced training and high-quality research in economics. CEIS organises seminars and conferences, organizes research in all fields of economics and establishes joint programmes with other universities, national institutions and international organizations.

The centre’s main activities are:
- policy oriented economic research 

- consulting services and technical assistance to private and public institutions
- publishing activities
- conferences and seminars

The centre is engaged in creating international research and higher learning networking in the major fields of economics. Its research agenda continuously changes to reflect new economic phenomena and new projects in partnership with other research centres of excellence and individual scholars. The centre is also involved in international research programs in the framework of bilateral and multilateral cooperation activities.

The research activities focus on the challenges of European economic integration, globalization processes and economic growth. The centre engages in empirical and theoretical analysis of economic policy issues giving special emphasis to international interdependencies between business cycles of regional areas and to the importance of rules and institutions in economic growth. The centre gives top priority to the development of methodologies and tools for the quantitative analysis of economic phenomena and policies.

entityDescription:
TANIT HORIZON - WHERE HEART MEETS SPACE
TANIT HORIZON is an innovative startup committed to develop advanced technological solutions for agriculture in extreme environments, both terrestrial and extraterrestrial.The company focuses on the research, development, production, and marketing of automated cultivation systems—hydroponic and aeroponic—integrated with technical substrates and technologies adaptable to critical or non-terrestrial climates, including the lunar, Martian, and other space environments.
Our vision stems from a dual challenge: enabling life in Space and improving the quality of life on Earth.Our systems are designed to support life on long-duration space missions, making a tangible contribution to astronauts' food self-sufficiency. At the same time, we bring these innovations to Earth, offering sustainable solutions for agricultural production in dense urban areas, desert regions, or climate-stressed areas.
Technology and sustainability merge in an intelligent system that integrates Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and LED lighting to monitor and adjust optimal growth conditions in real time, improving plant physiological development and optimizing water, nutrient, and energy consumption.
TANIT HORIZON represents a unique convergence of space research, agricultural innovation and environmental sustainability, with significant scientific, social, and humanitarian implications. We are helping to shape a future where food can be grown anywhere—from the International Space Station to our planet's urban centers—efficiently, resiliently, and resource-efficiently.

Snow Secure Oy is a Finnish company specialized in sustainable snow storage solutions for winter sports, events, and communities. We combine engineering, environmental responsibility, and digitalization to ensure reliable snow availability with minimal ecological footprint.

Why we apply
We are applying to ESA to develop validated digital models that integrates data via satellites, meteorological datasets, and IoT sensor observations. Our aim is to transform snow storage from a manual practice into a predictable, data-driven system that supports climate adaptation and operational planning. Focus 1: 24/7 data via satellite. Focus 2: Helping also glaciers and other extreme areas to store snow in sustainable way along all mass ski events in lower altitude Focus 3: Using our remote 24/7 montioring to benefit measuring snow conditions in mass ski events.

What ESA gains
ESA benefits from a new and concrete application area for Earth observation and satellite connectivity: snow storage as a climate resilience tool. entityDescription:
CAELUS is an Italian deep tech startup established in October 2023 by current CEO Alessio Iuvara that has set itself the goal of reducing the costs and time of designing, licensing, building and decommissioning nuclear reactors through its unified AI-based software suite. Specifically, the designed product is an enterprise software suite that employs a series of innovative advanced technologies such as AI/ML, NLP, GenAI, HPC/QC, Digital Twins, BIM/GIS, Robotics and other Industry 4.0/5.0 technologies.

Such a mix would allow the nuclear sector to be competitive with other sources of energy generation, and to make realistic the goal of tripling nuclear power, in global terms, necessary to achieve the Net Zero 2050 targets.

The uniqueness of the software is given by the combination of its holistic approach and its ability to follow the entire life cycle of the reactor thanks to architectural specificities, currently in the process of patenting, which can guarantee the complete VV&Q (verification, validation and quality certification) of AI systems, strictly necessary in the nuclear sector as well as for the defense sector. This makes the application usable in high-risk situations, ensuring complete abstraction and generalizability to any engineering of complex systems in highly regulated sectors such as aerospace, maritime and defense.

The product has an intrinsically innovative feature as it creates a new state of the art in the field of dismissal, design and management of nuclear reactors: these processes are currently managed completely by hand, especially for the regulatory field, thus involving a non-negligible amount of errors and delays often discriminating against the success or failure of an entire nuclear project.

CAELUS operates by means of Product Innovation (CAELUS Ecosystem), Process Innovation (Purpose-Specific AI/HW/Software Development and Qualification) and Technical Strategic Consultancy (Ancillary Services) plus operating Commercial Activities such as the Partners Program and the Qualification Program (making possible for companies in business like Aerospace and Defense to go towards the Nuclear market and vice versa by means of qualification, SW and services). Other Programs (Nuke4Africa, Nuke4Hydrogen, Nuke4Space, Coal2Nuclear, Nuke4Datacenters...) are on their way to be launched during the next year.

In this context,Space Technologies such as Satellites, Geospatial Data and Sensors are crucial to ensure efficiency, traceability and safety of the new nuclear sector, reason why we are interested in being inside ESA STAR and apply to multiple collaboration opportunities as they come available through the portal.

entityDescription:
AIRWORKS doo is a newly founded business in Slovenia, to provide physical and digital technologies for applications where performance and safety are mission critical. The company, established in 2025 and 80% owned by AIRWORKS srl and its shareholders (all Italian based), aims to complement the mother company's existing portfolio by adding new solutions in the areas of both space products and digitization.
 
Mechanisms are the primary space industry segment. 
Here AIRWORKS doo intends to provide technologies that address a) unmet needs in the existing market, 2) missing products required by future missions, 3) replacement of non-European components for an EU self-reliant space sector.
 
Business development in the space segment is implemented along two parallel paths: direct collaborations (OHB Group, ArianeGroup, ISAR Aerospace, etc) and open competition within ESA programmes. Having not a background with ESA as space entity yet, it is worth explaining how AIRWORKS doo operates in regard to ESA regulations for geographical return. 
 
AIRWORKS doo is a design and research center in Nova Gorica (Slovenia) that executes its contracts in Slovenia independently from the nationality of its shareholders, particularly from point of view of man labour and project knowledge. The developments are entirely performed by its experienced CTO Mr. Matija Brumat, a team of four competent Slovenian engineers and a few carefully selected local suppliers. Mr. Brumat has considerable heritage in the mechanism segment, being lead mechanism engineer on several Coarse Pointing Mechanism programmes, in respect to design, engineering and MAIT. AIRWORKS doo team is also strengthened by Mr. Paul McMahon, retired senior specialist mechanism engineer and deputy head of the mechanisms group at Airbus Defence & Space UK. Mr. McMahon acts as an engineering mentor providing part-time, “on demand” consulting to the team and will not perform direct work on ESA or commercial projects due to the nature of its contract (zero hours, no obligations of minimum hours from sides)
 
Within the next 1-2 years AIRWORKS doo plans are to expand the staff to 12-15 FTE and implement a facility suitable for space equipment AIT activities.
 
The Italian shareholders play an active role in AIRWORKS doo exclusively in the corporate governance (goal setting, risk management, etc) and as business development accelerators (i.e. connecting AIRWORKS doo with Large Space Integrators to discuss opportunities).

entityDescription:
GRID+ S.r.l. is an innovative startup founded within Sapienza University of Rome, combining scientific expertise and engineering capabilities to deliver advanced Artificial Intelligence solutions for enterprises and public administrations. The company operates across four main areas that reflect its integrated model.
Its consulting activities are based on a highly scientific and structured methodology that moves from preliminary analysis to prototyping and finally to the full integration of AI solutions within client systems. This approach ensures continuous support and covers a wide range of domains such as computer vision, time series forecasting, explainability of complex models, anomaly detection and large language models.
The company also develops proprietary products, with the AIaaS cloud platform at the core. This platform enables immediate access to services such as forecasting, anomaly detection, sentiment analysis and real-time recommendations, eliminating the need for hardware or dedicated staff. Alongside the platform, GRID+ has created advanced software for business process automation, multichannel communication management, content generation, decision support and customer interaction, with applications in sectors such as tourism, healthcare, marketing and entertainment.
Training represents another key asset, with programs designed for both managers and technical staff. Courses range from AI fundamentals to advanced topics such as Generative AI and the use of tools like Microsoft Copilot, and are always tailored to the vertical market of each client. Thanks to its strong link with academia, GRID+ ensures that its training activities are aligned with the latest scientific developments while remaining accessible to non-specialists.
Finally, research is central to GRID+’s identity. The company participates in Horizon Europe, ESA programmes and national R&D initiatives, while also collaborating with public and private organizations. A strategic scientific partnership with the Department of Information, Electronics and Telecommunications Engineering (DIET) at Sapienza University of Rome supports joint work on machine learning, deep learning, quantum computing and hyperdimensional computing, with applications in energy, healthcare, aerospace and urban systems.

entityDescription:
InCirT, founded in 2022 as a spin-off from RWTH Aachen University, has developed a novel data converter technology that achieves up to 100 times wider modulation bandwidths (today 8 GHz instantaneous bandwidth with a single converter) and up to 10 times higher energy efficiency compared to current solutions. The technology enables coverage of wide frequency ranges — for example, from L-band to X-band — and serves as a key enabler for simultaneous multi-band functionality. This allows for a significantly simplified system architecture, substantially reducing chipset size and manufacturing costs.
Usually, the bottleneck in these systems lies in their core component — the data converter (ADC/DAC). Existing solutions are too slow, consume excessive power, and are too costly. At the same time, physical and technological limitations, particularly the end of Moore’s Law, mean that conventional approaches can hardly achieve significant further progress.

entityDescription: The Tplus Engineering GmbH is a provider of engineering services for project work as well as for R&D activities. The company was founded in 2014 as spin-off from the Institute of Aerospace Thermodynamics at the University of Stuttgart, Germany. Since then, the company has specialized in the numerical simulation of aero-thermal problems and related activties. Our core competences are in combined fluid dynamics and heat transfer problems, which are characterized by a strong interaction of the flow field with the temperature field. For the work, a wide spectrum of simulation approaches from 1D modeling to 3D CFD is used. The modeling includes implementation and model development work for 1D tools or CFD codes. Simulation activities cover the topics fluid mechanics (both incompressible and compressible), heat transfer and multiphase flows. In our tools, we rely on state-of-the-art simulation and modeling software with an independent selection of the appropriate tool from both commercial and open-source solutions. Apart from project-based work, the company develops solutions for optimization and automation, from optimization workflows using genetic algorithms to fully automated CFD processes with the capability to run 24/7 without user input. Our services are tailored but not limited to the industries from aviation and aerospace, power generation, automotive and turbomachinery.

Simulation activities cover the topics fluid mechanics (both incompressible and compressible), heat transfer and multiphase flows. In our tools, we rely on state-of-the-art simulation and modeling software with an independent selection of the appropriate tool from both commercial and open-source solutions. Apart from project-based work, the company develops solutions for optimization and automation, from optimization workflows using genetic algorithms to fully automated CFD processes with the capability to run 24/7 without user input. Our services are tailored but not limited to the industries from aviation and aerospace, power generation, automotive and turbomachinery.

entityDescription:
University Medicine Greifswald
The origins of University Medicine Greifswald date back to the foundation of the University of Greifswald on October 1456, which also marked the establishment of the Faculty of Medicine. Today, University Medicine Greifswald combines a wide range of services, bringing together 21 clinics and outpatient departments, 19 institutes, and several central facilities.
Research Profile
The research profile of University Medicine Greifswald is defined by the complementary integration of Community Medicine and Molecular Medicine, resulting in the Greifswald Approach to Individualized Medicine. This approach enables the Faculty not only to achieve relevant results in basic, epidemiological, clinical, and health services research, but also to translate these findings directly into healthcare delivery.
Since 2021, this profile has been complemented by a third focus area: Digital Health. The digitization of healthcare data, digital technologies such as clinical decision support systems, and the application of artificial intelligence (AI) are expected to fundamentally shape and transform healthcare and the health economy. Building on these strengths, future research will further emphasize prevention. The goal is to establish an integrated and holistic approach to disease prevention that connects disciplines through overarching research questions and aligns them towards common objectives.
Academic Programs
University Medicine Greifswald offers a diverse portfolio of degree programs, including Biomedical Science, Human Medicine, Dentistry, and Clinical Nursing Science.

LINDSCHULTE, one of the largest planning firms in northwest Germany, has been established in Nordhorn for 50 years and employs approximately ~ 700 qualified employees at its headquarters and its branches nationwide.

From design and permitting, structural and execution planning to the preparation of specifications and project monitoring, they are at home in the main specialist areas of building and industrial construction, as well as transport, infrastructure, and environmental planning.

Our company focuses on the planning of process engineering and process plants, including the associated 3D design of the process plant and all piping systems, in various industries, such as the oil and gas industry,

description:
The Institute of Space Science (ISS) from Magurele, Romania is carrying out fundamental and advanced technological research in Space Physics and related fields based on previously acquired experience, and international collaborations. The opportunity of participating in in situ space research missions, as well as in major ground based experiments has a major impact on the competence level of staff. The Institute’s R&D activity is based on the concept of covering, whenever possible, all experimental and theoretical stages: from equipment development, experiments in cosmic space, ground based, underground or undersea related projects, data processing and interpretation, theoretical studies, to space utilization and knowledge dissemination to the general public including educational actions.

The mission of the Institute of Space Science is twofolded: to contribute to Romanian’s participation in the worldwide effort of investigation and peaceful uses of the cosmic space, including applications for increasing the quality of life on Earth; to contribute to the preservation and the development of Romania’s space capabilities and expertise to conduct frontier research in fundamental science. In more detail, we consider it our mission to: -
- lead and conduct research programs and carry out theoretical and experimental studies to push forward the human knowledge on the circumterrestrial, solar, galactic and extragalactic environments; 
- develop instrumentation for space and terrestrial experiments; 
- develop applications and transfer the - knowledge and technology for the benefit of the society; encourage the pursuit of appropriate partnerships with the industry; 
- train and develop human resources by involving students in the research process; commit ourselves to education and public outreach, and free dissemination of knowledge. 
The main domains of activity of ISS are: space related sciences and technology, applications of space communication techniques, hardware for on-board, ground segment and ground based experiments, appropriate computing technologies. 
The main directions for the Research & Development activity are: 
1. Theoretical Physics and Mathematical Physics 
2. High Energy Physics and Astrophysics 
3. Astroparticle Physics and Cosmology 
4. Space Technology and Hardware for Space Experiments (on-board and ground segment) and Satellite Data Processing 
5. Experiments, Data Analysis, and Theoretical Developments on Space Plasma 
6. Microgravity, Space Dynamics and Microsatellits 
7. Distributed and Parallel Computing in Space and Terrestrial Researches and Applications. 
8. Applications of Space and Communication Technologies

Neue Materialien Bayreuth GmbH (NMB) is a non-university research institution combining application-oriented development with scientific depth and technical excellence. We provide cross-material solutions using polymers, metals, functional materials, and their combinations—always tailored to specific requirements.
Our work focuses on sustainability, digitalization, and energy. We develop material solutions for closed-loop systems, conduct life cycle assessments, and apply digital technologies such as IoT, machine learning, and digital twins to make processes smarter and more efficient.
With infrastructure ranging from lab to near-industrial scale and comprehensive digital networking, we enable data-driven research and scalable processes. Our expertise includes particle foams, injection molding (including foam technologies), fiber-reinforced plastics, polymer-metal hybrids, thermal spraying, forming technology, metal powder development, and additive manufacturing with polymers and metals.
We collaborate closely with industry and research partners, including the University of Bayreuth, to transfer innovations from basic research into industrial practice.

entityDescription:
OLLOW is an innovative SME founded in 2018, specializing in the design and manufacture of tubular structures made from thermoplastic composites. The company has developed a patented automated manufacturing technology that enables the production of complex hollow parts with high mechanical performance and an excellent cost/volume ratio. OLLOW currently employs 25 people. Its business model is based on the sale of R&D/prototyping services and the sale of composite parts.
The company currently operates from its workshop near Bordeaux and by the end of 2025 it will move into its future 3,000 m² factory, currently under construction nearby. With an annual production capacity of over 100,000 parts, expandable to 1 million parts depending on the format, the site will be equipped with 10 MW. These capacities cover the entire value chain: design, research, development, prototyping, and mass production. The solutions offered by Ollow include the manufacture of complex structures using advanced processes such as textile preforming, rapid induction molding, injection, and overmolding. These technologies enable the production of robust, lightweight, customizable parts at low unit cost, while ensuring great design freedom. Its thermoplastic composite parts are as high-performance as they are resistant, while being easily recyclable, which significantly reduces their environmental footprint (by 35 to 65% compared to solutions currently produced in Southeast Asia).

entityDescription:
Massive Beams was founded in the heart of Berlin with the vision to become the leading platform for Open RAN Radio Unit (O-RU) development. With the emergence of 5G and 6G on the horizon, the importance of Open RAN - an open specification for how base station components communicate - is growing. This innovation will create an open and transparent marketplace, allowing vendors around the world to bring their cutting-edge solutions to mobile communications.
 
However, the road ahead is not without challenges. Many of the O-RU solutions available today are opaque, difficult to configure and time-consuming to integrate. Port Infrastructure Asset Integrity Web Platform

 Adapting ports to rising sea levels: an economic necessity for the future
As sea levels rise, port infrastructure - whether commercial, fishing or leisure - becomes increasingly vulnerable. Subjected to extreme weather phenomena, these ports, which are essential to the global economy, risk suffering considerable damage if proactive measures are not implemented. As an article in the French newspaper Le Monde points out, ‘the priority now is adaptation rather than inaction’, because the costs of inaction will far outweigh those of adaptation.

Adapt or incur the significant costs of inaction ⚠️
Ports that fail to adapt risk becoming increasingly vulnerable, while those that respond proactively to these challenges will enjoy a considerable competitive advantage. By modernising their port management and integrating cutting-edge technologies such as digital twins and artificial intelligence, they will ensure their competitiveness in the face of escalating climate challenges. Ports that embrace adaptation today will become the leaders of tomorrow.

ABIM: Robust solutions for the cities and ports of the future 
ABIM helps port managers anticipate climate-related challenges. By integrating spatial data (InSAR), digital twins and artificial intelligence technologies, we provide proactive management, predictive maintenance and risk assessment. This enables ports to improve their sustainability and efficiency.

 Anticipate consequences to mitigate expenses
The cost of adaptation is much lower than the cost of inaction. An EDFund report entitled ‘Early or Pay Later’ indicates that the costs of adaptation can be up to 90% lower than the costs of repairing infrastructure following extreme weather events. This approach could result in annual savings of $100 billion for the world's port infrastructures.

Resilient cities and ports are not just an option, they are an essential condition for the future !

Valeo is a leading global automotive supplier and technology company that focuses on designing and manufacturing innovative solutions for the automotive industry. The company was founded in 1923 and has since grown to become a major player in the automotive market.
Valeo specializes in four main business groups: Powertrain Systems, Thermal Systems, Comfort and Driving Assistance Systems, and Visibility Systems. These groups cover a wide range of products and technologies, including electrical systems, engine components, transmission systems, climate control systems, lighting systems, and advanced driver assistance systems.

As of 2022, the Valeo Group generated sales of 20.037 Bn Euros and invested over 10% of its original equipment sales in research and development. Valeo has 183 plants, 65 research and development centers and 15 distribution platforms, and employs 109 900 people in 29 countries worldwide.

The Business Group Valeo Comfort & Driving Assistance is leading the development of research projects and innovative solutions in the fields of Advanced Driving Assistance Systems, Automated Driving, User Experience, Telematics and Digital services.

entityDescription:
AMAREA Technology offers industrial 3D printers and high-performance materials based on Multi Material Jetting (MMJ) technology. We go beyond the limits that the creative freedom of additive manufacturing with a single material offers manufacturers.
MMJ enables printing with different materials, even with contrasting properties, both within the same layer and throughout the build volume. Materials within the same material class, such as metals, ceramics and plastics, or even different material classes, can be integrated into a single build job.
Features and specifications of the technology:
3D printers based on Multi Material Jetting (MMJ) represent an additive manufacturing process in which material is deposited drop by drop and layer by layer.
Each of the MMJ-capable materials is composed of the desired material as a powder embedded in a thermoplastic binder.
A print head contains one material and releases tiny droplets (containing the actual material powder) as required (nl size). The droplets solidify by cooling in a fraction of a second and become solid structures when they reach the build platform or another layer of MMJ-capable material. The neighboring droplets fuse together. Depending on the configuration, several print heads apply different materials drop by drop with high precision throughout the entire build volume.
During the subsequent thermal treatment, known as debinding and sintering, the binder is removed and the remaining material powder particles fuse together to form a solid component and produce the component with the desired properties.

With over 15 years of experience in software development and cloud technologies, I have built my career across Europe since 2012, working at companies such as Drei in Vienna while advancing my academic path.
I hold a Master’s degree in Software Engineering and Internet Computing from TU Wien, where my thesis focused on Serverless Edge Computing. My research developed a data-locality–aware Kubernetes scheduler that optimizes Machine Learning and data-intensive workflows by prioritizing tasks based on data location—maximizing edge resource usage and minimizing network traffic.
At Starbase, we are building a distributed AI platform where Earth Observation (EO) satellites send raw data directly to nearby LEO satellites for in-orbit processing. By combining EO data with in-situ sensor data from edge devices such as drones, our system enables real-time AI analysis in space—delivering disaster response insights, like wildfire detection, in minutes instead of hours.
Today, I combine industry expertise, academic innovation, and entrepreneurial vision to help organizations design, optimize, and scale their cloud-native, serverless, and edge-to-space solutions.

entityDescription: KEFAG Kiskunsági Forestry and Wood Industry Plc., under the management of the Ministry of Agriculture, which exercises ownership rights, manages more than 57 thousand hectares of the state forest areas of Bács-Kiskun County. Our primary field of activity is forestry, which includes seed and sapling production, silviculture and wood utilization, along with the related services, of course. Commercial activity occupies a prominent place in our management, which includes the production and sale of timber, forest seeds and saplings, and ornamental plants. A similarly important sector is hunting, where we practice our hunting activities on more than 41 thousand hectares. We carry out extensive woodworking activities, during which we process approximately 100 thousand m3 of our own and purchased sawn raw materials, primarily producing pallets. In addition to our traditional activities, we also perform numerous public welfare and public utility tasks. Among other things, we maintain and operate the uniquely beautiful Kecskemét Arboretum, the Vackor Vár Forestry School, which implements this activity at a very high level, and the Great Plains Forestry Museum, which presents the history of sand afforestation. We maintain numerous accommodations and key houses, but we also continuously maintain our park forests and educational trails serving the dissemination of knowledge and environmental education. As you can see, our main task is to manage the state-owned land in our area of operation professionally, in accordance with the requirements of sustainable forest management, as well as the regulations of the specialized authorities and the laws. We place great emphasis on fully satisfying the social demands placed on the forest. Therefore, in our everyday activities, we ensure the harmony of the diverse functions of the forest so that it can fully fulfill its economic, social and protective purpose. By implementing our long-planned ideas, we serve development, encourage the creation of a more livable environment, the increase in green spaces, and programs aimed at creating sustainable residential buildings.
