entityDescription: The team of Magnetic Future is developing a new generation of contactless, high-efficiency power supplies for superconducting (SC) magnets, unlocking their potential across critical industrial sectors including fusion energy, medical imaging, and space propulsion. Today, SC magnets are hindered by traditional power supplies based on metallic current leads, which cause massive thermal losses and require energy-intensive cryocoolers. This limitation severely affects their operational efficiency, with energy waste reaching over 10,000 EUR per Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) system per year and hundreds of kilowatts in future fusion plants. In the aerospace sector, this challenge currently blocks the adoption of superconducting technologies for high-performance electric propulsion systems such as Applied-Field Magnetoplasmadynamic (AF-MPD) thrusters. Magnetic Future addresses this problem through the development of patented Flux Pumps, superconducting power supplies that transfer energy without any direct electrical contact. This approach reduces current load thermal load by a factor of 2–3 and significantly shrinks the size and complexity of cryogenic systems, enabling deep-space superconducting applications previously considered unfeasible (typical weight budgets are in the order of tens of kilos, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2772830724000504?via%3Dihub). Our innovation builds on cutting-edge research conducted by the founding team and validated in collaboration with leading fusion and aerospace actors. Our business model combines custom system sales, IP licensing, and long-term service contracts. In the short term, we aim to complete prototype development, reach TRL 6, and close a second commercial contract. In the long term, we plan to expand into the aerospace sector (including aviation in the long term, as AIRBUS superconducting-based electrification projects demonstrate substantial opportunities in the future: https://www.airbus.com/en/newsroom/stories/2021-03-cryogenics-and-superconductivity-for-aircraft-explained) internalize manufacturing steps, and scale globally across SC magnets -enabled applications. With a strong IP strategy, clear market access, and an experienced team of electrical, mechanical, and cryogenic engineers, supported by academic leaders and industrial advisors, Magnetic Future is strategically positioned to become a key player in the superconducting revolution for space and beyond.

entityDescription:
Tuatara Ventures is a technology SME specialising in Earth observation analytics powered by artificial intelligence. The company develops advanced methods for processing satellite, aerial, and drone imagery, with a focus on innovative applications in agriculture, land monitoring, and automated object detection. Founded in 2018, it currently employs eight people and brings together a diverse team of leading EO scientists, data and IT specialists, and experts in production-grade system architecture and software development. 

It leads AgroSatCom, funded under INFOSTRATEG by Poland’s National Centre for Research and Development (NCBR), where it delivers AI models for crop classification, growth and condition assessment, and disease detection, alongside broader work on land condition and value assessment, including soil degradation monitoring. The team has proven experience in Earth observation and AI applications, including the successful completion of ESA Discovery EISI EOImageNET, which delivered a global dataset and a deep neural network for object detection on optical EO imagery. Team members have also contributed to ESA SEOM Global Land Cover – Sentinel-2, ESA Phi-Lab crop mapping with UNICEF, WFP, and Stanford, the EC Advanced Forest Fire Fighting 3 programme, and the SatAgro platform.

entityDescription:
Geosense is a reputable independent geological remote sensing consultancy that has gained global recognition for its top-quality remote sensing services. Over the last 35 years we have built up a unique experience in the use of satellite, airborne and ground based remote sensing technology and interpretations for mineral exploration.
Alteration mapping and target generation using spectral information from satellites (e.g., Landsat, ASTER, WorldView-3, Sentinel-2, EnMAP), aircraft (hyperspectral imaging) and portable infrared spectroscopy (field mapping and core logging) provides a very powerful exploration tool. Geosense covers different phases of exploration, from regional scale generative projects, for the identification of alteration systems and the detection of basement structures, to the project scale, for accurate mineralogical mapping and the structural geological setting of individual targets.
While spectral mapping techniques can be highly effective for detection of exposed alteration, there are many situations where this is not the case. There are many situations where an orebody is located at such depth that its alteration halo does not reach the surface, hence is not directly detectable with spectral methods.
Also, there are major parts of the world where the superficial signs of alteration are (partly) covered by an unrelated blanket (dense vegetation, snow, rock debris, alluvium, glacial till, wind-blown material, desert staining, laterites, etc.). In these cases, it can be important to look at indirect indicators, such as structure, stratigraphy, lithological changes geomorphology, land-use and vegetation patterns. Remotely sensed images, and their derivatives, such as Digital Elevation Models (DEMs), are very suitable tools to map these features with high accuracy and in great detail. Again, this can be done at a regional scale, using relatively low-resolution imagery, and at prospect scale, using very high-resolution data, such as <1m resolution satellite imagery, or even Drone imagery, with spatial resolution up to one or two centimeters. Many Geosense projects cover the whole range, from regional to prospect scale, to help understand the geological context of the targets across these scales.
Geosense has an all-round team of experts under one roof, and is able to cover the complete range of remote sensing services required for optimal support of a mineral exploration project.

entityDescription: Romanian Academy Research Institute for Artificial Intelligence “Mihai Drăgănescu” (ICIA) was set up in 1994 as a centre of competence and active dissemination of knowledge in the domain of Artificial Intelligence. ICIA has a core of permanent research positions and a small number of consultant researchers. Besides them, a variable number of contract-based positions, especially students, participate in the R&D activities of ICIA. Every year, since its foundation, ICIA was evaluated as an excellency institution by the Romanian Academy. In 2001 ICIA won the competition for Centres of Excellency (in Information Science and Technology) organized by the Ministry of Education and Science. In 2002 it was rated the best research institute of the Romanian Academy (from 60 institutes and centres). In 2002 ICIA was granted the right to organize doctoral studies in the Romanian Academy system. In 2008 ICIA was accredited as a research institution and as a research and development, member of the research and development system of national interest, in conformity with HG no. 551/2007. The main research projects of ICIA are in the areas of natural language processing, machine learning and knowledge acquisition, computer-aided instruction and integrated modelling of information and geospatial technology. ICIA has been a member ofEuropean Network of Excellence in Human Language Technologiesfor more than 10 years. The activities of ICIA also include know-how dissemination, education in artificial intelligence, and the organisation of national and international conferences (see the ConsILR series 200-2015), summer schools (the EuroLAN series 1993-2015), and seminars. ICIA took part in over 40 international and national projects, and in the international technical and scientific competitions to which they participated with their own systems they ranked among the winners and the leading characters of most of them (WA-NACL 2003: Edmonton-Canada; WA-ACL 2005: Ann Arbor-USA; QA-CLEF 2006: Alicante-Spain WSD-ACL/SEMEVAL2007: Prague-Czech Republic, QA-CLEF 2007: Budapest-Hungary, ResPubliQA-CLEF 2009: Corfu-Greece, etc.). ICIA has cooperation relations with universities, research institutes and industrial partners from more than 30 countries from Europe and the United States.

entityDescription:
The Intermunicipal Community of Coimbra Region (CIM-RC) is a legal public association composed of 19 municipalities, representing approximately 450,000 inhabitants and covering an area of 4,800 km². CIM-RC has substantial experience in the management of co-funded projects, having acted as an Intermediate Body for the Regional Operational Programmes of the Centro Region during the 2007–2013 (�90M), 2014–2020 (�60M), and currently 2021–2027 (�152M) programming periods.
CIM-RC is the designated Mobility and Transport Authority for 18 municipalities and coordinates the Urban Agenda for the EU (UAEU) Thematic Partnership on Water-Sensitive Cities. It is also an active member of the Sustainable Tourism and Culture and Cultural Heritage partnerships. The organisation is guided by an Integrated Territorial Development Strategy, underpinning its actions and investments in a coordinated, place-based approach.
CIM-RC has developed and approved both its Sustainable Urban Mobility Plan (SUMP) and its Intermunicipal Climate Change Adaptation Plan. It is a signatory of the EU Missions Adaptation to Climate Change and Restore our Ocean and Waters, and participates in other European networks and initiatives, including METREX, ERRIN, Industry 5.0, C4T, and NetZero Cities.
A key strategic asset of CIM-RC is the CGEO – Intermunicipal Centre for Geographic Information, which provides technical and scientific support in the domains of geographic information, spatial analysis, and georeferenced data management. CGEO supports informed decision-making for public policy and intermunicipal planning, contributing directly to areas such as land use, environmental management, mobility, risk prevention, and climate adaptation.
Currently, CIM-RC is involved in over 60 projects, including 19 European-funded initiatives under various EU programmes, actively promoting territorial cohesion, innovation, and sustainability across the region.

Entity Description – Dronex360 UG
Dronex360 UG is an early-stage technology startup developing intelligent drone systems for sustainable, autonomous operations. Based in Offenburg, Germany, the company focuses on enabling scalable and eco-conscious drone missions through a combination of custom hardware, AI-powered flight planning, and energy-efficient charging infrastructure.

Our solution integrates 3D-printed aerodynamic rotor components, a modular charging dock, and mission orchestration software connected via cloud APIs. This platform is ideal for use cases in environmental monitoring, infrastructure inspection, and precision agriculture.

Dronex360 is currently incubated at ESA BIC Baden-Württemberg, where the focus lies on system integration, simulation-based validation (via Hardware-in-the-Loop testing), and preparation for pilot deployments in late 2025.

entityDescription:
METCENAS o.p.s. is as an independent not-for-profit research and training centre established in 2011 in Prague, Czech Republic, aiming to set up technical and research cooperation amongst countries of Central and Eastern Europe and Third countries (with main focus on Danube River Basin, South Asia and Latin America). Thematically, activities of METCENAS are focused on climate change and climate services, ecosystem services, integrated water resources management, Nature based Solutions implementation, bioeconomy, resource efficiency, awareness creation, socio-economy, research focused on the community and the citizens and cooperation with the end users via different platforms (as FREEWAT platform, SPIDER, Danube Knowledge Platform,…). Started by researchers and practitioners and driven by the explicit requirements of the institutional network, METCENAS provides a broad spectrum of practical and advisory services. 
Key services provided:
- Provision of independent research outputs and available expertise, training and support services, knowledge transfer and Centre’s own capacity.
- Systematic training and education, especially for civil society and tertiary education.
- Analysis of user communities by setting-up and maintaining a multi-actor participatory processes and multi-actor community platform.
- Development of national comparative documents, e.g. for cross-border comparisons.
- Harmonization of methodologies used for environment assessments, policy measures, instruments and monitoring, environmental information analyses and dissemination.

entityDescription:
The Institute for the Protection of Maritime Infrastructures was founded in 2017 as one of seven new DLR institutes, and is provisionally managed by Frank Sill Torres.
The Institute’s scientific and technical activities focus on the resilience of maritime infrastructures. The objective of all of its concepts, analyses, developments and tests is to enable maritime infrastructures as complex systems – with support from various players, users and stakeholders – to recognise and prevent threats, adapt to them and counter their effects in a timely and efficient manner. DLR, through its Institute for the Protection of Maritime Infrastructures, is thus purposefully expanding its numerous competencies in the fields of technology development and maritime safety and security.
The current research activities are focused on threemissions. Firstly, they provide solutions to efficiently and effectively address global challenges such as security, mobility, the Energy Transition or changing values. Secondly, they provide security-related authorities and organisations with independent advice. In order to solve specific tasks, we further develop theoretical foundations, carry out simulations, build demonstrators and test them in a real environment together with their future users. All three missions should lead to a direct benefit for society as well as the economy.
At the Institute, particular attention is paid to the transfer of research results into real working situations, as well as their social and economic exploitation. To that end, the Institute is keen to participate, as early as possible, in the development of standards at national and at international level, to collaborate with companies and – in future – to support spin-offs established by employees of the Institute.

entityDescription:
Cristal Laser has been Europe's premier manufacturer of nonlinear crystals since 1990, while Layertec is a global leader in optical coatings. Nonlinear crystals from Cristal Laser have been successfully used in various space missions, including AEOLUS, Curiosity, and Perseverance, where LBO crystals play a critical role in generating visible (SHG) and UV (THG) light.

Cristal laser’s main products manufactured and marketed are
- LBO crystals for medium to high power visible and UV lasers. 
- KTP crystals for low power lasers.
- RTP crystals for electro-optic cells.
- KTA crystals for infrared OPO conversion.
.
Thanks to 33 years of experience and a strategy of continuous research and development, Cristal Laser stands out for the performance of its crystals, which is unparalleled and unique in the world. 

This expertise is reflected in four major achievements:
- Elimination of ageing effects in KTP crystals: Cristal Laser has developed innovative solutions to overcome the challenges associated with the ageing of KTP crystals. 

- Solving the problem of blackening of RTP crystals under DC voltage: The company has succeeded in significantly solving the problem of blackening of RTP crystals exposed to DC voltage, a technological breakthrough recognised for its global relevance.

- First to offer LBO crystals with a 90mm aperture: Cristal Laser made its mark on the industry by being the first to offer LBO crystals with a 90mm aperture, opening up new fields of application.

- World records achieved with LBO @532 nm @355 nm @257 nm: The company has set world records by exploiting the exceptional properties and sizes of its LBO crystals to generate specific wavelengths, consolidating its position as a world leader in laser frequency conversion.

As a result of this excellence, Cristal Laser has been recognised as a strategic company by the French Defence Procurement Agency (DGA). This classification reflects the confidence of the French authorities in Cristal Laser's expertise and strategic contribution in the field of nonlinear crystals.

MaxiHertz Technologies Ltd is a start-up dedicated to pioneering advancements in multi-domain radio technologies, with a strong focus on improving electromagnetic spectrum efficiency and minimising size, weight, and power (SWaP).
Our current R&D efforts centre on Joint Radar-Communication (JRC) systems, a transformative technology that integrates communication and sensing functions into a unified platform sharing the same frequency band and hardware. This innovation has the potential to address the escalating challenge of spectrum congestion and offers significant benefits across both defence and civilian domains where spectrum congestion is becoming a bottleneck. JRC systems can significantly enhance spectrum utilisation, reduce hardware redundancy and cost, and enable more agile, multifunctional, and scalable platforms.
As multi-domain operations and autonomous systems become increasingly vital to national security and commercial infrastructure, the demand for compact, efficient and multi-mission radio systems continues to grow. MaxiHertz was founded to meet this demand.

We are committed to developing cutting-edge, dual-use solutions that not only solve today’s technical and operational challenges but also shape the future of wireless communication and sensing. Our emphasis on innovation, scalability, and cross-sector applicability ensures that our technologies remain relevant and impactful in a rapidly evolving landscape.

Entity Description (English)
PanelSat GmbH is a privately held company based in Germany, focused on the development of lightweight, fuel-free satellite platforms for research, education, and advanced space applications. The company specializes in novel attitude control systems based on mass shifting and solar panel steering (SoSo-Steering), enabling scalable, modular spacecraft designs without the need for thrusters or reaction wheels.
Founded in 2025, PanelSat GmbH operates as a technology-driven micro-enterprise with a strong emphasis on prototyping, system architecture, and collaboration with academic and industrial partners. The company develops both physical demonstrators and CAD-based licensing models for institutions interested in alternative attitude control methods, formation flying, and long-duration, low-maintenance satellite missions.
PanelSat GmbH is currently preparing its first public demonstration at the International Symposium on Space Sailing (ISSS2025) in Delft and is in contact with ESA, universities, and space hardware manufacturers to explore early validation and flight test opportunities.

TRB Technologies (TRBT) goal is the creation of a self-contained biosphere for lunar or Martian colonies. Our vision for space colonisation thinking was efficiency of the whole food system, from: technologies to grow production and processing and waste minimisation and reuse. 
TRBT’s system includes converting the ‘food waste’ in to additional products and /or uses. TRBT aligns with UN SDGs and Net Zero policies to drive social, economic, and environmental impact, ensuring equitable food access while reducing food miles, fossil fuel use, and promoting local, climate-resilient food.

Space Industry Development Agency ZRT. (SIDA) is an independent Hungarian organization committed to advancing the sustainable commercial utilization of outer space. Key strategic functions include:
- Stakeholder Integration:Acting as a connector between commercial, academic, and governmental actors to create synergies and drive space industry growth.
- Space Sector Enablement:Supporting enterprises in translating their existing capabilities into space-compatible solutions, including downstream and upstream opportunities.
- Commercialization Support:Promoting and facilitating sustainable business models related to space-based applications and services.
- Innovation Platform:Providing access to technical, regulatory, and market intelligence to support innovation across satellite systems, communications, Earth observation, and emerging space markets.
SIDA’s operations are aligned with both national policy goals and international standards, including ESA frameworks, and the agency is registered in ESA STAR to participate in European Space Agency tenders and collaborations.

entityDescription:
Institute profile
Institut für Mikroelektronik Stuttgart carries out industrial-oriented microelectronic research in silicon technology, customized circuits (ASIC), nano structuring and image sensor technology as well as being involved in professional development. It is a foundation recognized as a non-profit organization under civil law with its headquarters on the Stuttgart-Vaihingen research campus. The research facility is a member of the Innovationsallianz Baden-Württemberg (innBW), a cooperation among twelve contract research organizations in Baden-Württemberg.
The foundation
The research facility was founded on July 18th, 1983, by the state of Baden-Württemberg.
Its legal form is a foundation under civil law. The foundation’s mission is to conduct research and development in the field of microelectronic circuits and systems and to ensure that the results of its work are implemented in industrial practice. This task particularly includes
- the construction and operation of research and development facilities for the design of microelectronic circuits and systems
- the construction and operation of process lines for the production of microelectronic experimental, sample and prototype circuits
- the execution of research and development projects on behalf of the federal government, the states and research institutions
- the promotion of practical training of scientific and technical personnel in the field of microelectronics.

Quality certificates and environmental protection declaration
As a research facility with our own pilot and small series production, we have current certification according to ISO9001:2015. Raydiant RF GmbH is a Berlin-based high-tech startup specializing in the development of advanced, application-specific directional antenna systems. Founded in August 2024, the company brings together decades of industrial experience and academic expertise. The founders served as antenna system architects in the Future Combat Air System (FCAS) program, one of Europe’s most advanced defense initiatives, and are recognized experts in high-frequency and beamforming technologies.
Raydiant RF delivers customized, fast-paced development with an optimized time-to-market approach. We provide highly efficient RF solutions tailored to demanding applications across point-to-point communication, sensing, space systems, and special-purpose antennas. Our systems are designed to achieve higher sensitivity, longer range, reduced interference, and lower power consumption.
We believe that hardware should be modular and scalable, enabling innovation instead of limiting it. That’s why our design philosophy focuses on adaptable architectures that accelerate research and development rather than slowing it down.

entityDescription:
Retail Rush – Company Summary
Retail Rush is a European technology and data company specializing in digital coupon solutions for retailers and brands. In strategic partnership with Epay, Global Digital Payment provider, Retail Rush delivers a closed-loop platform that supports every stage of a coupon campaign: from creation and distribution to validation, real-time redemption tracking, and advanced consumer profiling.
Retail Rush plays a key sales and marketing role for Epay’s validation and redemption services, promoting these secure solutions to brands and retailers across Europe. Epay, a Nasdaq-listed leader in digital transaction processing, provides POS-level coupon validation and fraud prevention at over 2,000 retailers across 27 countries. Retail Rush ensures that clients can access and benefit from this infrastructure via a seamless commercial process.
The Epay-Retail Rush offering includes:
Real-time validation and redemption of digital coupon codes using GS1 standards

Fraud prevention and campaign integrity through secure unique codes

Advanced AI profiling to segment and target consumers more effectively

Real-time campaign dashboards for actionable insights and performance tracking

Integration with ad platforms (e.g., Google, Meta) via Segment for automated, smart audience targeting

Through its partnerships and scalable architecture, Retail Rush empowers brands to execute high-impact digital promotions that replace paper coupons, reduce environmental footprint, and deliver measurable returns on advertising spend.
With a goal to enable over tenthousand campaigns annually by 2027, Epay-Retail Rush is setting a new standard for data-driven, secure, and intelligent couponing across Europe.

entityDescription:
Assarmatori is an Italian shipowners’ association based in Rome, Italy. Members include both national and international shipowners and ship operators which, regardless of their flag State, work within the Italian maritime cluster.
Assarmatori represents a large part of the merchant fleet registered in Italy and some of the major shipping operators which maintain regular shipping services in Italy contributing to the overall Italian maritime cluster.
As a national shipping association, Assarmatori is concerned with all technical, legal, environmental, safety and training, employment affairs and trade policy issues that impact on ship and port operations.
We give voice to shipowners and operators on key maritime issues to improve business conditions and support investments for more efficient maritime services and development of new technologies.
We represent shipping interests at the national and international levels, especially with the EU’s institutions, governmental and intergovernmental bodies, international shipping associations and other key players and stakeholders.
Assarmatori’s goals are to:
- to maintain a dialogue between Members and to provide support to them in dealing with the politics and the public administrations at all levels in Italy and abroad.
- to foster a level global playing field to promote a competitive and open business environment in Italy in order to enhance the Blue Economy.
- to ensure that every kind of maritime service is properly represented, giving protection to international operators owning transport lines, operating terminals or passengers’ stations in the Italian ports.
- to ensure that the views of its members are properly presented and listened to by the national, European and international governing bodies and institutions.
- to conduct, as an employers’ association, collective bargaining negotiations with seafarers Unions in Italy.
- to promote sustainable technical development through the application of innovative systems that reduce the environmental impact of emissions.

Lodz University of Technology (TUL) is one of the biggest public technical universities in Poland. It has more than 10000 students, 334 professors and 1220 academic teachers (as of 2024). It offers 64 fields of study within 12 scientific disciplines at 9 faculties. It also has special units: International Faculty of Engineering (IFE), where English and French are the languages of instruction and Interdisciplinary Doctoral School (IDS).

The European Commission awarded the HR Excellence in Research badge to Lodz University of Technology for ensuring attractive work and development conditions for researchers, which confirms that the University abides by the principles set down in the European Charter for Researchers and Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers. 
TUL is the first university of technology and the third academic school in Poland to be recognized by the EC. Lodz University of Technology is the only Polish university being an integral part of the elite network of the European Consortium of Innovative Universities (ECIU), which includes universities from the Netherlands, Denmark, Spain, Portugal, Ireland, Germany, Sweden, Norway, Lithuania, France, Finland, Italy and Mexico - one from each country.

entityName: ReCatalyst, razvoj, proizvodnja in prodaja katalizatorskih kompozitov, d.o.o.
description: ReCatalyst d.o.o. is developing a groundbreaking nanotechnology platform for producing advanced (electro)catalysts for fuel cells and water electrolysis, maximising the efficiency of platinum group metal use for decarbonisation of the energy and transport sectors with green hydrogen. It is a spin-out company from the National Institute of Chemistry (Ljubljana, Slovenia) founded in early 2021. The company holds a strong patented IP over flexible, customisable next-generation platinum-based catalyst solutions already proven in 19 customer pilots across hydrogen technologies value chains. We’ve invented and patented a process that cuts platinum usage by 60% without sacrificing performance. This efficiency also shrinks the fuel cell stack, reducing other components by 30% and overall production costs by 45%. Since inception, the company has received multiple awards such as the Slovenian Start-up-of-the-year 2023 and 2nd place at the EIT awards in the Venture section. The foundations of the start-up have been developed within the projects ERC ‘Proof of Concept’ StableCat and EIT Raw Materials Accelerator. In addition to the EIC Transition project ENABLER, the company has also successfully raised an oversubscribed Seed round of 1.7M EUR co-led by international investors HTGF, OCCIDENT and xista science ventures. ReCatalyst is actively building a global customer base, with projects already in five major G7 economies and across five continents. Among others, we also collaborate with chemical giants who enable large-scale manufacturing; 3 of the Big 6 are in active pilots with us. In the field of space applications, we would like to develop and use our nano technology in the Regenerative Fuel Cell (RFC).
entityDescription:
ReCatalyst is a spin-out (Start-up) company from National Institute of Chemistry (Ljubljana, Slovenia). Our core technology enables us to produce a wide variety of supported metal nanoparticle composites. The initial focus of the company are next-generation platinum-alloy PEM fuel cell catalysts. Our core mission is to make PEM fuel cells massively scalable by bringing the required platinum in PEM fuel cells down to the levels found in today's internal combustion engine vehicles. Additionally, another key competence of ReCatalyst also has a clear focus towards highly active, durable, and reliable catalyst materials and thus, the ability to provide customized solutions for also space applications.

Since incorporation in 2021, the team has reached a developed Minimum Viable Product as well as validated the scalability of their production process. In addition, the team has managed to so-far raised already over 200 000 EUR of non-dilutive pre-seed funding, obtained an exclusive licensing agreement for their technology, and is a holder of the prestigious ERC Proof of Concept grant StableCat, achieving already also first sales with customers this year and is raising their seed round to scale the technology.

description:
As a spin-off of the Tallinn University of Technology's Space Centre, Falconers' motto of "beating Moore's curse for sensing" was informed by the realization that much of (possible) satellite data is still under-communicated, under-processed and thus insufficiently valorized for end-users. Consequently, Falconers conducts its R&D at the intersection of sensing hardware and data processing, as both are needed for taking performance and efficacy to a new level. In ESA projects, we are interested in contributing with the following activities:

- Onboard processing

- AI image analysis

- Novel optronic sensors research

Falconers has experience from previous development projects in building remote sensing tools, multi-sensor integration and computing optimisation. We have participated in and led international R&D projects in various European formats, such as EDA novel optics OB-Study INOPTECH, where Falconers is prime contractor, and EDF STORE, EDF SPIDER and NATO SET-groups. 

Falconers' primary markets are defence ISR, forestry and agriculture. In the defence and ISR market, we develop HawkEye, an optical and computing payload for anomaly detection with a focus on camouflaged objects and decoys. HawkEye entered testing with the Estonian Defence Forces in Spring 2025. In forestry and agriculture, we develop FORSAIT, a remote sensing sensor fusion platform, integrating satellite and in-situ data, including multispectral drone imagery. FORSAIT has a fire simulation and anomaly detection capability, both from satellite and drone data.

description:
NEAT (www.neat.it) is a spin-off of the Italian National Institute of Nuclear Physics (INFN), led by Simone Cabasino and Mario Torelli, which, starting from ’80, under the coordination of Prof. Nicola Cabibbo and Prof. Giorgio Parisi (2021 Nobel laureate in Physics), has fully designed and developed a family of supercomputers able to perform complex algebra calculations to solve Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) simulations.
Today NEAT is a company providing hardware and software Intellectual Properties (Products and Reference Designs (software, firmware, electronic drawings, technical documentation) under licenses) with ancillary highly-specialised Engineering Services, for mission- and safety-critical applications for clients who play a major role in railway, avionics, aerospace, and industrial markets.
NEAT IP’s and engineering services allow clients, mainly in the railway and aerospace sectors, to acquire know-how and to save time and costs in the development of their own products.

NEAT has a highly-qualified technical staff composed by 75 specialists (including the controlled company Arakne S.r.l.), 63 of them possessing a master degree, a PhD or a fellowship in scientific disciplines (Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, and Information Technology). NEAT also includes a division (Arakne S.r.l.) focussed on enterprise software design and development, such as SW algorithms (classical, AI/ML, semantics), portals, web services and applications, mobile, IoT, big data...).

As far as concern the railway market, NEAT’s offering can be grouped in: 
•	Safety-critical platforms, which include GeminiX & GRIO platforms for safety-critical applications
•	Signalling Applications, that include RBC (Radio Block Centre) SW, Interlocking SW, Protocols (PVS, RASTA), KMC-Subset137 and Engineering services
•	Tools that include the "Design4 Rail" (D4R) ecosystem of products (Horizon, Workplace).

As far as concern the Aerospace market, NEAT’s products can be grouped in: 
•	HPSC (High Performances Spaceflight Computers), which includes HW platforms for satellite LEO applications
•	GeminiX-S, a generic low-level SW that implements a real-time OS-like environment, mostly independent from the specific HW. 
Other HPSCs for deep space applications are currently under design.

entityName: Budapest University of Technology and Economics - Department of Automotive Technologies
entityDescription:
The professional activities of the Department of Automotive Technologies are organised into five research groups, which are also responsible for education.
Under the umbrella ofBME Automated Drive Laboratory,we have three research groups, the Environmental Perception, Vehicle Dynamics and Control and Safety and Security Research Groups.
The research area of theCooperative Perceptionresearch group is related to intelligent transport infrastructure within autonomous vehicle control. We believe that safe autonomous transport of the future will not only mean smart, intelligent cars driving autonomously, but also smart, intelligent infrastructure. And these smart devices will work together to deliver safe and efficient automated transport.
The main research area of theVehicle Dynamics and Controlresearch group is vehicle control at and beyond the dynamic limit, one of the most striking examples of which is drifting in a car that is not driven by a human.
OurSafety and Securityresearch group has a long tradition in the field of traffic accident analysis and reconstruction. Today, we no longer separate safety and security, but treat them as one. We say that a failure can result in a cyber security problem, but equally a cyber security vulnerability can result in a safety problem or failure.
The vehicle-related areas are covered by theInnovative Vehicle Technologiesresearch group. The focus of education has shifted strongly towards electromobility, hydrogen powertrain and renewable energies.
TheLaser and Vehicle Manufacturing Technologiesresearch group focuses on materials science and manufacturing technologies used in automotive manufacturing. In the field of additive manufacturing, better known as 3D printing, we are mainly working with metals and the related selective laser melting process,which has been one of the outstanding activities of the department for many years.

description:
We are Falcon Payload Systems Ltd, a Bulgaria-based aerospace technology company established in 2025 and headquartered in Plovdiv. Our mission is to advance the design and integration of intelligent payload deployment systems and autonomous platforms for next-generation space and unmanned aerial missions.

At Falcon Payload Systems, we focus on developing innovative, mission-critical solutions that meet the growing needs of the European space and defense sectors. We specialize in:

 Payload Deployment Mechanisms – Modular and scalable release systems for CubeSats, small satellites, and UAV payloads, optimized for precision, reliability, and integration flexibility.

 Unmanned and Autonomous Systems – Engineering subsystems and components for UAVs and robotic platforms, with a strong focus on modularity and performance in complex environments.

 Prototyping and Systems Integration – In-house capabilities for rapid prototyping, system testing, and component-level integration, ensuring fast iteration and high fidelity.

 R&D and Engineering Support – Applied research in advanced materials, aerospace-grade mechanisms, and embedded control systems aligned with ESA and ECSS standards.

We aim to be a strategic partner within the European space ecosystem, supporting ESA-led missions and projects by delivering innovative, reliable, and cost-effective technology. Our goal is to contribute to Europe’s technological leadership and autonomy in space operations.

We are actively seeking collaboration under ESA programs such as GSTP, ARTES, NAVISP, and Horizon Europe, and we are open to joint ventures, subcontracting, and co-development opportunities.

entityDescription: Aviant is a Trondheim-based drone logistics company pioneering autonomous, on-demand delivery services across the Nordics. Founded at MIT in 2020, the company provides a full-stack platform of fixed-wing drones that fly beyond visual line of sight and can cover up to 124 km per trip. To date, Aviant’s aircraft have completed more than 5,000 flights and logged 50,000 km, transporting time-critical cargo such as blood samples, COVID-19 tests and urgent medication between hospitals as well as food through its Kyte service, directly to consumers’ doorsteps. Certified under the EU drone regulations, Aviant reduces delivery times and CO₂ emissions compared with road transport, helping hospitals, e-commerce retailers and remote communities get what they need faster and more sustainably. Backed by investors such as Bring Ventures and Luminar Ventures, the company is expanding across Norway and Sweden and aims to set a new standard for safe, efficient aerial logistics in Europe.

entityDescription:
Muon Solutions Oy (MUON) is an innovative deep-tech SME founded in Finland in 2016. MUON's innovative use of cosmic-ray muon detection exemplifies its commitment to advancing technology and addressing societal challenges in positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT), as well as subsurface imaging (muon imaging). The company specialises in the development and commercialisation of muometric technologies, with a focus on environments where traditional methods, such as GNSS, are ineffective, including underground, underwater, and indoor settings.
MUON holds exclusive global commercial rights to breakthrough intellectual property on muometric positioning and navigation (“vector-muPS”), originally developed through academic collaborations with the University of Tokyo and the Wigner Research Centre for Physics, Hungary. These technologies are supported by rigorous scientific validation.
The company maintains a strong European and international network, actively forming consortia (e.g., five ongoing Horizon Europe projects for muon imaging). MUON works with national metrology institutes, research centres, and private industry. In addition to PNT applications, Muon Solutions is a leader in applied muography, developing muon imaging services for mining, civil engineering, cultural heritage, and environmental monitoring.

- Engage Eastern Slovakia in international space projects.
- Attract and retain talent by developing specialized educational programs and vocational training, thereby enhancing the region's appeal to young professionals.
- Support innovative start-ups and companies that can leverage opportunities in the rapidly growing space sector.
Strategically located at the University Science Park TECHNICOM in Košice, the cluster benefits from a neutral environment that facilitates collaboration between academia and industry. entityName: National University of Science and Technology Politehnica Bucharest
entityDescription:
NUST POLITEHNICA Bucharest is the oldest and most prestigious engineer school in Romania. Its traditions are related to the establishment, in 1818, by Gheorghe Lazăr, of the first higher technical school with teaching in Romanian, at the Saint Sava Abbey in Bucharest. In 1832, it was reorganized into the St. Sava College.
On 1 October 1864, The School of Bridges and Roads, Mines and Architecture was established, which becomes, on 30 October 1867,The School of Bridges, Roads and Mines, with a duration of 5 years. Under the leadership of Gheorghe Duca, on 1 April 1881, the institution acquires a new structure, under the name of The National School of Bridges and Roads; on 10 June 1920, the Politehnica School of Bucharest was founded, with four departments: Electromechanics, Civil Engineering, Mines and Metallurgy, Industrial Section. From November 1920 the name changes to POLITEHNICA of Bucharest.
On 3 August 1948, the Polytechnic Institute of Bucharest was founded, which initially included 4 faculties and in which, since 1950, have appeared most of the current faculties. Based on the resolution of the Senate of November 1992, the Polytechnic Institute of Bucharest became University POLITEHNICA of Bucharest.
After the merger with the University of Pitesti, in 2023, the university was named the National University of Science and Technology Politehnica Bucharest.
NUSTPB assumes the mission to train specialists in different technical fields that are able to use valuable scientific, technical and cultural knowledge, to contribute to the technological, economic and social-cultural progress of the Romanian society and the contemporary world. NUSTPB ensures a performant education, developed and perfected through a complex research activity, continuing the tradition of the Polytechnic School of Bucharest, according to the exigencies and the means offered by the modern information society. It aims to create a new technical university profile, which promotes forms of training adapted to the requirements of a competing society, subject to the integration process in the European and international community.Its main mission is to train an engineer capable of adapting to the requirements of market economy and new technologies, with an economic and managerial knowledge and promote the principles of sustainable development and environmental protection.
The University focuses on achieving the objectives of developing economic and social cohesion in line with the goals set out in the 2020 Strategy. To accomplish the mission, it projects the processes and objectives that lead to the development of society. The students are at the centre of university’s concerns, so goals, action plans, policies, developed strategies, and applied principles serve their interests.
As a European member state, Romania must implement the programs designed in the European Areas of Higher Education and Research and meet the objectives of the Union’s agenda.
Education and Training 2020 seeks lifelong learning for EU citizens, improving the quality and efficiency of the education system, promoting social cohesion, active citizenship, and stimulating creativity, innovation and entrepreneurship in education.
The NUSTPB will propose for approval to the university’s senate a new strategy that seeks the following: 1) Maintain and develop skills in fundamental and engineering sciences, indispensable for the sustainability of technological development;2) Develop soft skills, social and relational skills; 3) Personal development of students; 4) Encourage the learning of modern languages; 5) Encourage student participation in mobility programs; 6) Ensure ongoing dialogue with students; 7) Encourage extracurricular activities; 8) Develop volunteering; 10) Encourage graduates with the best professional results in becoming teachers.

entityDescription:
The Pomurje Science and Innovation Center was founded as a public research institute in 2022. In a way, we are just beginning the journey of discovering the new and the unknown. And yet we have no time to grow up, because we are thrown into global chaos, which does not allow time for carelessness, playing in the sandbox and discovering the "correct" path. We face a set of challenges that we must meet if we want to justify our existence and the trust that has been placed in us.

On this basis, we want to establish Pomurje as an equal research region, whose scientific discoveries are judged only through the scientific method and not through the prism of centralism and the "political right" to scientific existence. The creation of the Pomurje Science and Innovation Center is proof that the state recognizes the scientific potential of Pomurje, which needs to be exploited.

Research activity takes place in several different forms. Depending on the organizational form, this includes basic research work, which researchers perform as their primary activity within the scope of their employment, then there are research projects and programs, which take place on the basis of applications for relevant tenders, whereby projects are, in principle, research activities with a target orientation in a shorter period of time, while the programs are basic research lasting longer.

KEKO Equipment is a medium-sized company that ranks among the world leaders in manufacturing advanced equipment for producing multilayer passive ceramic electronic circuits and other layer-based technologies. With 25 years of experience in the field, we have developed comprehensive expertise in designing and manufacturing both individual machines and complete, fully automated production lines.
Our company's origins trace back to when we operated as part of the former ISKRA consortium. Since becoming privately owned in 1995, we have built our success on a foundation of highly skilled and motivated engineers who drive our continuous innovation. Today, we serve global markets across Europe, Asia, America and Australia with our proprietary technologies.
At KEKO, we combine our extensive knowledge of established manufacturing processes with the flexibility to develop customized solutions tailored to our clients' specific requirements. Our capabilities span the entire spectrum from conventional production methods to cutting-edge applications in LTCC (Low-Temperature Co-fired Ceramic) and HTCC (High-Temperature Co-fired Ceramic) technologies.
To demonstrate our technical capabilities, we maintain a fully equipped demonstration room where clients can see prototype parts being manufactured using various multilayer technologies. This hands-on experience allows potential partners to evaluate our equipment's performance with actual LTCC, HTCC and other advanced ceramic components.
While our core focus remains on ceramic circuit manufacturing, we have successfully expanded into related fields including fuel cell production equipment. Our ability to adapt to market needs has made us a trusted supplier to several world-renowned manufacturers in these sectors.
What truly sets KEKO apart in the global marketplace is our unique combination of:
Deep technical expertise in multilayer technologies
Exceptional flexibility in equipment design
Continuous innovation driven by our engineering team
Comprehensive demonstration and prototyping capabilities
These strengths have earned our brand worldwide recognition and enabled us to develop successful technological solutions for diverse industrial applications. Our commitment to quality and customer satisfaction remains the cornerstone of our business philosophy as we continue to push the boundaries of multilayer manufacturing technology.

What truly sets KEKO apart in the global marketplace is our unique combination of:
Deep technical expertise in multilayer technologies
Exceptional flexibility in equipment design
Continuous innovation driven by our engineering team
Comprehensive demonstration and prototyping capabilities
These strengths have earned our brand worldwide recognition and enabled us to develop successful technological solutions for diverse industrial applications. Our commitment to quality and customer satisfaction remains the cornerstone of our business philosophy as we continue to push the boundaries of multilayer manufacturing technology.

Established in 2002, we have built a strong reputation with a diverse portfolio of cutting-edge products, including COFDM IP mesh radios and an extensive range of optical and thermal cameras, designed for both large-scale and small-scale deployments. We listen to our customers and over the last four years, have collaborated with multiple law enforcement agencies across Europe to develop, test, and validate emergency and community-focused software platforms and mobile apps. entityDescription:
The Hungarian name of the Foundation:Magyar Napfizikai Alapítvány

The Purpose of the Foundation:- To create an environment for Hungarian ground-based observations for solar and heliophysical scientific research and education. To carry out solar and heliophysical observations and to process and publish the obtained data via professional and educational forums.
- To indirectly and directly support solar and heliophysical research (e.g. via conferences, workshops, organizing and supporting summer schools and the participation in such, making research data accessible for a wider public).
- The promotion of solar and heliophysics both in a scientific and an educational aspect in Hungary and abroad.
- To support scientific research in astronomy, space physics, and environmental physics in a broader sense (primarily in Hungarian rural territories and in Budapest, secondly in direct cross-border areas, and thirdly in foreign locations). Furthermore, to carry out such research in accordance with the resources.
- To support public education, out-of-school activities and arrangement of irregular classes concerning the field of astronomy, space research, space physics and environmental physics in a boarder sense.
- Scientific and technical education involving wide-range social strata, while using diverse and interactive methods and techniques.
- To organize and carry out other public educational activities (displays, exhibitions, concerts, summer camps, meetings, conferences etc.) concerning solar physics, heliophysics, astronomy, space research, space physics and environmental physics. To provide and support study groups and club sessions.
- Talent management and educating the next generation. This is a priority objective in all areas of operation (natural sciences, technical fields and arts). The primary aim of this field of activity is to be involved nationwide in the preparations, in the organization, and in the participation in national student competitions in the field astronomy and astrophysics concerning solar and heliophysics. Furthermore, to assist the national team’s Olympic participation.
- Other research and development, as well as innovation activities in cooperation with partner institutions and companies, first and foremost regarding solar and heliophysical topics (e.g. the development of robotic solar physics telescopes, magneto-optical filters, and filters that are suitable for Doppler measurements). Secondly, research and innovation activities regarding topics concerning astronomy, environmental physics, space research, as well as certain particular environmental topics (e.g. light pollution, noise protection).
- Real estate management and renting.
- To retail the operation hours – not used or needed by the researchers of the Foundation – of the robotic solar physics telescope to other persons for scientific purposes.
- To operate one or more computer databases and content provider sites, to partially cover the cost of the maintenance, to update data and to continuously develop the server. The name of the database is GSD. To appropriately promote it, advertise it via all available media, especially via Web, Twitter and Facebook, which recently gained great significance.
- The achievement of all objectives and the extent of these objectives always depend on the current financial opportunities of the Foundation, as well as on discretionary managerial consideration. The Foundation does not commit itself to funding each objective in the same proportion every year.

entityDescription:
MagBoost Space is a deeptech venture developing a ground-based electromagnetic launcher designed to deliver robotic payloads to the Moon and beyond with drastically reduced cost and carbon footprint.
Our vision: enable the autonomous industrialization of space by focusing on two interdependent pillars:
Robotic systems with high autonomy to operate in space without human presence.

A reusable electromagnetic catapult capable of launching these systems at accelerations up to 50 g, well within robotic tolerances but incompatible with human passengers.

Unlike chemical rockets, our system:
Operates with zero direct CO₂ emissions,

Is entirely ground-based and reusable, and

Reduces cost per kg by an order of magnitude, enabling high-frequency access to cislunar space.

Our approach supports the deployment of robotic units for resource extraction, in-situ construction, and infrastructure pre-deployment, paving the way for permanent presence and eventual sovereignty over lunar industrial zones.
MagBoost Space is currently developing a scaled demonstrator and building collaborations with robotics manufacturers, launch infrastructure experts, and lunar mission planners.

entityDescription:
Soil Capital is a mission-driven company with long expertise in regenerative agriculture and low-carbon transition of farms. 
It was founded in 2013 as an independent agronomy firm by three farming and finance professionals. 
The initial structure renamed SoilCapital Farming (sister company) has advised and managed over 200’000 hectares of farmland in transition to more profitable and regenerative agriculture across 15 countries & 4 continents. 
These years of experience working alongside farmers lead Soil Capital to launch in 2019, Europe’s first certified carbon payment programme to accelerate the regenerative transition.

To date, the Soil Capital Carbon programme has engaged more than 1000 farmers, spread across France, Belgium and the UK. 
Three rounds of carbon payments totalling € 6’000’000 have been paid by supporting companies - mainly from the ag & fiber industry but not only - to farmers for their contribution to healthy soil & food systems. In 2022, Soil Capital became a B Corp company and took part in the creation of the Climate Agriculture Alliance as a founding member with the ambition to support the implementation of rigorous frameworks for implementing agricultural carbon finance in Europe.

entityDescription:
Ever since its foundation in 1949, the Military Technical Academy has been a military higher polytechnic education institution which has cultivated those important values characterizing the personalities of the future specialists in the field of engineering science: competence, scientific honesty, morality, the desire to accomplish the assigned missions.
The military polytechnic higher education has been developing in accordance with the standards of the national higher education and the requirements of the military, providing for the scientific, technical, military, moral competencies and qualities necessary both to the officers and the civilians graduates in engineering science.
The higher education in the Military Technical Academy meets the quality and efficiency national and international standards providing for the academy the possibility of having consistent international cooperation with higher education institutions all over the world, carrying out joint bachelor, master and doctoral programs or international research projects.
In 2008, based on the national regulations in force (GD no. 551/2007), the MTA was accredited by the National Research Authority – NRA, based on the Research Self-Evaluation Report, as a certified institution tot carry out research and development activities (NRA Decision no. 9673/2008).
MTA is certified to carry out scientific research, consultancy for technological development and technical expertise in the field of security systems technology in conformity with EN ISO 9001:2000 and AQAP 2110 standards.
MTA has the mission to carry out scientific research in its field of competence in conformity with the requirements of the defense, public order and national security structures and other beneficiaries, based on contracts.
MTA promotes the European dimension of education and scientific research by participating in programs of European Union and in partnerships with military and civilian universities through students, teachers and researchers mobility.

CIDETEC is a private organization for applied research founded in 1997 that seeks to contribute value to companies by harnessing, generating and transferring technological knowledge. Located in the Donostia-San Sebastián site of Gipuzkoa’s Scientific and Technological Park, CIDETEC is comprised of three international technological reference institutes in energy storage, surface engineering and nanomedicine.
· CIDETEC Energy Storage
The CIDETEC institute for Energy Storage specialises in creating new battery technology and facilitating its transfer to industry. The institute has the capacity to develop complete products and processes and offers material validation, pilot manufacture, pack engineering and battery testing services.
· CIDETEC Surface Engineering
The CIDETEC institute for Surface Engineering is a reference institute and the main thrust of an innovation pole specialising in the development of these technologies, providing surface solutions throughout the entire value chain for the automotive, aerospace, extreme environment and other sectors.
· CIDETEC Nanomedicine
The CIDETEC institute for Nanomedicine is devoted to the development of innovative materials in the field of biomedicine. The institute bases its activity on the creation of its own technology and currently has obtained patents for three product families, with several more applications pending. Its direct contact with industry enables it to complete technology transfer, reducing time to market.
Each institute has its own offices and installations furnished with top-of-the-line equipment, among them a pilot plant for integrated battery manufacture; equipment to synthesise, characterise and process polymers and advanced composites; laboratories completely equipped for surface study, characterisation and treatment; and 150 m2 of rooms classified and prepared for GMP-standard product manufacture in the biopharmaceutical sector.
CIDETEC currently employs a workforce of 183, 95% of whom are university graduates and 45% PhD holders. Its volume of activity came up to � 13M in 2019.

entityDescription:
FastHazard is a Dutch company focused on the development and use of innovative tools for assessment of natural hazards. In 2024, it started as a spin-off company from Twente University, with the launch of the “FastFlood.org” rapid flood simulation platform. Since then, the model has been used around the world by students, consulting companies, governments (e.g. RVO Netherlands) and international organizations (e.g World Bank, WFP,GCA). New functionality and tools are continuously being added, such as the FastSlide.org landslide simulation tool, and links with more and better global datasets. The ongoing strong collaboration between the company and the university drives research on the rapid flow simulation methods at the University, while allowing the company to leverage the network of student and professors in the commercial usage of the tools. The team now consists of 4 expert researchers in water and environmental dynamics, aiming to bring further innovation to fit-for-purpose tooling for disaster risk reduction.

FastFlood.org tool is an innovative flood simulation tool developed and maintained by Dr. Bastian van den Bout. FastFlood enables fast and efficient flood scenario calculations. Originally developed in 2021, the model has undergone continuous improvements and now offers over 97% accuracy, while being up to 1500 times faster than traditional flood modelling methods. This speed makes it an ideal solution for quick risk assessments and initial analyses. The model is available as a web-based application and free to use. Users can easily download relevant data from global datasets or upload their own data for more detailed simulations. FastFlood provides various features such as mitigation design, setting boundary conditions for coastal and river areas, running precipitation scenarios, and simulating infiltration and other dynamics. It also incorporates the CMIP6 downscaled climate datasets to easily model future scenarios. The model has proven useful for generating initial flood scenarios and is a powerful addition to discussions on flood risk and adaptation strategies.

TECOS Slovenian Tool and Die Development Centre was established in 1994 as a non-profit organisation to represent the collective interests of the Tool, Die & Mould-making (TDM) and Processing Industries in support of the various manufacturing sectors that serve as key drivers for Slovenian economic development. TECOS was founded by the Government of Slovenia – Ministry for Economy, Chamber of Commerce – GZS and Municipality of Celje and thus has a direct access to the most relevant governmental policy makers in Slovenia. 
TECOS today operates on three dimensional assets, as R&D Centre, International Business Cluster and VET Institution, providing top level services not only for TDM industry but also to all other manufacturing companies in Slovenia. TECOS’s R&D focus areas are: advanced manufacturing, robotics, nanotechnologies, packaging technologies and advancements for medical, home appliance, automotive and transportation industries. TECOS’s highly skilled personnel and otherwise wide range of expertise services for industry are in many ways related to bio-based products and eco-innovations. 
TECOS operates as a competent institutional support of Slovenian Manufacturing Industries in the transfer of this knowledge & technical support services, providing the latest information and advancements on the bio-economy benefits and prosperous potentials for entering and conquering new global markets. TECOS’s priority is to improve the members’ competitiveness through the provision of valuable resources, and in so doing, cluster actively assist in the positioning of the TDM industry. which holds a great hope for the future as manufacturers commit to more efficient technology practice and green engineering.

MPC's long term objective is becoming an intellectual forum and international landmark for excellence in material science.MPCpromotes and carries out activities in fundamental and oriented research, thus decisively contributing to knowledge generation based in research excellence, post-graduated training and spreading of popular science.

entityDescription:
The University of Tartu (UT) prides itself on being Estonia’s premier institution of higher learning and is steadily moving towards becoming one of the leading institutions for innovative education and cutting-edge research in the Nordic region. As the only university in the Baltic States, UT continues to be ranked in the top 1.2% of the world’s top universities, placing 358th in the latest (2023) edition of the QS World University Rankings and within the 301–350 range in the Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings 2023.

Established in 1632, UT is the oldest and largest university in Estonia both in terms of numbers of staff and students, as well as in terms of the volume of its teaching, research and development activities. UT alone accounts for more than a half of all the doctoral degrees conferred (129 in 2023) and research publications (2086 high-level publications published in 2022 according to the Estonian Research Information System), and national R&D financing in Estonia.
Membership in several high-level research university networks such as The Guild of European Research-Intensive Universities, the Coimbra Group, LERU-CE7, and the Europaeum, enables UT to play an active role in the shaping of European research and higher education policies, and facilitates a well-functioning exchange of information and mobility of researchers, staff and students.

Being the country’s only classical university, UT embraces a wide variety of academic fields ranging from medicine and genetics to philosophy, literature, and computer science. Cutting-edge research is conducted by more than 1000 researchers working in 31 institutes across the University’s four faculties: the Faculty of Arts and Humanities, Faculty of Social Sciences, Faculty of Medicine, and Faculty of Science and Technology.

Belonging in the top 1% of the world’s most cited research institutions in 15 research fields, UT has a strong track record in attracting financing from the most competitive research funds, including the prestigious grants awarded by the European Research Council (ERC), the EU’s frontier research agency.
 
In its research and development efforts, UT focuses on five main areas: entrepreneurial and socially responsible society; healthy and active long-lived people; resources and technologies for environmentally friendly economic growth; information and communication technology for developing an innovative society; and the sustainability of the Estonian language and culture in an open world.

description:
NeoDynamics develops a platform for the design, training, and deployment of reinforcement learning-based control systems in high-stakes, dynamic environments. Our technology enables users to define custom control problems, simulate system behavior at scale, and train agents that adapt through interaction, rather than relying on hand-tuned rules or static models.

We support organizations operating in domains such as space operations, defense systems, and advanced robotics—where traditional control approaches often struggle with uncertainty, real-time constraints, and nonlinear dynamics. By combining simulation, optimization, and machine learning, NeoDynamics provides a modular infrastructure to accelerate the development of intelligent autonomous systems.

entityName: LUH - INSTITUT FÜR PHOTOGRAMMETRIE UND GEOINFORMATION (IPI)
entityDescription:
The Institute of Photogrammetry and GeoInformation (IPI) is a leading university research institution in the field of photogrammetry, remote sensing and computer vision. Our main strengths are the development and implementation of new methods for the extraction of geometric and semantic 3D information from aerial and satellite imagery as well as from drone images. In addition, we are active in the processing of terrestrial images and image sequences, e.g. in the fields of 3D reconstruction, mobility and optical 3D metrology. A major methodological focus is on machine learning methods. We participate intensively in national and international research projects, often in interdisciplinary teams. In addition, we offer our services to public and private institutions in the fields of photogrammetry, remote sensing, geoinformation, computer vision and industrial metrology.
In teaching, we primarily participate in the BSc. and MSc. courses in geodesy and geoinformatics, but also in many other bachelor's and master's degree programmes at LUH.

description: PV2+ is a German deep-tech startup and spin-off from the Fraunhofer Institute ISE, developing a patented copper electroplating process to replace silver in solar cell contacts. The solution significantly reduces costs, improves performance, and eliminates the environmental impact of silver use. Initially designed for silicon-based cells, PV2+ is now working on adapting its technology for high-efficiency III-V solar cells such as GaAs, including space and concentrator applications. The company offers its process through a pay-per-use model, including technology licensing, implementation support, and proprietary consumables. PV2+ is supported by multiple public and private partners and is engaged in active collaborations with leading solar cell manufacturers and tool suppliers.

Additionally, we will manufacture Solid Rocket Motors with our proprietary SRM technology that maximizes range and velocity for PAC-3, SM-3, and SM-6 Interceptor programs.

We will Recondition, Reload, and Relaunch™ our rockets synonymous with how we use airplanes today for multiple daily flights in under 24 hrs., achieving reusability 2.0. Utilizing cutting-edge 3D printing and additive manufacturing technology, we’re dedicated to providing reliable and rapid access to space at a low cost. entityDescription:
Blockchain Solutions with Creative Expertise
More than a decade ago, the world woke up to a movement led by international communities of cypherpunks—mathematicians and programmers—who dedicated themselves to developing encrypted, internet-optimized data transmission systems. Their vision was a future driven by democratized, independent technological solutions. This vision gave birth to the first blockchains, which quickly became the greatest promise of the 21st-century digital financial markets.
Our team consists of some of the most experienced revolutionaries from these communities, leaving their digital footprints behind for over a decade.
Our mission is to develop functional blockchain-based business solutions that are stable, secure, cost-efficient, and standardized.
Beyond our market operations, we invest significant resources in building and mentoring both local and international blockchain communities.

Attila Vidákovics
CEO, Blockchain Specialist, Educator, Presenter
Attila Vidákovics is a recognized blockchain expert in Hungary’s fintech sector, playing a key role in the introduction of decentralized financial systems in the country. His project team was the first to develop a functional EVM-based blockchain in Hungary. His personal mission is to educate people about the operational logic of crypto markets, decentralized financial systems, and blockchains, facilitating a successful cultural shift.
As the CEO of Dlabs Kft., he follows a holistic approach, assessing the economic, technological, and user aspects of every business project before optimizing the development direction.
As an educator, he teaches courses at Corvinus University of Budapest and Milton Friedman University, and is a guest lecturer at the International Banker Training Center. Additionally, he hosts a weekly show, Kriptoverzum, on Trend FM.
A member of MENSA HungarIQa, he is the founder and leader of the Blockchain and Cryptocurrency group, as well as the co-chair of the MENSA International Blockchain Research Group.
Péter Molnár
CTO, Blockchain Strategist, Community Builder
With degrees in economics and engineering informatics, Péter Molnár's unique perspective has positioned him as one of Hungary’s first technology experts in crypto systems. He is one of the few professionals in the country capable of building functional blockchain networks.
For over five years, he has been a key figure in Hungary’s crypto developer community, advocating for the necessity of network democratization. His hands-on experience includes IT network infrastructure development, system operation, customized system configuration, and programming.
As the CTO of Dlabs Kft., he is characterized by strategic thinking, a systematic approach, and a continuous drive for innovation. His portfolio includes several bank security projects.
He is also active as an educator and community organizer, regularly giving lectures at Corvinus University of Budapest and Milton Friedman University. He is proficient in multiple programming languages, with expertise in Solidity, Erlang, and Rust.

entityDescription:
Fyous is the company behind the development of PolyMorphic moulding technology, initially targeted at creating bespoke footwear for athletes. Recognising the broader potential of their technology, Fyous has expanded its application to include medical and other industrial uses. Their proprietary manufacturing process allows for the rapid and accurate production of custom products, addressing significant challenges in various sectors.
PolyMorphic moulding is a shapeshifting, infinitely reusable moulding technology. It has the potential to transform the manufacturing industry, reducing the waste generated through tooling amends, coupled with the faster production times compared to 3D printing and traditional mould-making. By inputting a 3D CAD model, Fyous software generates the PolyMorphic mould shape. The PolyMorphic machine then shapeshifts the mould to create the intended product. On completion of the production, the PolyMorphic mould is returned to the machine, ready for the next shapeshift.
Co-founders Joshua Shires and Thomas Bloomfield have driven the company’s mission to deliver a revolutionary moulding technology that will disrupt the manufacturing sector enabling products to be bought to market that were previously not commercially viable or enable products to be bought to market much faster.

he Medical University of Gdańsk (MUG) is a modern academic centre, recognizable in the country and in the world. The MUG is gradually improving in the lists of leading universities. It is one of the best medical university in Poland according to the latest Ranking of Academic Universities of the Educational FoundationPerspektywy.
The MUG educates over 6000 students, doctoral students and postgraduate students. There are over 1000 foreign students among them, which constitutes over 16% of all students at the University. It is also more than half of all foreigners studying in Gdańsk. Every year, about 180 young people from abroad study at the MUG, which makes it the most internationalized university in Pomerania. Students benefit from a conveniently located student housing estate and a modern research library. They have at their disposal the Medical Simulation Center, a modern Sports Centre and the “Medyk” student club.
The University intensively develops scientific research, as evidenced by its leading positions in the ranking and numerous prestigious awards for employees, students and doctoral students.
Thanks to the funds provided by the Foundation for Polish Science under the International Research Agendas (MAB) program, a research centre specializing in research on genetic aberrations acquired during life as risk factors for cancer and other diseases has been established at the Medical University of Gdańsk. The project leaders are Prof. Arkadiusz Piotrowski from the Department of Biology and Pharmaceutical Botany of the Medical University of Gdańsk and Prof. Jan Dumański from the Faculty of Immunology, Genetics and Pathology of the University of Uppsala.

We envision a truly reusable spaceplane capable of reaching hypersonic speed in airbreathing mode, then transitioning seamlessly into rocket mode to exit the atmosphere. description:
Cold Plasma Devices and Advanced Polymers
Nadir is an innovative SME founded in 2008 by a group of researchers with over 10 years of experience in the nanotechnology sector who have worked as scientific consultants in the field of technology transfer between academia and industry. Since 2016 Nadir has focused its activity on the application of an innovative and proprietary atmospheric plasma technology and in the development of advanced polymer composites. Since 2020 Nadir has been recognized as a "key innovator" by the EC Innovation radar initiative (https://www.innoradar.eu/innovator/972500079 ). 
The company, after applying for an international patent on the new atmospheric plasma device, has obtained the related grants in countries such as the United States, China, Japan, Australia, Europe and Canada. 
The Nadir Plasma device is now entering in various application sectors ranging from advance manufacturing, biomedical, aerospace, electronics and 3D printing, for cleaning treatments, surface activation, deposition of functional coatings and metallic layers and improvement of adhesion between dissimilar materials. 
Similarly, the advanced polymeric materials proposed by Nadir, such as electro-conductive, responsive, antimicrobial and improved performance polymers, as well as being studied in various European projects, are now applied in the sectors indicated above. Currently the company has its operational headquarters in Venezia-Mestre (Italy), with a Plasma laboratory equipped for the design and development of new devices and the study of innovative surface treatment processes, and with a Polymers laboratory equipped with different melt compounding technologies for the study of new generations of active and bioactive fillers for the production of advanced polymer composites.
