entityDescription:
Pulsar Space Intelligence is a French deep-tech startup specializing in space environment risk mitigation for satellite operators. 
Our mission is to make satellite operations more resilient and cost-effective in the increasingly congested and disturbed low Earth orbit (LEO) environment.
We develop and operate a global network of passive ground sensors combined with a real-time digital twin of the near-Earth space environment. 
Our proprietary system fuses space weather forecasting, orbital traffic monitoring, and RF beacon tracking to deliver predictive alerts, maneuver recommendations, and environmental analytics.

Pulsar’s services enable satellite operators to:
- Reduce downtime caused by space weather and collision risks,
- Optimize fuel consumption for orbital maneuvers,
- Lower insurance premiums through better risk management,
- Extend mission lifetimes and delay costly satellite replacements.

Our core technological expertise spans:
- Radio frequency (RF) signal processing,
- Space weather modeling and prediction,
- Orbital mechanics and conjunction analysis,
- Machine learning for anomaly detection and forecasting.

Founded by engineers (Valentin STEE) and scientists (Anthony SALSI) with backgrounds in aerospace, space physics, and signal intelligence, Pulsar collaborates with leading academic institutions such as "Observatoire de la Cote d'Azur" and targets customers in the NewSpace industry, defense, public agencies, and satellite insurance sectors.

entityDescription:
The Swedish Space Corporation (SSC) is a leading global provider of advanced space services. Initially pioneering scientific rocket launches in northern Sweden, SSC have grown into a full-service supplier of state-of-the-art space engineering, satellite and launch services to commercial and institutional customers worldwide.
Since the 1960s, SSC has contributed to the development of space technologies.
Today, we offer to customers cutting-edgecompetence and technology within a variety of segments in space.
Our organization is structured in the following BUSINESS DIVISIONS:​
1. Science and Launch Services - Esrange Space Center
2. Satellite Ground Network Services
3. Space Operations and Engineering Services
4. Data analytics and Processing Services
As a forward-thinking organization, the SSC group actively engages in research and development activities to push the boundaries of space technology. We collaborate with national and international partners to explore new opportunities and drive innovation in the space sector.
With our rich heritage, technical expertise, and commitment to excellence, the Swedish Space Corporation continues to be a prominent force in the global space industry, driving advancements and unlocking the potential of space for the benefit of society and the world at large.
SSC Worldwide
SSC has established a number of operational subsidiaries and facilities across Europe and all around the World, in order to manage the distributed nature of its business. Based on their activity domain and expertise, each subsidiary or facility is included in a specific SSC division.
As italian subsidiary, we are part of the SSC Engineering Service division
Through our integration with the SSC group, SSC Space Italy gains access to a wealth of knowledge, resources, and industry-leading practices in service provision.
This setup empowers us to deliver unparalleled solutions, backed by cutting-edge advancements and best-in-class methodologies.
We are at the forefront of innovation, ready to revolutionize the way we cater to our clients’ requirements.
We can offer a wide range of skillsets, which covers the entire space product development life cycle.
The expertise we can provide in our Service & Support Portfolio spans from Preliminary Phase 0/A (conceptual mission design) to Phase F (mission operations, maintenance, and disposal).

description:
LA composite, s.r.o. (company limited) was founded in 1995 as joint venture of companies Letov, a.s. and ATG, s.r.o.. Later on, ATG, s.r.o. acquired the Letov's share and became an exclusive owner of LA composite.Since then, we have been continuing in the long-standing tradition of manufacturing of composite, sandwich and bonded structures for aerospace industry. Meanwhile, our range of product expanded into the terrestrial transport industry (railway vehicles, automotive) and into other applications (yachts, textile industry etc).We offer our customers wide range of complex services from design up to serial production of parts. 

LAC specializes in the production of composite parts using state-of-the-art technologies. A key part of our manufacturing process is autoclave curing, ensuring maximum strength and quality of the final products. We work with advanced resin systems, including epoxy, phenolic, and BMI, and focus on precision in every detail. Production takes place in climate-controlled clean rooms with laser projection for perfect material layering. For final processing, we utilize high-precision 5-axis CNC machining, and to maintain optimal material properties, we have a large-capacity freezing storage. By combining cutting-edge technology with years of expertise, we deliver top-tier composite solutions for the most demanding applications.
entityDescription:
(1) LA Composite, s.r.o. is a producer of composite parts, sandwich and bonded structures.
LAC represents: 
• Czech private company 
• 100% owned by ATG (Advanced Technology Group) – Czech company with core business in Non-destructive testing (NDT) 
• Approved EASA Part 21G and Part 145 organizations
• Established in 1995 (almost 25 years of experience in composite business) 
• Expertise in small and medium serious production 
• Staff: 65 employees 
• Turnover: 4.2 mil. EUR 
LAC supplies composite parts to aircraft and helicopters manufacturers in France, Germany, Italy and South Korea.
We take every effort to ensure top quality workmanship and provide individual approach to each customer. 
Our key advantage is our engineering team and scope of activities ranging from prototyping, serial production, tooling, treatment, assembly, finishing and quality control. 

(2) Facilities
LAC is based in Prague (in the aerospace area neighboring ATG’s customers GE Aviation and Latecoere). 
Our facility is equipped with 2 autoclaves, 2 ovens, 5 axis CNC machine and prepreg cutting machines, clean room with control parameters, freezing storage rooms, assembly room and others. 

(3) Core Business and Field of Activities
LAC Core Business is in the aerospace industry. The main capabilities are in the production of structural and interior parts according to technical documentation (as a “Build-to-Print“ manufacturer).
Our key technology is based on prepreg technology with curing in autoclaves. LAC has expertise with various materials in composite production. 
LAC also supplies its customers with additional services such as engineering, production of molds and fixtures, cutting, drilling holes, milling, assembly with metallic parts, rivets, bolts, painting (together with approved supplier), marking, testing etc.
 
LAC Secondary Business is in Maintenance, Repairs and Overhaul (MRO). LAC participates on repairs and upgrades of aircraft composite components for various customers together with ATG (mother company) and its complete NDT service package. 
LAC also conducts several modification of interior parts and the Company introduced new product - so called C-Spacer (class divider) for Boeing 737 cabin with its DOA partner. 
 
Additionally, LAC engineering skills support completely new aircraft structure. 
Together with partners, LAC develops and manufactures prototypes of composite aircraft including composite wings. The Company contributes to making a prototype of advanced civil helicopters with development of composite engine mounts. 
There are more R&D projects (in space industry as well) with involvement of LAC such as state-of-the-art ballistic protection, space applications – shielding, panels, etc. 

(4) Main Customers and Certifications
LAC has more than 15 years of on-going cooperation with Airbus Helicopters. LAC produces fire protection lining across Airbus aircraft family (A320, A320neo, A330, A350, A380). 
These parts are delivered to both Germany and South Korea for final assembly with door structures. For helicopter manufacturers, LAC produces composite bays/covers for both life raft and floatation systems. 
Other customers include: Leonardo Helicopters, Daher, Diehl and Korean Air.
LAC approvals: ISO EN ISO 9001:2015, AS 9100, rev. D, EN 9100:2018, EASA Part 21-G and EASA Part 145
LAC customers approvals: Airbus, Airbus Helicopters, Korean Air, Agusta Westland QRS01, Daher Socata IS18S13, Diehl Aviation

description:
Get2C was founded in 2011, leveraging more than 20 years of experience of its founders and team.
We work in the areas of climate change, energy, carbon markets, climate finance and sustainable development.
We have a global culture and are present in various countries in Europe, Africa and Latin America through our network of partners.

“Develop Smart Projects into a Cooler World” – materializes in the implementation of environmentally, socially and economically sustainable projects that lead us towards a cooler world.

We know it’s a long road and we’ll have to rethink the concept of efficiency in the use of natural resources. We believe that we have to define new patterns of services, consumption, production and behavior so that the concept of “less carbon” is not just a combination of two words. We know that we have to look at problems in an innovative and integrated way in collaboration, cooperation and partnership. Only in this way will we create future value in order to achieve a low-carbon economy.

We know it’s a path we want to take! A path that will lead us to a “Cooler World” with zero emissions by the second half of the century.

According to NASA’s Earth Observatory, the average global temperature on Earth has risen by around 1.04° Celsius since 1880. Two-thirds of the warming has occurred since 1975, at a rate of around 0.15-0.20°C per decade.

Although the results of the Copenhagen conference in 2009 fell short of expectations, it was the first time that the final text recorded the international commitment to a maximum limit of 2 degrees Celsius for the increase in the Earth’s average temperature in the future.

It is in this scenario, in which the average global temperature would rise by a maximum of 2 degrees Celsius, that Get2C drew inspiration. Although the impacts are already negative with this rise, the aim is to minimize them and create opportunities to seriously limit a global temperature increase of more than 2 degrees Celsius.

Get2C is committed to having a culture that involves the best of its employees and helps mobilize external partners. This commitment gives them the opportunity to use their skills, resources and management capacity to drive social progress, engaging with the community and new partners.
We are committed to being a Cool company by fostering an inspiring culture that encourages creativity, keeps employees happy and motivated, and promotes the development of qualities and professional fulfillment balanced with personal life.

Spectro-AI is a pioneering deep-tech company committed to advancing the use of spectral data, with a strong emphasis on space and satellite-based intelligence. Our core mission is to democratize access to high-quality spectral insights by combining cutting-edge hardware with advanced AI-driven software, enabling smarter, faster, and more scalable monitoring solutions.
With roots in research and innovation, we develop and deploy spectral technologies that operate seamlessly across space, aerial (drones), and ground platforms, offering complete and integrated data ecosystems. Spectro-AI’s end-to-end solutions are designed to support a wide range of real-world applications, particularly in the fields of agriculture, safety, and security.
From monitoring crop health and soil composition in real-time, to supporting incident management and environmental compliance, our products like Deep4Sat, Deep4Drone, and Deep4Sat43 deliver precise, high-resolution insights that empower decision-makers across sectors. Our long-term vision is to build a global infrastructure where satellite and drone data play a central role in sustainability, resilience, and strategic operations—from national policy implementation to on-the-ground interventions.

description:
FWR is developing a new generation of electric robotic arms for advanced manipulation and simple deployment in ANY existing environment. Although our robots are supposed to do what electric robots do, and certainly with some enhanced qualities, their distinguishing feature lies in their remote Actuation Box. This box houses all the critical components of the system – electronics, sensors and even electric motors – protecting them from any environmental factors, such as radiations, water, extreme temperatures, flammable gasses and dust (including regolith, why not). Therefore, reliability in challenging environments is unconditionally achieved as:
- the robotic arm is basically a simple, passive, and lightweight structure, free of any delicate/fragile components, and
- the Actuation Box offers effective cooling, shielding and sealing of critical components without affecting the properties of the arm structure (such as weight/inertia, shape/size, design complexity), which would not be possible relying on traditional design approaches.
Although remote actuation architecture can easily be considered as the ideal candidate for achieving reliability in harsh environments, its implementation is not straightforward due to the intrinsic challenges of developing transparent transmission systems capable of transferring the motion of the remote electric motors to the corresponding arm joints. Indeed, no state-of-the-art robot with remote actuation has yet demonstrated a suitable balance of performance, reliability, and low complexity. As a result, scalability, versatile deployment, and mass distribution of this kind of system remain unfeasible, ultimately making the benefits of remote actuation vanish.
With this exact problem in mind, we are developing Fluid Wires – flexible, fluidic transmission systems – presumably the most advanced transmission system for robotics, capable of making robots with remote actuation ready for real-world deployment and industrialization for the first time. Unlike existing transmission systems, Fluid Wires offer near-zero friction, large force-control bandwidth, and high load capacity, combining the efficiency of electric actuation (powering our system from within the box) with the high specific power of hydraulic systems. As a reminder, note that the proposed technology should not be mistaken for traditional hydraulic robots (with pumps, valves, etc.); our robots are fully electric in all aspects, with motors placed remotely and connected via fluidic transmissions. Additionally, considering the low inertia of our robotic arm – an almost empty structure – the proposed architecture enables high dynamic performance, allowing for fast movements with efficiency and good controllability. Moreover, the extreme transparency of Fluid Wires (low friction, high bandwidth) enables the electric motors to also function as torque sensors, eliminating the need for force/torque sensors, which are typically costly and prone to failure. Unlike traditional, highly geared robotic arms, which necessarily require torque or force sensors to implement impedance-control strategies, FWR robots enable sensorless force/impedance control in an accurate, robust, and impact-tolerant manner. This makes them particularly suitable for safe navigation (e.g., inspection, maintenance, assembling, and teleoperation) in unstructured environments. As a final remark, all the favorable characteristics analyzed above are implemented with simplified hardware. Fluid Wires are flexible and can be seamlessly integrated into the robotic structure. The design of the arm and the one of the Actuation Box are decoupled, offering significant design freedom to meet the project requirements, and our architecture is fully modular (with the same design and components applied to every joint), resulting in lower design and manufacturing costs, as well as easy customization.
Performance, safety and reliability, which traditionally belong to different families of robots, are merged here into a unified advanced design paradigm and embedded in smart mechanical structures, without trade-offs.

entityDescription:
Philosophy
GREENBOX's philosophy focuses on creating atmospheric and high-quality open spaces. The firm sees it as its task and responsibility to design open spaces that are not only functional, but also aesthetically pleasing and sustainable. This approach is particularly reflected in the planning and implementation of squares, promenades, parks, and open spaces, which are always integrated into an urban context. GREENBOX places great emphasis on a close connection between architecture and landscape in order to develop holistic and customized solutions for each location. Through intensive dialogue with the relevant stakeholders and a detailed examination of the location where a project is being implemented, open spaces are created that possess a strong identity and optimally meet the needs of the local people.

Strategic Orientation
GREENBOX's vision for the future and strategic direction are strongly aligned with the challenges of a changing society, particularly with regard to the effects of climate change and the increasing demands for sustainable, livable open spaces. The company strives to create competitive advantages through the use of modern, digital technologies and innovative working approaches. A central goal is to further expand internal structures and optimize processes in order to work even more efficiently.GREENBOX is aware of its responsibility to develop long-term, sustainable solutions that meet the needs of people and nature. With openness, curiosity, and creativity, the firm implements projects that offer individual solutions. The integration of digital technologies into the planning process plays a central role in creating holistic solutions. In addition to technical and creative development, GREENBOX places particular emphasis on developing its team. The goal is to be perceived as one of the most attractive employers in the industry by offering employees optimal conditions for their personal and professional development. The focus is on a collegial, appreciative working environment that fosters team spirit.

Core Competencies
GREENBOX's services encompass the entire spectrum of landscape architecture, from urban open space planning and renaturation to greening concepts and stormwater management. The firm supports construction projects from the initial assessment through design and execution planning to construction management. Complex tasks such as cost control and quality management are also handled, which are particularly crucial for large-scale projects with construction costs of more than €10 million for open spaces. Another key component of GREENBOX's work is participation in competitions. The firm views this as an essential building block of a vibrant building culture, in which new ideas and creative approaches are regularly tested and developed further. GREENBOX works in an interdisciplinary manner, collaborating with architects, urban planners, landscape and gardening companies, environmental planners, project developers, and many more, to examine projects from different perspectives and thus develop sustainable and viable concepts.
GREENBOX's main clients include municipalities and public clients, as well as large companies and private investors. The firm operates primarily in Germany, but has also participated in international projects in the past. Through its many years of experience in dealing with large-scale construction projects, GREENBOX has developed a deep understanding of the needs and requirements of cities and municipalities, which is reflected in the high quality of its implemented projects.

description: SensiPhi is an advanced optical fibre sensing company specialising in the design and development of High-Resolution Distributed Acoustic Sensing (HR-DAS) technology. Our core innovation transforms standard optical fibres into dense, large-scale arrays of virtual sensors capable of detecting and localising vibrations and strain with exceptional detail. Using HR-DAS, a single fibre optic cable becomes a continuous sensor capable of capturing vibration data at thousands of points along its length, with each point sampled at rates up to 1 million samples per second (1 MSPS). This level of resolution enables detection of high-frequency acoustic signals, including ultrasonic vibrations, making it a powerful tool for non-destructive testing (NDT) and structural health monitoring (SHM). Because of the fibre’s small size and passive nature, it can be seamlessly embedded into carbon composite structures during manufacturing, enabling real-time, in-situ monitoring without adding significant weight or complexity. This makes the technology especially suitable for aerospace, space structures, and advanced materials research, where performance, reliability, and early fault detection are critical. SensiPhi’s HR-DAS platform supports a wide range of applications, including: Structural integrity monitoring of spacecraft and aircraft, Ultrasonic NDT for defect detection in composite materials, Vibration analysis for launch systems and ground support structures, and Environmental sensing in harsh or remote conditions. By enabling high-resolution, distributed sensing with minimal infrastructure, SensiPhi is redefining the way structures are monitored and understood, paving the way for safer, smarter, and more resilient aerospace systems.

entityDescription: Sapienza boasts a long tradition as a protagonist of international aerospace activities, which began in the 1960s when, thanks to the initiative of a group of professors led by Prof. Luigi Broglio, Italy became the third country in the world, after the United States and Russia, capable of launching a scientific satellite into orbit. Over 100 tenured professors work in this sector at Sapienza, carrying out research in all fields of interest in aerospace, often with excellent results, recognized internationally. The creation of the Sapienza Aerospace Research Center (CRAS), established in June 2008, was therefore essentially motivated by the aim of creating appropriate synergies and providing strong and unitary visibility to the sector. This created an interdepartmental structure for the coordination of research activities that professors carry out mainly in their own departments. Participation in the Center allows for coordinated and synergic operations, as well as providing visibility that goes beyond the boundaries of the individual department, but benefits from the highest representation provided by Sapienza. CRAS boasts important relationships with industrial entities, both Italian and international, and collaborations with public bodies and ministries. In the field of relationships with industrial entities, in addition to the collaborations activated at a national level, the Framework Agreement signed with EADS-Astrium is significant, which will provide our researchers with the opportunity to be included in important European projects.

JTUS is a U.S.-based semiconductor technology company specializing in the research, development, and innovation of advanced communication and signal processing solutions. entityDescription: The HUN-REN Biological Research Centre, Szeged (HUN-REN BRC Szeged) is an outstanding institution of the internationally acknowledged Hungarian biological research. The HUN-REN Biological Research Centre was founded in 1971. The 4 institutes of HUN-REN BRC - the Institutes of Biophysics, Biochemistry, Genetics and Plant Biology - employ about 260 scientists whose work is hall-marked by highly appreciated international scientific publications and patents. The research topics include several fields of molecular and cell biology from the industrial utilization of bacteria through controlled improvement of cultivated plants to the problems of human health and environmental protection. HUN-REN BRC is mainly a scientific basic research centre, but scientists of HUN-REN BRC play an initiative role in the foundation and promotion of biotechnological companies, as well as in educational duties. The successful activity and high-level scientific research pursued in HUN-REN BRC were also acknowledged by the European Molecular Biological Organization (EMBO) and in 2000 the European Union awarded the title of “Centre of Excellence“ to HUN-REN BRC.

As an exclusively health sciences-focused educational and research institution, RCSI is uniquely placed to drive translational research which benefits patients and the community. With a focus on clinical and patient-centered research, we succeed in leading impactful discoveries which address key national and international health challenges. Our research agenda drives scientific breakthroughs, innovations and insights that allow us to understand and respond to changing healthcare needs. Key research areas include: Biomaterials, Medical Devices and Pharmaceutical Sciences; Cancer; Neurological and Psychiatric Disorders; Population Health and Health Services; Surgical Science and Practice; Vascular Biology and Cardiology; Respiratory and Critical Care.

entityDescription:
The Institute of Plant Protection – National Research Institute (IPP – NRI) is a public research unit supervised by the Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development, established on January 24, 1951. The main office of IPP – NRI is located in Poznań and the Branch Office is in Sośnicowice. The Institute also runs three Regional Experiment Stations: in Białystok, Toruń and Rzeszów, as well as a Field Experiment Station and an Agricultural Experiment Station in Winna Góra (Wielkopolska).
The Institute of Plant Protection provides research, implementation, promotion, and other services within the area of plant protection in Poland. The IPP – NRI performs its tasks as part of its statutory activity, financed by the Ministry of Science and Higher Education; the Multiannual Programme, financed by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, and various domestic and foreign projects (grants).
The Institute conducts studies pertaining to biology, harmfulness and methods of pest control, scientific basis of integrated plant protection, plant protection in organic farming, systems supporting decisions on the need to perform treatments, residues and quality of plant protection products, as well as Pest Risk Assessments (PRA). The IPP – NRI units are prepared to conduct research required in the registration process of plant protection products, fertilizers and biostimulators, crop plants, qualitative analysis of crops and risk assessment of pest resistance to plant protection products.
There are a number of well-equipped research units, unique for Poland, operating within the Institute:the Plant Diseases Clinic and Bank of Pathogens– providing services in the field of identification of viral, bacterial and fungal diseases of plants, andthe Research Centre of Quarantine, Invasive and Genetically Modified Organisms – a modern facility that meets the highest standards of phytosanitary safety (SL3). The following are the certified IPP – NRI units, authorized to conduct research on the effectiveness of all types of plant protection products: the Research Centre for Registration of Agrochemicalsin Poznań and the Pesticide Efficacy Testing Departmentin Sośnicowice, where a modern laboratory testing the quality, originality and residues of plant protection products is also operating. Within the Regional Experimental Station in Białystok, operates the Food and Feed Safety Laboratory, which conducts studies mainly on the use of plant protection products in crops for the risk of contamination of crops and food products with residues. The Institute also operates the Expert Centre of the Evaluation of Agrochemical Reports.
The Institute closely cooperates with government institutions, domestic and foreign research and development units, as well as with agricultural advisory centres and agricultural producers.
The Institute is authorised to confer doctoral and postdoctoral degrees in agricultural sciences in the field of agricultural sciences, namely agriculture and horticulture, and to conduct the procedure to confer the title of professor of agricultural sciences. IPP – NRI organises doctoral and postgraduate programmes, scientific sessions, conferences, seminars, workshops and trainings.
The IOR Hotel & Congress Centre– with 14 conference rooms fitted with audio-visual equipment (e.g. for simultaneous interpreting), 125 beds of various standards and attractive catering facilities, is perfect for both work and leisure.

entityDescription:
Csillagváros Kft.is a Hungarian company pioneering in the field of Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) with a strong emphasis on space-oriented crop research and vertical farming innovation.​

Company Overview
Established in 2021, Csillagváros Kft. operates theGrow Stars Institute Living Lab (GSILL), a state-of-the-art research and development facility dedicated to vertical farming and urban agriculture.The GSILL is equipped with five individually controllable vertical farm systems and three small-scale growth cabinets, enabling precise experimentation and cultivation under controlled conditions.​
Research Focus
The company's research extends beyond traditional agriculture, focusing on the cultivation of "colonisation crops"—plants suitable for long-duration space missions and extraterrestrial colonization. These crops, including pak choi, wheat, cabbage, radish, lettuce, parsley, dill, basil, mizuna, and romaine lettuce, are cultivated using technologies similar to those employed in the Veggie system aboard the International Space Station (ISS).​
Collaborations and Recognition
Csillagváros Kft. collaborates with academic and research institutions, such as the University of Debrecen, to advance its biotechnological research. The company's innovative approach has been recognized by its membership in the European Network of Living Labs (ENoLL), highlighting its commitment to open innovation and collaborative research in the CEA domain.

Partners:Csillagváros Kft. partners with theOrion Space Generation Foundation, as well as with academic, governmental, and civil organizations through their Grow Stars Institute Living Lab. Their collaborations extend into the European Network of Living Labs (ENoLL), highlighting their role in open innovation and scientific cooperation.
Objectives:Their main goals include advancingvertical farming and space agriculture, contributing to sustainable food production, supporting space colonization with “colonisation crops,” and integrating AI and circular economy solutions into controlled environment agriculture.

entityDescription:
Xnovo Technology ApS is the commercial result of more than 20 years of Synchrotron and Diffraction-Imaging research at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU).
Driven by an urge to make 3D crystallographic X-ray technology accessible for a wider range of materials scientists, Xnovo Technology ApS was founded in December 2012 by Senior Scientist Erik Mejdal Lauridsen, DTU-Energy Conversion, and Professor Henning Friis Poulsen, DTU-Physics.
The transition from university research into a commercial company was supported by the tech-oriented venture fund Capnova and Vækstforum Sjælland.
The first commercial application of Xnovo’s patent portfolio was the partnership withCarl Zeiss X-ray Microscopy Inc.The 3D crystallographic imaging solutionGrainMapper3D™ was made available as part of the LabDCT™ module on theZEISS Xradia 520 Versa X-ray Microscope mid-2015.
Through close collaborations with leading research institutions, Xnovo seeks to bring state-of-the-art analysis tools to our customers. To this end, we have engaged in a range of collaborative projects, and we are always interested in hearing from new potential partners.

entityDescription: QZabre offers high-performance, turnkey scanning Nitrogen Vacancy (NV) magnetometry microscopes, as well as scanning NV tips, pillar arrays, and custom diamond solutions. Scanning NV is revolutionizing the way magnetic and electric fields are measured at the nanometer scale. Our microscopes and scanning tips enable the quantitative imaging of complex topological structures like skyrmions, traditionally inaccessible antiferromagnetic domains, ultrathin 2D magnets, and cycloids in multiferroic materials. Beyond magnetometry, scanning NV can image current densities, take noise spectra and perform nanoscale thermometry. Since spinning off from ETH Zurich in 2018 we have made this technology widely accessible for academic as well as for industrial applications. We would be happy to discuss with you how scanning NV can help you with your Research. Reach out to us at info@qzabre.com or visit www.qzabre.com for more information

entityDescription: The Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (NCU) was founded in 1945. It is one of the largest universities in Poland, currently comprising 17 faculties (including 3 medical faculties at Collegium Medicum UMK in Bydgoszcz). It provides graduate and postgraduate courses for almost 30 000 students, offering education in over 80 fields of study, 100 specialisations and 50 postgraduate courses. The university employs 4300 staff on both Toruń and Bydgoszcz campuses, over half of whom are academic teachers. NCU alumni now number nearly 200 000. The university participates in student and staff exchange programs at both international (the Erasmus program) and national (the MOST program) levels. It develops studies in cooperation with universities abroad and is currently collaborating with the universities in Angers (economics) and Moscow (history). NCU has state-of-the-art research infrastructure including the National Laboratory of Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics (FAMO), the Center for Quantum Optics and the Interdisciplinary Center for Modern Technologies to name but a few, as well as modern teaching facilities comprising, among others, Collegium Humanisticum and the brand new University Sports Centre. The Centre for Astronomy in Piwnice near Toruń houses a unique 32-meter radio telescope. Spitsbergen (in the Arctic Sea) is home to NCU Polar Station. The university has also organized the Polish Historical Mission at the University of Würzburg. NCU researchers can boast a number of spectacular successes which include, among others, the design and construction of an Optical Coherence Tomography instrument, an ultra-modern device for medical eye examinations. The University Library holds an imposing collection of nearly 3 million printed volumes, periodicals and special collection items. NCU campus hosts the Academic Centre for Arts and Culture ‘Od Nowa’, one of the oldest students’ clubs in Poland. This has contributed to the Nicolaus Copernicus University’s position as one of the five best universities in Poland and it is also the reason why QS World University Ranking has placed NCU in the top 4% of universities in the world.

Nexus is Right Step’s offering for the Space sector, a modular platform to simplify and standardise the use of edge technologies in space research and provide remote monitoring capabilities of astronaut health for space operations. At its core is the ability to quantify musculoskeletal loading using a novel algorithm derived from the osteogenic index and low payload accelerometers. 
For Space Medicine
A holistic platform for remote monitoring of key astronaut health metrics, able to quantify and characterise exercise training programs, identify indicators of deconditioning and provide near real time readouts to support individulisation and adaption of astronaut training programs during long term space missions.
For Life Sciences 
To be the partner of choice for space researchers with a platform that traverses space research environments, simplifying and accelerating the transition of successful research from ground-based studies, through parabolic flight into space. Bridging the gap between research and operations allowing successful research outcomes to be accelerated into both medical operations in space and into clinical settings on earth through a single platform.
entityDescription:
Rightstep is an engineering team specialising in sensor integration, embedded systems, edge computing and applied AI. We design and build complete technology stacks that connect physical devices, collect high-quality data, execute algorithms close to the source and support reliable operation outside conventional cloud environments.
Our work spans embedded firmware, wireless communications, gateway hardware, Linux edge platforms, data pipelines, algorithm deployment and operational software. This allows us to address the full engineering chain—from integrating a new sensor and validating its data, through to running real-time analysis and delivering a system that can be used in research or operational settings.
Nexus N3 is the platform through which these capabilities come together. It provides a modular foundation for connecting sensors, managing distributed devices, deploying algorithms and operating data-driven workflows across laboratories, remote locations and other constrained environments.
We focus on turning research concepts and emerging technologies into dependable systems. That means designing for real hardware, variable connectivity, repeatable deployment, maintainability and the practical requirements of the people who will operate the system.

entityDescription:
Agrobit is an agtech startup that develops digital agriculture solutions and decision support systems (DSS) using crop images collected by optical instruments (smartphones, tractor-mounted cameras, drones). Agrobit's mission is to help farmers and technicians optimize/reduce the use of chemical inputs and water, reducing costs and the social and environmental impacts of agricultural activities, in line with the European Green Deal and the UN sustainability goals.
The flagship product is iAgro, an innovative DSS mobile app that transforms the smartphone into a 3D scanner and precision agriculture tool by exploiting artificial intelligence (AI), augmented reality (AR), computer vision, 3D modeling (digital twin) and cloud computing technologies. The app allows you to obtain biometric and biophysical data of tree crops, export reports, maps and the history of the health status of the field. Using smartphones and AR algorithms, the user performs a 3D scan on the target plant which is then analyzed by computer vision and AI algorithms, creating its 3D model and automatically calculating biometric parameters (thickness, height, canopy volume), vigor parameters (LAI, LWA, TRV) and optimal doses of agrochemicals and water to be distributed in the field. By repeating the scans in multiple points of the field, the app allows you to generate vigor maps (useful for optimizing fertilization) and prescription maps for optimized phytosanitary treatments. The main competitive advantage lies in the quantification of the dose of agrochemical for each area of ​​the field (quantitative DSS) and in making the smartphone a simple, scalable, widespread, economic agronomic tool: crucial factors for the concrete diffusion of precision agriculture practices.
The iAgro app already use GNSS data but new developments are going on like integrating Sentinel-2 EO data to spatialize the app measurements at a higher scale. This approach will be used to calculate firstly crop yields and crop CO2 absorption, using data fusion techniques between iAgro in-field measurements and satellite vegetation indices.

Hüttich Consulting GmbH is an independent consultancy specialising in the analysis and processing of environmental data, with a strong focus on satellite-based Earth observation (EO) services, including Copernicus data and other Big Data sources. Based in Germany, the company supports clients across public authorities, research institutions, and private enterprises in leveraging geospatial information for climate adaptation, environmental monitoring, and sustainable development.
With expertise in processing large-scale environmental datasets, Hüttich Consulting enables decision-makers to transform complex data streams into actionable insights. The company develops customised analysis workflows and advises on the integration of satellite data into operational processes. A key area of focus is the development of innovative business models and services that utilise EO data to address environmental challenges and create value for users.
Hüttich Consulting GmbH offers strategic advisory services, hands-on training, and concept development for data-driven solutions, helping organisations to build capacity and unlock the potential of Earth observation technologies. By bridging the gap between data providers and end-users, the company contributes to the wider adoption of satellite data in practical applications for climate resilience, land use management, and environmental risk assessment.

Biotech PRO ApS was established in Denmark in 2016 with a resource basis covering more than 30 years of professional experience in Bioprocesses covering several technological solutions within thebiomass technology sector, such as biogas plants, biomass liquefaction, a.o. with focus on developing structured, solid, consolidated, robust and economic solutions. 

Biotech PRO’s aim is to address and implement solutions in the fields of next-generation biofuels (fermentation optimization, innovativeconcepts, reactor configurations), bioproducts (new concepts, optimization, customer tailored solutions), biogas solutions (operation, monitoring and optimization), process modelling (predictionmodels within biosystems) and biorefineries (evaluation of concepts, testing, system analysis).

The company has been involved in several projects, among others in EU projects, such as the Fast-track Innovation project, Neosuccess, and in the EU Horizon Cronus. The company has also provided consultancy and design of specific equipment within the bioenergy sector for specific clients and manufacturers. Biotech Pro has extensive expertise in process design, upscaling from lab to pilot to demonstration and to full scale, system analysis and modeling. Biotech Pro was the core contributor to the Anaerobic digestion model “Biomodel”, improving the understanding of AD process inhibition mechnisms, pH balance and dynamic behavior from 1993 and onwards. Experience basis for full scale plant design includes Lemvig, Thorsø and Blaabjerg biogas plants in Denmark as well as numerous other energy plants across the world.

Xiphera, Ltd, based in Finland, designs and implements proven cryptographic security for embedded systems. Our strong cryptographic expertise and extensive experience in digital system design enable us to help our customers to protect their most valuable assets.
We offer secure and highly optimised cryptographic Intellectual Property (IP) cores, designed directly for Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) and Application Specific Integrated Circuits (ASICs) without software components. Our broad, fully in-house designed, and up-to-date portfolio, including implementations of Post-Quantum Cryptography, enables cost-effective development projects with fast time-to-market – providing peace of mind in a dangerous world.
Current ESA activity is related to Authenticated Boot and Hardware Root-of-Trust.

TÜV SÜD Energietechnik GmbH Baden-Wuerttemberg (TÜV SÜD ET) was founded on 1 April 1997 under the name of “TÜV Energie- und Systemtechnik GmbH Baden-Wuerttemberg”. It was a spinoff from the former “Nuclear Technology and Radiation Protection” Division of TÜV Bayern Hessen Sachsen Südwest e.V. The company changed its name to “TÜV SÜD Energietechnik GmbH Baden-Wuerttemberg” with effect from 1 April 2006. It is a legal entity (LE) of the TÜV SÜD Group. The company provides
- advisory, inspection and certification services in the fields of energy technology, systems engineering and nuclear technology as well as
- radiation-protection services.
It does so primarily within its activities as an independent and impartial company of experts, not subject to professional instructions from third parties, which is consulted by the supervisory authorities of the German state of Baden-Wuerttemberg pursuant to Section 20 of the German Atomic Energy Act.
TÜV SÜD AG undertakes to exercise its shareholder rights in TÜV SÜD Energietechnik GmbH Baden-Wuerttemberg only to the effect that the impartiality, independence and technical authority of TÜV SÜD ET to provide its services without being subject to professional instructions by third parties will be guaranteed at all times and that TÜV SÜD ET will be able to fully meet all its responsibilities.
The main field of activity of TÜV SÜD ET lies in the testing and inspection of nuclear facilities within the context of nuclear licensing and/or supervisory procedures. The experts of the company and/or its predecessor organisation have operated in this area from the earliest times of peaceful use of nuclear energy. They can thus draw on over 50 years of experience, in particular with nuclear power stations in Baden-Wuerttemberg.
Since the German government’s 2011 decision to phase out nuclear energy by 2022, TÜV SÜD ET has stepped up its efforts to use its know-how in contracts located abroad or placed by international companies, e.g. manufacturers of nuclear components. This business line, while still under development at present, is to be expanded further by the development of new products and the establishment of a sales structure.

entityDescription:
The Institute of Human Genetics, Polish Academy of Sciences (IHG PAS) was founded in 1974, and until 2003 operated under the name of the Department of Human Genetics, PAS.
The Institute has the right to confer doctoral degrees (since 2002) and habilitations (since 2010) in the field of medical sciences in the discipline of medical biology and postdoctoral medical sciences in the discipline of medical biology.
The Institute is the leading centre for human genetics research in Poland and a valued partner in scientific cooperation with many institutions in the country and abroad.
The main research areas of the Institute include molecular genetics, cytogenetics, cellular pathology, cancer genetics, and reproductive biology. In recent years, the Institute has also been developing innovative fields such as transgenesis, epigenetics, genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics. The genetic research conducted at the Institute not only focuses on expanding fundamental knowledge but also finds practical applications in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases through extensive collaboration with medical institutions.

NEXOFAB™ is a cutting-edge clean-tech and deep-tech company specializing in the development of sustainable, high-performance building systems for a variety of industries, including construction, defense, and aerospace. Our innovative approach combines advanced manufacturing technologies like LSAM (Large Scale Additive Manufacturing), FDM (Fused Deposition Modeling), and CFAM (Continuous Fiber Additive Manufacturing) to produce efficient, eco-friendly building components and solutions.
At the core of NEXOFAB™'s mission is the creation of modular, energy-efficient, and scalable structures that contribute to the reduction of CO2 emissions, reduce material waste, and optimize production processes. Our focus is on enhancing the construction industry’s sustainability and performance by offering lightweight, customizable, and cost-effective solutions that meet the demands of both temporary and permanent structures.
Through the use of LSAM, we are able to create large-scale parts with exceptional precision and scalability. FDM is employed for rapid prototyping and small-scale production, enabling quick iteration and testing of complex designs. Additionally, CFAM integrates continuous fibers into the additive manufacturing process, providing superior strength, durability, and performance in parts for high-demand applications.
NEXOFAB™ is committed to revolutionizing the way we build, utilizing advanced technologies and innovative materials to deliver scalable, energy-efficient, and environmentally responsible solutions. With a focus on both R&D and market expansion, we aim to lead the transition to a more sustainable future in the built environment, defense, and aerospace sectors.

AstaZero AB is a leading research facility in the field of automated and connected transport systems, operating a full-scale independent test environment for future automated transport systems. This support extends through the entire verification and validation process, ensuring that advanced safety systems function correctly in various traffic situations.
AstaZero maintains a digital twin of their proving ground, which is based on fused lidar, camera, and GNSS data. Additionally, we conduct accredited testing for UNECE requirements and Euro NCAP active safety rating tests, including AD grading and truck testing.

Cesbio is a public research laboratory which aims to better understand the functioning of continental surfaces and their interactions with climate and humans. Remote sensing is heavily used by Cesbio scientists to monitor the evolution of the planet at various scales and develop models to tackle societal challenges on biodiversity, climate change, food security, water resources, etc. The laboratory also contributes to the development and promotion of Earth Observation by participating in the definition, implementation and scientific exploitation of space missions.
CESBIO is a joint research unit with:

- National Center for Scientific Research (CNRS)
- Research Institute for Development (IRD)
- University Toulouse 3 Paul Sabatier (UT3)
- National Institute of Research for agriculture, food and environment (INRAE)
CESBIO is part of the Midi Pyrénées Observatory.

entityDescription: Our private company entitled EDGE - «EDGE IN EARTH OBSERVATION SCIENCES» was established by statute on 25/09/2018 with base in Athens, Greece. EDGE is a Research and Consulting company focusing in integrating cutting-edge approaches and technologies, to provide international stakeholders with optimized operational tools and policy-makers with efficient and synthetic information towards fulfilling the aspirations of major global agreements, such as the Sendai Framework on Disaster Risk Reduction, the Paris Agreement and the 2030 Agenda and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals. Some of the sectors that we focus on: Disasters: Monitoring disastrous phenomena before and after an event, including flood modelling, flood extent monitoring and mapping, flood modelling, geophysical hazards, monitoring of critical infrastructure, early warning of vector transmitted diseases as well as designing the appropriate mitigation measures. description:
Martel is a dynamic digital innovation agency with 30 years’ experience empowering organisations across Europe and worldwide throughout their journey from novel ideas to technological implementation, media and market strategy. 
After more than two hundred cutting-edge projects, Martel has grown from its origins as a small consulting agency into a thriving organisation with offices in Switzerland and in the Netherlands. 
Building on its foundation in the management of European Commission funded projects and EU consulting, Martel’s business has diversified to include research and development activities in several advanced domains, but also a broad palette of communication, marketing, media and training services. With a skilled and passionate international team, Martel helps its customers and partners achieve ambitious innovation goals in an impactful and sustainable way. 
Martel offers support and guidance spanning from securing funds and providing expertise in selected ICT domains, to strategic communication, marketing and engagement plans. Martel also offers dedicated training on European funding rules and mechanisms, on media and communication for science and technology, and on advanced topics in Cloud Computing, Edge Computing, Internet of Things, Artificial Intelligence, Non-Terrestrial-Networks, Network Virtualisation and open-source Software Engineering.

entityName: SIQ (Slovenian Institute for quality and metrology)
description:
SIQ is a professional, independent, and impartial institution that provides comprehensive solutions in the fields of product testing and certification, management system assessment, metrology, and education. The international recognition and professional level of our work are confirmed by numerous accreditations and memberships in international certification schemes and associations. We are a notified body for seven directives and two regulations. Our team consists of 184 employees and over 350 external expert collaborators, ensuring a high level of expertise and competence in standardization, inspection, testing, control, and verification. 
The entire list of accreditations and technical competences can be found on following link: https://www.siq.si/en/about-us/competences/

We actively conduct testing and compliance assessments for products and components across various industries, including automotive, medical, electronics, machinery, and laboratory and measurement equipment. More than 100 highly qualified testing engineers perform daily tests in electrical safety, electromagnetic compatibility, radio measurements, and climatic/mechanical impacts. Within our accredited scope, we cover more than 500 different standards and are part of international certification schemes, meaning our reports have global recognition. In terms of the number of issued international certificates, we rank in the top quarter of testing laboratories worldwide.
(https://www.siq.si/en/our-services/testing-and-certification-of-products/about-us/)

We conduct assessments and certifications of processes, organizations, and companies according to various international ISO standards. We cover a wide range of areas, including quality management systems (ISO 9001, AQAP), information security management systems (ISO 27001, ISO 22301), environmental management (ISO 14001), energy management systems (ISO 50001), and more. SIQ is an accredited body for management system certification and carbon footprint verification. Our certification portfolio also includes NATO AQAP standards for quality management. (https://www.siq.si/en/our-services/organization-certification/about-us/)

Additionally, in our offering there are also calibration services for various measuring equipment, ranging from simple scales and gauges to voltage/current meters and complex high-frequency devices for measuring radio interference and electromagnetic waves. Our department also engages in strong research activities, focusing on the development of new measurement methods and procedures, and we regularly participate in European development projects. (https://www.siq.si/en/our-services/calibration-and-inspection/about-us/)

As a hub of expertise and competencies, we have established a training department that provides professional education, competence development, and training in various technical fields. We offer specialized training programs in information security, quality management, and management systems. (https://www.siq.si/en/training/about-us/)

In our scope we also provide cybersecurity services, including penetration testing, security assessments of networks, applications, and systems, as well as audit reviews and compliance assessments based on various standards and regulations. Within our accredited scope, we conduct security evaluations of connected (IoT) devices.
(https://www.siq.si/en/our-services/information-technologies/overview/)

Furthermore, we have a dedicated department for testing and verifying equipment intended for installation in potentially explosive environments, ensuring compliance with European regulations. (https://www.siq.si/en/our-services/explosion-protection/about-us/)

entityDescription:
AndroMach is a pioneering French aerospace company developing autonomous spaceplanes to enable in-orbit manufacturing and advanced research in microgravity. Our mission is to provide a cost-effective and reusable platform for producing high-value materials in space while accelerating access to microgravity for scientific and industrial applications. 
Our flagship product is an automated orbital shuttle (100kg payload), designed to serve as a fully reusable in-space manufacturing platform. This vehicle will enable the production of high-value-added materials in LEO and return them to Earth efficiently. By leveraging automation and reusability, we aim to revolutionize space-based production, unlocking new opportunities in medicine and advanced materials manufacturing.
To pave the way for this vision, AndroMach is developing a suborbital demonstrator that will validate key technologies required for the orbital shuttle. This vehicle will be capable of taking off and landing on a runway while offering a phase of microgravity (5min), a capability never before realized. The demonstrator will serve as a testbed for flight systems, aerodynamics, and propulsion, while also offering commercial opportunities for short-duration microgravity experiments and aerospace technology validation (10-30kg payload).

entityDescription: We are a pre-revenue medical device company incorporated in Calgary, Canada in July 2018. entityDescription:
Deep Breathe is an advanced AI-driven medical diagnostics organization specializing in automated screening and early detection of serious respiratory conditions. Our technology is designed to enhance clinical decision-making by leveraging artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms to analyze medical imaging and other diagnostic inputs with high accuracy and efficiency.
In the context of space exploration and long-term human inhabitation of extraterrestrial environments, Deep Breathe plays a crucial role in addressing respiratory health risks unique to aerospace conditions. Our research and technological solutions are particularly relevant to:
Pulmonary effects of celestial dust exposure: Astronauts and space inhabitants are at risk of lung inflammation and fibrosis due to prolonged exposure to fine dust particles on planetary surfaces such as the Moon and Mars. Deep Breathe’s AI-driven screening tools can detect early signs of dust-induced pneumoconiosis and fibrosis, enabling timely interventions.

Pneumothorax risk from barometric pressure changes: Rapid decompression events and extended exposure to microgravity environments pose a heightened risk of lung collapse (pneumothorax), particularly during extravehicular activities (EVA) or pressurized cabin failures. Our AI diagnostic models are trained to recognize subtle radiological markers associated with pneumothorax, ensuring real-time risk assessment and early intervention protocols.

Pneumonia and respiratory infections in space habitats: As humans venture into long-duration spaceflight and planetary colonies, the potential for infectious respiratory conditions increases due to altered immunity, closed-loop life support systems, and microbial changes in space environments. Deep Breathe’s automated diagnostic systems enhance early pneumonia detection through imaging and biosensor data, supporting efficient onboard medical treatment strategies.

Deep Breathe’s AI-driven solutions offer a non-invasive, rapid, and highly scalable method for monitoring and diagnosing aerospace-specific respiratory conditions, providing a critical toolset for space agencies, commercial spaceflight operators, and planetary habitation planners. By integrating our technology into remote and autonomous healthcare solutions for space, we contribute to proactive health management, mission safety, and the long-term sustainability of human space exploration.
As a leader in automated diagnostics for pulmonary health, Deep Breathe aligns with ESA’s objectives to enhance astronaut health, mitigate mission risks, and develop robust medical infrastructures for deep-space missions. Our work represents a fundamental step toward self-sufficient healthcare systems for interplanetary exploration and settlement.

entityName: Leibniz Centre for Tropical Marine Research (ZMT) GmbH
entityDescription:
The Leibniz Centre for Tropical Marine Research (ZMT) is Germany-wide the only and unique research institute for the study of tropical marine ecosystems and their services to human societies.
The mission of ZMT is to provide a scientific basis for the protection and sustainable use of tropical coastal ecosystems by conducting research, capacity development and consulting activities in close cooperation with international and national partners. Those activities are rooted in an impact-oriented inter- and transdisciplinary approach, integrating social and natural sciences.
As one of the first research institutes in Germany, ZMT, from its very beginning in 1991, genuinely brought together the key disciplines for the holistic assessment of marine resource use and management in the tropics. Today, ZMT continues to play a leading role in the integration of social and natural science approaches, as well as transdisciplinary stakeholder involvement processes bridging the science-practice gap.
With its inter- and transdisciplinary approach to the study of tropical coastal systems, ZMT has earned a special position within the German marine research environment and plays a vital role in setting the agenda for coastal science cooperation between Germany and partner countries in the tropics.
The Articles of Association (Gesellschaftsvertrag) lay out the mission of ZMT as follows:
- fundamental scientific research in priority areas of tropical marine ecology and related fields
- scientific assessment of applied projects in the field of tropical marine ecology and related areas
- academic education and training in Germany and tropical countries
- transfer of research results
- provision of expert scientific advice
- advice in particular to the Free Hanseatic City of Bremen and the Federal Government on issues of marine research, especially its expansion and development as well as on matters of scientific cooperation with countries in the tropics
ZMT regards its mission as a great responsibility to conduct excellent research and to sustain its credibility. Its institutional culture is determined by self-responsibility, transparency, respect, reliability and an eye-level communication.

entityDescription:
Genoplant Research Institute is a non-profit organization focused on developing portable laboratory technologies for the upstream and downstream space industry. Our work integrates advanced biotechnology with space exploration, enabling research that supports both terrestrial agriculture and extraterrestrial habitats. Supported by the European Space Agency, we launched the Genoplant Analyzer in 2023, a compact laboratory system designed for greenhouse operators and farmers, providing real-time monitoring, disease detection, and plant health analysis to enhance agricultural efficiency and resilience.
Expanding into orbital research in 2024, we developed MayaSat-1, a biological incubator CubeSat designed to transport hundreds of biosamples to low Earth orbit as part of the Mission Possible program. This initiative investigates the effects of microgravity, radiation, and spaceflight on biological systems, generating critical data for space agriculture, life sciences, and biomedical research. Understanding these effects is essential for developing sustainable food production in space and supporting long-duration human missions.

Genoplant Research Institute also applies its expertise to terrestrial challenges, developing biotechnology solutions for plant resilience, food security, and adaptation to extreme environments. Our research bridges space-based and Earth-based agricultural developments, ensuring cross-disciplinary advancements that benefit both fields. In parallel, we actively engage in educational outreach, collaborating with universities, research institutions, and schools to provide hands-on learning experiences in space biosciences.
Our long-term vision is to develop laboratory platforms for future space stations, planetary bases, and deep-space missions, enabling continuous biological research in extraterrestrial environments. Through strategic partnerships with space agencies, industry, and academia, we are advancing the frontiers of space biosciences, laying the groundwork for sustainable human presence beyond Earth.

entityDescription:
The Kinotex technology was originally developed on behalf of NASA, who was looking for a collision detection sensor for robotic manipulators in space, i.e., for the International Space Station (ISS). 
KINOTEX® is a registered trademark and was patented by the Canadian Space Agency. 
The Kinotex pressure/displacement sensor utilizes a novel sensing principle based on deformation of an “optical integrating cavity”. The integrating cavity is normally a virtual space in an isotropic scattering medium, for example in polymer foams such as silicone or urethane. A simple optical transducer can sense the change in energy intensity in and around an illuminated integrating cavity. Deformation of the foam by an external force results in a change of the integrating cavity and thus a change in the optical properties results in a localized change of the illumination energy intensity. This change is measured. 
Sensitivity and compliance can be engineered to meet a broad range of requirements. There are nearly no constraints on the dimensions of the foam and almost any polymer material can be used. So fare polyurethane, latex and silicone foams have been the primary materials used. The physical properties of the foam can be selected to match the desired application. It can be open cell or closed cell, force resilient or a friable, energy-absorbing foam. The compression hardness can vary from soft to firm. Another advantage of the technology is that sensors can be manufactured in arbitrary shapes and dimensions. The number of tactile-cells (taxel) can vary from a single point sensor up to hundreds for a floor or medical bed sensor. 
 
Sensor devices can be configured to sense pressure from as low as 0.1 kPa to over 200 kPa and can sense deformation as minute as 0.025mm up to many mm with a sub-millisecond response. 
Being an optical technology KINOTEX devices are non-conducting, non-corrosive and immune to EMI/EMC. Operating temperatures can range from –90°C to over 240°C depending on the choice of materials.

entityDescription:
Nature Balance, z.s. is an environmental non-profit organization dedicated to the active protection of landscapes, the implementation of nature-based solutions, and engaging the public in the stewardship of nature and the environment. We are environmentalists, geographers, and geoinformatics specialists, but also hands-on practitioners who are not afraid to take up a scythe, saw, or spade to implement conservation measures directly in the field. We bridge scientific expertise with practical landscape management, perceiving the landscape in its spatial and ecological context. By integrating research with real-world applications, we contribute to preserving landscape diversity and natural heritage.

Our work is built on five key pillars:

1. Landscape and Ecosystem Restoration:We develop and implement sustainable solutions for soil, water, and biodiversity conservation directly in the field.
2. Geodata and Technology:Utilizing satellite imagery, drones, GIS, and analytical tools, we monitor landscapes and uncover ecological interconnections.
3. Education and Outreach:We organize workshops, excursions, and lectures for professionals and the public.
4. Research and Innovation:In collaboration with universities and research institutions, we engage in scientific projects and translate research findings into practical landscape solutions.
5. Cultural and Natural Heritage Conservation:We view the history of landscapes as a key to their restoration and sustainable management.

At Kayadaga, we bring over 25 years of specialized expertise in understanding and monitoring the complex relationships between landscape changes and water resources. Led by Dr. J. Schellekens, our team combines cutting-edge satellite technology with deep hydrological knowledge to support organizations in their landscape restoration initiatives.
Our foundation is built on extensive international experience, from tropical forests in Puerto Rico to reforestation projects in Slovenia, giving us unique insights into how landscape changes affect local and regional hydrology. We've successfully guided governments, NGOs, and companies worldwide in understanding and managing the hydrological impacts of their land use decisions.
What sets us apart is our pioneering approach to combining traditional hydrological expertise with modern satellite technology. Having worked with leading organizations like Planet Labs, Deltares, and various international research institutions, we offer sophisticated monitoring solutions that help you track and understand the effects of your landscape restoration projects in real-time.
Whether you're concerned about flood risks, drought management, or the long-term success of your restoration efforts, our team provides the scientific rigor and practical experience needed to support your environmental initiatives. We specialize in:
Analyzing hydrological consequences of landscape restoration

Assessing how land cover changes impact flood and drought patterns

Implementing tailored monitoring systems for restoration projects

Delivering actionable insights for adaptive management strategies

description:
Interstellar Mapping specialise in lunar thermal mapping and dual-use water extraction systems. Interstellar Mapping's team have extensive experience in lunar remote sensing, environment and 4-dimensional mapping, coupled with decades of engineering onsite experience working on natural resource projects in remote and harsh environments. This experience allows our team to utilise best practices from Earth based applications and apply them to lunar, providing solutions that reduce clients R&D costs, reduces operational risk, and improves the visibility of the lunar environment and geology.
Capabilities include:
• 4-dimensional thermal mapping of the entire Moon.
• Perform thermal site assessments for lunar equipment and components.
• Remotely locate critical lunar resources, including lunar volatile ice stability maps.
• Identify areas on the Moon that can support lunar volatiles that can impact human life.
• Develop large scale sub-surface geological analysis on the Moon.
• Create lunar operational risk assessments.

entityDescription:
The mission of the Future Farming Initiative (FFI) is to leverage the convergence of technology and biology to create innovative, sustainable solutions that address the challenges of diminishing natural resources and climate change. FFI aims to transform various industries by harnessing nature's design principles and manufacturing capabilities through a new approach called Nature Co-Design. Nature Co-Design represents a groundbreaking response to the needs of a fast-changing world, providing an innovative model that no longer considers nature as a resource to be exploited, but rather as a partner to be enhanced by applying design principles inspired by nature itself. The synergy between disciplinary fields such as biology, chemistry, materials science and nanotechnology will enable an excellent heuristic for the development of revolutionary innovations using nature as a manufacturing platform at the molecular level. This initiative aspires to make significant contributions to economic growth and sustainability by fostering a robust ecosystem for research and development.
Key aspects of the Future Farming Initiative's mission include: Advancing Nature Co-Design: FFI focuses on integrating advanced technologies with biological processes to develop sustainable and resource-efficient innovations. This approach is expected to disrupt industries such as agriculture and food supply, advanced materials, pharmaceuticals & nutraceuticals, manufacturing, chemicals; Promoting Sustainability:The initiative emphasizes the creation of environmentally sustainable solutions that are financially viable. This involves designing ecosystems that leverage renewable energy and minimize waste; Executing Market-Inspired R&D: FFI concentrates on developing market-ready research projects based on promising intellectual property (IP) and transferring these innovations to industrial partners or startups.4.Building a Collaborative Ecosystem: The initiative fosters a federated model that shares laboratory facilities and research platforms with global academic and research organizations, enhancing the pool of competencies and potential synergies. FFI's activities are centred around eight key R&D domains that align with the principles and objectives of Nature Co-Design. FFI research domanins focus on the following areas: Innovative Farming; Food Revolution; Space solutions; Bio-Materials; Breeding and Hacking; Bio-factories; Ecosystem Restoration and Circular Bio-Economy.

entityDescription:
Landscape Research Institute (Výzkumný ústav pro krajinu)

is a leading scientific institution in the Czech Republic, dedicated to interdisciplinary research in landscape ecology, environmental sustainability, and climate change adaptation. The institute integrates cutting-edge scientific knowledge with practical applications to develop innovative solutions for sustainable land use, biodiversity conservation, and ecosystem restoration.With a strong focus on geospatial analysis, remote sensing, and environmental data modeling, the institute plays a key role in advancing landscape research at national and international levels. Its expertise extends to ecosystem services assessment, nature-based solutions, land-use planning, and environmental impact assessment. The institute actively collaborates with research organizations, governmental bodies, and private stakeholders across Europe to support evidence-based policymaking and sustainable development.Equipped with state-of-the-art technologies, including GIS, remote sensing tools, and ecological monitoring systems, the institute provides expert consultancy, applied research, and strategic guidance for public and private sector partners. Through participation in international research programs, such as Horizon Europe and ESA-related projects, the institute contributes to the development of resilient landscapes and sustainable resource management, aligning with global environmental and climate goals.

entityDescription:
Montsecure was founded by David Rupprecht and Katharina Kohls in October 2022 as a university spin-off from Ruhr University in Bochum and Radboud University in Nijmegen. At Montsecure, we aim to eliminate the complexity of 5G and strive to make 5G security accessible by providing the propertools,trainingandresearch. We want to empower our customers to create a secure mobile network for the current generation of 5G, 6G and beyond.
Our main product, SEAL, is a tool that assesses mobile network security. It allows for testing vulnerabilities and simulating attacks in a 5G core network. It implements the 3GPP testing standard, making it suitable for the product evaluation schemes GSMA NESAS and BSI NESAS-CCS-GI. The tool offers fast testing cycles and an easy-to-use command line interface. It can be integrated into an existing test environment (CI/CD) for rapid development.
Currently, we see the following areas of application for SEAL to test the vulnerabilities of your network:
-Vendors:Easily integrate SEAL into development pipelines to meet security standards, ensuring compliance and providing actionable reports for improvements.
-Certification & Test Facilities:Simplifies complex 3GPP test cases, enabling easy NESAS and NESAS-CCS-GI certification without deep 5G security expertise.
-Mobile Network Operators (MNOs):Automates security testing in virtualized environments, delivering actionable reports for internal teams and auditors.
-Integrators:Verifies 5G campus network security, ensuring encryption and compliance, giving customers confidence in their network's safety.

The Fraunhofer IZI develops, optimizes and validates methods, materials and products within the business fields cell and gene therapy, drugs and vaccines, molecular diagnostics and immunodiagnostics, as well as extracorporeal therapies. Its areas of competence lie in cell biology, immunology, drug biochemistry, bioanalytics and bioproduction as well as process development and automation. Research in these areas is centered around developments in immuno-oncology and infectious disease pathology. The S3 safety laboratory allows research and development activities to be conducted and highly pathogenic agents investigated under biosafety level 3 conditions.
The institute works in close cooperation with hospital institutions and performs quality tests besides manufacturinginvestigational medicinal products in line with GMP requirements. Furthermore, it supports partners in developing processes for the pharmaceutical production of ATMPs and biologicals, for example by helping them to obtain manufacturing licenses.

IRIAF has eight agricultural research centers in operation throughout the region, each focusing on a specific area of agricultural and livestock production.

We are a fabless semiconductor company that designs hardware components (IPs) for the backbone of on-chip data management and interconnect infrastructure.
Our vision is to revolutionize computing with our innovative solutions for scalable System-on-Chip.
We deliver high-performance, efficient and reliable IP solutions that enable our clients to build SoCs targeting demanding AI and HPC applications.
We design and develops 3 products: HomeNode IP, Network-on-Chip (NoC) IP, Cache IP.Our products (IPs) solve the complex challenges of scaling up the processor chips with an increasing number of cores and accelerators that operate on large amounts of data, improving energy efficiency while maintaining high reliability which is crucial for computing in space. 
We sell our IPs to chip vendors to reduce their time-to-market and lower product development costs and risks by providing verified IP blocks that can be customized to their needs.

The team consists of 2 Professors and 4 Researchers who have researched and worked on our IPs since 2019. 
Together we have more than 100 person-years of R&D in computer architecture, interconnection networks, and hardware design & verification.

Consequent implementation of innovations from research results directly at the company partners and thus acceleration of product development
