entityDescription:
RADMOR is synonymous with reliable communication and secure data transfer on the modern battlefield, which is a key element of success for every military mission. As a technological leader in innovation, RADMOR has been supporting the defense sector for over 70 years by providing world-class advanced VHF FM mobile radio communication equipment.

The company's flagship products are specialist military radios for tactical communication manufactured by the experienced RADMOR engineering team, which have been successfully used for years by the armed forces of Poland and other countries such as the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Algeria, Nigeria, Malaysia, Morocco, Bangladesh, Indonesia and others. RADMOR also supplies mobile radio sets for armored patrol cars, handheld devices and civilian radios, including TETRA and DMR digital communication systems. The company is also involved in a number of European research programs.

One of them is the ESSOR (European Secure Software Defined Radio) program, which aims to develop a standard for European programmable radio, enabling cooperation between military communication systems of different EU countries. Thanks to its participation in the program, RADMOR has knowledge and experience in implementing and using the ESSOR HDR waveform, as well as SDR platforms. This has enabled the design and production of modern Polish military radios, ensuring the highest level of security of transmitted information. Solutions designed by RADMOR are used not only in the defense sector - the company flexibly adapts to market needs and responds to current customer needs, introducing solutions for the civilian sector to its offer. Among the users of RADMOR's innovative communication and communication tools are also uniformed services, energy, aviation and logistics industries.

entityDescription:
Higher education in civil engineering in Romania was founded in 1864, in Bucharest by setting up a "School of Bridges and Roads, Mines and Architecture" which, in 1867 became the "School of Bridges, Roads and Mines" and "the National School for Bridges and Roads" in 1888. In 1921, the "National School of Bridges and Roads" became the "Polytechnic School of Bucharest", where the engineers' training was carried out in the Engineering Department which, in 1938, came to be known as the Faculty of Civil Engineering. 
In 1948, following an Education Reform, the Faculty of Civil Engineering was separated from the Polytechnic School (which became the Polytechnic Institute) and became an independent higher education institution, called the Civil Engineering Institute of Bucharest. Starting with the academic year 1994-1995, the Civil Engineering Institute of Bucharest became The Technical University of Civil Engineering of Bucharest.

entityDescription:
ENVIROPLAN S.A. is an independent private consulting firm that was founded in Athens/Greece in 1990. The office provides a variety of Technical Consulting, Engineering & Project Management Services and is specialized in Environmental Management & Engineering Projects, with extended activities in many EU Member States, candidate states and other countries; Our activity extends to the Balkans (North Macedonia, Croatia, Serbia, Albania, Kosovo, Montenegro), Turkey, the Eastern Partnership Countries (Ukraine, Armenia, Georgia, Azerbaijan), the Mena Region (Lebanon, Palestine, Jordan, Egypt), the Middle East and Central Asia.
Our business model, developed in the past 20 years, consists of marketing the whole range of our services in a local market level, while we target to selected environmental services (mainly for solid waste and water/wastewater) at an international market level. The head offices of the company are in Athens/Greece and in order to run the international activities the company has also established a network of regional branch offices at Thessaloniki/Greece, Larnaca/Cyprus, Bucharest/Romania, Skopje/North Macedonia and Ankara /Turkey where we have also been registered for Turkish branch, under the name ‘ENVIROPLAN S.A. ANKARA MAIN BRANCH in TURKEY’. ENVIROPLAN’s network of strategically located offices enables us to provide timely responses and innovative, cost-effective solutions.
ENVIROPLAN’s mission is to provide specialised high level, professional services in the international market. We aspire to be a progressive consultancy firm in both local and international level, offering innovative, state of the art, environmental management services and solutions. Utilizing our long-term know-how, quality management and business policy, we aim to provide our clients with the services necessary to address their environmental needs in a safe and cost-effective manner. Our vision is to actively contribute to the creation of a sustainable future by maintaining a safe, healthy, and cleaner environment, in balance with economic development and social prosperity.
The firm is internationally recognized for its high level of expertise and has successfully elaborated up to date multiple projects covering many disciplines and providing a wide range of services. ENVIROPLAN has adopted a philosophy of multidisciplinary approach of the technical and environmental subjects, occupying more than 80 scientists and engineers from various disciplines. With innovative ideas, long term know-how and modern data processing techniques, ENVIROPLAN is capable and qualified to work on large projects and complex problems of environmental protection and sustainability.

entityName: GeoAtributo - Consultadoria e Informação para o Planeamento e Ordenamento do Território, Lda.
entityDescription:
GeoAtributo is a company specializing in studies and projects related to analysis, design, evaluation, and implementation in strategic planning, spatial management and urbanism, environment, and sustainable development.
We offer integrated services that provide effective and innovative solutions to the challenges these areas present, primarily focusing on territorial planning and development at the municipal level. A core strength of our work lies in our expertise in geographic information systems (GIS) and information-dependent technologies. Our focus is on strategic planning implemented through territorial and sectoral action plans.
Founded on 2003, GeoAtributo has operated continuously, primarily serving public entities.
Our multidisciplinary team leverages information technologies (IT), particularly GIS, to meet the evolving demands of an increasingly complex and interconnected market. This focus ensures quality and fosters long-term client relationships. Our team comprises permanent technicians and consultants with diverse higher education backgrounds, including environment, landscape architecture, law, civil engineering, forest engineering, geography, geology, mobility, civil protection, information systems, and urbanism.
With over two decades of experience, GeoAtributo possesses extensive expertise in preparing studies, plans, and projects with significant territorial impact. GeoAtributo maintains a Quality Management System (QMS) certified under NP EN ISO 9001:2015, covering ""Consultancy in Planning and Spatial Management, Emergency Planning, and Climate Change."" This QMS reinforces our commitment to service quality and client satisfaction. We also conduct Research, Development, and Innovation (R&D) activities related to the design and development of products and services in spatial management, emergency planning, and thematic cartography.

entityDescription:
Delta Reality (founded in 2009 under the name Diversitas IT sustavi d.o.o. in Zagreb, Croatia,https://deltareality.com/) is a Virtual & Augmented Reality studio with experience in numerous industries with over 200 projects!

As a team, we challenge industry standards, striving to comprehend the reasons behind existing practices and explore opportunities for improvement. We are enthusiastic about integrating various XR disciplines into a single project to forge compelling and impactful experiences.

We prioritize simplicity and tailored user experiences, guaranteeing that our XR solutions are accessible and effortless for all users. Additionally, we pride ourselves on surpassing expectations with each implementation, advancing limits, and providing astonishing experiences.

Our full service approach supports clients from the point of ideation to deployment, covering:

- Production Management
- Quality Assurance
- Software development
- 3D modeling & animation
- Design & Illustration
- Discovery and creative ideation
- Various multidisciplinary experts

We have a lot of experience with implementing VR/AR/XR solutions into:
- industry projects (our clients are companies such as Linde, Frauscher. Siemens, Vailant, Walt Disney, MIT, Samsung, T-Com, MasterCard, etc),
- European Defence Fund 2024 project proposal "CARGO HAWK - Combat Aerial Reconnaissance and Goods Operator for Heavy-duty Aerial Warfare Kit",
- EU projects such as “XR Communication and Interaction Through a Dynamically Updated Digital Twin of a Smart – DIGIPHY” project with University of Zagreb - Faculty of Electrical Engineering And Computing and Ericsson Nikola Tesla d.d. Croatia. 
The goal of the DIGIPHY project is to research and design technologies that enable immersive and intuitive eXtended Reality (XR) inter-personal communication and interaction, as well as the remote presence and interaction of persons and objects in the visual representation of a dynamically updated digital twin (DT), spatially and temporally synchronized with a physical smart space (equipped with sensors and actuators). Prototype XR-applications will be developed for two case studies, to be tested and validated in a 5G network in the laboratory prototype. 
Link:https://muexlab.fer.hr/muexlab/digiphy
Regarding drone solutions Delta Reality had the opportunity to work on the Drone Racing League Simulator and AI Robotic Racing Simulator,which enabled us cooperation with Lockheed Martin in the part of creating a simulator on which AIRR competitors tested their solutions. Also, one of the founders of the company, Mr. Vedran Škarica, is the holder of 1 patent and co-author of 4 patents within Drone Racing League (https://patents.justia.com/assignee/drone-racing-league-inc).

Mission & Vision
Immersea Srl is a pioneering technology company specializing in thedigitalization of marine environments and submerged cultural heritage. Through innovative solutions, the company aims toenhance accessibility to underwater ecosystems, making them more understandable and immersive for the public, researchers, and stakeholders.
Core Business Areas
Immersea Srl operates in multiple technological domains, including:
- Marine Environmental Monitoring– Development of cutting-edge solutions for underwater biodiversity assessment, including e-DNA detection systems.

- Submerged Cultural Heritage Digitalization– Creation of 3D models and immersive experiences for archaeological sites and marine protected areas.

- Advanced Visualization Technologies– Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) applications for museums, tourism, and scientific dissemination.

- Remote Sensing & Mapping– Integration of underwater optical mapping and Earth Observation (EO) data for high-precision environmental assessments.

- Scientific Research & Innovation– Collaboration with universities and research institutions to drive technological advancements in marine science.

Key Technologies & Innovations
- e-DNA Sampling & Analysis: Development of filters applicable to DPV/ROV systems for direct in-situ water sampling.

- 3D Underwater Mapping: Optical imaging and digital reconstruction of submerged environments.

- Telemetry & Positioning (Dead Reckoning): Precision tracking of data collection points.

- Data Management Software: AI-driven tools for cataloging and interpreting marine biodiversity data.

- Integration with Space Technologies: Use of satellite imagery and Earth Observation for validation of environmental claims.

Strategic Goals
Immersea aims to bridge the gap betweenscientific research, environmental conservation, and public engagement, leveragingcutting-edge marine and space technologies. By integrating in-situ data collection with remote sensing, Immersea aspires to set new standards inmarine monitoring, environmental certification, and cultural heritage preservation.

entityDescription:
We are a Slovenian company specializing in trading, consulting, and providing services in the fields of surface preparation and printing technologies.
Our primary activity revolves around surface preparation using plasma technology (Plasmatreat Openair®), which enables efficient cleaning and activation of surfaces without the use of organic solvents. Additionally, we offer plasma deposition and coating services.
Founded in 1997 as Rogač Plus, Irena Uranjek s.p., we officially transitioned to Rogač Plus d.o.o. in 2010. We have been official Plasmatreat agents since 1998. Our expertise has allowed us to build strong partnerships with industrial companies, universities, and research institutes. We assist in the development of projects, create tailored Plasmatreat solutions, supply equipment, and provide comprehensive after-sales support.
We possess state-of-the-art Plasmatreat test equipment and instruments, along with extensive experience in pretreating and coating surfaces using atmospheric pressure plasma and plasma deposition. Notably, we supplied the very first Plasmatreat Fine Powder Coating unit (plasma deposition at atmospheric pressure) to a Slovenian company, marking a significant milestone in the industry.
As an authorized partner of Plasmatreat, we also have access to a wide network of specialists and their laboratory facilities.
We hold a strong AA+ credit rating, reflecting our financial stability and reliability in the market.

entityName: DZNE - Deutsches Zentrum für Neurodegenerative Erkrankungen
entityDescription:
Dementia is a widespread disease. Dealing with it is a challenge for society and a burden for many families, because relatives are usually the ones who care for people with dementia3). The costs are also enormous: In 2020, they amounted to some 83 billion euros for Germany, according to estimates by DZNE, and the trend is rising4). The crux of the problem is that there are currently no therapies that could stop or at least slow down the disease process. This applies not only to the various types of dementia – including Alzheimer’s – but also to other neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s and ALS. Although all these diseases tend to manifest in late adulthood, research suggests that the course for healthy aging is set many years or even decades before. In fact, the potential of prevention is considerable and far from being fully utilized: According to studies, around 40 percent of dementia cases worldwide could be prevented – through beneficial lifestyle habits and medical interventions that address risk factors5).
Ten sites
In light of this situation, DZNE was founded in 2009 as a member of theHelmholtz Associationand the first member of the German Centers for Health Research (DZG). Today, it consists of ten sites –Berlin,Bonn,Dresden,Göttingen,Magdeburg,Munich,Rostock/Greifswald,Tübingen,UlmandWitten– and pools expertise distributed nationwide within a single research institute. More than 1,200 professionals collaborate to understand the causes of diseases of the nervous system and to find novel approaches for effective prevention, therapy, and patient care. Worldwide, DZNE is one of the largest research institutes dedicated to these topic. It is funded by the GermanFederal Ministry of Education and Research(BMBF) and by the federal states in which DZNE sites are located**).DZNEis involved in the implementationoftheNational Dementia Strategy for Germany.
Fading neurons
The common trait of the diseases researched by DZNE is “neurodegeneration”, a term that refers to a progressive decline and loss of neuron. Depending on which area of the nervous system is affected, neurodegeneration can lead to dementia, trigger movement disorders, or massively impair health in other ways. Examples includeAlzheimer’s disease,frontotemporal dementia,childhood dementia,Parkinson’s disease,Huntington’s disease,amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS),spinocerebellar ataxia, and age-related macular degeneration.
Transfer to application
Research at DZNE aims at preventing neurodegeneration and significantly improve the quality of life of affected individuals. Thus, DZNE dedicates its efforts towards all aspects of neurodegenerative diseases – from molecular mechanisms to health care and patient care. Company description: Dementia is a widespread disease. Dealing with it is a challenge for society and a burden for many families, because relatives are usually the ones who care for people with dementia3). The costs are also enormous: In 2020, they amounted to some 83 billion euros for Germany, according to estimates by DZNE, and the trend is rising4). The crux of the problem is that there are currently no therapies that could stop or at least slow down the disease process. This applies not only to the various types of dementia – including Alzheimer’s – but also to other neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s and ALS. Although all these diseases tend to manifest in late adulthood, research suggests that the course for healthy aging is set many years or even decades before. In fact, the potential of prevention is considerable and far from being fully utilized: According to studies, around 40 percent of dementia cases worldwide could be prevented – through beneficial lifestyle habits and medical interventions that address risk factors5).
Ten sites
In light of this situation, DZNE was founded in 2009 as a member of theHelmholtz Associationand the first member of the German Centers for Health Research (DZG). Today, it consists of ten sites –Berlin,Bonn,Dresden,Göttingen,Magdeburg,Munich,Rostock/Greifswald,Tübingen,UlmandWitten– and pools expertise distributed nationwide within a single research institute. More than 1,200 professionals collaborate to understand the causes of diseases of the nervous system and to find novel approaches for effective prevention, therapy, and patient care. Worldwide, DZNE is one of the largest research institutes dedicated to these topic. It is funded by the GermanFederal Ministry of Education and Research(BMBF) and by the federal states in which DZNE sites are located**).DZNEis involved in the implementationoftheNational Dementia Strategy for Germany.
Fading neurons
The common trait of the diseases researched by DZNE is “neurodegeneration”, a term that refers to a progressive decline and loss of neuron. Depending on which area of the nervous system is affected, neurodegeneration can lead to dementia, trigger movement disorders, or massively impair health in other ways. Examples includeAlzheimer’s disease,frontotemporal dementia,childhood dementia,Parkinson’s disease,Huntington’s disease,amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS),spinocerebellar ataxia, and age-related macular degeneration.

Daniela Bezdan’s Contributions to Space Health and Space Biology at the University of Tübingen
Daniela Bezdan has been a key contributor to Space Health and Space Biology research at the University of Tübingen, with a strong focus on multi-omics approaches to studying astronaut health. Her work has resulted in over 15 collaborative publications with the university, driving advancements in space-related biological research.
For three years, Daniela has been actively involved in biobanking astronaut biological samples and data, ensuring their long-term accessibility and utility for space health studies. She has also been a key collaborator on the ESA Space Omics Topical Team, contributing to international efforts in space biology.
Since the establishment of NASA GeneLab, she has served as the first chair of the GeneLab Microbe Working Group, leading research efforts on microbial data from spaceflight experiments. Additionally, she is a scientific advisory board member at BioAstra, the largest private astronaut biobank in the United States, where she provides expertise in space omics and biobanking to support astronaut health research.

entityName: Vasco da Gama CoLAB - Energy Storage - Associação
entityDescription:
Vasco da Gama CoLAB (VG CoLAB) is a collaborative laboratory, supported by the Portuguese Agencies for Science and Technology (FCT) and Innovation (ANI). VG CoLAB was established in 2019 in Porto as a non-profit private association, and the associates include public and private partners from academia and industry. VG CoLAB is an associate member of IPCEI EuBatIn and BEPA.
VG CoLAB develops innovative system-oriented technological solutions applying energy storage to enable the energy transition. Fuelled by industrial and services sectors, it delivers mid-TRL prototypes and business support services scaling up relevant and novel scientific research findings.
​It is positioned in the centre of the electrochemical energy storage value chain, developing innovation activities, such as prototypes and proto-products. 

- Battery scale-up: we are focusing on sodium-ion batteries, where we are designing and implementing a pre-industrial pilot production line (pouch and cylindrical formats). Additionally, we have active work lines on redox flow batteries, addressing both electrolyte and system-level challenges.

- Modules and packs: We focus on stationary applications with the complete design of modules, which are intended to be as modular and technology-agnostic as possible. Also, we are developing modular and encapsulated solutions that integrate power conversion systems (PCS), battery management systems (BMS) and other technology.

- Power electronics and Grid interface: we develop modular and configurable converters and inverters as well as distributed and decentralised controls. These solutions enable the rapid creation of hybrid battery systems that combine different battery chemistries or integrate batteries with other technologies such as hydrogen or supercapacitors. Our approach enhances the flexibility and efficiency of energy storage systems, allowing them to adapt to various grid and application demands.

entityDescription:
Our mission is to empower cities and territories to reach their climate neutrality targets by providing precise evaluations of public policies on greenhouse gases. Our user-friendly tool, based on fully automated real-time Greenhouse Gas atmospheric measurements, offers a unique interface for public communication, making climate action accessible to all.
Origins.earth finds its genesis in the ambition of the City of Paris to become the first capital city in the world able to constantly measure the GHG emissions of its territory. The project, fully realised and financed by Suez in collaboration with the Laboratoire des Sciences du Climat et de l'Environnement (LSCE) - a joint CNRS-CEA unit founded by Jean Jouzel - was a success not only in scientific terms but also in the total respect of the planned time and resources.
We developed Meteo Carbone®, the world's first technological solution for real time monitoring of urban GHG emissions. This tool, combining complex spatial processing algorithms, scientific atmospheric models and high-precision CO2 measuring stations, allows cities to assess the impact of public policies, simulate proposed actions and visualize results.
The measurement systems of Origins.earth have been referenced in 2021 by the World Meteorological Organisation of UN in their protocol for all 194 member countries and in 2022 integrated into ICOS, the European measurement network Integrated Carbon Observation System (ICOS).

entityDescription: Mission The long-term mission of the Institute is to perform frontier research (a leading research activity that co-determines world trends in development and applications) in Computer Science and to transfer the respective new knowledge to society in general and to scientific community, students and application areas in particular. The institute's long-term research plans/intentions have been naturally focused on certain specific domains reflecting the strength of institute's research staff. They are in agreement with recent trends and take into account the needs of potential application fields. In its research - in the selected areas of Computer Science - the Institute focuses mainly upon the problems inspired by current and emerging computing technologies and by the needs of the discipline and of the society. The emphasis is both on identifying and harnessing of new approaches to computing (such as nature-inspired ones) and reasoning, on their creative applications and on strengthening of existing classical methods. The institute's research objectives consist of two basic and two interdisciplinary research streams. * Theoretical activities concentrate in particular on basic research in computational mathematics, computational complexity theory, computational intelligence, computational statistics, computational learning theory, computational logic and cryptography. * Interdisciplinary and application oriented research aims at non-linear modeling and prediction, environmental informatics, medical informatics, neuroinformatics and bioinformatics. Applications are sought primarily in the fields of environmental protection, meteorology, medicine and health care, biology, banking, cognitive sciences, earth sciences, economy, business, and web technologies. In all these fields the Institute strives to contribute to and to participate in the formation of the contemporary research trends. The ultimate strategic goal is the transformation of the Institute into a renowned research center of excellence in Computer Science.

entityDescription:
Non-invasive scanning of objects and structures using so-called muon tomography - a technology similar to X-ray imaging but applicable also to large-scale areas. As this technology leverages natural cosmic rays, it's also totally passive method with free and constant source of data - big data (10,000 particles/min/m²).
We develop algorithms to process raw muon data into high-resolution 2D/3D images, detecting damages, cracks, voids, density variations, and hidden structural weaknesses. This enables precise decision-making: (i) resource explorations - reducing unnecessary drilling (e.g., from 13 test drills to pinpointed locations), (ii) infrastructure monitoring -early detection of structural issues, allowing preventive action, (iii) aerospace - scanning engine cores, combustion chambers, turbine blades, exhaust nozzles, and compressors without disassembly, (iv) nuclear waste management, (v) national security, (vi) space industry.

entityDescription:
Lambda-X High Tech SRL is taking over the development and manufacturing services of Lambda-X S.A. established in 1996 and recognized as a key player in the development and manufacturing of optical systems.
Lambda-X S.A. has, over the years, built a robust technological and managerial expertise by participating in various ambitious space research programs. 
This expertise has allowed the company to expand its activities into high-tech industrial sectors where Lambda-X provides high-level optical engineering services based on a wide range of technologies.
Lambda-X’s value proposition lies in selecting the most suitable technologies for market demands. We are committed to ensuring that the proposed solution operates under the environmental conditions dictated by the client's application while optimizing the performance-to-cost ratio. 
By adhering to these best practices, Lambda-X introduced its first revolutionary instrument 15 years ago, based on a unique technique, and quickly became the global leader in the metrology of ophthalmic lenses.
Given the significant growth in both of its divisions, the Board of Directors of Lambda-X S.A. has decided in 2023 to partially split the parent company into two distinct entities:
· Lambda-X High Tech SRL, a newly established company taking over all the service, development, and manufacturing activities of optical systems for space, security, medical diagnostics, life sciences, and industrial process control from Lambda-X S.A.
· Lambda-X Ophthamics SRL, solely specialized in ophthalmic applications.
This strategic decision will enable each of the two new companies to specialize in their respective fields and strengthen themselves technically, humanly, and financially to better serve their clients in the long term.
No operational changes distinguish Lambda-X High Tech SRL from Lambda-X S.A.: they share the same technical and administrative teams, location, and infrastructure (labs and production rooms), as well as the same shareholder structure. The ISO9001 and EN9100 certifications of Lambda-X S.A. will be transferred to Lambda-X High Tech SRL. Meanwhile, the quality system, in place for over 10 years, continues to operate under the leadership of our Quality Director.

description:
Developing solutions for the Aviation and Aerospace industry since 2010.
 Established in February of 2010, QuAero is a company founded by pilots who are also qualified in engineering, computer science, human factors and other hard sciences, brought together by an EU FP6 project as aviation technical experts. QuAero was created with research and innovation as its company vision and scope. We provide research services and participate in academic studies to help in the advancement of Aviation and Aerospace technologies. Even today, research and innovation are the lifeblood and raison d’etre of QuAero. Following the initial project that brought the company together, QuAero has actively participated in numerous research and innovation projects funded by the Malta Council for Science and Technology, all of which were in collaboration with the University of Malta. We also provide safety management consulting services, training and advisory services on software products. We help our clients create manuals for AOC compliance and train their personnel as required as well as advising on the development of software products for the aviation industry. Through our crew resource management (CRM) services we understand it is essential that pilots learn as much as possible about how best to manage all the resources available to them in the cockpit including other crew-members, procedures, the machine interface and themselves, recognising where they are most vulnerable and where their strengths lie. Lastly, we supply safety software for aviation organisations as well as various other industries, coupled with back-office consultancy such as manuals and operational systems development. QuAero is a licensed reseller of major software brands such as Centrik. Coupled with our expertise, our tech prowess and in-depth knowledge of the software make us a strong ally for our clients, in terms of operational efficiency and compliance.

description: Astrobiome Space SARL is a biotechnology company based in Luxembourg, specializing in space-enhanced formula of microbiome-based products, aiming to improve resilience and high-performance for both humans and plants.
entityDescription:
Astrobiome Space, S.à R.L. is the European HQ of Astrobiome, Inc., registered in Luxembourg in November 2023. 
Astrobiome provides leading-edge solutions for sustainable farming. Their primary products, such as bio-stimulants for plants, leverage space technology to develop super-microbiome-based farming solutions. 
The company's core focus is on harnessing the potential of highly beneficial microorganisms to naturally enhance soil health, stimulate plant growth, and significantly enhance agricultural sustainability, all while reducing the reliance on traditional chemical fertilizers and pesticides. 
The company continuously evolves its products to adapt to rapidly changing climates. This includes innovations such as root treatments and soil microbial therapy, designed not only to improve crop yields and extend shelf life but also to increase the micro-nutrient content of the crops. Astrobiome's approach relies on a feedback loop that integrates Research and Development (R&D) activities with field testing, including extreme environments like space, to expedite experimental processes. 
To achieve these goals, Astrobiome collaborates with a global network of world top scientists, universities, laboratories, Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) experts, and progressive farmers. This collaborative approach enhances the company's ability to develop and refine its agricultural solutions in a dynamic and responsive manner. 
The company's structure has been intentionally kept straight forward, serving as an initial framework to facilitate the inclusion of future investors at opportune moments. Currently, the company is under sole ownership, founded by Vera Mulyani, with a dedicated, top world's microbiome scientist team, based in Japan. This team plays a pivotal role in the creation of the unique formula, strain culturing, production, manufacturing, conducting tests, and delivering results for the end product.

description:
Descartes Développement & Innovation (DDI) is the information and promotion association of the Sustainable City Technopole at the heart of Cité Descartes, located in the East of the Paris Region. DDI also operates a Fablab, an Incubator and a French Tech Community as part of its scope of operations.
A Sustainable City refers to an urban space at the crossroads of the economic, social and environmental pillars necessary for sustainable development. It simultaneously meets citizens’ expectations in terms of comfort, services and resilience, as well as environmental challenges and the needs of future generations.
Within Paris-Vallée de la Marne territory, DDI facilitates serendipitous connections between academia, institutions and businesses with a state-of-the-art research ecosystem in the establishment of a Sustainable City.

At Talogy, we care deeply, we listen. Our experts craft impactfultalent solutionsthat fit your people challenges.
Talogy was born in 1946, with psychology pioneers Floyd E. Ruch, Raymond B. Cattell, Herb Greenberg, and Max Kostick individually launching assessment initiatives to help young adults and war veterans enter the workforce in the years following the second world war. While their industry leading assessment solutions were created in the 1960s, they still play a prominent role in global talent assessment today.
In the 1990s, the world of talent assessment and development started evolving rapidly, and great new solutions were brought to market by the companies founded by these pioneers as well as others. From 2017 onwards, through a series of acquisitions, many of these companies started to come together into one organisation offering an unmatched breadth of talent assessment and development solutions. All leading up to the year 2022, when Talogy as we know it today was born with the purpose to deliver people-focused talent assessment and development solutions to organisations around the world.

entityDescription:
The International Space University develops the future leaders of the world space community by providing interdisciplinary educational programs to students and space professionals in an international, intercultural environment.ISU also serves as a neutral international forum for the exchange of knowledge and ideas on challenging issues related to space and space applications.
It specializes in providing graduate-level training to the future leaders of the emerging global space community at its Central Campus in Strasbourg, France, and at locations around the world. In its one-year Master of Space Studies, two-month Space Studies Program and 5-week Southern Hemisphere-Space Studies Program, ISU offers its students a unique Core Curriculum covering all disciplines related to space programs and enterprises, space science, space engineering, systems engineering, space policy and law, business and management, and space and society. Each of these programs also involve an intense student research Team Project providing international graduate students and young space professionals the opportunity to solve complex problems by working together in an intercultural environment.
Since its founding in 1987, ISU has graduated more than 5000 students from over 110 countries. Together with hundreds of ISU faculty and lecturers from around the world, ISU alumni comprise an extremely effective network of space professionals and leaders that actively facilitates individual career growth, professional activities and international space cooperation.
Building on specialist knowledge already acquired, ISU relates this to all aspects influencing the successful outcome of space development and use. At ISU, programs are:
Interdisciplinary
Broad-based educational programs that encompass all disciplines relevant to space scientific, engineering, economic, regulatory, political and organizational provide students with a multi-dimensional perspective, vital for understanding and effectively dealing with complex space development and utilization issues.
International
Global networking opportunities and intensive teamwork practices at ISU give its diverse student body the edge when performing in competitive and collaborative international space programs.
Intercultural
Interacting with people from a variety of different backgrounds: academic, cultural and national, with varied approaches to problem solving and occasionally conflicting objectives, prepares ISU students for the multicultural environment of today’s world space community.

The Fénix Foundation’s work is built upon three key pillars. We leverage technology in order to: 
> Empower the lawyers of today by developing cutting-edge legal tools that can disseminate knowledge of international humanitarian, criminal, and human rights law to lawyers on the front-line of accountability work; 
> Educate the lawyers of tomorrow by prioritising cooperation with university legal clinics, where students learn about the intersection between law and the practical application of international humanitarian, criminal, and human rights law; and,
>Secure the rule of law in the digital age by providing high-level trainings for judges and other court officials in order to promote digital literacy, foster a critical understanding of digital tools (including generative AI), and promote knowledge of the value and pitfalls of digital evidence.

description:
Lechner Tudaskozpont Nonprofit Korlatolt Felelossegu Tarsasag (abbreviated official denomination in English: Lechner Non-profit Ltd.) was founded on January 24, 2013. Lechner Non-profit Ltd. is a professional background institution of the Prime Minister’s Office in the field of architecture, building and construction, real estate/land registration and geospatial issues. Its mission is to digitise and socialise wide range services connected to built environment and spatial data.

Its activities are focused on remote sensing, regional planning, smart city services as well as land surveying, earth observation and cartography tasks. Its services also include the operation of the Documentation Centre and IT services supported by e-administration.

Lechner Non-profit Ltd. acts as a mediator organisation between the architectural and co-professional fields and the wider public, its services reach both professional and residential users.

Since 2019 Lechner Non-profit Ltd. as background institution of the Prime Minister’s Office has become an organisation with the largest spatial data assets and the widest geospatial expertise. With transferring surveying, remote sensing and geospatial activities as well as land registration and cartography tasks from the former Office of the Capital City Budapest Department of Geodesy Remote Sensing and Land Offices (previously: Institute of Geodesy Cartography and Remote Sensing (FÖMI) to Lechner Non-profit Ltd., geospatial databases and resources are now concentrated in one single organisation.

#HorizonEurope

entityDescription:
SMHI, the Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute, is an expert Agency under the Ministry of the Environment and Energy. Through expertise in meteorology, hydrology, oceanography and climatology, SMHI contributes towards greater public welfare, increased safety and a sustainable society. SMHI administers and develops information about the weather, water and climate that provides social functions, trade and industry and the general public with knowledge and qualified decision guidance. National and international cooperation are extensive. SMHI offers tailored products and services that form the basis of important decision guidance for different activities. General forecasts and warnings, industryspecific services, simulations and analyses, statistics, climate studies and research assignments are just a few examples.
AGENCIES AND BUSINESS PARTNERS
SMHI’s activities are primarily financed in three ways: through grants, through commissions from other agencies and through business activities on commercial terms. There are distinct lines of activity that naturally are different, yet still based on the same fundamental principle, to contribute to greater public welfare, safety and a sustainable society. 
RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
SMHI conducts applied research in meteorology, hydrology, oceanography and climate. The research department develops knowledge, models and tools that describe processes in the atmosphere, in the sea and on land. These are needed to improve SMHI forecast models and decision guidance for practical public welfare. A great deal of the research conducted by SMHI is climate related. Researchers develop climate models, produce climate scenarios and participate in impact and adaptation studies. Mathematical models and methods that utilise data from satellites, radar systems and other observations are key in the research. SMHI’s research is mainly externally funded. Researchers collaborate in Swedish research projects, EU Projects and other international projects. 
CLIMATE WORK IN FOCUS
SMHI runs a national centre of knowledge for adaptation to climate change on behalf of the government at SMHI. The role of the centre is to act as a hub for knowledge about climate change and to be a meeting place for actors involved in climate change adaptation. SMHI is the contact point in Sweden for the UN’s climate panel, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). As the contact point, SMHI coordinates the Swedish IPCC work and establishes Contacts with the IPCC Secretariat in Geneva. Responsibility also entails nominating Swedish experts for the IPCC work. This can be in the role of author, reviewer or participating in workshops and other meetings.

entityDescription: QSENSATO s.r.l. aims to satisfy the growing market demand for sensors that are on the one hand robust, portable and miniaturized, on the other hand allowing ultra-precise and accurate measurements. Current atomic sensors lack such combined properties, due to the low versatility of the vapor cells used and the lack of integration with photonic structures. QSENSATO s.r.l. offers a solution based on an innovative fabrication method of laser-written vapor cells (LWVCs) with 3D versatility and unique integration with photonic waveguides and optical fibres. The company is developing and will commercialize the following products: 1. LWVCs tailored for different sensing and metrology applications. 2. atomic-photonic chips, i.e. LWVCs integrated with photonic structures. 3. complete quantum sensors such as optically pumped magnetometers, electric field sensors, frequency references, atomic clocks and gyroscopes. QSENSATO s.r.l. activities will also be devoted to research and development of technologies related to the main one.

QSENSATO s.r.l. offers a solution based on an innovative fabrication method of laser-written vapor cells (LWVCs) with 3D versatility and unique integration with photonic waveguides and optical fibres. The company is developing and will commercialize the following products: 1. LWVCs tailored for different sensing and metrology applications. 2. atomic-photonic chips, i.e. LWVCs integrated with photonic structures. 3. complete quantum sensors such as optically pumped magnetometers, electric field sensors, frequency references, atomic clocks and gyroscopes. QSENSATO s.r.l. activities will also be devoted to research and development of technologies related to the main one.

entityDescription:

Our flagship service, the MetSprite platform, provides "Atmospheric Profiling as a Service," delivering continuous, high-resolution atmospheric data to our clients.
With MetSprite, we offer hourly atmospheric profiles up to 2 km altitude, measuring calibrated temperature, relative humidity, and two-dimensional wind data. We also provide extended profiling up to 6 km and the option to integrate custom sensors, ensuring tailored solutions for a wide range of applications.
Our mission is to create a comprehensive atmospheric monitoring system that enhances weather and climate forecasting capabilities. Led by a team of experts in aerospace, physics, and meteorology—including our CEO John Mooney, Chief Aerospace Officer Peter Mooney, and Chief Meteorological Officer Ben Pickering—we are committed to advancing atmospheric science and operational meteorology.

entityName: University of Alexander Dubcek in Trencin
entityDescription:
University of Alexander Dubcek In Trencin (TnUAD) is a modern university in Slovakia, focusing on applied research and education in engineering, materials science, and technology. The university has robust capabilities in the development of advanced materials, surface engineering, and testing of innovative solutions, particularly in metallic and composite materials. Its research infrastructure includes state-of-the-art laboratories for material analysis, nanotechnology, and 3D printing, supporting applications in aerospace and space technologies.
TnUAD is actively engaged in international collaborations and interdisciplinary research aimed at innovation in lightweight materials, high-strength alloys, and thermal-resistant coatings. The university also offers expertise in computational modeling, structural optimization, and advanced manufacturing processes. With its focus on applied research and industry partnerships, TnUAD is well-positioned to contribute to the advancement of space technology and related fields.

The university comprises several key faculties and research units:

- Faculty of Industrial Technologies: Specializes in materials science, nanotechnology, and advanced manufacturing processes, with significant applications in aerospace and space technologies.

- Faculty of Special Technology: Focuses on robotics, mechatronics, and special-purpose machinery, providing high-precision solutions for technical challenges in various industries.

- Faculty of Social and Economic Relations: Supports interdisciplinary projects with economic and managerial expertise, fostering collaboration across sectors.

- Faculty of Health Care: Conducts research in medical technologies, complementing the university's engineering and technical research focus.

- FunGlass – Centre for Functional and Surface Functionalized Glass: A European center of excellence in glass research, specializing in functionalized glass materials with applications in space, aerospace, and high-tech

industries.
FunGlass is a leader in innovative glass technologies, focusing on lightweight, durable, and high-performance materials for extreme environments.

- The University Creative Center FabLab is an innovation and entrepreneurship hub supporting research commercialization, prototype development, and start-ups. It fosters collaboration between academia and industry, advancing solutions for space technologies and related high-tech fields.

entityName: University of Maribor, Faculty of Law
entityDescription:
The Faculty of Law at The University of Maribor represents an important part of Legal education in Slovenia and helps in developing not only the field of Higher education but also all other aspects of Slovenian society that the law is an integral part of. The law education in The Faculty of Law at The University of Maribor, is widely interconnected with the Slovenian judiciary, lawyers and prosecutors. Our graduates are highly valued when working in the State Administration and Local Government Bodies and mostly when working as lawyers in companies and financial institutions.

The development of The Faculty of Law at the University of Maribor deriving from the College of Law (in 1960-1990) and from the High School of Law (in 1990-1993) is a result of plenty years of effort of all employees, professors, assistants, researchers and other associates working towards a better Faculty and better study environment for its students. Law is one of the first fields ever to be studied by humans being, also, of major importance to other fields of study, especially those connected to social sciences, as all knowledge about society is somehow connected its order. Law is much more than a system of rules, it is a philosophy that expresses a unique overview of the world and all the people in it. By determining the basic Human Rights and freedoms, law contributes to the creation of a better society. Law is also sociology, in the way its regulation of social encounters sheds a light on them and on their nature – whether wanted, normal, good or bad, allowed or forbidden. Furthermore, law is also a strategy and a helpful instrument in changing the society.

entityDescription:
The Faculty of Agriculture and Life Sciences at The University of Maribor mission is research, education and knowledge transfer to meet the needs of agriculture, food processing and related industries and co-creation of public opinion and active policy in favour of food security, self-sufficiency in natural, environmentally friendly and locally produced food, preservation of cultivated agricultural land, increasing biodiversity, reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and other pollutants in the environment. Our values are based on honesty, curiosity, creativity, freedom of spirit, cooperation and knowledge exchange, care for people and sustainable development, enriching agricultural knowledge, raising awareness, strengthening humanistic values, creating dialogue, increasing quality of life and global justice. Our slogan is "Knowledge and Tradition".

We strive to produce internationally recognized research, to be an educational and innovative centre for agriculture, food and renewable resources. We create new cutting-edge fundamental and applied knowledge, which is passed on to national and international researchers and graduates, as well as to farms and businesses. Furthermore, we work on identifying the problems and challenges of the 21st century and on finding solutions through responsive research. We also try to redesign our study programmes in a way that we believe is fit for the future. Another aim is to be centre with intensive international exchange of professors, researchers and students, a development incubator and a space for demonstrations of innovation and analysis and an important stakeholder in agricultural, food, economic and environmental policymaking.

entityName: University of Maribor, Faculty of Medicine
entityDescription:
The Faculty of Medicine at the University of Maribor is an educational and research institution at which we educate students to acquire knowledge and skills needed for prevention of diseases, maintenance and recovery of health; an institution where we, within institutes, implement research work and where we are, besides this, concerned with integrated and sustainable development of an individual and social responsibility.

Our vision is to be a respectable, desirable, established, safe, internationally oriented and recognizable educational and research institution with the elements of excellence and to be a part of close and distant environment, known for knowledge and competency of physicians whom it had educated, professors, researchers and technical staff who work in it and known for moral standards which adorn it. We are concerned with consistent development of all chairs and institutes and also with the development of our clinical teaching bases. With intensive international exchanges of students and professors we facilitate, for students and professors, acquiring of additional knowledge and experiences. An important task for the future is intensification of research work, especially basic research, which we achieve in cooperation with other faculties at the University of Maribor which have already now been included as partners at the postgraduate study programme Biomedical technology, in cooperation with the University Clinical Centre Maribor and in cooperation with our partner faculties within the European Union. The Faculty of Medicine at the University of Maribor endeavour to continually renew study programmes in the sense of modernization, while cooperating with students and taking into consideration guidelines which are formed by international organizations such as AMSE (Association of Medical Schools in Europe) and AMEE (Association for Medical Education in Europe). For this purpose, a curriculum committee has been established which is responsible for constant modernization of curricula.

The basic task of the Faculty of Medicine at the University of Maribor as an educational institution of future physicians is education of our graduate in the technical sense and also in the sense of ethical norms. Competencies which must be mastered by our graduates are in congruence with competencies encompassed in the national Blue Book on education of physicians and also with the standards of our partner European faculties.

entityName: INSTITUTE OF ATMOSPHERIC PHYSICS OF THE ACADEMY OF SCIENCES - Department of Ionosphere and Aeronomy
entityDescription:
Department of the Ionosphere and Aeronomy performs investigation of the Ionosphere, middle and upper atmosphere. It mainly focuses on:
- Physics of the Ionosphere and Ionospheric weather monitoring
- Global changes (trends) in the upper atmosphere and ionosphere
- Ozone and stratospheric dynamics
- Infrasound propagation in the atmosphere and its application to atmospheric study
- Atmospheric electricity and global electric circuit

The department also deals with the development of instruments for satellite and ground measurements, the developed components include Digital Sun Sensors, Thermal Plasma Measurement Unit
The department operates two measuring sites at
Panská Ves Observatory and
Průhonice Observatory

SyntetiQ is an innovative company specialising in the development of a Data-as-a-Service (DaaS) platform designed to generate high-quality synthetic data to enhance artificial intelligence (AI) training in robotics. Our goal is to accelerate AI learning by creating diverse and realistic datasets that improve the perception, manipulation, and navigation capabilities of robotic systems.
We are actively collaborating with research institutions and industry partners to conduct pilot projects demonstrating the practical applications of our platform in real-world scenarios. These initiatives aim to showcase how our synthetic data can expedite AI development, reduce costs, and enhance the adaptability of AI models across various robotic applications.
Our target audience includes AI researchers, robotics developers, and industrial partners who require diverse and realistic datasets to improve the performance of their systems. We are committed to adhering to all regulatory requirements, including GDPR and Horizon Europe ethical standards, ensuring that all our AI models comply with data protection laws.
Recognising the critical role of advanced AI in space exploration and satellite technology, SyntetiQ is dedicated to supporting the space industry by providing synthetic data solutions that enhance the training and performance of AI models used in space applications. Our platform is designed to meet the unique challenges of space robotics, including autonomous navigation, object recognition, and environmental interaction, thereby contributing to more efficient and reliable space missions.
By leveraging our expertise in synthetic data generation, we aim to support the development of AI systems capable of operating in the demanding conditions of space, ultimately contributing to the advancement of space technology and exploration.

entityName: Ministry for Agriculture, Fisheries and Animal Rights - Agriculture and Rural Payments Agency (ARPA)
entityDescription:
The Agriculture and Rural Payments Agency’s mission is to serve as a customer focused organization delivering a quality service which includes the timely processing of payments and receipts, ensuring compliance with EU rules and regulations and disseminating relevant information to the farming community.

ARPA’s Role & Objectives
ARPA’s vision is to serve as a catalyst towards maximising the benefits from the Common Agricultural Policy. In this regard, ARPA’s objectives are to:
– Operate an effective administrative set-up
– Ensure efficient, effective and timely processing of claims
– Attain effective control procedures that would ensure that there is no risk to the use of public European Union funds
– Provide accurate and timely information to the European Institutions, local entities and most importantly to the local farming community.

Legal Basis
Paying Agencies are set up in accordance with the EU’s Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) legislation, and specifically with Regulation (EU) 2021/2116 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 2 December 2021 on the financing, management and monitoring of the common agricultural policy and repealing Regulation (EU) No 1306/2013.
The Malta Agriculture and Rural Payments Agency is established in accordance with Subsidiary Legislation 146.03 Paying Agency Regulations.

entityDescription:
The Energy & Water Agency's (EWA) mission is to ensure the security, sustainability and affordability of energy and water in Malta.
As an organisation of the Government of Malta, the EWA is responsible for drafting and actioning the Government’s national policies for these sectors, and abiding by EU legislation for energy and water sustainability. It is also our job to act on laws and develop policies for renewable energy, energy efficiency, water demand management, and the security of the local energy supply (for electricity, gas and water).
At the EWA, we carry out rigorous research to forecast Malta’s energy and water demands, so that these are met sustainably across the country, with a focus on circularity.
Our ultimate vision is to safeguard the long-term value of the energy and water sectors in Malta through resilient, environmentally sustainable and economically circular practices. In and of themselves, such practices promote the security of supply, universal affordability and the innovation of cutting-edge solutions to meet industry challenges in a sustainable manner.

entityDescription:
DABCO LIMITED (trading as “Pairpoint”) is a London-based joint venture between Vodafone and the global trading group Sumitomo, founded in 2023.
The rise of the Economy of Things (EoT) and its interconnected ecosystem of devices,presents a $10 trillion market opportunity, driven by secure, frictionless transactions between billions of connected devices.
Building trust through robust security is essential to unlock this potential.Without, devices risk becoming vulnerable entry points for malicious actors, and IoT device transactions (whether financial, operational, or data-driven) lose their reliability and value.
Pairpoint addresses this need by providing the foundation for secure and reliable interoperability.Pairpoint’s foundational principle is to enable secure business-to-things, device-to-device, device-to-platforms and device-to-people interactions, where data exchange and transactions are protected through verified identities, encrypted communications, and tamper-proof audit trails.This allows businesses to confidently scale their IoT operations, create new service models, and unlock the fullpotential of the Economy of Things (EoT).
By establishing a trusted environment where devices can securely share data and execute transactions, Pairpoint underpins the IoT value chain with confidence, enabling industries to create new service models, scale their operations, and unlock emerging use cases in mobility, logistics, energy, and beyond.
This next-generation platform seamlessly integrates security, identity, interoperability, automation and innovation, ensuring that IoT-connected devices, and the people and businesses behind them, can engage with confidence, efficiency, and peace of mind.
Core to Pairpoint is the ability to make IoT devices programmable, and create new value over-the-air as the IoT services evolve, from the trigging of actions, to notifications, to permissioned data sharing and financial transaction initiation when specific conditions have been met.Pairpoint’s software brings device automation, bridging the gap between what a device senses and enabling it to response without human interaction or supervision. This extends their value far beyond their original purpose, driving new value over multiples of their original IoT ROI.
Pairpoint's primary focus is on key sectors poised to benefit significantly from secure EoT solutions:
·Automotive:
OEMs and Fleets seeking secure in-car payments and new service models.
·Mobility merchants:
who use the platform to connect to OEMs/Fleets for automated services sales.
·Global trade, supply chain and Logistics:
companies involved in maritime, rail, and road transport, requiring enhanced data security, interoperability and in-field automation.
·Telecommunications:
MNOs and MVNOs, IoT Connectivity Players and IoT Application providers,leveraging Pairpoint's PaaS to build and deploy their own IoT solutions.
·Energy & Others:
Smart meter manufacturers, energy aggregators, utility companies ensuring cybersecurity compliance and exploring new energy trends, or even Drones and Drones applications, offering authentication, identity and security connectivity.
Pairpoint will launch its first commercially active devices in FY2026, with rapid growth projected to reach +40 million of contracted devices. This growth will be driven initially by our TrustTec product in logistics and other end-market IoT sectors, followed by increasing presence of Pairpoint PayTec product in the mobility sector

entityDescription:
SAB Space Logistics is a pioneering company within the SAB group, specializing in comprehensive space logistics solutions. The company's core business lies in services for space exploitation focusing mainly on launch services and in-orbit services.

SAB Space Logistics, leveraging on the know-how of the SAB Holding on this field, held primarily by the Italian SAB Launch Services, provides launch services on both European and international launch vehicles, catering to a wide range of auxiliary passengers, from cubesats to microsatellites up to 200kg.

SAB Space Logistics is an in-orbit servicing provider. Its aim is to establish a robust European ecosystem where multiple systems collaborate to deliver efficient and swift servicing activities to customers. To this purpose SAB Space Logistics proactively explores the emerging in-orbit servicing sector, conducting extensive market analyses and surveys to identify and understand potential business opportunities that are expected to unfold in the coming decade and beyond. The company's target servicing ecosystem is designed to offer a spectrum of services, including life extension services such as satellite refurbishment, upgrading, and refueling. Additionally, the company focuses on orbit sustainability services, encompassing activities like Active Debris Removal (ADR), end-of-life de-orbiting, and in-orbit recycling. Beyond these, SAB Space Logistics provides vital support services such as Attitude and Orbit Control System (AOCS) takeover, assisted orbital transfer, orbit injection, inspection, and controlled re-entry of space hardware.

ABB Measurement and Analytics business unit located in Quebec City, is part of ABB Canada, a member of ABB Group. Our business unit designs, manufactures and markets high-performance optical sensors for industrial processes, and space and defense markets. Industrial markets include Petroleum, Chemical, Life Sciences, Academic, Semiconductors and Metallurgy. In the space market, ABB Measurement and Analytics specializes in optical remote sensing instruments for space applications such as atmospheric science, environment monitoring, weather forecasting and astronomy. entityDescription:
Rocket Sciences has developed a bespoke methodology for emissions calculation, reporting and net zero strategy, based on >20yrs experience working with decarbonisation technology. As governments and large corporates commit to net zero 2050 (or earlier) it falls upon supply chain organisations to meet these commitments. We noticed that these organisations often do not have the tools nor understanding to determine their position with respect to net zero, let alone implement the solutions. In turn, we have developed a low-cost, bespoke methodology for emissions calculation and reporting, to underpin net zero strategy. We then facilitate solutions implementation, drawing from our extensive database of net zero innovations.
We recognise that emissions calculation, reporting and management is particularly complex for the farming and agricultural sector, whereby flows of Nitrogen and Carbon take place throughout the natural environment, altered by day-to-day management decisions. In turn, we wish to apply our bespoke approach to this industry by leveraging complex AI/ML – which we believe will unlock significant net zero and productivity opportunities for the sector.

entityDescription:
Latitudo 40 is an innovative start-up that combines the skills and expertise of a large company with the passion and ability to innovate of a lean organization that bases its success on the principles of user centered design. Enhancing the experiences of its founders in the ICT and Earth Observation fields, gained in university research contexts and in large companies, and the background of experience, skills and abilities of our multidisciplinary team, the company offers integrated solutions of geo-information in the cloud, based on images from earth observation satellites and innovative algorithms of artificial intelligence, machine learning and big data analysis.
In Latitudo 40 we strongly believe in the value that can be extracted from the images coming from earth observation satellites and we have made our utmost efforts to launch the EarthAlytics platform on the market which is able to transform pixels into information using an innovative and multi-sensor approach in a simple, effective and rapid manner in different application fields. We use a multi-sensor approach, putting together in a single application platform data coming from the satellites, IOT devices installed in the field and from sources external to the organization (weather forecasts, statistics, erp, etc.). We process these data through artificial intelligence and machine learning to give them meaning and provide the needed information to make the right decisions at the right time, without having to be experts in earth observation.
Latitudo 40 is incubated within the Business Incubator Center of the European Space Agency Business Incubation Center at the BIC LAZIO in ROME. The headquarter office is based in Naples.

entityDescription:
The Toulouse site, with its strong research potential in fundamental sciences, applied sciences and human and social sciences, will bring together teaching and research establishments, national research organizations, healthcare establishments, the CROUS and the Centre de ressources, d'expertise et de performance sportive (CREPS) de Toulouse around a common project.
As part of this project, they are committed to paying particular attention to key societal issues, notably through their scientific contribution to well-being and healthy living, the development of space and aeronautics, and the improvement of agricultural and agri-food sectors for a sustainable world.

An experimental public establishment (EPE), structured around the Toulouse III-Paul Sabatier University and its component establishment, the Purpan Engineering School, will bring together the academic strengths of Toulouse and its surrounding area. The two establishments share complementary training and research themes, a mutual focus on sustainable development, and common values of openness and benevolence.

This EPE will provide the site with the right conditions for the creation of a major multi-disciplinary research and training university of world renown, visible and recognized at both national and international levels. It will be characterized by a common signature and brand, rich in the diversity of the entities that make it up, and ready to commit to a principle of respect, trust and subsidiarity.

An inclusive place of innovation and experimentation in both training and research, the establishment is committed to the success and well-being of its staff and students. The EPE is committed to fostering a strong international dynamic, while remaining firmly rooted in its local area, with sustained interactions with local society and socio-economic ecosystems.

Last but not least, academic excellence, environmental and social responsibility, outreach, openness and public service visibility are the cardinal values of this future establishment, heir to the experimental COMUE Université de Toulouse.

VEO Partners GmbH is a consultancy and analytics company founded in 2024 by senior experts (Germany/Austria) spanning (re)insurance risk analysis & modelling, geoinformatics, Earth observation, forestry/agroforestry, and ESG compliance, currently employing 7 people. Our mission is to make climate- and nature-related risks measurable and actionable by applying our “Verify, Evaluate, Orientate” methodology across data, decisions, and implementation.
Our primary focus has been business consultancy for importers and traders of agricultural commodities and timber, helping them optimize supply chains and adapt to the stringent requirements of the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR). Our key clients operate in the forestry and wood-processing industries as well as in food production and commodity importing, including coffee and cocoa. Sustainability, resilience, and legal compliance are core values underpinning all our business solutions.
By combining state-of-the-art technological innovation with deep industry expertise, we help our clients not only meet regulatory requirements but also design sustainable and future-proof business processes.
VEO Partners stands for practical, efficient solutions that strengthen companies’ development and help address the global challenges posed by climate change in affected sectors.

entityDescription:
Founded in 1900, the Bernhard Nocht Institute for Tropical Medicine (BNITM), originally a department of the Hamburg Health Authority, has been an independent, non-profit research institution in the form of a foundation under public law based in the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg since 2008. In accordance with the purpose of the foundation, the BNITM is dedicated to research, teaching, training and further education as well as counselling and care in the field of tropical diseases and emerging infectious diseases.
The institute combines modern laboratory research on the biology of pathogens, their reservoirs and vectors with clinical research on the pathophysiology, epidemiology and disease control of tropical diseases in endemic areas. Current foci are malaria, worm infections and other parasitoses as well as diseases caused by arboviruses and haemorrhagic fever viruses, and the development of new diagnostics. For the handling of highly pathogenic pathogens and infected insects, the Institute has laboratories of the highest biological safety (BSL-3, BSL-4) as well as a safety insectarium (BSL-3).

entityDescription:
Founded in 2023, the Gulbenkian Institute for Molecular Medicine (GIMM) is a pioneering Portuguese private research foundation with an ambitious vision for fundamental scientific exploration and its profound impact on global health and well-being.
GIMM is dedicated to unraveling the fundamental mysteries of life and aims to be at the forefront of transdisciplinary research. From the beginning, GIMM has strived for scientific excellence and societal impact, driving the future of molecular medicine for a healthier world.
GIMM was born from the merger of two leading research institutes: Instituto de Medicina Molecular João Lobo Antunes (iMM) and Instituto Gulbenkian de Ciência (IGC). This strategic union combines both institutes’ strengths, expertise and resources, enhancing our research capabilities and fostering synergies to address complex scientific challenges.

Our Vision
To create a globally leading scientific research institute that will generate multi- and cross-disciplinary knowledge to answer fundamental questions of biology and human health in a fast-evolving environment. All while developing solutions to improve health outcomes and promote local and global health equity.
An integral part of this mission is a lasting commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion, reflected in our work and within our community.

Our Mission
At the Gulbenkian Institute for Molecular Medicine (GIMM), our mission is anchored in scientific excellence and societal impact, structured around five key pillars:
Challenging Frontier Science
We will promote curiosity-driven research and interdisciplinary collaboration, leveraging cutting-edge technologies. By recruiting top talent through international calls and hosting renowned programs, we will increase GIMM’s global visibility and attract the brightest minds.
Boosting Health Outcomes
We will bridge the gap between discovery and application through translational and clinical studies. We will engage diverse stakeholders to pioneer innovative, data-driven solutions to enhance global health outcomes and promote equity.
Fostering Innovation & Translation
We will prioritize translating scientific advancements into practical applications for disease prevention, diagnosis, and treatment, driving healthcare innovation.
Nurturing the Next Generation
We will nurture the next generation of scientists through innovative training programs and career development support, empowering individuals from diverse backgrounds to excel in transdisciplinary research.
Beyond GIMM walls
We will shape the national and European R&D landscape through collaboration, promote excellence in research and training, and engage society in scientific and cultural development.

entityName: Fondazione GAL Hassin - Centro Internazionale per le Scienze Astronomiche - Isnello
entityDescription:
The GAL Hassin Foundation carries on educational and research activities in the astronomical field through its astronomical center located in Isnello, Sicily, which was inaugurated in 2016.
The center offers a 10-meters digital planetarium, a museum of meteorites and terrestrial rocks and an external area with sundials and solar calendars. In addition, the GAL Hassin astronomical center is equipped with a 40cm aperture,f/D=3.8 robotic telescope (the Galhassin Robotic Telescope – GRT, MPC Code L34), extensively used since 2019 to perform astrometric and photometric characterization of Solar System’s minor bodies, space debris and artificial satellites.
The research capabilities of the center are going to significantly increase in 2025 thanks to a 1m aperture, f/D=2.1 prime focus telescope, built by Officina Stellare: the Wide-field Mufara Telescope (WMT, MPC Code M57).

description:
From high- and ultra-precision manufacturing to optical coatings and digitalization, this is where innovation begins! RhySearch, the Rhine Valley Research and Innovation Centre, is a partner of industry as well as academia and carries out research as a service to initiate high-tech projects. RhySearch has a technical infrastructure that is unique in Switzerland:
The Ultra-Precision Manufacturing Lab has expertise ranging from high-performance milling and diamond turning to laser micro-machining of steels, non-ferrous metals, ceramics and hard metals.

RhySearch works closely with its cooperation partners OST - Ostschweizer Fachhochschule, Empa, inspire AG, the University of Liechtenstein and the Swiss Innovation Park Ost. It is recognized by Innosuisse, the Swiss Agency for Innovation, as a research institution eligible for funding.

entityDescription:
The Port of Tyne in North East England is one of the UK’s major deep-sea ports. It is one of the biggest trust ports in the UK, covering 650 acres, of which 200 acres of deep-water quayside land is available for occupation / investment.
The Port has excellent connectivity – by rail via three dedicated rail paths to the east coast mainline, by road via the A1 and A19, by air with direct links to Newcastle International Airport and by Metro via its ‘Tyne Dock’ station.
The Port offers a full logistics service, is one of only three ports in the UK with the International Pilotage Standard and is accredited with AEO status.
The Port of Tyne operates in a wide range of markets.
Offshore: The Port is ‘offshore wind ready’ and is the site of the operations and maintenance base for the biggest wind farm in the world, Dogger Bank. The Tyne also houses an extensive offshore supply base and has partnerships with several colleges and universities in the region.
Containers: The Port has a dedicated container terminal capable of handling 100,000 TEU per annum with regular European feeder services.
Bulks: The Port handles a range of bulk commodities and project cargo, including biomass from North America which supplies two power stations, grain, aggregates, as well as rail vehicles from Japan.
Automotive: The Port is the UK’s second largest car exporter with customers including Nissan and VW.
The Port of Tyne also houses the UK’s first (and still the only) Maritime Innovation Hub, helping our customers collaborate with leading innovation partners both in the UK and globally.
