entityDescription:
Flexibilis Oy was founded in 1998 in Tampere, Finland. In communication technology, Flexibilis concentrated on wired Ethernet. In 2002, Flexibilis had already developed its first FPGA IP product. The product was named FFEC (Flexibilis Fast Ethernet Controller), and was an Ethernet controller IP block, programmable to an FPGA chip. In 2006, development of FPGA technology made it possible to upgrade the controller to gigabit speed. The name was changed to AFEC (Advanced Flexibilis Ethernet Controller), as “Fast Ethernet” implied support for 100 Mbps speed only. The IEEE 1588 PTP (Precision Time Protocol) was becoming a more and more widely used standard for time synchronization, and support for it was added to AFEC in 2007.
The development of another important Flexibilis IP product, FES (Flexibilis Ethernet Switch) started in 2007. FES is a standards compliant Ethernet switch. It was designed from the start to be gigabit, and to support the IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol. In July 2011 Flexibilis released a version of FES that supported the HSR (High-availability Seamless Redundancy) protocol. At first the product was called FES-HSR, to emphasize its origin. The product garnered wide interest, as it was the first HSR implementation to support gigabit speed. Support for PRP (Parallel Redundancy Protocol) was added and the name was changed to FRS (Flexibilis Redundant Switch).
Flexibilis has also designed complete devices. In 2007-2009 Flexibilis developed its first complete communication product. It was a time synchronization device targeted for use in harsh environments. It had a waterproof housing, and the electronics inside the housing were passively cooled. It was built using FPGA technology and both AFEC and FES IP blocks were employed. The device was able to achieve nanosecond class accuracy in clock transfer over Ethernet using IEEE 1588 PTP.
In October 2016, TTTech acquired Flexibilis and integrated the Flexibilis brand and products into its industrial and aerospace market offering. TTTech Computertechnik AG is an Austrian company and a global leader in the field of robust networking and safety controls.

entityDescription:
The Istituto Superiore di Sanità(ISS) (Italian National Institute of Health) is the main Italian research institute in the biomedical and public health field. It is the technical and scientific body of the Italian National Health Service. The ISS activities include: promotion and protection of national and international public health through research, surveillance, regulation, control, prevention, communication, counselling and training. The ISS produces knowledge through research and trials and disseminates scientific knowledge and evidence to decision-makers, professional workers and citizens in order to protect and promote public health.
 
The technical and scientific area of the Institute includes6 Departments(Cardiovascular, dysmetabolic and ageing-associated diseases,Environment and health,Food safety, nutrition and veterinary public health,Infectious diseases,Neurosciences,Oncology and molecular medicine)16 National Centres(Addiction and doping, Animal research and welfare, Chemicals, cosmetics and consumer protection, Clinical excellence, healthcare quality and safety, Control and evaluation of medicines, Disease prevention and health promotion, Drug research and evaluation, Global health, Health technology assessment, HIV/AIDS research, Innovative technologies in public health, Radiation protection and computational physics, Rare diseases, Telemedicine and new health care technologies, Blood, Transplants), 2 Reference Centres (Behavioural sciences and mental health, Gender medicine) and5 Technical-scientific Services(Biological Service, Core facilities, Grant office and technology transfer, Research coordination and support, Statistics). Anotified bodyauthorized to issue EC certification of medical devices according to Council Directives 93/42/EEC and 98/79/EC, operates within the Institute.

Research, Trial, Surveillance and Prevention
The ISS collaborates on research activities and clinical trials with national institutions performing public health functions such as the Ministry of Health and the Ministry for the Environment, regions, local health units, hospitals and scientific institutes for research, hospital care and healthcare. The ISS research activities include a wide variety of fields: research and therapies against HIV/AIDS and related syndromes; research and analysis of population health from a global perspective to combat inequalities in access to healthcare services; research to validate diagnostic practices and therapies in gender medicine; research in the field of mental health to detect environmental etiopathogenetic mechanisms and to promote psycho-physical welfare; research, surveillance and prevention of addiction and doping; assessment of health risks arising from the use of chemical substances and cosmetics, prevention and surveillance of harmful substances and poisoning exposures; prevention of risks deriving from exposure to ionizing and non-ionizing radiation and development of methods in computational physics; coordination of animal testing activities to protect animal welfare; research and monitoring on quality and safety of delivering healthcare services to patients; assessment of health technologies; research in telemedicine, new health information technologies and innovations.
Health promotion
Promotion and protection of public health are pursued through activities carried out especially in the areas related to the following types of diseases: neurological, psychiatric, oncological, haematological, genetic, infectious, cardiovascular, endocrine-metabolic, immune-mediated, and ageing-related.

description:
221e is a leading global supplier of intelligent precision sensing solutions for smart devices. Our hardware platforms and AI-powered sensor fusion algorithms provide exceptional accuracy and consistent results alongside significant cost advantages. Since 2012, we have delivered innovative sensing solutions to power a wide variety of products, including wearables, sports equipment and industrial devices. For over a decade of field testing and scientific research, 221e’s advanced sensing technologies have been continuously refined to meet the accuracy requirements of the most demanding applications.

Key Products:
MPE > inertial sensor fusion embedded software library
MPE™ (Motion Processing Engine) is 221e core sensor fusion software enabling the highest accuracy and performance for 6-axis and 9-axis inertial orientation estimation (IMU). Based on a dynamically adaptive Extended Kalman Filter implementation, offsets compensation and automatic calibration procedures; it is the product of 10 years of extensive research, experience, and field tests for the most demanding applications. This is the source of a strong competitive advantage that positions 221e among the elite benchmarks of the market.

NeuraSense > embedded edge AI software
NeuraSense™ is a set of intelligent sensing libraries for consumer, automotive and industrial applications. Optimized for the edge, it provides real-time inertial sensor data processing enabling context awareness, gesture recognition, activity tracking, motion control, dead reckoning navigation, platform stabilization, and 8 use cases. Using TinyML real-time classifiers NeuraSense enables pattern recognition, event/anomaly detection, predictive maintenance and decision automation combining multiple sensor inputs to enable deeper insights and better accuracy.

entityDescription:
Pixel Photonics GmbH, founded in 2021 and based in Münster, Germany, is at the forefront of innovation in photon detection technology. The company specializes in Waveguide-Integrated Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detectors (WI-SNSPDs), a cutting-edge technology that integrates superconducting nanowires with nanophotonic waveguides on a single chip. This unique approach enables exceptional performance in single-photon detection, making Pixel Photonics a key player in fields such as laser communication and free-space QKD.

Pixel Photonics’ WI-SNSPD technology delivers superior detection efficiency across a broad spectral range, high timing precision, and extremely low dark count rates, all of which are critical for optical quantum communication systems. A notable feature is its polarization insensitivity, which ensures consistent detection performance regardless of light polarization—a vital characteristic for free-space communication. The detectors are also highly scalable, utilizing CMOS-compatible, wafer-scale fabrication processes to reduce costs and increase production capacity. Integration with photonic circuits further enhances performance by minimizing optical losses in free-space and on-chip applications.
With a steadfast commitment to innovation in photonics and quantum technologies, Pixel Photonics delivers scalable, affordable, and state-of-the-art solutions. Its participation in European R&D projects highlights the potential of its technology to address critical challenges in emerging quantum and photonics applications. By enabling groundbreaking advancements, Pixel Photonics is shaping the future of high-performance photon detection.

entityDescription:
SPALLIAN is a technology company specializing in data intelligence and geospatial solutions. We develop innovative software and tools to help administrations and organisations harness the power of location-based data for improved decision-making. SPALLIAN’s products range from geospatial data visualization to advanced analytics, enabling clients such as local authorities to gain valuable insights and serve the public interest.
While we serve a diverse range of clients, one of our notable areas of expertise lies in providing tailored services to local administrations (cities, inter-municipalities, regions…), helping these entities unlock the full potential of geospatial data for more effective governance and decision-making.
At its core, SPALLIAN is committed to leveraging location-based data to address the unique challenges faced by local governments and other public-sector organisations. For this, we are developing a geospatial data visualization platform that allows government officials and planners to visualize complex data sets on interactive maps, making it easier to understand spatial relationships and trends. This capability is invaluable for urban planning, infrastructure development and climate
change response, as it enables decision-makers to assess the impact of various scenarios and make data-driven choices.
As a consulting company, our advanced analytics capabilities are another asset for administrations. By harnessing geospatial data through robust indicators, we can perform in-depth analyses to identify trends, patterns and anomalies. This enables municipalities to optimize resource allocations, such as determining the most efficient locations for public services like schools, healthcare facilities, and economic clusters.
We also understand the importance for local governments of engaging with communities. As such, we offer solutions for citizen engagement and participation through a geospatial mobile app called thelma. This platform empowers residents to provide input on local issues, access important information and collaborate with government official, fostering transparency and accountability in local governance. It is currently used in +150 municipalities in France for eight years, and it is now being spread across Africa, starting with the cities of Kigali (Rwanda) and San Pedro (Côte d’Ivoire).
In addition to these technical capabilities, we place a strong emphasis on providing training and support to local administrations. We work closely with government team to ensure they have the knowledge and skills needed to effectively utilize geospatial tools data. Our approach not only helps public-sector organisations maximise their investment in geospatial technology, but also fosters a culture of data-driven decision-making.
Our commitment to the public sector goes beyond just providing tech solutions. We are dedicated to contributing to the improvement of communities and helping local administrations fulfil their missions. Whether it’s improving transportation systems, optimizing land use, enhancing healthcare and education services, or formulating effective economic strategies, our expertise in data plays a vital role in shaping the future of local governance.

entityDescription: Quantopticon makes game-changing software to accelerate the development and adoption of Quantum 2.0 photonic devices. Developed over a period of 15 years by a respected theoretical physicist, Quantillion is the world's first state-of-the-art quantum simulation engine for design, modelling and optimisation of quantum-optical components. Prior to Quantillion, best practices in optimising such components involved initial guidance by classical photonics design software, followed by a series of iterative trial-and-error experiments - a protracted and expensive process typically lasting several months. Classical photonics software is inadequate for calculating the required design features, on account of omitting quantum processes from the picture. By virtue of a cutting-edge quantum theoretical framework, Quantillion is uniquely capable of accurately describing and predicting the quantum aspects of light-matter interactions in quantum-optical systems. Consequently, it can faithfully simulate, and then optimise, quantum-optical components in a fraction of the time and at a fraction of the cost, by removing the need for costly and time-consuming experiments.

2 Phase 2 (from the 6th year onwards): after financial and reputational consolidation of the company, the company will develop a series of innovative CubeSats applications (currently at TRL2-3) which will open a new commercial perspective on the small satellites market.

description:
TWI Ltd is one of Europe’s foremost independent research and technology organisations, working across all industry sectors, with expertise in solving problems in all aspects of manufacturing, fabrication and whole-life integrity management technologies. Services include a technical advisory service, information services, training, software and a range of different types of research/consultancy projects. The majority of TWI’s activity (75%) is contract research, funded by industrial members and built around the development of advanced technologies. TWI has over 600 industrial members in over 2,000 locations worldwide across a range of industries that includes automotive, engineering and construction, oil and gas, and aeronautics. 
TWI has worked on several programmes specifically for the aerospace sector. For example, in developing (process characterisation and validation testing) and applying the high integrity FSW process as the joining method of choice for the pressurised cryogenic external tank of the NASA Space Shuttle, in partnership with Lockheed Martin. The Institute was established as a public institution for the performance of spatial planning activities for the Split-Dalmatia County in accordance with the Law on Spatial Planning and Construction (Official Gazette, No. 76/07). The founder of the Institute is the Split-Dalmatia County.
ACTIVITY
- development, or coordination of development and monitoring of implementation of spatial plans at the regional level,- development of reports on the state of the space,- management of the spatial planning information system and its management within the scope of authority,- preparation of the starting point for development, or repealing of spatial plans for narrower areas,- issuing opinions in the process of development and adoption of spatial planning documents in accordance with the law,- development of the county spatial plan and development of spatial plans for cities and municipalities, urban development plans of importance for the State, or the county, if the development of these plans has been entrusted to the Institute by the competent ministry or county prefect,- performance of expert and analytical work in the field of spatial planning if the performance of these tasks is entrusted to the Institute by the competent ministry or county prefect.

entityDescription:
Nature Robots promotes regenerative and ecological agriculture through AI and robotics in harmony with nature and humans by supporting perennial and diverse cropping systems in their economic viability through innovative software and hardware solutions.
Based on temporally and spatially high-resolution three-dimensional plant maps, monitoring assistance systems as well as autonomous robotics applications are developed for natural arbitrary-structured environments, such as vegetable, fruit and viticulture or (agro)forestry / photovoltaics.
Nature Robots was founded in January 2022 as a fully independent Osnabrück-based start-up and is a spin-off of the German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence.
As a first use case, the technology will initially be applied by means of the specially developed agricultural robot Lero for bio-intensive vegetable cultivation, the so-called market gardens.

SpectralEO specializes in providing Earth Observation (EO) and Remote Sensing applications. The company delivers innovative geospatial solutions designed for precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, and decision support services, catering to both private enterprises and public organizations.
At its core, SpectralEO leverages satellite imagery, UAV data, and in-situ measurements to provide actionable insights that drive sustainable and data-driven decision-making. The company is currently developing a specialized precision agriculture platform, with a particular emphasis on viticulture, enabling vineyard managers to optimize their operations through advanced monitoring and analytics.
Beyond agricultural applications, SpectralEO offers tailored solutions for local governments, helping to enhance climate adaptation and resilience by addressing critical challenges such as green space management, coastal monitoring, urban heat islands, and wildfire risk assessment.
SpectralEO stands at the intersection of technology and environmental stewardship, equipping businesses and public institutions with the insights and tools needed to enhance operational efficiency and sustainability in an increasingly data-driven world.

entityName: National Museum of Natural History, France
entityDescription:
The French National Museum of Natural History, known in French as the Muséum national d'histoire naturelle, is the national natural history museum of France and a grand établissement of higher education part of Sorbonne University. The main museum, with four galleries, is located in Paris, France, within the Jardin des Plantes on the left bank of the River Seine. The museum now has 14 sites throughout France. Since the 2014 reform, it has been headed by a chairman, assisted by deputy managing directors. The Museum has a staff of approximately 2,350 members, including six hundred researchers. It is a member of the national network of naturalist collections.

The BOREA “Biology of Aquatic Organisms and Ecosystems” Lab aims to investigate biology and ecology of aquatic organisms and habitats in natural and impacted ecosystems. Using a transdisciplinary and integrative approach, the objective is to understand the origin, the role and the evolutionary mechanisms in aquatic biodiversity (from molecules to ecosystems), the interactions (i) between organisms and (ii) with their environment, as a response to global anthropogenic and climatic changes.

- Enables high-resolution tracking of debris as small as 1 cm
- Robust under low-visibility or nighttime conditions

- Proprietary algorithms for real-time trajectory analysis
- Automated risk assessment and advanced warning to satellite operators

Using a lean deployment strategy, Project-S can protect satellites in specific orbits without requiring a full-scale constellation from the outset. entityName: Paying Agency for Agriculture, Fisheries and Rural development (PAAFRD)
entityDescription:
The Paying Agency for Agriculture, Fisheries and Rural development (PAAFRD) is a payment public body entirely dedicated to the implementation of public policies at European, national and local levels.
The mission of the Paying Agency is to serve as a customer focused organization delivering a quality service which includes the timely processing of payments and receipts, ensuring compliance with EU rules and regulations and disseminating relevant information to the farming community.
The structure, scope of work and operations/duties are defined by the European Union legislation applicable in all member states. PAAFRD is the only one accredited institution in Croatia administering support measures for agriculture, rural development and fisheries. 

PAAFRD is responsible for keeping and updatingARKOD which is established on the basis of maps, land registry documents and other cartographic references.Computerised geographical information system (GIS) techniques are used, which preferably include aerial or spatial imagery. ARKOD system functions on the basis of a database on reference parcels allowing to locate agricultural parcels, which are declared by farmers as entitled to direct payments.

The system checks the declared area as to its eligibility (i.e. area eligible to payments under a given assistance scheme) and control as to overlapping of declarations for specific agricultural parcels.

Practically, this means that all fields are numbered and their images (taken by satellites) or orthophotos (taken by airplanes) are digitised. All these images are included in a geographical information system, which also contains the boundaries of the reference parcels and their (eligible) area.The limits of the reference parcels are also visible in the fieldif they correspond to natural boundaries,such streams, forests or roads.
From 2021. partially and from 2023. for all agricultural area of Croatia, Paying Agency uses Area Monitoring System (AMS) - procedure of regular and systematic observation, tracking and assessment of agricultural activities and practices on agricultural areas by Copernicus Sentinels satellite data or other data with at least equivalent value. For assessment of agricultural activities and practices AMS needs referent areas of crops – Features of interest (FOI). So automaticdelineation of FOI is crucial for good detection of agricultural activities.Results (traffic lights) are communicated with the farmers through the AGRONET to encourage them in their agricultural practises and there are the base for payments of agricultural subsidies. 

PAAFRD has a total of 850 employees in central and regional offices of which 150 employees work on administrative and OTS related to IACS.

entityName: University of Split - Faculty of Science
entityDescription:
The Faculty of Science in Split is one of the founders and one of the oldest faculties at the University of Split, and with approx. 900 students and 140 employees, it is one of the university’s larger departments. The core business of the Faculty is teaching, scientific-research and professional work in the areas of the natural, technical and social sciences, while research is further undertaken in the area of the biotechnical and biomedical sciences. The Faculty trains future teachers (bachelor’s degree and master’s degrees in education) in the field of mathematics, physics, computer science, technics, biology and chemistry, as well as engineers (master’s degrees in the field of mathematics and physics including a bachelor’s degree in nutrition.
The success of the Faculty of Science is confirmed by the quality of previous students. Graduates who acquire a tertiary education at the Faculty, receive comprehensive training in undertaking jobs for which they have been educated, as well as tracking the development of their profession by getting involved in lifelong learning. These graduates are highly esteemed on the labour market. The Faculty is also well known for its professional supplementary pedagogic-didactic-psychological-methodical education of future teachers. Over the last few years, the doctorate programme in Biophysics and doctorate programme in Education Research in Natural and Technical Sciences as the only interdisciplinary postgraduate programme in the area of education have received increasing recognition.

entityDescription:
Established in Milan in 1980, CSIL is an employee-owned research institute specialising in applied economics with specific expertise on research and innovation policy, industrial policy, regional development and market research. Since its origin, CSIL has been established as a centre of excellence concentrating on the diagnosis and design of sector strategies both for the public and private sectors, and the analysis of factors of competitiveness at regional, national and global levels.

In 40 years of activity, CSIL has gained considerable experience in supporting private and public decision making, working for EU and international clients including the European Commission, the European Parliament, the European Investment Bank, the African Development Bank, the OECD, the World Bank, CERN. For them, CSIL carried out comparative country analysis, reviews of policy frameworks and public expenditure planning and assessment to help understand the coherence and soundness of public interventions, as well as ex-ante, interim and ex-post evaluations to assess the economic and social effects which can be attributed to a policy, a programme, projects or individual measures.

CSIL has robust methodological expertise and developed guidelines and manuals related to the estimation of costs, benefits and impacts of policies, programmes and projects, as further explained in the next section with specific reference to research infrastructure and big science.

CSIL has strong credentials in various industry domains applications. description:
Ageospatial makes location intelligence accessible. (www.ageospatial.com)
We fuse near real-time satellite imagery, open (global, regional, global), national and proprietary geodata, and GeoAI models into one intuitive tool to support your decision making. With Geoforge you can quickly increase situational awareness, understand your location's context, identify risks, validate property claims, or coordinate mission briefings through natural language queries, no GIS expertise required. Our system automatically retrieves, enriches, processes and analyzes geospatial information, so you can make informed decisions with trusted data. Whether you’re optimizing insurance pricing, coordinating a mission briefing or planning a relief operation, Geoforge reduces costs and accelerates workflows. Our automated data fusion, interactive reporting, and real-time insights support geodata-driven decisions faster and at half the cost of traditional solutions.
entityDescription:
Professionals take geodata driven decisions and improve decision-making with rapid geodata enrichment
Professionals across insurance, government, and public safety sectors (defense, health, emergency services) are responsible for evaluating environmental and infrastructure risks for properties, mission planning, or improving decision-making. Traditionally, these tasks require manually gathering, processing, and validating large volumes of geospatial data from diverse sources. This labor, cost and time-intensive process takes several hours or days to compete, demand specialized experience with data and/or geodata, which delays decision making and increase operational risks.
With Geoforge, these professionals can instantly enrich their existing data with geospatial data by submitting natural language queries such as "Show flood risks around these selected buildings or marker," or "Generate a terrain vulnerability analysis for this area of interest that I drew on the map."
Geoforge’s agentic AI (GeoLLM) retrieves, fuses, and processes relevant open local, regional, federal, global and proprietary datasets, including those stored via Geoforge's data warehouse (Motherduck or AWS S3) or accessed through partner APIs. Near real-time satellite imagery (optical, infrared, radar) is called using an API and and specialized GeoAI models (e.g., heatwave, flood, or landslide detection) are incorporated using 4EI's API (UK-based partner company of Ageospatial specialized in GeoAI natural disaster algorithms)
Within seconds, the platform produces interactive web reports or downloadable PDFs featuring maps, charts, elevation profiles, processed geodata in a standard format (.geoparquet / .geojson for vector and .cog for raster) ready to be downloaded and used. These instant outputs reduce analysis time by over 90% and cut operational costs by thousands of CHF per evaluation, but also empower users to make geodata-driven, timely decisions. It supports to reduce financial exposure and support geodata driven pricing, verify claims, avoid financial losses and support payout decisions (insurance), mission planning, ressource allocation and incrase sitautional awarness and support tactical decisions.

entityDescription:
Cosmic is an innovative start-up of very recent constitution (January 2020) but born from a well-tested team and expert in water loss, data transmission and cosmic rays. The idea, born in 2018, is to innovate the water loss research system with something that was a "disruptive technology" and not a simple improvement of existing techniques. To do this, Riccardo Marchetto, as it was for satellite leaks research with “Neptune S.r.l.”, (a company already incubated by ESA in 2014, thanks to BIC Lazio – Italy, for the water leaks detection with satellite images analysis), he was looking for a new space-derived technology to apply to daily water leaks issues with a TTP (Technology Transfer Project) from space technologies to terrestrial applications. The research gave its fruit with the possibility to control the ground humidity checking the absorption of cosmic rays. These radioactive rays coming from Space, with many sources like Sun's internal explosions or supernova explosions, are continuously bombarding the Earth and some of these rays are stopped only by hydrogen. Hydrogen is a component of water (H2O), where there is a loss there is a lot quantity of water mixed with the ground, and therefore a big quantity of hydrogen is present, so the neutron of cosmic rays is absorbed causing a decrease in its counting. The idea is cultivated by searching the market for the most difficult component to find: the neutron detector. It is from here that the meeting with Luca Stevanato, a PhD researcher at the University of Padua, who has realized such a device, comes out. A partnership aimed at conquering the market with this technology was immediately born. 
Cosmic is structurally much leaner waiting to receive the first orders but is still supported by Neptune's technical and commercial support. Within the structure, the team is composed by 8 employees who coordinate in order to manage the administrative, technical and on site work of the startup. Employees are young people under 40 and, together with Riccardo Marchetto (CEO), are working in the startup. They are Anna Tormen (24, Funds research and application), Schiesaro Carlo (40, specialist on water leak detection),and 3 teams active at all times for verifications and water leaks detection.

entityDescription:
COBA – Consultores de Engenharia e Ambiente, S.A. is a company of Engineering and Environmental Consultants, founded in 1962. COBA provides engineering consultancy services ranging from basic and planning studies, technical, environmental and economic feasibility studies, preliminary design, design and construction design, design check, technical assistance, works supervision and project management, up to operation control and behaviour monitoring. Vast international experience in the fields of large hydraulic developments (namely dams, weirs, reservoirs, pumping systems and hydraulic structures), power generation (namely hydroelectric power projects) and transmission infrastructures, water supply and sanitation systems, water resources management plans, agriculture and rural development, transport infrastructures, geotechnical structures, environment, cartography and cadastre.
For this purpose, COBA relies on highly specialized multidisciplinary teams in its several areas of activity, from civil engineering – planning, geotechnics, structures, hydraulics, hydrology - to electromechanical and mechanical engineering, environmental engineering, agronomy and natural sciences, enabling the provision of state-of-the-art services and the preparation of studies / projects in an integrated manner. COBA’s mission is to comply with the Clients' requirements providing high standard engineering services, within the established delays and costs and to contribute to the reputation of the Portuguese Engineering worldwide.
With offices in three continents and experience in fifty-nine countries, COBA Group relies on the services of several companies, with specific fields of expertise or focal areas of activity. The close collaboration among all the Group’s companies allows the development of its activity in a complete way, by making use of its varied technical and logistical support all over the Group. 
In this way, COBA Group benefits from a deep interaction and a vast exchange of experience among the staff of several companies, which lead to synergies which enhance the specialized training of its members.
COBA has a permanent staff of about 200 people including the graduates, the technicians and the support staff. A significant number of their technicians have M.Sc. and PhD degrees obtained in Portuguese and/or Foreign Universities, with deep scientific and technical knowledge and a vast experience, forming the company’s nucleus of experts. The multidisciplinary teams cover all the sectors of activity of the company, thus allowing the permanent availability of all specialists necessary to the execution of studies and designs in an integrated and sustained basis, which is one of the basic principles of the firm.
COBA is a member of the Global Compact Network Portugal (GCNP), a Portuguese network of organisations representing the United Nations Global Compact (UN Global Compact), which is the United Nations’ corporate sustainability initiative.
GCNP is composed of national and international organizations operating in Portugal and aims to implement the Ten Principles of the UN Global Compact and the Sustainable Development Goals of United Nation’s 2030 Agenda by disseminating them to the interested parties and society at large, by sharing experiences among stakeholders worldwide.
COBA is NP ISO 45001:2019, NP EN ISO 14001:2015 and NP EN ISO 9001:2015 certified.

UROPEAN QUALITY ASSURANCE (EQA) is a specialized company with over 20 years of experience in verification and certification, focusing on project evaluation. Accredited as a Certification Body, EQA has managed more than 40,000 projects across 120 UNESCO disciplines. It is accredited in DNSH Environmental Verification and Certification of Environmental Management Systems under ISO 14001:2015 standards, demonstrating expertise in environmental evaluation.
Services and Expertise
EQA has extensive experience in providing evaluation and consultancy services to public and international institutions. It has successfully carried out projects for governments of Spain, Portugal, Croatia, Latvia, Lithuania, Italy, Ghana, Senegal, Kenya, Libya, and Chile. Collaborations with multilateral organizations like the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank further highlight its global reach and credibility.
Organizational Strength
EQA employs a team of 300 highly qualified professionals, supported by a network of over 10,000 international evaluators and partnerships with universities and technological centers. This enables the organization to deliver complex projects efficiently, complying with international standards.
Notable Credentials
- Financial Solvency: EQA’s financial stability ensures the successful execution of projects.
- Accreditations: Recognized by ENAC in Spain for certifying R&D&I projects across 100 UNESCO disciplines.
- Experience in Climate and Environmental Projects: Decades of expertise in climate change evaluations, GHG verifications, energy audits, and certifications.
- Skilled Workforce: A multidisciplinary team with specialists in project evaluation across diverse sectors.
- Global Network: Access to an extensive evaluator network for customized project needs.
Recent Experience
EQA has collaborated with innovation agencies and public bodies such as CORFO (Chile), CONAF (Chile), MICITT (Costa Rica), CONACYT (Paraguay), and MICINN (Spain). Its partnerships with regional European agencies, including ACCIÓ (Catalonia Government), Galician Innovation Agency (GAIN), and Basque Business Development Agency (SPRI), demonstrate familiarity with R&D&I project evaluations under stringent quality standards.
Project Suitability
EQA is particularly qualified to conduct ecological, hydrological, and socio-economic assessments, such as those required for the Bon Accord Lagoon and Kilgwyn Mangroves in Southwest Tobago, in comparison with Trinidad’s Caroni Swamp. The organization’s expertise includes:
- Managing complex environmental impact assessments.
- Leveraging advanced information management tools.
- Ensuring compliance with international quality benchmarks.
Collaborative Success
EQA’s successful track record with institutions like the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank underpins its capacity to deliver high-quality services. Its established methodologies and comprehensive evaluator network make EQA uniquely positioned for large-scale, multidisciplinary projects.

entityDescription:
COMEX pioneered in the development of equipment for human intervention in extreme environments: The group led the way in industrial deep diving in the oil and gas supply and service sector. At the height of its activities, hundreds of divers from COMEX worked at depths of more than 300 meters, using helium-based breathing mixtures. COMEX¿ robots and equipment operate successfully at depths over 1000meter. 

The developments in the field of deep-sea intervention naturally led COMEX to participate in the development and test of equipment for human spaceflight: 
COMEX was involved in the verification of the European shuttle HERMES of the manned space flight program under the auspices of ESA. In the frame of these activities it participated in the test and development of equipment for EVA and IVA in its Neutral Buoyancy Facilities. Members of the European astronaut corps trained microgravity EVA in COMEX¿ test pools on real scale mock-ups of HERMES and COLUMBUS. 
COMEX is involved in the study of the SeaOrbiter, a new generation of exploration vessel, which is developed in cooperation with NASA¿s undersea training program. SeaOrbiter has multi-level pressure modules, used to prepare the technologies for long distance journeys in confined habitats.

The HYPERBARIC EXPERIMENTAL CENTRE is designed for studying the effects of pressure (hyperbaric and hypobaric) and gases (oxygen, nitrogen, helium and hydrogen etc.) on biological samples and structural models. The laboratory is equipped with a fully automated hypobaric/hyperbaric bio-incubator for tests with all gases, including hydrogen. Our team has successfully conducted more than 5300 operations, including nearly 2700 predominantly physiological or technological experimental human dives. 

This expertise gives COMEX today the necessary tools to develop, verify and test life support equipment and structural models for human intervention in hostile environments.

The company’s core product, Magnorobocell, consists of small, intelligent robotic units capable of autonomously connecting, disconnecting, and forming complex 3D structures.
This technology addresses key challenges in the space sector, such as reducing transportation costs, enabling on-demand fabrication, and minimizing space debris. Designed for extreme environments, Magnorobocell provides a versatile solution for constructing and maintaining infrastructure in orbit or on extraterrestrial surfaces, enhancing mission efficiency and sustainability.
In addition to space applications, the technology offers significant potential in terrestrial markets, including architecture, industrial manufacturing, and disaster recovery. By combining adaptability, precision, and modularity, Magnorobocell bridges the gap between space innovation and practical uses on Earth, positioning itself as a key player in the advancement of modular robotics.

entityDescription: AI: Aerospace Innovation GmbH (AI) in Berlin develops special high-technology solutions and applications for the national and European aerospace industry and related agencies. AI is a precursor for new and innovative technologies, a provider of environmentally friendly and cost-efficient rocket propulsion systems for terrestrial and orbital operation as well as a centre of competence for strategic and technological space-related questions. Due to a long-standing experience in research and education along with extensive and detailed experimental work, AI is characterised by a unique technical know-how in the area of space transportation system design, rocket propulsion and propellant combustion as well as value analyses, cost modelling and modelling of complex socio-economic relations. AI was launched as an evolution of the aerospace engineering and consultancy company AI: Aerospace Institute, Lo, Adirim and Partners, that was founded in May 2000 within the frame of the Technology Transfer Program at Berlin University of Technology (TUB). When AI was founded in 2007 in order to provide complete system solutions and products in the field of aerospace propulsion, the core activities of AI: Aerospace Institute were transferred to the new company. Today, the team of AI consists of eight employees and two consultants. The company presently focuses on space transportation and propulsion system investigations as well as trend analyses, while the range of activities includes numerical simulations of complex dynamic processes, e.g. solid and hybrid rocket motor combustion, feasibility investigations for new technologies and systems as well as development and manufacturing of demonstrators and prototypes for customised propulsion solutions.

Overview of Keyrus Belgium
Keyrus Belgium is part of the Keyrus Group, a global consulting and technology company specializing in data intelligence, digital experience, and business transformation. Founded in 1996 and headquartered in France, the Keyrus Group has expanded worldwide to support organizations in unlocking the full potential of their data and accelerating their digital transformation. As a key regional entity, Keyrus Belgium combines local market knowledge with the broader expertise, capabilities, and resources of the global Keyrus network.

Core Competencies
1. Data Intelligence & AI
Keyrus Belgium helps companies leverage data as a strategic asset. From data strategy and governance through analytics, business intelligence, and AI-driven insights, the team designs and implements end-to-end solutions that boost decision-making, process efficiency, and innovation.
2. Digital Experience
With a focus on customer engagement and user-centric design, Keyrus Belgium delivers innovative digital solutions that enhance customer experiences, streamline interactions, and optimize digital channels. This includes e-commerce platforms, content management systems, and tailored user experiences.
3. Business Transformation
Beyond technology, Keyrus Belgium supports clients in rethinking and optimizing their operating models, processes, and organizational structures. By combining strategy consulting, change management, and robust technological expertise, Keyrus ensures transformations deliver tangible and sustainable business impact.

Local Expertise and Global Reach

While offering specialized local insight into the Belgian market and regulatory environment, Keyrus Belgium benefits from the Group’s global footprint. The entity draws upon an international network of more than 3,000 professionals, allowing it to provide multi-disciplinary teams with cross-border expertise and best practices. This blend of local presence and global knowledge positions Keyrus Belgium as a trusted partner for both regional and international organizations.

description: Founded in 2013, Geocledian is designing and providing custom crop monitoring solutions based on satellite technology. For this purpose, Geocledian has developed the comprehensive Ag|Knowledge V4 API, a crop monitoring platform providing near real-time analysis ready data, analytics tools and crop modelling with more than 90 different endpoints. It enables users to integrate remote sensing and weather-based crop analytics into end-user applications or workflow management systems with minimum effort and development time. These custom solutions can be tuned to a large variety of crops, cultivation types and regions. They may range from determining optimum harvesting dates for grains, to validating the provenance of a variety of supplied goods to fulfil contract obligations, or is enabling sugar mills to efficiently deal with thousands of small growers fields. Geocledian has built and improved this platform over the last 9 years. It uses open satellite data from Sentinel, Landsat but is also integrating commercial weather data and other datasets. Our Ag|Knowledge product is successfully used by multiple farm management systems, traceability systems and for compliance systems with a customer focus on Europe and Asia.

entityDescription:
Greenerwave is a French deep-tech startup based in the heart of Paris. Founded in 2016 by CNRS researcher Geoffroy Lerosey and Mathias Fink, professor at ESPCI Paris, to promote their pioneering research into shaping electromagnetic waves using smart materials and deep-physics algorithms.

In 2012, they took the concept of reconfigurable smart surfaces from the field of optics to that of telecommunications, with their first proof-of-concept of an intelligent indoor environment enhanced by a wavefront shaping approach. Since this first technological achievement, Greenerwave has continued its journey in the wireless communications industry. Company description: The IDA (Industrial Development Agency) is a state-owned, join-stock company under ownership supervision of the Chancellery of the Prime Minister of Poland. The IDA supports business enterprises in operation and development of business activity, as well as in the implementation of restructuring processes, and plays a major role in increasing competitiveness of Polish industry. The broad spectrum of support instruments includes both financial products and non-financial assistance in implementation of projects, such as providing access to investment areas and production facilities within Special Economic Zones administered by the IDA. The Company also makes it possible for business partners to liaise in implementing innovative projects. As part of the Polish Development Fund Group, the IDA cooperates with major Polish institutions supporting enterprises and provides comprehensive solutions in response to the current needs and challenges faced by businesses.
Since 2016, IDA has been conducting a dedicated support program for Polish space companies: “Comprehensive support program for Polish space technology sector”. This program defines and divides all IDA activities in four fields:
•Human Resources development;
•New business projects;
•Promotion;
•Financial instruments.
In each defined field IDA has developed support mechanism. Since 2016 each year IDA together with Polish Space Industry Association organises internship program. Up to 15 companies can hire an intern chosen in a contest for six months, IDA covers up to 50% of costs of such internship. During three finished editions, all together 43 young specialist were hired by 21 companies. IDA has also started initiative Space Academy, which main idea is to enable young engineers retrain from other speciality to space technology sector. Using competences of Warsaw University of Technology, Military University of Technology and Space Research Centre Polish Academy of Science training focused on Satellite Integration Phases – 0/A/B/C/D is offered with partial financing of IDA. 
IDA supports national programs dedicated to start-up acceleration, one of them is European Satellite Navigation Competition 2016, Space3ac Acceleration Program 2016 or European Rover Challenge 2018. Recently IDA become partner of MyGalileoApp competition of European Global Navigation Satellite System Agency. Additionally to improve cooperation between Polish large companies and SME’s, IDA provides service in searching and selecting innovative project for large companies in specified fields. Such activity/contest is done together with industrial partners and it’s called ARP Innovation Pitch. Since 2016 we have organised 20 such contests. One of ARP Innovation Pitch was dedicated to space technology.
Activities of IDA related with international promotion are: financial support of national stand on international conferences and trades: Paris Space Week 2016, SpaceTech Expo 2017 (Bremen) or International Astronomical Congress 2018 (Bremen). National promotion is implemented by organising large events: Satellite Forum 2017, European Space TechTransfer Forum 2019 or supporting existing ones: Space Sectore Forum (2016 and 2018). Since 2017 IDA has launched dedicated loan program for polish space companies. One of the financial support mechanisms is the Open Innovation Network project that involves animating and supporting technology transfer transactions to Polish SMEs sector. Enterprises can obtain the grants which refund up to 70% of costs invested in the purchase of innovative technologies. Project is financed form UE founds. IDA is active both Polish space technology sector and generally technology transfer. IDA has dedicated platform for technology transfer between polish companies: Technology Transfer Platform.

2) Accompany and accelerate innovative projects that drive progress, by coordinating and structuring a large community of researchers, administrations and companies in the fields of data and artificial intelligence, and by creating synergies between public and private players on a national, European and international scale.

entityDescription: Domenico Capolongo, PhD, is an Associate Professor of Physical Geography and Geomorphology at the University of Bari Aldo Moro, Italy. His research primarily focuses on geomorphological processes and hydrogeological risks, with particular attention to landslides and erosion in rapidly evolving landscapes. He employs advanced GIS and remote sensing techniques, integrating data from field surveys, drones, and satellite imagery with numerical modelling to analyze and predict hazardous processes. Professor Capolongo is involved in the PNRR project RETURN (REducing risks, enhancing ecosystem services, and fostering Resilient communities), which aims at risk reduction and sustainable land management in areas prone to hydrogeological instability. He has an extensive publication record, with numerous research papers and citations highlighting his significant contributions to the study of geomorphological hazards.

entityDescription:
elementarhy GmbH is an innovative green technology startup dedicated to transforming the hydrogen and space economy. Founded on more than 60 years of exceptional scientific research and energy management, the company aims to provide electrochemical energy solutions through the development of Membrane Electrode Assemblies (MEAs) for electrolyzers. The founders, Arne Birth and Dr. Gustav Sievers, recognized the urgent need for energy security and cost efficiency during the European energy crisis in 2022, positioning elementarhy as a leader in the green hydrogen supply chain
The hydrogen market faces significant cost challenges, including the reliance on fossil fuels and producing molecules in space adding the need to meet ambitious decarbonization goals set by governments worldwide. Current green hydrogen production methods involve high costs, reliance on critical raw materials, and limited scalability, creating a gap for more cost efficient and sustainable solutions.
elementarhy's revolutionary technology focuses on the production of cost-efficient and scalable MEAs, which are the key part in terms of performance and costs that generates green hydrogen. By minimizing the use of critical materials like iridium and ensuring high durability and performance, elementarhy's MEAs offer an environmentally friendly way to reduce the costs of hydrogen production up to 25% to scale the hydrogen production with Levelized Costs of Hydrogen (LCOH) below �2/kg.
The global hydrogen market on earth and space is experiencing rapid growth, with over 1,572 projects and an estimated USD 680 billion in investments. The demand for green hydrogen is projected to surge due to environmental concerns, technological advancements, and regulatory incentives and further space relevant applications like satellite thruster, logisitcs and human space exploration. elementarhy is poised to capture a significant share of this expanding market by providing innovative solutions that align with global sustainability targets.
We invite investors, partners, and industry stakeholders to engage with elementarhy to enable our electrolyzer manufacturer customers to provide cost competitive and scalable green hydrogen production and accelerate the transition to a zero-emission society.

Multiverse Computing is the leading quantum AI software developer company in Europe. We apply quantum and quantum-inspired AI to solve complex problems in finance, energy, manufacturing, defense, cybersecurity, life sciences, and chemistry, delivering practical applications and tangible value today. We provide hyper-efficient software to companies wanting to gain an edge with quantum computing and artificial intelligence. 

Our flagship product, COMPACTIFAI, is an AI model compression tool that reduces AI model size while maintaining performance, leading to lower energy consumption and costs. CompactifAI is ideal for real-time processing and edge computing applications. It has been adopted by enterprises in healthcare, automotive, and telecommunications, showcasing its versatility and impact.

entityName: HELMHOLTZ - ZENTRUM FUER UMWELTFORSCHUNG GMBH - UFZ
entityDescription: The UFZ is one of the world’s leading research centres in the field of environmental research, enjoying high social recognition. It demonstrates ways in which a sustainable use of our natural resource base is possible for the benefit of both mankind and the environment. Our Mission: Biodiversity, functioning ecosystems, clean water and intact soils all make up our natural resource base. In the face of global change, employees at the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research – UFZ are united by the goal of demonstrating ways to combine societal development with a healthy environment. The UFZ conducts excellent research and takes on a shaping role in the scientific community. As a reliable partner, the UFZ supports the political arena, the economy and the general public to better understand the consequences of human actions on the environment and to develop options for social decision-making processes. For this purpose, the UFZ responds to the stimuli created by society and by producing know-how and technologies that should help to rapidly identify problems comprising conflicting priorities between the environment and society. The UFZ will consequently work on precautionary measures. In dealing with complex environmental issues, the disciplinary borders between the natural-, engineering- and social sciences need to be overcome. The UFZ has extensive competences in integrated environmental research. It boasts innovative scientific infrastructures and nurtures indispensable national and international cooperation, enabling problem-solving at the highest level. The creativity and motivation of UFZ employees, their personal and professional development and the promotion of young scientists all within a positive working environment as well as highly attractive working conditions for leading international researchers are all key factors for the successful promotion of this mission.

The Amentum company is a global leader in advanced engineering and innovative technology solutions, trusted by the United States and its allies to address their most significant and complex challenges in science, security and sustainability. We, as an Amentum branch based in Slovakia, are mainly focused on decommissioning processes and managing radioactive waste in nuclear industry mostly in Europe, providing expertise in decontamination solutions, radiation shielding protection, radiation safety and chemical analysis for nuclear power plants and facilities. By leveraging advanced technologies, strong experience and a deep understanding of regulatory frameworks, Amentum helps clients achieve environmental stewardship and energy sustainability, contributing to a safer, cleaner future while supporting mission-critical operations. We established ourselves as a trusted supplier in many countries in Europe and Asia.

We primarily focus on:

entityDescription: The European Forest Institute (EFI) is a pan-European international organization. It has 29 Member Countries, and appr. 130 member organizations from appr. 40 different countries working in diverse research fields. EFI provides forest-related knowledge around three interconnected and interdisciplinary themes: bioeconomy, resilience and governance. With a staff of over 100 experts in several offices across Europe, EFI is in a unique position to generate, connect and share knowledge at the interface between science and policy. EFI excels in carrying out projects at the European level, and has a track record of over 30 projects carried out for the European Commission DGs during the past few years. EFI puts increasing emphasis on cross-sectoral approaches in its research and development activities. It is thus in a good position to have efficient access to social, economic and environmental expertise covering all of Europe’s bio-geographical regions. The work in the field of policy support includes enhanced support for decision takers and policy makers. For example, the high-level forum on forests, ThinkForest, brings together high-level policy makers and leading European forest scientists to generate science-policy dialogue on strategic forest-related issues. EFI is quickly becoming a leading science-policy platform providing forest-related knowledge to build a sustainable future: connecting knowledge to action. www.efi.int

entityDescription:
The Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg (OVGU) was founded in 1993 and is one of the youngest German universities. It was formed in a merger of three existing institutions to create a university with a distinctive profile, so that in many areas it is able to draw on a considerably longer tradition. It is located in Magdeburg, the capital city of the federal state Saxony-Anhalt. The University comprises 9 faculties and almost 13,200 students. 

Otto von Guericke Universitaet Magdeburg has a distinctive profile. It aims to create a lean and sharply-defined structure with its main focus of expertise in the traditional areas of engineering, the natural sciences and medicine. It also views economics and management and the social sciences and humanities as essential disciplines for a modern university in the information age. 
The most prominent areas of research emphasis are the neurosciences, dynamic systems in process engineering and biomedicine, plus automotive/digital engineering. In addition, transfer-related areas of emphasis include medical technology, renewable energies, fluidised bed technology, research into dementia, computational visualistics and experimental economics. 
Affiliated institutes and the University's Transfer and Entrepreneur Center act as links between academia and industry. They facilitate businesses' access to the University's research resources while simultaneously promoting innovation. The Faculty of Medicine and University Clinic, which are located on their own campus, are the “educational home” to around 1300 trainee doctors.

entityDescription:
Our vision is to democratise access to mission planning, spacecraft operations, and to enable cost-efficient Lunar exploration for Europe.
Operating a spacecraft is an expensive and difficult task which has historically been almost exclusively carried out by national agencies since space exploration began in the 1950’s. However, the 21st century has witnessed a rapid growth of private entities entering the field. Robust, well-tested software and trained personnel with niche expertise are required to run these activities, hence smaller companies generally rely on this as a costly service provided by more well-established enterprises. Luna Space’s mission is to level the playing field by turning this into an easily accessible service.
Luna Space will offer Mission Analysis and Flight Dynamics as a Service (MAaaS, FDaaS), delivered in the cloud with a quick turnaround time and at low cost to disrupt the current market. We will focus on the lunar market in the future, which is projected to boom in the next decade.
The team has decades of complementary expertise in the space, finance and business development domains, including developing and using robust, flight-proven flight dynamics and mission analysis software, as well as building and scaling business from the ground up.
At Luna Space, our mission is to propel Europe into the forefront of the emerging (lunar) space economy.

entityDescription:
The Faculty of Civil Engineering, Architecture, and Geodesy in Split (henceforth FCEAG) is a higher education institution that was founded in 1971 as the Split Department of the Faculty of Civil Engineering of the University of Zagreb. It became independent in 1977 and transformed into an autonomous higher education and scientific research organisation in July 1991. 
FCEAG is organizing and carrying out seven study programmes in the fields of Civil Engineering, Architecture and Urban Planning and Geodesy and Geoinformatics along with various lifelong learning courses and professional education. Scientific research is organized around FCEAG laboratories and research groups engaged in the national and international research projects. Our many years of experience in mechanical engineering allow us to tailor solutions to the needs of our customers, ensuring the best possible results.Comprehensive know-how, creative solutions, and flexibility are our strengths, making us a reliable and versatile partner for our customers.

Development and Design
We turn your ideas into finished products. With good ideas, rich mechanical engineering experience, and Computer Aided Design, we are your partner for streamlined development processes and successful projects. We are creative and innovative, leveraging our expertise in various fields to achieve success with you. Even at the design stage, we support you to eliminate sources of error in material selection or manufacturing processes. Every step in the development is carefully considered, resulting in the optimal solution – efficient and cost-effective.

Individual and Series Parts
Milling and turning parts are the daily business of a mechanical engineer and are thus part of our daily tasks, as well as manufacturing techniques like 3D printing and component finishing through special surface treatments. From ASAP production deadlines to extended workbench with stock retrieval. We are happy to support you and adapt to your processes. We advise our customers on the choice of processing technique. Whether milling, turning, welding, bending, gluing, or screwing, we always seek the best solution for your needs together with you. In doing so, we draw on our expertise in all aspects of mechanical engineering.

Workpiece Carriers

We develop and supply workpiece carriers for fixing the most diverse workpieces, from small and precise to heavy and cumbersome. With our workpiece carriers, components can be further processed, transported, or stored accurately and gently. The use of CTM workpiece carriers enables both manual and automated production processes. By coordinating with your production processes, quality and manufacturing costs remain in balance.

entityDescription:
The Fondazione Edmund Mach (FEM) is a leading Italian institution active in research, technology, and technology transfer related to the agro-food sector. FEM is a public agency under private law jurisdiction. FEM comprises a Research and Innovation Centre (CRI), a Training and Education Centre, and a Technology Transfer Centre, all carrying out activities in the fields of agro-food and sustainable development. Currently, FEM makes up a full-scale rural centre stretching out over a 14-hectare campus, with classrooms, greenhouses, offices. FEM owns 120 hectares of land cultivated with apple and grape and 80ha of forests. Nowadays around 800 students attend classes, assisted by over 100teachers. 58% of FEM personnel are males. The majority of collaborators are 30-50 years old. 15% percent is of foreign nationality. The Edmund Mach Foundation is organized into Centers geared to the specific aims of: 1. Education and Training (CIF); 2. Research and Innovation (CRI); 3. Technical Experimentation and Transfer (CTT). Today, the goal of improving the characteristics and potential of agriculture is reached through the integration between the school, the Research and Innovation Centre (CRI), and the technical support provided to companies and farms. FEM promotes and enhances, through research and innovation, the Trentino-land based economy in Italy, aiming at the improvement of agricultural and forestry productions and the improvement of the quality and nutritional value of food products. It also supports the region’s environmental resources through the development and promotion of low-impact agricultural practices, the study and preservation of biodiversity and the characterization of the alpine and subalpine ecosystems.FEM expresses research capacities at the highest international and national levels, as witnessed by a third-party official evaluation in 2022 (ANVUR): FEM ranked 18th (out of 65) in chemistry, 7th in agricultural and veterinary sciences (out of 39), and 3rd (out of 75) in biology, at the national level, when compared with all the involved institution. FEM ranked 4th overall within the above mentioned scientific groups when compared to homologous institutions.

In the coming 3 years (from 2022 to 2025) FEM will play a pivotal role at National level in the deployment of the activities related to research within the EU Recovery Funds and EU Green Deal framework. FEM will be involved in 3 major initiatives. In the National Research Centre for Agricultural Technologies (Agritech) aiming to generate Key Enabling Technologies, it will act particularly in the field of crop genetics and development of more resilient varieties. Within the National Biodiversity Future Center, FEM will favour the use of innovative approaches for biodiversity conservation, with a particular focus on water and terresterial ecosystems in the alpine area
From 2018 to 2022, more than 100 research projects have been granted to CRI researchers (of which more than 40 granted by the EU), both as partners or coordinators. About 50 projects were financed by the European Union

entityName: University of Aplied Sciences Hrvatsko zagorje Krapina
entityDescription:
The Study Programmes
The University runs three bachelor study programmes:
- Information Science
- Traffic Logistics
- Operational Management.
The main purpose is educating young experts who will eventually assume leadership of the business and infrastructure sectors representing the core of the economic and societal development of the Krapinsko-zagorska County.
The education programme for our students is based on exploring disciplines necessary for successful management of business operations related to traffic logistics, enterprise and information technology. The selection of specific subjects, their distribution per study year and the exploration span of each discipline are a harmonised principally with the defined needs of the student. Core disciplines such as mathematics, statistics, foreign languages, information science and economy provide students with general knowledge necessary in everyday trade. Specific subjects ensure the acquisition of competences necessary for successful professional performance and the performance of complex expert operations as well as specific knowledge needed for the further economic development of the County.
The documents, the work and the structure of the institution are completely congruent with the principles of the Bologna Declaration. The students receive 180 ECTS upon completion of the study programme, therefore satisfying the criteria for further postgraduate and doctoral studies.
The classes are held in small groups and the University has as its disposal space and equipment above the Croatian average. All main course holders are ether MA or PhD with tenure, lecturer, assistant professor or professor status. All classes are held in Krapina.
The institution is not allowed to divide profits among founders. It has the obligation to re-invest it in improving the study conditions.
The University is compatible with similar institutions within the EU, allowing it to engage in student exchanges, such as the Erasmus programme and other EU programmes, possibly also through bilateral agreements.

Development
The University is open for developing further study programmes. With the amendment of the founding contract, the County gained a leading role in proposing and inciting the development of new study programmes in the interest of developing the whole area of the County.
Within the bigger picture of the development of the County, the University represents a knowledge centre. There are many experts based in the County that had to seek work in Zagreb. They showed good will to get involved in the work of the University and become the core around which high expertise is developed and at the same time the motivation for further postgraduate studying that will inevitably result in a higher number of expert higher-educated people in the County.
Opening of the University “Hrvatsko zagorje Krapina” led to the advancement of the economic and social status of the citizens, together with the advancement of education and the improvement of the quality of life. All of these features result in motivating the higher-educated professionals for staying in the County.
The study programmes per se empower young experts for employment and entrepreneurial initiative.

It became an excellent scientific institute that mainly focused on mathematics, physics, nuclear chemistry, materials, electronics, IT and nuclear reactors. entityName: Competency Center for Advanced Engineering Nova Gradiška d.o.o.
entityDescription:
CEKOM NING, headquartered in Nova Gradiška, Croatia, is a leading organization dedicated to research, development, and innovation in advanced engineering. Established as a pivotal element of regional innovation infrastructure, CEKOM NING operates as a center for excellence, fostering technological advancement, knowledge dissemination, and industrial collaboration.
The organization specializes in high-speed metal processing, additive manufacturing, robotics, automation, and thermal treatment of materials. CEKOM NING offers a comprehensive suite of services, including education and training programs, contractual research for SMEs, and the development of innovative solutions for industry challenges.
CEKOM NING has built a robust track record of successful projects, including the flagship initiative, Competence Centre for Advanced Engineering Nova Gradiška, a €15.8 million project aimed at enhancing R&D infrastructure, promoting private sector investment in innovation, and driving economic growth. The organization has collaborated with renowned academic institutions such as FERIT Osijek, the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Naval Architecture in Zagreb, and regional high schools, thereby strengthening its ties with the academic and industrial sectors.
In 2024 alone, CEKOM NING provided training to over 200 participants, supported six startups through advanced engineering expertise, and extended its network of collaborators. The organization remains committed to addressing the skills gap in Industry 4.0, robotics, and automation by developing non-formal education programs in collaboration with national employment agencies.

Robosys is a leading provider of Artificial Intelligence (AI) powered Maritime Autonomy and Smart Shipping software with two decades of experience in the field.
Our VOYAGER AI software can transform a new or existing vessel into a fully autonomous Uncrewed Surface Vessel (USV), capable of independent navigation, autonomous collision avoidance, obstacle and anti-grounding with dynamic route optimisation.
We use our own cutting edge AI and Machine Learning (ML) algorithms to provide scalable levels of autonomy, from Remote Control up to and including full IMO degree 4 Autonomy.
In its simplest form, VOYAGER AI can also provide Collision Avoidance Decision Aid (CADA) support which is COLREGs compliant, for a vessel’s master to enhance the safety, productivity and efficiency of a lean crewed ships.
At the next stage as an AI based “Intelligent” Marine Pilot it can autonomously control a lean crewed ship. Or, in a fully fledged USV, VOYAGER AI enables remote control & piloting, fully autonomous navigation and control including obstacle, collision and grounding avoidance utilising the latest AI enabled vessel identification and perception systems.

entityDescription:
Founded in 2003, the University of Dubrovnik (UNIDU) is one of the youngest public universities in Croatia, situated in the southernmost region of the country on the Adriatic coast. Despite its relatively recent establishment, UNIDU has rapidly developed into a dynamic and interdisciplinary institution offering degree programmes and conducting research in fields such as digital economy, tourism, ecology, electrical engineering, computer science, maritime sciences, art and cultural heritage restoration. In recent years, the University has increasingly focused on emerging technologies, particularly in exploring the application of artificial intelligence, intelligent systems and information technologies to optimise and manage complex processes across various sectors. Through these efforts, UNIDU has positioned itself as an important regional knowledge hub capable of addressing the challenges faced by communities balancing the preservation of cultural, historical and natural resources with the demands of sustainable development and industry. 
As the most internationalised Croatian university in terms of Erasmus+ student share, UNIDU plays a unique role in fostering inclusive growth within the European Higher Education Area. It provides high quality education to a diverse and mobile student body, helping to shape future professionals who are able to contribute to their communities and beyond.
UNIDU’s integrated structure allows for strong interdisciplinary collaboration in both teaching and research. Its scholars from fields such as engineering, ecology, economics, biotechnology, maritime sciences, computer science and cultural heritage work together on innovative projects aimed at solving pressing global challenges. The University’s mission is to produce and transfer knowledge that is both academically sound and socially relevant, benefiting not only the local and regional environment but also a wider European and international context.

entityDescription:
Volvero is an app for sharing vehicles that connects owners with people who need one, saving time and money. We improve quality and security through AI and advanced technologies with crystal-clear full insurance coverage. Volvero is easier, safer and more reliable than any other app in the field.

Volvero is a drive sharing app where owners can share their vehicles with drivers. Our app creates a system in which one can have access to a car, a motorcycle, or commercial vehicle in the most efficient and sustainable way saving time and money. By registering on our platform owners can set the sharing time, distance, price, and other terms, being able to accept or decline drivers’ request. At the same time, drivers are able to choose any vehicle and terms of sharing that best suit their needs. With the help of AI and advanced technologies, Volvero guarantees maximum security and transparency providing necessary information such as the performance of owners, drivers, and vehicles. Overcoming outdated paperwork, Volvero creates smart contracts at the start of the ride while one of a kind built-in insurance covers drivers and all kinds of vehicles. 

Modern society is in need of new efficient transportation alternatives. Indeed, public transport is crowded, inflexible or absent, especially in extra-urban areas. At the same time, car rental services are rigid and expensive, thus people not owning a private vehicle are restricted from free movement. Still, car ownership is not feasible taking into account that the society is facing a high underutilization of vehicles with cars not being used 96% of the time occupying parking spaces and producing pollution. This includes corporations that own vehicles that could be monetized and car dealers that are looking for new business models as millennials are not interested in car purchasing. The problem, therefore, has three dimensions which are people in need of economic transportation for different needs, owners in need of reducing their vehicles’ costs, and the issue of overproduction and under usage of vehicles contributing to pollution and waste of resources.

By providing a marketplace Volvero connects owners and drivers effectively bringing to use underutilized vehicles and providing an extensive range of efficient mobility possibilities to the drivers. Having this access to transportation enhances people’s well-being by giving them freedom of moving, more possibilities, and eliminating social inequality. At the same time owners, both private and commercial can significantly reduce their vehicles’ costs and make the ownership feasible. Car rentals and dealers have a chance to switch from the outworn business model to a profitable modern one. With Volvero fewer vehicles wander in the cities as each one is utilized more, raising the actual average use of them and favouring a fast turnover of old cars with newer less polluting ones. These factors entail a pollution reduction, and traffic jams, reducing the need for urban spaces for parking areas, thus converting them into more useful and productive facilities.
