entityDescription:
National Institute of Chemistry (NIC) is the scientifically excellent, established and breakthrough research institution based in Slovenia, Europe. With our cutting-edge research, we are enriching the global treasury of knowledge by solving the most pressing challenges facing society including health, sustainable energy, climate change, circular economy and safe food. Basic and applied research are focused towards fields that are of long-term importance to both Slovenia and the world: biotechnology, environmental protection, empirical and theoretical chemistry, analytical chemistry, materials research, and chemical engineering, through which the Institute performs a world class basic research and supports the needs for technology transfer of the domestic chemical, pharmaceutical, and food industries.
Our research goals push the boundaries of science and create new values. We successfully transfer knowledge to industry and, in the long-term, support the role of science in the development of society. We enable scientific excellence through collaboration with the best global research institutions, groups and individuals. We are members of international multidisciplinary research networks, such as CERIC-ERIC, SUSCHEM, EMIRI, EERA Bioenergy, Fuel Cells and Hydrogen Joint Undertaking, Vision 2020, Slovenian Strategic Research and Innovation Partnership (SRIP), Centre of Excellence for Low-Carbon Technologies, Slovenian Business and Research Association. We aim to be provide the stimulating environment and open learning space where our 100 young researchers can develop their curiosity and realise their research creativity in PhD work. By doing so, we ensure future generations lives benefit from the profession. NIC has 350 employees, of which around 280 carry out research work in 8 departments & 2 infrastructure centres. We provide our employees with inspiring working conditions in which they can carry out their professional mission. We are proud that our interpersonal relationships are based on an open, integrated, equitable and inclusive culture that is not limited by gender or race. We strive to become the reason for excellent Slovenian scientists returning from abroad. With our mission, we contribute to the well-being of society and are an example of excellence.
NIC’s employees publish more than 200 scientific papers per year and are strongly involved in international basic and applied projects. Research is oriented towards the development of new technologies and products, which will help to ensure the long-term development of Slovenia, and which are internationally relevant. National Institute of Chemistry one of the leading Slovenian organisations for graduate-level education and training.
Industry is an important partner of the Institute in these endeavours. There is a number of Slovenian companies with whom the Institute has entered into a close long-term cooperation, as well as with a number of innovative international companies from pharma to nanomaterials. This kind of cooperation accounts for the 20% of the income of the Institute. NIC is also a constituting member of several excellence and competence centres, such as the Centres of Excellence ENFIST, Polymers and Low-Carbon Technologies.

SENER Sp. z o.o. is a subsidiary of SENER SIS, well recognised Spanish company operating in space sector since 1967.
In Space, SENER has developed from its beginnings mechanisms and mechanical systems that cover almost all the needs of the Flight Segment. Moreover, SENER supplies essential items for completing successful missions, such as Attitude or Control Systems (AOCS) and Guidance, Navigation and Control systems (GNC). All this is backed up with technical solvency, successfully proven with more than 20 satellites and spacecrafts currently operating with SENER equipment on board. In fact, SENER has a major history of meting deliveries, with which it has achieved a reputation for quality and reliability in Space. 
In its 40 years, SENER has supplied over 150 systems for 46 satellites without a single failure. The company has taken part in ESA and NASA missions such as the Hubble Space Telescope, Columbus, Envisat, Rosetta, Meteosat, Herschel and Planck, Metop, Mars Science Laboratory or GAIA, as well as commercial missions such as Hispasat, Spainsat or XTAR-EUR.
SENER Sp. z o.o. is operating as Polish company with activities performed fully in house but benefitting from support and technology transfer from SENER SIS on the basis of exploring the synergies and complementarities.
Activities of the company are focused on space segment and space system engineering in the following areas:
¿ Mechanical and Actuation Systems (elements, equipments and systems)
¿ Navigation & Space System Engineering (Systems Engineering, GNC/AOCS)
¿ Optical Systems (Complete sensors, Instruments).

entityDescription:
The French National Institute for Industrial Environment and Risks (Ineris) is an industrial and commercial public establishment under the aegis of the Ministry of the Environment.

Ineris was created in 1990 as a result of the merger between the French Centre for Studies and Research into Collieries (Cerchar) and the Institute of Applied Chemical Research (Ircha).
It has accumulated nearly 70 years of expertise and knowledge.
The Institute’s mission is to contribute to the prevention of risks caused by economic activities to health, environment, and the safety of people and goods.
It conducts research programs with the aim of improving our understanding of the phenomena that are likely to lead to risk situations or damage to health and the environment, and of further developing its expertise in prevention. It works to expand its scientific and technical capabilities in the fields of accidental risk, chronic risk, and ground-level / subterranean risks (mining), and makes them available to public authorities, local authorities, and businesses to help them make the decisions best suited to improving environmental safety.

entityDescription:
Autroni AS is a growth company founded in 2015, specializing in professional robotic lawnmowers for international airports. The company has developed innovative solutions that enable robotic lawnmowers to operate efficiently at airports without requiring closures during mowing operations.
While the initial focus is on grass cutting, Autroni’s technology has the potential to address other operational needs in airports, industrial areas, and public spaces where safety is paramount.
Autroni’s reliable mowing robots maintain airport safety areas in compliance with the strictest safety standards. Extensive testing at Stavanger Airport, Norway, demonstrated that robotic mowing is a cost-effective, sustainable, and round-the-clock solution tailored for airports. Additionally, it significantly reduces the presence of birds and mammals, enhancing aviation safety.
The company leverages the expertise of Yamabiko Europe, a leader in robotic mowing for large grass surfaces. Yamabiko Europe is part of Yamabiko, a globally recognized outdoor equipment manufacturer listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, renowned for its innovative products in agriculture, forestry, and landscaping.
Since 2017, Autroni has successfully deployed solar-powered mowing robots at Stavanger Airport. A fleet of 18 robots trims every square meter of safety areas at low height every 72 hours, drastically limiting the presence of birds and mammals in the turf and reducing bird strike risks. This automated approach simplifies operations and lowers costs by eliminating the need for off-hours personnel, extensive training, safety clearances, and heavy machinery.
Following the success at Stavanger, plans are underway to expand robotic mowing to other airports in the Avinor group.
Today, Autroni serves customers across Europe, Asia, America, and Australia, positioning itself as a global leader in robotic solutions for safety-critical environments.

entityDescription:
Compute Maritime is an innovation company providing AI-powered tools and solutions to help the maritime industry achieve its net-zero goals.

Our first tool in this effort is NeuralShipper™, the world’s first GenAI tool for ship design and optimisation. It is built on physics-informed diffusion and transformer models and trained on over 100,000 physically validated 3D ship hull designs across various ship types.NeuralShipper™ comprises three key modules: (I) design, (II) optimisation, and (III) simulation.

Our innovation lies in NeuralShipper’s design module, which integrates interactive and generative design capabilities into the preliminary design stage, enabling the creation of both customer-centred and high-performance designs. The generative design capability allows both experienced and novice ship designers to rapidly explore efficient design concepts. The interactive feature is particularly tailored for the yacht industry, where designs must be not only high-performing but also visually appealing.

In addition to design creation and optimisation, NeuralShipper™ enables users to develop machine learning-based surrogate models to bypass computationally expensive physical solvers for performance prediction. While surrogate modelling is not new, it has traditionally required strong machine-learning expertise. With NeuralShipper™, this process becomes straightforward, requiring only basic data and programming skills, making it easy for designers to get started.

We currently have four users on board. Among these, a key partner is Siemens, a leading provider of engineering design and simulation tools. The other users include two yacht design offices and MARIN, Europe’s largest research institution supporting the shipbuilding and offshore industries. Additionally, we are in discussions with well-known ship design firms, including Feadship, Delta Marine, and Damen.

entityDescription: Cerebri is committed to sustainable equality of care in the field of telemedical electroencephalography (EEG) diagnostics, so that an EEG will be possible for everyone, everywhere. Since almost 50% of all hospitals in Germany do not have EEG diagnostics available (especially rural hospitals) and patients can only receive an EEG with considerable resources and costs, Cerebri will lead to a reduction in costs and resources in the healthcare system. At the same time, we are responding to the challenges of false-positive or false-negative findings and the lack of transparency and diversity of medical findings by providing specialized neurology specialists with years of experience and assisting artificial intelligence. The need for EEG diagnostics - not only due to demographic change - is constantly growing, so Cerebri will also enable home applications such as long-term recordings (home monitoring) for patients. This will facilitate access to medical diagnostics where previously there were restrictions. With a location-independent telemedicine platform, Cerebri offers an innovative solution for broader availability and improved care.

entityDescription:
Materialise will celebrate its 35th anniversary this year (2025). Materialise incorporated over three decades of 3D printing experience into a range of software solutions, 3D printing services and applications. Materialise is headquartered in Leuven (Belgium) with branches worldwide. Materialise combines the largest group of software developers in the AM industry with the largest 3D printing facilities in the world. Open flexible solutions for Additive Manufacturing enable players in a wide variety of industries to make steps in applying AM for their business context, including healthcare, automotive, aerospace, art and design, and consumer goods. Materialise is known as an innovative company which strongly enables other players to build innovative 3D printing applications in their own domain.
Materialise has been built around three core competences: 3D-printing known-how, engineering of applications and software development. The unique value of our company is that these competences are present in one entity, and we can leverage on strong synergies between the different competence teams. For instance, software development can ‘crystallize’ the 3D printing know-how and benefit from early testing and validation of software in the Manufacturing division. The Manufacturing division benefits from state-of-the-art software solutions which are continuously improved in-house. Also engineering an AM application can be done in a fast way with custom and specialized software tools.
These core competences are brought to the market in different ways through our three business segments: Manufacturing, Medical and Software.

entityDescription: Transforming Textiles AB is a Swedish deep-tech company developing Re:Weave, a dual-use circular system platform integrating smart textiles, embedded sensing, and regenerative material cycles for space and Earth applications. The company is registered and headquartered in Sweden, with full ownership, decision-making authority, and intellectual property retained within the Swedish entity. At the core of the platform is Sense-Tex, a patented smart textile and yarn technology combining embedded sensing, antimicrobial protection, durability, and recyclability by design, enabling textiles to function as both human–system interfaces and recoverable material resources. Re:Weave extends this foundation into a system-level architecture supporting autonomous operation, reduced resupply dependency, and Zero Debris principles, aligned with ESA priorities for long-duration missions and future habitats. Earth-based applications in healthcare, professional use, and circular manufacturing are used as validation pathways while maintaining space-grade design constraints.

entityDescription:
HStar builds heavy-class, reusable spaceships and develops heavy-capable, global spaceports to sell launch services to customers around the world.

The HStar rocket is capable of unlocking the next phase of industry by deploying the biggest projects that will solve tomorrow’s problems on earth and accelerate many technological transitions.

HStar is a French-US initiative where both countries contribute to finance and build the global solution for worldwide application.

The HStar rocket uses proven technology which fills an undersupplied gap in the global launch market. It is an ITAR-free, non-dependent heavy launch capability using European very high thrust engines. A patent has been registered for France and Europe application.

HStar is a cohesive team with domain expertise building rockets and spacecraft. The company employs an experienced & proven team (eg. Kineis/CNES, SES, Eutelsat, ArianeGroup, SpaceX, NASA, etc). The team has developed a detailed, multi-horizon path to build Europe’s very heavy launcher, and then expand to sell global launch transportation services to the growing demand.

HStar leverages a public-private partnership model with key European partners and champions as well as European Member States to provide European response to US launch dominance. The distinct position among launch providers utilizes a lowest-risk, systems-integration approach. The company will provide global launch with spaceport partnerships, starting in French Guiana, the US, and Australia.

HStar has an accelerated path to first orbital launch in 2032, and launch services capable of one to two launches per week by 2036.

entityName: University of Zagreb Faculty of Geodesy - Chair of Satellite Geodesy
entityDescription:
The Chair of Satellite Geodesy is one of six departments within the Institute of Geomatics at the Faculty of Geodesy. Faculty members of the Chair include: Željko Bačić, PhD (Full Professor), Danijel Šugar, PhD (Associate Professor), Zvonimir Nevistić, PhD (Post.Doc researcher), Petar Jelić, MSc. (Assistant). 
The core areas of the Chair's activities cover all aspects of satellite positioning, space geodesy and geodetic astronomy, as well as the integration of space technologies with other sensors, and systems. The Chair’s educational activities are organized through seven compulsory and elective courses. At the undergraduate level: "Satellite Positioning", "Geodetic Astronomy" and “Engineering Informatics” and at the graduate level of Geodesy and Geoinformatics: "Navigation", "Integrated Systems in Geomatics", "Space Geodesy," "Satellite Geodesy - Project" and "Geodetic Astronomy - Project". 
The Chair's scientific and professional work focuses on the disciplines and courses it covers. In addition to these areas, Chair staff are actively involved in research on the application of GNSS for geodetic and non-geodetic purposes, investigating the effects of GNSS interference, monitoring the influence of the ionosphere on GNSS measurements, spatial data infrastructure, disaster risk reduction, drone applications, indoor navigation, application of spatial data in new concepts such as smart cities and digital twins and remote sensing.
The results of the Chair's work are reflected in a large number and wide range of published papers and participation in international and domestic conferences as well as leadership and participation in numerous scientific, professional, and educational projects (Erasmus+ CHBE and Strategic partnership). Chair staff lead and actively participate in the Copernicus Academy and Relay Croatia organizations and promoting space technologies in the Republic of Croatia through various channels.

entityDescription: Human in Motion Robotics (HMR) is a Canadian pioneer in developing next-generation exoskeleton technology rooted in advanced humanoid robotics and AI. Supported by a world-class team of engineers, scientists, and clinicians, HMR has created XoMotion™, an innovative lower-limb robotic exoskeleton designed to deliver superior rehabilitation outcomes that surpass the capabilities of existing technologies in the current rehabilitation model. XoMotion is the world’s most advanced wearable robotic exoskeleton, designed to assist individuals with mobility impairments due to spinal cord injuries, stroke, and other neurological conditions in standing up and walking. This humanoid robotics-based medical device offers unparalleled multi-directional locomotion support through self-balancing and hands-free functionality, enabling customizable and task-oriented robotic rehabilitation treatments across various stages of recovery. XoMotion™ not only enhances patient outcomes but also reduces cognitive load and physical strain on therapists in rehabilitation clinics. The technology has recently received Health Canada approval for sales in Canada and is currently undergoing clinical trials in the US for FDA approval. Also, it has recently received an Innovation Award for CES 2025 (Las Vegas, January 7-10, 2025), the world’s largest electronics and IT exhibition, in the robotics category. The CES Innovation Awards recognize outstanding design and engineering in consumer technology products across various categories. XoMotion, a cutting-edge robotic exoskeleton, has been acknowledged for its potential to revolutionize the field of robotic rehabilitation.

entityName: Fondation Française pour la Recherche sur la Biodiversité
entityDescription:
The French Foundation for Biodiversity Research (FRB) is a platform between the various scientific actors and the society stakeholders on biodiversity.

The FRB was created in 2008, following the Grenelle de l’environnement (a series of political meetings organised in France in September and December 2007), on the initiative of the ministries in charge of research and ecology, by eight public research institutions. They have since been joined by LVMH, Ineris, the University of Montpellier and the French Biodiversity Agency (OFB), bringing the number of founding members to 11.

The Foundation’s mission is to support and act with research to increase and transfer knowledge about biodiversity. The FRB is a foundation for scientific cooperation under private law. It operates independently and has about 47 employees. The FRB has been headed by Hélène Soubelet since April 2017, with Denis Couvet as President since January 2021.

entityDescription: The Seatizens for Plankton Planet (S4P2) Association is a non-profit non-governmental organization governed by French law, specifically the 1901 law on associations. Founded in 2016 during the pilot phase of the Plankton Planet project (Vargas et al., 2022, Frontiers in Marine Science), S4P2 brings together “seatizens”— i.e. all sorts of seafarers and sea users - who are eager to discover, measure, and understand the invisible living majority in the oceans: plankton or the ocean microbiome. The Association has two primary missions: (i) ocean microbiome literacy to raise awareness about planktonic ecosystems, and (ii) the recruitment, training, and coordination of seatizens to build up a cooperative, cost-effective, and sustainable global measurement of aquatic microscopic life. Overall, the goal of the Plankton Planet initiative (in which S4P2 is one of the running entity) is to establish, by 2030, the first seatizen-based standard measure of the surface ocean microbiome across planetary scales, allowing to monitor and understand the evolution and health of the ocean.

The Association has two primary missions: (i) ocean microbiome literacy to raise awareness about planktonic ecosystems, and (ii) the recruitment, training, and coordination of seatizens to build up a cooperative, cost-effective, and sustainable global measurement of aquatic microscopic life. Overall, the goal of the Plankton Planet initiative (in which S4P2 is one of the running entity) is to establish, by 2030, the first seatizen-based standard measure of the surface ocean microbiome across planetary scales, allowing to monitor and understand the evolution and health of the ocean.

entityDescription:
The Professorship for Space Technology focuses its research on three main areas: Nanosatellites for Extraterrestrial Missions, Space Systems & Higher Autonomy, and UAP & SETI Research.

Key achievements include the fully in-house developed, built, and operated nanosatellite missions SONATE and SONATE-2. SONATE-2, a 6U+ satellite launched in 2024, integrates AI technologies for in-orbit training and features an electric propulsion system and a novell star tracker, building on the experiences and components of its predecessor. The earlier SONATE mission pioneered autonomy in nanosatellites with systems like ASAP-Light for automated event detection and ADIA-Light for onboard diagnostics.

The professorship also operates a remote-controlled telescope in Spain for the detection of lunar transient phenomena, a telescope in Würzburg for SSA research, and a SkyCam-System for UAP detection. Additional expertise includes the design, construction, and operation of star trackers and subsystems for small satellites, as well as research into autorotative landing systems for interplanetary missions.

entityName: HELCOM - Baltic Marine Environment Protection Commission
entityDescription:
The Baltic Marine Environment Protection Commission – also known as the “Helsinki Commission” or “HELCOM” – was established in 1974 pursuant to and at the same time as theConvention on the Protection of the Marine Environment of the Baltic Sea Area(the “Helsinki Convention”).
The Helsinki Commission meets annually, with allContracting Partiesparticipating: Denmark, Estonia, the European Union, Finland, Germany, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Russia and Sweden. In addition, meetings at the Ministerial level are held every few years (usually every three years). The Contracting Parties are represented by Heads of Delegation (HOD).
The Commission adoptsRecommendationsrelated to the protection of the marine environment and sustainable maritime activities, decides on the budget and makes other key decisions. Decisions are made by consensus.
Thechairmanshipof the Commission rotates between the Contracting Parties every two years, according to their alphabetical order in English, the working language of the Commission.
The working structure of HELCOM consists of the meetings of the Helsinki Commission, the Heads of Delegation, and the eight mainHELCOM Working Groups. The HELCOM work and meetings are coordinated by the HELCOM Secretariat.

The HELCOM Secretariat coordinates the work and meetings of the Helsinki Commission, and ensures that theContracting Partiesmeet their obligations under theHelsinki Convention. The headquarters of HELCOM, the Secretariat, is located in Helsinki, Finland.

entityDescription: Herobots is an innovative startup focused on developing soft robotics solutions for extreme applications. Soft robotics represents a new frontier in robotics, enabling the execution of remote operations in confined and inaccessible environments where conventional robots cannot operate, with significant applications in the nuclear and space sectors. In these fields, there is a pressing need for solutions aimed at decommissioning, such as dismantling old nuclear facilities or decommissioning obsolete satellites, to support the green transition. To address this, Herobots proposes the use of long-reach soft robots capable of accessing confined spaces and performing operations with precision. However, the flexibility of these robots can pose challenges, such as positioning errors and unwanted vibrations if not properly controlled. To overcome this issue, Herobots has developed a series of software tools for predicting their mechanical behavior and for active control, helping remote operators safely teleoperate the robots.

entityDescription:
Our story began in 2020, when, after decades of working on the development of the first humanoid robots commercialized worldwide, we founded Keybotic in Barcelona with the goal of developing robotic technology to meet the specific needs of the industrial sector. We encountered dangerous inspections carried out by people because there were no alternatives: a maintenance technician supervising the plant and visually checking the equipment, inspecting confined spaces, or manually reading gauges in areas with toxic or asphyxiating gases.
To address this issue, Keybotic built fully autonomous robot dogs capable of accessing any location a human could reach, including stairs and unstable terrain, for industrial inspections. With this technology, we won first place at the DARPA Robotics Challenge, competing against MIT and the world’s best universities. This victory earned us the highest global recognition in robotics, awarded by the United States government, confirming that our autonomy and fleet coordination capabilities are the most advanced in the world.
The Keyper can access any area, including those dangerous for humans, and autonomously monitor facilities. It detects gas leaks, hot spots, steam leaks, reads instruments, detects intruders, and sends real-time alarms to the control center. Additionally, it generates 3D maps with point clouds to be used by engineering departments. In other words, the Keyper performs fully autonomous maintenance and security routes, inspecting facilities and alerting when there is an issue. This improves personnel safety, increases production uptime, and reduces costs through continuous monitoring and predictive maintenance.

entityDescription:
It should be noted that Frederick University is the registered Trade/Business name of Mesokeleas Ltd. I.e. both names correspond to the same legal entity. 
Frederick University (FredU) is an energetic and vibrant private university operating in the Republic of Cyprus. Since its establishment (2007), FredU managed to achieve significant growth, both in terms of student population, faculty members, and academic infrastructure. FredU employs about 250 (fte) faculty, with 4500 students enrolled annually on average and operates from two campuses. FredU is recognized as the University that offers novel and innovative programs of study that address societal needs and, primarily, as the university that exhibits high social sensitivity and responsibility. It offers a broad range of academic programs of study (more than 80) in the areas of Science, Engineering, Business, Arts, Architecture, Media, Humanities, Health, and Education. FredU has also developed the necessary experience and e-learning infrastructure for offering accredited programs of study through Distance Learning and has been awarded with the E-xcellence Associates in Quality label. 
Furthermore, FredU hosts an "UNESCO Chair on Lifelong Learning and Adult Education" since 2020. In the same year, FredU joined the Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN), becoming one of the founding members of Cyprus' national network. In the latest Times Higher Education Impact Rankings 2023, Frederick University ranked among the top 201-300 Universities, the only University in Cyprus and Greece to achieve this. It has also scored highly for its positive impact and meaningful work on specific SDGs, having ranked 44th globally for Quality Education (SDG4) and 100th for Affordable and Clean Energy (SDG7). As part of its internationalization strategy and further engagement with ERA and EEA, FredU has also joint EU CONEXUS a European University alliance for Smart Urban Coastal Sustainability. Furthermore, FredU has been ranked in the top 200 universities in the world in the QS International Trade Rankings 2023. Being the only Cypriot university to appear in this ranking indicates the strength and dominance of our Maritime Commence & Transport Department in the field.
FredU's academic staff, either organized in multidisciplinary teams or individually, is involved in a wide range of research, educational and cultural activities relevant to their specializations. The research initiatives and activities that are being carried out by its faculty, have been funded predominantly from external sources through competitive national and European programs, including HORIZON Europe/2020, LIFE, ERASMUS+, ESA, FP7 and from Regional Funds (INTERREG). Besides the self-funded creative and other projects, the University staff has implemented or currently running more than 320 RDI and consulting projects, the majority of which coordinated by FredU faculty and researchers. As a consequence, the necessary services have been developed (e.g. Research & Interconnection, Financial, International & Public Relations) that provide the required support for the administrative, legal and financial management of funded projects.

It is heavily involved in all aspects of scientific research into renewable energy generation, consumption, storage and distribution using photovoltaic systems in collaboration with European and National projects. entityDescription: Geofem is a SME consultancy specializing in the fields of Satellite Remote Sensing and Geotechnical Engineering. This combination of specializations, allows us to offer unique services to our customers. Our remote sensing projects are mainly in Earth Observation and cover a wide range of fields: ground and infrastructure displacement monitoring, water resources management, atmospheric pollution, agriculture, change detection, disaster monitoring and resilience, soil subsidence etc. Our engineers have a thorough grounding in satellite image analysis techniques and radar image analysis. For our projects, we use specialized software. For our satellite remote sensing work, we use ENVI-SARscape, SNAP and GIS tools to perform optical and radar satellite analysis. For our geotechnical work we use Plaxis 2D and 3D finite element analysis software, as well as other support software, to perform designs and assessments of geotechnical structures. We specify and supervise site investigations and interpret the results to obtain appropriate input parameters for soil models. We also authored the popular NAFEMS guidebook "Obtaining parameters for geotechnical analysis". Geofem staff are performing an important role in the evolution of Eurocode 7, particularly to improve its use with numerical methods, and we are experienced in the implementation of Eurocode 7.

entityDescription: Alpha Impulsion was founded in late 2022 and patented hybrid autophage propulsion, a space launch vehicle architecture proposing to use a solid fuel as the launcher's fuselage and tank for its liquid oxidiser. This disruptive technology removes the need for tanks, which represent half the dry mass, enabling a single-stage-to-orbit trajectory. These simplifications will allow the company to propose the lowest environmental impact ever for a launch service in 2028 and reducing the cost of access to LEO by an order of magnitude. This will allow this European launcher to compete with advantages against the american leader that currently dominates the European smallsat launch market. Alpha Impulsion will provide dedicated launches for smallsats up to 1000kg, evolving towards reutilization capability before 2035 to further improve the launch capacity. In April 2023, the company started developing Ambre, the first autophage rocket, and fired the engine for the first time in January 2024. Most ground tests were done at the present date (10/24), enabling a static fire at the end of the year and an atmospheric flight in early 2025. Going forward from this proof of concept, this technological breakthrough requires a 3-year R&D roadmap on the propulsion system and launcher architecture, which Alpha Impulsion is leading with an increasing number of European partners, being implanted in France and Italy to develop the architecture axis where the required skills are, and working towards a larger scale engine prototype with the University of Glasgow, one of the leading research bodies in autophage propulsion. The technology is also appliable to in-space propulsion for high energy missions (orbit raising, deorbitating, inter-planetary missions) and Alpha Impulsion is starting a line of development for a prototype system with Thales Alenia Space as the prime user.

Calirad is a company founded in 2022 and based in Zagreb, Croatia. Calirad specializes in robotics and IoT systems development and is co-founded by Juraj Peršić, a Ph.D. holder in robotics, and Marin Vuković, an associate professor in electrical engineering with expertise in cybersecurity and IoT, who is also a rally race driver and organizer.

entityDescription:
Design & Data GmbH is a privately owned company located in Cologne and Braunschweig, Germany. It is recognized as a leading provider of crossmedia services to the Aerospace and Science sectors. Design & Data has been operating for 6 years in providing crossmedia support to the European Space Agency (ESA), the European Southern Observatory (ESO), EUMETSAT, the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) and the German Space Agency (DLR). 

In 2014 Design & Data won several awards for their video and crossmedia productions such as DLR’s web site to mark the 10th anniversary of Mars Express and the Rosetta mission campaign for ESA. The Rosetta mission, which culminated in the landing of the space probe Philae on comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko, received major publicity and media coverage. To date our Rosetta Cartoon videos have been watched over 600.000 times on the ESA YouTube channel.

Below is a list of the awards won by Design & Data GmbH: 
- Silver Communicator Award 2014: 10th anniversary Mars Express web site for DLR
- Gold Communicator Award 2014: Rosetta mission campaign video “#WakeUpRosetta – Once upon a time…” 
- Gold W3 Award 2014: Rosetta mission campaign video: “#WakeUpRosetta – Once upon a time…” 
- FastForward Science web video competition (2nd Place #Scitainment): Rosetta mission campaign video: “Rosetta - Fabulous fables and tales of tails”

In addition Design & Data has taken a leading role in contributing towards the creation of a European entrepreneurial space sector with a thriving start-up community. In April 2015 Design & Data co-organized the 1st European Startup Weekend Space, a business hackathon event that brought 80 participants from 18 countries to Bremen and turned the event into a Silicon Valley style Makerspace of innovation. The event generated 27 pitches, 11 business concepts of which 3 have been awarded with prizes. Our long-term goal is to create an interdisciplinary ecosystem of entrepreneurship driven innovation to Europe's space sector.

Please consult our web page for references to our work:

entityDescription:
Pangea Aerospace is a company dedicated to providing advanced chemical propulsion systems for the space industry, from the Newton to the Mega Newton, based on three key principles: high efficiency, sustainability, and reusability. Our disruptive propulsion technology is aimed at increasing profitability for our clients, such as launch service providers, launcher manufacturers or satellite operators.
The range of products developed by Pangea Aerospace utilizes green propellants and provides higher performance compared to existing solutions on the market. 
In space propulsion devices run on HTP and kerosen. Thanks to their modular design, they are highly scalable, ranging from 1 N to the hundreds of N, and they enable plug-and-play functionality for versatile maneuvering.
On the other hand, our rocket engines, also modularly designed, range from a few hundred N to 1 MN, offering the best performance-to-cost ratio, thanks to Methalox-powered reusable aerospike technology. The technologies we have already mastered and the expertise we've gained pave the way to offer, as well, in the short term, a wide spectrum of solutions for high-thrust propulsion

LABORMET DUE , in Turin, is one of the most solid commercial structures in Northern Italy in the sector of scientific instruments for laboratories and quality controls. The added value of the services offered consists in the experience and professionalism acquired over the years, offering solutions tailored to the needs of customers, with the aim of solving problems related to the control of incoming materials, production control and, more generally, quality improvement processes. Labormet Due deals with the main characterization and measurement techniques: metallography , optical and electronic microscopy , image analysis , physical and mechanical tests , environmental simulation tests , chemical analysis , metrology in the research, production and quality sectors. For each supply, LABORMET DUE is able to guarantee the installation service , staff training , after-sales assistance , updates and certifications . The company's main activity is the marketing of control and measurement instruments and related consumables for the control of metal , ferrous and non-ferrous materials, plastic , rubber and composite fibres.

In addition to being able to supply the instruments, Labormet Dueoffers industrial computerized tomography services : reverse engineering , porosity evaluation, internal defect verification , dimensional analysis , are some examples of the use of this technology. entityDescription:
Disaitek’s mission:

Disaitek is dedicated to combating environmental damage and climate change by leveraging advanced Earth Observation and AI technologies.

Background: 

- Originating from space observation, Disaitek developed the first deep learning technology to detect variable orbital period exoplanets, validated by NASA and included in the Kepler database.

- Since 2021, our focus has shifted to Earth observation to address environmental issues.

Core achievements: 

Littering and illegal landfills detection platform: We have built the first platform that automates the detection and the monitoring of littering and illegal landfills with very high resolution imagery and AI. This task has been very challenging to tackle as it akin to anomaly detection and no dataset on the topic exists. Desplite this, it is now an operational platform with several customers and has been in production since mid-2022.
Canal Seine Nord Europe project: Awarded a contract with the Canal Seine Nord Europe, the largest civil engineering work of the decade in Europe, to monitor the progress and the environmental impact of the work, with satellite imagery and AI. For this we use optical VHR mono and stereo and SAR time series data. 

Technological expertise: 
Utilizing very high-resolution optical imagery, hyperspectral, and SAR time series.
Expertise in complex SAR stacks for producing interferometric products.
Developed a foundation model with high-resolution images and self-supervised learning for advanced land cover classification.

Team composition: 

Our team consists predominantly of PhDs in astrophysics, climate physics, and computer science.

Awards and recognition:

June 2023: Disaitek won the Paris Saclay Spring 50 Best Startup award in the New Space category 
October 2023: Disaitek won the Assises Nationales des Déchets award in the Technological Breakthrough category.
June 2024: Achieved 2nd place in the European Earth Observation award by EARSC, for the most innovative value-added product supporting the Green Deal agenda and Sustainable Development.

- Since 2021, our focus has shifted to Earth observation to address environmental issues.

Core achievements: 

Littering and illegal landfills detection platform: We have built the first platform that automates the detection and the monitoring of littering and illegal landfills with very high resolution imagery and AI. This task has been very challenging to tackle as it akin to anomaly detection and no dataset on the topic exists. Desplite this, it is now an operational platform with several customers and has been in production since mid-2022.
Canal Seine Nord Europe project: Awarded a contract with the Canal Seine Nord Europe, the largest civil engineering work of the decade in Europe, to monitor the progress and the environmental impact of the work, with satellite imagery and AI. For this we use optical VHR mono and stereo and SAR time series data. 

Technological expertise: 
Utilizing very high-resolution optical imagery, hyperspectral, and SAR time series.
Expertise in complex SAR stacks for producing interferometric products.
Developed a foundation model with high-resolution images and self-supervised learning for advanced land cover classification.

Team composition: 

Our team consists predominantly of PhDs in astrophysics, climate physics, and computer science.

Awards and recognition:

June 2023: Disaitek won the Paris Saclay Spring 50 Best Startup award in the New Space category 
October 2023: Disaitek won the Assises Nationales des Déchets award in the Technological Breakthrough category.
June 2024: Achieved 2nd place in the European Earth Observation award by EARSC, for the most innovative value-added product supporting the Green Deal agenda and Sustainable Development.

Archimede tackles global challenges with a platform that enables the creation of open-source decentralized applications, optimizing energy use and satellite connectivity, particularly for off-grid areas. During the 2023 Bridgestone World Solar Challenge, we traveled 3,000 km across Australia using solar energy and satellite connectivity, overcoming technological complexities and reducing costs to make satellite connectivity more accessible and reliable.
Our target market includes sectors like agriculture, smart cities, logistics, and defense, focusing on stable IoT connectivity. Key collaborations and pilot projects include:
- Monitoring over 40,000 vehicles for GLS and other logistics companies;
- Predictive maintenance for 10,000 coffee machines for MOAK Spa;
- Defense projects with RadioTech, with custom prototypes valued at over �150,000;
- Smart cities projects with ANCI, promoting sustainable mobility and data mining.
Archimede stands out for its optimized energy management, satellite connectivity, and open-source model, which ensures solutions are replicable and impactful. Revenue comes from hardware sales, SaaS subscriptions, a pay-per-use satellite API model, and strategic partnerships. We also offer premium customization and development services for clients who need tailored solutions like real-time monitoring and data analytics.
Our platform’s open-source nature allows developers to contribute, fostering a global innovation ecosystem. This ensures diverse, sustainable revenue streams and supports Archimede’s growth.
Recent Milestones
- January 2024: Archimede featured on Report (Rai 3) for the Australia challenge.
- March 2024: GLS offers a 370 sqm warehouse with a 30kW solar system for the Last Mile project.
- May 2024: Official foundation of Archimede srl.
- July 2024: Selected by Le Village by Crédit Agricole - PWC.
- July 2024: Joined ESA program with a �50,000 grant.
- August 2024: Sold first luxury solar car prototype for �150,000.
 
Sustainability Archimede supports the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):
- Goal 13: Combat climate change.
- Goal 7: Ensure access to sustainable energy.
- Goal 9: Foster sustainable infrastructure and innovation.
- Goal 10: Reduce inequalities within and between countries.
Vision In the short term, we aim to develop shared projects and launch the Archimede.world platform by 2026. By fostering global collaborations, we will scale and replicate our solutions in agriculture, smart cities, sustainable mobility, and defense, promoting Archimede's technology worldwide.

entityDescription:
CNR-ISAFOM (Institute for Agriculture and FOrestry Systems in the Mediterranean) is a research institute of the National Research Council of Italy focused on sustainable agricultural and forestry practices in Mediterranean climates.
It conducts studies on the impacts of climate change, particularly related to crop production and forest management. The institute combines various research areas, including agronomy, forestry, ecology, and hydrology, to develop solutions for sustainable land use. The aim is to improve both the quantity and quality of agricultural and forestry production, optimize the use of natural resources, and enhance the functions of agricultural and forest systems. This also involves developing and applying advanced research methods and technological innovations for monitoring and predicting the impacts and responses of agricultural and forest ecosystems to anthropogenic and climatic pressures.

entityDescription:
Obuda University (OU), established in 1879, is the second largest but highest ranked Technical University in Hungary. It aims to achieve the triplet of excellence in education, research, and innovation to address societal challenges and contribute to sustainable development on national, regional and EU level. OU has seven faculties and three doctoral schools, one excellence centre, and eight research labs. OU is participating in multiple international organizations and bilateral and international programmes (currently over 20 EU financed scientific projects). It has international relations with 90 countries, and participates 300 higher education programs and partnerships and has over 250 education and mobility agreements. OU offers innovative BA/BSc, MA/MSC, and PhD curricula, dual degrees, challenge-based approaches and an up-to-date, student-friendly, creative and supporting environment for students in order to enable them respond to the challenges set out by our globalized world, laying emphasis on both basic and applied research, internationalization, sustainable development, improvements in technology, RDI, lifelong learning, and interaction and cooperation with the industry. In the last 10 years, OU’s research is expanding into fields that are in the major problem areas of today’s societies: health and sustainability. ÓU’s mission and vision are underpinned by fundamental values such as nurturing entrepreneurship, openness, tolerance, dialogue and diversity to fulfil its responsibility as a higher education institution contributing to positive societal change.
Mission
The fundamental mission of the University is to serve the interest of society, the economy and our industrial partners through the transfer and constant development of high level knowledge and skills and innovation.
Vision/Core values
The highest value of the university are its students, as well as its qualified professionals, engineers, computer scientists, economists, engineering teachers and doctors who provide the trademark of the University. A key task in education is to improve students’ critical thinking skills to develop initiative, tolerant, empathetic behaviour, professionalism, creativity, entrepreneurship, national affiliation and relationship-building skills as well as a strong personality.
The main aim of the University is to develop a new, multifaceted model of higher education. A university that offers a network-based approach, practice-oriented, industry-oriented, high-level higher education vocational training, undergraduate, master’s and doctoral programs, as well as a wide range of international research and development and innovation activities to responsibly serve the needs of the society nationally, regionally and globally through educating the next generation of global citizens.
The University continuously develops its activities in the form of project-based education based on real corporate tasks and the establishment of incubator units by cooperating with key players of the economy and the local communities, the companies, their research sites and laboratories. The improvement of the internationalization in both education and research is of high priority at Obuda University.

entityDescription:
The Chair of Space Mobility and Propulsion at TUM advances sustainable and innovative space technologies. Its research spans propulsion systems, in-space mobility, and resource-efficient systems like water electrolysis and solar-thermal propulsion. Focus areas include reusable and throttleable space propulsion systems for access to space and landing capabilities, in-space propulsion for autonomy and sustainability, advanced control systems leveraging AI and ML models. The team integrates teaching, experimental projects, and real-world applications, including the ASCENT rocket hopper and SPARK initiatives. These efforts focus on advancing propulsion and mobility solutions to enable future space missions. Explore more:

entityDescription:
UAB SPACEUNION is focused on the counter-drone cutting edge lase-based technologies for detection of unauthorized drones, identification, tracking and neutralization by LASER DIRECTED ENERGY weapons to disable or intercept rogue drones. 
Those disruptive C-UAV solutions can aslo be used not only in military sector but for increasing the resilience of critical infrastructure contribute in improving monitoring, risk assessment, forecast, mitigation and modelling techniques aimed at increasing the resilience of critical infrastructures, also of border and customs facility, validating multi-hazard scenarios, creating interactive hazard maps supported by Earth Observation and other data sources.

SPACEUNION Anti-Drone Solutions are thus a great tool against exploitation attacks, protecting borders against attacks, penetrations, and smuggling with radar capability up to 3km detection range for small UAV’s (up to 50cm diagonal) and up to 5 km for UAV with diagonal 1,0m and more. For some application like preventing intelligence activities or smuggling of goods using balloons, we are deploying special solution –“laser drone” with the low power. When such a threat is detected by the radar, a “laser drone” is sent to the given coordinates and burns through the shell so that the balloon lands vertically down. This solution is also quite effective in combating reconnaissance FPV drones. When such targets are detected, the “laser drone”, operator directs the laser beam to the video camera and blinds it.

Electrek Explorer is an innovative software and data platform designed to transform electric mobility and travel by integrating nature-focused geospatial data with advanced mapping and navigation systems. The platform curates and analyzes environmental, ecological, and experiential data to enable businesses, organisations, and travelers to access alternate route guidance and curated experiences that emphasize sustainability, biodiversity, and natural exploration.
At its core, Electrek Explorer offers a suite of geospatial data and APIs that can be integrated into third-party platforms to enhance electric mobility and outdoor travel experiences. Through its "Explorer Route" feature, the platform enables users to discover scenic, eco-friendly routes while connecting with local conservation projects and biodiversity hotspots.
Key functionalities include:
Alternate Route Guidance: Integration of curated nature-focused routes into mapping systems for electric vehicles, bikes, and other modes of sustainable transport.

Geospatial Data Solutions: Providing comprehensive datasets for outdoor experiences, including eco-friendly charging points, wildlife observation areas, and protected natural reserves.

Platform Integration: Seamless integration into existing mobility, navigation, and tourism platforms to enhance user engagement and promote sustainable exploration.

By fostering deeper connections between technology, mobility, and nature, Electrek Explorer aims to create meaningful travel experiences, support conservation efforts, and encourage responsible exploration of interconnected ecosystems.

description:
CeraNovis produces, applies and develops ceramic coatings for harsh environments. One of the application fields, are thermo-optical coatings for satellite surfaces
 This white ceramic coating (calles NV14) has been developed within the framework of the ESA’s Bepi Colombo Mission. The task was to develop a white, UV-resistant reflecting coating that is particularly inert to thermal shocks. Currently, this flexible coating can be applied to substrates such as titanium, titanium foils, steel, CFRP and aluminum. It withstands temperature changes of -200°C to +500°C. I can be thermally sintered but simple drying under ambient conditions is also sufficient. Due to the low sintering temperatures the substrate properties remain unchanged. The ageing resistance of the coating has been determined by simulation tests under high vacuum, high temperature and high UV load (11 solar constants) over several years. CeraNovis offers the complete coating of components, also with complex geometries.. Upon request we offer documentation in the form of a CoT (Certificate of Test) with microscopic investigation, tape tests and process control samples.

entityDescription: The Aerospace Mechatronics Group is a research unit at the University of Toronto Institute for Aerospace Studies (UTIAS) in Toronto, Canada, under the supervision of Prof. M. Reza Emami. He was also the Founding Chaired Professor of Onboard Space Systems and Director of Asteroid Engineering Centre at the Luleå University of Technology, Sweden, in 2015-2020. He obtained his Ph.D. and postdoctoral fellowship in Robotics and Mechatronics from University of Toronto, and M.A.Sc. and B.Sc. in Aerospace Engineering from Sharif University of Technology, and worked in the industry as a licensed Professional Engineer and Project Manager before joining the academia. His research focuses on concurrent engineering of multidisciplinary systems, such as spacecraft, robot manipulators and rovers. Some of his current research includes: space systems miniaturization, space debris mitigation and remediation, concurrent base-arm control of free-flying space manipulators, satellite formation flying, asteroid redirection for exploration and mining, intelligent heterogeneous rover/satellite teams, and reconfigurable manipulators. entityDescription:
ICEE Space is an international space test-, research- and development startup specialising in empowering and operating analogue missions for high-fidelity simulation of crewed and robotic space missions.

We provide cutting-edge technology such as ready-to-use mobile inflatable habitats and analogue space suits, infrastructure to set up research test-beds in extreme environments on Earth, as well as analogue consultancy services. Our goal is to aid future interplanetary exploration on the Moon, Mars, and beyond, as analogue research is key to unlocking deep space research.

Our product is our analogue astronaut toolkit, comprising an inflatable habitat, analogue spacesuits, communication systems, power systems, MCC procedure and guidelines, mission design and research methodologies, training suits, and environment monitoring software. The kit provides everything an aspiring space researcher might need to design and run an analogue mission, anywhere in the world. It allows various research groups to organise scientific expeditions with high science returns in human performance, human-robotic interactions, and AI in extreme environments, while also promoting high and uniform industry standards.

Additionally, we also provide analogue consulting services and run analogue expeditions, with 4 already under our belt.
In 2021, our team had the first campaign in the lava tube of Stefánshellir, Iceland. This and subsequent ICEE.Space missions (CHILL-ICE II, APICES, CASTHELS) serve as test-beds for our astronaut toolkit and help refine our expertise. Our next analogue mission, CHILL-ICE III, is planned for August of 2024.

We are backed by ESA BIC, the biggest network of incubators supporting European space startups.

entityDescription:
Medical University - Plovdiv
The Medical University of Plovdiv (MU-Plovdiv) is a state-accredited institution, founded in 1945, with over 37,700 alumni from 65 countries across Europe, Asia, America, and Africa. As a member of the European University Association, MU-Plovdiv holds the prestigious Erasmus University Charter, allowing participation in EU educational programs. This ensures high-quality education, alongside mobility opportunities for both students and faculty members. The university's educational activities are also certified under ISO 9001:2015.
MU-Plovdiv is comprised of four faculties: Medicine, Dental Medicine, Pharmacy, and Public Health. It also includes a Medical College and a Department of Languages and Specialized Training. The university aligns its curricula with other European institutions, promoting the European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System (ECTS). This system facilitates the mutual recognition of qualifications and encourages student mobility. Clinical training is carried out at six affiliated university hospitals. Since 2007, MU-Plovdiv diplomas have been recognized by all EU and EEA member countries.
The academic staff includes over 200 professors and associate professors, as well as 600 assistant professors. These professionals are known for their significant scientific achievements and extensive teaching experience. Many are active members of international research teams and organizations, contributing to advancements in medical science and education.
Research at MU-Plovdiv is overseen by the Vice-Rector of Science and Research, supported by the Council of Science and Research, as well as other experts and auxiliary units. The university offers nearly 70 doctoral programs spanning medicine, dental medicine, pharmacy, public health, and the natural sciences.
The research community at MU-Plovdiv benefits from advanced research and innovation centers that foster interdisciplinary collaboration. These centers are equipped with cutting-edge technologies, promoting both basic and clinical research, with a strong focus on translating scientific findings into clinical practice. The recently renovated Vivarium provides additional facilities for experimental and preclinical research. Research findings are often disseminated through MU-Plovdiv's academic journal, Folia Medica, which is indexed in Scopus. The university also supports young researchers through the Youth Scientific Association, encouraging their involvement in research projects and scientific events.
MU-Plovdiv's international relations are managed by the International Relations and Foreign Students Department. The university has signed over 150 academic agreements, including Erasmus+ inter-institutional agreements with universities across the EU and beyond. It is also a member of over 15 international academic organizations, offering diverse exchange opportunities through programs such as Erasmus+, CEEPUS, OMI, and Fulbright.
The Department of Medical Physics and Biophysics at MU-Plovdiv upholds the university’s high academic and research standards. The department's research focuses on a variety of experimental animal models, including in vivo, in vitro, and ex vivo studies. Research includes preclinical testing of newly synthesized biologically active molecules, the development of new drug delivery systems, biophysical experiments investigating cell pathways using isolated smooth muscle samples, and cytotoxic studies on primary cell cultures using a real-time cell analyzer. In recent years, the department has embarked on microgravitational studies using rats and mice. To support this research, part of the team developed a modified random positioning machine, suitable for both in vivo and in vitro experiments.

entityDescription:
A venture studio “à mission” focused on space
TheSpaceBuilder is a venture studio dedicated to space, aiming to create start-ups from research laboratories and the exploitation of technological innovations developed by public and private players.

entityDescription:
MetaPlanet's aim is to make the vast amount of data about the Earth collected from space available to the general public in an unprecedentedly simple way.

The company's objective is to develop a basic artificial intelligence model for Earth observation that uses time series of high-resolution satellite images to construct a 4D (space and time) representation of the planet with a high level of detail, using techniques such as super-resolution, generative AI and monocular depth estimation.

The AI system consists of two parts: MetaPlanet and AI Analytics. MetaPlanet is a generic AI model and machine representation of the world (different from the usual digital twins), optimised to be queried by other AI agents. An LLM can connect to MetaPlanet. MetaPlanet will thus become an exploitable source of information for all companies and individuals outside the space sector.

entityDescription:
Barcelona School of Economics (BSE) is an institution for scientific cooperation for research and graduate education in Economics and Data Science. It was founded in 2006 by four academic institutions: the Department of Economics and Business at Universitat Pompeu Fabra (UPF); the Unit of Foundations of Economic Analysis at Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (UFAE-UAB); the Institute for Economic Analysis (IAE-CSIC); and the Center for Research in International Economics (CREI).
BSE was founded to pursue research excellence, it is driven by a world-class faculty and draws on the strengths and reputation of its four academic units. The BSE research community includes Affiliated Professors, Post-docs, Visitors, and PhD students. BSE has obtained three consecutive Severo Ochoa accreditations (2012-15, 2016-19 and 2020-24), which has supported BSE to become one of the leading clusters of economics research in Europe and worldwide.
Barcelona School of Economics is an institution where graduate education and research are closely linked. The core of all BSE educational and research activities are the Affiliated Professors. BSE Affiliated Professors are tenured or tenure-track faculty members from the four academic units (DEE-UPF, UFAE-UAB, IAE-CSIC and CREI). In April 2024, BSE had 152 Affiliated Professors: 122 have a PhD from a non-Spanish university and 78 of them are non-Spanish. Among them 18 are ICREA Research Professors. A total of 42 ERC Grants have been awarded to current BSE Affiliated Professors since the beginning of the program. 10 BSE Affiliated Professors are Econometric Society Fellows. According to RePEc, the reference data repository in Economics, 22 Affiliated Professors are ranked among the top 5% and 50 are ranked among the top 10% of economics researchers worldwide. The BSE research community includes also 16 Post-doctoral researchers, 2 BSE research Fellows (external academics with a stable collaboration with BSE) and 98 pre-doctoral researchers, enrolled in the two PhD programs co-organized by BSE: Economics, Finance and Management PhD program at Universitat Pompeu Fabra (UPF) and International Doctorate in Economic Analysis, at Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (UAB).
BSE offers two master degrees in Economics and one master degree in Data Science, besides short courses for professionals. The BSE programs are very international (on average 90% are international students) and are recognized and respected by prestigious universities, companies, and organizations across the globe. In addition, these master programs are a gateway to prestigious PhD programs.
On the research side, BSE has since its inception the ambition to be recognized as one of the top institutions in Europe and worldwide for research in Applied Economics, Macroeconomics Microeconomics and Data Science. To achieve that, BSE community is engaged by plenty of research activities, such as seminar series, the BSE Lectures, the Calvó-Armengol International Prize Lectures, in collaboration with the Andorran government, and the BSE Summer Forum, a two-week conference with more than 30 workshops that attracts hundreds of researchers from around the globe to Barcelona to present cutting-edge research.

entityDescription:
Quantum Network Design specialised on the design, development but also simulation of quantum networks and their associated protocols in realistic, noisy scenarios. The studied models include noise stemming from gates and storage in NISQ devices alongside noise in channels connecting quantum networking nodes. The simulation engine uses a variety of different computational approaches including efficient classical simulation methods for the study of complex quantum networks running distributed quantum applications in a realistic scenario. These scenarios include not only the noise quantum operations, storages and channels but also all the classical messaging, waiting times and computation times amongst other crucial parameters.
The core competences of Quantum Network Design lie in:
Design, simulation, architecture and protocols for quantum networks

The founders of Quantum Network Design (Wolfgang Dür and Alexander Pirker) have a demonstrated and internationally recognized history in proposing and developing protocols for quantum networks. The protocols include protocols to distribute entangled states within a network, to also combat large-distances amongst nodes but also protocols for generating arbitrary graph states within a network. Furthermore, protocols to achieve reliability have been developed, underlining this competency of Quantum Network Design. Furthermore, Quantum Network Design implements a simulator for quantum networks in a highly configurable manner, allowing operators to change storage and gate noise models but also channel noise models connecting individual nodes. The simulator takes into account for waiting times due to operations, classical messaging but also the dynamic availability of channel and nodes in a network.
Security aspects in quantum networks

Both founders of Quantum Network Design have worked on the security of quantum networks relying on entanglement purification protocols. It was proven that security in a quantum network is always feasible in case the end-nodes have the capability to run entanglement purification protocols, under the assumption of powerful eavesdroppers controlling the entire network. This background is vital to designing a secure DQC network as part of this project.

entityName: Jan Evangelista Purkyne University in Usti nad Labem
entityDescription:
Established in 1991 on the basis of the former Pedagogical Faculty, our university currently comprises eight faculties (Faculty of Art and Design, Faculty of Arts, Faculty of Education, Faculty of Environment, Faculty of Health Studies, Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, Faculty of Science, and Faculty of Social and Economic Studies).
We have adopted the name of the renowned North-Bohemian native of LibochoviceJ. E. Purkyně(1787–1869), an outstanding biologist, pharmacologist and anthropologist, and one of the founders of modern physiology. Just as well-rounded a personality Purkyně in his time was, we too, in these days, offer a wide variety of study programmes (more than 50 programmes with more than 150 specialisations) focusing on the most varied areas of human activities. We educate around 8500 students and employ a staff of about 900, of those around 500 in academic positions (that is a student-to-faculty ratio of 17:1).
We are proud of being the only university founded and located in northwest Czechia, the region with stunning environmental diversity as well as a turbulent political and economic history over the last two centuries. This all, along with diverse intellectual traditions at our university, create a unique research and educational ecosystem to address the most pressing challenges faced by the society in our region and beyond.

Nr. 19196644, and registered in the Commercial Register maintained by the Municipal Court in Prague, Section C, Folio 382890 (“Company”).

entityDescription:
Blue Orbit Space Systems is a company focused on the space and plasma technology sector, dedicated to research and development of advanced propulsion systems and related technologies. Founded in 2022 by a multidisciplinary team of highly skilled and passionate scientific and engineering professionals, Blue Orbit aims to become a leader in the field of space propulsion and space exploration.
This leadership within the space industry will be achieved through the unique expertise brought in by each of the founders. Firstly, future Dr. Rene Cartaya Lopez, a Physics graduate specializing in plasma process chemistry and passionate about space technology. Secondly, Engineer Ahymerd Riveras, specializing in production and telecommunications, with a keen interest in system optimization and efficiency. Thirdly, Dr. Abraham Vivas Borda, a mechanical engineer with a PhD in renewable energies, devoted to realizing a sustainable vision for the future of space. Fourthly, MSc. Felix Konefka, a specialist in plasma physics, a generator of innovation in the space sector. Lastly, Engineer Marco Cen Puc, a mechatronics specialist, enthusiastic about system automation.
Our focus is on developing advanced propulsion technologies that drive space exploration in a more efficient and sustainable manner. We work closely with space agencies, academic institutions, and private companies to promote innovation and take our solutions to the next level. Moreover, our commitment to excellence extends not only to science and engineering but also to the customer experience, providing personalized solutions and exceptional service. We strive to understand each customers unique needs and deliver tailor-made solutions that propel their success and help them reach new heights in space exploration.
Our primary goal is to turn bold ideas into tangible realities and contribute to scientific and technological advancement on a global scale. Challenging ourselves every day to push the boundaries of what is possible and forge new paths towards the stars.
In addition to our endeavors in space, Blue Orbit is also exploring terrestrial applications of plasma technology. Among these applications are: seed treatment through cold plasma exposure, where we can stimulate growth, increase resistance to diseases and pests, and improve overall performance. Activated Plasma Water, through the use of cutting-edge technologies, we develop systems that activate water at a molecular level, enhancing its quality and properties. This activated water has applications in various fields such as agriculture, health, and industry. Lastly, leveraging the properties of plasma, we develop innovative processes to decompose and transform waste materials, thus contributing to reducing environmental impact and promoting a circular economy.
In summary, at Blue Orbit, we are passionate about space and believe in the power of technology to drive human progress both in space and on Earth. We are committed to excellence, innovation, and leadership in the space industry. Join us on this exciting adventure towards an interplanetary future and discover how we are transforming the space landscape to pave the way for humanity to reach the stars.

entityDescription:
Our company is advancing industrial-grade EEG technology through early-stage, proof-of-concept solutions designed to meet the unique demands of high-stakes environments, including space missions, maritime operations, and industrial transport. Currently at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 3, we are focused on developing and validating proprietary artifact deletion algorithms alongside rugged, adaptable EEG hardware tailored for extreme conditions where conventional EEG devices cannot operate effectively.
At this stage, our core R&D efforts center on refining our artifact correction technology, a key component of our intellectual property (IP) strategy, to ensure high-fidelity, real-time brain monitoring in challenging industrial contexts. This includes testing our algorithms in simulated environments to validate their effectiveness in filtering out environmental noise and physiological artifacts—an essential requirement for safety-critical applications.
Our collaborations with hardware manufacturers and research institutions support this validation process, allowing us to co-develop prototypes that can withstand the operational demands of industrial and remote settings. Additionally, we are building partnerships with OEMs and industry stakeholders in health tech, focusing on IP licensing and modular integration options for future commercial deployment.
At TRL 3, we are laying the groundwork for patentable IP and proof-of-concept demonstrations that will underpin our transition to field-ready EEG solutions. Our mission is to create technology that not only elevates safety standards in critical industries but also enables accurate, non-invasive neurological monitoring where it has never been possible before. As we progress, we aim to secure additional research funding and partnerships that will support our journey toward scalable, compliant EEG solutions designed for the most demanding environments.

entityDescription:
Natsionalna Elektricheska Kompania EAD (NEK EAD) was incorporated in late 1991 and over the years it has established its position in the power industry and the economy of the Republic of Bulgaria. The mission of NEK EAD is to provide safe, efficient and uninterrupted power supply. NEK EAD is a sole-owner joint-stock company. Since 2008 the capital of NEK is held by Bulgarian Energy Holding EAD. The main businesses of NEK EAD include electricity generation and trading. The Company is managed by a three-member Board of Directors.

NEK EAD operates one of the largest dams and hydropower schemes in the country, applying stringent requirements on their O&M safety and efficiency. The Company lies at the heart of the electric power system of Bulgaria, producing electricity at 31 hydro-power and pumped storage hydro-power plants, with a total installed generating capacity of 2737 MW and pumping capacity of 931 MW. The flexible generation facilities of the company have a key role in ensuring security of supply and reliability and security of the grid system of Bulgaria. The total capacity of the dam reservoirs operated by NEK EAD represents 55% of the total controlled water resources in the Republic of Bulgaria.

Licenses issued to NEK EAD by the Energy and Water Regulatory Commission:
- Hydro (HPP&PS) generation license;
- Public power supply license expanded to include the rights and obligations of a "Special Balancing Group Coordinator".
- Electricity trading license expanded to include the rights and obligations of a "Standard Balancing Group Coordinator".
- Supplier of Last Resort license expanded to include the rights and obligations of a "Special Balancing Group Coordinator".

entityName: Hochschule für Technik und Wirtschaft Dresden
entityDescription:
With around 4,800 students, the Dresden University of Applied Sciences (HTW Dresden) is the second largest university in the state capital of Saxony, Germany. Founded in 1992, it is now one of the top German universities of applied sciences. It offers more than 40 degree courses in the fields of civil engineering, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, computer science, economics, geoinformatics, agriculture, environment, chemistry and design which lead to Bachelor's, Master's and Diplom degrees.

Teaching and research are closely linked at HTW Dresden and are strongly practice-oriented. Students can participate in research projects at an early stage, benefit from close contacts with industrial partners and also have the opportunity to do a doctorate as part of a cooperative doctoral program.

Research at HTW Dresden is primarily oriented towards the three interdisciplinary profile lines: Securing Natural Resources, Developing Sustainable Mobility and Infrastructure, and Designing, Networking and Digitalizing the Economy and Work. With its application-oriented research, the university is an important partner, especially for SMEs in Saxony, and is very well networked with the numerous technology and research centers in Dresden as a science location.

The University of Applied Sciences supports start-ups from the university environment in the development and implementation of innovative business ideas and arranges contacts with cooperation partners in business and industry. In addition to excellent study conditions and a first-class education, students in Dresden can expect an environment with a high quality of life, art and culture, great leisure activities and a beautiful landscape.The degrees obtained at HTW Dresden are highly recognized by companies as well as research and educational institutions. This is proven not only by current studies and university rankings, but above all by the successful placement of the graduates in practice.

Viridian is a highly technical micro-company specialising in the advanced modelling, design and quantification of Nature-based Solutions. We have developed HydroloGIS: a truly unique method for identifying the most effective, natural solutions to a host of water problems - such as flooding, drought or river pollution - then ranking all alternative option for how much impact they will have on local problems. It blends scientific rigour with commercial pragmatism during the advanced, mathematical modelling of ecosystem services.
To this we integrate a whole spectrum of more standard benefits, such as carbon sequestration and biodiversity, so that stakeholders have all the technical advice they need to decide on the best course of action in their community or region – all while meeting project objectives. 
This human-centric, participatory design helps stakeholders 'own' solutions, so we rapidly build consensus and make the whole process quick, inexpensive and successful.
