entityDescription:
OUR MISSION
We believe that maps and location technology is heavily influencing the way we understand the world we live in and we are passionate to ensure it is used well.
We have great people in our team at NGIS that work in partnership with like-minded organisations to implement location technology and solutions that provide a positive impact.
We streamline business, solve the toughest problems and make our world more livable by making location intelligence accessible and easy to use.

GEOSPATIAL TECHNOLOGY CAN HELP TURN YOUR IDEAS INTO WORLD-CHANGING OUTCOMES
At NGIS, we are passionate about the power of geospatial technology - from something as humble as a customised Google Map, to an advanced Earth Observations project that has the ability to enact positive change at a global scale.
We know the potential to create a more sustainable world is possible when you have the right tools at your fingertips - the opportunities to be discovered and actioned with geospatial technology are endless.
Thought leadership and problem solving with geospatial technology is at the heart of what we do: we advise clients on spatial technology, consult in GIS services, build fit for purpose solutions, train our clients technically and partner with the industry's best technology providers such as; Google, Planet, Skyline Digital Twin and more. As a full service consultancy we can help you set a path, build capacity or create a solution that enables data driven decision making.
Our philosophy – People Partnership Success – reflects the way we approach our business. The expertise of our people, the long-term client relationships we form, the active participation within our industry and the strategic partnerships we have created since 1993, demonstrates that we invest in relationships. We know that understanding your business underpins the success of every project we undertake.

- Has clients in all states/territories in Australia and 31countries throughout Africa, Asia and North America.

entityDescription:
AERIANE SA is a Belgian company established in 1988, provides a spectrum of Engineering, Design, prototyping, and high-performance mechanical and composite production services. It is equipped with a 5-axis machining center designed for complex and large-sized parts.
In an increasingly specialized industrial landscape, AERIANE acts as a singular and responsive point of contact, delivering a comprehensive solution from design to manufacturing, installation, or maintenance.
With more than 33 years of experience, AERIANE has cultivated a reputation for responsiveness, and a steadfast commitment to quality and reliability in the diverse and ambitious projects it has undertaken throughout the years.

In its history, AERIANE has encountered numerous opportunities across various domains. Commencing with aircraft manufacturing, the two founders were presented with the chance to embark on an R&D delta wing project. This early venture compelled them to swiftly innovate, creating and testing solutions for this new version of the glider.
Among the notable and remarkable opportunities, AERIANE played a role in the design team for the Princess Elisabeth Research Station. Additionally, AERIANE contributed to the OPERA project, an international collaboration with CERN in Geneva. The objective of the Opera project was the detection of neutrinos emitted from CERN accelerators, situated 731km away in Gran Sasso (central Italy). AERIANE was responsible for manufacturing a network of scintillation fibers that aided in locating the occurrence of neutrinos. 
Furthermore, AERIANE has amassed significant experience in mechanical design through the two "rolling floor projects" commissioned by IBA. This expertise is continually evolving in ongoing development efforts.

entityDescription:
MCAST Mission Statement
“To provide universally accessible vocational and professional education and training with an international dimension, responsive to the needs of the individual and the economy.”

Established in 2001, the Malta College of Arts, Science and Technology is the country’s leading vocational education and training institution. Six Institutes in Malta and the Gozo Campus, MCAST offers over 190 full-time courses and over 300 part-time vocational courses ranging from certificates to Doctoral level (MQF Level 1 to Level 8).
The six MCAST Institutes namely the Institute of Applied Sciences, the Institute for the Creative Arts, the Institute of Engineering and Transport, the Institute of Business Management and Commerce, the Institute of Community Services, the Institute of Information and Communication Technology and the Gozo Campus provide all the technical and professional expertise towards the delivery of the programmes at MCAST. They also maintain the aim of driving forward all the areas of study under their respective responsibility. This corporate structure enables focused strategies, which address the specific needs of students at each level while maintaining a healthy dialogue with all interested stakeholders in order to provide the best programmes for the needs of the local economy and society.

MCAST’s relationship with industry stimulates the College’s success – its programmes are flexible, relevant and responsive to the aspirations of the students and to the needs of industries which are constantly evolving to meet the challenges of a changing global economy. The College supports small and medium-sized enterprises through a multidisciplinary approach. This encompasses work-based learning through the Apprenticeships Programme, the various entrepreneurship initiatives and through MG2i (MCAST’s commercial arm) services whereby it provides training courses tailor-made to their needs. The College is focusing on increasing the portfolio of MG2i by developing new programmes in Life Long Learning, accrediting new programmes at different levels, including Master’s degrees, and introducing more professional development programmes. It is working on the internationalisation of MG2i through the Training and Professional Development Programmes and joint-venture opportunities in different vocational areas.

MCAST collaborates in numerous projects, both of a National and European level. During the last few years MCAST research portfolio has rapidly grown in applied research, consistently attracting local and internationally funded projects. MCAST is committed to developing the next generation of researchers, scientists and academics through collaboration across disciplines. The establishment of the Applied Research and Innovation Centre in 2019 has had a positive impact on the research funds available at MCAST.
Over the past 5 years it has secured 50 externally funded research projects with a total funding value exceeding Eur 5M.

entityDescription:
Perpetual Atomics is a space nuclear power, space science and exploration spinout company from the University of Leicester. The University of Leicester team that has formed Perpetual Atomics has been leading the development of radioisotope power technologies as part of a European Space Agency funded programme since 2010. Perpetual Atomics is focused on the commercialisation of radioisotope space nuclear power technologies. It has a range of products it is developing including: radioisotope heater units, radioisotope thermoelectric generators, Stirling engine based power generation systems, terrestrial power systems and nano reactor concepts for space. All of the radioisotope power systems are based on the utilisation of the decay heat from americium-241.

Perpetual Atomics also provides services related to the design of space science and exploration mission enabled by nuclear power as well as the applications of radioisotope technologies.

Gdynia Maritime University (GMU) is the biggest maritime university in Poland. The University offers undergraduate engineering and master’s degrees for prospective merchant marine officers, as well as engineering and managerial personnel for the maritime industry. GMU is home to four dynamically developing faculties: Electrical Engineering, Marine Engineering, Navigation, and Management and Quality Science. Between them, the facultiesconduct scientific research and provide education in 43 disciplines, across 10 academicfields of study, bothmarine and land-based. The University has the powers to award doctoral/postdoctoral degrees.

The Maritime Institute is GMU’s research unit dedicated to the implementation of commercial projects, projects financed from external sources, and scientific research for the benefit of the maritime and related sectors, including the energy sector; maritime transport and ports; maritime tourism; and cultural heritage. The Maritime Institute has for years been a leader in the Polish offshore industry in environmental research and preparing environmental, geophysical, geological and geotechnical documentation for maritime investments, especially inwind power. The Institute also acts as a competence centre, a centre for the processing andevaluation of information on the needs and priorities of the maritime industry, as well as the use of marine resources, including the management of marine areas.
Moreover, the Maritime Institute is involved in research and development projects in the protection of the environment, and water and marine resources ecology, including sea fishing; carrying out specialist laboratory analyses in marine geotechnics, chemistry and biology; providing expert knowledge on marine hydrotechnics; and the implementation of artificial intelligence to optimise transport processes and support ecological forms of transport.
The Project Management Centre provides support for the Institute’s Departments andLaboratories inpreparing, submitting applications, and final settlement of research projects, especially those financed by EU programmes. As a result, the Institute creates, develops, and leads international research and development projects financed by national and international funds.
The priorities of the Maritime Institute, which are part of the development strategy of Gdynia Maritime University are: the implementation of research and the development of innovative research and analysis methods for the marine environment; support for companies andadministrations in investment processes; and the development of educational competencies forthe needs of the offshore wind energy industry.
RESEARCH DEPARTMENTS OF GMU MARITIME INSTITUTE
· Marine Ecology Department 
· Economics and Spatial Policy Department 
· Offshore Geotechnics Department 
· Maritime Hydrotechnics and Electronics Department
· Operational Oceanography Department 
· Environmental Protection Department 
The Maritime Institute has three accredited research laboratories. The Institute operates anintegrated administration system based on ISO 9001, ISO 14001, and OHSAS 18001. 
An important role in the work of the Maritime Institute is played by its research vessels, which include R/V IMOR — a floating multipurpose oceanographic research laboratory. All vessels are equipped with modern equipment and measuring devices.

entityDescription:
Experience, performance, flexibility - key success factors for your validation process
AneCom AeroTest support international turbomachinery OEM’s in the validation of their technologies, modules and complete products. Our unique in-house Compressor Test Centre started its operation in 2003 and combines 3 different aerodynamic/acoustic test beds in a perfect symbiosis. Besides testing we design and manufacture not only heavily instrumented module test vehicles but also measurement solutions for all types of turbomachinery and its components. 
The portfolio range includes a complete package for test vehicle design and manufacturing, including the procurement of hardware, associated instrumentation application and assembly of the test vehicle, testing and delivery of the test data collected to the customer. Vigorous project management ensures top quality, delivered on time and within budget of such complex projects. The overall project is complemented by our standard, as well as special measurement technology and equipment – from design and application up to data collection during the test. Fan and compressor tests are carried out on one of our three inhouse test beds at the Wildau site. AneCom AeroTest operates two of these test facilities for aerodynamic tests and one for aero acoustic tests in our Anechoic Chamber, measuring approximately 10.000 m³. Combustor and turbine tests are conducted at certified partner facilities within Germany and if required worldwide.

entityDescription:
Core Focus:
Research Engine is a partnership dedicated to advancing the field of additive manufacturing through innovative solutions in material extrusion and the use of high-performance polymers. Our expertise focuses on niche extreme thermoplastics from ultra soft TPEs to high performance materials.
Specialization:
We are pioneers in Fused Granulate Fabrication (FGF), a material extrusion 3D printing technology that utilizes thermoplastic pellets instead of traditional filaments. Our approach is versatile, adaptable to both large-scale industrial applications and small-scale precision manufacturing, allowing us to push the boundaries of what’s possible in additive manufacturing.
Research Engine’s process harnesses all available thermoplastics, from conventional polymers to advanced high-performance materials such as PEEK, and elastomers. We specialize in optimizing these materials for use in demanding environments, including applications requiring high-temperature resistance and extreme flexibility.
Key Areas of Expertise:
- Material Extrusion: Cutting-edge solutions in fused granulate fabrication, offering efficiency and precision in 3D printing.
- High-Performance Polymers: Engineering thermoplastics that withstand extreme conditions, including heat, mechanical stress, and chemical exposure.
- Additive Manufacturing: Focus on advanced 3D printing techniques that deliver high precision, tailored for both prototyping and production-scale use.
- High Temperature Applications: Expertise in materials and processes designed for high-temperature environments, ensuring stability and performance.
- Ultra-Soft & Elastomeric Materials: Precision fabrication of soft, flexible materials for specialized applications (such as large expansion, 3D printed inflatables) requiring adaptability and durability.
- System Modeling & Mechanical Engineering: Integrated design and system modelling capabilities to optimize the entire manufacturing process from material selection to final part production.
Vision:
At Research Engine, our vision is to drive next-generation manufacturing solutions by enabling the use of advanced materials and innovative extrusion technologies. We are committed to pushing the limits of 3D printing and transforming how industries approach high-precision fabrication.
By combining our expertise in high-performance materials and fused granulate fabrication, we aim to deliver practical, scalable solutions that meet the complex needs of aerospace, automotive, medical, and industrial sectors.

entityName: Burgas State University Prof. Dr Asen Zlatarov
entityDescription:
Prof. Dr. Assen Zlatarov University is the only state university in Southeastern Bulgaria. It was founded on 6thOctober 1963 by Decree № 162 of the Council of Ministers as the Higher Institute of Chemical Technology. Five years later, the Institute was renamed the Higher Institute of Chemical Technology "Prof. Dr. Asen Zlatarov", which forever links it with the name of its patron. In 1995, by a decision of the National Assembly, it was established as “Prof. Dr. Assen Zlatarov” University.
Education at the University is carried out in five faculties - Faculty of Technical Sciences, Faculty of Natural Sciences, Faculty of Social Sciences, Faculty of Public Health and Health Care and Faculty of Medicine. It comprises three colleges - the Technical College, the Medical College and the College of Tourism and two departments - the Department of Language Teaching and the Department of Qualification and Professional Development of Teaching Professionals (DQPDP).
Education at “Prof. Dr. Assen Zlatarov” University is carried out in 18 professional fields in 45 accredited Bachelor and over 30 Master programs.
The Central Research Laboratory and the Electronic Computing Centre occupy a worthy place in the structure of the University. Students studying at the University acquire the educational qualification degrees of "Professional Bachelor", "Bachelor" and "Master", as well as the scientific and educational degree "Doctor".
The University has over 320 highly qualified lecturers, 127 of whom are habilitated. The organization and management of the educational process at the University is in accordance with the European requirements and criteria for a quality educational and research process. The University system for evaluation and maintenance of the quality of education has been developed. In terms of the quality of scientific research the University is ranked among the first in Bulgaria according to the Hirsch system for contribution to science. In pursuance of the management's policy of rejuvenating and improving the qualifications of the academic staff, the practice of announcing competitions at all levels - from "assistant" to "professor" - has been established.
Prof. Dr. Assen Zlatarov University has modern necessary equipment, which is in accordance with the state requirements for high quality education. It consists of six academic buildings, a sports facility, three student hostels, three student canteens and a medical service centre. The bedding stock of the student hostels enables accommodation for all students who are not residents of Burgas.
The library and information complex includes the Central Library and three branches. The library and information complex provides materials from a wide range of fields of knowledge - social, economic, humanities and technical sciences. The reading rooms are equipped with 150 seats for reading. Access to the scientific databases Scopus, ScienceDirect, EmBase, Web of Knowledge is provided.
The academic management makes systematic efforts for the maintenance, expansion and effective use of the available necessary equipment, its modernization and renewal.
The University has established active scientific relations with institutes and universities from England, France, Germany, Russia, Romania, Turkey, Spain, Italy, Hungary, Serbia, Poland, Slovenia, Slovakia, etc. They create opportunities for scientific specializations and teaching practice of lecturers and students, for exchange of lecturers, teaching and scientific literature.
The motto of the Burgas State University ''Prof. Dr. Assen Zlatarov'' is: "CONTINUITY, INNOVATION, GROWTH, SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT".

entityDescription:
Bar.on is building the "Spotify for (fermented) drinks". 

We're pioneering a new, sustainable distribution model for fermented drinks, avoiding the shipment of billions of liters of water across the globe and therefore significantly minimizing the industry's ecological footprint as well as saving huge shipping costs. Our company is on a mission to transform the distribution of fermented drinks through innovative dispensers - a hardware platform that instantly crafts high-quality, customizable drinks on demand. 

Bar.on specializes in fermentation analogues, creating beverages with a texture and mouthfeel far more complex than typical sodas. From non-alcoholic beers to functional beverages enriched with adaptogens and nootropics, for example, Bar.on’s technology is redefining how people experience their favorite drinks. Currently, we focus on four main categories: non-alcoholic beer, cold brew coffee, fermented ice tea, and kombucha, with non-alcoholic wines in the pipeline for next year. 

The Problem: The beverage distribution industry is inherently unsustainable. Every year, billions of liters of water are shipped across the globe in the form of beverages, contributing to massive carbon emissions, excessive packaging waste and significant environmental degradation. Despite the growing demand for more sustainable practices, the industry remains heavily reliant on outdated distribution methods that prioritize volume over ecological responsibility. 
Our Solution: Bar.on's dispensers are poised to revolutionize the industry by eliminating the need for global beverage transportation. Our cutting-edge technology enables the on-site production of beverages, instantly mixing high-quality ingredients into fresh, fully customizable drinks. By digitizing the beverage production process and using advanced molecular mixing technology based on a set of flavor cartridges, we ensure superior taste and quality while drastically reducing the environmental impact. 
This approach minimizes packaging waste, cuts down on transportation emissions and significantly lowers the carbon footprint of the entire beverage supply chain. Additionally, Bar.on's solutions offer valuable data capture and community-building opportunities, providing insights that further enhance consumer engagement and satisfaction.

entityDescription:
The automotive industry is undergoing a monumental shift towards e-mobility, with significant challenges centered around the vehicle’s battery. Issues such as long charging times, high costs, limited range, and safety risks are not just inconvenient – they’re major barriers to widespread adoption. While many companies focus on optimizing battery cell chemistry, the optimization of everything surrounding the cell remains largely untapped. This approach offers significant cost savings while achieving similar benefits.
This is where ivilion comes in. Our revolutionary battery pack design features a patented load-bearing cooling structure that enables rapid charging in under ten minutes, substantial cost reductions, enhanced safety, and extended vehicle range.
To enter the market gradually, ivilion offers engineering and prototyping services as an initial step. Utilizing a fully digitalized, model-based design process allows us to respond agilely to individual customer needs and develop tailored solutions. For mass production, we rely on a licensing model and leverage existing production capacities within the supplier industry.
ivilion’s vision is to become the go-to provider for top-tier battery pack solutions, thereby accelerating the transition to electric mobility.

entityDescription:
AgroRisk is a platform to help financial companies, corporates, and farmers manage climate risks in agriculture. It is being developed by Envira ApS, which is a Danish SME company fully dedicated to developing AgroRisk. 
AgroRisk is a climate fintech platform to quantify financial risks for agricultural farms due to climate-related events and changing weather. It can be used by banks and insurance companies to determine credit risk and insurance premiums, by farmers to adapt their practices, and by food companies to manage climate risks across supply chains.
The solution uses multiple geospatial data sources and advanced modelling techniques to generate precise risk assessments at both field, farm, and portfolio level, now and in the future. This enables more informed decisions in credit provision, insurance coverage, risk evaluation, farming practices, and reporting. With seamless integration into existing systems, AgroRisk aligns perfectly with the new sustainability regulations, empowering both financial companies and corporates to effectively manage and report on ESG-related risks and model climate scenarios. 
Our vision is to provide the best global climate risk solution for agriculture to enable farmers, companies, and society to adapt to a changing climate and support decarbonization of the sector.

entityDescription:
Anisopter Insightful Research, S.L. is a young and small startup devoted to design, research and develop advanced technologies for the efficient construction of lattice structures. To this end, our resources are mainly invested in carrying out R&D projects together with industrial, technological and academic partners. Our ultimate goal is designing ultra-efficient lattice structures made of tubes that can be easy- and cost- effectively assembled.

On EARTH, we are devoted to reduce the economic and environmental impact of electricity production and transport infrastructures (e.g. wind turbines, solar panels or lattice towers for overhead transmission lines). Our structural solutions are able to reduce both materials utilization and on-site construction cost thanks to our patented node-based connection systems.

In SPACE, we seek to reduce the manufacturing, optimization and design costs of primary structures for launchers and satellites, mainly those based on lattice or “grid” solutions (i.e. grid, isogrid or anisogrid structures). For example, we aim to design and fabricate much lighter and versatile structures for rocket interfaces or payload adapters, as well as, for large off-earth constructions.

Our small size and low inertia paves the way for the fast development and validation of new connection technologies at minimal cost and lag time.

The R&D projects we carry out are intended to find and validate new structural solutions for industry. Our proprietary technologies provide key benefits to companies that rely on high performance lattice structures and where weight, efficiency and cost are critical.

Due to the large number of industrial sectors that could benefit from our solutions, the business model is constantly evolving. However, it is based on three main pillars:
- Industrial Property Rights: Patented connection systems to efficiently construct lattice structures with tubes (no welding required).
- Efficiency: Development and application of customized structural optimization solutions for lattice structures (software methodologies) to automate and leverage the value of our construction solutions.
- Research: Planning and execution of R&D projects (public or private) in order to adapt and validate our technologies in any industrial sector.

In summary, Anisopter Insightful Research is devoted to maximize the commercial and social impact of our structural solutions.

entityDescription:
SHFT is dedicated to transforming how runners train and improve by combining cutting-edge technology with personalized coaching. The company's core product,SHFT Run, is an advanced AI-powered running coach that utilizes smart Pods and real-time data to provide tailored feedback on running technique and performance.
What SHFT Does:
- Technical and Performance Coaching:
SHFT offers two core coaching systems:
- Technical Coaching: SHFT analyzes key aspects of running form, such as Stride Per Minute (SPM), Ground Contact Time (GCT), and foot landing position. By providing real-time audio feedback, the system helps runners improve their form to reduce the risk of injury and increase running efficiency.
- Critical Speed (CS) Performance Coaching: SHFT regularly tests a runner's Critical Speed and lactate threshold, tailoring personalized training plans based on these metrics. By focusing on optimizing performance, SHFT helps runners increase their speed and endurance.

- Real-Time Feedback:
SHFT uses wearable smart Pods, which track detailed movement patterns. As runners move, the AI coach provides immediate voice-guided instructions on adjustments to posture, cadence, and foot placement. Immersia is a leading company that is revolutionizing the augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) industry by developing innovative near-eye display (NED) technology. Despite advances in AR and VR, many of today's solutions are limited by the constraints of traditional optics, particularly when it comes to achieving a fully immersive experience with high image quality over a wide field of view (FOV), all while maintaining a lightweight and aesthetically pleasing design. Inmersia addresses these challenges with its patented NED, which incorporates the innovative InMirror system.

The system integrates advanced components designed to effectively direct image light to the user's eye, with additional elements that control light and enhance visual performance. Combined with a sophisticated optical module that includes image processing, eye-tracking capabilities and intermediate optics, this technology represents a major leap forward in the evolution of NED design.

With its expertise and innovative technology, Immersia is positioning itself as a leader in the AR/VR space, driving the adoption of these technologies with its superior, compact and immersive display solutions.

entityName: Institute of Chemical Process Fundamentals, Czech Academy of Sciences
entityDescription:
The Institute (originally called “Institute of Theoretical Foundations of Chemical Technology – ÚTZCHT”) was formally established in the Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences in 1960 by two existing teams, which already had a longer tradition at the time. The first one was the Department of Chemical Technology at the Institute of Chemistry headed by Professor Vladimír Bažant and the other was the Department of Chemical Engineering headed by Professor George Standart. Professor Bažant worked in the field of organosilicon compounds and heterogeneous catalysis, while Prof. Standart continued his research of distillation and extraction processes. In 1964, a group from the Institute of Physical Chemistry dealing with thermodynamics and phase equilibria headed by Prof. Hála joined the new institute. The founder and the first director of the institute was Prof. Bažant until his passing in 1973. Another personality who achieved great recognition and co-created the “image” of the institute was Prof. Eduard Hála.
In 1964, the institute moved to a new campus in the northwestern suburbs of Prague (on the border of Suchdol and Lysolaje area). The new, more spacious buildings allowed for the hiring of new employees, bringing the number of employees to 330 at the end of the 1960s. In addition, other fields of chemical engineering and chemical technology have been newly introduced, such as reactor engineering, homogeneous catalysis, the study of non-Newtonian fluids, sublimation, separation processes, dynamics and control of chemical systems, and others. Most of these new sub-areas have been introduced as needed support for a large multi-year project of development of a complete technology for the production of terephthalic acid and other polyesters.
Since 1989, several reorganizations have taken place, which have led to a gradual reduction in the number of employees by approximately 50%. Heterogeneous and fragmented multidisciplinary research has been rationally integrated, which is reflected in the current structure of the institute. The name was also changed to the more apt “Institute of Chemical Processes”; the traditional English name – “Institute of Chemical Process Fundamentals” has been retained.
Since 2007, the status of the institute has been changed in accordance with Act No. 341/2005 Sb. to a “public research institution (v.v.i.)” with appropriate adjustments of the governing and scientific bodies.

We focus on research in the field of chemistry, new materials, and a number of engineering disciplines. In addition to systematic basic research, we also focus on applied research, where we transform gained knowledge and ideas into concrete outputs with social impacts.

Company description: The Institute (originally called “Institute of Theoretical Foundations of Chemical Technology – ÚTZCHT”) was formally established in the Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences in 1960 by two existing teams, which already had a longer tradition at the time. The first one was the Department of Chemical Technology at the Institute of Chemistry headed by Professor Vladimír Bažant and the other was the Department of Chemical Engineering headed by Professor George Standart. Professor Bažant worked in the field of organosilicon compounds and heterogeneous catalysis, while Prof. Standart continued his research of distillation and extraction processes. In 1964, a group from the Institute of Physical Chemistry dealing with thermodynamics and phase equilibria headed by Prof. Hála joined the new institute. The founder and the first director of the institute was Prof. Bažant until his passing in 1973. Another personality who achieved great recognition and co-created the “image” of the institute was Prof. Eduard Hála.
In 1964, the institute moved to a new campus in the northwestern suburbs of Prague (on the border of Suchdol and Lysolaje area). The new, more spacious buildings allowed for the hiring of new employees, bringing the number of employees to 330 at the end of the 1960s. In addition, other fields of chemical engineering and chemical technology have been newly introduced, such as reactor engineering, homogeneous catalysis, the study of non-Newtonian fluids, sublimation, separation processes, dynamics and control of chemical systems, and others. Most of these new sub-areas have been introduced as needed support for a large multi-year project of development of a complete technology for the production of terephthalic acid and other polyesters.
Since 1989, several reorganizations have taken place, which have led to a gradual reduction in the number of employees by approximately 50%. Heterogeneous and fragmented multidisciplinary research has been rationally integrated, which is reflected in the current structure of the institute. The name was also changed to the more apt “Institute of Chemical Processes”; the traditional English name – “Institute of Chemical Process Fundamentals” has been retained.
Since 2007, the status of the institute has been changed in accordance with Act No. 341/2005 Sb. to a “public research institution (v.v.i.)” with appropriate adjustments of the governing and scientific bodies.

We focus on research in the field of chemistry, new materials, and a number of engineering disciplines. In addition to systematic basic research, we also focus on applied research, where we transform gained knowledge and ideas into concrete outputs with social impacts.

Ground Control Studios is a innovation-driven startup that is focused on the creation of disruptive experiences using XR and AR. We achieve this under two scopes: B2B and Gaming.

For us technology comes along with creativity. So we combine them both to create unique experiences, interactions or solutions to problems. That lead us to develop internal VR, AR and XR SaaS products applicable to the markets of Hospitality, Entertainment, Retail, Construction/Architecture and Manufacturing that have been deployed on Power Companies, Hotel Chains, Retail Chains, Realestate developers, Tourism Boards, City Councils, among others.

For B2B we have developed projects for clients such as Activision-Blizzard, Volkswagen, Citirama or the Portuguese Airforce, among others. These projects range from R&D/Proof-of-concepts to full-fledged solutions/products to be used on a daily basis.

For Gaming we are ID@Xbox Developers, Nintendo Switch Certified Developers and PS4 Approved Studio with a game to release soon on all those platforms, along with PC. Our mobile titles reached around 2.5 Million players between 2011 and 2012.

We believe we grow with the help of our partners. To this effect we have long-lasting technological partnerships with Oculus Inc., Microsoft (Kinect, XBox, Hololens, Azure and Bizspark), Leap Motion, Samsung, Nintendo, Sony, HTC and Valve Inc. We also have product partnerships with relevant Portuguese companies such as Infraspeak (Facility Management) and Impresa Group (Mass-Media Group) where we work together to deploy XR solutions that solve or
improve their operations and add value to their services/clients.

Aero Vision Ltd was founded in 2015 with one main goal - to provide the best services for aerial photography, surveillance, monitoring and services!
 
By the end of 2015 we within the company was designed and manufactured multirotor UAV with the capability of maximum take-off weight of 16 kg and payload of 9 kg. The multirotor was designed as a heavy lifter and further was upgraded with sensors and telemetry system for radioactivity analysis and sending the data in real time to the ground station. That machine was grant with gold medal on the International Technical fair in Plovdiv in 2016 for the category "Ecology and Energetics".

The projects of the company also include specialized training for the special police forces (operational and tactical training with the use of specially equipped multirotor) and training for the Forestry agency (specialized training for localizing of fires and determination of the regions under fire risk with the use of specially equipped UAV with thermal sensors and cameras).

Additionally, Aero Vision Ltd has great experience with international cooperation with different research and development companies and universities within the field of innovative products and technologies.

entityDescription:
The overall aim ofIMDEA Foodis to undertake world class research into food, nutrition and health, and to identify nutritional strategies of economic and social value. Its founding mandate is to translate health and nutrition research into benefits for the economy of the Madrid Region and wider Spain, and into the wellbeing of the country's inhabitants.
Given the high rate of morbidity associated with chronic diseases - the onset and progress of which may be nutrition-associated - and faced with a food industry in Spain that shows strong international competition, Spanish society needs food R&D results.
Nutrition can be an effective tool in the prevention and treatment of chronic disease as different nutrients and food products have been shown to play vital roles in the body's molecular mechanisms. Knowledge of these processes, and the possibility of controlling them via what we eat, has opened up the field of personalised nutrition.
This seeks to invest dietary strategies aimed at improving health with the greatest effectiveness. This, however, can only be achieved when the genetic profile of individual persons, and the context in which they live (together dictating their physiological status), are taken into account. With this knowledge, precision, individualised nutritional interventions can be prescribed, a concept that in the coming years will form part of our everyday lives.
The Institute's activities are orientated towards studying the molecular mechanisms of the human body, the physiological effects of chronic disease, and how these are related to the nutrients we consume.Nutritional strategies need to be designed and validated with precision nutrition in mind, and must therefore focus on individuals and their particular characteristics, i.e., their genetic profile and particular physiological status.
 
Strategic axes
IMDEA Food organises its activities around three strategic axes:
- Axis 1. Science: Advancing scientific knowledge in the area of food and health, with a special focus on the prevention of chronic diseases.
- Axis 2. Business: Contributing towards the economic development and competitiveness of the food industry via the design and validation of nutritional strategies and food products of proven effectiveness in the prevention and treatment of chronic diseases.
- Axis 3. Society: Contributing towards the reduction of healthcare costs and improving the wellbeing of the population through the study of the relationship between diet and health, the execution of communication programmes, and via the dissemination of nutrition advice.

entityDescription: Perspectives Climate Research, based in Freiburg/Germany, is an independent, internationally active, and highly qualified not for profit research think-tank. Perspectives carries out research for governments, international organizations, non-governmental organizations and the private sector, while maintaining high standards of methodological and ecological integrity. Perspectives has an international inter-disciplinary team with extensive expertise in political science, economics, climate engineering, international climate and energy policy and UNFCCC negotiations. As a result of more than two decades of research, we have established an international network of contacts in industry, governments, research and NGOs. Perspectives has in-depth experience with successful baseline and monitoring methodology development under the Kyoto Mechanism’s CDM and JI, NAMAs, NDC establishment and updating, and climate finance. We have developed several studies on the transition of existing market-based mechanisms into Article 6 by assessing potential pathways of transition and implications for specific countries. We are actively engaged in research, evaluation and consultancy projects in numerous sectors, including energy, waste, transport, industry, LULUCF and forestry. We receive funding from a range of government and research institutions, including the World Bank, the Swedish Energy Agency, the Nordic Environment Finance Corporation, the Norwegian Government, the German Ministry for Research and Development, and the German Environmental Agency.

Magellan has expertise in the design and production of rapid and low-cost sounding rocket and microsatellite missions, science experiments aboard the Space Shuttle and the International Space Station, as well as spacecraft subsystems and small satellite bus platforms. Customers have included space mission primes from the commercial space sector, as well as government agencies such as NASA, the European Space Agency (ESA), the Canadian Space Agency (CSA), and the Canadian Department of National Defense (DND).
Magellan Aerospace offers a family of customizable spacecraft bus solutions consisting of the Microsatellite-class MAC-100, MAC-150 and the Smallsat-class MAC-200. Customizable for diverse mission needs, Magellan’s buses are rigorously designed and tested for high reliability and optimum mission performance. Magellan’s flight-proven satellite subsystem equipments can be found today on several Earth orbiting satellites as well as a deep space exploration missions.
On the ground, Magellan’s Canadian-based Advanced Satellite Integration Facility (ASIF) is a unique hub for innovation that turns Magellan’s investment in knowledge and technology into a global advantage for the advancement of our national space industry. Jointly operated with the University of Manitoba, ASIF connects industry with academia in the research, development, construction and testing of satellite buses and subsystems.

description:
At Moofind, we encourage digitalization of the livestock farming, to revolutionize existing practices. Our app enables farmers to remotely monitor the position and well-being of their cattle, as well as select optimal grazing areas, all from the comfort of their home. 
Traditionally, farmers have had to conduct physical inspections of fields to ensure their livestock remains within the paddock boundaries and to monitor their well-being. Additionally, determining optimal grazing areas has relied heavily on the farmers' experience and intuition, often requiring manual inspections. 
Our aim is to streamline operations, enhance productivity, and boost efficiency. Ultimately, this saves valuable time and reduces the daily workload for farmers, allowing them to focus on other important tasks.

entityDescription: ENTROPI.space Ltd. is focusing on advancing tools for microgravity research and simulations, with an emphasis on developing Random Positioning Machines (RPMs) that rotate biological or physical samples to simulate microgravity. Our RPMs are designed to function in challenging environments such as MRI, explosive, and chemically aggressive conditions, offering versatility for specialized experiments. Additionally, we are working on an initiative to provide more accessible zero-gravity flights using a monowing aircraft. This aircraft will be capable of handling up to 6 kg of payload, offering researchers a cost-effective alternative for conducting microgravity experiments, as zero-g flights on larger aircraft are often prohibitively expensive and require complicated planning. Furthermore, our goal is to provide the transport of Earth-tested samples to space stations for further experimentation in true microgravity conditions as a Samples-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution.

entityDescription:
LEAM Technologies GmbH is an innovative developer and provider of advanced additive manufacturing technologies based in Munich, Germany. The company offers a new add-on technology that enhances the extrusion additive manufacturing process by integrating localized radiation heating using focused beams of incoherent light. This technique ensures precise temperature control during the material extrusion process, enabling the production of parts with isotropic properties comparable to conventional manufacturing methods.
LEAM's technology primarily addresses the production of high-performance thermoplastics, which are essential in demanding sectors such as aerospace and space industries. The application of LEAM's system allows for the creation of complex geometries in critical structures, without the material waste associated with traditional manufacturing methods.
LEAM's technology introduces heat exactly where needed, ensuring optimal bonding of the material layers and preserving the stability of previously deposited layers. This approach not only enhances the material properties of printed parts but also significantly increases the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of the additive manufacturing process.
LEAM Technologies GmbH positions itself as a key enabler in the industrial adoption of AM by overcoming existing material quality limitations and setting new standards for material performance in additive manufacturing.

entityName: Centro Regionale Information Communication Technology scrl
description:
The “Regional Centre on Information Communication Technology - CeRICT scrl” is a company that acts in Information and Communication Technology (ICT) domain, with particular focus on the applied research projects.

CeRICT headquarter is placed in Benevento, town located in the middle of the Campania Region.

The Centre’s mission answers the regional and national productive network’s demand for medium and long term advanced research in the ICT sector. Its work is geared towards the technological transfer of results attained and the creation of new productive entities through spin-offs or the establishment of specific businesses.

CeRICT is an organization for accessing competencies and relationship within ICT national and international system. It derives from CRdC ICT project, which was set up at the end of the year 2002 as an initiative of the Campania Region. CRdC ICT project aim was to build a Competence Network in Information and Communication Technologies.

CeRICT was created by ten Partner, in particular by Universities and Public Research Centres of Campania Region, in order to increase their economical and social value by means of the application of their specific competencies. The aim of the CeRICT is to meet the medium and long-term research needs by the interaction of ICT firms, ICT big enterprises, small software houses, authority and public administrations. The mission of the CeRICT is to guide the results of the fundamental research (developed within the academic environment) towards applicative projects realized together with companies, in order to respond to ITC sector’s needs. The technological transfer of the results and the creation of new industrial companies (via spin-offs or specific company build-up) complete the background where the organization carries out its mission.

CeRICT is non profit and Cerict distribuites no profit its members in any way.

More than 200 Professors/Researchers/Technicians, from the Partners, are the “virtual” staff of the CeRICT. Structure of virtual connection that combines intellectual, scientific and entrepreneurial resources characterizing which node of the coordination of the activities of the Regional Program of Search. Each Partner works as an "access portal" to the whole set of competencies available in the region, for each specific area. The direction and management (planning and responsibility) is distributed in the whole region.

entityName: Institute of Psychology of The Czech Academy of Sciences
entityDescription:
The Institute of Psychology of the Czech Academy of Sciences focuses on research in the field of psychology in the Czech Republic with an international impact. The mission of the Institute of Psychology CAS, v. v. i. (founded in 1967) is to conduct scientific research on the human psyche, human behaviour, and functioning in general. We focus on studying human personality development, maturation, and functioning, social processes in small groups and large communities, and mental processes such as perception, attention, language, emotions, and motivation. We are engaged in the advancement of existing and the development of new methods of psychological research.
Our institute includes the Laboratory of Behavioral and Linguistic Studies (LABELS), where we conduct experimental studies in psychology and other behavioural sciences. The results of our research are published in international scientific journals, and we also publish our journal, Czechoslovak Psychology, which features articles in both Czech and English. We participate in organizing scientific conferences and educational events. In cooperation with universities (primarily Charles University and Masaryk University), we educate doctoral students in psychology and related fields. We operate a specialized library accessible to the public and popularize findings from psychological science through the media.

entityDescription:
Heaven Labs s.r.o. is a relatively young company focused on the development and production of nutritionally complete meals - Mana™. We produce and deliver nutritionally complete meals to the EU and nearly every corner of the world. Our nutritionally complete food can be ordered here: https://mojemana.cz/ . The goal of the long-term strategy of Heaven Labs s.r.o. is to reach a point where all products are produced within a closed environmental chain with zero carbon footprint. To achieve this goal, the company is seeking new ways to reduce waste, find the most eco-friendly packaging materials, and use more renewable energy in all production processes. As part of this effort, the company aims to find excellent nutrients for its products and become self-sufficient in their production. The research and development team is continuously working on improving the composition of the already produced foods and will also work on finding suitable ingredients and ensuring their in-house cultivation. As part of the long-term development, the company aims to develop new products that will be nutritionally rich and serve as a plant-based alternative to products from the traditional meat, bakery, and fishing industries. The development strategy includes clinical studies comparing the nutrient utilization of these products in the body to that of animal-based products.The design and research & development team proudly boasts experience from the prestigious NASA Deep Space Food Challenge, where they contributed to innovative solutions in food technology for space missions. The team developed a robust system for assembling, producing, and distributing nutritionally complete meals, capable of sustaining a four-member crew on a three-year mission in deep space. All of this was achieved with minimal energy requirements and maximum efficiency, while minimizing waste and reducing any negative impacts on the spaceship.
The company has thus capitalized on its 10 years of expertise in the field of nutritionally complete meals, along with its innovative spirit and commitment to advancing human knowledge, science, and technology as a whole.

entityDescription:
NOW Systems (Nologin Oceanic Weather Systems SLU) has a strong experience in operational oceanography, supporting services (using regional/coastal ocean models and data assimilation schemes, together with remote sensed and in-situ observational data products) and building ad hoc co-designed end-user applications for an inspiring access to environmental data. 
NOW has a strong engagement with the Copernicus Marine Service (CMS), being operational provider (previously as Nologin) in 2 of its Production Centres: Nologin/NOW co-leads with MOI the CMS Iberian-Biscay-Ireland Monitoring and Forecasting Centre (IBI-MFC), being responsible of the operational delivery of near-real-time model forecasts and multi-year reanalysis model products for the European Atlantic façade. As partner of the CMS Insitu Thematic Assembly Centre (INS-TAC), NOW deals with the operational provision of in-situ observational products for the IBI region. 
NOW is quite experienced in product quality assessment, making combined uses of model, satellite and in-situ data sources, and generating new products using AI-based approaches.Together with the regional and coastal operational services focused on the near-real-time monitoring and short-term forecast, NOW Systems is contributing to build climate services, generating multi-year regional reanalysis products, and making coastal downscaling of climate change scenarios to generate appropriate ocean climate indicators.
NOW participates in several R&D projects and innovative actions at International, European and national level (i.e. through the EU H2020 and HE programmes, the UN Ocean Decade collaborative action, etc.). 
NOW Systems provides to its customers solutions, knowledge, and services for a more sustainable and cost-effective management of marine and coastal activities; being a reliable partner to build the operational services and Digital Twin approaches, needed and envisioned by our customers.

- deploy more software packages on shared payload satellites
- reduce the size of the software package - faster upload / updates; use less memory and processor resources - maximize the power of the on board compute chip
- facilitate edge computing on board the satellite - process the data in space and send only the useful insights to the ground

description: Know Center (KC) is Austria’s leading research center for trustworthy AI. As a renowned research organization with excellent science team, large partner network, successful business venture, and proven organizational structure, we apply for COMET funding for our ambitious research program on Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence & Data for Sustainability, Industry 4.0, and Life Sciences. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a universal tool, providing opportunities for solving global challenges and generating massive economic benefits in the twin green & digital transformation. However, the European population distrusts AI & Data. Europe must regain technology and data sovereignty and develop a vision of AI based on humanistic values to restore trust in the digital transformation. 360-degree vision for Trustworthy AI & Data. We have derived our 360-degree vision from EU’s definition of Trustworthy AI (TAI). Our interdisciplinary research will investigate technical robustness, safety, privacy, data governance, transparency, diversity, non-discrimination, fairness, accountability, as well as human agency and oversight. Our vision develops these requirements into scientific challenges and research fields and identifies application areas in business ecosystems, which together form a holistic and interdisciplinary research program for Austrian leadership in Trustworthy AI & Data.
entityDescription:
Know Center Research GmbH (KC) is Austria’s leading center for trustworthy AI research. With an outstanding team of scientists, a robust partner network, successful industry collaborations, and a proven organizational structure, Know-Center is committed to advancing the frontiers of data science and artificial intelligence (AI). Our current application for COMET funding is centered on a visionary research program addressing Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence (TAI) & Data for Sustainability, Industry 4.0, and Life Sciences.
AI has emerged as a transformative technology, capable of addressing global challenges and driving the twin green and digital transformation, resulting in significant economic opportunities. Yet, there remains a pervasive mistrust of AI and data within the European population. Restoring this trust is critical, and Europe must take the lead in developing AI grounded in humanistic values to ensure technology and data sovereignty.
To address this, Know Center has developed a comprehensive 360-degree vision for Trustworthy AI & Data, aligned with the European Union’s definition of TAI. Our interdisciplinary research agenda will focus on the critical dimensions of AI: technical robustness, safety, privacy, data governance, transparency, diversity, non-discrimination, fairness, accountability, and human agency and oversight. We aim to transform these requirements into scientific challenges and new research fields, while identifying strategic application areas in business ecosystems that establish Austria as a leader in Trustworthy AI & Data.
The research program is structured around six core research areas—Data Management for AI, Data Privacy for AI, Methods & Algorithms for AI, Human-Centric AI, Fair AI, and Digital Transformation Design—each conducting cutting-edge research on fundamental aspects of TAI & Data. Additionally, three strategic projects will integrate this interdisciplinary research along the AI lifecycle, culminating in the development of open-source software frameworks: KnowAIDE, KnowTWINS, and KnowCERTIFAI. Furthermore, twelve applied research projects will foster AI specialization in three critical business ecosystems, in collaboration with a consortium of 40 company partners.
The success of this initiative is bolstered by a strong alliance of 26 scientific partners, supported by a network of over 280 European and 20 international leading scientific institutions. This extensive collaboration will enable us to drive impactful research and technology transfer to three key business ecosystems: (1) Environment, Energy, and Sustainability, (2) Production, Automation, and Logistics (Industry 4.0), and (3) Medicine, Pharmaceutics, and Health (Life Sciences). Our work will contribute significantly to Austria’s position in achieving the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the EU Green Deal.

entityDescription: Masaryk Memorial Cancer Institute (MMCI) is the largest cancercenter in the Czech Republic in terms of the number of primarily treated adult patients with solid tumors and the provision of preventive cancer care. Almost 5 000 newly diagnosed cancer patients start treatment in MMCI every year. MMCI currently plays the role of the National cancer center in the network of Czech Comprehensive Cancer Centers. MMCI is an internationally recognized Institute, an accredited member of the Organization of European Cancer Institutes(OECI) and ESMO Designated Centre of Integrated Oncology and Palliative Care. MMCI is also a member of ERN network for rare adult solid cancers EURACAN and for genetic tumor risk syndromes GENTURIS. MMCI serves as a national node of the BBMRI-ERIC research infrastructure for biobanking and is a partner of Czech Clinical Research Infrastructure Network (CZECRIN). MMCI is providing health care services, research and education in the areas of prevention, diagnosis and treatment of solid tumors. MMCI is affiliated to Masaryk University, within which it cooperates with two other university hospitals, namely University Hospital Brno and St. Anne‘s University Hospital. MMCI operates its own facility for basic and translational research called RECAMO (Research Centre for Applied Molecular Oncology) and provides full support for clinical research, including Phase I Clinical Trial Unit, biobanking and precision oncology programme.

entityDescription:
Carboneg Group s.r.o.

Carboneg stands for the innovative synergy between future-proof agricultural practices and environmental responsibility. By assisting farmers in transitioning to regenerative agriculture, Carboneg plays a key role in the development of sustainable and resilient food systems. Farmers engaged in the Carboneg program are financially compensated for their contributions to capturing carbon in the soil, enhancing water retention, and promoting increased biodiversity. In terms of revenue generation, Carboneg is harnessing the potential of carbon credit sales to cater to its corporate clientele. To be able to tackle the needs of local environments, ecosystems and communities, Carboneg works closely with its local Agents. Agents are responsible for signing up and onboarding farmers for the Carboneg program. Through its Agent network, Carboneg is currently present on four continents with farmers and ranchers operating their livelihoods on more than 150000 hectares of land. As the world of agriculture gets increasingly challenged by the loss of biodiversity, distorted water cycles and ever more demanding food supply chains, the scale of needed transformation is unprecedented. Carboneg is now looking for new Agents to be part of this pioneering change. This document unfolds the details about the synergy between the impact Carboneg is making directly and the opportunities it creates for its critical stakeholders, farmers and Carboneg Agents alike. The Manual serves as the primary guideline to successfully operate the Carboneg program. The mission of Carboneg is to contribute to carbon negativity and healthier soil. The vision of Carboneg is to sequester 1 billion tonnes of CO2 in the soil by the year 2030. Carboneg was born in the Czech Republic in 2021 as a spin-off project of the employee benefits service company Benefit Management Ltd. Carboneg as well as Benefit Management Ltd was founded by Mr Vaclav Kurel who currently serves as Carboneg’s Chief Executive. After almost half a year of its existence, Carboneg managed to attract around 27 farmers into its regenerative farming program covering around 3 000 Ha of land in the Czech Republic and Slovakia. In 2022 Carboneg expanded its operations further abroad, specifically through partnerships in Kyrgyzstan and Romania. By 2023, Carboneg extended its team to 17 members covering all key functions and is currently well established for further international development. By the end of the year 2023, Carboneg aims to cover the total area of 250000 hectares of cropland and pastures under its flagship Program.

entityDescription:
Guardian Space aims to transform how communities and professionals manage risks and respond to disasters through its innovative community hubs. These hubs act as localized networks that connect residents, businesses, professionals, and insurers, facilitating the sharing of resources, collaboration, and access to real-time disaster intelligence.
Under the Community Hubs umbrella, we offer tailored solutions for both individuals and professionals:
CommunityHub.me equips individuals and small businesses with tools to find insurance coverage, manage claims, and facilitate payouts. Partnering with insurance providers, this platform incentivizes risk reduction through discounted rates and community-based risk diffusion, ensuring users obtain the most appropriate coverage.
CommunityHub.pro is designed for EMTs, firefighters, police, and other experts who require advanced tools and dashboards to monitor and mitigate risks. It provides real-time insights across 18 disaster types, enabling informed decisions that enhance community resilience.
On the insurance side, our Insurance EVENT360 Dashboard offers a comprehensive view of community risks and claims. Insurers can track incidents, assess claims efficiently, and identify opportunities for risk reduction, fostering collaboration with communities to create tailored insurance solutions.
Guardian Space promotes a collaborative approach to disaster management and risk reduction, equipping communities and professionals with the necessary resources and information to build safer, more resilient environments.
Our success is supported by collaborations with key partners such as the European Space Agency (ESA) and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). Our innovations have been recognized by institutions including the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) and the United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs (UNOOSA).

Green Elephant Biotech is a start-up founded in 2021 by Dr. Joel Eichmann and Felix Wollenhaupt in Giessen, Germany. Green Elephant Biotech aims to offer both academic institutions and the manufacturing industry a way to reduce their carbon footprint while enabling process intensification by developing and distributing novel, technologically innovative, plant-based, single-use laboratory consumables.
Green Elephant is a worldwide pioneer in using the plant-based polymer Polylactic Acid (PLA) for labware. The company enables the production of novel cell and gene therapies and biopharmaceuticals by offering efficient and scalable cell cultivation devices and consumables. In doing so, they contribute to a healthier world for both people and the planet.

entityName: Consorzio Interuniversitario Nazionale per la Scienza e Tecnologia dei Materiali - INSTM
entityDescription:
INSTM. The acronym may be short, but in the world of Italian and international research, it carries considerable weight. Indeed, INSTM, theNational Interuniversity Consortium of Materials Science and Technology, is the largest consortium of its kind in Italy, drawing on the expertise of no less than52 universities – and all those that are active in Italy in researching advanced materials and technologies. The individual universities' voluntary affiliation with INSTM allows their Research Professors and Fellows to participate in the Consortium's activities through the presentation of research proposals. In the last few years,over 2700tenured professors, research fellows, holders of research and scholarship grants and doctorate students have taken advantage of this opportunity, and the numbers are growing year on year.
This is a great success by any measure, especially if we consider that consortia like INSTM typically have limited budgets. Like other such organisations, INSTM's chargeis to unite and concentrate the efforts of its affiliatesto help them become more competitive both in Italy and abroad in securing funds and financing. And it is here that INSTM excels, providing the organisational, technical and financial support necessary topromote research activities in science and technologywithin its affiliate universities. Its efficiency in bringing together andmanaging their considerable talents creates an effective critical mass that renders them highly competitive in taking on innovative research projects. Such projects may benefit Italy's business community, or may support initiatives in the development of technology transfer, providing significant opportunities for the academic and industrial spheres to benefit from their mutual interaction.
The success of this strategy is undeniable. This is underlined by thesheer number and quality of the domestic and international projectsinvolving INSTM's research groups that have been financed to date. It is further confirmed by theConsortium's partnerships, developed right from its inception, with important public and private research organisations, laboratories and companies active in the sector.

description: Our Technology The Varadis radiation detection sensor is a microelectronic chip, specially engineered to be sensitive to high energy (ionizing) radiation. Small, robust and requiring no power to detect radiation, our cost-effective RADFETs (Radiation Sensing Field Effect Transistor) can be easily integrated into electronic systems. Our innovative technology enables us to offer the world's most effective and dynamic radiation monitoring components, devices and dosimeter systems to some of the globe's most recognized organizations.
entityDescription:
Varadis is a deep technology product company, focused on building and selling the world’s most effective and dynamic radiation monitoring components, devices and systems.
Varadis is a spin-out company from Tyndall National Institute in Cork , Ireland and are building a global portfolio of customers within the Space, Government, Industrial and Healthcare markets.
Varadis is also part on the European Space Agency BIC in Cork. Our RADFETs have previously been supplied to the International Space Station and programs such as NASA's Living with a Star Program, EuCPAD dosimeter for astronauts, GlobalStar, Rosetta, Gallileo, Alphasat, ESA's STRV-1c, JAXA's MDS-1 & SDS-1 and ESA's Chimera experiment.

Varadis Radiation Sensing Field Effect Transistors (RADFETs) come packaged as plastic or ceramic hermetically sealed, robust, discrete MOS transistors optimised for the detection of ionising radiation. 
They are small and lightweight, combining the positive features of zero power passive dosimeters and the dynamic capability of active dosimeters.
Varadis RADFETs measure radiation exposure or dose together with an associated reader which converts the measured quantity in the sensor into an absorbed dose measurement for the user.
Optimized for radiation sensitivity to ionizing radiation: gamma rays, X rays and protons, Varadis RADFETs are ideal for space applications, including housekeeping of satellites, space radiation environment studies, shielding analysis and monitoring of radiation-hardened electronic components.

Our suite of products centres on enhancing the dependability of onboard data systems that embed COTS SoC-FPGAs, where solutions with radiation-hardened devices fail to meet performance re-quirements and SWaP-C constraints.

entityDescription:
For more than 125 years, Goodyear has developed tire technologies and solutions to give people the confidence to go further and faster. It’s Goodyear’s spirit of innovation that keeps vehicles on roads of every surface, around racetracks, in the air and even on the moon.
Goodyear’s innovative tires have been industry leaders for more than 125 years. The company introduced the first “all-weather” tire, sent tires to the moon and claims the winningest racing tires around the world. Throughout its history, Goodyear has enhanced mobility from streets and highways to farms and work sites and even in the skies. It has developed tires that improve traction on slippery roads, maximize fuel economy and continue to run even when flat.
Goodyear’s scientists, engineers and researchers have continually discovered new solutions and opportunities for changing mobility needs. For example, polymer research led to the development of synthetic rubber for use in tires and beyond. Material science unearthed new components to enhance performance and durability. And new technology was applied to tire design and enabled virtual tire testing.

Goodyear is more than a tire manufacturer. Since its founding, Goodyear has evolved to become a technology-driven company that enables mobility. Along the way, it also has innovated its business models, expanded its manufacturing and sales and even became the first tire brand to sell directly to consumers online. More breakthroughs, such as mobile tire installation, are setting the pace for the industry for the next 125 years.

entityName: Mikrobiologicky ustav AV CR, v. v. i.
entityDescription:
The Institute of Microbiology of the CAS represents the largest scientific body extensively exploring life cycles, molecular mechanisms and regulatory systems of various microorganisms such as bacteria, yeast, fungi and algae) as well as mammalian cell lines with respect to basic research questions as well as their prospective practical exploitation in medicine and industry.
The main research interests of our Institute represent cellular and molecular microbiology, genetics and physiology of microorganisms and their resistance to antibiotics, production of microbial metabolites and their biotransformation, and grading up production strains by genetic modifications etc.
Another main research direction is embodied by soil ecology, ecotoxicology and microbial degradation of organic pollutants in the natural environment. An immunological section of the Institute then studies the importance of microorganisms in phylogenetic and ontogenetic acquisition of immunity as well as during the onset of autoimmune diseases and, last but not least, it is also focused on immunotherapies of oncogenic diseases.
Institute of Microbiology of the CAS has an internationally recognized collection of basidiomycetes and its own biotechnological unit, which is mainly used to monitor microbiological and biotechnological processes at a semi-operational scale.
IM CAS has three satellite working units outside of Prague; the first of which is in Trebon (research on phototrophic microorganisms) the second is in Novy Hradek (gnotobiology) and third is in Nove Hrady (Center for Nanobiology and Structural Biology).
Despite the fact that the Institute of Microbiology of the CAS is preferentially focused on the basic research, many of its outputs find or will find practical use in pharmaceutical as well as biotechnological industry as documented by a genuine interest of a number of private companies in our scientific work.

entityName: Fundación del Sector Público Estatal Centro Nacional de Investigaciones Oncológicas Carlos III (F.S.P. CNIO)
entityDescription:
The Spanish National Cancer Research Centre (CNIO) was founded in 1998 within the Instituto de Salud Carlos III (ISCiii). The CNIO operates as a public foundation, governed by its Board of Trustees. It conducts research of excellence in oncology, translates scientific knowledge into clinical practice, and transfers the technology developed at the CNIO to the productive sector.
Employing more than 500 researchers, our scientific activities are undertaken by 28 Groups, 18 Core Units and 3 Sections. The Groups are organized in a Basic Research Area (Molecular Oncology and Structural Biology Programmes) and a Patient-Oriented Research Area (Human Cancer Genetics and Clinical Research Programmes). Also, there are two Programmes under the Innovation Direction, the Biotechnology Programme, providing scientific and technological support, and the Experimental Therapeutics Programme, focused on early drug discovery.
The CNIO is recognised as one of the top leading Cancer Research Institutes worldwide, and its scientific contributions are published in top journals. During the last five years, the CNIO has increased its scientific productivity, with 395 publications in journals with impact factor higher than 10 (vs. 330 in the period 2014-2018). According to the latest SCImago Report, the CNIO occupies the 8th position among cancer-focused research centres worldwide, and the 3rd in Europe. In the ranking of Nature Index 2024, the CNIO holds the 9th position worldwide, the 2nd in Europe, across cancer research centres.

entityDescription:
Mare Ingeni Lab P.S.A. (MI Lab) is a startup emerging in the space market in Poland. It was founded by individuals who initiated national capabilities and the SSA system in Poland within the Polish Space Agency from 2015 to 2021 through the establishment of the National SSA Operations Center, a network of sensors, and Poland's accession to EUSST. These founders include Prof. Maciej Konacki, Lt. Col. Arkadiusz Chimicz, and Adrian Malacz.
Due to the knowledge and experience of its personnel, the company possesses profound expertise in the area of SSA system requirements, achieved through the implementation of tasks in sensor research, observational capabilities, architecture optimization, and orbit calculations. These capabilities have been reinforced by various courses attended by key personnel (ESA SSA Basic Course, STK/ODTK course, AMOS course), seminars, articles (AMOS), and SST observations (AMOS).
The team members combine scientific competencies in astronomical observations, engineering skills in mechatronics, data analysis and processing, and organizational capabilities. The rapid and efficient construction of the SSA system and the quality of implemented and maintained sensors in Poland, despite financial constraints, is the best testament to the expertise of the individuals forming the company. This ensures the reliability and quality of the work performed within the project.

entityDescription:
The Italian Academy of Forest Sciences, is an independent Institution, under the umbrella of the Ministry of Cultural Affairs. The present Statute dates from 1952. The Academy is organized in 4 sections: Forest economics, policy and law; Silviculture and Environment protection, Forest Engineering, Forest technology and industries.
The Italian Academy of Forest Sciences was founded on June 21st, 1951, with a decree signed by Prof. Amintore Fanfani, then Minister of Agriculture and Forestry. The first President, in office until 1980, was Prof. Generoso Patrone. His successors have been Alessandro de Philippis and Fiorenzo Mancini. At the moment the President is Orazio Ciancio.
The aim of the Academy is to contribute to the progress of forest sciences, and related juridical, historical and economic aspects, considering their implications in silviculture, as fundamental elements for national prosperity.
The Academy promotes research on scientific, technical, economic and law issues related to forest management and environmental protection;organises conferences, workshops and seminars in these fields;publishes academic proceedings, technical and scientific studies, surveys, monographs, collections of essays and journals and has a library specialized in forest sciences.
In all these activities, theAcademycooperates with similar national and foreign institutions.
