description: Curf specializes in guiding industries towards the effective implementation of artificial intelligence. At the heart of our transformative approach lies Synigen, an innovative solution designed to empower businesses through integration of synthetic data. Synigen not only facilitates seamless transitions to automated processes and artificial intelligence, but also accommodates organizations with limited or sparse datasets. With Curf as your partner, you can embrace AI's potential, regardless of your initial data resources. With our hardware solutions and machines, CSI-100, we're here to help you future-proof your quality control, self-diagnostic solutions or spatial situational awareness for detecting anomalies.
entityDescription:
Computer vision (CV) is a discipline that focuses on developing techniques through which computers can perceive and interpret the content of digital images. CV is used in many industrial applications for quality control or anomaly detection, and increasingly, CV systems are based on artificial intelligence (AI) for image analysis. In AI developments, data is the most crucial and valuable pillar. In the real world, collecting accurate and high-quality data is complex, expensive, and time-consuming. A certain portion of the labelled data will contain inaccuracies due to human interaction in the annotation process. Additionally, for rare defects / anomalies, the difficulty of collecting a sufficient number of images is even greater, especially in space applications where products or applications are produced in very small batches. 
With our product, Synigen, the customer can generate accurate, high-quality, automatically annotated, and labelled realistic synthetic images of a 3D object or scene with the automatic integration of anomalies or defects on the chosen objects. The intuitive graphical interface allows the user to create large datasets of a product containing defects/anomalies even before the actual production begins. This dataset can be used as input for training an AI model that can be used in any computer vision task. The advantages compared to real data are: 
- Speed: there is no need to wait for the "real-world" setup to capture a sufficient number of images suitable for anomaly detection, even for rarely occurring anomalies. 
- Accuracy: our images are automatically labeled and annotated, eliminating biases/errors introduced by human interaction in the process. 
- Flexibility: the models can be easily updated or modified without costly impact. 
- Cost: compared to "real-world" images, our synthetic images cost only a fraction.
With our approach, non-software people can create the necessary data, leaving the software/machine learning engineers use their skills and talent to other complicated tasks. 
A CV based on our solution would be a perfect add-on for: 
• automated anomaly inspection (defects, wrong assembly, PCB…) or for self-diagnostics of systems 
• automated object recognition for spatial situational awareness (debris or adversarial entities) or for part detection 
 
Besides the software, our company is specialized in the development of the needed hardware, with or without robots, for capturing the needed anomalies in an image as well as doing inference on these images allowing self-diagnostics or situational awareness.
The existing NDT (non-destructive testing) for major aerospace suppliers (materials, engine parts, bolts…) can benefit of our solution. In a further future, automatically conditioned and functioning farms and systems will be necessary in long distance travelling (to Mars) or missions on the surface of Mars / Moon. Therefore, an AI system helping the detection of anomalies will be inevitable.

Aquila Bioscience (ABL, www.aquilabioscience.com) is a life sciences company dedicated to developing innovative, effective, and technologically advanced products inspired by nature to protect people from natural and man-made biothreats, including COVID-19, H1N1, and Anthrax. Founded by a world-leading expert in carbohydrate biology (glycoscience), ABL leverages its core expertise in exploiting carbohydrate-protein interactions—essential for pathogens to bind to surfaces and hosts—to develop cutting-edge Pathogen Capture Technology (PCT) for decontamination. Committed to sustainability, ABL focuses on creating environmentally friendly solutions that are both effective and sustainable.
ABL secured support from the European Defence Agency and the European Union’s H2020 programs to develop the decontamination technology aimed at combating biothreats and infectious agents. With proven efficacy against Category A pathogens and viruses, Aquila Bioscience’s protein-carbohydrate based PCT was also awarded a European Innovation Council Accelerator Grant to scale up the commercial production of ABwipeTM, addressing the market's need for safer and more effective decontamination products during COVID-19 pandemic, saving countless lives and significant economic resources.

entityName: University of Zagreb Faculty of Geodesy - Chair of Geoinformation
entityDescription:
The Chair of Geoinformation is part of the Institute of Cartography and Photogrammetry at the University of Zagreb Faculty of Geodesy, which was established in 2005 through the merger of two historic institutes: the Institute of Photogrammetry (founded in 1941) and the Institute of Cartography (founded in 1956). The Institute is comprised of three chairs: Chair of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing, Chair of Geoinformation and Chair of Cartography.

The Chair of Geoinformation focuses on teaching courses related to the handling and management of geoinformation, with a particular emphasis on cartography and Geographic Information Systems (GIS). In 2013, the Chair established Croatia’s first Open Source Geospatial Lab (OSGL), which is part of the global GeoForAll network. The lab's mission is to connect academia, industry, and public administration in the use and development of open-source geoinformation systems and data.

In addition to its educational activities, the Chair conducts scientific research in areas such as open data, service-oriented cartography, and GIS.

entityDescription: Bulduri Technical School(former "Bulduri Horticultural High School") is located on the territory of the ancient Bilderliņi crown manor on the banks of Lielupe, Bulduri, Jūrmala, near the sea. Since 1910, future specialists in the field of horticulture and horticulture have been educated in this place. Today, the training of young specialists in landscape gardening and construction, floristry, tourism, hospitality and catering industries is equally taking place! Here is the small ideal Latvia, where the truly Latvian - functional, aesthetic and durable gene is born. However, Bulduru Technical University is not only an educational institution, but at the same time it is also a company where various innovative business ideas are implemented. Young people have the opportunity to be with the introduction of the latest technologies, gain unique experience and become sought-after specialists or brave young entrepreneurs. In the territory of the technical school, there are modernly equipped greenhouses with an area of ​​2400 m2, as well as a practical training area - fields and beds with an area of ​​23 ha. The technical department has materials at its disposal - technical base and garden equipment. Advantages of training in Bulduri - theory is learned in practical work in the school's learning park, garden and greenhouse. Modern garden equipment and one of the most modern greenhouses in Latvia are available. The technical school hasa plant biotechnology laboratory, where horticulture students study and school students do practical work. An opportunity to develop the Student's Scientific Research Work. Research is also carried out in the molecular biology laboratory. Agrochemical laboratories are also under construction. Our technical school is the only vocational education institution in Latvia, which has a laboratory of this type, in which school students undergo training. A unique project has been created at the Technical University - the onlysmart garden in Latvia"Latvijas i-Dārzs". The goal of the project was to make a robot that moves between the plant beds, photographs and scans the plants with different cameras to follow the development of the plants. The control functions of the robot operate the watering system, determine the appearance of diseases and pests in time, and collect information in the database.

entityDescription:
1/About Amnovis

Amnovis is an additive manufacturing production and engineering companythat's built on no-nonsense entrepreneurship.
At Amnovis, we believe the full potential of additive manufacturing can be unlocked through thoughtful innovations, which we intend to enable for the utilization in regulated and high-tech industries.To achieve our purpose, we strive to be the catalyst of the innovation process, continuously looking for technical challenges and opportunities to redefine the state-of-the-art in AM.

2/Technologies
Bespoke 3D printing in metal and plastic

Titanium 3D printingfor demanding industries
We are innovating various titanium 3D printing applications across a broad spectrum of medical device types. As innovators of AM technology, material and applications, we are able to manufacture faster with higher quality, both standard and personalized implants.

Copper 3D printing ofstrong, conductive components
The past years, we researched and engineered the manufacturing of highly conductive copper components using the L-PFB process. We use proprietary material and process expertise to manufacture copper components with state-of-the-art electrical, thermal and mechanical properties.

Stereolithographyfor medical purposes
Our expertise in medical device 3D printing and strong focus on quality systems make us a preferred manufacturer of plastic components in medical markets and other highly regulated industries.
3/ Services

Contract manufacturing
as it should be

Increased product performance throughAM engineering
Our engineering services target customers who envision breakthrough products. The specialist of Amnovis co-engineer AM products by working closely with customers to take advantage of the full potential of AM. This effort may be focused on a one-off custom product or may lead to high-volume production. We are able to increase product performance through our innovation-driven approach focused on process, technology, material and quality.
Research and development that shapes the future of AM
As part of our drive for innovation, Amnovis is actively involved in multiple R&D programs. These cover internal projects, as well as projects in collaboration with external organizations. We also engage in R&D projects with customers to shape and boost their product innovation roadmap.

description: UrbanSens is a data-driven startup focused on delivering high-resolution environmental insights through a combination of satellite imagery, IoT networks, and cloud-based technology. By leveraging advanced datasets and innovative tools, we help businesses, governments, and communities make informed decisions to better manage environmental impacts and promote sustainable development.
entityDescription:
UrbanSens is a geospatial technology company specialising in satellite Earth Observation, geospatial AI and data-driven decision-support services for the utility, energy and urban infrastructure sectors. The company develops methods to translate space-based observations and complementary geospatial data into operational information for distribution system operators, municipal utilities, cities and infrastructure planners.
UrbanSens is convinced that the transformation of energy, utility and urban systems cannot be planned with static, fragmented or outdated information. Its mission is to make Earth Observation actionable for real-world infrastructure decisions, from demand assessment and network planning to urban development and environmental resilience. With this approach, UrbanSens aims to move from observing change to enabling it: from Earth Observers to Earth Changers.

description:
Custom designed and advanced turnkey solutions to any inspection problem you might have.
JLI Vision A/S was founded in 1985, and is one of the oldest dedicated vision companies in the world. With more than 39 years of industry experience, 400+ years of compiled experience and 1800+ systems shipped worldwide and counting, we make custom designed & advanced turnkey solutions to any inspection problem you might have. We have experience working with inspection of glass cartridges, with defects down to the tens of micrometers in size, to large-scale steel and other metal surface inspection, microchip inspection, plastics, wood and much more. We offer independent consulting to tailor the inspection solution to your needs and desires, and are working with you throughout the entire process. We are generally known for finding solutions to "impossible" inspection problems. 
Our solutions in the past have involved 2D and 3D inspection, Hybrid-vision, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, general Computer Vision approaches and much more. We are a well-known System Integrator for some of the largest Danish companies, as well as for many companies worldwide. We are capable of either delivering end-to-end systems that takes care of the entire inspection process for you, or integrating and installing our systems seamlessly into existing machinery and systems on-site. Following installation of our solutions, we can take care of the system maintenance, patching and optimizing for you to ensure the solution remains viable and competitive years down the line. We have extensive experience working in demanding industries with very low margins of error, such as the medical industry. Here we have complied successfully with the many additional and extensive requirements for vision systems in this industry, such as audit-trailing, GAMP-5 category 5, URS, FAT, SAT and many others. We meet the very high requirements of vision systems that are also present in the aerospace and space industry.
For information on how we approach vision solutions with very high demands and thorough documentation standards, please refer to the following hyperlinks to two videos from our vision lab: Why machine vision for medical is difficult and how we solve the challenge, Creating a validated machine learning solution for Pharma.

Our services are available to you no matter where you might be in the world, and we have installed and serviced systems in countries like Brazil, China, Japan, The United States, Malaysia, most European countries and more. Our team consists of 40+ highly competent engineers from various engineering and scientific backgrounds, ensuring a broad technical profile to solve any task, utilizing the latest and best technology on the market. We are good at thinking outside of the box, and combining approaches and techniques from different fields to find new and innovate approaches to any problem. We also dedicate a large sum of money for our R&D department to ensure we follow along with the latest research trends and don't stagnate or fall behind due to more "conservative" approaches. We see ourselves as enemies of the "that's the way it's always been done"-type of mindset. 
For further insight into how we approach various inspection problems, please use the following hyperlink to view our Vision Lab video series on our website: JLI Vision's Vision Lab video series.

entityDescription: Igence Radar Ltd was founded in 1995 to develop and exploit models of all aspects of radar operation and performance. The team has many years of experience of radar research and technology leading to an understanding of the scientific principles of EM scattering, radar signal & clutter fluctuations and processing, which underpin the operation of modern radar systems. Radar signal processing algorithms and concepts, developed for the detection of small targets in clutter, have been widely implemented in both experimental and operational radars. We have also considerable experience of tracking including the development and implementation of novel tracking algorithms and the production of mathematical models characterising their performance. We have a solid track record of rapidly prototyping radar software applications to analyse trials data to assess radar performance and to de-risk upgrades to radar signal processing. This capability is built on our Virtual Radar Library (ViRad), which is a library of tried and tested C++ classes for radar simulation, signal processing and performance modelling. It allows us to construct a wide range of reliable, bespoke, radar applications in a timely and cost effective manner. In addition to our work on radar our areas of expertise include: Radar Signal processing (including Maritime Surveillance, Synthetic Aperture, Pulsed-Doppler); Radar project support; Radar modelling, performance prediction and simulation; Bayesian techniques including Bayes Nets and Tracking algorithms; Mathematical modelling; Image exploitation, classification and automatic target recognition; Synthetic Aperture Radar image formation, motion compensation and autofocus; Electromagnetic Scattering e.g. propagation modelling, integral equation description of low grazing angle scattering of microwaves; Change detection (coherent and incoherent SAR change detection, optical change detection); Rapid prototyping of software applications.

entityDescription:
Prometheus Sensing Ltd
 
Wildfires can cause significant damage to ecosystems, the environment and communities and cost billions of dollars every year around the world - including the UK. While some ecosystems have evolved to require occasional burning, wildfires are increasing in frequency, severity and range. This increase is due to a number of factors including global warming and human activity. It is reported that between 65% and 90% of wildfires have an anthropogenic cause.
Satellite-borne infra-red cameras have been used for a number of years to detect wildfires although the spatial and temporal resolution has been a limiting factor. Recent advances in the resolution of these systems provides an opportunity to detect wildfires much earlier in their life when they are small and manageable. Prometheus Sensing Ltd are developing a system that uses these high resolution images to not only detect wildfires but to provide the following services.
- Extract fire characteristics from the images such as growth rate, fire-line intensity, spot fire density, etc.

- Provide pseudo real-time information to command and frontline firefighters.

- Deploy Uncrewed Air Vehicles (UAV) autonomously to tackle early-life wildfires and to support conventional firefighters with larger fires.

Prometheus Sensing's mission is to reduce the environmental, societal and financial costs of wildfires as well as reducing the risk of harm to firefighters through timely and effective interventions.

description:
Danish Aerospace Company (DAC) is a high-tech company operating in the area of advanced medical instrumentation and other engineering fields primarily within space applications. Our products are based on many years of specialized research and development. These consist of developing, integrating, and applying new as well as established medical technologies to the challenges of functioning and remaining reliable in space. These products and services bring the potential of space research and experience from space operations down to Earth for the benefit of all Mankind. 
The hardware from DAC (more than 3,2 ton) has flown on the majority of todays manned and unmanned space transportation vehicles. This includes flights on: All US Space Shuttles (Now retired) Soyuz capsules from Russia (manned) Russian Progress vehicles (unmanned) European ATV-transport vehicles (unmanned) HTV-transport vehicles from Japan (unmanned) Commercial Dragon-capsule from SpaceX.

entityDescription:
From 2010, ASYGN started to deliver actual designs to its first customers focusing on low power analog, Radio Frequency and Sensor circuits. As the design teams grew, including digital design, test engineers, firm ware and software designers, project leaders…), so did the addressed circuit complexity. Going one step further ASYGN decided, starting in 2015, to move fabless and provide its customers with dedicated chips (/chip families) that could directly fit their purpose namely focussing on four main fields :
– RF (SATCOM, wide band conversion, Front End, PLL…)
– Sensor interface (Capacitive / Resistive MEMS interface, circuits to interface inertial transducers, Strain, Humidity sensors, low power analog interfaces)
– RFID sensing : world’s first provider of UHF RFID sensor chips enabling battery-free sensing applications. Our IC’s are powered by any RAIN RFID reader, it works with standard EPC Global Gen2 protocoland requires no special commands. These chips can measure the temperature, strain gage, relative humidity/moisture, ambient light.
– Green AI (Database construction, Dedicated Network optimization, low power Inference chip design, that can easily be deployed combined with a small solar cells)
The company initial founders include Loic Joet, Nicolas Delorme, Daniel Saias and Joel Monnier. They wished to build the frame in which they enjoyed working. entityDescription:
Company information
Organizational structure and key information
SpaceIQ (SIQ) is a one-man start-up company addressing research and development in space physics with a focus on data analysis, methods, and instrumentation. SpaceIQ performs additionally tailored courses for industry and the public sector. The company was started in 2024.
 
Relevant experience
The owner of SpaceIQ has a strong cooperation and links with the section for Plasma and Space Physics in the Department of Physics at the University of Oslo (UiO) and the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) in the DTU Space section. He is a professor at UiO in space weather and plasma physics and have had a similar position at DTU Space.
Studies of the polar ionosphere are carried out using GNSS receivers, radars, sounding rockets, and satellites, providing high resolution in-situ measurements of plasma phenomena.
SpaceIQ has a stronger involvement in the ESA SSA Expert Centres for the ionosphere (I-ESC) and the Earth magnetic field and SWARM satellite (G-ESC) based on previous activities and experience by the owner of SpaceIQ. G-ESC is now led by DTU Space in the ESA Space Situational Awareness programme (SSA). SpaceIQ participates as a scientific advisor to DTU Space and G-ESC.
The development of I-ESC products is done at workstations at the premises of SpaceIQ. The SpaceIQ operational data products is transmitted to DLR in Germany. At a later state this task will be performed within SpaceIQ.
 
Involvement in related ESA activities
SpaceIQ is involved in ESA satellite projects contributing to the development of payload instruments (GNSS, iGNSS-R, Langmuir probes, and electric field instruments). The GNSS and iGNSS-R instruments and the associated data retrieval software are performed in cooperation Norwegian and Swedish companies.
The involvement in the ESA SWARM mission has been related to the development of polar cap products (polar cap patch detection and their characterization, plasma scintillations, as well as density gradients, the growth rates of plasma instabilities, space weather).

entityDescription:
Matteriall, headquartered in “Innovation & Incubation Center KU Leuven”, accredited and funded by the “European Space Agency Business Incubation Programme” is set up to come up with a material portfolio consisting of the most ever superior materials which are feasibly manufacturable and applicable for the applications primarily in the space and aerospace, healthcare and electronics industries. The objective of the Matteriall project is delivering the ultimate theoretical characteristics of the most advanced nano-scaled structures to every macro-scaled structure with minimum attenuation in order to enhance the life quality.
Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are remarkable objects that look set to revolutionise the technological landscape entirely in the near future. CNTs can have 50 times more mechanical strength than armour steel and 1000 times more current carrying capacity than copper. CNTs are the best heat conducting material ever known and they are chemically very stable like graphite. And above all, they are very light, their density is one sixth of that of steel. Tomorrow’s society will be shaped by CNT applications, just as silicon-based or plastic technologies dominate the society today.
However, today, delivering these theorotical nano-scaled material characteristics of CNTs to a macro-scaled level is the bottleneck of the current state of the nanotechnology. The objective of Matteriall is to develop a chemical spinning technique which will eventually enable to bring these extraordinary characteristics in real life applications. Matteriall’s unique manufacturing technology will deliver fibers, yarns and films that are made of essentially pure CNTs with superior properties. The outcome and first go-to-market product of the pilot production process will be the lightweight, strong, electrically and thermally conductive, flexible, corrosion resistant and biocompatible Carbon Nanotube Fibers/Yarns/Films.

entityDescription: The Royal Institute and Observatory of the Spanish Navy, located in San Fernando, Cádiz, is a reference institution in the fields of astronomy and geodesy. entityDescription:
Brunel University London, founded in 1966, is a university located in Uxbridge, London, United Kingdom. It was named after the Victorian engineer Isambard Kingdom Brunel and in2016, Brunel celebrated 50 years as a university.

Brunel is organised into three colleges – Engineering, Design and Physical Sciences; Business, arts and social sciences; and health and life sciences – and three major research institutes – energy futuresand environment; health and societies; and materials and manufacturing.

Brunel is a campus-based university, which means students are never more than 10 minutes away from halls of residence, social and sports facilities, lecture theatres, or the library.

It is also a member of the Association of Commonwealth Universities, the European University Association and Universities UK.

Brunel is just a tube ride away from the bustling city of London, making it a go to for students wishing to experience a variety of cultural and social activities.

Its students have access to specialist laboratories for electronic imaging, bioprocessing and experimental techniques, flight, driving and train simulators and a 3D body scanner.

Many undergraduate students may also choose to undertake practical placements and projects as a part of their courses in the form of a sandwich year.

A yearly design exhibition is held by Brunel's Department of Design called ‘Made In Brunel’ to promote and showcase the work of final year students to the rest of the design industry.

Notable alumni include Jo Brand, an English comedian, writer and actress, John McDonnell, a British Labour Party politician who was appointed Shadow Chancellor in September 2015, and Sophie McShera, an English actress.

entityDescription:
Waves Team was founded in 2023 to implement ideas in the field of remote sensing and contact measurements.
Our goal is to develop new and improve existing remote and contact methods for measuring wave parameters and wind speed in the World Ocean and inland waters, measuring the area of the ice cover and assessing its concentration.
Our mission is to develop and promote practical applications of satellite oceanographic information through collaboration with industry, academia and commercial research organizations.
In our activities, we rely on more than 20 years of scientific research experience, including the development of theoretical models and numerical simulations, the development of algorithms for processing satellite data and the retrieving of thematic information, the formation of databases, the development and manufacture of unique underwater acoustic wave gauges for sub-satellite measurements.

We understand that purely satellite solutions rarely provide complete information to users, so we use an integrated approach. This may be a combination of satellite data, numerical models and regional measurements.

entityDescription:
OKRA
Designing meaningful places
We are OKRA: an international and interdisciplinary team in the field of landscape architecture, working from Utrecht, the Netherlands. Together we design and realise resilient landscapes, healthy cities and sustainable water strategies. 
We envision the world of tomorrow as a place with positive impact on people and nature. To attain this, we combine three decades of international experience and thorough research with inventiveness and craftmanship to provide creative, leading and award-winning solutions for today’s and tomorrow’s challenges. 
Our goal is to design resilient landscapes that encourage social life and enhance ecology. We achieve this by adopting an open design approach, drawing inspiration and knowledge beyond given boundaries. Interdisciplinary collaboration and investment in research, both outside and inside the scope of our discipline, are central to our strategy. This allows us to address contemporary issues such as climate resilience, biodiversity, and social inclusiveness.

In our projects, we create valuable, habitable spaces for people and nature. We envisioncities as natural habitats, places where people and nature live together in healthy ways. We conceive innovative solutions and designs forliving with water, empowering sustainable and adaptive ecosystems. Our landscape design process focuses on rediscovering landscapes. In doing so, we uncover and reinterpret physical and historical layers as the basis for new interventions.By uniting nature and culture, we create landscapes that are full of meaning for both. 
OKRA’s multidisciplinary team consists of about 50 landscape architects, urban planners, architects, designers and other specialists. The partners, Martin Knuijt and Wim Voogt, work alongside a team of associates, Tom Wierts, Pierre-Alexandre Marchevet, Rani Izhar, Guiliana Sibilia, Nefeli Kalantzi, Melle van Dijk and Suzanne in ‘t Veld. 
Our specialists work together in dynamic project teams, combining their diverse talents to create high-quality designs. This collaborative approach, coupled with our extensive experience in navigating complex processes, enables us to overcome challenges and inspire collaborative partners to excel in every aspect of a design.
We always aim to provide high-quality design solutions to any challenge we are given, carefully considering local context and culture across our international portfolio. We are proud to see our projects being recognised by renowned organisations throughout the years. Our work has been awarded both nationally and internationally with, among others, the European Prize for Urban Public Space, Rietveld prize, and ARC awards.

entityDescription: FibreCoat GmbH is a technology-oriented spin-off from the Institut für Textiltechnik (ITA) of RWTH Aachen University, that started its business in February 2020. The researchers involved in FibreCoat were able to use the state-of-the-art machinery at the ITA in order to develop their novel process and patented material. The technological core is a single filament online coating system for glass and basalt fibres during their production with a polymer or aluminum sheath at a production speed of up to 1,000 m/min. The aim of FibreCoat is to supply a novel and innovative lightweight construction preform for composite production. That product will aid in solving the challenges of our modern mobility. The resulting material outperforms any available solutions for thermoplastic composites on the market and can reduce cycle time, costs and weight by up to 50 %. Thus, opening improved lightweight construction for a broad range of applications.

description:
Siranga is set to develop an entirely new kind of image sensing method and devices, photodetectors, and image sensors, collectively called quantum-tunneling imaging photodetectors (QTIP) for a broad range of applications from violet to visible light down to near infrared (NIR) as well as hyperspectral optical detection systems for scientific and industrial applications such as LIDAR. 

The range of applications is extremely wide and spans everything from consumer camera modules through-to imaging systems in satellite Earth observation. The advantage of QTIP is the ultrafast imaging enabling real time monitoring, high sensitivity of the QTIP to low-light applications and the large spectral wavelength range with high sensitivity.

The combination of QTIP with a hyperspectral filter will enable fast real-time monitoring of the food crops, vegetation, deforestation, human migrations, drought, or greenhouse gas emissions. This entirely new technology will contribute to precision farming and digitally automated agriculture, spot detection of global problem areas and other critical applications contributing to alleviating societal and environmental problems.

We envisage next-generation wafer size ~Peta-pixel QTIP sensors for Satellite Earth observation.

Our advances fall into the category of “deep-tech”. Starting from an idea and a vision well founded in the laws of quantum physics. Our resonant quantum tunnelling based cross-grid photodetectors, capable of Tera-pixel imaging is an outstanding example of exploiting the profound and fundamental laws of nature to create instruments for the most practical use cases.

entityDescription:
SpacePharma-EU is located in France in Strasbourg and Sophia-Antipolis. The SpacePharma team is both diverse and experienced, includes experts from both strong Life-Science, Chemistry, Space technology, and international Business Development backgrounds.
OUR VISION: Being a world leader in microgravity research and production solutions by making it accessible, affordable, and reliable serving the biopharma, material sciences, nutrition, agri-tech and chemical industries.
BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY: The Life-related Sciences and Industry market (pharmaceutical, cosmetics, biotechnology, materials, food, etc.) needs a low-cost, available, and easily accessible platform to perform complex experiments and manufacturing in microgravity environments. Today there are very limited, often expensive solutions.
SPACEPHARMA’s SOLUTION: innovative miniaturized remotely controlled microfluidics chemistry/biology laboratory on Nanosatellites and space station payload to perform R&D, manufacturing, shorten time-to-market and cut costs for innovative life science applications. SpacePharma provides low cost one-stop-shop end-to-end turnkey upstream, downstream and analytics solution, including:
• In-Orbit Facility (research, development, production).
• Ground station for remotely laboratory control.
• Customer front-end allowing customers to monitor, develop and modify
the experiment procedures and receive experimental data from their 
location on Smartphones.
• Return to Earth if needed.
ACHIEVEMENTS IN SPACE MISSIONS: After a successful experiment demonstrated in parabolic flight in 2016, SpacePharma has launched two Nanosatellites (“DIDO” missions) with full success and advanced lab has already been deployed ten times onboard the ISS– that didn’t require any Astronauts’ operation after setting the lab in place. These deployment methods opened a new era that is meeting the above-mentioned needs while closing the gaps with high User-Friendly End-To-End solution.

- Democratic political culture
- Economy
- Culture and art
- Human rights
- International cooperation
- Education, science, and research
- Sustainable development
- Social activities
- Technical culture
- Nature and environmental protection
The Society achieves its goals through various activities such as nature and environmental protection, citizen education, promotion of social values, encouragement of arts and culture, and providing social assistance and support.
The Society's economic activities include:
- Publishing activities
- Organization of educational, recreational, and tourist activities
- Organization of camps, festivals, and sports events
- Creation of studies and analyses
- Providing consulting services and report preparation
- Production and sale of products
- Organization of courses, seminars, and conferences
The Society's work is public and is ensured through timely reporting to members, use of information and communication technologies, public events, and other appropriate means.

entityDescription:
Vision

Nucleus Aerospace envisions a future where human potential is limitless, driven by innovation and advanced aerospace technologies. Our vision is to be the driving force behind the next generation of aerospace solutions, creating a world where air and space travel is accessible, sustainable, and transformative. With new materials, production methods, innovative research, technological advancements, and a commitment to sustainability, we aspire to inspire future generations, redefine the aerospace landscape, and contribute to a future where the impossible becomes possible.

Achievements

Over the past year, we have made significant organizational changes, such as registration and other bureaucratic processes. Our team includes individuals knowledgeable about Croatia's and the EU's legal systems, ensuring compliance and improving institutional relationships. Despite bureaucratic challenges, we completed five projects, emphasizing the dual nature of research and promotion for optimal scientific and social outcomes.
1. Curie I: Our first experimental rocket reached a height of 750m and a maximum speed of 0.7 Mach (Research project).
2. Curie I v2: An improved version with a reliable recovery system (Research project).
3. Curie I-EX: A more advanced rocket reaching 1.3km and a maximum speed of 0.98 Mach (Research project).
4. Ventus I: Part of the "Svemir za mlade" (Universe for the Young) project, this high-altitude weather balloon reached 40km, equipped with cameras and DIY measuring devices. These cameras captured the first student pictures of Croatia from such heights (Research/Science promotion project).
5. Svemir za mlade: Conducted at the Gymnasium of Velika Gorica, this project included lectures on astronomy, rocket fuel, and electronics, followed by student-built measuring devices used in the Ventus I project (Science promotion project).
Our rockets are 3D printed from special composite materials, ensuring stability, durability, and low mass, reducing fuel consumption and environmental impact.

Mission

1. Innovative Research and Development: We relentlessly pursue innovation, particularly in 3D-printed rockets and parts, advancing aerospace technologies through rigorous research and development, fostering creativity, and solving challenging aerospace and defense problems.
2. Sustainable Space Exploration: We aim to make space exploration sustainable and accessible by designing technologies that minimize environmental impact, promote renewable resources, and ensure long-term viability.
3. Defence and Security: We are dedicated to strengthening defense capabilities with state-of-the-art aerospace solutions to ensure national safety and global stability.
4. Educational Outreach and Inspiration: We inspire future aerospace pioneers through educational programs, mentorship, and support for academic research in STEM fields.
5. Ethical and Responsible Innovation: We uphold integrity, transparency, and social responsibility, promoting ethical practices across the aerospace industry. 
6. Global Collaboration: We foster partnerships with space agencies, research institutions, and private enterprises to accelerate technological progress and achieve shared goals for humanity.

Conclusion

We are a team of college and high school students driven by an inexhaustible will to learn, work, and achieve our missions. Despite being less than a year old, we have executed five projects, demonstrating that age is not a barrier to realizing dreams. However, financial, institutional, educational, and professional support remain challenges that we are determined to overcome.

As iBioscience, we are eager to contribute to and collaborate with ESA to advance space exploration and biotechnology. Our expertise in biotechnology and life sciences positions us uniquely to support ESA’s goals in integrating space into European society and fostering a globally competitive space sector. We offer cutting-edge research and innovation in space health, sustainability, and life support systems, essential for long-duration space missions. By partnering with ESA, we aim to develop groundbreaking biotechnological solutions that enhance astronaut health, improve life support systems, and ensure sustainable space exploration.

iBioScience Ltd (https://ibio.hu/) is a genetics-related innovative service provider company specializing in large-scale diagnostic and research-related NGS (Next-Generation Sequencing) and microarray services utilizing our proprietary panels. As a leading company in WGS sequencing in Hungary, we offer personalized diagnostics prepared within a three-week timeframe. We also provide comprehensive BioIT training services, along with tests, databases, and consulting, catering to both academia and industry.
Together, we can drive scientific discoveries, stimulate economic growth, and inspire future generations, positioning Europe as a leader in space biotechnology. Join us in pushing the frontiers of knowledge and creating effective solutions for societal challenges through the strategic use of space technologies.

entityDescription:
The Institute of Agricultural Economics Nonprofit Kft. (AKI) is a private scientific institute supervised by the Ministry of Agriculture. Building on the rich heritage of its predecessor, the Research Institute of Agricultural Economics, established in 1954, AKI continues as a research and knowledge centre with the most extensive agricultural economics databases and the most significant policy expertise in Hungary, performing both public duties and state functions. One of the principal tasks of the Institute is to develop recommendations for agricultural and rural policy decision-makers. These recommendations are based on the results of research applying state-of-the-art methods and focusing especially on the implementation and the execution of the European Union’s Common Agricultural Policy.
As a leader in the digitalisation process of Hungarian agriculture, AKI operates and is engaged in the further development of EU and national agricultural information systems of outstanding importance, i.e., the Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN), the Market Price Information System (MPIS), and the Agricultural Statistical Information System (ASIS). By the extensive collection and processing of data, policy analysis and decision support, AKI provides valuable assistance for progressing agriculture and strengthening rural livelihoods.
The careful maintenance of the right balance between expertise services, domestic and international scientific research, and policy decision support is of key importance for AKI. The cooperation with professional organizations and the active professional involvement are well-integrated into the daily operations of the Institute. To retain a close relationship with the agricultural community, AKI regularly publishes new information and the results of its research projects in a comprehensible and appropriate form.
AKI has been developing its services according to the principles of promptness, targeting, transparency, and design. The Institute is keeping pace with the development of research methods, and with the changes in legislation affecting the provision of its services. AKI has been and will remain a bridge between research, policy making, and market participants.

With our extensive long-time experience in production, development, maintenance and support of inertial systems for positioning, navigation, surveying, guidance, stabilization, control and communication (PNT / PNTC) we provide leading systems and solutions destined to a wide range of applications, for unmanned and manned platforms, in industrial, automotive, aerospace, geodetic and defence environment, from stock or as customized solution.

entityDescription:
Marotta S.r.l. has been operating in the precision mechanics sector since 1957 and over the years it has specialized by increasing its know-how and continuously comparing itself with the advances in technology.
A continuous challenge to overcome one’s limits and guarantee its customers a high quality service in precision mechanical machining in Naples. Specialized in the design and production of scientific instruments for aerospace research and astronomy.
The experience, passion and dedication of the company towards this sector are amply rewarded by the important collaborations established during the long activity of Marotta S.r.l.: Leonardo-Finmeccanica, Mecaer, Adler Group, Gavazzi Space, ESA (Agenzia Spaziale Europea), ASI (Agenzia Spaziale Italiana), ESO (European Southern Observatory), CIRA (Centro Italiano Ricerche Aerospaziali) and many others.
Marotta Ltd. Is a small Italian firm, but one “that can face the great ones”, as described by Lino Grosso, mechanical engineer and CEO of the Company, in an interview appare on the Italian newspaper “La Repubblica” in 2010.
Even today, nearly sixty years after its founding, the company is still a milestone point in Italy for precision machining, interested not only in succeeding in this field, but also in keeping Made in Italy alive.
Over the years, significant projects in the field of aerospace research and telescopes have been mostly carried out by young and very driven employees.
Two generations of engineers and skilled workers grew professionally in the structure of Cercola (near Naples) and almost all of them have started their own careers right after their work in Marotta Ltd.

Marotta Ltd. designs in-house all the equipment necessary for the production of NC machines and for dimensional testing, and offers the same service to its customers, using the most modern design systems such as CATIA V5 and Mechanical Desktop.
Beyond this, it also has experience in designing and building assembly ports, assembly lines, (Jig, Rig, etc) and equipment movements (MGSE, Crane system, Recovery System, Transport Container etc.).

Over the last few years, Marotta Ltd. has set up an internal department of design, research and development; this way, we can now provide a complete service to our customers. Currently, the level of know-how has been gained in different areas such as:
- Aerospace (scale model for wind tunnel);
- Earth Observation (optical instruments and telescopes);
- Structures for space applications (payload and boxes).

Marotta Ltd. uses modern numerical control (both horizontal and vertical ones) machines, up to 4 controlled axes and palletized, in order to work keeping up with high precision and speed of up to 6 meters in length.
The quality is guaranteed not only at the system level, but also on the sophisticated device. In the air-conditioned room there is a 3D measuring machine (2500 x 1300 x 1000) DEA Scirocco with SIT certification.

entityDescription:
Public Institution SEA AND KARST carries out the activities of protection, maintenance, and promotion of protected areas in the Split-Dalmatia County with the aim of protecting and preserving the authenticity of nature, ensuring the uninterrupted conduct of natural processes, and sustainable use of natural resources, as well as overseeing the implementation of conditions and measures for nature protection in the protected areas managed by the Institution.
The Institution also manages the ecological network area in accordance with the Nature Protection Act and related regulations.
In accordance with the Nature Protection Act, the Institution carries out direct supervision in protected areas, specifically:
- Over individual plant and animal species, and supervises protected natural values through the chief supervisor, supervisors, and nature guards.
- Supervision of the implementation of conditions and protection measures in the area it manages.

entityDescription:
The purpose of the Foundation is to contribute to the strengthening, enhancement, growth and competitive improvement of the information and communication technologies (ICT) sector in Galicia, through the promotion of excellence in research and the transfer of technologies, as well as the production, promotion, advice and dissemination of knowledge, in the field of ICT, and the training of expert personnel in said field. As a priority but not exclusively, this object will be concreted in the promotion of CITIC and the Faculty of Computer Science of the University of A Coruña.
a) Carrying out research and consultancy projects financed with own funds or from competitive calls.
b) Carrying out research, innovation or consultancy projects financed by contracts of companies or entities or administrations. public
c) Management of research projects and technical consultancy financed by competitive calls or by companies and administrations developed by CITIC.
d) Coordination of groups or other agents in research or innovation projects in public, national or international calls, promoting the relationship between university groups and public or private agents.
e) Dissemination of research results and transfer through courses, conferences or meetings.
f) Promotion of collaborations with other public or private R+D+i centers, specialized in the ICT sector
g) Establishment of collaborations and other cooperation mechanisms with public administrations and the private sector, to improve their technological capacity.
h) Favor the transition from research to technology transfer of the research groups attached to CITIC.
i) Organize and participate in national or international events in the scope of the foundation's object and purposes.
j) Promote the relationship between the CITIC, the Faculty of Informatics of the UDC and the productive sector, and other research centers, to create an R+D+i pole in the field of ICT in Galicia.
k) Promote the creation of all the necessary infrastructure for the development of the CITIC of the UDC.
l) Any other similar or analogous activities to those listed in the previous lines, which the Board of Trustees considers to be of interest for the achievement of the foundational object.

entityDescription:
HEROTECH8 is a robotics company based at Cranfield University in the UK, specializing in on-demand aerial imaging services through the deployment of automated drone stations. These stations, also known as "drone-in-a-box" systems, store, charge, and provide secure and weather-resistant enclosures for drones. The company leverages its network-bridging technology to allow remote pilots to conduct drone operations with low latency.
Founded in 2018, HEROTECH8 initially focused on manufacturing and selling these automated drone stations to industries such as energy, security, construction, and critical infrastructure. Since mid-2022, the company started offering low-cost, automated drone services through its "Open Air" platform, which allows customers to request and schedule drone flights for various applications, including building inspections, construction surveys, security patrols, and environmental monitoring.

entityDescription:
The Euro-Atlantic Resilience Centre (E-ARC) is a centre of excellence in the field of resilience, a partner of NATO and the EU, acting for the benefit of these organisations, as well as Member States or partners.
The establishment of the Centre was recognized and welcomed in the joint statement of the heads of state and government gathered on the occasion of the Brussels Summit in June 14th, 2021: „We will continue to take a whole-of-government approach to enhancing the resilience of our societies. […]We welcome the establishment of the Euro-Atlantic Centre for Resilience in Romania.”
The Centre carries out its activity in synergy with the objectives of the EU and NATO in the field of resilience, without being directly subordinated to either of these organisations. In this way, E-ARC can also offer expertise to states in the Black Sea area which are not EU or NATO members (Moldova, Ukraine, Georgia, etc.).

According to Government Decision 565 of May 19, 2021, the mission of E-ARC is to develop concepts, doctrines and methodologies in the field of resilience, to provide training courses and to offer a platform for the transfer of expertise between the government institutions, the private sector, civil society and academia. E-ARC is not a national resilience authority and does not have operational responsibilities.
Supporting NATO's efforts to create the new concept of layered resilience, E-ARC is coordinating, in partnership with the Romanian Ministry of Defence, the development of NATO doctrine on Response Planning, one of the seven thematic areas that form the Alliance's Layered Resilience strategy.
At NATO's Riga seminar in April 2023, the Centre was formally invited by Allied Command Transformation (NATO ACT) to present the Euro-Atlantic vision of societal resilience. Similarly, E-ARC is already working, in coordination with NATO, on missions to assess and support resilience in states in the Black Sea region.
Since November 2023, E-ARC has been organizing, in Bucharest, in collaboration with NATO Defence Policy & Planning Division, the Course dedicated to resilience experts, to strengthen the Organization's capacity to respond in a coordinated manner to crises that threaten the resilience of member states.
The Centre’s experts have offered training sessions, courses, and high level briefings on strengthening resilience for Romanian and foreign diplomats, as well as for government officials from EU member states and partners, for example a session in partnership with EUAM Ukraine. So far, the courses have covered topics such as institutional resilience, societal resilience, resilience of transport infrastructure and resilience of communication systems.

entityName: RTU - Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Technologies and Transport Institute
entityDescription:
Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Technologies and Transport Institute(MATTI) is an innovative and development-oriented educational and research institution actively operating in the field of engineering and technology. The institute prides itself on a wide range of research areas, including:
- mechanical engineering technologies
- biomedical engineering
- applied mechanics
- thermal engineering
- manufacturing automation
- nanoengineering
- powder materials technologies
- mechatronics
- tribology
- metrology
- welding technologies
- space technologies
- air transport
- land transport
- mobility technologies
- smart textiles.
MATTI scientists are actively involved in both national and international projects, making a significant contribution to the advancement of science and technology. Research results are regularly published in internationally recognized scientific journals. The institute has created several patented inventions and developed knowledge that fosters innovation.
MATTI is a place where science and technology meet practical application, creating solutions that change the world.
Scientific Competencies
MATTI's scientific activities cover several significant areas. The main research competencies include mechanical engineering, with a special focus on metrology and tribology, biomedical engineering with an emphasis on nanoengineering and smart sensors, as well as theoretical mechanics, exploring nonlinear vibrations. In addition, the institute specializes in industrial engineering, focusing on CNC machining, as well as heat and cold transfer technologies and industrial design.Scientific activities also coverdevelopment of space mission designs, research on aircraft and drone design, studies on material and component fatigue, development of autonomous control solutions, road traffic safety analysis, and research on sustainably sourced fuels.
Scientific Laboratories
MATTI includes several specialized scientific laboratories that ensure high-quality research and development work. Among them are the Biomedical and Nanoengineering Laboratory, focusing on biochip technologies and smart textiles, the Powder Materials Laboratory, the Welding and Thermal Processes Laboratory, as well as the Metrology Laboratory, which provides precise measurements and calibrations. In addition, research is conducted in the fields of mechanics, biotextile materials, machine and mechanism dynamics, and tribology in the institute's laboratories.
Research Directions
MATTI's research directions cover a wide spectrum, ranging from 3D biotextiles with nanocomposite-enhanced protective properties to experimental research and modeling of composite materials. The institute also conducts research on multifunctional nanostructured smart coatings and the micro and macro mechanical and tribological properties of surfaces. Other significant research areas include improving the efficiency of heat supply operations and replacing fossil fuels with alternative energy sources, as well as industrial design.
MATTI is a place where science and technology meet practical application, creating solutions that change the world. The institute invites both students and industry representatives to collaborate in shaping the future together.

entityDescription:
Research at the Institute of Quantum Optics focuses on highly controlled interaction of light and matter. Typical topics are the physics of ultracold quantum gases, quantum logic spectroscopy based on cooling and trapping of ions dealing with fundamental principles of physics, the physics of ultrashort laser pulses and the control of plasmas in the sub-femto region and applications of nonlinear optics in medical therapy and diagnostics. The institute also provides central parts of the education within the Bachelor and Master courses in physics and related topics.

The Institute of Quantum Optics (IQO) at Leibniz University Hannover specialises in fundamental and applied research on laser physics and light-matter interactions. It explores extremes from Bose-Einstein condensates to femtosecond/attosecond plasmas, spanning ultracold atoms, molecules, and biological systems, with extensions into quantum information and relativistic satellite experiments.​
Research Focus
Key questions drive the work: improving lasers, their applications, and insights from light-matter interactions. Efforts target precise atomic clocks/sensors, atom-molecule control, laser surgery innovations, cell manipulation, quantum computers, and X-ray lasers.​
- Internal groups: Guided Matter Wave Interferometry (Dr Schlippert), Molecular Quantum Gases (Prof Dr S Ospelkaus), Quantum Atom Optics (Prof Dr Ertmer, apl Prof Dr Klempt), Theory of Quantum Sensing (Dr Naceur Gaaloul), Quantum Sensing (Prof Dr Ertmer, Prof Dr Rasel), Trapped-Ion Quantum Engineering (Prof Dr C Ospelkaus), Ultrafast Laser Laboratory (Prof Dr Morgner et al).​

- External sites: Biophotonics (Prof Dr Heisterkamp), Nanoengineering (Prof Dr Chichkov), Laser Components and Fibres (Prof Dr Ristau), Quantum Logic Spectroscopy (Prof Dr Schmidt), Quantum Clocks and Complex Systems (Prof Dr Tanja Mehlstäubler).​

Collaborations
The institute partners locally with Laser Zentrum Hannover (LZH), PTB Braunschweig, NIFE, and DLR-SI, plus national/international institutions. Major initiatives include QUEST Leibniz Research School, Clusters of Excellence (PhoenixD, QuantumFrontiers, Hearing4all), QVLS Quantum Valley Lower Saxony, and funding from DFG, EU, ESA

entityDescription:
hansa-express logistics GmbH is a logistics service provider in the explosives and military sector that performs all transport-related services centrally in one company. With its headquarters in Germany, hansa-express logistics GmbH is located in the heart of Europe and has been operating worldwide from this base for over 30 years. The global multimodal logistics solutions combine the advantages of sea, air, rail, road and storage facilities.

Own trucks for European transports up to 16 tons NEQ equipped for the highest requirements in explosives transport as well as certified drivers, enable responsive solutions. A global network of long-term reliable providers is deployed for sea, air and rail transportation services worldwide.

For the storage of war weapons, radioactive material and explosives up to 3,100 tons ADR 1.1 NEQ, hansa-express logistics GmbH operates customs bonded warehouses in Germany. The depots also handle 20' and 40' IMO containers - including stuffing and stripping, labeling and marking in common with documentation of the packing and stripping process - depending on customer requirements and IMO regulations.

Being AEO (Authorized Economic Operator) certified simplifies customs formalities to be completed. A highly specialized department staff consists of experts for transit licenses and all special weapons and explosives regulations within European countries. Furthermore, hansa-express logistics GmbH was granted the BKA exemption permit for the transportation of forbidden weapons. The additional set-up security department ensures protection for sensitive shipments. The security personnel of hansa-express logistics GmbH is qualified to escort the freight both unarmed and armed.

MBS is a reliable service integrator and service provider for critical communication networks. We operate data and voice communication via satellite and data networks - worldwide and in space. Our expertise ranges from classic satellite services to customized applications in the New Space application field. 

Since 1978, we have also been a provider of managed gateways (earth stations) and operate infrastructure for our customers worldwide. Essential for the provision of our services is a team of more than 90 specialists from the fields of: Communications Engineering, Electrical Engineering, High Frequency Engineering and IT. MBS technicians and engineers cover the entire service delivery process: Design, planning, implementation and operation. Our company serves various verticals, including Government, Defense & Intelligence, Media, Managed Gateways, New Space, and Application & EO Data Provider.

Our solutions include the worldwide connection of units on land, at sea or in the air. Our customers (e.g. public authorities) also rely on satellite communication solutions that enable a connection on vehicles such as ships and cars, even while they are in motion. Such systems can be easily swapped between platforms, for example. However, MBS also has solutions in its portfolio for stationary or permanently installed requirements for longer periods of use.For our solutions in the area of critical & resilient networks, we use satellite connections (in various orbits) and from various providers, as well as mobile and radio relay technologies and terrestrial networks.

entityDescription: Creotech Instruments S.A (Creotech) was established in 2008 as a spin-out of a scientific project „Pi of the Sky” carried on by scientific institutions. The scope of activities of Creotech includes: • development and production of specialised measurement electronic signal processing systems • development and production of advanced imaging systems based on high-end, high resolution digital cameras • development and production of electronics for space industry • electronics assembly according to IPC, MIL, ECSS standards Areas of applications include: • space satellite and ground segment • scientific applications, e.g. astronomical observations, large scientific facilities, e.g. high-energy, thermonuclear laboratories • industry applications, e.g. CCD cameras for monitoring, embedded computers, telecommunication devices and specialised measurement systems, intelligent power suppliers. Creotech objective, supported by its strategic investor, is to become the leader of the Polish space industry. Thus Creotech federates and facilitates other Polish companies’ activities in the space applications’ domain. Projects realised by Creotech can get financial warranty of Industrial Development Agency. entityDescription:
Climate Resource S GmbH is a small specialist climate science software and advisory firm. It was founded in 2024 as a wholly owned subsidiary of Climate Resource Pty Ltd, to be the European arm of Climate Resource Pty Ltd. Climate Resource Pty Ltd was incorporated in 2020 in Australia. Climate Resource Pty Ltd and Climate Resource S GmbH together form the Climate Resource Group, although there is no legal entity which represents the Climate Resource Group and the two companies operate on arms’ length principles. The Climate Resource group now has staff based in Melbourne, Australia; Vienna, Austria; Berlin, Germany and Hanover, Germany. All of the European staff are employees of Climate Resource S GmbH.

The Climate Resource Group’s network of clients and collaborations has expanded rapidly to include multilateral organisations, governments, financial institutions, consulting firms, and science research organisations including the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project International Project Office (CMIP IPO) and Australia’s national science agency (CSIRO). The Climate Resource team has decades of experience in climate science and policy, particularly climate projections using reduced complexity climate models for the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) and quantification of the emissions consistent with country pledges in nationally determined contributions (NDCs) and long-term low-emissions development strategies (LT-LEDS) submitted to the UNFCCC. Multiple members of the team contributed to the IPCC’s Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) and the Scientific Director, Malte Meinshausen, has been contributing to IPCC reports since the Fourth Assessment Report (AR4). Members of the team have also been contributing greenhouse gas concentration input model forcing data to CMIP since CMIP5. In addition to their scientific credentials, the Climate Resource Group also specialises in research software engineering. The team has experience in delivering high-quality research software tools, with a particular focus on reproducibility, transparency and robustness, a key requirement for operationalisation of existing scientific workflows.

As a note: in the absence of financial statements for Climate Resource S GmbH (Climate Resource S GmbH was only established in 2024 so there are obviously no financial statements for 2023 or earlier) we have included the audited financial statements of Climate Resource Pty Ltd in Section 9.

entityDescription:
As a leading telco provider, Deutsche Telekom has shaped the networking of our society for over 20 years – and knows that universal connectivity requires equally comprehensive security measures. The most effective weapon against cyberattacks is not even technology itself – but the people who work for Telekom. Their expertise about vital security architecture, its configuration and customization for customer infrastructure is what counts most. Boosting and sharing this know-how is a top priority for Telekom. In this way, it can offer future-oriented security in a connected world.
Therefore, Telekom Security was founded as a business unit within T-Systems in early 2017 – and transformed into a separate legal entity within DTAG group on July 1, 2020 (Deutsche Telekom Security GmbH or Telekom Security for short). With over 250 million euros of revenue, Telekom Security is the market leader in Germany and one of Europe’s top cybersecurity providers. 
Telekom Security addresses its customers holistically in accordance with a governance, risk & compliance approach. Its comprehensive solutions for networks, cloud services and end-customer applications give data privacy and compliance the attention they need.
Telekom Security cooperates closely with leading producers of security technology as well as innovative start-ups. Based on concrete customer demands, Telekom Security also influences further development of its partners’ products – along the entire life cycle from threat identification and protection, detection & response to recovery.
We feature differentiated solutions in combination with our Managed Services – offering customers the same highly professional services and technologies that we ourselves use to protect Deutsche Telekom worldwide. We know just how crucial security is: For example, on a single day in April 2020, we registered 48 million attacks on Deutsche Telekom’s IT infrastructure. In the same month, 5.3 trillion botnet packages were detected in the backbone of our landline and mobile networks. 
The information we collect about the respective attack vectors is stored in a database – the Telekom Threat Library, which contains many millions of entries about malware, APT attacks and zero-day exploits, and is continuously expanded to include new attack patterns. Our self-learning platform converts these patterns into indicators. All our customers automatically profit from the protection that results from this activity. 
In the course of security tests, the latest attack methods are applied and further developed. The goal is to achieve a high measure of robustness in the tested systems. This ensures the demanding level of quality we need in order to protect our own critical IT infrastructure.
These experiences and the respective, accumulated knowledge also influence Telekom’s own innovative and future-oriented software development – incorporating machine learning, artificial intelligence, protection for mobile devices, vulnerability scanning, identity management and an intelligent attack, detection and monitoring system. 
The centerpiece of our monitoring efforts is our integrated Cyber Defense & Security Operation Center (SOC) in Bonn, launched in 2017. With more than 240 employees worldwide and 24/7 availability, it is currently the biggest of its kind in Europe. All SOCs in Germany along with those in Hungary, Austria, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Poland, Spain, Greece, South Africa, the USA, Mexico, Brazil and (new in 2019) Singapore form an international SOC network.

In the course of security tests, the latest attack methods are applied and further developed. The goal is to achieve a high measure of robustness in the tested systems. This ensures the demanding level of quality we need in order to protect our own critical IT infrastructure.
These experiences and the respective, accumulated knowledge also influence Telekom’s own innovative and future-oriented software development – incorporating machine learning, artificial intelligence, protection for mobile devices, vulnerability scanning, identity management and an intelligent attack, detection and monitoring system. 
The centerpiece of our monitoring efforts is our integrated Cyber Defense & Security Operation Center (SOC) in Bonn, launched in 2017. With more than 240 employees worldwide and 24/7 availability, it is currently the biggest of its kind in Europe. All SOCs in Germany along with those in Hungary, Austria, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Poland, Spain, Greece, South Africa, the USA, Mexico, Brazil and (new in 2019) Singapore form an international SOC network.

entityDescription:
VOCSens is a spin-off from the Sensors, Microsystems and Actuators Laboratory of Louvain (SMALL) research group, within the Electrical Engineering Department (ELEN), Institute of Information and Communication Technologies, Electronics and Applied Mathematics (ICTEAM), Université catholique de Louvain (UCLouvain), Louvain-la-Neuve, Belgium. UCLouvain is one of the most prestigious universities in Europe and home to worldly recognized laboratories. It relies on a strong expertise based on more than 10 years research on CMOS-compatible environmental sensors development and characterization, including gas, temperature, humidity and pressure sensors, as well as the CMOS design of read-out interfaces.

The spin-off aims to the development and commercialization of ultra-low-power low-cost multi-pixel CMOS gas microsensors dedicated to selective gases and volatile compounds detection in the Internet of Things and the Industry 4.0. The first product, EnviCam®, reflecting the concept of "environmental camera", efficiently combines gas, particulates, temperature and humidity sensors in a unique low-cost smart sensing platform featuring wireless communication through LPWAN networks. The main applications are found in environmental monitoring and industrial control (EHS, HVAC systems, alarm, etc.).

VOCSens products are pioneering in terms of autonomy, accuracy, versatility and portability, while ensuring continuous measurements in an active way, helping companies and institutions to unveil their environmental parameters, strengthen safety and health.

How We Do It
At Qaleon we guarantee data integrity and confidentiality, promoting sustainable transformation practices.

ETL process and data enrichment
At Qaleon, we collect data from all possible sources. We cleanse and structure it, laying the foundation for efficient analysis and consistent results. Data enrichment amplifies its impact by adding layers of additional information in a responsible manner, enabling sustainable transformation.

The strategic value of data enrichment
We are committed to improving the quality and relevance of data, gaining deep insights to anticipate trends, mitigate risks and improve operational efficiency.

Automation in the ETL Process

Machine Learning for continuous improvement
We integrate Machine Learning techniques into the ETL process allowing dynamic adaptation to changes in data and emerging patterns. Through machine learning algorithms, we improve trend identification, forecasting and anomaly detection, providing additional intelligence to the data.

Artificial Intelligence
Artificial Intelligence takes data enhancement to new heights. Our AI algorithms not only analyze large data sets, but learn from them to make autonomous decisions, allowing us to anticipate trends, personalize experiences and proactively optimize processes.

Company description: VOLTA pioneers a groundbreaking technology enabling ZERO-VOLUME ENERGY STORAGE: Volta Structural Batteries (VSB). Our state-of-the-art multifunctional batteries serve as structural frames for spacecraft, aircrafts and trucks and virtually any transport vehicles, seamlessly integrating energy storage capabilities with their revolutionary architecture and constituent materials. VSB maximizes storable energy, power and, consequently, range within a given system without compromising the mass or volume required for passengers or cargo transport.
This groundbreaking advancement allows spacecraft ranging from 3U CubeSats to large 500+ Kg platforms to allocate 80% to 100% of the original battery pack volume to additional payload, resulting in a 40% reduction in the original battery pack mass and a 2X to 5X increase in available power.

Volta's architecture incorporates state of the art sodium-ion chemistry, the combination of this chemistry with the innovative design results in a highly advanced product with market competitive features such as:
· Higher overall system energy density;
· Fast charging: full charge in less than 15 minutes;
· High power density: maximum power output for demanding applications;
· High cycling and very long battery life, comparable with that of the systems in which it is integrated;
· High mechanical strength and stiffness: properties typical of advanced sandwich composites;
· High safety: robust safety features, even in cases of severe damage.
· High customization: panels of different shapes, sizes and thicknesses can be made according to mechanical and electrochemical requirements, and different materials can also be used for the outer layers, such as high-performance composite materials for aerospace applications or metal and plastic materials for more low-cost applications. 
Volta's solution is also engineered to be produced on a large scale at low cost due to the possibility of using existing production techniques and abundant materials, and with a manageable supply chain even at the national/European level.

entityDescription:
SpaceForest's Rocket Technologies business unit specializes in the development and deployment of advanced rocket systems, focusing on the PERUN suborbital rocket, hybrid propulsion, advanced electronics, and composite materials.

PERUN Rocket
The PERUN rocket is a single-stage, guided suborbital launch vehicle designed for carrying payloads up to 50 kg to altitudes of 150 km. It is powered by a hybrid rocket engine, which uses liquid nitrous oxide as the oxidizer and various polymers as fuel, ensuring eco-friendly operations. PERUN features advanced thrust vector control (TVC) systems for improved stability and precise flight trajectory​.
Advanced 

Rocket Electronics
SpaceForest develops sophisticated electronics for rocket applications, including tracking, telemetry, and telecommand systems. The RASEL system provides reliable real-time communication and data transmission during rocket flights. This system employs directional antennas and onboard transceivers to maintain high-bandwidth, bidirectional communication under extreme conditions.

Composite Technologies
SpaceForest is also proficient in producing high-strength, lightweight composite materials for rocket construction. These materials are essential for various rocket components, such as tubes and nozzles, offering excellent durability and performance. The company uses advanced manufacturing techniques, including tow-winding, vacuum bagging, and infusion, to create these composites, which are also designed to withstand the harsh conditions of rocket launches and re-entry​

It has established a strong partnership with the Department of Information Engineering and Mathematical Sciences at the University of Siena, in order to promote innovative strategies for that purpose. The main Moebeus’s activities are to work with associations, companies, young entrepreneurs and youth workers in order to increase their awareness about sustainability, circular economy strategies and skillls and ESG impact, trough technology. The co-founders of Moebeus are no. 4 people with specific innovation skills in different fields: the multisectoral nature of the staff's expertise represents the main added value of startup activities. Moebeus Digital skills are Moebeus Digital skills are related with cloud software application development embracing agile methodology (Scrum, SAFe) as well as smart analytics, blockchain, decision support systems, artificial intelligence and virtual/augmented reality. 
Moebeus is the owner of a patented Data Analysis tool, named BeCircular, based on smart analytics and mathematical models, which automatically aggregates data for identifying corporate positioning on ESG, SDG and circularity issues of business process, products, and services, human behaviors.
