entityDescription: The Department of Industrial Engineering, formerly the Department of Mechanical Engineering, has been a core part of the University of Rome Tor Vergata since 1982. The mission of the Department is to promote and valorize education, culture, research and innovation on several subjects that fall within industrial fields. This makes the Department not only incubator for leading research, but also allows for close collaboration with industries. The Industrial Engineering Department coordinates three Bachelor’s programs in Mechanical Engineering, Energy Engineering and Engineering Sciences and two Master’s programs in Mechanical Engineering and Energy Engineering. The Department organizes also a PhD program in Industrial Engineering and four International Master courses. With these programs the department provides education to approximately 500 students. The research of the Department of Industrial Engineering is focused on several knowledge pillars as materials and mechanics, energy and flow, physics, systems dynamics and control, power technologies, space and security. Several research teams collaborate in a interdisciplinary manner by means of a theoretical-numerical approach and simulation, and experimental activities in many of the Department’s laboratories.

entityDescription: Ogólnopolskie Towarzystwo Ochrony Ptaków (Eng. Polish Society for the Protection of Birds, BirdLife Poland, hereinafter OTOP) is NGO established in 1991, reg. number KRS:0000015808. OTOP's statutory goals are: to protect wild birds and their habitats, to spread knowledge about birds, their importance and threats thereto, to collect data on national bird populations, to develop and implement conservation measures, to carry out legal actions for the protection of birds and their habitats. OTOP is an association of 1338 members (as of February 2024) employing 44 staff and supported by ca.600 volunteers. OTOP operates on a nationwide scale running a main office in Warsaw and five regional offices, closely related to the nature reserves managed by OTOP. In Poland OTOP maintains a website otop.org.pl and a database Ornitho.pl - a European citizen science internet platform for collecting data on the abundance and distribution of birds. OTOP is the only Polish partner of BirdLife International - the largest global organisation protecting birds.

entityDescription:
The Brandenburg Wilderness Foundation took the opportunity to found wilderness on the sites of four selected former military training grounds. Founded by private and public partners in 2000, it now owns and takes care of over 14,400 hectares that are unique in Germany for their size, lack of roads and wilderness development. The wilderness areas are located on the former military training grounds of Jüterbog, Heidehof and Lieberose south of Berlin and Tangersdorf north of Berlin. All of the purchased areas are designated nature reserves, some of them being additionally assigned FFH or SPA status. With the aim of supporting, experiencing as well as exploring wilderness (“Wildnis stiften, erleben und erforschen”) the Foundation has taken a holistic approach from the beginning, striving to promote wider knowledge of wilderness and to make its beauty and fascination accessible for the public.
We regularly record selected animal and plant species in wilderness areas. Our rangers study wolves and wildcats using photo traps and genetic samples, record nightjars and bats or observe warmth-loving newcomers such as the praying mantis. Forest development and the condition of various biotopes are also scrutinised. Scientific photo monitoring documents the natural succession. Every few years we commission a biotope type mapping, which is carried out using aerial photographs. This is also about recording succession. 

Making nature in its beauty and fascination accessible is the stated goal of Brandenburg Wilderness Foundation. The Foundation constructs hiking trails, picnic areas and vistas in selected areas. Visitors can discover the landscape on their own on the paths cleared of munitions. Furthermore guided hikes and bike tours offer exciting insights into areas that are normally not accessible.

description:
FOTEC Forschungs- und Technologietransfer GmbH is the research subsidiary of the University of Applied Sciences Wiener Neustadt, Austria. Founded in 1998, FOTEC initiates and manages research, development, technology, and innovation projects. With more than 40 employees, it supports the University in implementing its research and development strategy for both bachelor’s and master’s programs.

With 20 people, the department of Aerospace Engineering has long experience, not only in terms of development of space electric and chemical propulsion systems for space applications, but also in terms of diagnostic systems and test stands to characterize their performances such as thrust balances, Retarding Potential Analyzers (RPAs) and Digital Faraday Cups (DFCs). Through the development of integrated electric propulsion systems such as the IFM NANO Thruster, FOTEC has built up knowledge in the field of measurement, control, high voltage, power electronics and firmware development. The focus is laid not only on high efficiency and performance but also on high reliability and radiation safety.
Recently FOTEC has reached an important milestone in the development of chemical mono- and bi-propellant thrusters based on green propellants to replace the carcinogenic propellant Hydrazine which is still in common use. In particular, the developed and tested catalysts for the mono-propellant thruster show outstanding performance in terms of reliability, stability, and longevity. FOTEC has also been developing Active Spacecraft Potential Control devices (ASPOC) for decades. NASA integrated 32 ASPOC devices on their two MMS satellite in 2015 to enable highly accurate magnetic field measurements. The ASPOC devices have been in operation since then and are still fully operational. These devices are currently being miniaturized for future application on smaller satellites (e.g., CubeSats).
A large aerospace engineering laboratory is available at FOTEC, equipped with modern high vacuum chambers of various sizes, as well as facilities for environmental tests (TVAC, shock, vibration, ATOX - currently in development) and devices for material investigation (SEM/EDX, various microscopes). A dedicated cleanroom for assembly as well as a cleanroom tent allow handling of sensitive space hardware and loading of the test facilities.

The Engineering Technologies department is an interdisciplinary team of 9 people with competences in additive manufacturing, chemistry, and mechatronics systems. Since 2014 several ESA-funded projects have been carried out with European partners and primes such as Thales Alenia Space or Airbus Defense & Space. The main objectives of the R&D work of the Engineering Technologies department is the transformation of existing manufacturing routes of mechanical components or assemblies into additive manufacturing. Some examples are the antenna deployment and pointing mechanism (ADPM) bracket from the NEOsat platform, various RF antenna components in the C- and Ku-band range, and flexible metal bellows. Furthermore, this department is involved in the ISRU topic (In-Situ Resource Utilization) and is working with Martian regolith simulants in representative Martian environmental conditions (reduced pressure and CO2 atmosphere). The laboratory is equipped with state-of-the-art additive manufacturing hardware, 3D-scanners, powder analyzing analyzers, and a machine shop for post processing and interface machining.

GeoSolutions is a specialized in the processing and dissemination of raster and vector geospatial data with Open Source software according to the standards created by Open GeoSpatial Consortium (OGC) and the ISO Technical Committee 211 which provide the base building blocks for the INSPIRE regulations.The GeoSolutions team is composed by renowned international professionals with leading roles in some of the main Open Source products for the geospatial fi eld like GeoServer, GeoNetwork and MapStore for which GeoSolutions provides Enterprise Support Services. GeoSolutions counts among its customers more than 30 major national and international government agencies as well as private companies worldwide. 
Mission
Thanks to the wide experience gained in supporting mid-size and large enterprise Environments for mission critical projects, GeoSolutions is able to provide highly customized solutions based upon Open Source products with proven reliability in order to respond promptly and efficiently to the customers¿ needs. The primary objective of GeoSolutions is the integration and the complete interoperability with COTS software and/or pre-existing infrastructures.Objective
Our goal is to make geospatial interoperability completely transparent. We aspire to hide all the complexities of accessing location-based information and handling geospatial services. We hope to achieve systems and services that are understandable, accessible and usable by everyone, everyone.
GeoSolutions' field of expertise includes, but is not limited to,  geospatial data fusion, geospatial data management and dissemination, image processing, 2D advanced visualizations techniques and distributed applications.

Founded in 2005, Testonica Lab has become a world-wide pioneer and leader in developing automated synthetic and virtual embedded instrumentation. Currently TL offers cutting-edge technologies and tools for high-speed test access and at-speed test application based on JTAG and FPGAs, which are used by leaders in consumer electronics, telecom, automotive, military, aerospace, industrial electronics, entertainment and fundamental science segments. TL is a product-oriented company that sells licenses for its tools via globally-present strategic partners.

TL has deep competence in the area of building highly optimized on-chip health monitoring networks for in-situ real-time fault recovery as well as self-health awareness through in-field error detection, diagnosis, and classification. TL has a broad experience with many computational platforms including embedded CPUs, microcontrollers and FPGAs. 

TL has strong relations in academic world and TL’s R&D team is a solid compound of experienced engineers, fresh PhDs and PhD students. TL continuously participates in numerous research activities both at national and EU levels. TL has recently completed an ESA-funded EXPRO+ and GSTP activity 4000124897/18/NL/CBi SoC-HEALTH: On-Chip Health Monitoring and Fault Management for SoC Health-Awareness in Space Missions.

Company description: UNEP/GRID-Warsaw Centre was established on 17 September 1991 pursuant to the official agreement signed between the Director of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the Polish Government (Ministry of the Environment, Forestry, and Natural Resources), as a centre working within the Global Resource Information Database (GRID) network. Formally, the Centre has been established in the structures of the National Foundation for Environmental Protection (hence, it has the non-profit status).
The Centre actively co-operates with self-government authorities, educational institutions and private companies pursuing corporate social responsibility (CSR) principles in a wide range of projects devoted to effective environmental management, application of remote sensing, geographic information systems (GIS), and environmental education.
Specific areas of expertise and activity of the UNEP/GRID-Warsaw Centre entail the following:
· geoinformation and remote sensing: analyses of spatial data on environmental and socio-economic phenomena and processes; geodatabase development and maintenance (incl. data harmonisation according to the INSPIRE implementing rules); development and market application of GIS solutions and geoportals; practical implementation of result of scientific discovery related to novel geoinformation tools and methods;
· environmental governance and reporting: thematic mapping and geovisualisation, incl. 3D modelling; development of GIS and ICT applications to support decision making and spatial planning by public administration units; use of mobile GIS-based tools and techniques to support monitoring and rapid mapping activities; implementation of the INSPIRE Directive in Poland;
· capacity building: specialized trainings, workshops, seminars, conferences; e-Learning courses; educational materials and publications – targeted primarily at public administration bodies and related to the use of remote sensing tools, GIS tools and applications (with focus on open source solutions), spatial data for environmental management, spatial planning, crisis management, etc.
· environmental campaigns, environmental education, public participation: using modern multimedia and other ICT solutions; youth education and awareness building on issues related to environment/nature protection, community involvement, building ICT literacy; fostering public and inter-institutional consultations, e.g. in spatial planning procedures, aided by geoinformation tools and methods (geo-consultations); citizen science; CSR and sustainable business practices;

Company description: The ENTENTE pour la forêt méditerranéenne, known as ENTENTE VALABRE, is an independent public administrative body that works closely with the Ministries of the Interior, Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion (MTECT) and Agriculture. As a key interdepartmental player at both institutional and territorial level, VALABRE's main challenge is to protect people and areas from major natural hazards.
Bringing together 31 local authorities, including 15 départements, 15 Services Départementaux d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) and the Collectivité Territoriale de Corse, its missions focus on the pooling of skills and resources, as well as consultation with its partners, with the aim of optimising the management of major risks. The organisation is divided into 4 departments:
- The Information and Prevention of Major Risks Department ;
- The Civil Security Training School (ECASC);
- The Test and Research Centre (CEREN);
- The Innovation and New Technologies Centre (PONT).
 
The PONT offers its members a suite of technological solutions covering all the needs associated with managing forest fires and fires in natural areas, from prevention to operational response, feedback and continuous improvement. VALABRE is strategically positioned as a provider of shared operational solutions, with a coherent vision at territorial level. The COP CRIMSON, used by the Centre Opérationnel de Gestion Interministérielle des Crises (COGIC), the 7 Centres Opérationnels de Zone de défense (COZ) and more than 50 fired departments, continues to be deployed in France (SDIS, departmental councils, local authorities) and internationally. The CRIMSON tool also provides real-time information to the ORSEC and SYNAPSE national crisis management platforms, making VALABRE the only French entity authorised to supply these Ministry of the Interior networks. Once operational, the NEXIS project, which aims to pool the Alert Management Systems (SGA) and Operational Management Systems (SGO) used in the SDIS, will also incorporate a CRIMSON gateway.
The PONT also keeps a proactive watch on innovative technologies, with the aim of enhancing its services to end users (emergency services, civil protection, inter-municipalities, regional authorities, etc.). For example, PONT was commissioned by MTECT to carry out the PANOPTÈS study, the aim of which is to deploy a system for the early detection (<5 minutes) of all forest fires and fires in natural areas on a national (metropolitan) scale, and to monitor them in near-real time (burnt areas, fire fronts, fire breaks, hot spots, etc.). This early detection is in line with the national operational doctrine of "massive attack on incipient fires".

entityDescription:
Swiss TXT AG is a wholly-owned subsidiary of SRG SSR, the Swiss public broadcaster. It serves as the leading competence center for Digital Media Operations and Accessibility for all national Swiss Radio & TV stations.
With a strong emphasis on operations and Cloud Solutions, Swiss TXT AG has been at the forefront of guiding Switzerland into an increasingly complex digital future. For over 35 years, Swiss TXT AG has provided infrastructure, content management, and commercialization services to SRG, including access services such as captions and subtitling for various language areas throughout Switzerland. Notable customers of Swiss TXT AG include SRF 1, SRF zwei, SRF info, RTS Un, RTS Deux, and more.
In the past decade, Swiss TXT AG has expanded its services beyond broadcasters and now caters to companies like SBB and governmental organizations such as Parliaments. Its technical services encompass a wide range of offerings, including 4K delivery via IP, multimedia playout, multi-CDN operations, HbbTV distribution, operation of the Swiss Media Hub, as well as the development and operation of the Swiss national content Exchange for private media houses and publishers. Additionally, in the field of Managed Cloud, Swiss TXT AG provides Storage solutions (6PB), VOD, and the Kaltura Hub Europe.
All distribution channels offered by Swiss TXT AG support live streaming and Video on Demand functionality. The comprehensive backend operation covers the entire workflow, which includes Digital Rights Management (DRM), Encoding Transcoding, Media & Digital Asset Management (MAM/DAM), Transfer & CDN (Content Delivery Network) with multi-CDN functionality.
A dedicated department within Swiss TXT AG focuses on providing access services for foreign languages and people with hearing or visual impairments, utilizing advanced technologies. These access services encompass captioning, subtitling, audio description, and signing. In addition to serving SRG, Swiss TXT AG also extends these services to external customers such as Sky and Pro7. This year, Swiss TXT AG introduced remote access services for individuals with hearing impairments and the deaf community in educational institutions across Switzerland.
Committed to innovation, Swiss TXT AG strives to develop, implement, and operate cutting-edge technologies while maintaining a strong focus on quality. Notably, the company has created the NerStar tool, which measures the quality of live subtitling and is currently utilized by broadcast regulators in various countries including the UK, Canada, Switzerland, and Spain.

entityName: Instytut Systematyki i Ewolucji Zwierząt Polskiej Akademii Nauk
entityDescription:
The Institute of Systematics and Evolution of Animals of the Polish Academy of Sciences (PAS) was founded in 1989 from the Department of Systematic and Experimental Zoology PAS. However the history of the Institute goes back to the year 1865, the founding year of the Physiographic Committee initiated by the Kraków Scientific Society. The Natural History Museum was established at the same time under the original name of the Physiographic Museum. Today, the museum is an integral part of our Institute.
Our Institute combines traditional scientific disciplines, systematics of contemporary and extinct animals and modern karyological and genetic investigations. Our scientists have begun research in new fields, for example, in archaeozoology and ecology. 
The Institute employs 35 researchers including 17 professors and habilitated drs. The Institute is authorized to grant doctorates and habilitations in the biological sciences.
Our collections include over 2 millions, often unique, specimens of fossil and contemporary vertebrates and invertebrates. Our library contains one of the largest collections of zoological books in Poland and contains over 100 thousand books and periodicals.

entityDescription:
Euc Inovaçao Portugal, established in 2015, is a forward-thinking Portuguese company headquartered in Lisbon, with an operational branch in Porto. Specializing in coordinating the strategic and technological development of digital twins across various application sectors, Euc Inovaçao Portugal has carved out a significant niche in this advanced technological field. The company's expertise and innovative approach to digital twin technology have been recognized through grants and sub-grants from the European Union and its Agencies.
Lisbon Headquarters
The Lisbon headquarters of Euc Inovaçao Portugal is at the heart of the company's operations, focusing on the development of digital twins in the industrial, environmental, urban and smart cities, and ecosystem sectors. This office is pivotal in pioneering digital solutions that enhance efficiency, sustainability, and resilience across these critical areas. The work conducted in Lisbon includes: 
Industrial Sector: Developing digital twins for manufacturing processes, machinery, and supply chains to optimize production, reduce downtime, and anticipate maintenance needs. 
Environmental Sector: Creating digital twins of natural environments and ecosystems to monitor changes, predict impacts of human activities, and develop conservation strategies.
Urban and Smart Cities Sector: Implementing digital twins for urban planning, infrastructure management, and smart city initiatives, enabling cities to become more livable, sustainable, and responsive to citizens' needs. 
Ecosystem Sector: to simulate and understand complex ecological interactions, supporting efforts in biodiversity conservation and ecosystem management. 
Porto Operational Branch 
The Porto branch of Euc Inovaçao Portugal is dedicated to harnessing digital twin technology in the health sector. This focus area encompasses projects that aim to revolutionize healthcare through personalized medicine, predictive diagnostics, and advanced treatment planning. The Porto office's initiatives include: 
Personalized Medicine: Developing digital twins of individual patients to tailor treatments based on their unique genetic makeup, lifestyle, and health history.
Predictive Diagnostics: Utilizing digital twins to simulate disease progression and the impacts of different therapeutic approaches, enabling earlier and more accurate diagnoses. 
Advanced Treatment Planning: Creating precise digital models of patients' anatomy to guide surgical procedures and treatment plans, enhancing outcomes and reducing recovery times. 
Collaborations and Recognitions Euc Inovaçao Portugal actively collaborates with numerous Portuguese and international universities and research centers, fostering an environment of academic and scientific exchange that enriches its projects. These partnerships are instrumental in keeping the company at the forefront of digital twin technology, ensuring access to the latest research, talent, and innovations. The company's contributions to its fields of expertise have been recognized through prestigious EU grants, affirming its role as a leader in digital twin development.

entityDescription:
DronePrep is a government backed software platform which is helping drone companies and end users unlock new possibilities in low-level airspace to enable new dynamic Drone use cases.

The future of drone delivery involves use of low-level airspace and landing locations not previously used for manned flight i.e. low-level airspace over property and access to land to landing and take-off purposes. 

The DronePrep platform facilitates communication between landowners, external stakeholders and end users allowing drone users to understand where they can and cannot and can fly and help communicate which landowners are receptive to delivery.

In 2020-21, DronePrep led collaboration projects, have enabled the UK’s first NHS medical deliveries, brokered the UK’s first airspace leases to enable drone flight in low-level airspace and to support the UK’s first ‘drone enabled’ fully autonomous Farm (and now Royal Mails first ever delivery by Drone).

Our software is designed to communicate landowner drone access policies and delivery locations for 56million land parcels in the UK and is supported by BEIS, HM Land Registry, Registrars of Scotland, Ordnance Survey, what3words and Worcestershire’s tech accelerator BETADEN.

entityName: UNB - Radio and Space Physics Laboratory
entityDescription:
The Radio and Space Physics Lab (RSPL) at the University of New Brunswick is involved in several aspects of the near-Earth and planetary space environments, including fundamental and applied ionospheric and space plasma research, ionospheric modeling, and development of radio instruments for ionospheric monitoring. RSPL operates Space Weather Ionospheric Network Canada (SWINCan), one of the world's largest ionospheric observation networks. RSPL includes several research scientists, graduate and undergraduate students, and technical staff. Some specific projects of RSPL are outlined below.
The Canadian High Arctic Ionospheric Network (CHAIN) was the original project of RSPL. Since 2008, CHAIN has collected GNSS and high frequency (HF) ionosonde data in order to measure and model the state of the ionosphere spanning polar, auroral, and sub-auroral regions. Currently, there is GNSS data being actively collected from 25 sites across the far north of Canada. CADI data is being collected from 8 sites, co-located with several of the GNSS sites.

SWINCan is the new, expanded ionospheric monitoring network of RSPL, and includes current CHAIN locations. SWINCan is a pan-Canadian network of GNSS receivers and HF sounder systems. This network will be the single largest unified network of GNSS sites in Canada, with 143 locations across the country. HF sounders will be deployed at 20 SWINCan locations. This network will observe the multi-scale structuring and dynamics of the high-latitude ionosphere with unprecedented detail, providing essential measurements to resolve the internal and geospace coupling processes that drive this complex behaviour. SWINCan will also provide essential input for enhancing three-dimensional empirical modeling capabilities of ionospheric plasma density, and for mitigating the effects of space weather on modern technological systems such as position, navigation, and timing (PNT), radio communication, and over-the-horizon-radar, services critical to social, military, science, and major economic sectors.
The Canadian High Arctic Ionospheric Models (CHAIM) project involves advanced modelling of the ionosphere. CHAIM incorporates data from CHAIN and several other ground and satellite sources. The Empirical Canadian High Arctic Ionospheric Model is the current state-of-the-art for the high latitude ionospheric densities, while assimilative-CHAIM (A-CHAIM) provides the near-real-time ionospheric state by ingesting real-time, multi-source data. CHAIM web applications and software are readily available on the RSPL website.
RSPL is developing next-generation Modular Ionospheric Sounders (MODIS) which will replace the Canadian Advanced Digital Ionosondes (CADIs) being used as part of CHAIN. MODIS systems take advantage of the latest developments in software defined radio and signal processing technology. While providing ionograms and 3D ionospheric drift velocity at a fraction of the cost of current CHAIN ionosondes, MODIS also features scalable coherent timing with nanosecond subsample precision and multi-channel, remote controlled operation. The ionosonde application includes stand-alone and oblique sounding, and permits interdependent experiments with other ground and spaceborne radio systems. The system hardware is designed for operation and maintenance in harsh, remote environments such as the Canadian Arctic.

entityDescription:
People in Need organization was established in 1992 by a group of Czech war correspondents who were no longer satisfied with merely relaying information about ongoing conflicts and began sending out aid. It gradually became established as a professional humanitarian organization striving to provide aid in troubled regions and support adherence to human rights around the world.
Throughout the 30 years of its existence, People in Need has become one of the biggest non-profit organizations in Central Europe. In addition to humanitarian aid and human rights, it now also targets education and helps people living in social exclusion.
We are part of Alliance2015, a strategic network of seven European non-governmental organizations engaged in humanitarian aid and development projects. This collaboration increases effectiveness, both in working in the target countries and in campaigns aimed at influencing the attitudes of politicians and the general public in Europe.

entityDescription:
Little Place Labs strive to become the leader in the relatively new satellite edge computing sector. We create sustainable and scalable advanced software and edge computing capabilities for satellites, with the ultimate mission of exploring, protecting our environment, and improving humanity with our Space-based solutions.
Our core products are special machine learning models that can be deployed and run on remote sensing satellites. Raw imagery and other data would be processed to generate usable insights while in orbit, instead of needing to first download massive amounts of raw data to the ground. This not only saves resources and money but enables near real-time insights for quick responses.
Our technology will help to accelerate and improve the identification and analysis of time-sensitive events (such as forest fires, floods, oil spills, logistics, defense, etc) and optimize the efficiency of the delivery of intelligence to decision-makers on the ground. Our wide range of potential customers includes satellite operators, and end-users like governments, local authorities, emergency responders, traders, and insurance companies.

description: boltzplatz is an engineering service provider and a spin-off from the University of Stuttgart (Germany), offering numerical simulations of rarefied gas and plasma dynamics. At the heart of the company lies the open-source software PICLas, which was originally developed to simulate space systems, including atmospheric entry and in-space propulsion. Thanks to a successful technology transfer, companies in the semiconductor manufacturing and vacuum coating industries developing vacuum and plasma technologies can leverage our numerical simulations. This reduces the need for costly prototypes and extensive testing, saving both time and expenses. Potential applications include the prediction of the performance of vacuum pumps, determination of the gas and plasma distribution in vacuum coating equipment, and the characterization of electron and ion beam properties. Beyond complete simulation projects, boltzplatz offers technical support and software development for PICLas.

Imendo is an experienced IT partner with four business divisions and was recently named "Austria's Leading Company" by PwC, Die Presse and the Kreditschutzverband (1st place in Austria in the category of turnover up to EUR 10 million). This is the most important business award in Austria - we were not only recognized for our innovative solutions, but also for our many years of stable growth and excellent company figures. The 4 business areas are

-Enterprise Content Management & Intranet solutions based on Microsoft SharePoint, PowerPlatform and Teams (M365 Collaboration & Communication)
-Customized software development and software integration
-Data analytics & reporting solutions and data warehouse projects
-Cyber Security

More than 90 experienced software engineers, project managers, infrastructure experts and business consultants ensure that your projects are delivered on-budget, on-time and in-quality - but above all that you receive solutions that really support you and your company. Imendo competencies that form the basis of a successful project:

-Customizing close to the standard:
In particular in SharePoint Online-based projects we implement and customize close to Microsoft standards. In this way, we ensure that your SharePoint Online-based ECM solution can continue to be operated on the latest SharePoint configuration even after Microsoft updates.
-Functionality and design:
Imendo's software engineering is characterized by a flexible architecture tailored to the use case and optimal functionality paired with user-friendly interfaces.-Customer needs have priorityWhere individual solutions are necessary, these are adapted to the customer's processes and requirements. Processes are redesigned in consultation with the customer at those points where efficiency/throughput time or usability are required. Extensions can be made as required. Imendo ensures optimal adaptation to your business requirements with great foresight.
Multi-device / flexible use:
Cross-platform development is used to create applications that can be used on a wide variety of devices. Depending on specific requirements, the advantages of the different end devices are also used to create an appealing user experience (example: production / warehouse management vs. back office)
-Scaled, cloud-capable infrastructure:
The setup, configuration and customization of infrastructure components - especially for individual extensions - is implemented by Imendo according to the principles of the Microsoft Well-Architected Framework. Preference is given to the implementation of infrastructure components and the operation of applications based on the Azure Cloud Stack. The implementation of applications on the .NET platform enables the development of backend and web applications that can be integrated into almost all server infrastructures. Delivery and hosting can also take place in the form of Docker containers after customer coordination in order to enable hosting independently of the infrastructure or in a hybrid setup (on-premise in the data center, Azure Cloud or AWS).

entityDescription: The University of Évora is composed of the Schools of Arts, Sciences and Technology, Social Sciences, Health and Human Development and Nursing. The most relevant research centre for the present project is the Comprehensive Health Research Center (CHRC). The CHRC is a multidisciplinary, multi-institutional and integrated research centre, aimed at supporting, developing and promoting clinical, public health and health services research. Other pillars and core activities of the CHRC are health education and training, innovation, digital health and entrepreneurship. It is organised in 4 thematic lines: Health promotion, public health and lifestyles; Diseases with high impact and high mortality rate; Health policies and healthcare development; Innovation in health. Peter Scott pioneered the idea that taking action to save wetlands and their wildlife involves both inspiring people to care about wetlands and undertaking direct conservation. He set up WWT at Slimbridge, Gloucestershire, as a centre for science and conservation. Uniquely at the time, he opened it to the public so that everyone could enjoy getting close to nature.
WWT is now one of the largest and most respected wetland conservation organisations in the world. We welcome over a million visitors every year to our ten wetland centres and reserves across the UK and we have global reach for our projects to protect wetlands for the people and wildlife that rely on them. In recognition of our expertise in promoting sustainable development through wetland conservation, WWT has been endorsed as one of only six International Organisation Partners by the 170 countries that are signatories to the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands.
We are pioneers in saving threatened wetland wildlife, world experts in wetland management and creation, and a centre for excellence in conservation science.

Company description: The National Institute for Agrarian and Veterinarian Research I. P. (INIAV) is the State Laboratory of the Ministry of Agriculture and Food, that develops research activities in the agricultural and veterinary fields. It has the task of carrying out scientific and policy research to support public policies, while defending the national interests and the deepening of Europe’s common policies. - To develop the scientific and technological basis that supports the definition of the public sector policies;

- To ensure its National Reference Laboratory role, broadening the spectrum of laboratory testing particularly in the areas of food safety, animal health and plant protection and health; 
- To cooperate with related scientific and technological institutions, and participate in national and international science and technology activities.

entityDescription:
Aardvark Sensing provides an autonomous robotic ecosystem designed for large-scale and long-running soil surveys. Our durable robots operate continuously for extended periods without human intervention, conducting systematic scans of agricultural land with navigational accuracy at the centimeter level and a continuous connection to the cloud.
Carrying various sensing payloads on board, including spectrometers, cosmic ray neutron detectors, acoustic sonar, ground-penetrating radar and more, each robot gathers essential data on soil characteristics. These measurements include surface roughness, soil compaction, soil moisture, mineral content, nutrient levels, sub-surface soil structure, and more.
Our primary goals are to improve soil classification models derived from Sentinel data and enhance the resolution of soil moisture assessments from SMOS satellites. By providing ground truth data to improve satellite data application, we leverage the vast availability of satellite data.
We offer our ecosystem as a research tool to research institutes, enabling systematic soil research. By exploring the research community, we constantly discover new potential applications and needs, such as levee integrity monitoring through ground-penetrating radar, the quantifying of soil quality and pollutants for compliance with the EU Green Deal, and peacetime landmine clearance

Scanway S.A. was founded in 2016. Scanway is a Polish technology company that designs and implements optical solutions for two industries: space (high-resolution telescopes and observation instruments) and manufacturing (machine vision systems). Scanway products make it possible to observe any object and area in a precise, continuous manner and with an accuracy greater than the human eye. The company consists of two teams - Scanway Space, which specializes in creating observation systems for micro- and nanosatellites, and Scanway Industry, which develops industrial quality control systems. The founding team is composed of 3 engineers that have deep knowledge and experience in team building and company development. Founders were able to develop Scanway from scratch in 2016 up to ~80 employees in 2025, while maintaining major control over the company through the investment processes.
Scanway, from January 2023 is an operator of the operational STAR VIBE satellite with the most accurate imaging of the Earth in the history of Polish satellite systems. Company products are on board EagleEye, PIAST satellites and rockets such as Ariane 6 and ISAR Aerospace.
Scanway has gained experience in implementing and managing R&D projects and commercializing R&D results through the numerous projects.

description: Imagine you could analyze every place on earth every day from the stratosphere or lower with a reusable device carried by the wind and solar energy. Imagine internet and communication possibilities all over the world at far lower costs and space debris compared to today’s satellites. Imagine economically friendly UAVs that fulfil those long missions, which today have to be done by manned aerial carriers, like helicopters or planes, like the analysis of large areas e.g. for agriculture, resource exploration surveys, forestry and many more. These are the challenges we started to tackle. The h-aero® flight system combines the established flight concepts: airplane, helicopter and balloon. Thereby the advantages of the concepts are retained, while disadvantages are eliminated. The flight system is made of high-tech-materials (fiber composites, canvas and high-density foils). With solar cells on and under the large hull, it can fulfil 24h and autonomous flight-missions. In case of an emergency, the structure acts like a parachute. The hull is filled with helium and ensures natural buoyancy. At the same time the hull provides a comparable aerodynamic behaviour as a Frisbee. The technical description can be read in the patent documents DE102006028885A1 and PCT EP2017/063221. Our first carriers are made to harvest the "low hanging fruits" of this technology and to raise social acceptance. At the same time we tought it to fly autonomous.

entityName: Centre of Polymer and Carbon Materials Polish Academy of Sciences
entityDescription:
The research carried out in the Centre is of an interdisciplinary character and covers a wide range of topics related with such areas of science as chemistry, physics, biology and medicine. The main aim of the research is to develop novel polymers, carbon-polymer materials, carbon materials and to examine their properties so as to utilize them in biotechnology, microtechnology, optoelectronics, protection of the environment and healthcare.
The currently performed studies comprise the following issues:
- Materials to be used in biology, biochemistry and healthcare:- polymers reacting to stimuli from the environment for controlled release of biologically active materials
- carbon materials for oxygen biosensors
- thermo responding substrates for growing cell sheets
- polymeric resorbable surgical systems with shape memory
- polymers and oligomers of 3-hydroxybutyric acid to be used in medicine
- polymer systems for the controlled drug release - influence of the drug on the hydrolytic degradation of polymers

- Materials for the protection of the environment:- polymers for packaging undergoing organic recycling, including cosmetic industry packaging
- polymer and polymer-inorganic hybrid membrane materials for gas and liquid separations
- novel catalytic materials to improve the properties of diesel fuels by removal of organic sulphur compounds
- new catalysts for reduction of nitrogen oxides emission from flue gases

- Construction materials:- systems based on epoxy and cyanate ester resins
- core-shell nanoparticles utilized as polyester resin fillers
- biomorphous composites prepared using monolithic porous carbon supports derived from carbonised vascular plants and selected polymers, e.g. chitosan and poly(furfuryl alcohol)
- carbonaceous materials derived from blends of coals and selected porous carbon materials
- nano carbon tubes and fibers used as catalysts and composite material fillers

- Materials for electronics and optoelectronics:- polymer-semiconductor hybrid layer structures
- luminescent polymers
- polymer materials for photovoltaic cells

- Methods and techniques of structural research:- utilization of novel methods of high resolution nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (NMR) in structural analysis of biodegradable copolymers
- microstructure studies of macromolecular chains by means of NMR spectroscopy (acrylate - methylacrylate copolymers)
- structural studies of biodegradable copolymers using mass spectrometry and soft ionization techniques
- properties of linear and nonlinear macromolecules in solutions, and methods of their characterization

entityDescription:
Zeleros is a Spanish startup pioneering the development of hyperloop technology, focusing on innovative propulsion systems to propel pods through low-pressure tubes at high speeds. At the core of their propulsion technology lies a combination of magnetic levitation and propulsion.
- Magnetic Levitation (Maglev): Zeleros utilizes magnetic levitation to suspend the hyperloop pods above the track, eliminating friction and allowing for smooth, efficient movement. This technology relies on powerful magnets and high-performance non-linear control algorithms to lift and propel the pods, reducing energy consumption and enabling high-speed travel.

- Propulsion: Zeleros employs electric drivetrains and batteries to propel the hyperloop pods forward along the track. Zeleros ensures safety and tailored solutions for an efficient acceleration, essential for achieving the rapid speeds characteristic of hyperloop travel.

Zeleros' propulsion technologies are designed to optimize energy efficiency, minimize environmental impact, and ensure passenger safety. Through continuous research, development, and testing, Zeleros is advancing the feasibility and scalability of hyperloop transportation, positioning itself as a key player in the future of high-speed, sustainable travel.

description: Azulfy provides accurate measurements and reports about water, air and soil pollution for any location in the world and in any date, using Space and Local readings. Azulfy delivers environmental pollution analysis (both in real-time and historical) to help public services and tourism platforms to accurately gauge the level of pollution in the ocean, rivers, beaches and atmosphere at a given coordinate.
entityDescription:
Azulfy (formerly known as Green Travel Spots and GTS Space Technologies) was the winner of the Portuguese edition of the 3rd Cassini Hackathon, and second place in the European Cassini Competition. Azulfy uses space technology – namely Earth Observation – to perform pollution analytics and assessments over machine learning algorithms. Through the analysis of Satellite Images, we aim to monitor several pollution indicators from water, air and soil, providing reliable alerts to local governments and policy makers – our main clients. The indicators monitored by Azulfy were defined by the EU2030 goals and also feedback from potential clients.
The problem identified by Azulfy, still during the Cassini Hackathon, was that the methods for pollution monitoring by local municipalities were too manual, depending on the skills of the staff allocated to the department of the Environment. In that sense, when a pollution issue or disaster occurs, governments do not have adequate tools to monitor the impact of these events or evaluate damage, while also using unofficial multiple sources of information that makes it impossible to drive intelligent decisions.
Azulfy covers these issues through its Pollution Crisis Management System, a SaaS platform that provides daily status of several pollution variables. In addition, our platform provides automatic alerts when a certain variable level is above threshold, allowing an instant reaction from local governments. Currently, the monitoring of pollutions variables is made through laboratory analysis, which may take up to 15 days to present results. Azulfy’s platform also creates a chat channel for each alert, allowing the environment team to not only use the platform for exchanging information, but also to store local pictures, laboratory analysis and any other relevant information related to that alert. As a result, our platform can be used as a repository of information from pollution events, while also generating reports with all information to be printed or digitally stored in other systems. Azulfy is currently an Incubatee at ESA Business Incubation Centre in Portugal – IPN, and was awarded with a first round of investments from Portugal Ventures.

entityDescription:
Xona Space Systems was founded in 2019 with a mission of supporting modern technology to operate safely in any environment. To that end, Xona is deploying the first commercial satellite navigation infrastructure needed to support intelligent transportation systems like self-driving cars. In the last two decades, satellite navigation has revolutionized many industries. With more than 6.5 billion enabled devices, Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) find utility in nearly all facets of modern life, from the source of time for our communications networks to the source of safety-critical positioning in civil aviation. Now, another revolution is on the horizon, one which promises disruption of transportation, mobility, and safety. 
Autonomous systems in the form of self-driving cars, autonomous aerial platforms, and mobile robotics are on the rise, targeting improved access to the mobility of people, goods, and services. This transformation is one whose complexity demands more than what navigation systems today can provide. Xona Space System’s PULSAR satellite constellation will address this gap by delivering ultra-precise and highly reliable positioning data, essential for the safe and efficient operation of these autonomous systems. By advancing beyond the capabilities of current GNSS technology, Xona's PULSAR system is poised to be a cornerstone in the infrastructure of the emerging era of autonomous transportation, ensuring higher standards of accuracy and reliability in a world moving towards greater automation and connectivity.
To date, Xona US has been the central location for development of the core mission and engineering of the PULSAR system. Xona Canada has established itself as a small centre for R&D and is developing service operations to support critical needs of the service.
Xona UK was incorporated in 2019. Its priority has been as a gateway to business development in the UK. This project serves to springboard Xona UK’s development as a centre for commercialisation-based testing and validation. Eventually it is our goal to host mission operations in the country, splitting the role across continents and mitigating risks to using only a single location. 
Xona Canada was also incorporated in 2019 and hosts the office of the CTO (Tyler Reid). Its operations have focussed on R&D projects such as ionospheric modelling and as a development centre for work in precise point positioning (PPP) and corrections service backend. Work is underway to grow the potential of our Canadian offices to include service operations.

entityName: Mobile Monitoring Sp. z o. o.
entityDescription:
Mobile Monitoring is a system that combines water and air quality control with smart solutions that facilitate and streamline the analysis of collected data. Our product allows for a quick response to environmental pollution events and minimizes their impact. The Mobile Monitoring System consists of:
- IoT solution along with a monitoring and analytical platform
Devices for continuous monitoring of water parameters, such as: Buoys and measuring floats - control parameters like oxygen content, redox potential, pH, water conductivity, nitrogen, phosphorus, algae, chlorine, which are used as indicators to detect undesirable processes in water. Water buoys for detecting leaks of oil-derived substances. Water drones for precise pollution mapping and creating water quality maps. A mobile device for temporary measurement of water quality. Data from drones and measuring devices are transmitted in real-time to the analytical platform, which controls water parameters and informs about exceedances. The system performs automatic data analysis, notifying users of deviations from the norm, allowing for a quick response and taking action to prevent the spread of pollution or the occurrence of an ecological disaster. Continuous monitoring using measuring devices is crucial because water pollution is often detected too late, with visible consequences. Real-time monitoring is essential, and sometimes even constant monitoring may be insufficient. In cases where minor deviations do not clearly indicate dangerous events or the extent of pollution, water drones provide a two-dimensional water quality map. Mobile Monitoring is a solution for every entity involved in water monitoring. Potential Mobile Monitoring clients include ports, local governments, environmental protection agencies, and industrial plants, who are legally obliged to monitor water quality.

Our product allows for a quick response to environmental pollution events and minimizes their impact. The Mobile Monitoring System consists of:
- IoT solution along with a monitoring and analytical platform
Devices for continuous monitoring of water parameters, such as: Buoys and measuring floats - control parameters like oxygen content, redox potential, pH, water conductivity, nitrogen, phosphorus, algae, chlorine, which are used as indicators to detect undesirable processes in water. Water buoys for detecting leaks of oil-derived substances. Water drones for precise pollution mapping and creating water quality maps. A mobile device for temporary measurement of water quality. Data from drones and measuring devices are transmitted in real-time to the analytical platform, which controls water parameters and informs about exceedances. The system performs automatic data analysis, notifying users of deviations from the norm, allowing for a quick response and taking action to prevent the spread of pollution or the occurrence of an ecological disaster. Continuous monitoring using measuring devices is crucial because water pollution is often detected too late, with visible consequences. Real-time monitoring is essential, and sometimes even constant monitoring may be insufficient. In cases where minor deviations do not clearly indicate dangerous events or the extent of pollution, water drones provide a two-dimensional water quality map. Mobile Monitoring is a solution for every entity involved in water monitoring. Potential Mobile Monitoring clients include ports, local governments, environmental protection agencies, and industrial plants, who are legally obliged to monitor water quality.

entityDescription:
CGIAR is a global research partnership for a food-secure future. CGIAR science is dedicated to transforming food, land, and water systems in a climate crisis. Its research is carried out by 13 CGIAR Centers/Alliances in close collaboration with hundreds of partners, including national and regional research institutes, civil society organizations, academia, development organizations and the private sector.
For 50 years, CGIAR has been a leader in agricultural science and innovation for development. From specific food crops to water systems to policy, CGIAR’s Centers across the globe – working independently and together in partnership – have produced science that has brought benefits to hundreds of millions of the world’s poor.Today, the planet is facing escalating climate and biodiversity crises. Research in agriculture, food, land and water is more multi-disciplinary than ever before. We know much more about the interconnected nature of our food, land and water systems. Traditional funding models have shifted dramatically.The world has changed. And CGIAR is changing with it. CGIAR adopts a holistic view of the food system, from farm to fork, recognizing that many other systems influence it, and that our solutions should minimize trade-offs between increased agricultural productivity and climate and environmental goals.In 2019, CGIAR began a reform to better wield its combined expertise and resources across its Centers.
CGIAR’s Centers are independent legal entities and research organizations collectively home to more than 9,000 scientists, researchers, technicians and staff working in over 80 countries.Each Center has its own local footprint with a host country agreement granting privileges and immunities (including no liabilities for taxes), and each with its own external auditor. Although the Centers draw on the same pooled funding via the CGIAR Trust Fund, and have adopted certain shared policies and procedures, the Centers are governed by their own respective constitutive documents and boards.
The CGIAR System Organization is governed by theCharter of the CGIAR System Organization,and in collaboration with theCGIAR System Council, provides governance to the CGIAR System. The System Organization has an important role in facilitating and overseeing the development, effective and efficient implementation of the2030 Research and Innovation Strategy. The System Organization enters into agreements with the trustee of the CGIAR Trust Fund,Funders, Centers and other relevant entities for funding CGIAR Research and other activities of theCGIAR System.

description:
Founded in 2018 and based in Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany, ResearchConcept io GmbH (RC) specializes in research and development services and consulting services for international organizations, universities, public and private companies and the general public. Under the leadership of its founder, RC has an impressive track record in innovative research and model development, particularly in the areas of aerosol composition and climate modeling.
RC's expertise spans various areas, including the study of hygroscopic growth of aerosols through the ongoing development of the gas-liquid-solid aerosol equilibrium distribution model (EQSAM). In addition to climate modeling, RC also offers advanced point forecasts for solar radiation and atmospheric visibility, combining innovative aerosol composition models with artificial intelligence. RC has been actively involved in the CAMS team and is committed to improving the source codes of the atmospheric composition prediction system, IFS-COMPO. IFS-COMPO is used to produce the CAMS forecasts for the global distribution of aerosols and trace gases under the coordination of ECMWF. The collaboration extends across various projects, including CAMS2_35 and the HORIZON Europe project CAMAERA, since 2024.
The integration of AFB SolarTec Ltd in 2021 and the establishment of the uniWeather team in 2022 demonstrate the continuous growth and expansion of RC's areas of activity. With a highly motivated and experienced team, RC continues to help the public adapt to climate change.

entityDescription:
The Municipality of Turin, with its 908.000 inhabitants, its 130 kmq of territorial extension and its GDP of 55.000 millions of Euros (which is 4.5% of the national GDP), is one of the most important city in Italy.
Since the 1990’s Torino has been following a path that has transformed it from an industrial capital - a sector which continues to play a fundamental role - into a pole of innovation, culture and improved quality of life. Torino first started a process of territorial transformation, thanks to the 1995 Town Master Plan, then a process of territorial marketing, through the first and second metropolitan strategic plans in 2000 and 2006, and it is nowadays multiplying its efforts towards a more and more sustainable development.
The urban sustainable development is, indeed, one of the key-themes of the City Strategic Guidelines, that is the programmatic document containing the political-administrative Mayor’s plan. In this plan, the Municipality government describes its strategic action-lines for the City development and, among the others, it affirms its commitment to foster the environmental quality of the town territory, to increase the capability of technological innovation and to make Turin a real “Smart City”.

entityDescription:
Rzeszow University of Technology (RUT), named after Ignacy Łukasiewicz, is a leading technical university in southeastern Poland. Established in 1951, it currently educates over 11,200 students across 7 faculties and plays a key role in Poland’s aerospace and innovation ecosystem.

Aviation and Space Competences

RUT was the first university in Poland to educate civil aviation pilots through an academic program. Its Aviation Training Centre in Jasionka and Gliding Centre in Bezmiechowa combine advanced pilot training with applied aerospace research.

The Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Aeronautics houses:

- Department of Aerospace Engineering – focusing on aerodynamics, structures, propulsion, UAVs, and hybrid systems;

- Department of Avionics and Control – developing flight control, navigation, and autonomous aircraft technologies;

- Laboratories for aerospace structures and materials, including hydrogen combustion and fatigue testing.

RUT is involved in major R&D initiatives related to hybrid and hydrogen propulsion, fuel cells, and flight tests with alternative-energy platforms.

Scientific and Industrial Focus

Key research areas include Mechanical Engineering and Materials Engineering, supported by doctoral programs and active industry collaboration. Topics range from machine design and robotics to space-grade materials.

RUT coordinates the AERONET–Aviation Valley Center, connecting 12 Polish universities and institutes to deliver innovation to the national aerospace sector.

Future Vision

RUT aims to:

- Lead in European aerospace and engineering education,

- Expand hydrogen and electric aviation technologies,

- Enhance technology transfer and university-industry collaboration across advanced manufacturing and aerospace sector,

- Advance space-related R&D, including material testing under ECSS, small satellite systems, and UAV-based high-altitude platforms,

- Be a central player in Poland’s and CEE’s space economy development.

entityDescription:
The transformation of the food industry has a significant impact on mitigating the climate crisis. The consumption of regionally and locally produced food from farms is a central 'lever' for the economical, ecological and social sustainability transformation of the food system. However, systematic cooperation between small farms and the large chains of food retail, which would pay off enormously, is currently prevented by structural differences between the supply and demand sides.
In detail, this is due to the following:
1.The core competence of agricultural producers is the production of food, rather than its professional marketing in food retailing.
2.Although local products in the product portfolio are highly attractive for food retailers, the high coordination and transaction costs associated with the large number of small suppliers, together with their incompatibility with the logistics systems of EDEKA, REWE, Globus, etc. prevent them from being offered.
 
LOKORA addresses this constellation with its innovative business model withthe help of the following core elements:
1.A unique transaction and collaboration platform enables efficient communication between market participants, the processing of the transactions,field quality analysis and demand forecasting based on satellite data as well as the scale-oriented bundling of supply and actual demand.
2.With the help of machine learning approaches, an intelligent, platform-based micrologistics system ensures resource-optimized, decentrally organized direct deliveries to food retail outlets with GNSS based real-time fleet management of e-delivery vans, thus redefining local value chains in a multinational scalable way.
3.An integrated range of services in the areas of logistics, sales and marketing.

We help organisations make use of, and benefit from, satellite technologies, and bring together multi-disciplinary teams to generate ideas and solutions in an open innovation environment.
Our aim is to support UK industry by accelerating the growth of satellite applications and to contribute to capturing a 10% share of the global space market by 2030. Satellite Applications Catapult is at the heart of the satellite services and space technology revolution, driving take-up of space technology and applications to shape, and sustain, the world of tomorrow. We’re driven by how our actions help the organisations we work with, both large and small, bring new services to market. By connecting industry and academia we get new research off the ground and into the market more quickly.

entityDescription:
DRONE VOLT founded in 2011 is an international reference group specializing in the development of new aerial technologies, more particularly in civil drones manufacturing and embedded artificial intelligence.
Three brands are brought together within the DRONE VOLT Group: DRONE VOLT aeronautical manufacturer and expert in professional civil drones. AERIALTRONICS specialized in artificial intelligence and DANDRONE online DJI drones and multi-brand accessories distributor for civil and commercial applications.
The leading brand DRONE VOLT designs and manufactures commercial drones in its two production centers based in France and in the Netherlands for various civilian applications in the energy, construction, security and agricultural sectors.
The Group, led by Stefano Valentini, employs around fifty people in France and abroad: Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands, Switzerland, the US and Canada.
With its technical expertise and experience, DRONE VOLT offers industries global solutions including associated services but also more specific solutions such as the development of custom drone projects with our engineering consulting and design office, aerial data acquisition services, professional drone training with DRONE VOLT ACADEMY, assistance, maintaining and legal support.
DRONE VOLT listed on the Euronext Growth market in Paris provides UAVs to various administrations and industrial groups such as the French Army, the Ministry of the Armed Forces, Airbus, Engie, Total, RTE, Bouygues ES, ADP, the Gendarmerie des Transports Aériens (GTA) and international government agencies.
Our drones are based on more sustainable electrical technology. They generate 0% CO2 and thus help reduce the environmental impact of our partners.
DRONE VOLT is qualified as an “Innovative Company” by Bpifrance.
Our Philosophy
At Dronevolt, we don't build drones, we build flying tools.
We understand that drones are often associated with recreational or military activities, but at Dronevolt our goal is to design flying tools that can be used in professional applications. We believe drones can be used to improve business operations and industries by providing unique insights and automating dangerous or difficult tasks.
Our drones are designed to be reliable, robust and suitable for harsh environments. They are equipped with advanced technologies such as automatic stabilization, GPS navigation, high resolution camera and real-time data transmission. These features allow users to perform high-quality inspections, accurate mappings and real-time monitoring of their business activities.
We also collaborate with companies and organizations to develop customized solutions that meet the specific needs of our customers. We have previously worked with companies in the oil and gas industry, renewable energy companies, environmental organizations and emergency services to help them improve their operational efficiency and reduce their environmental impact.
At Dronevolt, we build disruptive technologies that will change the paradigm of many industries and activities to methods that are more environmentally friendly and safer for human operators. Our goal is to disrupt traditional helicopter missions in many of these activities.
We believe our disruptive technology can play a key role in the transition to a more sustainable and environmentally friendly economy. We are convinced that drones can become an essential tool in many fields and we are determined to continue our mission to make them more accessible and more efficient for companies and end users.

entityDescription:
The CERAU, Centre d'Etudes et de Recherches d'Architecture et d'Urbanisme (ww.cerau.com) was established in 1968 as de-facto association. In 1980, the CERAU transformed its legal status to become a private limited company (SPRL). 
The partners have organized a collective leadership ensuring, through the contribution of the personality and skills of each architect, the company’s efficiency and creativity.
The CERAU is currently run by three managing partners architects Cestmira VESELA, Rémy RASCOL, Aleksander PRIFTI and recently extended the partnership to two younger architects.
Besides the partners architects and urban-planners, the CERAU team is made up of more or less twenty people. The employees are divided into teams around a project manager and under the leadership of the partners architects. The partners contribute to the training of the younger architects and architects-interns, by offering young colleagues varied and creative activity in the studio. 
 
CERAU’s activity extends from designing architecture projects to the mission of construction management and the acceptance of completed works. It encompasses all the analyses, surveys, developments in urban planning and land use planning. It also covers the areas of industrialization, decoration and layout of outdoor spaces.
The diversity of the projects treated go from specific urban and regional planning studies to the interiors through the full range of architectural tasks relating to housing, office space, industry and equipment.

Pilotage
The CERAU has many years of solid experience in terms of steering groups of architects. Achievements such as the European Parliament and the La Plaine office complex or ongoing housing projects such as Tivoli Green City and the Alliance residential park.
 
Sustainability and energy saving
The CERAU has extensive practice in energy efficiency for buildings and master the regulations of the Brussels region. To cite only the most illustrative projects, the Bridge Building part of the Porte d’Ostende complex in Berchem -Saint -Agathe, was the first BREEAM certified office building in Belgium, Ateliers Mommaerts et Choux de Bruxelles projects were labeled "BATEX" (exemplary Buildings) by IBGE and the SIBELGA project, one of the first "passive" office spaces in the Brussels region. In terms of housing, our many references include the new Tivoli sustainable neighborhood in Laeken (Brussels) where all the housing units are “passive” and about 30% of them are “zero energy” and the Alliance residential park in Braine-l'Alleud (Wallonia) where the apartments are either "low energy" or "passive". Recently, the Tivoli Green City project obtained the Belgian Environment and Energy award for 2018.
 
BIM
The CERAU has acquired the necessary tools to develop its projects following the BIM method (Building Information Modeling) that integrates in a single database, all the buildings’ architectural parameters; technical, descriptive, and quantitative, throughout their life cycle, from their creation to their destruction.
 
CERAU is member of: 
▪ EAA|European Architect’s Alliance|www.eaa-eu.com
▪ BECI|Brussels Enterpr. Commerce & Industry|www.beci.be
▪ Cluster Ecobuild|http://cluster-ecobuild.com/
▪ G30|Association d’Architectes |www.g30.be

entityName: AECSIC - Instituto de Microelectronica de Sevilla
entityDescription:
The Institute is dedicated to the field of Physical Science and Technologies, one of the eight areas into which research activity is divided by the CSIC. Its main area of specialization is the design and testing of analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits in CMOS technology, as well as their use in different application contexts such as biomedical devices, wireless communications, data conversion, smart imagers & vision sensors, cybersecurity, neuromorphic computing and space technology.
The IMSE-CNM began its operations in October 1989 under the auspices of an agreement signed by the Junta de Andalucía (the Andalusian Regional Government), the CSIC and the Universidad de Sevilla. Its founding research group was initially based on the premises of the Centro de Informática Científica de Andalucía (CICA – Scientific Computing Center of Andalucía), as a subsidiary department of the Instituto de Microelectrónica de Barcelona (Barcelona Institute of Microelectronics). Later, in 1996, it was established by the Governing Board of the CSIC as a Institute in Formation, occupying a building next to the CICA ceded by the Junta de Andalucía. In late 2008, the Institute was enlarged and relocated in new premises purpose-built by the CSIC in the Parque Científico y Tecnológico Cartuja (Cartuja Scientific and Technological Park). On October 2015, by means of a Specific Collaboration Agreement signed by the CSIC and the Universidad de Sevilla, the center became a Joint Institute of both institutions.
The IMSE-CNM staff consists of approximately one hundred people, including scientists and support personnel. Most of them work for the CSIC and the Universidad de Sevilla. IMSE-CNM employees are involved in advancing scientific knowledge, designing high level scientific-technical solutions and in technology transfer. Their duties include both research and teaching activities, the latter mainly at official master and PhD degrees.
The projects undertaken at the Institute mostly correspond to EU research initiatives, National R+D Plans and Research Plans funded by the Junta de Andalucía. They focus primarily on implementing innovative concepts in silicon, using either the CNM's own clean room at the Instituto de Microelectrónica de Barcelona (IMB-CNM) or external foundries, mainly from Europractice or CMP IC services.
The Institute also participates in several technology and knowledge transfer activities with microelectronics companies, at both national and international level. These activities take the form of collaboration in numerous research contracts, the organization of training courses and the provision of scientific and technical consultation services for companies and government departments.

entityDescription:
High Precision Capillary Printing (HPCAP) is the smallest fountain pen in the world: a unique additive manufacturing technology invented by Hummink. Inspired by atomic force microscopy, it exploits the strength of capillary forces to print any ink on any substrate with resolutions ranging from 100 nm to tens of microns and an unprecedented positioning precision. HPCAP doesn’t require external source of pressure, voltage, or UV, hence alleviating common issues of printing technologies such as satellite drops or material limitations.
HPCAP bridges the resolution gap between lithography and more conventional additive manufacturing (i.e: inkjet printing) to address state-of-the-art challenges in the fields of semiconductor and printed electronics.

High Precision Capillary Printing (HPCAP) is an additive manufacturing technology invented by Hummink. Inspired by an established know-how in atomic force microscopy from the Ecole Normal Supérieure in Paris, Hummink spun-off in 2020 to develop HPCAP technology.

entityName: INSTITUTE OF ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING OF THE SLOVAK ACADEMY OF SCIENCES
entityDescription: The Institute of Electrical Engineering (IEE SAS) is a scientific institution based in 1953. Researchers of the Institute implement international projects supported by EU, projects supported by ERDF, and national projects supported by APVV and VEGA agencies. The Institute is focused on the research and development of semiconductor, superconductor, oxide and magnetic materials and devices, including theoretical and experimental study of their structural, optical, transport properties and devices for the information technology and power engineering. The semiconductor research is focused on future Si-based memory devices, technology and study of GaN, GaAs, and InP quantum heterostructures. Our work leads to several outputs, as for example capacity sensors, advanced sensors of magnetic field, x-ray detectors and others. The superconductor research is centered on technology and testing of superconducting MgB2 tapes and conductors, developed for power engineering such as transport cables, transformers and superconducting magnets. The Institute of Electrical Engineering is accredited to provide the doctoral studies as an external educational institution in collaboration with Slovak University of Technology and Comenius University in the following doctoral study fields : physics of condensed matter, electronics, electrotechnology and electrical engineering.

entityDescription:
Travel Hands charity relieves the needs of Visually Impaired People (VIP) by facilitating safe, convenient, and inexpensive outdoor travel so they can attend formal appointments, recreational activities and community events.
Travel Hands eases the outdoor commute of VIP by pairing them with sighted & verified volunteers to walk together to similar destinations. Since 44% of VIP in the UK use smartphones, we operate in a hybrid model: call centre and mobile- web apps. Customer service monitors the journeys of our users when they are active for improved safety. With our technology, a journey request is sent by a VIP or by the backend team on behalf of VIP to nearby available volunteers. The accepting volunteer will then pick up the VIP and walk towards the requested destination.
The VIP pay a small fee per journey and Volunteers flexibly help VIP and walk more. They are vetted by the Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) and trained with our online or in-person course. As a Thank You, our volunteers get reward incentives that can be redeemed from our app.

The Armagh Observatory was established in 1790 by Archbishop Richard Robinson.  It is the oldest scientific institution in Northern Ireland and the longest continuously operating astronomical research institute in the United Kingdom and Ireland.   The Armagh Planetarium was founded in 1968 by Dr Eric Lindsay, the seventh Director of the Armagh Observatory.  It is the oldest operating Planetarium in the UK and Ireland, celebrating 50 years in operation on 1 May 2018 as the public face of space and astronomy in Northern Ireland.
Armagh Observatory and Planetarium is sited in a heritage environment with a rich scientific history at the forefront of astronomy.  Now unified as a single organisation, the Armagh Observatory and Planetarium (AOP) delivers internationally-recognised research in astronomy and related sciences and vibrant educational and outreach programmes for all ages.

From 1 April 2016 the Charity Commission for Northern Ireland registered The Governors of The Armagh Observatory and Planetarium, (changed to The Armagh Observatory and Planetarium in 2023) as a charity under reference number NIC 103948.

CEA-Liten is an institute of the CEA (the French alternative energies and atomic energy commission) and is a member of the institut Carnot Énergies du futur, a consortium dedicated to research partnerships with businesses. CEA-Liten has facilities on the CEA-Grenoble campus and at French national solar energy research institute INES in Chambéry. CEA-Liten research programs focus on the energy transition.
Specifically, the institute explores solar energy, grid management, and energy storage, including batteries and hydrogen. Energy efficiency and the circular economy form an integral part of CEA-Liten’s research. The technologies developed address several markets, from power generation and distribution to transportation, and from industrial processes to greentech. CEA-Liten has leveraged its position within the CEA, one of the world’s most innovative government research organizations, to lead the development of complementary, cost-competitive, and more environmen-tally-friendly solutions to support an energy strategy built on multiple energy vectors and time and space scales.
