entityDescription:
Sanzar is a private Spanish entity founded in 2019 whose activity sector is aerospace and agro-tech, specifically oriented to the design and integration of control systems for aerospace vehicles. In space, we can provide specific control for agile satellites with high angular speeds (3-6º/s) through an innovative patented configuration. This solution will reduce the control weight of the satellite (>100%) and increase its manoeuvrability (>75%), allowing more efficient operations in manoeuvres, such as adjusting cameras and other satellite observation objects. In the case of air vehicles will enable them to operate where aircraft are currently limited, increasing manoeuvrability by more than 50% and allowing them to operate in conditions of low or no speed and short takeoffs. entityDescription:
RespiQ (Respiro B.V) is a company founded in 2019 with the aim to develop a hand held universal analyzer for chemical characterization of gases. RespiQ is now focused on the development of a breath analizer for the early detection of respiratory diseases and for the aid of chronic patients that suffer from diseases such as lung cancer, COPD and cystic fibrosis. The device developed is based on glow discharge, where the photons emitted by the breakage of the molecules are measured with a spectrometer. The spectrometer measures the intensity and wavelength of the photons and thanks to machine learning algorithms we will be able to determine the concentration and molecule or chemical identity. The molecular identity will then be related to a certain disease and a prognosis.
While the development of the breath analyzer is focused on medical applications, we are aware that the applications of the technology could every useful in space and environmental monitoring applications. The main advantage of this patented technology is the portability, sensitivity and simplicity, while keeping the costs low. Currently we have a working prototype that we are aiming to increase its sensitivity.
Recently, we have been awarded several European and local grants including a Eurostars and EIC project (4 Million Eur) to continue the development of our technology. We are aiming at developing this technology further and we are looking for a potential collaboration with ESA given the environment where this technology could be potentially used (atmospheric readings, space probes, rovers).

entityDescription: IMEL-Analitika j.d.o.o. is a company established under the law of the Republic of Croatia as a simple limited liability company for information and service activities. The company was founded on 19/07/2017 at the Trade Court in Zagreb (The decision on establishment is attached in the registration system). The main business of the company is the provision of various information and analytical data processing services (data science), especially in the segment of natural resources (agriculture, forestry, nature and environmental protection), related publishing activities and market research. The company's recent activities are focused on the tailoring and production of applications related to Earth observation (Copernicus products), exploring the needs and commercial possibilities of EO applications in the various mentioned domains. The company was primarily founded as a private spin-off, mainly with the aim of examining market opportunities and participating in smaller, freelance jobs, and was mostly not particularly active until 2023 (the owner or director is a permanently employed person in a public research organization). The company completed its first significant job and revenue in 2023. After the previous personal experience of the owner through participation in EU projects such as ESA, HORIZON 2020, INTERREG, and many other national projects in the field of Earth observation, the need to establish a spin-off company like this was recognized, where personal broad domain expertise can be efficiently linked with auxiliary information sources such as EO with an aim to produce customizable products. In this way, the approach to the market, potential stakeholders, analysis of their needs and requirements can be much more proactive and benefit-driven. The company is currently in the phase of establishing business relations with a larger number of customers, i.e., companies in Croatia (and abroad) whose activities are primarily related to the production of various environmental impacts assessments, nature protection assessments, green urban development strategies, forest and agriculture monitoring, or related activities in which there is potential for the application of products based on Earth observations.​

entityDescription:
Hydro-EO is an Earth Observation research, development, and innovation company advancing satellite-based water intelligence across the full water continuum—from drought and scarcity to floods and coastal systems. The company develops scientific and analytical capabilities to support the assessment of water availability, environmental change, and hydrological risks at regional to global scales. Its work is situated within a rapidly evolving climate context, where water systems are increasingly characterized by both intensifying extremes and longer-term shifts in availability.

Building on expertise in multi-sensor Earth Observation, Hydro-EO combines satellite observations with physics-based and AI-enabled approaches, supported by hybrid modelling, to monitor and anticipate water dynamics across land and coastal environments. The team integrates knowledge from remote sensing, hydrology, climatology, and data science to interpret changes in water systems and identify their underlying drivers.

Hydro-EO is a Portuguese subsidiary of H2O Geomatics Inc. (Canada), building on established expertise in Earth Observation, particularly in the cryosphere (ice and snow), while extending capabilities into liquid water systems.

entityDescription:
The DFMR is a Governmental Department of the Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment, with personnel of around 80 people (scientific, technical and administrative expertise). The mission of DFMR is the sustainable management and development of fisheries and aquaculture and the protection and preservation of the marine environment through an integrated scientific approach. The DFMR is the competent authority for the implementation of the Habitats Directive (92/43/EC) on the part related tothe sea, the European Marine Strategy Framework Directive (MSFD, 2008/56/EC), and the Water-Framework Directive(WFD, 2000/60/EC) for its part related to the coastal waters. It can therefore directly influence national/regional/localpolicies. Its activities include, among others: 
a) Implementation of the Habitats Directive (H.D) (92/43/EC) on the part related to the sea: In this framework,management monitoring programs are applied for the different species and habitats under the Directive (e.g.the turtle Conservation Project, Posidonia oceanica and Mediterranean monk seal Monachus monachusmonitoring program, etc.). It is noted that the Mediterranean Monk Seal and Marine Turtles are also protectedby the National Fisheries Law (CAP 135) and consolidated 1990 Fishery Regulations of DFMR.
b) Implementation of the Protocol for Specially Protected Areas and Biological Diversity in the Mediterranean ofthe Barcelona Convention, which has been ratified by the Law 20(III)/2001.
c) Establishment of marine protected areas (Natura 2000) under H.D. 92/43/EEC and SPAMI areas under the Protocol of Specially Protected Areas and Biodiversity in the Mediterranean, of the Barcelona Convention.
d) Implementation of the MSFD (2008/56/EC) in Cyprus. DFMR carries-out a comprehensive monitoring program and participates in the activities of implementation of the Directive at European level (e.g. meetings of Marine Directors, Working Groups etc).
e) Implementation of the WFD (2000/60/EC) for its part related to the coastal waters. Since 2007, in accordance with Article 8 of the WFD, the MED implements a comprehensive monitoring program for the assessment ofthe ecological [(4 Biological Quality Elements, Benthic Macroinvertebrates, Macroalgae,Phytoplankton(chlorophyll-a) and Angiosperms (Posidonia oceanica)] and chemical status of the coastal waters of Cyprus.

a) Implementation of the Habitats Directive (H.D) (92/43/EC) on the part related to the sea: In this framework,management monitoring programs are applied for the different species and habitats under the Directive (e.g.the turtle Conservation Project, Posidonia oceanica and Mediterranean monk seal Monachus monachusmonitoring program, etc.). It is noted that the Mediterranean Monk Seal and Marine Turtles are also protectedby the National Fisheries Law (CAP 135) and consolidated 1990 Fishery Regulations of DFMR.
b) Implementation of the Protocol for Specially Protected Areas and Biological Diversity in the Mediterranean ofthe Barcelona Convention, which has been ratified by the Law 20(III)/2001.
c) Establishment of marine protected areas (Natura 2000) under H.D. 92/43/EEC and SPAMI areas under the Protocol of Specially Protected Areas and Biodiversity in the Mediterranean, of the Barcelona Convention.
d) Implementation of the MSFD (2008/56/EC) in Cyprus. DFMR carries-out a comprehensive monitoring program and participates in the activities of implementation of the Directive at European level (e.g. meetings of Marine Directors, Working Groups etc).
e) Implementation of the WFD (2000/60/EC) for its part related to the coastal waters. Since 2007, in accordance with Article 8 of the WFD, the MED implements a comprehensive monitoring program for the assessment ofthe ecological [(4 Biological Quality Elements, Benthic Macroinvertebrates, Macroalgae,Phytoplankton(chlorophyll-a) and Angiosperms (Posidonia oceanica)] and chemical status of the coastal waters of Cyprus.

Mediconnect 360 is a pioneering healthcare technology company at the forefront of utilizing cutting-edge satellite data technologies, including Galileo, Copernicus, and Satcom, to transform the healthcare industry. Our mission is to revolutionize the way medical data is accessed, managed, and leveraged for the benefit of patients and healthcare providers alike.
In a rapidly evolving healthcare landscape, access to timely and accurate information is paramount. Mediconnect 360 harnesses the power of satellite data from Galileo, Europe's global navigation satellite system, and Copernicus, the European Earth Observation program, to enhance healthcare in the following ways:
- Telemedicine Reach: Leveraging Satcom technology, we extend the reach of telemedicine to remote and underserved areas. Patients can access medical consultations and diagnostic services regardless of their geographical location.

- Real-Time Patient Monitoring: Our platform integrates satellite data to enable real-time monitoring of patients' vital signs and health conditions. This ensures prompt interventions and enhances patient safety.

- Emergency Response: Mediconnect 360 utilizes satellite communication for rapid emergency response coordination, particularly in disaster-stricken regions, helping to save lives during critical situations.

- Global Health Insights: By tapping into Copernicus' Earth observation data, we provide healthcare organizations with valuable insights into environmental factors affecting public health, such as air quality, disease spread, and disaster preparedness.

- Secure Data Exchange: We prioritize data security and compliance, ensuring that all satellite-transmitted healthcare data remains confidential and adheres to healthcare regulations.

entityDescription:
IOER Leitbild 
The Leibniz Institute of Ecological Urban and Regional Development (IOER) is a non-university research centre and a member of the Leibniz Association. With the present vision and mission statement (Leitbild) we formulate strategic directions for the future development of the IOER. The Leitbild provides long-term orientations for our research and transfer activities, which are further operationalised in our research programme. It equally stipulates principles in terms of organisation, management and cooperation. The Leitbild was developed in an open co-creation process with the staff members and is updated regularly.
Our research subject
Current scientific evidence underlines the urgent need for socio-ecological transformations in spatial terms in order to achieve fundamental sustainability goals. Human activity exerts spatially differentiated pressures on the Earth system at all scales. Processes of industrialization and demographic change drive excessive local or telecoupled environmental pressures, with major regional variation in growth dynamics. This includes ecosystem destruction, species extinction, resource extraction, pollutant emissions, soil sealing or waste disposal, among others. In turn human settlements are increasingly exposed to diverse natural hazards with highly uneven geographical distributions. In this, technologies and especially digitalization play an ambivalent role since they can both reinforce and alleviate pressures and risks.
In view of these challenges we investigate the features, patterns and dynamics of socio-ecological-technological spatial configurations. Our research focuses on landscapes, the built environment, land use and economic interactions to explore and compare their development and transformation, particularly in the territorial context of urban districts, cities and agglomerations, urbanized and rural areas, as well as regions and countries - including cross-border areas. Key environmental factors we examine are the regional climate, ecosystems, biodiversity, resources and natural hazards. As corresponding physical factors of society we study technologies, materials and energy. Ultimately, our principal concern is the spatial coevolution of these factors with societal institutions, cultures and practices regarding sustainability and resilience impacts. This implies especially considering the role of different individuals and actors, their intersectionality and interactions, as well as society as a whole in co-shaping spatial developments.

entityDescription:
Transform Transport is a non-profit research foundation based in Milan (Italy) and focused on innovation in mobility and transport planning. It provides innovative, inclusive, and sustainable mobility solutions for shaping the future of society and cities worldwide in line with the UN’s SDG 11 (Sustainable cities and communities).
 
It grounds on 30 years of Systematica’s work and explores how disruptive technologies, increasingly and rapidly influencing urban mobility, can have a positive impact on cities, neighborhoods, and buildings, collaborating closely with municipalities and companies, and using Big Data for greater insights.
 
Transform Transport actively participates in lectures, talks, and hackathons in partnership with Universities, mentoring and sharing methodologies with students. It also promotes and develops research studies, disseminating them through books, publications, conferences, public talks, and events.
 
Our focus is from one side on researches and on the presentation of proposals at Italian and International levels.
 
Regarding the main strategic themes on which TT aims the research, the topics are the following:
 
1. Urban Mobility Metrics (as e.g. Wi-fi data, Carsharing data and Walklability for children)
2. Livable Street (as e.g. Milan Sidewalks Map and 15-minute City Model)
 
With reference to the proposals submitted, STEP UP – Walkability for women in Milan has been awarded by Fondazione Cariplo and it focuses on the needs and expectations of women while walking.
Transform Transport is coordinating the project for 12 months in collaboration withTeMA Lab– Università degli Studi di Napoli Federico II,Sex and the City, andWalk21 Foundation.
The project results will help identify challenging areas or neighborhoods in the city of Milan, which can serve as the analytical testbed to develop a set of policy recommendations aimed at enhancing the level of walkability for women in cities. In particular, the collected disaggregated data will be used to support the definition of guidelines and policies for the design of future transport services, focusing on the impact of individual characteristics of pedestrians in relation to their gender on the perceived level of walkability. In the event of the identification of distinct problematic areas or zones, the project outcome will also highlight potential physical interventions via tactical urbanism approaches in public spaces.

entityDescription:
Skypuzzler is a pioneering company, revolutionising the aviation industry by offering a breakthrough solution for managing drone air traffic. Our team comprises of experienced air traffic controllers and computer scientists, supported by a professional board of directors with decades of business and technical knowledge.

Imagine a puzzle in the sky, where drones need to navigate through a complex network of airspace without colliding with each other or other objects. Skypuzzler has developed advanced software that works as a Digital Air Traffic Control system specifically designed to manage drones as a module integrated into the existing digital infrastructure (Unmanned traffic Management systems). This technology allows drones to fly safely and autonomously by providing clear paths and instructions. One of the most exciting aspects of our solution is the concept of "Free Route Airspace” for drones, enabling efficient and safe flight paths, while also fostering drone business growth.

As the drone industry grows unprecedentedly, efficient and safe airspace management becomes more critical than ever. A robust Digital Air Traffic Control system is essential to harness the full potential of drones across various sectors, such as logistics, agriculture, surveillance, and even public services. This technology is the key to scaling the drone industry, ensuring seamless operations, collision avoidance, and regulation compliance. In addition, our solution indirectly contributes to the global goal of reducing CO2 emissions by making drones a preferred choice for last-mile deliveries, thus reducing the environmental impact of transportation.

entityDescription:
Cosmodity SRL is an innovative deep-tech startup developing a conceptually new technology and service, called muLINER, for long-term Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) exploiting the natural phenomenon of highly-penetrating Cosmic Rays as a stable straight-line reference.
This technology combines proprietary hardware and software with complex reconstruction algorithms to directly measure mm-level displacements at multiple points of a structure that are tens of metres apart, while maintaining this accuracy constant throughout many years.
These aspects make muLINER particularly suitable for monitoring large multi-storey buildings, bridges, viaducts, underground tunnels, etc.
 
The know-how comes from extensive research at the intersection of fundamental high-energy physics and detector R&D for hadron-therapy applications.
The commercialisation of this technology has been supported by a Technology Transfer grant from the Italian Institute of Nuclear Physics (INFN Torino) to reach TRL5, while further R&D is expected to bring this technology to TRL9 with the financial and technical support from ESA.

entityName: Luka Koper, port and logistic system, public limited company
entityDescription:
The Port of Koper is Slovenia’s only multipurpose seaport and a strategically important logistics hub for hinterland markets. Located at the northernmost point of the Adriatic Sea, the port integrates maritime, rail, and road transport services, enabling efficient cargo handling and transport operations. Owing to its favourable geographic position and strong hinterland connections, the Port of Koper serves as one of the main maritime gateways for markets of Central and Southeastern Europe. Through its economic activity, the port significantly shapes the urban and economic development of Koper and the wider Slovenian coastal region. At the same time, it plays a vital role in strengthening Slovenia’s international trade competitiveness and logistics connectivity within the European TEN-T transport network. The port is particularly recognised as an important container and automotive hub in the Adriatic region, with a strong dependence on sustainable rail transport, as more than 50% of cargo is transported by rail. 
In 2008, Luka Koper d.d. entered into a concession agreement with the Republic of Slovenia for the provision of port services, as well as for the management, development, and regular maintenance of port infrastructure within the Koper cargo port area. In accordance with the Slovenian Maritime Code, the concession was granted for a period of 35 years and covers the entire concession area of the Port of Koper.
Luka Koper d.d. operates all 12 specialised terminals within the port, each tailored to specific cargo categories and equipped with modern handling equipment and advanced port technology. Through these terminals, Luka Koper d.d. provides cargo handling, transhipment, warehousing, and value-added logistics services, ensuring comprehensive support across the supply chain. In addition to its commercial activities, Luka Koper d.d. performs two mandatory public utility services: the regular maintenance of port infrastructure intended for public transport and the collection of ship-generated waste within the port area. The company is also responsible for managing the port’s economic zone and for the continuous development of port infrastructure and suprastructure, supporting the port’s long-term competitiveness and sustainable growth.

Decent Cybersecurity Sp. z.o.o. is specialised in designing, implementing, securing and testing the highest security standard blockchain infrastructure. Applying basic types of attacks to real world cases our solution can help our customers secure: supply chain attacks, physical attacks - infrastructure tampering, computer network exploitation, cloud infrastructure multi tenancy and operation, data corruption or modification and also  software and hardware vulnerabilities.

Services offered:
Private Blockchain
- Customised Integration: Private blockchains running on DCore protocol can be flexibly customiszed for individual use cases to meet highest security and performance standards.
- Cloud Hosting or Dedicated Servers: With automated implementation, it’s possible to efficiently deploy infrastructure on AWS/Azure or dedicated infrastructure.

Blockchain & Log Security
- Proving the Integrity and Authenticity of Log Files: Log files are a means to precisely govern all activities in an IT-heavy business. Logs can, however, be manipulated with, if not protected appropriately. Blockchain makes sure your infrastructure logs are free from manipulation and exploits.
-Proving the Integrity of Configuration Files: Using a decentralised system is a guarantee for your configuration files to stay exploit-free inside your infrastructure

Blockchain& IoT
-Top-Notch Security for IoT Devices: Considering the interrelated manner of IoT devices, employing superior security standards is not only essential but critical. By integrating blockchain technology, the number of attacks on IoT devices can be reduced to negligible amounts
-Protecting Smart Homes: In today’s world of what seems to be an uprising of “smart” systems, building a smart home has become easier than ever before—there is a catch, however: privacy compromises. Blockchain offers a solution to interconnect all devices efficiently and in the most secure way possible

Blockchain & SCADA
-SCADA Security: Rogue attacks that can interfere with and alter communication between two parties, known as man-in-the-middle attacks (MITM), can cause devastating damage in critical infrastructure. Blockchain’s advanced security measures can make sure such outcome is easily prevented
- An Extra Layer of Security: With its intrinsic security-focused nature, blockchain can be implemented to existing infrastructures as an additional security layer.
- Hardware & Software Fusion: Our solutions easily combine software and hardware integrations toward absolute efficiency and security.

entityDescription:
Super Garden is freeze dried food production company which focuses on a special food preservation method - lyophilization. With competitive RnD department Super Garden have created 3D printer which is capable to print vegetable and other mixtures. 

Company it self was born out of... practicality. When you have a craving for something delicious. When you want the sort of food that everyone would love and be excited about. When you want to avoid calorie-dense foods and products that can throw your daily recommended sugar intake off the charts. We wanted something that would take you back to the warm, sunny embrace of summer.
One sunny Saturday morning, Laura, the founder of Super Garden, was having a familybreakfast with her children. She noticed that her children went straight for the freeze-driedberries in their cereal bowls and ate them first. “These berries could make a perfectreplacement for sweet sugary foods,” Laura thought to herself, and started searching for freeze-dried snacks that she could buy. But she was unable to find any. While doing her research, she kept discovering more and more about the benefits of such type of products.She learned that freeze-dried foods are natural, they retain their nutrients, have a long shelf life and are very light-weight so you can carry them anywhere. Passion for this type of products inspired her to set up a company. And that’s how Super Garden was born.

entityDescription:
DRASS GALEAZZI
With over a century of uninterrupted business, DRASS Galeazzi is recognized as one of the founders of Italy’s rich history of subsea innovation. 
During naval trials in 1930, the Galeazzi atmospheric diving suit broke world records for the deepest descents ever reached, to a staggering depth of 300 msw, with worldwide demand for many decades. 
DRASS’ state-of-the-art range of diving helmets and personal diving equipment remain popular to this day.
With a tradition of defence products dating back to World War II, DRASS continue to supply navies with state-of-the-art midget submarines, swimmer delivery vehicles, submarine rescue solutions: submarine rescue vessels and equipment as well as submarine training and lockout solutions.
DRASS is the leading supplier of diving systems worldwide, having designed and manufactured the majority of certified diving systems built since 1967. Commercial diving solutions cover saturation diving systems and equipment, hydraulic LARS (launch & recovery systems), surface diving systems, personal diver equipment and diving components.
A fierce proponent of hyperbaric therapy since the 1950s, DRASS solutions continue to include cutting-edge hyperbaric chambers for oxygen therapy, hyperbaric chambers for tunnel boring machines, environmental control systems for confined/controlled areas, hyperbaric wet and dry simulators for commercial and defence sectors.
DRASS is a complete production facility able to develop in-house advanced welding activities, skidding for hydraulic gas and water systems, PLC control and gas management systems, and electrical panels. Its facilities also support modular deliveries, including containerization and mobilization for onshore/offshore commissioning.
Leaders in innovative, safe and cost-efficient systems and equipment in compliance with the highest industry standards, DRASS values personal and professional growth of its people in an eco-friendly harmonious working environment, and builds long-term trusted relationships with its business partners.

entityName: Fundación Centro de Estudios Ambientales del Mediterráneo
entityDescription:
The Mediterranean Center for Environmental Studies (CEAM) is a centre of research, development and technological innovation to improve the natural environment in the Mediterranean.
Our activity centres on offering comprehensive proposals for environmental management in the domain of the atmosphere, ecosystems, human activities and their interactions. This requires the participation of multidisciplinary teams who have accurate knowledge to describe and understand natural processes and those amended by human activities for the purpose of developing and offering sustainable management options that adapt to Mediterranean conditions.
Our scientific and technical team includes experts in meteorology and climate, atmospheric chemistry and atmospheric pollutants dynamics, numerical simulation, high-precision analytical instruments for laboratory and field use, the carbon cycle, ecosystems dynamics, fire ecology and forest restoration.
During more than 25 years of research, this team has applied its knowledge and experiences to forecast extreme meteorological events (heat waves, torrential rain), to mitigate and adapt to climate change, to prevent forest fires and to recover burnt or desertified mountains, and to analyse and assess atmospheric pollution in urban, rural and industrial environments, and its impacts. We have carried out these activities directly or in collaboration with leading international environmental research centres and we have applied them throughout the Mediterranean
Such activity is performed through research projects, which are included in five research areas:
· METEOROLOGY AND CLIMATOLOGY
· POLLUTANT DYNAMICS
· ATMOSPHERIC CHEMISTRY
· AIR POLLUTANT EFFECTS AND THE CARBON CYCLE
· FOREST RESEARCH
CEAM’s activities range from basic research, into finding solutions for priority environmental problems, to the development of new technologies and applications, which are set up as pilot projects where the advances made on the management scale are demonstrated. Basically, therefore, these activities are of the essentially pre-competitive R&D kind.
R&D activity also leads to scientific counselling tasks in the themes that CEAM’s competences cover, and it specifically contributes to environmental management policymaking at various levels, from the local level to that of the European Union.

description: Founded in 2020, GyroPlant is an R&D-led company that is tackling the problems of single-use substrates in indoor farming. Although indoor farming can help provide food efficiently, if current substrate practices continue, farms will produce a vast amount of emissions and waste, as well as generate quality and cost issues. GyroPlant is an R&D-led company which aims to make indoor farming more accessible, sustainable, and resilient by eliminating single-use substrates. Description of product or service: Taking a first principles approach to indoor farming, GyroPlant undertook 18 months of R&D with leading vertical farms, leading to the launch of GyroCup in early 2023. GyroCup is a reusable growing superstructure which brings a circular economy approach to indoor farming. As an alternative to conventional substrates, it eliminates the reliance on single-use, costly and inefficient conventional substrates in the industry, while also enhancing crop growth and quality. Our system is integrated into 125+ global growing systems for R&D. GyroCup serves as a versatile physical platform for growing various crops, including leafy greens and strawberries, as well as supporting plant breeding across a diverse range of indoor growing systems, including space technology applications.

entityDescription:
With the rising number of satellite launches and impending regulations on space debris, there's a critical need for in-space servicing solutions. Existing options rely on costly, imprecise control from Earth, pricing out 90% of the satellite market.

SPAICE is applying generative AI and deep learning to enable the first end-to-end autonomous approach for in-orbit services. Their software tools to perform navigation and robotic services are ready to integrate off-the-shelf, enhancing existing satellites’ capabilities.

They developed the largest photorealistic dataset of orbiting assets, encoding space material properties to provide robust simulation-to-real transfer. Learning perception features and control policies directly from data patterns, their systems generalize to multiple missions, being agnostic to targets and hardware configurations.

Founded by a top technical team from renowned institutions like Imperial College London, ETH Zurich, Oxford, and Stanford, SPAICE is validating their technology with PoCs with the best European players including Leonardo and Thales Alenia Space, with more awaiting inthepipeline.

entityDescription:
AIRBORNE ROBOTICS is a leading developer of professional drones with offices in the UK, in Germany and in Austria. Our high performance systems are sold worldwide and used for manual and automated flights mounted with sensors for:
- Agriculture and forestry;
- Measuring, mapping, surveying and mining;
- Inspection and documentation of buildings, construction sites, critical infrastructure and power assets;
- Surveillance and search & rescue (SAR);
- Photography, film and movies;
- Industrial applications & automation; and
- Research.
IMPACT & MEANINGFUL RESULTS
We manufacture probably the greenest means of payload transportation in the world. Our drones are equipped with the newest generation of efficient batteries, similar to electric cars, with enhanced duration and extended charging cycles (up to 1,000x). We supply companies that strive to run their operations responsibly –sustainable & energy efficient, workflow-optimized and FUTURE ORIENTED.Our customers fly drones not to congest the airspace but to conduct meaningful work with meaningful sensors.
What impact does your business make? Drones are only a small part of it but a great start.
EYE IN THE SKY
Enhance your ground-based workflows and procedures through aerial information for inspection, analysis and documentation. Collect meaningful data with professional sensors. In order to fully exploit the potential of aerial imagery for site overview, zone mapping, 3D photogrammetry or inspection of critical assetsmount the highest quality camera you can afford.Increasing the resolution of an image decreases its ground sampling distance (GSD) and thereby increases the accuracy of the map or the 3D model. We recommend ordering a 24.3-megapixel camera or higher for drone mapping and surveys. Thermal inspection of buildings, power lines, pipelines, infrastructure or other critical assets is only meaningful with highest quality cameras.
TECHNOLOGY & INNOVATION
Based on long-term experience in manufacturing professional drones we have optimized manufacturing processes and results to arrive where we stand today. Our AIR8 drone is the ultimate technology bundle and the “power package” in the airspace reserved for UAV traffic: Laserscanning / LiDAR images are made accessible – environmentally & cost efficient – and can be performed for small and large projects. Multiple sensors can be mounted and deployed at one and the same flight.
Our customers win tenders and mandates because they can convince through our state-of-the-art UAV equipment, in particular through:
- REDUNDANCY (enhanced fail-safety from two electronic circuits; essential for Operating Safety Case)
- PERFORMANCE (payload, flight time, power reserve, stability)
- OPEN PLATFORM (ability to mount any sensor or payload)
- CUSTOMIZATIONS (systems tailored to your specifications)

who we are
A small core crew of AI and Web veterans with connections. We approach our projects like a Miles Davis band, valuing competence, a good sense of humor, originality and collaboration.
Leave the AI hype on the doorstep, we make real applications that work. We run a reality-check on the toughest challenges, and if we decide to take on it, it means we are certain to succeed.
what we do
We build high end production software that embeds the latest AI advances with rigor and creativity. Our software runs on the premises of very large corporations and startups alike.
We integrate and build AI for real-world applications. We're experts in Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Reinforcement Learning, Stochastic Optimization, Search Engines, P2P systems and more.
We make beautiful applications out of maths: Data Visualization and Exploration through Web technologies, Big data exploration with VR, embedded hardware and installations.
The industries that trust us are eclectic because AI is pervasive. They range from large cybersecurity players to top art institutions, AI hardware startups and manufacturers, aerospace leaders and machine learning startups around the globe.
open source
Our experience is clear: bullet-proof software is Open Source. We like creating, contributing, learning and sharing. Most of our work is publicly available and Open Source.

description:
Sylatech's passive microwave, waveguide assembly, component, slotted array antenna and investment casting capabilities continue to support the Space sector and strengthen its Space heritage. AS9100 QMS underpins the Company's design, manufacturing and quality controls. We provide a comprehensive manufacturing capability including Nadcap accreditation. Our dedicated engineering team generates waveguide assembly designs using the latest engineering tools (CST / Solidworks) and our manufacturing process employs a number of braze, assembly, finishing and verification / metrology techniques. 
Sylatech is privately owned UK SME company. Established in 1964, employing 140 people and with an annual sales turnover ~£10 million. 
Sylatech is undergoing a major 3-year Business Transformation Programme (BTP) with the aim to grow our revenue and profitability; build stronger customer relationships; strive for operational excellence; become an employer of choice and expand our process capability. To help this along, we are developing our culture to have fun and enjoy work, create high value jobs locally and attract talent, developing technical engineering and sales skills, and focus on recruitment and retention. Our targeted investments will be aligned to respond to market needs and support our technology roadmap. Typical investments include de-risking our dip-braze requirements, extending Nadcap accreditation and providing additional manufacturing capacity and factory upgrades. 
The Company is a supplier to Airbus, Thales Alenia Space and OHB. The latest Space project is supplying slotted waveguide antennas to Thales Alenia Space Italy for the Platino satellite. Other projects include the supply of cast waveguide bends to Cobham USA for use on the One Web project; 5 channel multiplexers to Elisra of Israel, diplexers to OHB; INET/ONET Components for Eutelsat (Airbus) and in addition, various power combiners and waveguide antennas to Airbus UK.

entityName: FTMC - Department of Chemical Engineering and Technology
entityDescription:
The department carries out researches of decontamination processes of hazardous chemical waste (mainly aqueous solutions) using modern methods and equipment in order to utilize or regenerate valuable chemical substances. For many years, the research-based technologies are used successfully in economic – commercial activities of the FTMC decontamination of hazardous chemical waste bar, providing services to the country‘s industrial plants.
For many years, researches of water and industrial wastewater treatment processes are carried out successfully using the following sorbents: modified activated carbons, zero-valent irons, nano-sorbents, synthetic and natural (chitosan) sorbents and iron oxides/hydroxides nanoparticles prepared using iron wastes from drinking water treatment plants.
An important scientific research trend is a development of environmentally friendly technological processes. It includes a development of plastic chrome - free metallization technologies applying different than usual methods of plastic activation and etching against chemical metallization. The results of these researches were successfully commercialized in Germany and the USA.
The department has a laboratory of chemical coatings that provides services for economic entities, forming coatings with aluminium anodic layer with special properties.
The department consist of following laboratories: Tribology Laboratory; Electrochemical Energy Conversion Laboratory; Crystal Growth Laboratory; Bioelectrochemical Technologies Laboratory; Hazardous Waste Detoxification Laboratory.

CORAmaps GmbH is a company founded in December 2019 out of the Technical University of Darmstadt. The current technology is based on research in the field of earth observation and the processing of large amounts of data (big data), which has been continuously pursued since 2008. CORAmaps has its own hardware infrastructure for fast and targeted processing of all earth observation and geodata, so that all processes are carried out in-house.
The team has extensive expertise in the fields of remote sensing, machine learning, imaging radar, geodesy and agricultural and environmental sciences. 
CORAmaps is an independent and research-driven company that finances the development of a wide range of products and services through public research funding and its own sales.
In addition to applications in the field of spatial analysis using satellite data, we are also active in the provision and use of geodatabases and the development of server infrastructures. 
We are convinced that the ki-based interpretation of satellite-based radar data is the key technology for providing up-to-date information on the state of land cover anywhere in the world.

entityDescription: Ternow’s mission is to create a near real-time HD digital twin of the Earth from space. Accurate maps are valuable across use cases, but they’re expensive and lack real-time updates. Terrestrial vehicles generate maps that are precise but costly and delayed. Satellite images are cost-effective but lack accuracy and timeliness. By harnessing the power of existing satellite imagery and soon our CubeSats, we will map the Earth down to a resolution of 5cm. We create our global 3D HD maps with remote sensing, computer vision, and AI at low costs and hourly update rates using a new class SAR-Optical cube satellite. Thereby, we enable use cases across industries, from autonomous driving to navigation, insurance, disaster management, construction and infrastructure.

entityDescription:
Seilio Douar is a specialized company that offers a range of geospatial and algorithmic mapping services, making it a valuable partner for the European Space Agency (ESA). They excel in the following key areas:
- Algorithmic Design: Seilio Douar creates custom algorithms tailored to specific needs, including data processing, pattern recognition, and geospatial modeling. Their expertise in cartographic algorithms and geospatial analysis ensures optimized results.

- GIS Analysis: The company leverages GIS source code for comprehensive spatial analysis. They excel in large data analysis, deep learning, and spatiotemporal fusion, providing valuable insights for various applications, including agriculture, environmental analysis, and more.

- OpenGeo Hardware & Software Integration: Seilio Douar integrates open-source hardware and software to offer holistic geospatial solutions. From data collection with open-source microcontrollers and sensors to visualization with open-source GIS software, they emphasize customization and efficiency.

Their previous works include projects such as precision farming autopilots, SMS alert systems for weather monitoring, salinity-sodicity modeling, coastal zone erosion assessment, historical land use change analysis, lava flow identification, and contributions to open-source GIS development.
Seilio Douar's commitment to open technologies, customization, and efficiency makes them a valuable partner for ESA, as they can contribute to a wide range of geospatial and algorithmic mapping needs, providing innovative solutions that align with ESA's objectives and projects.

entityDescription:
The Institute for Applied Informatics (InfAI) e.V. has existed as a registered non-profit association since 2006. The InfAI‘s main areas of expertise and activity are aimed at promoting science and research in the fields of computer science and business informatics as well as knowledge transfer with the goal of developing and making usable ICT-supported software products based on innovative research results.
The Institute has been a recognised affiliated institute of the University of Leipzig since 2008 and has since developed into one of the largest and most third-funded research institutes at the University of Leipzig. The institute‘s more than 160 employees work with renowned participants from science (e.g. ScaDS.AI, German Research Centre for Artificial Intelligence, Helmholtz Centres, Fraunhofer Institutes, Leibniz Institutes, Max-Planck-Institutes), international universities and companies from practice (Siemens, Daimler, BMW, SAP, T-Systems, Heidelberger Druckmaschinen AG, Software AG, ERGO Group, Mercateo) on national and international research and industry projects. The InfAI contributes the expertise of numerous competence centres and associated professorships. This includes both technology and computer science-related topics (AI, Big Data, IoT, sensor connection, semantic, linked data, language technology, enterprise systems) as well as technical and methodological focal points (structured problem solving, process design). The InfAI also covers a wide range of topics from the application domains: From agriculture, logistics and mobility to energy, smart living, health, smart city and production to higher education / training and knowledge management.
Furthermore, the InfAI regularly organises meetings, workshops, symposia and conferences to strengthen the exchange between excellent researchers and between science and industry. Currently, these events include, for example, the „SEMANTiCS“, the „Leipzig Semantic Web Day“, the „AI Hub Saxony“ and the workshop series „Big Data and AI in Business“. As a business-oriented research and transfer institute, InfAI is an innovation driver for solutions based on current ICT technologies for the Leipzig region, for Saxony and beyond.

entityDescription: Egide designs, manufactures, and sells hermetic packages to protect and interconnect several kinds of electronic or photonic chips. The purpose of these packages is to protect integrated electronic systems or complex, and therefore fragile, chips, which are sensitive to harsh thermal, atmospheric, or magnetic environments. These components are the result of a complex expertise, drawing upon several disciplines: material structure, particularly special alloys; chemistry and surface treatment; mechanics and thermodynamics, electronics; optoelectronics, and hyper frequency modeling. Egide is one of the few companies to master the ensemble of technologies surrounding the two types of material used for these packages in the world today; glass-to-metal and ceramics. The company manufactures its own ceramics and, thanks to its English and American subsidiaries, produces its molded metallic components and glass beads internally.

entityName: Institute for Housing and Urban Development Studies (IHS)
entityDescription:
The Institute for Housing and Urban Development Studies, Rotterdam, the Netherlands 
Introduction 
The Institute for Housing and Urban Development Studies (IHS) is the international institute for urban management of Erasmus University Rotterdam working in developing and transitional countries. It offers specialized post graduate training, advisory services and applied research in the fields of urban management, housing and urban environment. IHS and its staff are committed to co-creating and sharing cutting-edge knowledge with urban professionals from across the globe to transform urban practice to make cities work. This work will also support the New Urban Agenda and contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals, which provides a frame of reference for all our projects. IHS was established in 1958, and joined the Erasmus University Rotterdam as an independent institute in 2004. This unique status allows the institute to draw on the extensive academic and institutional resources of the University whilst remaining dynamic, enabling effective innovation and quick responses to clients’ needs and changes in cities. Its mission is to develop the human and institutional capacities necessary to reduce poverty and improve the quality of life in cities worldwide. The institute works closely with local governments, international and local non-governmental organizations and the private sector worldwide, mainly in Asia, Latin America, Central and Eastern Europe, and Africa. Its mission is to develop human and institutional capacities and provide support to policy makers to reduce poverty and improve the quality of life in cities worldwide.

AVL is the world’s largest independent company for the development, simulation and testing technology of passenger cars, trucks, and large engine powertrains (hybrid, combustion engines, transmission, electric drive, batteries, and software). Moreover, for more than ten years AVL has been supporting a variety of vehicle manufacturers in the series development of safe and reliable driver assistance functions (ADAS/AD) that exactly meet the complex requirements and high standards of OEMs in every phase of vehicle development. 

To this end, AVL Hungary, a cutting-edge research-development centre drawing on over a century of Hungarian automotive expertise and the innovation of the global AVL Group, has partnered with the modern and unique vehicle testing and development facility ZalaZONE. This new partnership, AVL ZalaZONE Proving Ground Ltd., has been in operation since November 1st, 2019. 

Specifically, our scope of activities includes the proving ground’s promotion, marketing, and business development, all in combination with products and services necessary for delivering the optimum test conditions and environment for your organization, whether you be an OEM, Tier 1, SME, or Engineering Services Provider. 

Our business directive is focusing on you, by combining the required infrastructure which is in-line with the needs of the global automotive market, together with our professional industry-specific management experience and significant developmental engineering competencies. These competencies involve generic module-based software and control environments to cover all levels of automation, allowing for flexible solutions regarding components and systems of different suppliers, with results ranging from feasibility studies and the development of progressive algorithms/simulations up to concept demonstrations in vehicles.

entityDescription:
Neurobus is a new start-up that aims to bring neuromorphic perception and processing into space. It specializes in AI-powered data processing and spiking neural network training using neuromorphic processors for satellite communication on the edge. It contains all relevant experience between industry experience in space and defense, previous start-up experience, and deep knowledge and expertise in neuromorphic hardware and algorithms. In particular:

Florian Corgnou is a multi-time entrepreneur, having gained experience at the European headquarters of Tesla before co-founding Trezy, a fintech startup that has raised $4 million in funding and currently employs 12 people. He holds an MBA and MSc in International Business, as well as pursuing an MSc in Executive Innovation & Entrepreneurship fromHEC. In addition, Florian completed a 6-month Space Entrepreneurship program in partnership with Airbus DS.
Jerome Gilleron is a SUPAERO and Georgia Tech graduate, with an MS AE in 2016. He co-founded Space Eternity, an orbital data center, in 2018, and served as CEO until 2019. From 2019 to 2022, Jerome worked as an advanced system engineer at Airbus Defense and space. Currently, he is serving as the Deeptech startup accelerator program director at Starburst.
Dr. Gregor Lenz is a neuromorphic engineering Ph.D. graduate from Sorbonne University who specializes in event-based sensors and spiking neural networks. With a passion for developing open-source software for spike-based machine learning, he is currently working as a Neuromorphic Machine Learning Engineer at SynSense in Zurich, Switzerland.
Dr. Simeon Bamford is a highly experienced neuromorphic engineer with a proven track record of success in both academia and industry. With previous start-up experience at Inilabs AG and Inivation AG in Switzerland, Dr. Bamford has a deep understanding of the neuromorphic hardware, algorithms, and applications space. His expertise in the field has enabled him to design and develop cutting-edge technologies that mimic the functionality of biological systems, paving the way for new advances in artificial intelligence and machine learning.

entityDescription:
The Secretariat for Catholic Education supports over fifty Catholic Church schools in Malta and Gozo. Church schools cater for about one-third of the student population and provide education at kindergarten, primary, secondary and sixth-form levels.
The Secretariat falls under the jurisdiction of the Maltese Episcopal Conference. The Secretariat is also answerable to the Conference of Major Maltese Superiors and works closely with the Church Schools Association.
The main offices of the Secretariat are located very close to the Archbishop’s Curia in Floriana. The Secretariat has recently added more offices in Balzan.
The Secretariat serves as an important link to the Education Department at the Ministry for Education and Sports and the Malta Union of Teachers and other educational stakeholders.
The Secretariat provides provides administrative, curricular and psycho-social support to Church schools. The Secretariat administers the admission process into Church schools at Year 1 Kindergarten, Year 2 Kindergarten, Year 1 primary, Form 1/Year 7 secondary and when necessary at Year 4.
The Secretariat is also a member of the:
- OIEC (Catholic International Education Office)
- ECCE (European Committee for Catholic Education)
His Grace the Archbishop of Malta appoints a Delegate for Catholic Education who is responsible for the overall running of the Secretariat. Rev Dr Charles Mallia holds this office and is supported by Dr Ian Mifsud, as Director General. Directors and Assistant Directors sustain the work of the Delegate and Director by managing the various services provided by the Secretariat in schools:

The Secretariat employs over one hundred professionals ranging from administrative staff, psycho-social professionals and curricular specialists. These include:
- Head of departments of various subjects who support teachers and provide them with short courses.
- Administrative staff.
- Counsellors who visit schools to support students overcome their difficulties.
- Social Workers who help students and parents with the social requirements.
- Service managers for various services.
- Career Advisors.
- Youth Workers.
- Educational Psychologist who assess the educational requirements.
- Inclusive Educations Coordinators.
- Coordinators who are responsible for the inclusive education which involves in assessing children`s needs, as well as assisting children with special needs.
- Literacy Support Teachers who are responsible for the programmes such asLet me Learnand theMalta Writing Programme; Programmes targeted to improve teacher`s teaching abilities.

entityDescription:
More than 8,000 tons of space debris endanger all space activities. Satellite operators pay more than 14 million euro a year for evasive maneuvers and 1 billion USD in insurance premiums. Orbit Recycling is changing this. Space debris is transported from the orbit to the Moon and recycled there. More than 150 tons of aluminium can be regained from Ariane 5 upper stages alone. Large parts of the lunar station can be built with it, e.g., walls, power lines or heat storage systems. Since the debris is picked up in orbit, small propulsion units are sufficient for the transport to the moon, which are to launch cost-effectively with European rockets. This saves more than 50 billion euro in transportation costs.
Orbit Recycling is a Berlin based NewSpace organization which works with several universities and industry partners on proving the feasibility of this space debris recycling concept.

entityDescription:
Fields at Work GmbH was founded in April 2014 as a spin-off company of ETH Zurich. We are dedicated to provide expertise in engineering electromagnetics for applications in Health Research, Life Science and general engineering, i.e. monitoring of everyday electromagnetic fields and electromagnetics and optics for application in diagnosis and therapy. Our expertise is based on research and development carried out by the "Electromagnetics in Medicine and Biology Group" at the former Laboratory of Electromagnetic Fields and Microwave Electronics (now Institute of Electromagnetic Fields) of ETH. The first product arising out of our research collaborations was a first version of a portable radiofrequency exposure meter that was used within several European epidemiological studies on potential health effects of electromagnetic fields. Since then the devices of the ExpoM platform are gaining popularity worldwide and are used by Universities, Environmental Agencies and Industry.
The company has three activity branches, own product development and sales, contract development and research projects. The own products include two measurement device and components to integrate the measurement devices into an IoT platform. This also includes the entire backbone architecture. Examples of contract development can be found on our webpage. Currently we are involved in the EU project ETAIN (https://www.etainproject.eu/) where we provide experimental setups and a smartphone based data collection infrastructure together with our extensive expertise in exposure assessment and experimental studies on potential influences of RF-EMF on biological organsims and the environment.

entityDescription:
COMPANY
Alpha Impulsion was founded in 2022 and is 12 people strong as of 2025 in Toulouse, with 3 additional collaborators in the Torino subsidiary. The founding element is a patent on hybrid autophage propulsion, a rocket propulsion technology applicable to launchers, in-space thrusters and missiles. The architecture proposes to use a solid fuel to as the launcher's fuselage and tank for its liquid oxidiser, and to burn this propellant rod like a candle. This disruptive technology removes the need for tanks, which, for instance, represent half the dry mass of a launcher, enabling a single-stage-to-orbit (SSTO) trajectory. Similar benefits are found in other applications. The mass reduction and overall reduction in parts number allows significant savings in manufacturing and logistics.

COMMERCIAL AIM
The company aims to commercialize several products and services ased on the autophage technology:
- OPAL, a versatile, storable in-space chemical propulsion subsystem for high thrust, high ΔV needs using H2O2. The pre-design for the Shakthisat mission (https://www.shakthisat.org/) with a non-clustered OPAL of circa 200kg shows an improvement of 40% in spacecraft payload capacity for a moon mission propelled by autophage propulsion from LEO. This also leads to savings at launch. 
- GRENAT, a launch service for satellites with the lowest environmental footprint. Pre-design shows that the launch event uses circa 40% less propellant mass than competing technologies (Gros et al., 2023, https://hal.science/hal-04704331). The launch service is dedicated to smallsats with a target capacity of 1000kg (SSO 500km), as opposed to rideshare, and is able to compete on price due to the simplification in manufacturing and logistics brought by the SSTO architecture and miniaturisation. This will allow this European launcher to compete with advantages against the American leader that currently dominates the European smallsat launch market. Reusing the launcher is not necessary for these goals, and represents an improvement.

R&D STAGE
From 2023 to 2025, the company developed AMBRE, the first hybrid autophage propulsion demonstrator, and ran several test campaign with progressive subsystems integration. In 2024, the combustion chamber was fired and the fuselage feeding system was developed. In 2025, TRL3 was validated with the largest autophage engine ever fired, demonstrating the functions of inserting the fuselage with its liquid oxidant into the combustion chamber and burning them, with modest funding. Alpha Impulsion aims to achieve the technological breakthroughwith with an increasing number of European partners. Next steps include engineering models in the development of OPAL, and scaling up the engine prototype for the launcher roadmap with the University of Glasgow, the leading academic actor in autophage combustion, and other key partners in structural mechanics and GNC.

entityDescription:
ACTeon is a human size research and consultancy that supports ecological and climate transitions in Europe. ACTeon works in a wide range of policy domains, addressing sustainability and resilience related to freshwater, marine ecosystems, coastal management, biodiversity or transversal climate change adaptation issues. ACTeon is involved in projects and initiatives from the local to the European (e.g. European Commission, European Environment Agency, WWF European Policy Office...) and international levels (OECD, United Nations...), mobilising human science knowledge and tools for investigating social and economic issues, carrying out policy evaluation, supporting forward looking processes, analysing governance and institutions, or supporting stakeholder processes and communication. Overall, ACTeon has strong expertise in awareness raising, capacity building and communication to a diversity of target groups, and in the facilitation of stakeholder processes at all scales bringing together a diversity of views and opinions. 
ACTeon works in particular on maritime and marine issues with expertise and experiences related to: (a) social and economic assessments (e.g. social challenges related to marine policy implementation valuation of services provided by marine ecosystems, growth and employment impacts of Blue economy sectors, costs and benefits of the MSFD…); (b) the upscaling of innovations (e.g. nature-based solutions, bioeconomy, the role of algae to address climate change challenges, multi-use platforms at sea); (c) ocean literacy and drivers to behaviour change (e.g. coordination of EU4Ocean coalition for strengthening ocean literacy). (d) (a) EU policy, strategies and management (e.g. the EU Marine Strategy Framework Directive, Maritime Spatial Planning, Integrated Coastal Zone Management, Sustainable Blue Economy…); (e) governance (regional sea basin and international Ocean Governance scales) including the “blue” science-policy-society interface and how knowledge effectively support policy making and implementation;

entityDescription:
Solver Unio Kft. was founded in 2005 with the aim of providing engineering expert services in the field of technical sciences - mainly production management, risk management, logistics optimization and quality management - to large companies operating in the field of energy and the mechanical industry (mainly the vehicle industry), or for medium and small businesses operating in their supplier network.

The coordination of R+D processes soon took on an increasingly central role in our assignments, so from 2010 the activities of Solver Unio Kft. were concentrated on research and development activities. In our current assignments in the field of R+D+I, we play an interface role between actors in science and economy.
In the last two or three decades, the world of scientific research has changed more than in the previous three centuries. Scientific discoveries not only radically reshape our world view of the macro- and microcosm, but thanks to the applied research results, they become more and more integrated into everyday life, causing changes at the social level. Even small research projects have now grown into complex enterprises requiring significant financial and intellectual capacity, which can typically only be realized in the framework of cooperation involving several scientific fields, so our company also has excellent research-collaborative partnerships with domestic and international business and research institute partners, from which a number of business relationships that are still active today.
The ability to dynamically adapt to the changing environment and the stability of our values, which have been consistently maintained since our establishment 15 years ago, are present in our assignments. Solver Unio Fejlzéstési Tanácsadó Kft. has increased its sales by about four times in recent years, and is constantly developing its human resources, IT and measurement technology background necessary for its engineering services and research activities.

entityDescription:
The Malta Business Bureau represents the Malta Chamber of Commerce, Enterprise and Industry and the Malta Hotels and Restaurants Association (MHRA) in Brussels and Malta. It does so by liaising directly with the European institutions, the Maltese Permanent Representation and with umbrella organisations such as BusinessEurope, EUROCHAMBRES and HOTREC on all policy and funding issues affecting Maltese business interests.
The MBB is currently composed of two offices, the Head Office in Malta and a Representation Office in Brussels, the operations of which are overseen by MBB Chief Executive Officer, Joe Tanti.
One of the main tasks of the organisation is to provide information to the Maltese business community with regards to EU policy and legislation related to their operations, while also keep them up to date in the sphere of EU funding for business.The MBB also has vast experience in EU funding projects which bring together the EU vision and the interests of the Maltese business community. In addition, the MBB has experience in the field of business support, especially through its Enterprise Europe Network (EEN) service-provision.
In Brussels, the organisation plays a key role in continuing to develop and strengthen the organisation’s ties with its Pan-European networks and European partners. The MBB’s technical experts make it possible for the organisation to thrive in its EU advocacy and policy work, continue following business-related EU policies and also make it possible to target legislative lobbying in Brussels with European legislators, allowing MBB to play an active role in the EU’s legislative process.

entityDescription:
Ambjent Malta background
Setup in 2018 Ambjent Malta Department (AM) is responsible for the preservation and enhancement of Malta’s natural capital and biodiversity in rural, urban, coastal and marine landscapes. AM is responsible for implementing green infrastructure projects and habitat restoration measures for maintaining and restoring natural areas and protected sites, including zones forming part of the Natura 2000 network.
Since its inception, together with other public entities and non-governmental organisations with a vested interested in Malta’s natural capital, AM implemented numerous environmental projects including installation of green walls in urban areas, removal of invasive and non-native plants, planting of over 60,000 indigenous species all over the Islands, landscaping projects, and management of protected areas.AM is also implementing schemes to increase Malta’s tree cover and promote environmental awareness including the 34U sponsorship scheme and planting of an indigenous tree or shrub for every birth.Ambjent Malta raison d'être- Protect and enhance Malta’s natural capital
- Conserve and ameliorate Malta’s biodiversity
- Improve ecosystem functioning and provision of services vital for society’s well-being
- Implement plans, policies and programmes of theEnvironment and Resources Authority (ERA)
- Manage protected areas includingterrestrialandmarine ​Natura 2000 sites
- Provide green recreational facilities to the general public
- Disseminate environmental awareness

​
What is natural capital, biodiversity, and ecosystem services?Natural Capital

All the natural assets that make up the Maltese Islands including its abiotic (non-living) features such as geology, soil, air, water and biotic (living) such as flora and faunaBiodiversity

Biological diversity referring to the variety of living things at all its levels, including genes and ecosystems, encompassing the evolutionary, ecological and cultural processes that sustain life on EarthEcosystem Services

Ecosystem services are any benefits that wildlife or ecosystems provide to humans. The Millenium Ecosystem Assessment (2005) identified four major categories: provisioning; regulating; cultural and supporting services

description:
The first GHGSat satellite was launched in 2016 as a demo that measured surface-level methane emission plumes with high spatial resolution. Fast forward to 2023, GHGSat operates the largest constellation of methane detecting satellites at high resolution (12 by end of 2023). 
The patented instrument is a wide-angle fixed-cavity Fabry–Pérot (F–P) imaging spectrometer able to resolve methane (CH4) absorption lines in the shortwave infrared (SWIR), where water (H2O) and carbon dioxide (CO2) absorption lines are also present. GHGSat satellites are Polar, sun-synchronous, with local times at des. node between 09:00h and 14:00h, at an altitude of ~500km.
 The distinguishing features of GHGSat satellites are its combination of high spatial resolution (25 m), fine spectral resolution (~ 0.1 nm) and compact package. To this day the GHGSat satellites remain the only greenhouse gas sensing satellites with such characteristics. This combination enables unique capabilities for imaging and quantifying emission plumes with unambiguous attribution at facility scale, with a industry leading detection threshold of ~100kg/h.
At company level, GHGSat counts +110 employees, with a team of +12 scientist working full-time in advancing the science of remote sensing of methane beyond the state-of-the-art, having been successful in R&D projects with renowned institutions such as CSA, ESA, NASA, Stanford and SRON. GHGSat data is part of ESA TPM program from 2021, and NASA's CSDA from 2023.

entityDescription:
The SEI Incubator was established in 2020 in Avellino as an innovation hub in Italy's rural areas. SEI was born thanks to a group of young professionals and entrepreneurs who shared the goal of revitalizing rural regions by nurturing entrepreneurial ideas, with a focus on sustainability, ethics, and innovation. SEI provides support and training to all young entrepreneurs that want to create a startup, offering them a physical space to work on their ideas independently and without constraints. SEI also offers consulting and training services to SMEs, assisting them in bringing innovation to their ecosystem through open innovation pathways.

Today, SEI has opened a new hub in Benevento and is planning to open additional spaces in other parts of Italy. The SEI Incubator has supported over 50 startups and entrepreneurial teams, investing a total of 64,500 euros in 5 companies. They regularly engage in incubation, acceleration, training, and networking activities and have established partnerships with universities, research centers, SMEs, and industry associations.In late 2020, SEI launched its first call for ideas, "Demetra," for startups, receiving over 54 applications from all over Italy. In three years of operation, SEI has developed an innovative, strategic, and scalable model with the aim of expanding nationally, providing vitality to entrepreneurship in rural areas by replicating the model established in Avellino.In late 2022, SEI launched its second call for ideas, "Traiano," in Benevento, which received more than 30 applications. Their support for startups includes incubation, go-to-market strategies, and fundraising.SEI has organized and managed two hackathons, over 20 specific webinars, and two innovation programs with local SMEs. They host often Demo Days for their startups with investors and actively participate in most startup events and industry fairs.

MACOM European Semiconductor Center (MESC) was acquired by MACOM Technology Solutions (MACOM) in May2023. The facility in Limeil-Brevannes has a 40+ year heritage in material science, III-V semiconductor wafer processing and MMIC design. Its differentiated Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) and Gallium Nitride (GaN) compound semiconductor manufacturing capabilities include multiple semiconductor processes and products. This site is a French company “MACOM Technology Solutions (FRANCE) SAS”, registered under 920 593 571 R.C.S. Creteil, with head office located 2 rue du Moulin, 94450 LIMEIL-BREVANNES. 
MACOM designs and manufactures high-performance semiconductor products for the Telecommunications, Industrial and Defense and Datacenter industries. MACOM services over 6,000 customers annually with a broad product portfolio that incorporates RF, Microwave, Analog and Mixed Signal and Optical semiconductor technologies. MACOM has achieved certification to the IATF16949 automotive standard, the ISO9001 international quality standard and the ISO14001 environmental management standard. MACOM operates facilities across the United States, Europe, Asia and is headquartered in Lowell, Massachusetts.

entityDescription:
AeroPhoto Co Ltd, founded in 2014 and based in Thessaloniki, Greece, is an aerial survey and geospatial data processing company with expertise in acquisition, analysis, mapping and delivery of geospatial information. It is committed to airborne spatial data acquisition of the earth’s surface and its advanced processing, leading to value-added geo-information products. With our long experience and reliability, we provide high quality and accurate topographic and geospatial raw data and derivatives, such as aerial photography and LiDAR data, using state-of-the-art cutting-edge technologies, cameras and sensors. The company successfully operates missions in Greece, across European Union and in Middle East territories. 

Customer-focused and committed to innovation, our products and services are constantly evolving to meet the needs of a broad range of market sectors e.g. forestry, land administration, transportation and infrastructure, archaeology, natural disaster management, pipelines, and requirements of the most complex projects. AeroPhoto Co Ltd undertakes aerial photography, LiDAR, thermal and hyperspectral survey missions operating the most up to date and advanced aerial survey equipment, and as such is in the position of being able to provide customers with high quality, unique and cost-effective solutions. In collaboration with private and public sector, universities and institutes we participate in research programs whose prerequisite is ultra-high resolution aerial images or LiDAR datasets.

Flight missions for the acquisition of ultra-high-resolution aerial imagery and LiDAR data, are carried out by specially modified, EASA certified aircrafts. Aircrafts are equipped with a wide range of airborne mapping systems, digital large and medium format aerial cameras (e.g. Vexcel Ultracam Eagle Μ3, Phase One iXU-RS 1000), LiDAR sensors (e.g. Riegl LMS VQ-1560ii, VQ-880-G II), hyperspectral and thermal cameras (e.g. CASI & TABI), accurate GPS/IMU systems and other scientific equipment. Our sensors and aircrafts allow us to execute capture with a GSD range of 1.5 to 50cm.

entityDescription:
The Laboratory of Spectroscopy is one of the largest laboratories at the ISSP UL and it combines a variety of research methods related to optical, magnetic and electron spectroscopy.
The range of materials includes both bulk and polycrystals, glass, thin films, nanomaterials, liquids and gases. The available infrastructure includes both standard measurements (absorption, excitation, steady-state and time-resolved luminescence spectra) over a wide temperature range (6 K to 700 K) as well as vibrational (Raman and Fourier infrared) spectroscopy, ellipsometry, electron paramagnetic resonance , optically detectable magnetic resonance, subnanosecond luminescence characterization, thermostimulated luminescence measurement, ablation spectroscopy and X - ray photoelectron spectroscopy equipment.
The staff of the laboratory has extensive experience in the spectroscopic characterization of solid state materials and actively provides services to academic and industrial partners.

description:
Transform Environmental Data into Sustainable Solutions
At GEONOX GmbH, we believe in the transformative power of geospatial insights. As our world becomes increasingly interconnected and complex, understanding the environment around us is paramount. That's where we come in. 
- Discovering Patterns: Utilizing cutting-edge GIS (Geographic Information System) tools, we specialize in unveiling the stories that data tells. We go beyond traditional mapping, interpreting, and connecting our world through data, offering clarity in the midst of environmental intricacies. 
- Sustainability Through Spatial Intelligence: By analysing geospatial data, overlaying diverse datasets, and leveraging spatial intelligence, we provide holistic solutions to ecological challenges. From habitat restoration to biodiversity conservation, our insights consistently lead to sustainable outcomes. 
- Excellence and Expertise: With a seasoned team of GIS & Ecology professionals, we bring together profound knowledge and hands-on experience. Our track record showcases the tangible differences our data-driven strategies have made across diverse sectors. 
- Future-Driven: Our current projects include managing GIS data to support wild honey bees and utilizing satellite imagery for mangrove forest resettlement. 
Join us on our mission to transform environmental data into sustainable solutions. Dive deep into geospatial explorations with GEONOX GmbH, where data meets geography, and decisions are crafted with utmost clarity. For collaborations, inquiries, or to learn more, connect with us here or explore our official website.
