description:
We have a long track record of processing (https://cryotempo-eolis.org/) and disseminating (https://cs2eo.org/) CryoSat-2 data for ESA, as well as having overseen the Digital Twin Earth - Antarctica Project. We would like to take the lead on ingesting, processing and disseminating CryoSat-2 within a proposed HIGHWAY consortium. CryoSat-2 has been named as a priority Earth Explorer mission within the ITT text, and Earth Explorer missions generally have higher risk, lower commonality processes than other data sources. We believe this justifies the inclusion of specialist consortium partners to handle them. 
Further, our experience with CryoSat-2’s geospatial point cloud data will be valuable when dealing with other, similar data sets such as those of Sentinel-3. Drawing on our successful cs2eo.org service and our currently in-development service Specklia (https://pypi.org/project/specklia/), we can offer innovative, advanced data access techniques for geospatial point cloud data to a consortium, allowing it to pull ahead of competing consortia who might be overly focussed on raster data. Lastly, we are recognised by ESA as proven experts on the conversion of CryoSat-2’s geospatial point clouds to a raster form (the CryoTEMPO-EOLIS Gridded Product – an operational product for ESA).

entityDescription:
Atrineo AG is a based independent, owner-managed company specialised in the commercialisation of technology and knowledge and active in European markets. The identification, assessment, further development and commercialisation of technologies and knowledge is our core business. We offer our services to leading public research organisations, innovation and start-up creation networks and internationally oriented companies, both corporates and SMEs.
In the field of public research, Atrineo AG is working for all four major research organisations (Max Planck Society, Fraunhofer Society, Helmholtz Association, Leibniz Association) as well as for leading universities in Spain and Europe.
Typical projects of Atrineo AG are the further development of activities in the field of knowledge and technology transfer, i.e. the design, establishment and optimisation of structures, systems and processes as well as the support and consultancy service for singular transfer cases.

Beyond public research organisations, Atrineo AG also works with Knowledge Innovation Communities such as InnoEnergy, EIT Health, EIT Food or Climate-KIC. Typically, Atrineo AG is a service provider for business creation (technology and market assessments for start-up companies, coaching services, business development services and fund raising), Innovation projects (business case development, market studies, evaluation of proposals, WP activities, partner quality and satisfaction surveys) and Education (conduction of trainings and seminars, MOOCs and blended learning offerings and sustainability support for education offerings). entityDescription: PHOTONICPARTS works in the field of joining and assembly technologies and production of laser components mainly for the photonic market. Beside laser technology itself, the core know-how of lies in the production of homogeneous large-area solder joints for any materials or material pairings. The focus is on the customer's requirement for a thermally stable and robust solder joint with the lowest thermal and electrical resistance between two or more joining partners. Major fields of application are the packaging, adjustment and thermal management of laser crystals, optics and fiber optics in the markets of laser technology, aerospace and quantum technologies. Example applications are the assembly of laser crystal packages and frequency converter modules. Currently the automated alignment of optical setups is being developed, which enables the customer to remelt the solder-interface and repeatable align optical elements in liquid solder. Both founders have >25years of experience in ultra-short pulse beam source and component development and production due to their former work at FRAUNHOFER ILT and AMPHOS GmbH.

entityDescription:
RYD Engineering is a European company specialized in high-performance composite materials engineering and their manufacturing process, with headquarters in San Sebastián and Barcelona (Spain). RYD is a 100% privately-owned company.
 
RYD boasts a multidisciplinary engineering team with over 20 years of experience and extensive knowledge in the fields of complex structure design, manufacturing, and assembly, complying with European regulations.
 
They provide a comprehensive service, including FRP (Fiber Reinforced Polymer) material research and qualification for specific environments (temperature, strength, vacuum, radiation, etc.), component construction and qualification. We also conduct physical characterization tests, validate production processes, design parts, molds, and tools, perform economic analysis, prototype and produce parts, as well as industrialize series production. We rely on composite technologies, in-house CNC manufacturing, and Additive Manufacturing of plastic and metallic materials.
 
RYD Engineering has four main business units: space, industrial, automotive and science. Our evolution in these sectors has enabled organic and natural growth, allowing us to participate in increasingly larger projects, leading to more opportunities, internal resources and team expansion.
 
RYD Engineering's strategy is rooted in the constant pursuit of excellence and innovation. Since our inception, the focus has been on pushing the boundaries of material behavior through innovative designs, adding extra value. Our mission at RYD is to manufacture structures with high mechanical properties to improve existing solutions and introduce new ones that don't yet exist. This approach translates into reduced component weight, contributing to a global reduction in environmental footprint.
 
Research and development (R&D) are common features across all of RYD's business lines, enabling development and growth, setting it apart from competitors. We have two main R&D strategies: firstly, to enhance existing market products to make them more efficient, competitive, and profitable. Secondly, to launch our own lines of innovative development, enabling next-generation advancements, albeit with a higher development risk, to establish a leadership position in the market.

description:
ASTELCO Systems is your partner for professional astronomical telescopes, Optical Ground Stations / Terminals (OGS / OGT) and related accessories of any kind.
To the benefit of research teams all over the world, ASTELCO designs, develops, builds and services advanced mechanical and optical systems, special instrumentation and dedicated software as well as enclosures, domes and towers.
ASTELCO is committed to quality, reliabilty and close connection to science and space industry. ASTELCO has designed a series of Alt-Az telescopes from 0.6m to 3.0m aperture, as well as a series of 0.4 to 0.6m telescopes that can be operated on a universal mount in either Alt-Az, Alt-Alt or equatorial (EQ) mode, reflecting the needs of special applications.
ASTELCO is building Optical Ground Stations for various countries, according to SDA standards.
All designs use industry-leading, state-of-the-art technology. Rather than using old-fashioned style or technique, many details of ASTELCO's telescopes have been re-designed "from scratch", using latest components and technology available to make them more reliable, more stable and more effective in every day's operation.
entityDescription:
ASTELCO Systems is your partner for professional Astronomical Telescopes and related accessories of any kind.
Founded in 2004, as a global leader in advanced optomechanical systems, telescopes, enclosures and hard- and software control solutions, as well as Optical Ground Stations/Terminals according to SDA standards for optical laser communication, ASTELCO offers a broad range of reliable, high-quality and high-precision telescopes, based on industry-leading design and state-of-the-art technology, robotized and fully remotely operated.

ASTELCO builds OGS Optical Ground Stations for SAT-COM / QKD satellite-communications, SLR Satellite Laser Ranging, space awareness, space debris detection, Satellite Tracking & Identification Telescopes, including Laser Guide Star and AO Active / Adaptive Optics technology, as well as Laser Launch Telescopes.

ASTELCO builds completely retractable enclosures, Clamshell domes and fast-rotating domes from 2m to 12m Ø, as well as towers, such as for Seeing-Monitors, and related technology.

The entire ASTELCO team consists of people that have been involved with astronomy, telescopes and telescope control systems for a very long time. Our software engineers have more than 20 years' experience in telescope control.
ASTELCO is committed to quality, reliability and close connection to science.

All ASTELCO products are Made in Germany and are built in one of the ASTELCO facilities in Germany.
Customers include NASA, ESA, ESO, DLR, CNRS, ONERA, ISRO and others.

entityDescription:
Company Overview: Datalya is a specialized technology company that combines the fields of machine learning, remote sensing, and data engineering. Its primary mission is to leverage advanced data analysis techniques to extract valuable insights from remote sensing data related to Canada's geographical landscape. The company operates with a small but highly skilled team comprising remote sensing scientists and data engineers.
Core Focus Areas:
- Remote Sensing Data Curation: Datalya specializes in gathering, processing, and curating remote sensing data. Remote sensing involves the collection of information about the Earth's surface and atmosphere using various sensors mounted on satellites, aircraft, or ground-based platforms. Datalya focuses on collecting and organizing this data, ensuring its accuracy and relevance.

- Integration with Socio-Economic Data: Datalya's unique approach involves combining remote sensing data with socio-economic data. This integration is a critical step that allows the company to provide comprehensive insights to its clients. Socio-economic data includes information about population, economic activities, infrastructure, and more. By merging these datasets, Datalya can offer a holistic view of the relationship between the natural environment and human activities.

Key Services: Datalya offers a range of services to public and private organizations:
- Informed Decision-Making: By providing curated and integrated remote sensing and socio-economic data, Datalya empowers its clients to make informed decisions. This includes decisions related to land use planning, resource management, environmental conservation, disaster risk assessment, and infrastructure development.

- Risk Assessment and Mitigation: Datalya's expertise is instrumental in assessing risks associated with natural disasters, climate change, and other environmental factors. By analyzing historical and real-time data, the company can help clients identify potential risks and develop mitigation strategies.

- Infrastructure Monitoring: Datalya's capabilities extend to monitoring critical infrastructure, such as transportation networks, utilities, and natural resource extraction sites. Continuous monitoring enables proactive maintenance and enhances the overall resilience of infrastructure systems.

Client Base: Datalya serves a diverse clientele, including government agencies, research institutions, environmental organizations, urban planners, and private companies. These clients benefit from Datalya's data-driven insights to address complex challenges and make evidence-based decisions.
Impact: Through its work, Datalya contributes to sustainable development, environmental conservation, and improved disaster preparedness. The company's insights have the potential to enhance the quality of life for Canadians by fostering more efficient resource management and infrastructure development.
In summary, Datalya is a specialized machine learning company that excels in remote sensing data curation and its integration with socio-economic data. Their work empowers organizations to make informed decisions, assess and mitigate risks, and monitor critical infrastructure, ultimately contributing to the betterment of Canada's diverse and expansive geography.

ML has revolutionised how science is being done and taking advantage of this new numerical toolset should not require having a full time ML scientist on the team to design, develop and deploy systems. Qruise is developing ML for Science as a productised toolset making ML driven discovery accessible to all. 

Our first offerings address the growing pains of controlling current generation noisy quantum computers (NISQ devices) and provide improvements in operational fidelities through the use of ML & Quantum Optimal Control.

entityName: L-Universita' ta' Malta - Department of Geosciences
entityDescription:
With an ever-increasing awareness of the need for sustainable development, the understanding of geohazards, climate and ecosystem monitoring, vulnerability and risks, resource management and technological advancement, it is clear that a sound knowledge base about our planet, and more specifically, about our national terrestrial, marine and atmospheric environment, will assume more importance in the near future.
Although the Maltese Islands are small in size, there is still much that needs to be better understood about the physical environment of our land and surrounding seas, their interaction with the hydrosphere and atmosphere, their relationship with the surrounding region of the central Mediterranean and the rest of the planet, and the impact on society in general. Moreover, the very nature of Malta’s marine, terrestrial and atmospheric environments link inextricably to the economic and social dimensions of human activity in the country.
The Department of Geosciences within the Faculty of Science is intended to spearhead the response of the University of Malta to these challenges and opportunities. Our Department is largely an applied research institution in the earth-related sciences, founded on a strong base of interdisciplinary science, with a focus on operational oceanography, seismology and geophysics, marine geology, and atmosphere and climate research.
We strive to be a national reference point for matters related to the scientific understanding of the land, marine and atmospheric environments, at local, regional and larger scales. With the launch of the undergraduate course, and a number of postgraduate student opportunities, it aspires to be also an exciting and challenging hub for student participation in fundamental studies and applied research, using the latest technologies and international opportunities.
The primary research areas within the Department of Geosciences are:Atmospheric and Climate Studies; Geology and Geophysics;Operational Oceanography

entityName: L-Universita' ta' Malta - Institute of Aerospace Technologies
entityDescription:
The Institute of Aerospace Technologies (IAT) was established by the Council of the University of Malta in 2014. The scope of the Institute is to exploit the strong track record and international reputation that the University has developed in niche areas of aeronautics since the early 2000s and to further extend activity to the broader scope of aerospace. 

The Institute of Aerospace Technologies (IAT) within the University of Malta (UM) hosts one of the strongest research activities of the UM, that in the field of aerospace and aeronautics. The IAT focuses on technologies associated with vehicles operating in the atmosphere and beyond. In the past decade the IAT has attracted over �5 Million in contractual research funding to the University. Through these activities, the Institute has developed a strong and diverse portfolio that ranges from design of safety critical-surveillance systems to airborne Human-Machine Interface (HMI) design, flight operations, trajectory optimisation, air traffic management applications and support activities such as safety assessment, design of experiment, simulation, test and evaluation.

The University of Malta has extensive experience in participation in projects funded under the European Commission Framework Programmes 6 and 7 as well as by the National R&I Programmes. EC-funded projects in which the University of Malta has participated in include FLYSAFE, ALICIA, ODICIS, e-CAB, HIRF-SE, ACROSS, CLEAN SKY and SESAR, whilst those funded by the national R&I programme include CLEAN FLIGHT, TOUCH-FLIGHT, CLEAN FLIGHT 2, SAGRO,eMRO, SMARTCOPTER, SmartFDM, NEVAC, SATMET, ACSAGO, KERS-air, WAGE and BEA. Other international projects include Sino-Malta funded projects such as REACTIVE. Collaborations in these and other projects has involved a wide range of partners, including European industrial primes such as Airbus, Thales, BAE Systems, and Selex ES, national research centres such as CIRA (IT), NLR (NL), DLR (DE) and Onera (FR), airline operators, air navigation service providers and major European universities in the sector.
Through their research activities, IAT academics have published over 150 academic publications and 100 industrial research documents, has MT, US and GB patents granted for inventions in avionics systems and has patents filed for 5 other inventions awaiting award. The IAT has employed over 20 graduates to work on research contracts and has awarded several Masters and Doctoral degrees in the field of avionics and air traffic management.

entityName: L-Universita' ta' Malta - Institute of Space Sciences and Astronomy
entityDescription:
The Institute for Space Sciences and Astronomy (ISSA) at the University of Malta, established in 2014, brings together faculty members from the Science, Engineering, and ICT departments. We engage in a multitude of global collaborations while concurrently advancing our in-house infrastructure to support a wide spectrum of disciplines, including supercomputing capabilities and pioneering theoretical physics research.

Within the realm of big instrument processing, ISSA has garnered notable recognition in both radio and optical astronomy. Our contributions are evident through the publication of numerous journal and conference papers spanning antenna design, signal processing, data acquisition systems, monitoring and control systems, optical instrument optimization, imaging pipelines, and space debris monitoring systems.
Presently, ISSA plays a pivotal role in various ambitious big data instrument initiatives, including the Square Kilometre Array (SKA), Euclid, REACH, CATAMARAN, and the Northern Cross. For the SKA, ISSA is at the forefront, developing software for the data acquisition system of the low-frequency telescope. In the context of EUCLID, ISSA spearheads the design and development of cutting-edge image processing algorithms, set to significantly enhance the instrument's image quality. ISSA assumes the role of digital signal processing leader for the REACH telescope, an instrument with wide-band capabilities designed to measure the 21cm line, allowing it to delve into the cosmic dark ages. At the Northern Cross, ISSA has deployed two pioneering instruments: the BIRALES bi-static radar space debris monitoring system and the Fast Radio Burst (FRB) surveying system. Moreover, ISSA collaborates with INAF in Italy for CATAMARAN, working on the development and benchmarking of machine learning software for radio astronomical source detection, classification, and segmentation methods.
The cosmology research group within ISSA is dedicated to addressing the cosmic tensions problem. We utilize the latest observational data, including the ESA Planck Mission legacy data sets and publicly available data, to explore new physics beyond the standard cosmological model. Our research primarily involves the creation of cosmology simulators, aiming to illuminate how alternative physics can resolve the growing challenges posed by these tensions.

SUAVIA FORUM is a company specialized in Geographic Information Systems (GIS) services. GIS is a computerized tool that enables the capture, storage, manipulation, analysis, and presentation of geographic data. SUAVIA FORUM focuses on providing customized GIS services to mining companies, with the aim of helping them optimize their processes related to mineral exploration, extraction, and production.

The services offered by SUAVIA FORUM include the collection and analysis of geospatial data, the creation of thematic maps, and the generation of specialized reports. Furthermore, they provide tailored solutions for integrating GIS systems into the technological infrastructure of mining companies.

The centerpiece of their work is the development of the UAVIA project. UAVIA is a platform and a novel product based on the integration of existing technologies, aiming to revolutionize the Global Mining Support Activities Market.
To develop UAVIA, collaborations have been established with various technological centers, Earth Observation (EO) companies, mining enterprises, and European geological institutes. UAVIA builds on the experience gained from over 20 projects.
SUAVIA FORUM has maintained a close relationship with leading mining companies in the market, with whom they have collaborated on joint projects for the development and implementation of their products. This has allowed them to gain firsthand insights into the needs and challenges of the mining industry and develop customized solutions to address them.

Here is an overview of the key features and core activities of QVADIS Srl:
- Innovative Indoor Navigation: QVADIS Srl offers an advanced indoor navigation service based on proprietary technology called QVAD. This system uses QR codes and immersive 360-degree real images to guide users inside complex structures such as convention centers, shopping malls, airports, and more. The QVAD technology provides a precise and engaging navigation experience.

- Transportation Service Management: In addition to navigation, QVADIS Srl allows users to book transportation services directly through the QVAD application. This includes taxi bookings, public transportation, and more, making it easier for people to move within large structures and cities.

- Patient Care: QVADIS Srl offers integrated solutions for patient care management in healthcare facilities. This may include medical appointment bookings, guidance to departments, and healthcare resource management.

- Human Resource Management: The company also provides solutions for human resource management, helping organizations optimize staff allocation and planning efficiently and effectively.

- Global Reach: QVADIS Srl has a global vision and has registered the QVAD trademark internationally. This reflects the company's ambition to expand its presence worldwide and make its services accessible to a global audience.

- Ecology and Sustainability: QVADIS Srl places great emphasis on environmental sustainability. It uses recyclable materials and seeks to reduce the environmental impact of its solutions by avoiding the use of radiofrequency or Bluetooth-based technologies.

- Ease of Use and Accessibility: QVADIS Srl's approach aims to make its technology accessible to the widest possible audience. The use of QR codes simplifies access, and the technology is designed to be usable by people with diverse abilities.

In summary, QVADIS Srl is a cutting-edge company that seeks to improve people's daily lives through technological innovation. Its mission to make indoor navigation more inclusive and simplify the management of essential services makes it a key player in the field of technology and services.

entityDescription:
SERE is the European chapter of theSociety for Ecological Restoration, the global non-profit organisation forecological restoration. We are aEuropean-wide association,with 475 (as of February 2023) scientific and practitioner members across Europe, the Mediterranean and globally, including restoration research centres and private companies. We operate as a‘network of networks’in collaboration with national restoration organisations across the EU.

Ourmissionis to advance the science, practice, and policy of ecological restoration to sustain biodiversity, improve resilience in a changing climate, and re-establish an ecologically healthy relationship between nature and culture.
We actively promotebest practicesand effectiverestoration policy.We work to ensure that ecological restoration is recognized and utilized as a fundamental component of global conservation, biodiversity and sustainable development programs, and that projects aredesigned and implementedto provide people with the opportunity to repair ecological damage and improve human wellbeing.We do this through practical and policy dialogue, networking, training, guidance, quality standards, publications and alike.

Joint Stock Company "Latvijas valsts meži" (LVM), translated as "Latvia`s State Forests" manages and administers 1.62 million ha of land, including 1.60 million ha of forest land, which incorporates 1.41 million ha of forest.The main product of the company is timber. In addition to forestry, LVM also provides hunting and recreational services, produces selected seeds and saplings for reforestation, offers subsoil resources and land leases for subsoil resource extraction, and provides geospatial IT development services.

The Business System Solutions department of LVM offers remote sensing services that include processing, analysis and service development of data obtained from various remote sensing instruments. Remote sensing data is an important informational resource and support for decision-making processes. Remote sensing data provide information on terrain, overgrowth, land use, objects and other geospatial information relevant to economic activities—data which would otherwise be impossible to obtain from field inspections alone.

The LVM has created LIDAR digital elevation model, LIDAR tree crown sufrace model, LIDAR vegetation sufrace model to support JSC Latvia's State Forests business needs. These models provide significant information about forest stand age, forest stand height, forest density, relief, ravines, drainage ditches and other geospatial features. These remote sensing modules are available to clients who use our products and also they are available to any user as open WMS service.

entityDescription:
The University of Malta (UM) is the sole public and highest teaching institution in Malta, with its structures being in line with the Bologna Process and the European Higher Education area. UM has a 400-year history and presently hosts 11,500 students including 1,000 foreign/exchange students from nearly 92 different countries, following full-time or part-time degree and diploma courses. The study programmes are designed to produce highly qualified professionals with research experience who will play key roles within industry, commerce and public affairs. Around 3,500 students graduate each year. Currently, the University comprises 14 faculties, 115 academic departments, 1 academy, 17 institutes, 13 centres, 3 schools and 11 administrative directorates. The University operates from four campuses located in Msida, Valletta, Marsaxlokk and Gozo, with three outreach centres in Argotti, Cottonera and Fawwara. The University is one of the largest employers in the country, employing 3080 people: 880 full-time and 810 part-time academics, and 1,070 full-time and 320 part-time staff in administrative, technical and industrial roles.

During the last 15 years, the UM was involved as project coordinator and project partner in 365 EU-funded projects, through various funding channels. These include Horizon 2020 (70 projects), Horizon Europe (14 projects), Erasmus+ (114 projects), INTERREG EU, MED, ITALIA-MALTA (44 projects), FP7 (47 projects), Lifelong Learning Programme (76 projects). The UM is also involved in national funding programmes, other international initiatives and is even represented in a number of European and International University networks and groups. It currently has around 300 active projects.

The UM project teams are resident academics and research support officers who are backed by support structures to assist during the application phase, throughout the life-cycle of the project and in all technical and financial reporting periods, right up to project closure. The departments in question concern:
- Research Support Services Directorate
- Project Support Office
- Knowledge Transfer Office
- Communication Office
- Centre for Entrepreneurship and Business Incubation
- Human Resources Office
- Procurement Office
- Legal Office and
- IT services
The University of Malta values equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) and is committed to make the necessary changes to ensure that an equitable environment is created, while celebrating diversity, promoting inclusion and protecting the human rights of all individuals working or studying within this entity. For this purpose, a gender equity plan taking an intersectional approach, was created and is publicly accessible on the UM website.

Furthermore, the HR Strategy for Research (HRS4R) brings the UM human resources policies and practices in line with the European Charter for Researchers and the Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers. The Charter & Code ensures that researchers can enjoy the same rights and obligations in any European country.

entityDescription:
Dryad Networks GmbH provides ultra-early forest fire detection as well as health and growth monitoring solutions for public and private forests.
Dryad's Wildfire Sensors have been designed for deployment in remote, outdoor locations, avoid the use of potentially dangerous lithium-ion batteries and instead use a combination of solar panels and super capacitors. Embedded in the forest and using AI-powered gas sensors, Dryad’s Wildfire Sensors can provide ultra-early detection of wildfires during the smouldering phase, hours before optical solutions can detect the fire.
Dryad's Silvanet Mesh Gateways have been designed for deployment scenarios in forest areas, providing off-grid operation with solar power and extending the reach of the IoT sensor network to remote, off-network coverage locations using a unique LoRaWAN mesh network technology.

For more than 100 years, Ottobock develops innovative products. Meanwhile, the med-tech company also takes care of the full treatment cycle all over the globe. entityDescription: MF Research Labs is a startup focusing on cutting-edge GNSS research and consulting. We specialize in GNSS snapshot receivers, which enable GNSS tracking using unprecedentedly small amounts of energy. For instance, a GNSS receiver could run several years using a single coin cell battery, as our former research at ETH Zurich shows. MF Research Labs innovates both in software and hardware areas. One of our current goals is to enable real-time maximum likelihood GNSS positioning. Maximum likelihood positioning is a more robust positioning method than classical least-squares positioning. Also, maximum likelihood positioning allows for easy integration of GNSS spoofing mitigation capabilities, whereas current receivers can usually only detect GNSS spoofing, but not recover their position.

entityDescription:
Dutch Butterfly Conservation, the name De Vlinderstichting uses outside the Netherlands, was founded in 1983, with conservation and restoration of the Dutch butterfly fauna as its chief aims. Since then, it has extended those aims to include dragonflies and moths. Furthermore, our area of activity has grown over the border, where we now work with sister organisations in Europe. Conservation is of great urgency, because the numbers of these insects have been decreasing drastically since the beginning of the twentieth century. Our work is only possible with the help of more than 1500 volunteers, and the financial support of those who donate to our cause, at present, numbering some 6000.
The key to protecting insects is protecting the habitat they live in. We collect large amounts of data on insects and use these data as input for (spatial) modelling to identify suitable habitat, but also advise on proper management.

Arthur Strategies & Systems, headquartered in Amsterdam, and part and tradename Arthur’s Legal B.V. is an international research-based strategic and legal organisation incorporated in 2001, covering the unique combination of technology, strategy, impact, ethics and rule of law, focusing on (inter)national, regional and global strategy and policy aspects in this Digital Age. It has a global practice with multiple relevant ventures, programs and projects in the EU, UK, EEA and USA in the public, private and public-private sectors, on sovereignty, safety, security, privacy, critical infrastructures where sensitive data (either personal, non-personal, confidential, proprietary or otherwise) is the common denominator, as well as digital identity, data sharing, people-centricity, nuances of trust, trustworthy cyber-physical ecosystems of ecosystems, dynamic assurance and accountability.
For once, it is member of the EU Alliance of Industrial Data, Cloud and Edge, leading both the taskforce on digital sovereignty, and the taskforce on cybersecurity. Furthermore he is advisory board member, security advisory board member, ethical board member, data protection officer respectively partner in more than 25 European projects that are partially co-funded by the European Commission and for the other part funded by Arthur Strategies & Systems itself. Also, it is one of the stakeholders of UKRI TAS-S: Trustworthy Autonomous Systems Node in Security, where its director, Arthur van der Wees is chair of the Advisory Board.
Arthur Strategies & Systems are not consultants, but practitioners. It does not only talk, but actually walks the talk in real-life as it believe it is all about walking the talk (while continue to talk). We already do this for more than 20 years, and will continue our straight road forward. Arthur Strategies and Systems has created and deployed a novel collaborative and co-creative approach, which we call the Collaboration Framework Methodology. In short, it caters for trust between multiple partners such as multi-vendor, multi-sector and multi-data sources collaborations, where each is working together with each other; not working for each other. We have supported several hundreds of customers in several thousands of deals where digital data, communication, spectrum, IT, software, cloud, OT, edge, far edge/IoT, service levels, data processing, cyber-physical or other digital ecosystems were the subject matter, both in the public and private sector and both from vendor/supply-side as from demand/customer-side.
We have developed and successfully deployed various common reference models, methodologies and tools. These are proprietary of Arthur’s Legal and are and have been deployed both in the public and private sector and both from vendor/supplier-side as from customer/user-side. For once, Arthur Strategies & Systems creates and help design, enable and facilitate advanced trusted data sharing (TDS). This includes sharing contextual data, attributes, information and knowledge, based on trust, for optimising tactical and operational availability, usefulness and performance as well as increased security, safety and sustainability of the particular system, its subsystems, components, connectors, sensors and the like, as well as their respective interdependencies, throughout their entire - individual, combined and holistic - life cycles. Data sharing – or better, the lack of data sharing – is one of the most discussed and most urgent topics in almost all domains and sectors, and in the Space Sector including its supply chain ecosystems in particular.

entityDescription:
Agcurate BV is a Dutch earth observation company, which has expertise in the software development and AI in the agriculture domain. We leverage satellite imagery (SAR and multispectral) and additional data sources (climate, soil properties) to offer comprehensive insights into the cultivation cycle and support agricultural operations. Using machine learning and deep neural networks, we classify land cover and crops, estimate yields, and employ biophysical crop models to monitor soil water balance and detect irrigation needs. Generative AI enables us to adapt and generate data for regions with limited data availability.
Via our AI co-pilot FieldOps, we help consumer packaged food producers to monitor their return on investment on agricultural operations consistently, by providing them with actionable insights on their fields using satellite imagery and AI. We aim to make the agriculture investable, sustainable and resilient against the climate change.

entityDescription:
The Society for Conservation Biology Italy Chapter (Società di Biologia della Conservazione) constitutes the primary scientific entity of reference in Italy for professionals and experts in biodiversity conservation. The society advocates for diversity, equity, and inclusivity.
The Chapter's objectives are as follows:
- Promote membership in the Society and participation in Chapter activities.
- Advance scientific research in the field of conservation biology through an interdisciplinary approach.
- Support the professional development of individuals engaged in the field of conservation biology at both national and international levels.
- Raise awareness and engage civil society in conservation biology topics through communication and scientific outreach activities.
- Advocate for the positions of the Society and the Chapter regarding national and international public policies.
- Assist in decision-making processes and assessments within the context of environmental sustainability for biodiversity conservation.
- Uphold a high level of professional integrity and expertise in the field of conservation biology.

entityName: INSTITUT DE LA PROPRIETE INTELLECTUELLE LUXEMBOURG
entityDescription:
Intellectual Property Institute Luxembourg (IPIL: www.ipil.lu) was established on August 1st 2014. IPIL is the official counterpart of Luxembourg’s IP Office. Its missions are to:
• coordinate the set-up of the public IP policy,
• develop and provide support services for enterprises, research actors, public institutions and other publics, 
• develop and provide training as well as promotion and awareness activities, 
• conduct projects and studies to provide advices to the authorities. 
IPIL is a spin-off company of the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST: www.list.lu), that was based on former Henri Tudor Centre-CVT Department (created in 1994). It can count on a core, multicultural and multilingual experienced team of specialists (Luxembourgish, French, German, Spanish and Turkish) in their field of activity.
IPIL has developed IP-related services and activities that are provided to companies (with a special focus on start-ups, scale-ups and SMEs) as well as to Public Research Institutions and for patent and trademarks attorneys. These activities cover the whole range of IP matters, from industrial property to copyright and related rights and to soft IP. As the main actor in the country involved in IP awareness, training and services provision to economic actors and general public, it aims at developing IP and its exploitation including knowledge and technology transfer. 
IPIL develops its own and specific working tools, such as IP audit/diagnosis, IP information analysis methodologies, IP information searches methodologies, IP training scheme (e-learning and on-site) and develops related services that are proposed to companies.
Concerning those services to Luxembourg’s enterprises, IPIL is in charge of: 
• providing IP awareness raising activities and tools,
• providing IP support services, 
• organising IP training events,
• the national Patent Information Centre (Patlib network managed by the EPO).
Conscious of the importance of IP exploitation, IPIL is continuously investigating the state-of-the-art solutions developed and provided to companies, and is active in developing its own methodologies to help the national economy. 
Thanks to its proximity with the national IP authority and to proven years of experience within the framework of the EU-funded projects, IPIL has established sustainable and strong connections with the majority of the national and international IP offices (EUIPO, EPO, WIPO) in Europe, along with SME associations and business organisations.

entityDescription:
EAT freedom GmbH & Co. KG is a German start-up specializing in healthy and gourmet full meals for adventurers who undertake long expeditions in extreme and highly stressful environments. For the development of its meals, the company constantly collaborates with groups of polar explorers, speleologists, high-altitude mountaineers, extreme sailors, and rowers to study and test the factors that influence food choices and habits during a mission. Examples are the organoleptic decay that occurs at altitude and the food fatigue that takes over as a stress factor after weeks of consuming a limited variety of dehydrated foods. Understanding the profound impact of food on a healthy and performing body and mind, EAT freedom uses premium quality ingredients for which it prefers low-temperatureprocessing, to preserve their full value, while offering a long shelf life. The start-up also focuses on the choice of whole grains, high-quality proteins, and healthy fats, makes limited use of salt and sugar, and ample use of herbs and spices to naturally enhance the flavour. In 2021-2022, the balanced recipes inspired by the Harvard Healthy Eating Plate found positive feedback in the collaboration with the European Space Agency for the supply of bonus food for the Minerva mission, during which the nutritional requirements set by the team of nutritionists and doctors supporting the mission were fully satisfied while meeting the astronaut's taste preferences.

The start-up was founded in 2021 by Dr. Sara Rocci Denis. Born and raised near Turin, she has always had a passion for exploration and mountaineering, which has led her to scale several peaks of 4,000m and beyond, her first at the age of 11. The idea of creating a line of gourmet meals that are quick to prepare and easy to transport, suitable for supporting high physical performance, was born in a tent in a high camp on Mount Cho Oyu, in Tibet, in 2011, where Rocci Denis, lacked the right nutrition to stay strong throughout the mission and to reach her adventure goal. In 2016, the meeting with Chef Stefano Polatomarked the formal beginning of the development of the prototype recipes. Chef Polato isa renowned food consultant who already developed bonus food for several astronauts prior to becoming Chef and Head of Food Development of EAT freedom project and developing with Dr. Rocci Denis the bonus food allowance for mission Minerva.

entityDescription:
Apisense provides beekeepers with insight about what's going on inside their hives without having them look inside each one.
Apisense is an all-in-one solution that integrates data from multiple sources to reduce the time needed to perform the most time-consuming day-to-day tasks every beekeeper faces each day.

BeeSmart.AI platform has following functionalities:
- Insight from the sensor data inside the hive:- Hive weight
- Temperature
- Humidity
- Atmospheric pressure
- Sound analysis
- CO2 and CO levels
- Total volatile organic carbon levels
- Hive GPS location
- Vibration sensors

- Alerts and notifications:- Colony health
- Varroa detection
- Swarming events
- Colony under attack events
- Queen death/escape
- Sudden weight loss
- Honey production complete events
- Vandalism, intruder and theft detection
- Flowering crop event in the area

- Insight from the external sources:- Weather forecast
- Flowering phenology events
- Crop type location information in the area
- Apiary location optimization

- Non-chemical varroa mite treatment with ultrasounds
- Knowledge sharing space:- Apiary reports and notes
- Beekeeping forum
- Getting started boards for beekeeping novices
- Farmer and orchard grower partnerships

Value we provide

The features mentioned above provide a foundation to gaining complete insight into your apiary.
- They can help you save the time needed to perform your daily work - you no longer have to look inside every hive on a weekly basis
- Colony health reports and varroa detection will help you plan the necessary treatments and reduce the cost of loosing the bees
- Ultrasound varroa treatment provides a chemical free solution to the problem
- Alerts and notifications will inform you if your immediate attention is needed
- Flowering phenology event notifications and flowering crop fields localisation near your apiary will help you locate the best spot to place your hives
- Beekeeping forums and boards are a great source of information if you are in a need of advice
- Farmer and orchard grover partnership program will help you get in touch with people in need of bee-aided pollination. This is great for both the farmer (natural pollination is much more effective and more eco than chemical one) and for you the beekeeper - you'll now have the opportunity to produce different types of honey more effectively!

Business model: integrated and sustainable agro-food chain. 
Objective: to integrate agro and food - agriculture on the plateInnovation ecosystem in agriculture, partner of numerous international organizations on innovationCertifications: INPS Quality Agricultural Work Network; EU organic production (CB IT-BIO-004l, operator code 47170); disciplinary of social farming; Artusi’s Foundation official supplier; GlobalGap-GRASP; I.F.S.

Precision agriculture with satelite control: Precision seeder and transplant on biodegradable mulch and drip irrigation using satellite technology for performance control.
and EU pilot project for carbon farming: Agronomic management for the capture of organic carbon in soil. emission reductions through carbon accumulation in soil shall be achieved through improved agricultural management (bait) in terms of g CO2eq/MJ and shall be assessed using the following formula:

Adjusted Emission savings Soil Carbon Accumulation via improved agricultural management (esca) in terms of g CO2eq/MJ should use the following formula to calculate their actual values: 
bait = (CSA – CSR ) x 3.664 x 106 x 1/n x 1/p x B x N – ef 
 
Where:
CSR is the mass of soil carbon stock per unit area associated with the reference crop management practice in Mg of C per ha.
CSA is the mass of soil estimated carbon stock per unit area associated with the actual crop management practices after at least 10 years of application in Mg of C per ha.
3,664 is the quotient obtained by dividing the molecular weight of CO2 (44,010 g/mol) by the molecular weight of carbon (12,011 g/mol) in g CO2eq/g C.
N is the period (in years) of the cultivation of the crop considered.
P is the productivity of the crop (measured as MJ biofuel or bioliquid energy per ha per year).
B = index of biodiversity measured as Mj of organic matter per Ha per year
N = fixation of N in soil by leguminoses is a parameter to evaluate the quality of soil
Ef emissions from the increased fertilisers or herbicide use

entityDescription:
Spirit AeroSystems is one of the world's largest manufacturers of aerostructures for commercial aircraft, defence platforms, and business/regional jets. Built on more than 100 years of aviation experience, Spirit is headquartered in Wichita, US, with ~14,800 employees globally. It has facilities in the US, UK (Belfast (Short Brother PLC) and Prestwick), France, Malaysia and Morocco.
With expertise in aluminum and advanced composite manufacturing solutions, Spirit’s core products include integrated wings and wing components, fuselages, pylons and engine nacelles. It also has a growing aftermarket and space business.
Spirit UK is one of the largest aerospace companies in the UK, with a total of ~ 3600 employees across its sites in Northern Ireland (c2,700) and Prestwick (c900). It is a major driver in the local economies where its sites are based. Spirit UK has over 700 approved UK suppliers, and is a key mentor in the aerospace industry’s SC21 supply chain development programme, working with suppliers to improve their competitiveness and win more high-value global work packages.
Spirit UK is a research-intensive company, and its two UK sites are centres of excellence for the design, manufacture and after-market support of complex aerostructures in metal and advanced composites, including wings, nacelles, fuselages and spoilers.
The principal activities of Spirit’s Belfast operations are the design, development, manufacture and assembly of major aircraft structural components (including wings, fuselages, engine nacelles and flight components) and provision of aftermarket component repair and overhaul, as well as other engineering services. Many of the programmes in which the company is involved has required significant R&D investment, including in the A220 advanced composite wing programme. At over �520m, this was the largest ever single inward investment in Northern Ireland, which will sustain over 1000 high-value jobs at peak production and many more in the UK supply chain.
Spirit Prestwick’s main activities are the design, development, manufacture and assembly of airframes, which consist principally of wing structure components. New product development includes design, development and materials research. The site has also formally opened its new Aerospace Innovation Centre – a �25m investment – where it will be collaborating with industrial, academic and supply chain partners on developing the new technologies and skills required for future sustainable aircraft platforms.

entityName: TECHNISCHE UNIVERSITAT DRESDEN - Chair of Space Systems
entityDescription:
FROM OUTER SPACE TO EVERYDAY LIFE - TECHNOLOGIES FOR AND FROM SPACE
Aerospace… is the technology driver for high-tech developments par excellence: smaller, lighter, more efficient and extremely energy efficient are not just keywords but the framework for each and every space project. At the Chair of Space Systems we offer a comprehensive research and training programme, ranging from the fundamentals of rocket and satellite technology to scientific payloads and experiments; developed, tested and flown in collaboration with students (e.g. on own satellites, sounding rockets, or at the International Space Station ISS).
Our research focuses in particular on novel propulsion systems (e.g. miniaturised ion thrusters, height-adaptive nozzles), energy systems and miniaturised gas sensors. We closely co-operate with partners from industry on terrestrial applications (spin-offs) of our space technologies. Fundamental research devoted to revolutionary drives ("breakthrough propulsion physics") and new concepts for next generation spacecraft are being conceived and explored within our institute.

entityDescription: Leading Edge Technology and Business with a Global Orientation The University of Applied Sciences Technikum Wien has achieved international reputation through its high quality of teaching and emphasis on applied studies. The University of Applied Sciences Technikum Wien has some of the best qualified academic staff in Austria, many of whom are actively involved in the business and engineering world. The dynamic exchange between our full-time academic staff and part-time professional lecturers who are active in business and industry creates a unique innovative academic environment from which everyone involved benefits. Unified Concept of Success The University of Applied Sciences Technikum Wien promotes research and development by incorporating applied theory in the classroom and encouraging collaborative research partnerships with industry and business. With an emphasis on applied learning, many of the school's research projects have resulted in innovative solutions for various technical problems in the industry. Full-time students acquire additional job skills for their future careers by completing a six-month intensive work internship. Furthermore, there is also the possibility of spending up to one year abroad at one of our international partner universities. Academic Programs The University of Applied Sciences Technikum Wien is committed to the pursuit of academic excellence and has achieved an international reputation for the quality of its education. The university offers full-time and part-time programs, custom-tailored to the needs of the students. By offering Bachelor and Master programs, the University of Applied Sciences Technikum Wien has taken important steps towards the internationalisation of educational opportunities and the integration of European and non-European university systems.

entityDescription:
Planetum

Planetum is a brand of the contributory organization Observatory and Planetarium Prague, which includes two observatories (Stefanik observatory, Dablice observatory) and one planetarium in Stromovka.At observatories you can admire large telescopes. During the day you can look at the Sun using special telescopes, on clear nights you can observe the Moon, details of the planets, places where stars are born in the universe, or distant galaxies. In the planetarium, the universe is projected onto an artificial sky in the shape of a hemisphere. Both observatories and the planetarium have a rich selection of programs - from fairy tales for the little ones to documentaries on astrophysics and cosmology. You will also find unique interactive exhibits dedicated to the exploration of space and cosmonautics. You can sit in the cockpit of the space shuttle, explore the Apollo lunar lander and much more.
The planetarium is a time machine that can travel to the past and the future, a spaceship with which you can fly to the planets, among the stars or leave the Galaxy and look at our home from a distance of tens of billions of light years. All this thanks to modern digital technology that keeps moving forward. As early as 2023, the projection area will be transformed into a giant LED screen with an area of ​​867 square meters – the Prague Planetarium will have the first so-called LED-dome in Europe.
Planetum also became the first institution of its kind in the world to send its own satellite into orbit. The Planetum-1 satellite was launched on May 25, 2022, on a Falcon 9 rocket from Florida's Cape Canaveral. It is the first purely educational satellite in the world. In the foyer of the planetarium, you can take a look at its operations center.

entityDescription:
HyImpulse UK Ltd is the wholly owned UK subsidiary of HyImpulse Technologies GmbH which is a New-Space start-up based in Hardthausen, Germany. 

HyImpulse UK Ltd is registered in Shetland where a motor test facility has been developed and also uses offices in Edinburgh. We are developing a mini launcher using disruptive technologies to provide low-cost small-sat launch opportunities for Europe and the whole world. HyImpulse was founded by 5 DLR employees with excellent experience in chemical and hybrid rocket propulsion as well as a good network in the international space industry. We are sure that disruptive technologies and ways of thinking can lower the cost of orbital launches and at the same time increase flexibility for our customers. These disruptions include in the first place inherently safe hybrid rocket propulsion systems with advanced paraffin-based fuels. Our launcher therefore will use "green propulsion"​ without toxicity and environmental harms. Other important disruptive technologies include COTS components for avionics, state of the art production technology for light weight composite structures, 3D printing of various parts, and decreasing cost by serial production. For example, our main engine will be used several times on the launcher. Our first product in development is a single stage sounding rocket using a hybrid rocket engine to deliver institutional and commercial experiments into a micro gravity environment during a suborbital flight. Based on that technology demonstrator, a mini launcher with a target payload of 400 kg into a Low Earth Orbit will be developed.

entityDescription:
Argo Semiconductors was founded in 2021 by a group of semiconductors and antenna professionals that have built and brought to the market numerous successful RFIC products and antenna products. 
Argo Semi’s vision is to deliver silicon RF and antenna technologies that will make the modern cellular radios more accessible to large and needy populations, such as in India and Africa. Argo Semi has developed unique solutions that allow substantial cost savings for 5G Radio Units and it has established relations with tier-1 semiconductor providers and operators. 
Solution & Product
ArgoSemi has developed silicon and antenna technologies that allow the decoupling of the number of data processing chains in a sub-6GHz radio from the number of the antenna elements attached to these chains. Consequently, a smaller number of data processing chains can be traded for antenna arrays with a larger number of antenna elements. Part of this solution is a true 2-dimensional antenna panel for the 3.5GHz band that relies on low cost Printed Circuit Board (PCB) manufacturing, as opposed to 3D structures requiring expensive customized manufacturing used by the competition. The value to the end-user is the flexibility to control the trade-off of coverage-vs-capacity in the deployment, allowing substantial cost savings.

Innovation & Scalability
The solution offered by ArgoSemi is enabled by multiple innovative elements, such as embedded active splitter/combiners, innovative antennas for massive MIMO, as well as the small cell, distributed beamforming techniques and digital intensive RF architectures. ArgoSemi is possessing an expanding patent portfolio, presently including one granted patent and five pending ones. Our patent portfolio creates a barrier-to-entry for the competition and allows our company to pursue its objective, that is, to trade unneeded performance to achieve a substantial cost reduction. Our unique proposition has already attracted the attention of large potential customers, primarily in the APAC geographical area. 
Traction & achievements
Argo Semi collaborates with tier-1 semiconductor companies that wish to exploit the Open Radio Access Network (ORAN) and penetrate the cellular market. Argo Semi has in-house developed sub-6GHz silicon RF technology that can be used for RFIC complements of these tier-1 semiconductor companies. Furthermore, Argo Semi has launched its second generation of the pioneering printed circuit antenna array product. The above have been achieved while the company operates in a self-financed mode. 
Team & Why Us
Argo Semi has been founded by a team of industry professionals with long experience in the semiconductor industry and the antenna industry, both at the engineering/product development domain and the business development. The core team is formed by old colleagues from Broadcom, one of the largest semiconductors companies in the world with specialty on communications circuits, they have developed products that collectively have been sold in billions of units and they hold tenths of patents. Presently, ArgoSemi’s team of about 25 people, including either employees or long-term outsource engineers, has senior and talented junior engineers, about half of them holding a PhD degree and most of the remaining ones holding an MSc degree.

entityDescription: A startup space company developing a specialised construction brick for use in orbit to build an industrial platform. The platform would be called the orbital locker and would allow for in orbit service providers to produce a standardised module that can fit into the locker allowing the company to maintain a permanent base of operations in orbit without the need to relaunch new satellites. This platform would also facilitate the integration of orbit service providers and improve efficiency and cooperation, each company would be able to utilise each others activities and streamline production processes. The locker would provide power and other essential resources needed for the modules continued life in space. Space debris could be collected along with defunct satellites, brought to the locker, decomissioned or broken down, then passed to another module for refining and another to be used for 3D printing.

entityDescription:
URBASOFIA is a town and regional planning company based in Bucharest and established in 2011. The company has a significant portfolio of implemented projects across Europe, and is supported by the expertise of a core team that is diverse in gender and nationality, experts in urban and regional planning, community planning and co-design, social innovation and social inclusiveness, geography as well as Smart City interventions. 
The core values of the company are: quality, accountability, creativity, innovativeness, integrity and trust, equality, collaboration and long-term vision. As a laboratory for urban development, policy design and territorial cohesion, the high-level academic research conducted revolves around more integrated, participatory, realistic and smart-oriented solutions to pressing urban problems, both socio-economic as well as environmental. In short, the company designs and manages complex planning processes and EU projects directed to urban, environmental and territorial studies, with specific expertise centred on: 
• Town and regional strategic and environmental planning,
• Urban policy design and implementation,
• Methodologies for testing (monitoring and evaluation of results) innovative urban actions and pilots initiatives under urban development research projects, 
• Social inclusion and social innovation, 
• Urban regeneration,
• Community co-designing and youth involvement in the planning process,
• Smart city strategies,
• Training, communication and dissemination, and
• Management of European-funded projects.
The company has been involved in an extensive number of European projects (ICT-PSP, Horizon 2020 and Europe, Interreg South-East-Europe and Danube Transnational Programme, URBACT, National Italian and Romanian ESF and ERDF programmes, etc.). The clients are a high number of cities across Europe, and URBASOFIA has extensive linkages with national and international public authorities at local, regional and national level, as well as Architecture and Planning Universities and relevant planning institutions. 
With 11 employed staff in total, URBASOFIA provides a team of highly skilled individuals, three of them holding doctorates and the rest of the team (urban planners, regional planners, experts in governance and participatory processes, geographers) being specifically qualified to implement planning processes. URBASOFIA is certified SR EN ISO 9001:2015 for Urban and Regional Planning, Research services and Project management via RINA SIMTEX Certificate no. 34055/16/R.

Sustainable Business solutions
Nextek delivers business-focused projects and solutions for Government agencies, Industry Groups, Universities and Research Institutes as well as Private SME’s, Retailers, Brand owners, Manufactures and multinational fortune 500 organisations.
Recycling Technology Expertise
Nextek works directly with leading equipment suppliers in the waste and recycling industry completing trials and process evaluations to optimise performance and outcomes for our clients. 
Solving Waste Challenges
Nextek provides expertise and solutions for complex waste challenges. Our approach is to work closely with clients to design products for recyclability and improve resource efficiency to deliver effective business outcomes. 
Circular Economy
Nextek’s approach is to work together with our clients to help them develop sustainable products with high recycled content aligned with their environmental goals and a focus on the circular economy.
